It underscores the importance of generosity and kindness, assuring that acts of goodness are beloved by Allah. By contributing to welfare and avoiding greed, believers uphold the virtue of selflessness, ensuring the spread of goodness in society.
orig: وأنفقوا في سبيل الله ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة وأحسنوا إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And complete the Hajj and 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] – then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned [home]. Those are ten complete [days]. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse provides detailed guidance on the rituals of Hajj and 'Umrah, emphasizing the completion of these acts purely for Allah's sake. It acknowledges practical challenges like illness or being prevented from reaching the Kaaba, offering alternatives such as fasting, charity, or sacrificing an animal. The verse also highlights the interconnectedness of Hajj and 'Umrah, mentioning the specific practices for those unable to afford the sacrificial animal. It concludes with a reminder to fear Allah and be conscious of His severe punishment, underscoring the importance of sincerity and adherence to divine instructions in these significant acts of worship.
orig: وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله فإن أحصرتم فما استيسر من الهدي ولا تحلقوا رءوسكم حتى يبلغ الهدي محله فمن كان منكم مريضا أو به أذى من رأسه ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك فإذا أمنتم فمن تمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج فما استيسر من الهدي فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجعتم تلك عشرة كاملة ذلك لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: The Hajj is (in) well-known months. So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein (by entering the state of Ihram), there is (to be for him) no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do, Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding.
interpretation: This verse outlines the sacred months designated for the performance of Hajj and emphasizes the behavioral conduct expected from those undertaking the pilgrimage. Pilgrims are instructed to abstain from sexual relations, sinful acts, and disputes, upholding the sanctity of this significant religious observance. Additionally, it is advised to prepare adequately for the journey, stressing that the best form of preparation is piety and consciousness of Allah. Ultimately, it calls upon people of understanding to be mindful and fear Allah, highlighting the spiritual and ethical dimensions of pilgrimage beyond its physical acts.
orig: الحج أشهر معلومات فمن فرض فيهن الحج فلا رفث ولا فسوق ولا جدال في الحج وما تفعلوا من خير يعلمه الله وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى واتقون يا أولي الألباب

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord [during pilgrimage]. But when you depart from 'Arafat, remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram. And remember Him, as He has guided you, for indeed, you were before that among those astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the permissibility of seeking lawful benefits and provisions from Allah during the Hajj pilgrimage. It emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah, especially at specific holy sites like Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, following the rites of 'Arafat. The verse also serves as a reminder of Allah's guidance and the transformation from a state of misguidance to one of enlightenment through His mercy and guidance.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله عند المشعر الحرام واذكروه كما هداكم وإن كنتم من قبله لمن الضالين

translation: Then depart from the place from where all the people depart and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse instructs pilgrims during the Hajj to follow the common practice of leaving from a specific place, likely referring to Arafat, which is a crucial part of the pilgrimage rites. It emphasizes unity and conformity to collective actions in religious practices. Additionally, it advises seeking Allah's forgiveness, reminding believers of His boundless mercy and readiness to pardon those who repent.
orig: ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your remembrance of your forefathers or with [much] greater remembrance. And among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he will have in the Hereafter no share.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah, especially after completing the prescribed rites of pilgrimage. It draws a comparison between the customary respect and remembrance given to ancestors and the even greater remembrance that should be directed towards Allah. Highlightedly, the verse also addresses the contrast in human attitudes towards worldly and spiritual gains, warning that those who focus solely on worldly desires and neglect their spiritual responsibilities may find themselves devoid of any reward in the Hereafter.
orig: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

translation: And among them are those who say, 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the balanced supplication of believers who seek both worldly and spiritual benefits. They pray for good in both this life and the Hereafter, showing their understanding that success is not limited to the material world. Additionally, they ask for protection from the punishment of the Fire, indicating their awareness of the spiritual consequences of their actions and their desire for salvation and mercy from Allah. It underscores the holistic approach to well-being that Islam encourages, encompassing both the temporal and eternal aspects of life.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار

translation: For them is a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and divine justice. It indicates that people will receive the outcomes of their actions, whether good or bad. It also serves as a reminder that Allah's judgment is not delayed; He is swift in holding individuals accountable for their deeds. This can instill a sense of urgency in believers to act righteously and be conscious of their behavior, as divine recompense is both certain and prompt.
orig: أولئك لهم نصيب مما كسبوا والله سريع الحساب

translation: And remember Allah during specific numbered days. Then whoever hastens (his departure) in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays (until the third) - there is no sin upon him - for him who fears Allah. And fear Allah and know that unto Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse pertains to the rites of Hajj, specifically the practice of remembering Allah during the days of Tashreeq. It emphasizes flexibility in completing certain rituals over two or three days, signifying that there is no sin in either choice as long as one maintains piety and consciousness of Allah. The overarching message is to observe God-consciousness (Taqwa) and to remain aware of the inevitable return to Allah for the final gathering and accountability.
orig: واذكروا الله في أيام معدودات فمن تعجل في يومين فلا إثم عليه ومن تأخر فلا إثم عليه لمن اتقى واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم إليه تحشرون

translation: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of certain individuals who outwardly display commendable behavior and speak in pleasing ways, yet inwardly harbor ill intentions. They invoke God as a witness to their sincerity, but their actions reveal a stark contrast. Such individuals are in fact deeply contentious and oppositional, highlighting the discrepancy between outward appearances and inner realities. This serves as a caution to be discerning in judging people's character based solely on their outward demeanor.
orig: ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام

translation: And when he goes away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocritical behavior of certain individuals who, when in positions of authority or power, actively work to create disorder and devastation. Their actions lead to the destruction of agriculture and livestock, disrupting life and prosperity. The verse highlights that such behavior is detested by Allah, emphasizing the divine disapproval of corruption and the moral responsibility to maintain harmony and goodness in the world.
orig: وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل والله لا يحب الفساد

translation: When it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride in the sin takes hold of him. Hell is enough for him, and it is a terrible resting place.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and obstinacy of some individuals who, when reminded to be conscious of Allah and avoid sin, react with pride and become more entrenched in their wrongdoing. The verse warns that such arrogance and persistence in sin leads to a dire consequence: Hell, which is described as a dreadful and terrible abode. This serves as a stern reminder of the gravity of ignoring divine counsel and the serious repercussions of allowing pride to prevent repentance and righteousness.
orig: وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم فحسبه جهنم ولبئس المهاد

translation: But among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sacrifices and dedication of certain individuals who are willing to give up their own desires and even their lives to achieve the pleasure of Allah. It emphasizes the high level of selflessness and devotion required to attain such a state. Furthermore, it reassures that Allah is compassionate and caring toward His devotees who make such sacrifices, acknowledging and valuing their profound commitment and actions.
orig: ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: O you who have believed, enter into Islam completely [and perfectly] and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to embrace Islam in its entirety, urging them to commit fully to its principles and practices. It also warns against being swayed by the deceptive schemes of Satan, who is explicitly recognized as a clear and outright enemy. The verse emphasizes the importance of wholehearted devotion to faith and the dangers of succumbing to evil influences.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ادخلوا في السلم كافة ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: But if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse cautions the believers against deviating from the path of righteousness after receiving clear guidance and evidence. It underscores the attributes of Allah as both powerful and wise, implying that any deviation will be met with His judicious authority. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the divine guidance and the importance of adhering strictly to the teachings provided.
orig: فإن زللتم من بعد ما جاءتكم البينات فاعلموا أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Are they waiting for Allah to come to them in the shadows of the clouds along with the angels, and (then) the matter will be decided? And to Allah [all] matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate accountability to Allah. It reminds people that divine intervention will be unmistakable and awe-inspiring, and that all matters will return to Allah for final judgment. This serves as a warning against heedlessness and encourages individuals to reflect on their actions and spiritual state in anticipation of this divine encounter.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة وقضي الأمر وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many a clear sign We have given them. Whoever changes the favor of Allah after it has come to him, then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel of the numerous clear signs that were given to them by Allah. The mention of these signs underscores the importance of recognizing and valuing divine guidance. The latter part of the verse warns against altering or misusing the blessings and guidance provided by Allah. It emphasizes that such ingratitude and distortion of Allah's favors will result in severe punishment, reflecting the seriousness of remaining steadfast and true to the divine path once it has been shown.
orig: سل بني إسرائيل كم آتيناهم من آية بينة ومن يبدل نعمة الله من بعد ما جاءته فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: The life of this world has been made appealing to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe. But those who fear Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It explains how disbelievers are often enamored by the material aspects of life and tend to mock the believers, who prioritize their faith and piety. The verse reassures the believers that, despite any ridicule they face, they will have a higher status on the Day of Resurrection. Additionally, it emphasizes Allah’s boundless provision, which is bestowed upon whom He wills without any calculation.
orig: زين للذين كفروا الحياة الدنيا ويسخرون من الذين آمنوا والذين اتقوا فوقهم يوم القيامة والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: Mankind was [of] one religion [before their deviation]; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. And none differed over the Scripture except those who were given it – after the clear proofs came to them – out of jealous animosity among themselves. And Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity of mankind in their original state of faith before deviating into differing factions. It points to the divine wisdom in sending prophets with glad tidings and warnings, and Scriptures as authentic criteria to resolve disputes. The verse further identifies that divergences were not due to the lack of clarity, but arose from envy and animosity among people who had received clear evidence. It emphasizes that divine guidance, bestowed upon the believers by Allah's will, leads to the truth and the straight path. This signifies the importance of divine revelation and guidance in achieving unity and understanding among humanity.
orig: كان الناس أمة واحدة فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين وأنزل معهم الكتاب بالحق ليحكم بين الناس فيما اختلفوا فيه وما اختلف فيه إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم فهدى الله الذين آمنوا لما اختلفوا فيه من الحق بإذنه والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: Do you think that you will enter Paradise without having the likes of those who passed away before you? They were afflicted by suffering and adversity and were so shaken that even the messenger and those who believed with him said, 'When will the help of Allah come?' Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trials and tribulations that believers must endure as a test of their faith, much like those experienced by past communities. It highlights that such hardships are a part of the journey towards attaining Paradise and serves to reassure the believers that despite these challenges, the assistance and support of Allah are always close.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يأتكم مثل الذين خلوا من قبلكم مستهم البأساء والضراء وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول والذين آمنوا معه متى نصر الله ألا إن نصر الله قريب

translation: They ask you what they should spend. Say, 'Whatever you spend of good is [to be] for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.'
interpretation: This verse instructs believers on the proper allocation of their charitable spending, emphasizing prioritizing family members, orphans, those in need, and travelers. It underscores the importance of consciously acting with goodness and reminds the believers that Allah is fully aware of their benevolent actions, thereby encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in their charitable endeavors.
orig: يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل ما أنفقتم من خير فللوالدين والأقربين واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that human perception is limited and often flawed. What we might see as difficult or unpleasant, such as the obligation to fight in just circumstances, can have hidden benefits. Conversely, what we desire or love might be harmful in ways we cannot foresee. The verse serves as a reminder to trust in Allah's wisdom and knowledge over our own limited understanding.
orig: كتب عليكم القتال وهو كره لكم وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم وعسى أن تحبوا شيئا وهو شر لكم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: They ask you about the sacred month—about fighting therein. Say, 'Fighting therein is great sin, but averting people from the way of Allah and disbelief in Him and [preventing access to] al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater [evil] in the sight of Allah. And fitnah is greater than killing.' And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever—for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse addresses the concerns about fighting during the sacred months, which were traditionally times of peace. While acknowledging that such fighting is a grave sin, it delineates that greater injustices, such as obstructing the path of God, denying faith, barring worshippers from the sacred mosque, and expelling its people, are considered far more severe transgressions. The verse informs the believers that their adversaries will persist in battling them with the intent to make them abandon their faith. It warns that those who renounce their faith and die as disbelievers will find their deeds nullified, and they will be consigned to an eternal punishment in Hell.
orig: يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه قل قتال فيه كبير وصد عن سبيل الله وكفر به والمسجد الحرام وإخراج أهله منه أكبر عند الله والفتنة أكبر من القتل ولا يزالون يقاتلونكم حتى يردوكم عن دينكم إن استطاعوا ومن يرتدد منكم عن دينه فيمت وهو كافر فأولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of faith, migration, and striving in the path of Allah. It reassures believers that their sacrifices and efforts are recognized and valued by Allah, who promises them His mercy. The mention of Allah being forgiving and merciful highlights His readiness to accept and reward the sincere efforts of His servants despite their flaws and shortcomings.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمت الله والله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, 'In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.' And they ask you what they should spend. Say, 'The excess [beyond needs].' Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you might give thought.
interpretation: This verse addresses queries about the permissibility and consequences of wine and gambling. It acknowledges their dual nature, recognizing both the benefits and the substantial harms they cause. The emphasis is on the greater weight of sin over the benefits, guiding believers to avoid them. Additionally, the instruction on spending focuses on giving from one's surplus, promoting a balanced approach to charity and personal responsibility. The verse underscores the divine intent to provide clarity for thoughtful consideration by believers.
orig: يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: In this world and the Hereafter. They ask you about orphans. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best; and if you mix your affairs with theirs, they are your brothers. Allah knows the corrupter from the amender. Had Allah wished, He could have put you into difficulties. Surely Allah is Mighty, Wise.’
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of caring for orphans and treating them with kindness and equity. It encourages the integration and fair treatment of orphans within the Muslim community, highlighting that they should be seen as siblings. Allah's awareness of each person's true intentions is a reminder to act sincerely and justly. The verse also reflects Allah's compassionate nature, showing that He does not wish to impose undue hardship on people, thus guiding them towards righteous actions with wisdom and strength.
orig: في الدنيا والآخرة ويسألونك عن اليتامى قل إصلاح لهم خير وإن تخالطوهم فإخوانكم والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح ولو شاء الله لأعنتكم إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. A believing slave woman is better than a polytheistic woman, even if she pleases you. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. A believing slave man is better than a polytheistic man, even if he pleases you. Those invite [you] to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and to forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His signs to the people that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of religious faith in marital relations, advising Muslims to marry only those who share their belief in Islam. It suggests that faith is a more crucial criterion than social or material status, highlighting that a believing slave is better than a free polytheist. The verse also warns of the spiritual dangers posed by associating closely with those who might lead one away from the path of Allah, contrasting the destructive potential of polytheism with the promise of paradise and forgiveness offered by Allah. This directive is ultimately aimed at safeguarding the spiritual well-being of believers and ensuring that their closest relationships are rooted in shared faith and values.
orig: ولا تنكحوا المشركات حتى يؤمن ولأمة مؤمنة خير من مشركة ولو أعجبتكم ولا تنكحوا المشركين حتى يؤمنوا ولعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك ولو أعجبكم أولئك يدعون إلى النار والله يدعو إلى الجنة والمغفرة بإذنه ويبين آياته للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: They ask you concerning menstruation. Say: it is a discomfort. So keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are purified. When they are purified, then approach them as Allah has enjoined upon you. Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of menstruation and provides guidance on the appropriate conduct. It emphasizes that menstruation is a natural state of discomfort, during which intimate relations are to be avoided. Once the period ends and purification is achieved, normal marital relations can resume. The verse underscores the importance of both physical and spiritual cleanliness, linking it with Allah's love for those who frequently seek repentance and maintain purity.
orig: ويسألونك عن المحيض قل هو أذى فاعتزلوا النساء في المحيض ولا تقربوهن حتى يطهرن فإذا تطهرن فأتوهن من حيث أمركم الله إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين

translation: Your wives are a place of sowing of seed for you, so come to your place of cultivation however you wish and put forth [righteousness] for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically compares wives to fertile ground, emphasizing the lawful aspects of marital relations and the procreation and nurturing of offspring within the boundaries set by Allah. It encourages mutual respect and legitimate intimacy in marriage. The directive to 'put forth [righteousness] for yourselves' encourages believers to engage in good deeds and maintain piety, mindful of their accountability before Allah. The verse concludes with a message of hope and reassurance for the believers, emphasizing the rewards and good tidings for those who adhere to these principles.
orig: نساؤكم حرث لكم فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم وقدموا لأنفسكم واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And do not make [your oath by] Allah an excuse against being righteous and fearing Allah and making peace among people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse advises against using oaths by Allah as a pretext to avoid good deeds, righteousness, or reconciliation among people. It emphasizes that swearing by Allah should not impede fulfilling obligations of righteousness, piety, and peacemaking. The reminder that Allah is Hearing and Knowing underscores His awareness of one's intentions and actions, promoting sincerity and moral integrity.
orig: ولا تجعلوا الله عرضة لأيمانكم أن تبروا وتتقوا وتصلحوا بين الناس والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah does not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He imposes blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and understanding nature by emphasizing that He does not hold individuals accountable for unintentional mistakes or thoughtless statements. Rather, accountability is tied to deliberate, conscious actions and the true intentions of the heart. This underscores the importance of sincerity and intentionality in one's faith and actions. Moreover, it reaffirms that Allah is both forgiving and patient with His servants, indicating His willingness to pardon and his patience in dealing with human shortcomings.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم والله غفور حليم

translation: For those who take an oath of abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months is ordained. But if they go back, then Allah is surely Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses husbands who swear to abstain from marital relations with their wives. It indicates that such abstinence should not extend beyond a four-month period. If the husbands choose to reconcile and end their abstinence within this period, they should know that Allah is merciful and forgiving, encouraging them to resume their marital duties and mend their relationships.
orig: للذين يؤلون من نسائهم تربص أربعة أشهر فإن فاءوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if they decide on divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the decision to divorce is a significant and serious one, taken with the awareness that Allah fully hears and knows the intentions and reasons behind it. It implies the importance of being mindful and sincere in such personal and impactful decisions, keeping in mind the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. This also serves as a reminder that one should act justly and within the ethical boundaries set by Islamic teachings, trusting that Allah is ever-aware of the actions and thoughts of individuals.
orig: وإن عزموا الطلاق فإن الله سميع عليم

translation: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves for three monthly periods, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have the better right to take them back in that period if they desire reconciliation. And they (women) have rights similar to those (of men) over them in kindness, but men have a degree (of responsibility) over them. And Allah is Exalted in Power, Wise.
interpretation: This verse lays out the waiting period ('iddah) that a divorced woman must observe before she can remarry, which is three menstrual cycles. It emphasizes that during this period, women must not conceal any pregnancy, as this would have implications for rights and responsibilities. Additionally, it grants the former husband the right to reconcile and take the wife back during this waiting period, provided the intention is to reconcile and improve the relationship. The verse also highlights that while men and women have mutual rights and responsibilities towards each other, men have a degree of responsibility and authority over women, which is seen in the context of familial and societal structures. This provision is part of the broader framework of Islamic law that aims to ensure fairness, justice, and stability within families, recognizing both gender-specific roles and mutual obligations.
orig: والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك إن أرادوا إصلاحا ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف وللرجال عليهن درجة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Divorce may be pronounced twice, then the wife may either be retained honorably or released kindly. It is not lawful for you to take back anything you have given the women unless both fear that they cannot maintain the limits set by Allah. If you fear that they cannot maintain the limits, there will be no blame on either of them if the woman redeems herself. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. Those who transgress the limits of Allah are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the process and conditions for divorce within Islamic law, emphasizing both the limitation and structure of divorce (allowing it only twice before final separation) and the necessity of fair treatment (either holding onto the wife in an acceptable manner or releasing her with kindness). It also addresses financial aspects, prohibiting husbands from reclaiming any dowry or gifts they have given unless both parties fear they cannot abide by Allah's rules. If fears arise about adherence to divine limits, then there can be no blame if the wife offers compensation to secure her separation. This verse underscores the importance of observing the boundaries set by Allah and warns against overstepping them, declaring that those who do so are unjust.
orig: الطلاق مرتان فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان ولا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا مما آتيتموهن شيئا إلا أن يخافا ألا يقيما حدود الله فإن خفتم ألا يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به تلك حدود الله فلا تعتدوها ومن يتعد حدود الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And if he has divorced her (for the third time), then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. And if the latter husband divorces her, there is no blame upon the woman and her former husband for returning to each other if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah. These are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the laws of divorce in Islam, specifically after a husband has divorced his wife three times. It indicates that a woman who has been divorced three times by the same man cannot remarry him until she has genuinely married another man, highlighting the seriousness and finality of a triple divorce to prevent its misuse. The verse underscores that, if the second marriage ends in divorce, the woman and her former husband are permitted to remarry, provided they believe they can adhere to the divine limits and values set forth by Allah. This demonstrates the importance of intention and respect for divine laws within the marital relationship, urging both parties to reflect on their ability to maintain the boundaries established by Allah for a harmonious and righteous life together.
orig: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره فإن طلقها فلا جناح عليهما أن يتراجعا إن ظنا أن يقيما حدود الله وتلك حدود الله يبينها لقوم يعلمون

translation: When you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, either retain them honorably or release them honorably. Do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress. Whoever does that has indeed wronged himself. Do not take the verses of Allah in jest. Remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom, by which He instructs you. Fear Allah and know that Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating women with fairness and respect during and after the process of divorce. It advises against holding onto them with the intention of causing harm or inconvenience. The verse urges believers to remember the teachings and blessings they receive from Allah, highlighting the need to act with piety and integrity. It underscores that any act of transgression, particularly in matters of divorce, is a wrong against oneself, as Allah’s knowledge encompasses every action.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو سرحوهن بمعروف ولا تمسكوهن ضرارا لتعتدوا ومن يفعل ذلك فقد ظلم نفسه ولا تتخذوا آيات الله هزوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: When you divorce women and they have reached their waiting period, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves in a lawful manner. This instruction is for whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day; that is more virtuous and purer for you. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse advises against obstructing women from returning to their previous husbands after their waiting period (iddah) post-divorce, provided they mutually agree. It underscores the importance of upholding principles of fairness and seeking what is lawful and good. The guidance is particularly directed at believers as an expression of faith and moral conduct, emphasizing that Allah's wisdom surpasses human knowledge. The verse highlights the virtues of compassion, fairness, and purity in relationships and decision-making.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن إذا تراضوا بينهم بالمعروف ذلك يوعظ به من كان منكم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ذلكم أزكى لكم وأطهر والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Mothers may breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing [period]. Upon the father is their provision and clothing according to what is acceptable. No person is charged with more than their capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, and no father through his child. And upon the [father's] heir is [a duty] like that [of the father]. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon either of them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon you provided you give payment according to what is acceptable. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the shared responsibilities of both parents in the upbringing and care of their children. It states that mothers are encouraged to breastfeed their children for two years, while fathers are responsible for providing for them in a fair and just manner. The verse also emphasizes that no one should be burdened beyond their capacity, and that no harm should come to either parent on account of their child. Additionally, it allows for flexibility and mutual agreement between parents regarding weaning and the use of a wet nurse, while reminding them to be mindful of their duties before Allah, who is aware of all their actions. The underlying principle is to ensure the well-being of the child while maintaining fairness and compassion between the parents.
orig: والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين لمن أراد أن يتم الرضاعة وعلى المولود له رزقهن وكسوتهن بالمعروف لا تكلف نفس إلا وسعها لا تضار والدة بولدها ولا مولود له بولده وعلى الوارث مثل ذلك فإن أرادا فصالا عن تراض منهما وتشاور فلا جناح عليهما وإن أردتم أن تسترضعوا أولادكم فلا جناح عليكم إذا سلمتم ما آتيتم بالمعروف واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those of you who die and leave wives behind - they (the widows) shall wait concerning themselves for four months and ten days. Then when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an appropriate manner. And Allah is Fully Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse outlines the waiting period (iddah) for widows, which is four months and ten days after the death of their husbands. The purpose of this period is to ensure that the widow is not pregnant and to provide a time of mourning and adjustment. Once this period is over, the widow is free to make decisions about her own life, such as remarrying, without any blame or societal criticism, provided her actions are appropriate and in accordance with Islamic principles. The mention of Allah's awareness serves as a reminder that God knows all of one's actions and intentions.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا فإذا بلغن أجلهن فلا جناح عليكم فيما فعلن في أنفسهن بالمعروف والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: There is no sin upon you if you hint at a proposal of marriage to women or keep it concealed in your hearts. Allah knows that you will remember them. But do not make a secret promise with them except that you speak an honorable word. And do not decide on the marriage contract until the prescribed waiting period reaches its term. And know that Allah knows what is in your hearts, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah provides guidance on how to navigate the period of waiting ('iddah) after a woman's husband has passed away or after a divorce before she can remarry. It reassures believers that there is no sin in hinting at a marriage proposal or keeping such intentions in their hearts while emphasizing the importance of respectful and honorable communication. Importantly, it prohibits making secret promises, emphasizing transparency and propriety. The verse reminds the believers of Allah's omniscience, encouraging sincerity and caution in their actions, while also highlighting Allah’s attributes of forgiveness and forbearance, offering comfort and hope.
orig: ولا جناح عليكم فيما عرضتم به من خطبة النساء أو أكننتم في أنفسكم علم الله أنكم ستذكرونهن ولكن لا تواعدوهن سرا إلا أن تقولوا قولا معروفا ولا تعزموا عقدة النكاح حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه واعلموا أن الله غفور حليم

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women you have not touched nor specified for them an obligation. But give them a gift of compensation, the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability - a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of divorce before the marriage is consummated or a dowry is specified. It emphasizes that, in such cases, men should provide a decent gift of compensation to the women, reflective of their financial status. This act of providing for the woman, even in the absence of a consummated marriage or agreed mahr (dowry), is a gesture of goodwill and obligatory for those who embody virtuous behavior and righteousness.
orig: لا جناح عليكم إن طلقتم النساء ما لم تمسوهن أو تفرضوا لهن فريضة ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره متاعا بالمعروف حقا على المحسنين

translation: And if you divorce them before you have touched them, while you had already specified a dowry for them, then [give] half of what you specified—unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes it. And to forgo it is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of divorce before the marriage is consummated and a dowry has been specified. It dictates that in such cases, the wife is entitled to half of the dowry unless she chooses to forgive it or the husband, who holds the marriage contract, decides to forgo it. The verse emphasizes that forgiving the dowry obligation is closer to righteousness, encouraging both parties to exercise graciousness and mutual respect. It underscores the importance of maintaining decency and kindness even in the difficult circumstances of divorce, reminding that Allah is aware of all actions, and thus guiding the believers towards moral and considerate behavior.
orig: وإن طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن وقد فرضتم لهن فريضة فنصف ما فرضتم إلا أن يعفون أو يعفو الذي بيده عقدة النكاح وأن تعفوا أقرب للتقوى ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Guard strictly your (habit of) prayers, especially the Middle Prayer; and stand before Allah in a devout (frame of mind).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the regular observance of prayers, highlighting the significance of the 'Middle Prayer' which is often interpreted as the Asr prayer. It instructs believers to approach prayers with a sense of devotion, humility, and mindfulness. The directive to 'stand before Allah in a devout state' underscores the need for sincerity, focus, and a submissive attitude during prayer, reflecting a deep commitment to one's faith and reverence towards Allah.
orig: حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وقوموا لله قانتين

translation: But if you fear (an enemy), then pray on foot or riding. But when you are secure, then remember Allah, as He has taught you that which you did not (previously) know.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges situations of fear or danger where the prescribed formal prayer may not be feasible in its usual manner. It permits flexibility in how one performs their prayers, such as praying while moving. However, it emphasizes that once safety is restored, believers should resume their regular practice and remember Allah in the way He has instructed. This reflects the balance between adherence to religious practices and practical considerations of safety and necessity.
orig: فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: And those of you who die and leave wives behind, the wives should wait for four months and ten days. But if they leave [i.e., depart from the waiting period], there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the waiting period (iddah) that widows must observe after their husband's death, which is four months and ten days. It is a period for them to mourn and respect the deceased. However, if widows choose to remarry or move on in life in a respectable way after this period, there is no sin on them or on others in what they do. This command reflects Allah's wisdom and might in legislating rules that consider the emotional and practical aspects of life.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا وصية لأزواجهم متاعا إلى الحول غير إخراج فإن خرجن فلا جناح عليكم في ما فعلن في أنفسهن من معروف والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical responsibility towards divorced women. It underlines that they should be provided for in a respectable and proper manner. The term 'muttaqeen' (the righteous) implies that those who fear Allah and are conscious of their duties towards Him are expected to honor this provision. This highlights the Qur’anic principle of fairness and kindness even in circumstances of separation, ensuring that divorced women are treated with dignity and respect.
orig: وللمطلقات متاع بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you might use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose behind the revelations and signs provided by Allah: to encourage understanding and contemplation. It underscores the importance of using reason and intellect to comprehend the divine messages and guidance. Through reflection and rational thought, believers are urged to recognize the wisdom and truth in the verses revealed by Allah.
orig: كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in many thousands, fearing death? God said to them, 'Die'; then He restored them to life. Indeed, God is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse recalls an event where a large group of people fled in fear of death, showcasing their lack of trust in God's plan. God caused them to die and then brought them back to life to demonstrate His power over life and death. It serves as a reminder that God's grace is abundant, but human beings often fail to appreciate it. This event is meant to strengthen the believers' faith, illustrating that fear should not lead one to forget God's ultimate control and mercy.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم أحياهم إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: And fight in the way of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving and struggling in the path of Allah, which can encompass not only physical combat but also standing up for righteousness and justice. The concluding part reminds the believers of Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, reassuring them that their efforts and sacrifices are acknowledged and guided by divine wisdom and justice.
orig: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله واعلموا أن الله سميع عليم

translation: Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to offer their wealth in the way of Allah (charity, good deeds) with the promise that Allah will richly reward them. By describing it as a 'goodly loan,' the verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly possessions and the act of giving as an investment in the Hereafter. The assurance that Allah manages wealth and resources – by withholding or granting abundance – reminds believers of Allah's ultimate control over all affairs, urging trust in His plan and generosity. The reminder that everyone will ultimately return to Allah underscores the eternal significance of their actions in this life.
orig: من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له أضعافا كثيرة والله يقبض ويبسط وإليه ترجعون

translation: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after [the time of] Moses when they said to a prophet of theirs, 'Send to us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah'? He said, 'Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting was prescribed for you?' They said, 'And why should we not fight in the cause of Allah when we have been driven out from our homes and from our children?' But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse calls attention to the Children of Israel after the era of Moses, highlighting their request for a king to lead them in battle for the sake of God. The prophet questions their resolve, predicting that they might avoid fighting even if it is ordained. Despite their assertion that they would fight due to their displacement and suffering, many of them ultimately retract when faced with the actual command to fight. This brings to light the discrepancy between words and actions, and it serves as a reminder that God is fully aware of those who are unjust and hypocritical in their commitments.
orig: ألم تر إلى الملإ من بني إسرائيل من بعد موسى إذ قالوا لنبي لهم ابعث لنا ملكا نقاتل في سبيل الله قال هل عسيتم إن كتب عليكم القتال ألا تقاتلوا قالوا وما لنا ألا نقاتل في سبيل الله وقد أخرجنا من ديارنا وأبنائنا فلما كتب عليهم القتال تولوا إلا قليلا منهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Their prophet said to them: 'Indeed, Allah has appointed Talut as a king over you.' They said: 'How can he have kingship over us while we are more deserving of the kingship than him, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature. And Allah gives His sovereignty to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing, all-Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a significant moment when the Israelites were informed by their prophet that Allah had appointed Talut (Saul) as their king. Despite their objections, based on his lack of wealth and their own aspirations for leadership, the prophet clarifies that divine choice and qualities like knowledge and physical capability, which Talut possessed, are the true criteria for leadership. It emphasizes that Allah’s wisdom and authority surpass human judgment and that sovereignty is granted by Allah to whom He wills, based on His encompassing knowledge and wisdom.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن الله قد بعث لكم طالوت ملكا قالوا أنى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن أحق بالملك منه ولم يؤت سعة من المال قال إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم والله يؤتي ملكه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Their prophet said to them, 'The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord and remnants of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights that as proof of the newly appointed king's legitimacy, a sacred Ark will be delivered to them, symbolizing divine approval and containing elements providing spiritual peace and continuity from prophetic lineage. The transportation of the Ark by angels underscores heavenly sanction, and it serves as a test of faith for the people.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت فيه سكينة من ربكم وبقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون تحمله الملائكة إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Then when Saul marched forth with his army, he said, 'Indeed, Allah will be testing you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, excepting one who takes [from it] in the hollow of his hand.' But they drank from it, except a [very] few of them. Then when he had crossed it along with those who believed with him, they said, 'There is no power for us today against Goliath and his soldiers.' But those who were certain that they would meet Allah said, 'How many a small group has overcome a large group by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient.'
interpretation: This verse recounts a significant test during Saul's leadership, where he commands his troops not to drink from a river, with limited exceptions. This test serves to distinguish the truly obedient and disciplined followers from those who lack self-control. When they encounter Goliath's formidable forces, the remaining loyal soldiers initially despair, feeling overpowered. However, the truly faithful ones, those who firmly believe in meeting Allah, draw strength and assurance from their faith. They evoke historical instances where smaller, righteous groups have triumphed over larger forces through Allah's permission. This narrative underscores the importance of patience, faith, and obedience to divine commands in facing and overcoming seemingly insurmountable challenges, highlighting the theme that Allah supports those who are steadfast and faithful.
orig: فلما فصل طالوت بالجنود قال إن الله مبتليكم بنهر فمن شرب منه فليس مني ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني إلا من اغترف غرفة بيده فشربوا منه إلا قليلا منهم فلما جاوزه هو والذين آمنوا معه قالوا لا طاقة لنا اليوم بجالوت وجنوده قال الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو الله كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: And when they went forth to (face) Goliath and his troops, they said, 'Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.'
interpretation: This verse depicts a moment of profound faith and reliance on divine assistance in the face of overwhelming odds. The believers, as they prepare for battle against Goliath and his forces, pray for patience, steadfastness, and victory. It emphasizes the importance of seeking God's help when facing challenges and trusting in His support to overcome adversity.
orig: ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: So they defeated them by Allah’s leave, and David killed Goliath; and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of that which He wills. And if it were not for Allah's repelling some men by means of others, the earth would certainly have been corrupted; but Allah is Gracious to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support granted to the believers in their battle against the disbelievers, exemplified by David's victory over Goliath with Allah's permission. It underscores that David's subsequent endowment with kingship and wisdom is a gift from Allah. The verse also stresses a broader principle: the wisdom in Allah's governance, where He uses the conflicts and struggles among people as a means to prevent corruption and maintain balance in the world. This divine intervention is portrayed as an expression of Allah's grace towards all of creation.
orig: فهزموهم بإذن الله وقتل داوود جالوت وآتاه الله الملك والحكمة وعلمه مما يشاء ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض ولكن الله ذو فضل على العالمين

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Indeed, you are among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truth of the messages being delivered to the Prophet Muhammad. It affirms the authenticity of the revelations and reinforces the Prophet's role as a true messenger of Allah, tasked with conveying God's guidance to humanity. The verse serves to provide assurance and legitimacy both to the Prophet and to the followers of his message.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وإنك لمن المرسلين

translation: These are the messengers; We endowed some of them above others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke directly, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. If Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought each other after clear proofs had come to them. But they differed, so some of them believed and some disbelieved. If Allah had willed, they would not have fought each other, but Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the distinct statuses and roles of various prophets, highlighting specific examples such as Moses, who spoke directly with Allah, and Jesus, who was supported by the Holy Spirit. It underscores divine wisdom in the differentiation of their missions and actions. The latter part addresses human free will and the discord among the people who came after these prophets, noting that while Allah's will is overarching, human disputes and conflicts occurred due to differing beliefs and choices. It emphasizes that Allah's ultimate authority encompasses all occurrences, whether unity or division.
orig: تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات ولكن اختلفوا فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر ولو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, spend from that which We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange, no friendship, and no intercession. And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers to act with charity and generosity, sharing the resources and blessings that God has bestowed upon them. It emphasizes the urgency of performing good deeds by indicating that a Day will come (the Day of Judgment) when earthly transactions, friendships, or intercessions will hold no value. This situation contrasts with the plight of disbelievers, who are ultimately deemed as wrongdoers due to their rejection of faith and failure to act righteously.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا مما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة والكافرون هم الظالمون

translation: Allah! There is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi (throne) extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse, known as Ayat al-Kursi, emphasizes the absolute singularity and sovereignty of Allah. Describing Allah as the Ever-Living and Sustainer underscores His eternal existence and active maintenance of the universe. The attributes of neither drowsiness nor sleep affirm His uninterrupted vigilance and omnipotence. All entities in the heavens and the earth are under His dominion, and His exclusive authority over intercession reflects His ultimate control over all matters. His knowledge encompasses all times, past and future, while human understanding remains limited to what He permits. The imagery of His throne extending over the heavens and the earth symbolizes His supreme authority and extensive power, further reinforced by His tireless preservation of the universe. The verse concludes by acknowledging Allah's sublime and magnanimous nature.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء وسع كرسيه السماوات والأرض ولا يئوده حفظهما وهو العلي العظيم

translation: There is no compulsion in religion, for the right way is clearly distinct from error. So whoever disbelieves in false deities and believes in Allah has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphatically states that faith should be chosen freely without pressure or coercion. The path of righteousness is evident and distinguishable from falsehood. True belief involves rejecting all forms of idolatry or false gods and solely believing in Allah. Such true belief is likened to holding onto a firm and unbreakable support, symbolizing unwavering faith. It reassures believers that Allah is fully aware and attentive to all choices made by individuals, emphasizing His omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: لا إكراه في الدين قد تبين الرشد من الغي فمن يكفر بالطاغوت ويؤمن بالله فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى لا انفصام لها والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into the light. But those who disbelieve, their allies are the false gods. They take them out of light into darkness. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the contrast between the supporters of believers and disbelievers. Allah is depicted as the protector and guide of those who have faith, leading them from ignorance and misguidance to enlightenment and truth. Conversely, disbelievers are aligned with false gods or corrupt leaders, who lead them away from truth into deeper misguidance and ignorance. The verse concludes by stressing the eternal consequence of these choices, highlighting that the disbelievers will face perpetual punishment in Hell for their actions.
orig: الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور والذين كفروا أولياؤهم الطاغوت يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, 'My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death,' he said, 'I give life and cause death.' Abraham said, 'Indeed, Allah brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west.' So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights a debate between Prophet Abraham and a king who claimed the same power as God due to his earthly authority. Abraham challenges the king's claim by pointing out the divine control over the natural world, specifically the rising and setting of the sun, which the king cannot replicate. This illustrates the limits of human power and serves as a reminder of the ultimate sovereignty of Allah over all creation. The verse concludes by emphasizing that Allah does not guide those who are unjust and arrogant in their disbelief.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك إذ قال إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال أنا أحيي وأميت قال إبراهيم فإن الله يأتي بالشمس من المشرق فأت بها من المغرب فبهت الذي كفر والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Or like the one who passed by a town which had fallen into utter ruin. He said, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him up. He said, 'How long have you remained?' The man said, 'I have remained a day or part of a day.' He said, 'No, you have remained for a hundred years. Look at your food and drink; they have not spoiled. And look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. Look at the bones, how We raise them, then We cover them with flesh.' When it became clear to him, he said, 'I know that Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the tremendous power and capability of Allah to resurrect and give life after death. It tells the story of a man who doubted how a decaying town could be brought back to life. Through divine intervention, the man is made an example: Allah causes him to die and revives him after a century. This miraculous event shows that Allah’s will defies the natural process of decay, as evidenced in the man's preserved food and the revival of his donkey. By demonstrating the reconstruction of bones and their transformation back into a living being, the verse underscores that Allah’s power to give life is absolute and beyond human comprehension. This serves as a sign to strengthen faith in His dominion over all existence.
orig: أو كالذي مر على قرية وهي خاوية على عروشها قال أنى يحيي هذه الله بعد موتها فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم قال بل لبثت مائة عام فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنه وانظر إلى حمارك ولنجعلك آية للناس وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها ثم نكسوها لحما فلما تبين له قال أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' [Allah] said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied.' [Allah] said, 'Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a conversation between Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim) and Allah. Abraham asks to see the process of resurrection to strengthen his faith. Allah instructs him to kill and scatter the parts of four birds on different hills and then call them back to life. This miraculous event serves to demonstrate God's power over life and death, thereby fortifying Abraham's belief and showing that Allah's decrees are always executed with wisdom and might. The lesson is that asking questions to strengthen one's faith is acceptable, and through evidence and reflection, one's conviction and understanding can grow deeper.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أولم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبي قال فخذ أربعة من الطير فصرهن إليك ثم اجعل على كل جبل منهن جزءا ثم ادعهن يأتينك سعيا واعلم أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed (of grain) that sprouts seven ears; in every ear is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse draws an analogy to illustrate the immense and multiplied reward for those who spend their wealth for the sake of Allah. Just as a single seed can produce numerous grains, the spending in the path of Allah can yield exponential rewards, reflecting the infinite grace and knowledge of Allah. It underscores the concept of divine generosity and the limitless potential of sincere charitable acts.
orig: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة أنبتت سبع سنابل في كل سنبلة مائة حبة والله يضاعف لمن يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and do not follow up their spending with reminders of their generosity or with injury will have their reward with their Lord. They will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of genuine charity in Islam. It encourages believers to spend their wealth for the sake of Allah without seeking recognition or causing harm to the recipients. The promise of a reward from Allah, accompanied by freedom from fear and grief, serves as a powerful incentive, highlighting that sincere charitable acts bring immense spiritual benefits and divine contentment.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله ثم لا يتبعون ما أنفقوا منا ولا أذى لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: A kind word with forgiveness is better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the manner in which charitable acts are performed. It stresses that the value of a kind word and forgiving attitude far surpasses that of a material donation if the latter is followed by hurtful behavior. The verse highlights the significance of intention and conduct in acts of charity and reminds believers that Allah is self-sufficient and patient, implying that charity should be given genuinely and without expectation of recognition or reciprocation.
orig: قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى والله غني حليم

translation: O you who believe, do not render in vain your charities by reminders of your generosity or by injury, like him who spends his wealth to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a rock covered with dust; then a downpour strikes it, leaving it bare. They are unable to keep anything they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse warns believers about the nullification of their charitable acts through boasting or causing harm to the recipients. It highlights the importance of sincere intentions behind charity, likening insincere charity to a superficial layer of dust on a rock, easily washed away by rain, leaving nothing behind. Believers are reminded that acts performed for show and without real faith are fruitless as Allah does not guide those who are insincere in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب فأصابه وابل فتركه صلدا لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and to strengthen their souls is like a garden on high ground which is hit by a heavy rain, so it yields its produce in double. And even if it is not hit by a heavy rain, a drizzle is sufficient. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a garden on elevated ground to describe the rewards for those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah with sincere intention and faith. Just as a well-situated garden produces a rich harvest when it receives sufficient rain, the actions of these believers yield abundant rewards from Allah. Even minimal effort, likened to a light drizzle, is recognized and rewarded by Allah, emphasizing His awareness and appreciation of all good deeds, regardless of their scale. This encourages the faithful to remain sincere and steadfast in their efforts, trusting in Allah's perfect knowledge and judgment.
orig: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم كمثل جنة بربوة أصابها وابل فآتت أكلها ضعفين فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden with date palms and grapevines, with rivers flowing underneath, and all kinds of fruits for him therein—while he has grown old and has weak offspring—then it is hit by a fiery whirlwind and is burnt down? Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, so that you may reflect.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a beautiful, fruitful garden destroyed by a sudden calamity to illustrate the transient nature of worldly possessions and the importance of safeguarding one’s deeds. The imagery of the garden highlights the blessings and bounties that one may have in this life, but it also underscores their vulnerability and impermanence, especially without the protection of faith and righteous actions. The verse encourages believers to reflect upon the reality of their existence, to focus on lasting spiritual and ethical investments rather than ephemeral material wealth, and to recognize Allah’s signs in the world around them as reminders of deeper truths.
orig: أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب تجري من تحتها الأنهار له فيها من كل الثمرات وأصابه الكبر وله ذرية ضعفاء فأصابها إعصار فيه نار فاحترقت كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the defective therefrom, spending [from that] while you would not take it [yourself] except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to spend in charity from the best of their lawful earnings and the produce of the earth. It emphasizes that they should not offer in charity what they themselves would not accept without hesitation. The underlying message is that offering substandard items as charity shows a lack of respect and gratitude towards the blessings given by Allah. The verse concludes by reminding that Allah is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, encouraging sincerity and quality in acts of giving.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه واعلموا أن الله غني حميد

translation: Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the different paths offered by Satan and Allah. Satan exploits the fear of poverty to lead humans towards immoral actions, making them believe that unethical behavior is necessary for survival or prosperity. In contrast, Allah provides reassurance of His forgiveness and generous blessings, emphasizing His vast knowledge and capacity to sustain and forgive. This verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's promises and resist the deceptive whispers of Satan.
orig: الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا والله واسع عليم

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever has been granted wisdom has certainly been given much good. And none will remember except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that wisdom is a divine gift bestowed by Allah upon those He chooses. It underscores the immense value of wisdom, equating it with great good, and suggests that true comprehension and mindfulness of this gift are possessed only by those who have profound insight and intellectual discernment.
orig: يؤتي الحكمة من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: And whatever you spend in charity or whatever vow you make, surely Allah knows it. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all actions, whether one gives in charity or makes a vow. It serves as a reminder that God is omniscient and vigilant over human deeds. Additionally, it warns that those who commit injustice and wrongdoing will ultimately have no allies or supporters to aid them against divine retribution. The underlying message is to act with righteousness and sincerity, recognizing that all actions are observed by Allah and will be accounted for.
orig: وما أنفقتم من نفقة أو نذرتم من نذر فإن الله يعلمه وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds [thereby]. And Allah is [fully] aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of giving charity, both openly and secretly. When charity is given openly, it can serve as a good example to others, encouraging them to act similarly. However, giving in secret, especially to the poor, is considered better because it ensures sincerity, avoids public praise, and preserves the dignity of the recipients. Additionally, secret charity helps in purifying the giver's intentions and contributes to the expiation of their sins. Ultimately, Allah is aware of all actions, and His knowledge ensures that the intention behind the act of charity is understood and rewarded accordingly.
orig: إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: It is not upon you [O Muhammad] to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you [believers] spend is for yourselves, for you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever you spend of good - it will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance is in the hands of Allah alone, and it is He who decides whom to guide. The responsibility of believers is to spend in the way of Allah with the sincere intention of seeking His pleasure. The verse reassures that any good spending will be rewarded fully by Allah, ensuring that the believers do not suffer any injustice or loss in their efforts. Thus, it encourages a selfless approach to charity and good deeds, underscoring the importance of pure intentions and trust in divine recompense.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: For the poor who have been restricted for the cause of Allah, unable to move about in the land. An ignorant person thinks them to be free from need because of their restraint, but you will know them by their [characteristic] sign. They do not ask people persistently, and whatever you spend of good – indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the condition of the poor who are engaged in the cause of Allah, who cannot seek sustenance by traveling in the land. It emphasizes their dignity and restraint, making them appear self-sufficient to those unaware of their true condition. The verse urges believers to recognize their subtle indications of need and encourages charity, reminding that Allah is fully aware of every act of goodness.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the night and the day, secretly and openly, they will have their reward with their Lord. There will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of charity and generosity, highlighting that those who give their wealth in various circumstances—whether publicly or privately, by day or by night—are promised a reward from Allah. Such individuals are assured of protection from fear and grief, indicating divine approval and spiritual tranquility. The verse encourages believers to be consistent and sincere in their charitable acts, knowing that Allah recognizes and rewards all types of sincere contributions.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, 'Trade is [just] like interest.' But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns [to dealing in interest or usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of engaging in interest-based transactions, highlighting the spiritual and moral decay it causes. The metaphor of being beaten into insanity by Satan illustrates the detrimental effect of usury on a person's soul and social fabric.
