It emphasizes that thoughtful and discerning individuals, those endowed with intellect and insight, can perceive the existence and attributes of God through the wonders and patterns of the universe. The creation of the heavens and the earth, along with the regular succession of night and day, serve as accessible and powerful indicators of divine wisdom and omnipotence, encouraging reflection, gratitude, and spiritual awareness.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], 'Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of constant mindfulness and remembrance of Allah in all positions—whether standing, sitting, or lying down. It highlights the importance of contemplation of the natural world as a means to understand and appreciate the purposeful creation by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing in creation is without purpose and encourages believers to seek protection from the consequences of disbelief and heedlessness, specifically the punishment of the Fire. It underscores the importance of submitting to Allah’s greatness and seeking His mercy.
orig: الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السماوات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate disgrace and dishonor that comes with being placed in Hellfire, emphasizing that it is a result of one's own wrongdoing. It also underscores the absence of any aid or support for those who commit injustice, reflecting the complete and final nature of divine justice and punishment for the wrongdoers. The verse serves as a stern warning to avoid evil deeds and seek righteousness to achieve divine grace and protection.
orig: ربنا إنك من تدخل النار فقد أخزيته وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea to Allah from the believers who have responded to the call of faith. They acknowledge having heard the message to believe in Allah and have faithfully accepted it. Consequently, they seek Allah's forgiveness for their sins, ask for the removal of their wrongdoings, and wish to be gathered among the righteous at the time of death. It signifies a sincere commitment to faith and an appeal for divine mercy and guidance in life and the hereafter.
orig: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان أن آمنوا بربكم فآمنا ربنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وكفر عنا سيئاتنا وتوفنا مع الأبرار

translation: Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from the believers to Allah, asking Him to fulfill the promises made through His messengers. It reflects their trust in Allah's promise and their hope for His mercy and protection from disgrace on the Day of Judgment. The plea underscores their belief in the certainty of Allah's promises and His justice.
orig: ربنا وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة إنك لا تخلف الميعاد

translation: And their Lord responded to them, 'Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were expelled from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed - I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as a reward from Allah. And Allah has with Him the best reward.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s promise of justice and the reward for those who strive in His cause. It assures that the efforts and sacrifices made by every believer, regardless of gender, are acknowledged and valued equally. This includes those who have endured hardships, such as migration, expulsion, persecution, and even martyrdom in the path of Allah. Allah promises to expiate their sins and grant them entrance into Paradise, highlighting His ultimate grace and the supreme nature of the divine reward.
orig: فاستجاب لهم ربهم أني لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم من ذكر أو أنثى بعضكم من بعض فالذين هاجروا وأخرجوا من ديارهم وأوذوا في سبيلي وقاتلوا وقتلوا لأكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلنهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ثوابا من عند الله والله عنده حسن الثواب

translation: Do not be deceived by the [uninhibited] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land.
interpretation: This verse advises believers not to be misled or overly impressed by the apparent freedom and prosperity enjoyed by those who reject faith. It emphasizes that such worldly success is temporary and should not cause believers to envy or question their own path of faith and righteousness. Ultimate justice and reward are determined by one's adherence to divine guidance rather than earthly metrics of success.
orig: لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد

translation: Brief enjoyment, then their ultimate abode is Hell, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and comforts, juxtaposed against the eternal consequences of one's actions in the hereafter. It serves as a warning that indulgence in fleeting material benefits at the cost of one's spiritual and moral duties leads to dire outcomes in the form of eternal suffering in Hell. The phrase 'evil is the resting place' underscores the severity and negativity of this fate, urging believers to prioritize their long-term spiritual well-being over short-term worldly gains.
orig: متاع قليل ثم مأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting those who are conscious of their duty to God and strive to live a righteous life. It highlights the eternal nature of paradise, promising unending bliss and comfort. It serves as a reminder that the rewards from God surpass any worldly gains, affirming the ultimate value in piety and obedience.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نزلا من عند الله وما عند الله خير للأبرار

translation: Among the People of the Book are those who truly believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them. They humble themselves before Allah and do not sell Allah's revelations for a small price. They will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges that among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) are some who have true faith in Allah, recognizing both the revelations given to Muslims and to their own communities. These individuals are sincere in their devotion, humble towards God, and do not exploit divine revelations for worldly gain. The verse assures these sincere believers of their reward from God and reminds that Allah's judgment is swift and just.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to exhibit patience and perseverance in their faith and actions, continually engage in steadfastness, and maintain their commitment (possibly in their duties or in a metaphorical sense of posting in defense of their community). It underscores the importance of having a constant awareness and fear of Allah as a means to achieve ultimate success. It emphasizes the need for sustained effort, resilience, and vigilance in one's spiritual and communal life, suggesting that such qualities are essential for attaining true prosperity and divine favor.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Verily, Allah is ever an Observer over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of God-consciousness and the recognition of the common origin of humanity. Every individual has been created from a single soul, highlighting unity and equality among people. The verse stresses the sanctity of human relationships and urges respect and mindfulness towards kinship and social interactions. Ultimately, it reminds individuals that Allah is always watching over them, and thus, they should act with righteousness and integrity.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا

translation: And give the orphans their wealth and do not substitute the defective [of your own] for the good [of theirs]. And do not consume their wealth into your own. Indeed, that is ever a great sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and integrity in dealing with orphans. It instructs believers to return the wealth and property that rightfully belong to orphaned children and warns against exploiting or misappropriating their assets. By prohibiting the mixing and consumption of the orphans' wealth with one's own, the verse underscores the gravity of the sin associated with such acts. The directive upholds the principles of fairness and protection for the vulnerable, highlighting the moral responsibility of society to safeguard the rights and interests of orphans.
orig: وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم إنه كان حوبا كبيرا

translation: If you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hands possess. That is more suitable that you may not incline [to injustice].
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of justice and fairness in dealing with orphans and wives. It allows Muslim men to marry up to four women if they fear they cannot be just to orphans, which might imply looking after their welfare along with managing a family. However, it underscores the importance of fairness by stipulating that if a man fears he cannot treat multiple wives equitably, he should marry only one or consider those whom his right hand possesses. The verse highlights the principle of justice and the importance of equitable treatment in marital relationships, aiming to ensure that societal and familial structures do not lead to injustice or neglect.
orig: وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع فإن خفتم ألا تعدلوا فواحدة أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ذلك أدنى ألا تعولوا

translation: And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously. But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving women the dowry (bridal gift) as a rightful obligation without reluctance or hesitation. It also acknowledges that if the woman, out of her own free will, chooses to return any part of it, the recipient can accept it without guilt or resentment. This highlights the themes of fairness, respect, and voluntary generosity in marital relations.
orig: وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا فكلوه هنيئا مريئا

translation: And do not give the weak-minded your property, which Allah has made a means of sustenance for you. But provide for them with it and clothe them and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse advises against entrusting financial responsibilities to those who are not capable of managing wealth wisely, as this could jeopardize the communal resources meant to sustain the community. Instead, it emphasizes the importance of providing for their needs, such as food and clothing, while treating them with respect and kindness. The emphasis is on ensuring the equitable distribution and responsible management of resources to maintain societal stability and welfare.
orig: ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم التي جعل الله لكم قياما وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgment, deliver to them their property. And do not consume it excessively and quickly, fearing that they will grow up. And whoever, [i.e., guardian] is rich should refrain [from taking a fee], and whoever is poor, let him take according to what is acceptable. Then when you deliver to them their property, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the treatment of orphans' property. Guardians are instructed to assess the maturity and judgment of orphans before transferring their assets to them. The verse advises against the misuse or hastening in consumption of the orphans' property. It also instructs financially well-off guardians to abstain from taking fees, whereas those in need can only take what is fair and reasonable. Finally, it emphasizes the importance of transparency and accountability, recommending the presence of witnesses during the transfer of property, reminding that Allah is the ultimate judge and accountant.
orig: وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much—a determined share.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of inheritance rights for both men and women. It underscores the importance of fair distribution of assets left by deceased parents or close kin, ensuring that both male and female heirs receive a defined portion, regardless of the amount. This signifies the Qur'an's emphasis on justice and equality in matters of inheritance.
orig: للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون وللنساء نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون مما قل منه أو كثر نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And when the relatives and the orphans and the needy are present at the time of division, then provide for them from it and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of generosity and kindness towards relatives, orphans, and the needy, especially during the division of inheritance. It encourages providing for these groups from one's wealth and advises addressing them with respectful and kind words. This reflects the broader Islamic values of compassion, family ties, and social responsibility.
orig: وإذا حضر القسمة أولو القربى واليتامى والمساكين فارزقوهم منه وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And let those [executors and guardians] fear [injustice] as if they [themselves] had left weak offspring behind and feared for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of empathy and justice, especially when acting on behalf of others. Executors and guardians should consider the vulnerability of children or those dependent on them and act with the same care and integrity as they would for their own children. It calls for mindfulness of Allah and encourages speaking and acting with fairness and righteousness, promoting a society where the rights of the weak and vulnerable are protected.
orig: وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم فليتقوا الله وليقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire. And they will be burned in a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse sternly warns against the exploitation and unjust consumption of orphaned children's wealth. It emphasizes that such an act is not merely a worldly injustice but is equivalent to feeding oneself with fire, leading to severe punishment in the Hereafter. This serves as a broader ethical directive to protect and uphold the rights of orphans and vulnerable individuals, highlighting the grave consequences of exploitation and injustice.
orig: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are (only) daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one’s estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one’s parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents (alone) inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers (or sisters), for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he (may have) made or debt. Your parents or your children—you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. These shares are an obligation from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse lays down specific inheritance rules, ensuring a fair distribution of wealth among family members. It emphasizes the importance of familial bonds and responsibilities, with a detailed breakdown of shares for children (both male and female), parents, and siblings. The underlying principle is equity and justice, ensuring both genders and various familial relations are considered. These rules are portrayed as divine mandates, highlighting the knowledge and wisdom of Allah in legislating such affairs. The instructions also balance emotional attachments by stressing that humans cannot discern who among their relatives will be most beneficial to them, but Allah's command ensures justice for all parties involved.
orig: يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك وإن كانت واحدة فلها النصف ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس مما ترك إن كان له ولد فإن لم يكن له ولد وورثه أبواه فلأمه الثلث فإن كان له إخوة فلأمه السدس من بعد وصية يوصي بها أو دين آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا فريضة من الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: You shall inherit half of what your wives leave if they have no children, but if they have children, then you shall inherit a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they have made or debt. They shall inherit a quarter of what you leave if you have no children, but if you have children, then they shall inherit an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you have made or debt. If a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or sister, each one of them shall inherit one-sixth. If they are more than that, they shall share in a third, after any bequest or debt, provided that the bequest does not harm anyone. This is a commandment from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules of inheritance for Muslims, ensuring that wealth is distributed fairly among family members. The guidelines specify different shares for spouses, children, and siblings in the absence of direct descendants or ascendants. It underscores the importance of fulfilling any bequests or debts before distributing the inheritance and prohibits any actions that could harm others through unjust bequests. Overall, the verse emphasizes justice and compassion in financial matters, reflecting Allah’s wisdom and patience.
orig: ولكم نصف ما ترك أزواجكم إن لم يكن لهن ولد فإن كان لهن ولد فلكم الربع مما تركن من بعد وصية يوصين بها أو دين ولهن الربع مما تركتم إن لم يكن لكم ولد فإن كان لكم ولد فلهن الثمن مما تركتم من بعد وصية توصون بها أو دين وإن كان رجل يورث كلالة أو امرأة وله أخ أو أخت فلكل واحد منهما السدس فإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فهم شركاء في الثلث من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين غير مضار وصية من الله والله عليم حليم

translation: These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally; and that is the great achievement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine limits and laws established by Allah. It underscores the significance of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger (Prophet Muhammad). The reward for such obedience is the promise of eternal bliss in the form of paradisiacal gardens with flowing rivers, symbolizing everlasting peace and fulfillment. This eternal residence in paradise is described as the ultimate success and achievement for the believers.
orig: تلك حدود الله ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: But whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits - He will put him into the Fire to abide eternally therein, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disobedience to Allah and His Messenger, and of transgressing the divine boundaries set by them. It indicates that those who act defiantly against God's commands and the teachings of the Prophet will face eternal damnation in Hellfire and suffer a humiliating punishment. The intent is to underscore the gravity of such actions and to serve as a stern warning to uphold the limits set by divine law.
orig: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها وله عذاب مهين

translation: As for those of your women who commit immoral conduct, call four witnesses from among you to testify against them. If they testify, confine the guilty women to their houses until they die or until Allah ordains for them another way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the punishment for women who commit acts of indecency, prescribing a method which involves bringing forth four witnesses to testify against the accused. If the testimony is confirmed, the women are to be confined to their homes for the rest of their lives or until Allah provides another directive. This reflects the seriousness of maintaining moral conduct within the community, as well as the process which needs strong evidence, emphasizing both justice and mercy as the cornerstone of Islamic legal and ethical system.
orig: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم فإن شهدوا فأمسكوهن في البيوت حتى يتوفاهن الموت أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا

translation: And the two among you who commit it, punish them. But if they repent and correct themselves, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the treatment of those who commit immoral acts. Initially, it instructs believers to administer a form of reprimand or punishment to those who engage in such actions. However, the verse also emphasizes the importance of repentance and reform. If the individuals demonstrate genuine remorse and make efforts to correct their behavior, they should be forgiven and left unmolested, highlighting the compassionate nature of Allah, who is always willing to accept repentance and show mercy to those who sincerely seek it.
orig: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما إن الله كان توابا رحيما

translation: Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance [or carelessness] and then repent soon after; it is they to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's acceptance of repentance is specifically extended to those who commit sins out of ignorance or unmindfulness and then quickly turn back to Him in repentance. It assures believers that sincere and timely repentance will be accepted by Allah, who is both fully aware of their circumstances and infinitely wise in His judgment. This demonstrates Allah’s mercy and compassion, highlighting that genuine efforts to seek forgiveness are valued and rewarded.
orig: إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: But repentance is not [accepted] of those who [continue to] do evil deeds up until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now,' or of those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sincere repentance must occur before death is imminent and cannot be opportunistically delayed until one faces the final moments of life. It also highlights that repentance is not accepted from those who die in a state of disbelief. The verse underscores the importance of genuine and timely repentance, warning that procrastination and insincere declarations of repentance at the moment of death will not be accepted, and such individuals will face a severe punishment.
orig: وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take back part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes respect and fairness in marital relationships. It prohibits coercive inheritance of women, a practice prevalent before Islam, to ensure women's rights. It also discourages making life difficult for wives to reclaim dowries unless they commit blatant wrongdoing. The verse advises living with spouses kindly, acknowledging that personal dislikes might overlook hidden goodness endowed by Allah, urging a broader perspective on marital relations.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وعاشروهن بالمعروف فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

translation: And if you want to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a large amount [in gifts], do not take back from it anything. Would you take it in injustice and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse addresses the ethical and moral responsibilities of men in the context of marriage and divorce. It emphasizes that if a man chooses to replace his wife with another, even if he has given her a significant amount of wealth, he must not take any of it back. Doing so would be considered an act of grave injustice and a clear sin. The verse thus underscores the importance of fair treatment and integrity in marital relationships, advocating for the protection and respect of a woman's rights in the event of a marital dissolution.
orig: وإن أردتم استبدال زوج مكان زوج وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse addresses the injustice of reclaiming a bridal gift after consummation of marriage, emphasizing the gravity and sanctity of marital commitments. It underscores the deep bond created through marriage and the vows made, highlighting the seriousness of the covenant taken before God and society.
orig: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And do not marry those [women] whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and hateful [to Allah] and was an evil way.
interpretation: This verse prohibits marrying women who were previously married to one's father, a practice that was allowed in pre-Islamic times. The verse highlights that such actions are considered extremely immoral, detestable, and a wrongful path. This injunction is meant to uphold family sanctity and moral integrity within the community. The prohibition also emphasizes the importance of respecting familial boundaries and preserving the dignity of relationships.
orig: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

translation: Prohibited to you [for marriage] are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your father's sisters, your mother's sisters, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your [milk] mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives' mothers, and your step-daughters under your guardianship [born] of your wives unto whom you have gone in. But if you have not gone in unto them, there is no sin upon you. And [also prohibited are] the wives of your sons who are from your own loins, and that you take [in marriage] two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the clear prohibitions regarding who a Muslim is forbidden to marry, emphasizing the sanctity and respect required in familial relationships. It lists the categories of women with whom marriage would violate social and moral boundaries, acknowledging the importance of maintaining proper family ethics. Additionally, it makes a concession regarding prohibitions that might have been inadvertently violated in the past, underscoring Allah's attribute of being forgiving and merciful. The verse seeks to ensure that familial lines are respected and protected, fostering a sense of order and ethical conduct in personal relationships.
orig: حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن فلا جناح عليكم وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And [forbidden to you are] married women except those your right hands possess. [This is] the decree of Allah upon you. And lawful to you are [all others] beyond these, [provided] that you seek them [in marriage] with [gifts from] your property, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse. So for whatever you enjoy [of marriage] from them, give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree to beyond the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the boundaries of lawful and forbidden relationships, particularly in the context of marriage. It specifically addresses the prohibition against marrying women who are already married, with the exception of captives. It emphasizes that seeking chaste and lawful marital relationships is permitted and that financial compensation to wives is a required duty. It further highlights that mutual agreements beyond this financial obligation are also permissible, underlining the importance of consent and mutual respect in marital relations. The verse concludes by reminding that Allah is all-knowing and wise, framing these injunctions within divine wisdom and knowledge.
orig: والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم أن تبتغوا بأموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة ولا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به من بعد الفريضة إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry the free believing women, then marry those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave girls. And Allah is most knowing about your faith. You [believers] are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their families and give them their due compensation according to what is acceptable. They should be chaste, not those who commit unlawful sexual intercourse or take [secret] lovers. But once they are married, if they commit adultery, they receive half the punishment of free women. This [concession] is for those among you who fear sin. But to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of marriage for those who cannot afford to marry free believing women, allowing them instead to marry believing slave girls under certain conditions. It emphasizes the importance of faith and piety, the necessity of permission from their families, and fair compensation. Additionally, it highlights that such women should be chaste, not engaging in unlawful sexual relationships. The verse also provides a more lenient punishment for slave women who commit adultery in comparison to free women. Ultimately, it advises patience as a better course of action and reminds that Allah is forgiving and merciful, emphasizing His compassionate and understanding nature toward human frailties and socio-economic disparities.
orig: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات المؤمنات فمن ما ملكت أيمانكم من فتياتكم المؤمنات والله أعلم بإيمانكم بعضكم من بعض فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن وآتوهن أجورهن بالمعروف محصنات غير مسافحات ولا متخذات أخدان فإذا أحصن فإن أتين بفاحشة فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ذلك لمن خشي العنت منكم وأن تصبروا خير لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah wants to clarify things for you and guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in mercy. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's intent to make His guidance clear to humanity, reflecting on past examples to show the correct path. It highlights Allah's mercy as He repeatedly offers opportunities for repentance and correction. By describing Himself as Knowing and Wise, Allah assures believers of His perfect understanding and judgment in all matters, further reinforcing trust in His guidance and commands.
orig: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And Allah wants to accept your repentance, but those who follow [their] desires want you to deviate [into] a great deviation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting intentions between Allah and those who are driven by their desires. Allah’s will is centered on forgiveness and guiding believers towards repentance, whereas those who follow their base desires seek to lead others astray significantly. It emphasizes the merciful nature of Allah and the destructive influence of succumbing to sinful temptations.
orig: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

translation: God wants to lighten your burdens, for man was created weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's compassion and understanding of human limitations. It reassures that the divine instructions and laws are meant to be a source of ease and not hardship, acknowledging the inherent frailties and susceptibilities of human beings. It serves as a reminder of the innate human need for divine guidance and mercy.
orig: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it (in bribery) to the rulers in order that you might sinfully consume a portion of the wealth of people, while you know (it is unlawful). And do not kill yourselves (or one another). Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, urging them to refrain from unethical practices such as consuming wealth wrongfully or engaging in corrupt activities like bribery to unjustly gain others' possessions. It emphasizes fairness in dealings, specifically highlighting that economic transactions should be based on mutual consent and justice. Moreover, it extends the prohibition to taking life unlawfully, underscoring the sanctity of life and the mercy of Allah towards the believers. The guidance serves to nurture a just and morally upright society.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم إن الله كان بكم رحيما

translation: But whoever does that in aggression and injustice, then We will drive him into a Fire. And that, for Allah, is always easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of acting with aggression and injustice. It reinforces the idea that such actions are deeply detested by Allah and that His punishment for these actions is inevitable and definitive. The phrase 'We will drive him into a Fire' underscores the seriousness of such sins and the inevitable divine retribution. Additionally, it highlights that enacting justice and punishment is effortless for Allah, reminding believers of His supreme power and authority in upholding righteousness.
orig: ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden from, We will remove from you your minor sins and admit you to a noble entrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding major sins in the eyes of God. It promises believers that if they steer clear of these serious transgressions, God will forgive their minor sins and grant them an honorable place in the afterlife. The 'noble entrance' refers to a dignified and respected admission to paradise, highlighting God's mercy and the reward for maintaining piety and obedience.
orig: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما

translation: And do not desire what Allah has given some of you over others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse advises believers not to covet or be jealous of the blessings and advantages that others have received from Allah. It emphasizes that both men and women will receive rewards proportional to their own efforts and achievements. Instead of envying others, the believers are encouraged to seek Allah's grace and bounty for themselves through prayer and righteous actions. This notion underscores Allah's comprehensive knowledge and wisdom in distributing His blessings and serves as a reminder of the importance of contentment and trust in His divine justice.
orig: ولا تتمنوا ما فضل الله به بعضكم على بعض للرجال نصيب مما اكتسبوا وللنساء نصيب مما اكتسبن واسألوا الله من فضله إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And for everyone We have made heirs to what is left by parents and relatives. To those also with whom your oaths have bound you, give them their portion. Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of observing the rights of inheritance and fulfilling agreements made with others. It indicates that God has designated specific heirs for the property left behind by one's parents and relatives, ensuring that their rights are respected. Additionally, it underscores the necessity to honor any pledges or agreements made, reflecting the ethical principle of fulfilling covenants. By stating that Allah witnesses all actions, it serves as a reminder of divine accountability and the importance of justice and honesty in dealing with the distribution of wealth and fulfilling promises.
orig: ولكل جعلنا موالي مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون والذين عقدت أيمانكم فآتوهم نصيبهم إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has given one more (strength) than the other, and because they support them from their means. Therefore, the righteous women are devoutly obedient and guard in the husband’s absence what Allah would have them guard. As to those women on whose part you fear disobedience, admonish them (first), (next) refuse to share their beds, (and last) beat them (lightly); but if they return to obedience, seek not against them means (of annoyance): for Allah is Most High, Great (above you all).
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the responsibilities and duties within the marital relationship. Men are emphasized as protectors and maintainers, which includes providing financial support. In return, women are encouraged to be obedient and faithful, particularly in the husband's absence. The verse provides a structured approach for resolving marital discord, starting from verbal admonishment, escalating to temporary separation in bed, and, as a last resort, physical discipline. However, it stresses that if a wife returns to obedience, the husband should not seek further means of annoyance, highlighting the importance of reconciliation and maintaining harmony in the marriage. It underscores the values of responsibility, protection, and the resolution of conflicts within the parameters of respect and love in a marriage.
orig: الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause harmony between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse instructs believers on the process of conflict resolution between husband and wife. When marital disputes arise and there is a fear of an irreconcilable rift, it advises involving impartial arbitrators from both sides - one from the man's family and one from the woman's family. The role of these arbitrators is to mediate and work towards reconciliation. The verse emphasizes that if both parties sincerely wish for harmony, Allah will facilitate their reconciliation, as He is all-knowing and fully aware of the complexities involved in human relationships.
orig: وإن خفتم شقاق بينهما فابعثوا حكما من أهله وحكما من أهلها إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما إن الله كان عليما خبيرا

translation: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be kind to parents. And to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is near, the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Verily, Allah does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and outlines the fundamental aspects of ethical behavior in Islam. It emphasizes worshiping Allah alone without associating any partners with Him and extends this ethical monotheism to social conduct as well. The verse enumerates specific groups of people to whom kindness and good treatment should be extended: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbors (both near and distant), companions, travelers, and servants or those under one's care. The closing part warns against arrogance and pride, traits that are detested by Allah. Thus, the verse calls for humility, compassion, and a sense of community responsibility in addition to the spiritual commitment to monotheism.
orig: واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا وبذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب والصاحب بالجنب وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty - and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of those who are miserly and who encourage others to also be stingy. It condemns the act of hiding the blessings and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon them, which could benefit others. Such actions are seen as a rejection of Allah's generosity and a failure in their moral and social responsibilities. For those who act in this manner, Allah warns of a degrading and severe punishment, specifically targeting those who deny or disbelieve in His guidance.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by the people and do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day. And whoever has Satan as a companion - then what a terrible companion he is!
interpretation: This verse criticizes the insincerity of those who spend their wealth for the sake of showing off to others rather than genuinely seeking the pleasure of Allah. It underscores the lack of true faith in both Allah and the Day of Judgment amongst such people. The verse also highlights the detrimental effect of associating with Satan, illustrating that such companionship leads to negative consequences and misguided actions.
orig: والذين ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس ولا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا

translation: And what burden would it be on them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent out of what Allah has provided for them? And Allah is ever, about them, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the simplicity and non-burdensome nature of belief in Allah, the Last Day, and charity. It reassures that Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions, encouraging faith and generosity by highlighting that these acts are inherently beneficial and not difficult or overbearing. The rhetorical question suggests that such belief and spending of their provision in charity would not harm them, but rather bring them closer to divine approval and mercy.
orig: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر وأنفقوا مما رزقهم الله وكان الله بهم عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom’s weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah. It reassures that no matter how minuscule an action may be, it is accounted for justly by Him. Specifically, any good deed, no matter the size, is vastly rewarded, underscoring Allah’s generosity and mercy. The verse highlights both the precision of divine justice and the boundlessness of divine grace.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما

translation: How will it be then when We bring from every people a witness and bring you as a witness over these people?
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity and seriousness of the Day of Judgment. It underscores the concept of accountability and the role of witnesses. Every nation will have a witness, and the Prophet Muhammad will be a witness over his people. This serves as a reminder of the Prophet's significant position and the responsibility of delivering the message, emphasizing the thorough nature of divine justice.
orig: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا

translation: On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them. And they will not [be able to] conceal from Allah a [single] fact.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and despair of those who rejected faith and disobeyed the Messenger on the Day of Judgment. They will wish to be completely obliterated to avoid facing the consequences of their actions. It underscores the ultimate accountability before Allah, where nothing can be hidden and everything will be exposed.
orig: يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ولا يكتمون الله حديثا

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of janabah (impurity), except when traveling on the road, until you have bathed. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands with it. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers on maintaining the sanctity and mindfulness required during prayer. It emphasizes the importance of being in a clear state of mind and physical purity when performing prayers. The provision for tayammum (dry ablution) signifies Allah's consideration for the difficulties believers might encounter, showcasing Divine compassion and forgiveness. This highlights both the rigor of personal preparation for worship and the flexibility within Islamic practice to accommodate various circumstances without neglecting spiritual duties.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم إن الله كان عفوا غفورا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, purchasing error and wishing you would lose the way?
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have received part of the divine revelation, implying they knowingly choose misguidance over guidance. The verse criticizes them for deliberately adopting falsehood and attempting to lead others astray from the correct path. This can be interpreted as a warning against the manipulation and misuse of spiritual knowledge for misleading purposes, urging believers to remain vigilant and steadfast in the true path.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies; and sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that Allah has full knowledge of who their enemies are, even if they themselves do not. It highlights the sufficiency of Allah's support, suggesting that no greater ally or helper exists beyond Him. Believers are encouraged to rely on Allah's wisdom and protection in the face of adversities.
orig: والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا

translation: Among those who are Jews, there are some who distort the words from their proper usages and say, 'We hear and disobey' and 'Hear but be not heard' and 'Rāʿinā,' twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said, 'We hear and obey' and 'Wait for us to understand,' it would have been better for them and more suitable. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of some individuals among the Jews who practiced distortion of their scriptures and showed disrespect towards divine instructions. By altering words and mocking the messages, they exhibited an attitude of disobedience and defamation towards their religion. The verse suggests that had they chosen to listen and obey sincerely, their situation would have been better. However, due to their persistent disbelief and inappropriate behavior, they are described as being cursed by Allah, which results in only a few of them truly believing. This implies a call to integrity and sincerity in following divine guidance.
orig: من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ويقولون سمعنا وعصينا واسمع غير مسمع وراعنا ليا بألسنتهم وطعنا في الدين ولو أنهم قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا واسمع وانظرنا لكان خيرا لهم وأقوم ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down [to Muhammad] confirming that which is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them toward their backs or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers. And ever is the decree of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to believe in the Qur'an and the prophetic message of Muhammad, which confirms the previous scriptures they have. It warns of severe consequences, such as losing their dignity or being cursed, similar to how the Sabbath-breakers were cursed, if they persist in their disbelief. This verse emphasizes the seriousness of ignoring the divine message and the decisive nature of Allah's decree.
orig: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا مصدقا لما معكم من قبل أن نطمس وجوها فنردها على أدبارها أو نلعنهم كما لعنا أصحاب السبت وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of associating others with Allah (shirk), which is considered an unforgivable sin if maintained until death. It emphasizes Allah’s mercy in forgiving all other sins for whom He wills, but it also serves as a dire warning that polytheism or idolatry is a fundamental violation of the principles of monotheism and thus a grave transgression. The verse calls believers to uphold the purity of worship solely for Allah.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد افترى إثما عظيما

translation: Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged [even by] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance of people who boast about their own righteousness and purity. It serves as a reminder that true purification and righteousness come from Allah alone, and not through self-praise. Only Allah has the authority to bestow purity upon individuals, and He does so according to His wisdom and will. Furthermore, it emphasizes Allah's justice, assuring that everyone will be treated with absolute fairness, even to the minutest detail.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: See how they invent lies about Allah, and that is enough as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of fabricating falsehoods against Allah, emphasizing that such deceit is a clear and severe sin. It serves as a stern warning about the moral and spiritual consequences of attributing lies to the Divine, underscoring the importance of truthfulness and integrity in faith.
orig: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in superstition and false objects of worship and say to the disbelievers that they are better guided than the believers regarding the way.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who were given knowledge of previous scriptures but have abandoned true faith to follow falsehood and idolatry. It highlights their misguided judgment in considering disbelievers to be better guided than believers. This serves as a warning against deviating from the true path and the consequences of forsaking divine guidance for unfounded beliefs.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يؤمنون بالجبت والطاغوت ويقولون للذين كفروا هؤلاء أهدى من الذين آمنوا سبيلا

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whomever Allah curses - you will not find for him a helper.
interpretation: This verse signifies the immense severity of Allah's curse upon certain individuals. When Allah curses a person, it indicates a complete withdrawal of His mercy and guidance. The verse emphasizes that once someone is forsaken by Allah, no earthly or heavenly force can provide support or assistance to them. It underscores the importance of seeking Allah's favor and mercy, as His wrath results in total abandonment and helplessness.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله ومن يلعن الله فلن تجد له نصيرا

translation: Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then [if that were so], they would not give the people [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the selfishness and greed of those who, if they possessed any share of power or dominion, would be so stingy that they wouldn't give people even the tiniest bit. It is a reminder of the importance of generosity and equitable distribution of resources, as opposed to withholding and hoarding wealth or power.
orig: أم لهم نصيب من الملك فإذا لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who harbor envy towards others for the favors and blessings they have received from Allah. It reminds them that divine favor is not a new phenomenon; Allah has historically bestowed His bounties, including scripture, wisdom, and dominion, upon the family of Abraham. The verse challenges the envious to reflect on their sentiments and recognize that Allah's distribution of blessings is based on His wisdom and purpose. Envy, therefore, is misplaced and counterproductive.
orig: أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وآتيناهم ملكا عظيما

translation: Among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it. And sufficient is Hell as a blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of different people to the message of the Qur'an. Some accept and believe in it, while others reject it and turn away. The verse serves as a stern reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, stating that Hellfire is a sufficient and just recompense for those who deny the truth. This duality underscores the importance of faith and the serious repercussions of disbelief.
orig: فمنهم من آمن به ومنهم من صد عنه وكفى بجهنم سعيرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the divine messages and signs of Allah. The graphic description of continuously renewed punishment suggests the seriousness and severity of the consequences of disbelief. The renewing of the skin underscores the idea of enduring punishment without cessation. The final part of the verse, highlighting Allah's might and wisdom, emphasizes that this punishment is not borne out of cruelty, but out of a profound system of justice administered by a wise and powerful deity. It conveys that the purpose of such severe punishment is to ensure that the disbelievers experience and comprehend the full extent of the consequences of their actions.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. They will have purified spouses therein, and We will admit them to deepening shade.
interpretation: This verse promises eternal rewards for those who combine faith with righteous actions. It highlights the concept of Paradise, depicted vividly with flowing rivers, eternal dwelling, and pure companionship. The mention of 'deepening shade' signifies immense comfort and peace, contrasting with any earthly discomforts. This verse aims to inspire believers to maintain their faith and good deeds by envisioning the divine and eternal rewards awaiting them.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا لهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وندخلهم ظلا ظليلا

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two fundamental principles of ethical behavior: fulfilling trusts and practicing justice. The first part highlights the importance of returning what is entrusted to someone else back to its rightful owner, emphasizing honesty and integrity in personal and communal dealings. The second part underscores the necessity of fairness and impartiality when making judgments or resolving disputes among people, advocating for justice as a cornerstone of societal harmony. Allah’s attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Seeing reinforce the idea that God is fully aware of human actions and intentions. This divine oversight serves as a reminder to act righteously in both public and private actions.
orig: إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها وإذا حكمتم بين الناس أن تحكموا بالعدل إن الله نعما يعظكم به إن الله كان سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah, His Messenger, and those in positions of authority among the believers. It also offers guidance for resolving disputes by advising believers to refer disagreements to the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. This indicates that aligning actions with divine guidance and prophetic teachings is considered the most righteous and effective way to achieve harmony and proper outcomes.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut (false judges) while they were commanded to reject it, and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse is admonishing those who, despite professing faith in the revelations sent to Prophet Muhammad and previous prophets, hypocritically seek judgment or resolution from sources contrary to divine guidance, specifically 'Taghut' (false deities or tyrants). It underscores the inconsistency and disobedience in their actions, highlighting that seeking such misguidance is contrary to the command to reject falsehood. Moreover, it points to the influence of Satan, whose aim is to lead them into deep misguidance, emphasizing the spiritual danger of their actions and the imperative to adhere strictly to divine guidance.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك يريدون أن يتحاكموا إلى الطاغوت وقد أمروا أن يكفروا به ويريد الشيطان أن يضلهم ضلالا بعيدا

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of hypocrites when invited to follow Allah's revelations and the Prophet. It highlights their deliberate refusal and aversion, underscoring their insincerity and a lack of commitment to genuine faith. Their turning away is a clear indication of their internal resistance to true guidance.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول رأيت المنافقين يصدون عنك صدودا

translation: But how [will it be] when disaster strikes them because of what their hands have put forth and then they come to you swearing by Allah, 'We intended nothing but good conduct and accommodation.'
interpretation: This verse points to the hypocrites who commit wrongdoings but when they face the consequences, they try to justify their actions under the pretext of having good intentions. It warns that facing the consequences of one's actions is inevitable and posing false intentions before the Prophet (peace be upon him) and Allah is futile. Sincerity in action and genuine repentance are emphasized as opposed to deceit and hypocrisy.
orig: فكيف إذا أصابتهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم ثم جاءوك يحلفون بالله إن أردنا إلا إحسانا وتوفيقا

translation: Those are the ones Allah knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them but admonish them and speak to them a far-reaching word.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah is fully aware of the true intentions and feelings within people's hearts. Despite this knowledge, believers are instructed to distance themselves from such individuals, while still offering them counsel and communicating in a profound and impactful manner. This guidance aims to help them reflect and encourage positive change, underscoring the importance of wisdom and compassion in interactions.
orig: أولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم فأعرض عنهم وعظهم وقل لهم في أنفسهم قولا بليغا

translation: We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of sending messengers, which is to be obeyed as per Allah's command. It also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, illustrating that even those who have wronged themselves have the opportunity for forgiveness if they genuinely repent and seek intercession through the Prophet Muhammad. The verse underscores the compassion and readiness of Allah to accept repentance and show mercy to those who sincerely seek it.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا ليطاع بإذن الله ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاءوك فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله توابا رحيما

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authority of the Prophet Muhammad as a divinely-appointed judge in matters of dispute among believers. True faith is characterized not only by outward acceptance of the Prophet's decisions but also by inward agreement and complete submission. The verse underscores that genuine belief requires both an acknowledgment of the Prophet’s judgments and an absence of inner resistance to these rulings, reflecting a holistic submission to divine guidance.
orig: فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت ويسلموا تسليما

translation: And if We had decreed upon them, 'Kill yourselves' or 'Leave your homes,' they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith].
interpretation: This verse reflects on human nature and the challenges of obedience to divine commandments. It suggests that even if extraordinary demands were made by God, such as self-sacrifice or abandoning one's home, most people would struggle to comply. However, had they adhered to God's commandments, it would have resulted in a better and more stable state of faith for them. The verse underscores the importance of obedience and how it ultimately benefits the believer, strengthening their faith and resolve.
orig: ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا

translation: And We would surely have given them from Us a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise and assurance from Allah of a significant and rewarding compensation for those who are righteous and follow His guidance. It reflects the principle of divine justice and the certainty of a substantive reward for faithfulness and obedience to God's commands.
orig: وإذا لآتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما

translation: We would have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's willingness to guide those who turn to Him sincerely. It underscores the concept that divine guidance is accessible to all, but requires an earnest pursuit of righteousness. The 'straight path' symbolizes a life of moral integrity and devotion to God's commandments. This path leads one towards spiritual fulfillment and ultimate salvation.
orig: ولهديناهم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to both Allah and the Prophet Muhammad as a means to attain the companionship of the most esteemed and honored individuals in the hereafter - the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. It highlights both the spiritual reward and the high status granted to those who adhere to divine guidance, implying that true success and ultimate honor lie in following the path ordained by Allah and His Messenger.
orig: ومن يطع الله والرسول فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

translation: That is the grace of Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that any favor or blessing one may receive is a grace from Allah, reflecting His generosity and mercy. It further underscores that Allah's knowledge is comprehensive, implying that He fully understands who is deserving of His grace and why. Therefore, believers should trust in His wisdom and decisions, recognizing that His awareness is all-encompassing and perfect.
orig: ذلك الفضل من الله وكفى بالله عليما

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and either go forth in companies or go forth all together.
interpretation: In this verse, believers are being instructed to be vigilant and prepared, emphasizing the importance of readiness and unity in the face of potential threats. The directive to go forth in companies or all together suggests different strategies may be employed depending on the situation, but the underlying message remains to stay alert and act with coherence and collective strength.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات أو انفروا جميعا

translation: And indeed, there is among you he who lingers behind; and if disaster strikes you, he says, 'Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy and cowardice among some individuals within the community. It highlights the behavior of those who intentionally avoid participating in collective efforts or struggles. When adversity strikes the community, these individuals boast about their avoidance of the situation, falsely attributing their absence to divine favor rather than acknowledging their lack of solidarity and courage. The verse serves as a criticism of such attitudes and an encouragement to demonstrate true solidarity and commitment to the collective cause.
orig: وإن منكم لمن ليبطئن فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن معهم شهيدا

translation: But if you receive a bounty from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him, 'Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment.'
interpretation: This verse discusses the hypocrisy and insincerity of certain individuals. It indicates that there are those who, when they witness others receive blessings or favors from Allah, express envy and regret that they were not part of it, despite having had no genuine connection or affection with those blessed. This reveals a superficial desire for the benefits rather than a sincere and supportive relationship.
orig: ولئن أصابكم فضل من الله ليقولن كأن لم تكن بينكم وبينه مودة يا ليتني كنت معهم فأفوز فوزا عظيما

translation: Let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And he who fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory - We will bestow upon him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to fight for the cause of Allah by prioritizing the eternal life of the Hereafter over the transient life of this world. It promises that those who engage in such righteous battles, whether they attain martyrdom or triumph, will be rewarded greatly by Allah. It emphasizes the spiritual and moral significance of striving for justice and defending faith, highlighting the assurance of divine reward regardless of the immediate earthly outcome.
orig: فليقاتل في سبيل الله الذين يشرون الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة ومن يقاتل في سبيل الله فيقتل أو يغلب فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?'
interpretation: This verse calls on the believers to rise and take action against injustice and oppression. It addresses the reluctance or inaction of some people when it comes to fighting in the cause of Allah, especially when the cause involves defending the oppressed, including vulnerable men, women, and children. The verse highlights the plea of these oppressed individuals who seek divine intervention to deliver them from the tyranny and appoint a protector and helper from among the believers. It underscores the moral responsibility to support and defend those who are suffering from injustice and emphasizes that this struggle is not only a duty to God but also a duty to humanity.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut (false deities or tyrants). So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak.
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between the motivations of believers and disbelievers. Believers are motivated by their faith in Allah and fight for His cause, while disbelievers fight for unjust or false causes symbolized by Taghut. The verse then encourages believers to oppose those aligned with Satan and assures them that Satan's schemes are inherently weak and destined to fail. This serves to strengthen the resolve of believers by highlighting the moral and spiritual superiority of their cause.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands [from fighting] and establish prayer and give zakah'? Then when fighting was ordained for them, at once a party of them feared men as they fear Allah or with [even] greater fear. They said, 'Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? If only You had postponed [it for] us for a short time.' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears [Allah]. And injustice will not be done to you, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].'
interpretation: This verse addresses a group of believers who were initially instructed to focus on spiritual obligations like prayer and charity while restraining from combat. However, when the command for jihad (fighting) was later given, some among them displayed fear and hesitation, questioning the necessity and timing of this command from Allah. The verse highlights the contrast between fear of human beings and fear of Allah, emphasizing that the transient pleasures and safety of this world are insignificant compared to the everlasting rewards of the Hereafter for those who are pious. It reassures the believers that no injustice will befall them, not even the smallest amount, reminding them to trust in Allah's wisdom and justice.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you are, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. But if good comes to them, they say, 'This is from Allah'; and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you.' Say, 'All things are from Allah.' So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death, regardless of one's attempts to avoid it, highlighting that it will reach individuals even in seemingly secure and fortified places. It also addresses a common human tendency to attribute positive outcomes to divine intervention and negative outcomes to human or external sources. The verse corrects this misconception by clarifying that all occurrences, whether good or bad, are under the dominion of Allah. Furthermore, it points out the lack of comprehension among those who fail to recognize this fundamental truth, indicating a deeper spiritual and intellectual deficiency.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever good happens to you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from your own self. And We have sent you, [O Muhammad], to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the duality of human experiences, attributing all positive outcomes to the grace and mercy of Allah. It emphasizes that any adversity or misfortune is a result of individual actions, thereby reinforcing personal accountability. Additionally, it affirms the role of Prophet Muhammad as a divinely appointed messenger, with Allah as a sufficient witness to his mission. This highlights both the responsibility of the individual towards their actions and the divine endorsement of the Prophet's message.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: He who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the Prophet Muhammad as a means of obeying Allah. It underscores the divine authority given to the Prophet and his role as a guide for the believers. However, it also acknowledges that ultimately, guidance is in God's hands and those who choose to turn away are beyond the Prophet's responsibility, as he is not their keeper or controller. This emphasizes the notion of personal responsibility and the limits of prophetic duty.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: And they say, 'Obedience.' But when they leave you, a group of them plan by night contrary to what they say. And Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some individuals who verbally express obedience, but secretly plot against the teachings or commands. It underscores the importance of sincerity and warns that Allah is fully aware of their hidden schemes. The instruction to the Prophet is to disregard these hypocritical actions and place his trust in Allah, who is the ultimate executor of affairs and whose support is sufficient for handling such deceit.
