orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Do they not then reflect on the Qur'an? If it had been from anyone other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting deeply on the Qur'an to understand its divine origin. It suggests that the consistency and coherence of the Qur'anic message are evidence of its divine source, implying that a text from any other origin would be riddled with contradictions and inconsistencies. This serves to strengthen the faith of believers in the divine nature of the Qur'an and encourages careful and thoughtful study of its teachings.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: When there comes to them some matter touching [public] safety or fear, they spread it about. But if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who can draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it. And if it had not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responsible communication and the role of leaders and those with knowledge in interpreting and responding to critical matters. It indicates that spreading information hastily can lead to chaos and misinformation. Instead, the proper course of action is to refer such matters to the Prophet or knowledgeable authorities, ensuring a more informed and accurate decision-making process. This guidance highlights the need for wisdom and discretion in dealing with sensitive issues, and it also underscores the protection and guidance provided by Allah, reminding believers that without His favor, many would fall into error due to following harmful impulses or misinformation.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers [to join you] in the hope that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in punishment.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to engage in jihad (struggle or fight) for the cause of Allah, while emphasizing that his responsibility is his own actions and not those of others. It also encourages the Prophet to motivate the believers to join him in this cause. The verse conveys optimism that Allah might weaken the power of those who oppose faith while reminding that Allah's power and ability to exact punishment far surpass any human force.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a reward from it; but whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a share in its burden. And ever is Allah, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in intercession. Those who assist in or advocate for positive, righteous actions will share in the blessings and rewards of those deeds. Conversely, those who support sinful or harmful actions will bear part of the resulting burden or punishment. It underscores the comprehensive awareness and authority of Allah, highlighting that He meticulously oversees and recompenses all actions, whether good or bad.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: When you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with what is better than it, or (at least) return it (in a like manner). Indeed, Allah is ever an Accountant over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to greetings with kindness and respect. It instructs believers to either respond with an equivalent greeting or preferably with a better one. This promotes social harmony and goodwill among people. Additionally, the verse underscores that Allah is aware of all actions, reinforcing the idea that one should act righteously in every interaction, knowing that they are accountable to God.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah! There is no deity except Him. He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse asserts the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah and His role as the ultimate judge. It emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Resurrection when all humans will be gathered for judgment, reinforcing the idea that Allah's promises are absolute and truthful. The verse invites reflection on the reliability and truthfulness of Allah's words compared to anyone else's.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: What is [the matter] with you [that you are] two groups concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has made them fall back [into error and disbelief] for what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And he whom Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers who are divided in their stance towards the hypocrites. It reminds them that Allah has caused the hypocrites to revert to error due to their own actions. The verse questions the believers' desire to guide those whom Allah has already led astray, emphasizing that guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and if He has chosen to misguide someone, no one can provide a path for them. It reinforces the concept of divine will and the futility of trying to override Allah's decisions with human efforts.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieve so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, warning them against forging alliances with those who wish for their disbelief and are hostile to their faith. It emphasizes the importance of loyalty and faithfulness to the cause of Allah. The verse also indicates the gravity of the threat posed by those who actively seek to undermine the believers, suggesting stringent measures against them if they become adversarial. The broader message underscores the need for discernment and caution in relationships and alliances, ensuring that they do not compromise one's faith and commitment to the path of God.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except for those who join a group between whom and you there is a treaty, or those who approach you with their hearts restrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you a cause for fighting against them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting treaties and peace agreements. It provides an exception to the general directives of combat for those who have either aligned with a group that has a treaty with Muslims or those who come with peaceful intentions, avoiding conflict. It underscores the principle that combat is not obligatory against those who seek peace or are part of alliances honoring treaties. The mention that Allah could have given such people power to fight if He willed, but chose not to, serves as a reminder of divine control over all matters and the mercy and wisdom in the allowance for peaceful coexistence.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to be secure from you and secure from their people. Yet whenever they are enticed back into corruption, they fall back into it. So if they do not stay away from you, offer you peace, and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. We have given you clear authority over them.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of individuals who attempt to maintain security with both the Muslim community and their own people, yet consistently fall back into corruption when it arises. The verse instructs that if these individuals do not desist from their harmful actions, make peace, or cease their hostilities, they are to be captured and killed wherever they are found. The clear authority over them given to the believers symbolizes the divine validation of upholding justice and protecting the community from persistent corruption and treachery.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: It is not for a believer to kill another believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay compensation to the deceased's family unless they waive it. If the deceased belonged to a people at war with you and he was a believer, then (the penance is) to free a believing slave. If he belonged to a people with whom you have a treaty, then (the penance is) to pay compensation to his family and to free a believing slave. But whoever does not find (one or cannot afford to free one) then (he must fast for) two consecutive months as a repentance from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the grave sanctity of life in Islam, reiterating that killing another believer is strictly forbidden except in the event of an accident. It mandates specific compensatory actions and penance for accidental killing, reflecting the importance of both justice and mercy. Compensation and freeing a slave emphasize restitution and human dignity, while fasting is prescribed for those unable to fulfill these acts, underscoring the significance of spiritual atonement. The verse underscores the pervasive nature of Allah’s knowledge and wisdom, guiding believers towards just and compassionate resolutions.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally. And Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of intentionally killing a believer in Islam. The punishment is described in very strong terms, indicating eternal damnation in Hell, accompanied by Allah's wrath and curse. This underscores the sanctity of life in Islam and the grave consequences of violating this principle. It serves as a powerful deterrent against murder and highlights the importance of justice and respect for fellow believers.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you a greeting of peace 'You are not a believer,' aspiring for the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many acquisitions. You too were like that before; then Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate. Indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to exercise caution and verify the true intentions of others when they are in the pursuit of Allah's cause, particularly during times of conflict. It warns against hastily judging someone who offers peace, potentially dismissing them as non-believers for materialistic gains. The verse highlights that believers themselves were once in a similar state of seeking understanding and guidance. Therefore, they should be grateful for Allah's guidance and show patience and discernment. This underscores the importance of fairness, empathy, and the avoidance of rash judgments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those of the believers who sit [at home] - except those who are disabled - and those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree. And to both Allah has promised the best [reward]. But Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit [at home] with a great reward -
interpretation: This verse draws a distinction between believers who engage in physical and financial struggle in the cause of Allah and those who do not, except for those who are incapacitated. It emphasizes the value and higher status of active participation in the path of Allah, indicating that those who make sacrifices are held in higher esteem by Allah. However, it also reassures that all believers are promised good rewards, yet those who strive actively receive a greater reward. This conveys an encouragement towards taking an active role in one's faith and contributing to the broader well-being of the community.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: There are degrees [of grace] from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the multifaceted blessings that come from Allah which include spiritual elevation, forgiveness, and an abundance of mercy. It emphasizes Allah’s boundless capacity to forgive and His inherent nature of mercy, suggesting that believers should strive for these divine rewards through faith and righteous deeds. The mention of degrees signifies that these rewards can vary based on one's actions and sincerity.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take (in death) while wronging themselves (the angels) will say, 'In what (condition) were you?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' The angels will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious (enough) for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who, while they were able to emigrate to avoid oppression, chose to stay and thereby wronged themselves by failing to fulfill their religious duties. When the angels question them at their death, they admit to being oppressed, but they are rebuked for not having sought Allah's earth which is vast enough to find a place to practice their faith freely. The punishment for their negligence and failure to act upon their faith is the Hellfire, signifying severe divine displeasure and the dire consequences of inaction when faced with the ability to pursue righteousness.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for those who are weak among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they able to find a way out.
interpretation: This verse addresses the plight of those who are genuinely helpless and unable to fend for themselves. It highlights Allah’s recognition of the vulnerable groups within society—men, women, and children—who lack the capacity or means to make strategic decisions or find a way to improve their situation. This exemption underscores the importance of mercy and understanding towards those in dire circumstances, acknowledging their genuine struggles and lack of resources or guidance.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: For those, it is possible that Allah will pardon them. And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's capacity for forgiveness and mercy. It highlights the hope and possibility of divine pardon for individuals who might have transgressed but are now seeking forgiveness. By stating that Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving, it reassures believers of the boundless and continuous nature of Allah's mercy, encouraging them to repent and improve their conduct with the hope of receiving Allah's clemency.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense spiritual reward and ample provision awaiting those who undertake the difficult journey of migration for the sake of Allah, seeking to uphold their faith. It reassures believers that even if they face death in the course of this righteous endeavor, their efforts will not be in vain as their reward is guaranteed by Allah. The verse also highlights Allah's immense capacity for forgiveness and mercy, encouraging believers to trust in His benevolence and justice.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse provides a concession to the believers, allowing them to shorten their prayers while traveling, especially under the fear of attack or disruption from disbelievers. This flexibility underscores the pragmatic nature of Islamic practices, prioritizing the safety and well-being of the believers. Additionally, it reiterates the clear enmity that disbelievers hold towards the faithful, reinforcing the need for vigilance and precaution during travel.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: When you (O Prophet) are among them and lead them in prayer, let one party of them stand up [in prayer] with you, taking their arms with them. When they finish their prostrations, let them take their positions in the rear, and let the other party who have not yet prayed come forward and pray with you, taking all precaution and bearing arms. The disbelievers wish that you should neglect your arms and baggage so that they can come down upon you in one single attack. But there is no blame on you if you put away your arms because of the inconvenience of rain or because you are ill, but take (every) precaution for yourselves. Indeed, Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the actions and precautions to be taken by the Muslim community during times of conflict, especially during the act of prayer. The directive ensures that a portion of the group remains vigilant and armed while the other prays, maintaining security against potential attacks. This balanced approach underscores the importance of both spiritual practices and practical awareness in safeguarding the community. Furthermore, it highlights the inherent danger posed by disbelievers who are described as eagerly watching for any lapse in preparation to launch a unified assault. Finally, it offers leniency under adverse conditions but reaffirms the necessity of caution, with the promise of divine retribution against those who oppose the believers.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of maintaining the remembrance of Allah in all situations, whether standing, sitting, or lying down. It also emphasizes the significance of re-establishing regular prayers once one feels safe and secure, highlighting that prayer is an obligation prescribed at specific times for believers. The verse shows the flexibility in worship while ensuring the principle of constant devotion and discipline through regular prayers.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, they are suffering as you are suffering, but you have hope from Allah that they do not. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is urging the believers not to lose heart or weaken in their pursuit of their adversaries, despite the pain and suffering they are experiencing. It emphasizes that their enemies also feel pain and suffering similarly. However, the key difference highlighted is that the believers have hope and expectations from Allah, something their enemies do not possess. The verse reinforces that Allah is all-knowing and wise, providing believers with assurance and encouraging them to persevere in their faith and efforts, despite the challenges they face.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the deceitful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting its purpose as a guide for just judgment among people based on divinely revealed principles. It also warns against defending those who are deceitful, emphasizing the importance of integrity and fairness in leadership and judgment.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness. It underscores the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah, reassuring that His mercy is ever-present and that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him with sincerity and repentance.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are habitually deceitful and sinful.
interpretation: This verse warns against defending or supporting individuals who commit deceit and wrongdoing. It emphasizes that Allah disapproves of those who make a habit of treachery and sinfulness. The message is to maintain integrity and not align oneself with dishonest actions, acknowledging that such behavior is disliked by Allah.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They conceal [their evil intentions and deeds] from the people, but they cannot conceal [them] from Allah. And He is with them when they spend the night in discussions He disapproves of. And Allah is All-Encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who try to hide their sinful actions from other people but fail to realize that they cannot hide anything from Allah. It reminds believers that Allah's knowledge and presence encompass everything, including their private discussions and actions, and encourages them to act with sincerity and awareness of Allah's omnipresence.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: Here you are—arguing on their behalf in this world. But who will argue with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection? Or who will be their defender?
interpretation: This verse addresses the futility of defending wrongdoing in this worldly life as it highlights the ultimate accountability before Allah on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that while one might find advocates in this world to defend their wrongful actions, no one can defend them before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. It emphasizes that earthly arguments and defense mechanisms are insignificant compared to divine justice, and reminds believers of the importance of genuine righteousness and accountability.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs themselves but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It emphasizes that no matter how serious one's transgressions or self-inflicted wrongs may be, seeking sincere repentance can lead to divine forgiveness. It assures believers that Allah's mercy is always accessible, highlighting the importance of turning towards Allah with a genuine heart when seeking pardon for one's sins.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever commits a sin only earns it against himself. And Allah is Ever-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions. It asserts that sins and wrongdoings ultimately affect the individual who commits them, both in this world and in the Hereafter. Moreover, it reassures that Allah's knowledge encompasses all actions and intentions, and His wisdom ensures that everyone will face just consequences for their deeds. Therefore, individuals are urged to be mindful of their actions and maintain righteousness, understanding that they cannot escape divine justice.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: But whoever commits a sin or an offense and then blames an innocent person for it, he has certainly burdened himself with slander and a clear sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe wrongdoing of not only committing a sin or offense but also unjustly imputing it to an innocent person. It highlights the gravity of the compounded sin—both the original wrongdoing and the act of slander and false accusation—stressing that it leads to clear and unmistakable guilt in the sight of God. The verse serves as a moral directive to uphold justice, truth, and integrity in human interactions.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: If it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, acknowledging the divine protection and guidance bestowed upon him by Allah. It underscores that despite attempts by some to mislead him, these efforts are ultimately futile, and such individuals only hurt themselves. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an and wisdom given to the Prophet, highlighting unknown knowledge granted to him through divine favor. Additionally, it reflects on the greatness of Allah's mercy and favor, which have been instrumental in the Prophet's mission.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in much of their secret talks, except for those who enjoin charity or that which is right or conciliation between people. Whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that most private conversations hold no inherent goodness unless they are aimed at encouraging acts of charity, righteousness, or reconciliation among people. It underscores the importance of aligning one's intentions with seeking Allah's pleasure. Acts driven by genuine, righteous motives, specifically those that promote social harmony and alleviate hardship, are highly valued and assured of a significant reward from Allah.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: But whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows a path other than that of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of knowingly opposing the Prophet Muhammad and deviating from the path of true believers after the truth has been made clear. It underscores the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet and the community of believers. Those who choose to follow a different path despite clear guidance will face dire consequences, both in this life and in the Hereafter, with Hell being their ultimate abode. The verse serves as a stern warning to remain steadfast in faith and unity with the Muslim community.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah) which is considered the gravest sin in Islam and one that Allah does not forgive if a person dies upon it without repentance. All other sins may be forgiven by Allah's will. The verse reiterates the severe consequences of shirk, indicating that those who commit this sin are led astray from the true path of monotheism and divine guidance.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: They call but upon female deities besides Him, and they call but upon a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: This verse critiques the idol worship prevalent among certain pre-Islamic Arab tribes, who would call upon female deities or goddesses instead of Allah. It also highlights that their worship of these false deities is essentially a worship of rebellious, misleading forces, embodied in the figure of Satan. The emphasis is on the futility and misguidance in turning away from the One True God towards worship that is ultimately influenced by demonic forces.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: Allah has cursed him. And he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion.'
interpretation: This verse refers to Satan's defiance after being cursed by Allah. Satan declares his intention to mislead a predetermined number of God's servants, emphasizing his ongoing rebellion and determination to oppose divine guidance. This highlights the perpetual challenge between good and evil, and serves as a warning to believers to remain vigilant and steadfast in their faith.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: I will mislead them, and I will create in them false desires; I will order them to slit the ears of cattle and to deface the (fair) nature created by Allah. Whoever, forsaking Allah, takes Satan for a friend, has indeed suffered a manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan and his intent to lead humans astray by instilling false hopes and instructing them to perform acts that alter the natural creation of Allah. These actions symbolize the extent to which followers can deviate due to Satan's influence, thus emphasizing the severe consequences of forsaking divine guidance in favor of following Satanic temptations. The use of specific examples such as mutilating cattle and altering Allah’s creation serves to illustrate the perverse actions that result from being misled. The final statement underscores the significant and clear loss faced by anyone who chooses Satan as a guide over Allah.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: He promises them and fills them with false hopes, but what Satan promises them is nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan's promises. It warns that Satan lures people with false hopes and illusions, leading them astray. Despite the apparent attractiveness of his promises, they ultimately lead to disappointment and deception. This serves as a cautionary reminder to seek truth and guidance from Allah, rather than being seduced by empty promises that lead to spiritual ruin.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Their abode will be Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable and inescapable fate of those who have committed grievous sins and have turned away from the guidance of God. It serves as a stern warning about the severe consequences of disobedience and the certainty of divine justice. The verse is meant to invoke a sense of accountability and urge believers to adhere to righteous conduct to avoid such a dire fate.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. [It is] the promise of Allah, [which is] truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rewards awaiting those who have faith and perform good works, promising them eternal bliss in paradise as described by flowing rivers. It emphasizes the certainty of Allah's promises and asserts that no one speaks with greater truth than Allah, reinforcing the reliability and truthfulness of His words.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It will not be according to your desires or the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does wrong will be requited for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability for one's actions rather than relying on wishful thinking or affiliations with particular religious groups. It clearly states that every individual will face consequences for their deeds, and no external relationship or belief system will shield them from divine justice except through the protection and assistance of Allah. This serves as a reminder to maintain righteousness and be mindful of one's own conduct.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged [even by as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equality of men and women in terms of their capability and opportunity to earn God's favor through righteous deeds. It also underscores the importance of faith in conjunction with good actions. The promise of Paradise and assurance of absolute justice highlight the boundless mercy and fairness of God.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate merit of complete submission to Allah, coupled with righteous action and adherence to the pure monotheistic faith exemplified by the Prophet Abraham. It emphasizes that true religiosity is marked by sincere devotion, virtuous conduct, and following the example of Abraham, who is revered as a close and beloved friend of Allah. This underscores the significant spiritual connection between Abraham and Allah, serving as a model of faith for others.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and all-encompassing dominion of Allah over all creation. It highlights that everything in the heavens and the earth is under His control and ownership. Furthermore, it underscores that Allah's knowledge, power, and authority extend over all things, leaving nothing beyond His grasp. This serves to remind believers of Allah's ultimate sovereignty and encourages them to place their trust and reliance upon Him.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: They ask you about women. Say, Allah gives you a ruling about them and about what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is decreed for them—and yet desire to marry them—and about the helpless children. And that you should deal justly with orphans. Whatever good you do, Allah is certainly All-Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse addresses inquiries about the treatment and rights of women, particularly orphaned girls and the helpless. It emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fulfilling the rights decreed to them, especially regarding marriage and inheritance. By highlighting these specifics, the verse stresses the necessity of fair and ethical treatment of the vulnerable, assuring that all good deeds, especially those safeguarding the rights of orphans and the weak, are known to Allah and are rewarded.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: If a woman fears harsh treatment or desertion from her husband, there is no sin on them if they settle their differences amicably, for reconciliation is best. Although human souls are prone to selfishness, if you act kindly and maintain righteousness, surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses situations where a woman feels neglected or mistreated by her husband. It encourages both parties to seek reconciliation through mutual agreement without feeling guilty about it, emphasizing that making peace is better than living in discord. Additionally, it acknowledges human tendencies towards selfishness but underscores the importance of kindness and piety, reassuring that Allah is fully aware of one's actions and intentions.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: You will never be able to be perfectly just between your wives, even if it is your ardent desire. But do not incline completely [to one], leaving another hanging. And if you amend and fear Allah, then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the inherent human imperfection in achieving perfect justice between wives in a situation of polygamy. It advises against total favoritism towards one wife, which would cause harm to the other, thus highlighting the importance of maintaining fairness and balance. The verse reassures that despite these challenges, if one strives to act righteously and maintain their piety, Allah's forgiveness and mercy are always available, emphasizing His compassion and understanding of human limitations.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: But if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His bounty. And ever is Allah all-Encompassing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of separation (such as divorce) between a husband and wife. It reassures that if such an event occurs, Allah will provide for both individuals from His vast resources. The verse emphasizes that Allah's capacity to provide is boundless and that His wisdom encompasses all aspects of such human experiences. It underscores Allah's ability to sustain and support individuals even after separation, highlighting His all-encompassing knowledge and wisdom in dealing with human affairs.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty and ownership over all creation, as well as reiterating the consistent divine directive to recognize and revere God's authority. It addresses both the followers of previous scriptures and the current believers, emphasizing the importance of God-consciousness (taqwa). The verse also serves as a reminder that disbelief does not diminish Allah's dominion or glory, for He remains self-sufficient and worthy of all praise regardless of human belief or actions.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It reminds believers of Allah's omnipotence and the fact that He is the ultimate provider and caretaker of all things. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs' emphasizes that Allah alone is adequate to manage and oversee all matters, encouraging believers to put their trust fully in Him.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation. And Allah is Powerful over that.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over His creation. It emphasizes that humanity's existence is contingent upon Allah's will. If He wishes, He has the capability to replace people with another creation. This underscores the importance of humility, gratitude, and the recognition of our dependence on God's mercy and power. It also serves as a warning against arrogance and disobedience, reminding believers that their existence and continuation are solely by Allah's permission.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world—then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that seeking worldly rewards alone is shortsighted. True and complete rewards, encompassing both this life and the Hereafter, lie with Allah. It also emphasizes that Allah is aware of our intentions and actions, being both All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and thus encourages believers to align their desires and efforts with the pursuit of Divine rewards, balancing worldly and spiritual aspirations.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and truthfulness, even when it is difficult or against one's own interests or those of close family members. Believers are called to be impartial and equitable, not letting personal biases or social status influence their actions. Rich or poor, everyone deserves fair treatment. The warning against following personal inclinations underscores the critical need for integrity. Ultimately, God is fully aware of all actions and intentions, serving as a reminder that divine justice will prevail.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He has sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity for the believers to reaffirm their faith in Allah, His Messenger, and the scriptures revealed, both the Qur'an and those before it. It serves as a reminder that belief in the fundamental aspects of faith—Allah, the angels, the holy books, the messengers, and the Last Day—is essential. Failure to uphold these beliefs is presented as a profound deviation from the path of righteousness and truth, indicating the gravity of disbelief and its consequences.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the condition of people who oscillate between belief and disbelief, ultimately increasing in their rejection of faith. It highlights that persistent apostasy and growing disbelief result in the closure of divine mercy and guidance. The verse serves as a stern warning against the frivolous and insincere treatment of faith, emphasizing the gravity of steadfast disbelief and its consequences.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that there is for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief or insincerity. It emphasizes that mere outward declarations of belief without genuine faith and righteous actions will lead to severe consequences in the Hereafter. The 'painful punishment' signifies both the spiritual and physical torment that awaits hypocrites due to their deceit and duplicity.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honor through them? Verily, all honor belongs to Allah.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of loyalty and alliance, highlighting the behavior of individuals who seek support and honor from disbelievers rather than believers. The verse questions the rationale behind their actions and emphasizes that true honor and dignity are derived solely from Allah. It serves as a reminder that one's allegiance should be aligned with the believers and ultimately with Allah, for all forms of honor and might originate from Him alone.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation. Otherwise, you would be like them. Surely, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to distance themselves from those who mock or deny the revelations of Allah. By refusing to join in such gatherings, believers uphold the sanctity of God's words and reject any form of disrespect towards them. The warning is stern, equating passive attendance with active participation in the mockery. This signifies the importance of actively defending the faith and maintaining righteousness, as Allah promises that He will ultimately gather those who are hypocritical or reject the faith in Hell, highlighting the severe consequences of such actions.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait and watch for you. Then if you gain a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if the disbelievers have a share of that victory, they say, 'Did we not gain the advantage over you, and did we not defend you from the believers?' But Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection. And never will Allah grant to the disbelievers a way (to triumph) over the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical behavior of those who are insincere in their faith. They try to position themselves in a way to benefit regardless of which side wins. When the believers are victorious, they claim allegiance to them, but when the disbelievers gain an advantage, they assert their role in thwarting the believers. The verse reassures the believers that ultimate judgment and justice will be rendered by Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and He will not allow the disbelievers to triumph over the believers in the end.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitful nature of hypocrites who pretend to be devout believers but lack genuine faith. It emphasizes that their attempts to deceive Allah are futile, as Allah is fully aware of their intentions and will treat them accordingly. The verse also criticizes their lack of sincerity in worship, as they perform prayers sluggishly and primarily to be seen by others, rather than out of true devotion, reflecting a minimal remembrance of Allah.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Wavering between them, [belonging] neither to these [believers] nor to those [disbelievers]. And whoever Allah leaves astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of individuals who are indecisive and lack firm commitment, swaying between belief and disbelief. It underscores the position of those who do not fully align themselves with either the believers or the disbelievers. The verse also emphasizes that when Allah allows someone to go astray due to their own choices and actions, no guidance can lead them back to the right path.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: This verse advises the believers to avoid forming close alliances or friendships with disbelievers at the expense of their loyalty to fellow believers. It emphasizes the importance of solidarity within the Muslim community and cautions against actions that might lead to divine disapproval. The phrase 'clear case' suggests that such alliances could be seen as a contradictory and evident offense, resulting in divine consequences.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire; and never will you find for them a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment reserved for hypocrites, those who outwardly profess faith but internally deny it or act contrary to its principles. Their deception is considered a grave sin because it undermines the foundation of trust and sincerity in the community. The 'lowest depths of the Fire' signifies the most severe level of Hell, indicating the severe consequences of hypocrisy. The verse also highlights the absolute nature of their punishment by stating that there will be no helper for them, emphasizing their isolation and the futility of seeking intercession or relief from their punishment.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent and correct themselves and hold fast to Allah and are sincere in their religion for Allah; for those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the merciful nature of Allah, emphasizing that even those who have erred can find redemption if they genuinely repent, make amends, clench to Allah, and purify their faith solely for Him. Such individuals are assured a place among the true believers and are promised immense rewards from Allah. This speaks to the inclusive and forgiving nature of Islam, where sincere repentance and reformation are always met with divine grace and acceptance.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And ever is Allah Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reflects the merciful and just nature of Allah, emphasizing that He does not intend to punish His servants unnecessarily. Rather, if individuals express gratitude and maintain their faith, they secure Allah’s appreciation and mercy. It underscores the importance of gratitude (shukr) and belief (iman) as fundamental qualities that shield one from divine retribution, highlighting Allah's comprehensive knowledge of human actions and intentions, and His readiness to reward rightly guided conduct.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public utterance of hurtful speech unless it is by someone who has been wronged. And Allah is Ever-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the conduct regarding speech and behavior towards others. It emphasizes that Allah dislikes the expression of harmful or offensive words in public, except in cases where an individual has been wronged and is expressing their grievance. It also serves as a reminder that Allah is always aware and listening, thus urging believers to be mindful of their speech and conduct, while granting leniency to those who speak out in response to injustice.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you disclose a good deed or conceal it, or pardon an offense, then indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in good deeds whether openly or in secret, and to hold a disposition of forgiveness toward others' wrongdoings. It underscores Allah's attributes of being immensely forgiving and powerful, reassuring the believers that God’s forgiveness is boundless and His capability absolute. This serves both as a moral guideline for personal conduct and as a reflection of the divine qualities that believers should aspire to emulate.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to separate Allah from His messengers, saying, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others,' and wish to adopt a way in between.
interpretation: This verse asserts the seriousness of disbelief in Allah and His messengers, emphasizing that such disbelief is not simply rejecting faith but also entails a desire to create divisions between Allah and His messengers. This compromise, where one accepts parts of the divine message while rejecting others, is highlighted as an unacceptable and deceitful approach to faith. The verse underscores the importance of holistic belief in the entirety of the divinely sent messages without picking and choosing according to one's preferences.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: They are truly the disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse identifies those who reject faith as true disbelievers and underscores the gravity of their rejection by stating that a humiliating punishment awaits them. The emphasis is on the certainty of their disbelief and the consequence that has been divinely ordained for such a state of rejection. It serves as a warning about the serious repercussions of disbelief in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them, He will give them their rewards. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in all of Allah's messengers without discrimination. It signifies that true faith requires acceptance of all prophets sent by Allah. Those who uphold this complete belief are promised rewards from Allah, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and mercy. It serves as a reminder of the inclusive nature of faith and the comprehensive compassion of Allah towards believers.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they had asked Moses for even greater than that and said, 'Show us Allah outright,' so the thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf after what had come to them of clear evidences, and We pardoned that. And We gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse addresses the demands made by the People of the Scripture (referring to Jews and Christians) for a miraculous sign, similar to the requests made to Moses. It highlights their persistent demands for proof of divine authority, which led to their punishment when they sinned by worshipping the calf. Despite their transgressions, God's mercy is shown through His forgiveness and the granting of clear guidance and authority to Moses. The verse emphasizes the recurring theme of human arrogance and the need for faith without constant demand for miraculous signs.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised over them the Mount for [refusal of] their covenant; and We said to them, 'Enter the gate bowing humbly'; and We said to them, 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Children of Israel and their obligations under a covenant with Allah. The 'raising of the Mount' is a symbol of the serious warnings and the significant weight of the covenant they accepted. Entering 'the gate bowing humbly' signifies obedience and humility before Allah's commandments. 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath,' emphasizes the importance of the Sabbath as a day of rest and worship, highlighting their breaches of rules set by Allah. The 'solemn covenant' underscores the gravity and seriousness of their promises to adhere to these divine commandments.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing of the prophets unjustly and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped', But, Allah has sealed them due to their disbelief, so they believe not except for a few.
interpretation: This verse addresses the consequences faced by certain groups for their actions, which include breaking their covenant with Allah, rejecting His signs, and killing the prophets unjustly. Their assertion that their hearts are protected is rebutted by Allah, who clarifies that their disbelief has led to their hearts being sealed, preventing them from true belief except for a few among them. It highlights the concept of divine retribution for persistent transgression and disbelief.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And [We cursed them] for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of false accusations and slander, particularly those directed towards virtuous individuals like Mary. It signifies the severe misguidance and transgression of those who disbelieve and the consequences that arise from their actions. This false accusation reflects a deep moral corruption and injustice, which is condemned and detested by Allah. The emphasis on 'a great slander' underlines the seriousness of the sin and the profound impact of such malicious lies.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And their saying, 'Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.' And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse addresses a central belief in Islamic theology regarding the fate of Jesus Christ (Isa in Arabic). It refutes the assertion made by some that Jesus was killed or crucified, stating instead that it only appeared to them as such. This is interpreted to mean that someone else was made to resemble Jesus, and it was this person who was crucified in his place. The verse highlights that those who claim otherwise are merely following conjecture and do not possess certain knowledge. It underscores the Islamic belief that Jesus was not crucified but was instead raised up by Allah.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself, and Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is speaking about the event of Allah raising Jesus (Isa) to Himself, protecting him from his enemies. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom, indicating that Allah's actions are both powerful and perfectly wise. This serves to reassure believers that divine intervention is guided by ultimate wisdom and might, even in moments of seeming crisis.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of acknowledgment and belief in the truth of Jesus Christ by the People of the Scripture (i.e., Jews and Christians) before their death, whether during their lifetime or at the moment of death. It also emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Jesus will serve as a witness against those who denied his true message and failed to follow the divine guidance as conveyed by him.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: So for wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We made unlawful for them certain good foods which had been lawful for them, and for their averting many from Allah's way.
interpretation: This verse addresses a historical context where a group among the Jews committed injustices, leading to certain good and lawful things being forbidden to them as a form of divine retribution. This punishment also reflects their role in diverting others from following the path of Allah. The verse underscores the principle of divine justice and accountability for actions that violate moral and ethical standards.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And for their taking of usury while they had been forbidden from it, and their wrongful consumption of people's wealth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to certain transgressions committed by people: engaging in usurious practices despite clear prohibitions and consuming others' wealth unjustly. These actions are highlighted as grave moral failings, which are met with a stern warning of severe punishment from Allah. The verse underscores the importance of ethical conduct in financial dealings and adherence to divine commandments to avoid dire consequences.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those among them who are well-grounded in knowledge and the believers, believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you. And those who establish prayer and give alms and believe in Allah and the Last Day, it is they to whom We shall grant a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of deep knowledge and true faith among believers. It acknowledges the sincerity of those who follow the divine revelations brought by different prophets. Emphasis is placed on consistent acts of worship, such as praying and giving alms (zakat), which demonstrate one's devotion and righteousness. Belief in Allah and the Last Day underscores the importance of an enduring faith that transcends time. Those who embody these qualities are promised a significant reward from Allah, reflecting both spiritual and potentially material blessings.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of divine revelation throughout history. It establishes that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is part of a long line of prophets who received guidance from God. This lineage includes distinguished prophets recognized in Judaic and Christian traditions, thereby reinforcing the monotheistic message shared by all. Additionally, it underscores the unity of the divine message and the importance of adhering to it, fostering a sense of brotherhood and continuity among the followers of these faiths.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And We sent messengers about whom We have told you before and messengers about whom We have not told you. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: This verse underlines the diversity and multitude of God’s messengers, some of whom have been explicitly mentioned in the Qur’an, while others have not been detailed. The direct conversation between Allah and Moses is highlighted as a special distinction, portraying the unique nature of divine communication and emphasizing the honor and responsibility bestowed upon Moses.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and warners so that mankind would have no argument against Allah after the (coming of) Messengers. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the role of the messengers as those who bring glad tidings and deliver warnings, intended to guide humanity along the correct path. By sending these messengers, Allah ensured that people would have no excuse or argument against Him for their actions, as they were provided clear guidance. The verse highlights Allah's wisdom and authority in implementing this system, emphasizing His might in commanding respect and obedience, and His wisdom in providing guidance through His messengers.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has revealed to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as a witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truth of the revelation given to the Prophet Muhammad. Allah Himself testifies to the authenticity of the message, underscoring that it is sent down with His perfect knowledge. Additionally, the angels, who are beings of truth and purity, also bear witness to the revelation. This dual testimony reinforces the trustworthiness and significance of the Qur'an. Ultimately, it declares that Allah is the most reliable and sufficient witness, whose testimony surpasses all others in authenticity and authority.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences for those who not only disbelieve in the message of Islam but also actively obstruct others from following it. Their actions not only lead them away from the Truth but also misguide others, resulting in a deviation that takes them far from the path of righteousness and salvation. It emphasizes the gravity of hindering others' spiritual journeys and the profound extent of their misguidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit wrong [or injustice]—never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who both disbelieve and engage in acts of injustice. It stresses that such individuals will be deprived of Allah's forgiveness and guidance. The emphasis here is on the combination of disbelief and wrongdoing, suggesting that their persistent rejection of faith and engagement in oppressive behavior create barriers that prevent them from receiving divine forgiveness and being guided towards righteousness. The severity of this consequence highlights the critical importance of faith coupled with just actions in seeking Allah's mercy and guidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the path to Hell, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning about the consequences of unrepentant sin and disbelief. It emphasizes that the path to Hell is a direct result of one's actions, leading to eternal punishment. The statement that this is 'easy for Allah' underlines His absolute power and justice, indicating that such outcomes are within His ability to enact effortlessly, serving as a reminder of the seriousness of straying from righteous behavior and belief.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse calls upon all humankind to recognize and accept the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad, as it is the truth from their Lord. Believing in this message is in their best interest. However, if people choose to disbelieve, they should remember that Allah is the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, implying His absolute authority and control over all matters. Moreover, Allah's knowledge and wisdom are emphasized, indicating that His guidance and decrees are based on His profound wisdom and complete understanding of all things.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Book, do not go to extremes in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was only a Messenger of Allah, and His word which He directed to Mary, and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, 'Three'; desist – it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, particularly Christians, urging them not to exceed the proper bounds set by their religion. It emphasizes the importance of truthfulness in speaking about Allah, highlighting that Jesus (peace be upon him) is a revered prophet and messenger, not divine himself. The verse refutes the concept of the Trinity, emphasizing the oneness of Allah and His transcendence above having any offspring. It reminds believers of Allah's absolute control and sufficiency in managing the affairs of the universe, thus encouraging a correct understanding of monotheism.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels who are near [to Him]. Whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them all to Himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that neither Jesus (the Messiah) nor the angels are too proud to serve Allah. It refutes any notions of their divinity or claims that they would shirk from being Allah’s servants. The verse further warns that those who arrogantly reject worshiping Allah will ultimately be brought before Him for judgment. It underscores the concept of humility and servitude to Allah as honorable traits and positions arrogance and disdain as pathways to divine accountability.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: As for those who believe and perform righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and even increase them out of His bounty. But as for those who disdain and are arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse delineates the dichotomy between the fates of believers who do good deeds and those who are prideful and dismiss the divine message. Believers are promised not only the full recompense for their faith and good actions but also an additional bounty from Allah's grace. On the other hand, those who act arrogantly and reject faith are warned of severe punishment and the absence of any savior or ally besides Allah, emphasizing the gravity of pride and disbelief.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse is addressing all of humanity, emphasizing that a decisive and unmistakable evidence from God has been provided to them. Additionally, it mentions the revelation of a 'clear light,' referring to the Qur'an, which serves as a guiding illumination to lead people out of darkness and into understanding and righteousness. The verse underscores the significance and clarity of the divine guidance that has been bestowed upon mankind.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: But those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them to His mercy and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who have faith in Allah and sincerely adhere to His guidance. It highlights that such individuals will be encompassed by Allah's mercy and blessings. Additionally, it assures them of divine guidance along a righteous and direct path, leading them towards spiritual and moral success and ultimately towards the pleasure of Allah.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: They ask you for a ruling. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah: if a man dies, leaving no children but has a sister, she will receive half of what he leaves. And he will inherit from her if she has no children. If there are two sisters, they will receive two-thirds of what he leaves. If there are brothers and sisters, the male will have the share of two females.' Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of inheritance in cases where the deceased does not have direct descendants (children).
