orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And your people have denied it while it is the truth. Say, 'I am not over you a manager.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that despite the truth of the message, some people will choose to deny it. It also underscores the Prophet's role as a messenger rather than a controller over people's acceptance or rejection of the message. The responsibility lies in conveying the message, not in ensuring people's belief or adherence.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every news (i.e., prophecy) there is a (time) limit, and you will know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept that every prophecy or statement has a designated time for its fulfillment, and its truth will become clear in due course. It conveys the idea of divine timing and patience, ensuring believers that God’s promises will be realized at the appropriate moment.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to avoid engaging with individuals who mock or dispute the divine revelations with disrespect. It encourages maintaining one's dignity and not to participate in or endorse such inappropriate discussions. Furthermore, it acknowledges human fallibility by mentioning that if one forgets and stays in such company, upon realization, they should immediately distance themselves from the wrongdoers. This promotes the importance of surrounding oneself with respectful and righteous company.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And there is nothing upon those who fear Allah from their account, but (it is) a reminder so that they may fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are mindful of Allah and act righteously should not worry about being held accountable for the behavior of others. Their primary responsibility is to remind others of the importance of piety and righteousness, hoping that this reminder may lead to greater mindfulness and fear of Allah among the people. It underlines the individual responsibility in one's actions and the collective duty to encourage good.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And leave those who take their religion as play and amusement and whom the worldly life has deluded. But remind with the Qur'an, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it earned; it will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah. And even if it offers every compensation, it will not be accepted from it. Those are the ones who are given up to destruction for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse commands leaving those who trivialize and take their religion lightly, being more absorbed in worldly pleasures and distractions. It urges reminding them with the Qur'an to warn them of the consequences of their deeds, indicating that they will have no support or intercession except Allah. The verse emphasizes that even if they tried to compensate for their actions, it will not be accepted. It highlights the dire fate awaiting those who earn destruction through disbelief and misdeeds, depicting their suffering through extreme punishments in the hereafter as a result of their rejection of faith.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, 'Shall we invoke other than Allah something that neither benefits us nor harms us and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us? [We would then be] like one whom the devils enticed to wander upon the earth confused, [while] he has companions inviting him to guidance, [calling], "Come to us." Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of worship and the futility of turning to anything other than Allah. It highlights the irrationality of invoking deities or entities that can neither benefit nor harm. Turning back from monotheism to polytheism after receiving divine guidance is likened to a person lost and confused, misled by devils, ignoring the call to true guidance. The verse affirms the ultimate guidance as that which comes from Allah, reiterating the importance of submission to Him as the sole purpose of life. This submission is presented as a fundamental commandment, essential for achieving the rightful path.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him; and it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing prayers regularly as an act of worship and devotion to Allah. It also highlights the significance of having consciousness and fear of Allah's presence and power. The verse concludes by reminding believers that ultimately, everyone will be gathered to Him for judgement, underscoring the accountability that comes with faith and actions in this life.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the day He says, 'Be,' and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power and sovereignty in creation and judgment. It emphasizes that God created the heavens and the earth with purpose and truth. The phrase 'Be, and it is' illustrates God's effortless command over existence. The reference to the Day when the Horn is blown indicates the Day of Judgment, reasserting God's ultimate control over all matters, both seen and unseen. Finally, it reassures believers of God's comprehensive wisdom and awareness of all things.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: When Abraham said to his father, Azar, 'Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Prophet Abraham and his father Azar regarding the practice of idolatry. Abraham challenges his father's beliefs, emphasizing the misguided nature of worshipping idols. This confrontation reflects the broader theme of monotheism in the Qur'an, where the emphasis is placed on the worship of the one true God and rejecting false deities. Abraham's courageous stance underscores the importance of questioning and reflecting on one's beliefs, even when it involves close family members, to uphold the truth.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: Thus did We show Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among those who have sure faith.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine revelation and insight granted to Prophet Abraham, highlighting his unique connection with the divine wisdom and the spiritual realms. The purpose of showing him the dominion of the heavens and the earth was to reinforce his faith and certainty in God's omnipotence, preparing him for his prophetic mission and strengthening his resolve in the face of challenges.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: When the night grew dark upon him, he saw a star and said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I do not love those that set.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Prophet Abraham's (Ibrahim) journey of discovering the truth about the Creator. By observing the natural phenomena and contemplating their impermanence, he deduces that the true Lord must be eternal and unchanging. This process marks his rejection of celestial bodies as deities, emphasizing the attribute of constancy as essential to divinity, guiding believers toward monotheism and the worship of Allah alone.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

translation: When he saw the moon rising, he said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the misguided people.'
interpretation: This verse represents Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in his quest for understanding the true nature of God. He observes the moon and initially considers it divine due to its brilliance and presence. However, when the moon sets, he acknowledges its impermanence and realizes that it cannot be a true deity. Ibrahim’s declaration highlights his dependence on divine guidance to avoid being misguided, illustrating a key Islamic teaching about seeking and following true knowledge and rejecting false idols.
orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, 'This is my lord; this is greater.' But when it set, he said, 'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.'
interpretation: This verse recounts a moment in the life of Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim), illustrating his journey towards understanding the oneness of Allah. Initially, he observes the natural phenomena and considers them as potential deities due to their grandeur. However, he rejects each one as they disappear, asserting that such transient entities cannot be worthy of worship. Ultimately, he renounces idolatry and proclaims his disassociation from the polytheistic practices of his people, emphasizing the necessity of worshiping the eternal, unchanging God.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have set my face towards He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse conveys a declaration of monotheistic faith, emphasizing a resolute commitment to worshipping the Creator of the heavens and the earth alone, without associating any partners with Him. It underscores the importance of pure and devoted worship, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And his people argued with him. He said, 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him [of false gods] unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge; then will you not remember?'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet is addressing his people who are disputing with him about his faith in Allah. He emphasizes that Allah has guided him, and he has no fear of the false gods that they associate with Allah, unless Allah wills otherwise. He also asserts the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, urging them to reflect and remember the truth of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience. The verse highlights the futility of idol worship and the protection and guidance provided by true faith in Allah.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how should I fear what you associate with Him while you do not fear associating others with Allah for which He has not sent down any authority upon you? So which of the two parties is more deserving of security, if you should know?
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker challenges the notion of fearing the deities that the disbelievers associate with Allah. The argument is made that fearing these baseless entities lacks justification because there is no divine authority or revelation supporting their legitimacy. Instead, the verse encourages reflection on who truly deserves a sense of security: those who are faithful to the one true God, or those who follow baseless associations. The rhetorical question posed at the end implores listeners to use their understanding to determine which path provides true safety and peace - adherence to monotheism or polytheism.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice, they will have security, and they are the guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure and sincere faith, free from any form of injustice or wrong. It suggests that true believers, who maintain their faith without compromise and avoid oppressing others or allowing falsehood to cloud their belief, will be granted a sense of security and protection. Furthermore, it highlights that these individuals are the ones who are rightly guided on the path of righteousness and truth.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine wisdom and knowledge of God in granting Abraham the ability to present compelling arguments against the idolatry of his people. It highlights the concept that God can elevate individuals in rank and wisdom according to His will, emphasizing His ultimate authority and the underlying wisdom in His decisions and actions. This demonstrates that divine elevation is tied to God's profound wisdom and extensive knowledge of every individual’s capabilities and righteousness.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob - all [of them] We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lineage and guidance provided to the prophets, indicating a divine continuity and favor upon Abraham's descendants. It underscores that the guidance and rewards from Allah are given to those who are righteous and do good deeds. The mention of various prophets emphasizes the unity and consistency in the message delivered by these chosen individuals.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias—all were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the righteous nature of several prophets: Zechariah, John (Yahya), Jesus, and Elias (Elijah). It signifies their piety, devotion, and high status in the eyes of God, serving as exemplary figures for believers to emulate in their faith and conduct.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot, and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse references several prophets who are held in high esteem within the Islamic tradition. The mention of these figures signifies their righteousness and the special favor they received from Allah. Each of them played a crucial role as a messenger, guiding their respective communities towards divine truth. The phrase 'We preferred over the worlds' highlights the elevated status these prophets hold in comparison to the rest of humanity, showcasing their exemplary character, unwavering faith, and the significant contributions they made in fulfilling God's commands.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And of their fathers and their descendants and their brothers, and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine selection and guidance bestowed upon certain individuals and their families. It highlights that the blessings of being chosen and guided to the right path are not limited to the prophets themselves but extend to their progeny and siblings. The emphasis here is on the continuity and inclusiveness of divine grace, indicating that guidance and righteousness can be a familial trait, nurtured across generations, through God’s mercy and choice. This serves as a reminder of the importance of lineage and the potential for sustained virtue within families.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills from among His servants. But if they had associated others with Him, surely what they did would have been in vain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah in granting guidance to whomever He wills among His servants. It underscores the concept of divine will and the importance of monotheism. Even those who are guided and perform righteous deeds must remain steadfast in their monotheistic beliefs, for associating partners with Allah nullifies all their good actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the critical nature of maintaining pure monotheism in order to preserve the value of one's deeds in the sight of Allah.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Those are the ones to whom We have given the Book, the wisdom, and prophethood. If these people disbelieve in it, We have certainly entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges that God has bestowed the scriptures, wisdom, and prophethood upon certain individuals. If current communities choose to reject these divine gifts, it highlights that there are other communities who are entrusted and faithful to these divine teachings. Therefore, divine guidance and the message of God are sustained and preserved by those who truly believe and adhere to it, regardless of rejection by others.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: They are those whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, 'I do not ask you for any reward for it. It is only a reminder for the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those individuals who have been guided by Allah are worthy of being followed in their guidance. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to tell people that he does not seek any worldly compensation for delivering the message of Islam; his responsibility is to remind humanity of the divine guidance. The verse highlights the selfless and sincere nature of prophetic mission, focused solely on the spiritual well-being of all people.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: They did not value Allah as He should be valued when they said, 'Allah did not reveal anything to a human being.' Say, 'Who revealed the Book that Moses brought as a light and guidance for the people, which you made into separate sheets, showing some but hiding much, and you were taught that which neither you nor your fathers knew?' Say, 'Allah [revealed it].' Then leave them to play in their vain discussions.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have not recognized Allah's true greatness and greatness. By denying that divine revelations were sent to humans, they fail to comprehend the tradition of prophethood. The verse responds by reminding them of the Torah given to Moses, highlighting its guidance and wisdom. The criticism focuses on how they fragmented the sacred texts to manipulate knowledge, displaying portions while concealing much. This behavior resulted in incomplete understanding and forgetfulness of divine teachings meant to uplift humanity. Allah is identified as the source of all revelation. The faithful are advised to leave those who engage in frivolous arguments so they can continue their discourse without distraction, thus emphasizing patience and focus on true understanding.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have revealed, confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around her. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an is a divinely bestowed, blessed scripture that corroborates the previous revelations. It emphasizes the duty of the Prophet to warn the central city of Makkah (referred to as the 'Mother of Cities') and its surrounding regions. It underscores that true believers in the afterlife will naturally have faith in the Qur'an and will be diligent in their prayers, showing a link between belief in the Hereafter and adherence to the spiritual practices prescribed by the Qur'an.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or says, 'It has been revealed to me,' while nothing has been revealed to him, and one who says, 'I will reveal something like what Allah revealed.' If you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the throes of death while the angels extend their hands, [saying], 'Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth and [that] you were, toward His verses, being arrogant.'
interpretation: This verse denounces the severe wrongdoing of those who falsely claim divine revelation or mimic what Allah has revealed. It highlights the ultimate fate of such unjust individuals during their final moments, where angels compel them to surrender their souls, foreshadowing the humiliating punishment they will face. The cause of this severe consequence is not only their lies about Allah but also their arrogance and disdain towards His signs and verses.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind whatever We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners with Allah. Certainly, the bond between you is now broken, and what you used to claim has strayed from you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality of the Day of Judgment where individuals will stand before Allah alone, just as they were created, without any of their worldly possessions or false deities they associated with Him. It underscores the futility of relying on any intercessors or partners besides Allah, as these supposed partners will be powerless and absent on that Day. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability to Allah and the insubstantial nature of the false claims made in the worldly life.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Cleaver of grain and date seeds. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless power and creativity of Allah. By describing Allah as the one who splits the grain and date seeds, it emphasizes His role as the initiator of life and growth from seemingly lifeless objects. Furthermore, by stating that He brings life from the dead and the dead from the living, the verse underscores the continuous and cyclical nature of life and death, controlled entirely by Allah. This passage serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the need for humans to recognize His authority and not be led astray from this fundamental truth.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: He is the One who breaks the dawn, and made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for calculation. That is the design of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and control of Allah over the natural world. It emphasizes His power in bringing about dawn, creating the night as a time for rest, and setting the sun and moon in precise orbits for timekeeping. This serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme authority and wisdom in the creation and maintenance of the universe.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And it is He who has made the stars for you so that you may be guided by them through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine purpose behind the creation of stars, emphasizing their role as navigational aids for humans in both terrestrial and maritime journeys. It underscores God's providence in supplying guidance and direction through natural phenomena. The verse also points to the meticulous detailing of signs by God, which are meant to be understood by those who possess knowledge and wisdom, indicating that the natural world is filled with guidance for those who seek to comprehend it.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And it is He who produced you from one soul and [gave you] a place of dwelling and of storage. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and unity of human creation, emphasizing that all humans come from a single soul, symbolizing the inherent equality and interconnectedness of all people. It also mentions the concepts of a temporary dwelling and a final resting place, perhaps referring to this life and the hereafter, urging reflection and understanding of the divine signs provided for those who are perceptive and seek knowledge.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We bring forth thereby the growth of all things. We bring out from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees, of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And We produce gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Look at its fruit when it yields and its ripening. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty and creativity in the natural world by emphasizing the process of how rain from the sky leads to the growth of various forms of vegetation. The detailed descriptions of different plants and fruits underscore the complexity and diversity of God's creation. By urging people to observe these natural phenomena, the verse serves as a reminder of the signs of God's existence and majesty, which are evident in the details of the natural world. It calls upon believers to reflect on these signs as evidence of divine power and wisdom.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they attribute to Allah partners - the jinn, while He has created them - and they falsely attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glorified and Exalted is He above (all) that they describe.
interpretation: This verse addresses the erroneous beliefs and practices of attributing partners to Allah, such as the jinn and claiming He has offspring, without any sound knowledge or evidence. It emphasizes the oneness and purity of Allah, asserting that He is far above and beyond these false attributions. The mention of glorification and exaltation underscores His perfection and the futility of associating any partners or likenesses with Him.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion? He created everything and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and transcendence of Allah. It rejects the idea that Allah could have a son, pointing out that having offspring necessitates a partner, which Allah does not have. It asserts that Allah is the Creator of everything and possesses complete knowledge of all things. The verse underscores Allah's majestic and unparalleled nature and His complete independence from creation.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him, and He is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It calls for exclusive worship and devotion to Him alone, recognizing that no other deity exists beside Him. The term 'Disposer of all things' indicates that Allah has complete authority and control over all matters, reinforcing the necessity of placing trust and reliance solely in Him.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transcendence and omniscience of Allah. It means that God's essence cannot be fully grasped or perceived by human senses or intellect, emphasizing His absolute uniqueness and incomparability. However, He is fully aware of and comprehends all things, including every detail of His creation. 'The Subtle' implies that His ways are beyond human comprehension, delicate, and intricate, while 'the Acquainted' denotes His complete and intimate knowledge of all existence.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever will see does so for the benefit of his soul, and whoever is blind [does harm] against it. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility in accepting or rejecting divine guidance. The enlightenment provided by the Lord is accessible to all, but each person's response is their own responsibility. Those who choose to see and follow the guidance do so for their own benefit, while those who ignore it harm only themselves. The Prophet Muhammad, as the messenger, is not responsible for ensuring that people accept the guidance; rather, his role is to convey the message.
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: Thus do We diversify the signs so that they might say, 'You have studied,’ and so that We may make it clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deliberate manner in which Allah presents His signs in various forms and contexts. This diversification serves multiple purposes: it challenges those who might dismiss the Prophet Muhammad's recitation as mere study or fabrication, and it aims to provide clarity and understanding to those who seek true knowledge. The audience is encouraged to reflect on the signs and recognize the divine wisdom behind them.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord - there is no deity except Him. And turn away from those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the divine teachings and revelations provided by Allah, acknowledging Him as the sole deity. It instructs believers to avoid engaging with or being influenced by those who practice polytheism or associate others with Allah in worship. The directive is clear: maintain firm faith in the Oneness of God and distance oneself from any form of idolatry.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated others with Him. And We have not made you a guardian over them, nor are you a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine will and human free will. It underscores that if Allah had willed, people would not have fallen into polytheism. It also clarifies the Prophet Muhammad's role, stating that he is not responsible for people's choices and actions. His duty is to convey the message, not to enforce belief. This reflects the broader theme of individual accountability and the limits of human control in guiding others towards faith.
orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse advises Muslims not to insult the deities or religious figures that others worship, as this could lead to reciprocal insults against Allah driven by ignorance and animosity. It emphasizes the principle of respect and tolerance for different beliefs. Further, it suggests that each community finds its own actions pleasing and justified, and ultimately, everyone will return to Allah who will judge their actions and inform them of the reality of their deeds. The verse underscores the importance of maintaining respect, avoiding unnecessary conflict, and trusting in Allah's ultimate judgment.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign were to come to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, 'The signs are only with Allah.' And what will make you perceive that even if it [sign] came, they would still not believe?
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demand miraculous signs as proof before they will believe. It highlights their insincerity, noting that even if the signs were provided, their hearts are so hardened that they would still not believe. It underscores that faith is not just about witnessing miracles but about a sincere openness to the truth. True belief comes from within and is fostered by God’s will and guidance, not merely through external signs.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: We will turn their hearts and their sight away, as they refused to believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of persistent disbelief and rejection of the divine message. When people repeatedly reject the truth and indulge in excessive wrongdoing, their hearts and perceptions are turned away from guidance, leading them to remain in a state of confusion and persistent wrongdoing. It underscores the spiritual consequence of continual denial and rebellion against divine guidance.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: Even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead spoke to them and We gathered all things before them, they would not believe unless Allah should will it. But most of them, [of that], are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubbornness and unwillingness of certain people to believe, despite the presence of undeniable signs and miracles. It underscores the principle that true faith comes from the will of Allah and suggests that intellectual or sensory proof alone is not sufficient for belief without divine guidance. Additionally, it highlights human ignorance and the limitation of understanding in recognizing the truth unless aided by divine will.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy—devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorated speech in delusion. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and that which they invent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that opposition to prophets is a consistent pattern throughout history, with adversaries coming from both humans and jinn who deceive and allure through embellished and misleading speech. However, it underscores the overarching divine will, implying that such opposition is allowed by Allah's command. This serves as a test and a means to delineate true believers. The verse also encourages patience and endurance, advising to leave these adversaries to their fabrications because their actions are ultimately under the control of Allah's wisdom and decree.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: So that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, that they may be satisfied with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the tendency of disbelievers to be attracted to and satisfied with erroneous beliefs or actions. Their rejection of the Hereafter leads them to follow falsehoods, ultimately resulting in their perpetuation of sinful behavior. It highlights the link between disbelief and moral corruption, as well as the accountability for one's actions.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: Shall I seek a judge other than Allah while it is He who has sent down to you the Book explained in detail? Those to whom We gave the Scripture know that it has been sent down from your Lord in truth. So do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance and judgment solely from Allah, who has provided a detailed and comprehensive scripture. It also affirms that the previous recipients of divine scriptures recognize the truth of the Qur'an's origin from Allah. Therefore, believers should not entertain any doubts about its divine source and guidance.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infallibility and unchangeability of God's words and promises. It reassures believers that God's judgments and decrees are always founded on truth and justice. It also highlights the omnipotence and omniscience of God, affirming that He is both all-hearing and all-knowing, fully aware of all things and ensuring the fulfillment of His divine will without any alteration.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow nothing but assumption, and they are but misjudging.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of blindly following the majority, emphasizing that most people may not necessarily be on the right path. It warns believers to be cautious and discerning in whom they follow, as many people base their actions and beliefs on conjecture and assumptions rather than on true knowledge and divine guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to seek truth and follow the guidance provided by Allah, rather than being swayed by the erroneous beliefs and practices of the masses.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ultimate knowledge and wisdom. It assures that Allah is fully aware of those who deviate from His path as well as those who are rightly guided. This implies that human judgments are limited, and only Allah can truly discern the states of people's faith and actions.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of invoking the name of Allah before consuming food. It serves as a reminder for the believers to maintain consciousness of Allah even in their daily acts, such as eating, and to follow the guidance provided by Him. This command also signifies a deeper level of faith and adherence to religious teachings, highlighting the spiritual and ethical aspects of dietary laws in Islam.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden you, excepting that to which you are compelled? But indeed, many lead [others] astray through their own desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord – He is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming what has been slaughtered in the name of Allah, highlighting the clarity provided by divine guidance on what is forbidden. It warns against following personal desires without proper knowledge, acknowledging that many people mislead others in this manner. Allah's superior knowledge of intentional violators is affirmed, ensuring accountability.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: Abandon open and secret sin. Indeed, those who commit sin will be recompensed for what they used to perpetrate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding both outward and hidden sins, urging believers to maintain inner and outer piety. It serves as a reminder that all sins, regardless of their visibility to others, are known to God and that those who engage in sinful actions will face consequences for their deeds. The verse underscores the concept of divine justice and moral accountability.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reverence for Allah in all aspects of life, including dietary practices. It emphasizes that consuming food not blessed in the name of Allah is considered sinful. The verse also serves as a warning against being swayed by those who challenge and debate religious commandments with the intent to lead believers astray. Obedience to such misguided influences equates to shirk, associating partners with Allah, which is the gravest of sins in Islam.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful metaphor comparing the state of a believer who has been spiritually revived by God's guidance to someone given life and light, enabling them to navigate through life with clarity and purpose. Conversely, it contrasts this with the disoriented state of disbelievers, who persist in their erroneous ways, finding comfort in their actions despite being engulfed in darkness. This comparison underscores the profound transformation and enlightenment that faith and divine guidance bring, while highlighting the persistent ignorance and self-deception of those who reject it.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And thus We have placed within every city its greatest criminals to conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in every community, there are influential individuals who engage in wrongdoings and plots. However, their scheming ultimately harms themselves, though they may not realize or comprehend the extent of this self-damage. The verse highlights the self-destructive nature of evil actions and serves as a reminder of the moral order where wrongdoing inevitably leads to negative consequences for the wrongdoers.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: When a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah.' Allah knows best where to place His message. Humiliation from Allah and severe punishment will befall the criminals for their plots.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and demands of some individuals who refused to believe in the divine message unless they received the same favors and signs as the prophets. It emphasizes that Allah, in His infinite wisdom, decides where and to whom His message should be given. Those who disrespect or defy this divine wisdom out of malice or deceit are warned of dire consequences, including disgrace and severe punishment. This serves as a reminder that God's decisions are based on profound wisdom and that rejecting His message arrogantly leads to severe retribution.
orig: وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته سيصيب الذين أجرموا صغار عند الله وعذاب شديد بما كانوا يمكرون

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide - He opens his breast to Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine control over guidance and misguidance. When Allah wills for someone to be rightly guided, He makes their heart open and receptive to Islam, symbolizing ease and acceptance. Conversely, for those whom Allah wills to mislead, He makes their chest tight and constrained, resembling the difficult and struggling feeling of ascending to the sky, indicating rejection and hardship in accepting faith. This signifies that guidance is a gift from Allah and misguidance a consequence of one's own rejection and disbelief, upon whom Allah decrees defilement as a result of their lack of faith.
orig: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And this is the path of your Lord, [leading] straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and straightforwardness of the path prescribed by Allah for His followers. It reassures believers that God's guidance is clear and well-defined. The detailing of the verses refers to the comprehensive and elaborate nature of the revelations in the Qur'an, aimed at guiding those who reflect and take heed, encouraging mindfulness and adherence to divine instructions.
orig: وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يذكرون

translation: For them will be the Home of Peace with their Lord, and He will be their protecting friend because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for the righteous who have acted upon their faith with good deeds. They are promised 'Dar al-Salam' (the Home of Peace) with Allah, signifying eternal peace and security in Paradise. The verse also emphasizes that Allah will be their protector and friend, a guardian who appreciates and acknowledges the sincere efforts of the believers. Their peaceful abode and close companionship with the Divine are portrayed as direct results of their good actions and righteousness in their earthly life.
orig: لهم دار السلام عند ربهم وهو وليهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: On the Day He will gather them all together [and say]: 'O company of jinn, you have misled many of mankind.' And their allies among mankind will say, 'Our Lord, we made use of each other, and we have [now] reached our term which You appointed for us.' He will say, 'The Fire is your residence, wherein you will abide eternally, except for what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the accountability of both jinn and humans on the Day of Judgement. It highlights the seduction and mutual exploitation between the two groups, demonstrating that both have taken advantage of each other in ways that diverged from righteous living. The verse emphasizes the inevitable consequence of their actions—eternal residence in the Fire—while also acknowledging Allah's ultimate wisdom and knowledge concerning their fate. The passage serves as a warning about the corrupting influence of negative associations and underscores the comprehensive justice of Allah.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice, wherein God permits wrongdoers to become allies and support one another as a consequence of their own actions and misdeeds. It implies that the interconnectedness of their transgressions leads to a collective accountability and consequence. This reflects the broader principle that the moral and ethical choices individuals and communities make will determine their relationships and the outcomes they face.
orig: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They will say, 'We bear witness against ourselves.' And the worldly life had deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses both jinn and humans, emphasizing the universality of the message sent by God through His messengers. It highlights the role of these messengers in delivering God's signs and warnings about the Day of Judgment. The verse illustrates the regret and self-realization of people and jinn who were deceived by the temporary allure of worldly life, causing them to reject the truth. In the end, they acknowledge their own failure and disbelief, bearing witness against themselves.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا شهدنا على أنفسنا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for injustice while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse conveys the principle of divine justice, highlighting that Allah does not punish people or destroy communities unjustly. Instead, there must be a clear wrongdoing or immorality, and the people must be aware of their actions. It emphasizes that ignorance and the lack of knowledge of one's sins are considered in divine judgment, thus ensuring that punishment is meted out fairly and justly.
orig: ذلك أن لم يكن ربك مهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها غافلون

translation: For all there are degrees [of recompense] for what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability. Each person's actions are weighed and evaluated, resulting in different levels of reward or punishment. It underscores God's omniscience, reminding believers that nothing escapes His knowledge. Everyone's deeds are recorded, and they will be compensated accordingly in the hereafter. This serves both as a warning to those who commit wrongdoings and as an encouragement for righteous behavior, knowing that God is fully aware of all actions.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the supreme power and independence of Allah, emphasizing that He is self-sufficient and merciful. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of human existence and the ease with which Allah can replace one generation with another, stressing that humans are ultimately dependent on His will and mercy for their existence and continuity.
orig: وربك الغني ذو الرحمة إن يشأ يذهبكم ويستخلف من بعدكم ما يشاء كما أنشأكم من ذرية قوم آخرين

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you are not able to cause failure [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of God's promises and the inevitability of their fulfillment. It underscores that humans cannot escape or hinder what God has decreed. The verse conveys a sense of divine power and the idea that God's plans are unstoppable and will come to pass regardless of human actions or resistance.
orig: إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position, [for] indeed, I am working; and you are going to know who will have succession in the home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: In this verse, God instructs the Prophet Muhammad to declare to his people that everyone should continue to act according to their principles and efforts, but ultimately, it will become clear who gains the final, favorable outcome in this world and the Hereafter. It emphasizes the futility of wrongdoing, underscoring that those who commit injustices will not achieve success. This serves as both a warning to the unjust and a reassurance to those striving for righteousness.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And they assign to Allah a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock, and say, 'This is for Allah': in their claim, 'and this is for our partners.' But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse addresses the misguided practices of polytheists who unjustly partition their resources, attributing portions to Allah and others to their false deities. It highlights their flawed logic and unjust practices, as the portion meant for their deities would not be given to Allah, whereas the portion for Allah would be redirected to their deities. This exposes their insincerity and the irrational basis of their religious judgments.
orig: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا فقالوا هذا لله بزعمهم وهذا لشركائنا فما كان لشركائهم فلا يصل إلى الله وما كان لله فهو يصل إلى شركائهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And thus, their so-called partners have made the killing of their children seem pleasing to many of the polytheists in order to lead them to ruin and confuse them in their religion. If Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and their fabrications.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive influence of false partners or deities worshipped by polytheists, who convince them to commit grievous acts such as killing their own children. The purpose behind these acts is to lead them towards destruction and to cause confusion about their faith. However, it is emphasized that such actions only occur with the permission of Allah. Therefore, the instruction given is to leave these individuals to their falsehoods and fabrications, indicating that their misguided actions are ultimately part of a divine will and plan, and it is not the duty of the believers to force them to change.
orig: وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ليردوهم وليلبسوا عليهم دينهم ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And they say, 'These are livestock and crops prohibited; none may eat from them except whom we will,' by their claim. And there are those camels whose backs are forbidden [by them], and those upon which the name of Allah is not mentioned – [all of this] is an invention about Him. He will punish them for what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the misguided claims and practices of some people who, out of their own fabrications, deem certain livestock and crops as forbidden for others except those they specify. They also create baseless restrictions regarding the usage of certain animals and neglect to mention Allah's name upon them, which contradicts the divinely ordained guidelines. Such actions are construed as falsehoods and fabrications against Allah, and they will be held accountable and punished for these unjustifiable fabrications and attributions they have made.
orig: وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر لا يطعمها إلا من نشاء بزعمهم وأنعام حرمت ظهورها وأنعام لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها افتراء عليه سيجزيهم بما كانوا يفترون

translation: And they say, 'What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females.' But if it is [born] dead, then they are all partners in it. He will punish them for their description; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses certain customs and superstitions among the pre-Islamic Arabs regarding the division of the produce and meat of cattle. They would unjustly claim certain portions exclusively for males and deny them to females, unless the animal was dead, in which case both could share. This practice is criticized as illogical and unfair, and it is indicated that Allah will hold them accountable for such baseless and discriminatory actions. The verse highlights that Allah's wisdom and knowledge encompass and rectify such misguided customs.
orig: وقالوا ما في بطون هذه الأنعام خالصة لذكورنا ومحرم على أزواجنا وإن يكن ميتة فهم فيه شركاء سيجزيهم وصفهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: They are lost who have killed their children foolishly without knowledge and have forbidden what Allah provided for them, inventing lies against Allah. They have gone astray and were never guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who, out of ignorance and irrational customs, used to kill their children and forbid lawful provisions given by Allah. It stresses that these people have fabricated falsehoods against Allah, have deviated from the right path, and are not among those who are rightly guided. The verse underscores the gravity of these acts and highlights the importance of adhering to divine guidance and knowledge rather than misguided cultural practices.
orig: قد خسر الذين قتلوا أولادهم سفها بغير علم وحرموا ما رزقهم الله افتراء على الله قد ضلوا وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And He is the one who created gardens, both trellised and untrellised, and date palms, and crops of different flavors, and olives, and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat from their fruit when they produce and give their due on the day of their harvest. But do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and abundance in God's creation, indicating His boundless mercy and sustenance provided to mankind. It encourages people to enjoy the produce of the earth but also to fulfill their social obligations by giving a share to the needy. Moreover, it admonishes against wastefulness and extravagance, promoting a balanced and mindful consumption of resources. This teaches a lesson in gratitude, responsibility, and temperance.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ جنات معروشات وغير معروشات والنخل والزرع مختلفا أكله والزيتون والرمان متشابها وغير متشابه كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: And of the cattle (are some) for burden and some for meat; eat of that which Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings Allah has bestowed upon humanity in the form of cattle, which serve multiple purposes such as carrying burdens and providing meat. It encourages believers to utilize these provisions gratefully and responsibly, and warns against following the deceptive paths of Satan, who is a manifest enemy dedicated to leading them astray from gratitude and righteousness.
orig: ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا كلوا مما رزقكم الله ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: Eight pairs: of sheep two, of goats two. Say, 'Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse is challenging the pagan customs which arbitrarily classified certain animals as lawful or unlawful to eat. It questions whether it is the male or female animals that are forbidden, or what their wombs contain, emphasizing the absurdity of these distinctions and urging them to provide evidence if their prohibitions are truthful. It highlights the importance of genuine knowledge over unsubstantiated traditions.
orig: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين نبئوني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And of the camels two, and of the cows two. Say, 'Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this? Then who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse questions the wrongful assertions made by some people regarding the prohibitions of certain animals’ meats without any divine basis. It challenges the notion by asking whether there is a prohibition on males, females, or what is in their wombs, while making it clear that this was not a commandment given by Allah. The rhetorical questions emphasize the baselessness of these claims and the severe injustice in attributing falsehoods to Allah, which leads to misguiding others. Ultimately, the verse asserts that Allah does not guide those who commit such wrongful acts.
orig: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين أم كنتم شهداء إذ وصاكم الله بهذا فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا ليضل الناس بغير علم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, 'I do not find within that which was revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse outlines specific dietary prohibitions in Islamic law, emphasizing that certain items are forbidden due to their inherent impurity or because they were dedicated to other than Allah. However, it also underscores the principle of necessity and divine compassion, permitting consumption under duress when no other options are available, demonstrating Allah's forgiveness and mercy in cases of genuine need.
orig: قل لا أجد في ما أوحي إلي محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن ربك غفور رحيم

translation: And to those who are Jews, We prohibited every animal that has claws; and of the cattle and the sheep, We prohibited to them the fat except what adheres to their backs or the entrails or what is mixed with a bone. That was their recompense for their rebellion, and indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse explains specific dietary restrictions imposed upon the Jews as a consequence of their unjust behavior and rebellion. It indicates that these prohibitions were a form of divine retribution. The verse also emphasizes the truthfulness and justice of God's decrees. Essentially, it serves as a reminder of the moral and spiritual consequences of disobedience and transgression.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم وإنا لصادقون

translation: But if they deny you, then say, 'Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy; but His punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad is instructed on how to respond to those who deny his message. He is to remind them of Allah's immense mercy, emphasizing that despite their rejection, Allah remains compassionate and merciful. However, the verse also serves as a solemn warning: Allah’s mercy does not negate His justice. Those who persist in their wrongdoing and criminal behavior cannot escape His punishment. This dual message underscores both the boundless mercy available to all and the inescapable consequences for persistent injustice and rebellion against divine commandments.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, 'If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him], nor would our forefathers, nor would we have prohibited anything.' Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, 'Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow not except assumption, and you are not but falsifying.'
interpretation: This verse addresses a common argument made by polytheists who justify their actions by claiming that if Allah had not willed it, they would not have engaged in shirk (associating partners with Allah) or prohibited what they did. The verse refutes this justification by noting that such excuses have been used by previous peoples who also faced punishment for their denial. It challenges the polytheists to present any concrete knowledge to support their claims, emphasizing that their beliefs are based on assumptions and falsehoods, rather than any factual evidence. The verse calls for a critical examination of inherited practices and encourages relying on true knowledge instead of conjecture.
orig: سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من شيء كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم حتى ذاقوا بأسنا قل هل عندكم من علم فتخرجوه لنا إن تتبعون إلا الظن وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون

translation: Say: With Allah is the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and decisive argument that belongs to Allah alone. It highlights the concept of divine will, indicating that if Allah had willed, He could have guided all of humanity. This underscores the notion of human free will and the belief that guidance is a privilege and a mercy granted by Allah. It serves to remind believers of Allah's supreme wisdom and the importance of seeking His guidance.
orig: قل فلله الحجة البالغة فلو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: Say, 'Produce your witnesses who will testify that Allah has forbidden this.' But if they testify, do not testify with them; and do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim that Allah has prohibited certain things without evidence. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to ask for witnesses to their claims. However, even if they produce witnesses, the Prophet is told not to align himself with them. This guidance highlights the importance of not being swayed by false testimonies and not following those who distort Allah’s signs or disbelieve in the Hereafter and associate partners with Allah. It underscores the necessity of steadfastness in true faith and in adherence to divine revelation over human whims and fabricated laws.
orig: قل هلم شهداءكم الذين يشهدون أن الله حرم هذا فإن شهدوا فلا تشهد معهم ولا تتبع أهواء الذين كذبوا بآياتنا والذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وهم بربهم يعدلون

translation: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. He commands that you do not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities—what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason.'
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah communicated through the Prophet Muhammad, outlining a series of ethical and moral guidelines for the believers. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism by prohibiting any form of association with Allah. It underscores the significance of treating parents with kindness and compassion. The verse also addresses socio-economic concerns by forbidding the killing of children due to poverty, assuring believers that Allah provides sustenance for all. It cautions against engaging in any form of immoral behavior, whether overt or covert. Additionally, it enjoins the sanctity of life, barring the taking of life except in justifiable circumstances. The overarching message is one of wisdom and reason, urging believers to reflect and adhere to these divine commandments.
orig: قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Do not come near the orphan's property, except to improve it, until they reach maturity. Give full measure and weight with justice – We do not burden any soul beyond what it can bear. When you speak, be just, even if it concerns a close relative. Fulfill the covenant of Allah. This is what He enjoins upon you so that you might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical treatment of orphans and their property, urging believers to act only in ways that benefit the orphan until they can manage their affairs. It also calls for honesty in trade, fairness in speech, and adherence to divine promises. These instructions aim to cultivate a sense of justice, responsibility, and remembrance of Allah’s commands among the believers.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى وبعهد الله أوفوا ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And, [moreover], this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the path outlined by Allah, which is described as straight and true. It warns against following alternative paths that deviate from this divine guidance, as doing so would lead to division and confusion, taking believers away from the righteous way. The verse concludes by highlighting that this command is given so that believers may attain piety and righteousness, indicating the ultimate spiritual and moral benefits of following Allah's path.
orig: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, perfect for the one who does good, and an explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy so that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive and perfect nature of the scripture given to Moses (the Torah). It emphasizes that the scripture was detailed, providing guidance and mercy, to encourage faith in the eventual meeting with God. The reference to it being 'perfect for the one who does good' suggests that the scripture is most beneficial and fully realized when applied by those who practice righteousness. The overall message is about the completeness of divine guidance and its ultimate purpose to reinforce faith.
orig: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب تماما على الذي أحسن وتفصيلا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة لعلهم بلقاء ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and blessed nature of the Qur'an. It urges people to follow its guidance and to be conscious of Allah’s commandments. By adhering to this path, individuals are promised mercy. This reflects the Qur'an’s role as a source of moral and spiritual direction, encouraging adherence to its teachings as a means to achieve divine compassion and mercy.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: So you will not say, 'The Scripture was sent down only to two groups before us, but we were unaware of their teachings.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the universality of God's message, highlighting that revelation has been sent to multiple communities throughout history. It addresses any potential excuse that people might use to justify ignorance of divine guidance by arguing that past scriptures were exclusive to certain groups. The verse emphasizes that no community is left without guidance and it is the individual's responsibility to seek and understand it.
orig: أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا وإن كنا عن دراستهم لغافلين

translation: Or you [people] may say, 'If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they.' So there has [now] come to you a clear evidence from your Lord and a guidance and mercy. Then who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst of punishment for their having turned away.
interpretation: This verse addresses the excuses some people might use for not following divine guidance, suggesting they would have embraced it had it come to them directly. However, it affirms that Allah has indeed provided clear evidence, guidance, and mercy. The verse critically questions who could be more unjust than those who not only reject Allah’s signs but also turn away from them, indicating that severe punishment awaits such individuals due to their deliberate avoidance and denial.
orig: أو تقولوا لو أنا أنزل علينا الكتاب لكنا أهدى منهم فقد جاءكم بينة من ربكم وهدى ورحمة فمن أظلم ممن كذب بآيات الله وصدف عنها سنجزي الذين يصدفون عن آياتنا سوء العذاب بما كانوا يصدفون

translation: Are they waiting for the angels to come to them, or for your Lord to come, or for some of the signs of your Lord to come? The day that some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or had not earned any good through its faith. Say, 'Wait; we too are waiting.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine judgment and the futility of last-minute repentance. It stresses that waiting for supernatural signs or divine intervention as a precondition for faith is a flawed approach. When certain unmistakable signs of the divine manifest, the opportunity for sincere belief will have passed, making late conversions or superficial acts of faith worthless. It serves as a stern reminder to maintain faith and good deeds consistently, rather than delaying spiritual commitment.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي ربك أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك يوم يأتي بعض آيات ربك لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا قل انتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects—you, [O Muhammad], are not [associated] with them in anything. Their affair is only [left] to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity in faith and condemns divisions within the religious community. It communicates that Prophet Muhammad is not aligned with those who create sects and divide the religion. The judgment and consequences of their actions are left to Allah, who will ultimately inform them of their deeds. It calls for maintaining the unity and integrity of the faith, as dissension leads to discord and weakens the community.
orig: إن الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا لست منهم في شيء إنما أمرهم إلى الله ثم ينبئهم بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will receive ten times as much, and whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed only with its equivalent; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and justice of Allah. Good deeds are multiplied tenfold, showing His generosity and encouragement for individuals to strive towards righteousness. On the other hand, evil deeds are only recompensed with their equivalent, demonstrating fairness and ensuring that people are not punished beyond their due. The final part of the verse reassures that no one will be wronged, reinforcing trust in divine justice and the moral balance maintained by Allah.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion - the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not among those who associated others with Allah.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance received by the Prophet, affirming that the path he follows is one of righteousness and monotheism, in line with the pure faith of Prophet Abraham. It underscores the distinction between true monotheistic worship and polytheism, highlighting that true guidance is firmly rooted in the rejection of associating partners with Allah, reflecting the unwavering monotheism that characterized Abraham's faith.
orig: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
