translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to engage in combat with the non-believers who are near them and to demonstrate firmness and strength in their demeanor. It emphasizes the importance of standing firm in the defense of their faith and community. The verse reassures the believers that Allah's support is with those who are pious and righteous, urging them to maintain their integrity and fear of God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, there are some among them who say, 'Which of you has this increased in faith?' As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing reactions among people when a new surah (chapter) of the Qur'an is revealed. It contrasts the skepticism of some, who question the impact of the revelation on others' faith, with the believers' experience. For true believers, the revelation strengthens their faith and fills them with joy, underscoring the reinforcing power of divine guidance on those who are receptive to it.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: But those in whose hearts is disease, it has only increased them in evil upon their evil, and they died while they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals whose hearts are corrupt and filled with hypocrisy or disbelief. Instead of benefiting from divine guidance, their inner sickness causes them to spiral deeper into misguidance and sin. Their rejection of faith ultimately leads to their demise as disbelievers, illustrating that their diseases of the heart prevented them from recognizing and embracing the truth.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice? Yet they neither repent nor do they take heed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the continuous tests and trials that people face as part of their lives. The fact that these tests occur regularly highlights the importance of self-reflection and repentance. It emphasizes the need for people to use these experiences as opportunities to turn back to God and to remember His guidance, rather than ignoring the lessons that these tests are meant to impart.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, they look at each other, [as if saying], 'Does anyone see you?' and then they dismiss themselves. Allah has dismissed their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those individuals who, when a chapter of the Qur'an is revealed, respond with skepticism and disregard, glancing at each other as if questioning whether they are being observed. Their subsequent dismissal of the message reflects their internal rejection and lack of comprehension. Allah's act of turning their hearts away is a consequence of their arrogance and unwillingness to grasp the divine message, symbolizing a spiritual blindness and a resistance to faith.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the empathetic and compassionate nature of the Prophet Muhammad towards his followers. His deep concern and care for the well-being and guidance of his community are evident, depicting his role not just as a messenger but as someone who feels their struggles and strives for their welfare. The description of his emotional connection with the believers underscores his dedication and the profound sense of responsibility he carries for them.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, [O Muhammad], say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'
interpretation: This verse provides reassurance and guidance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the face of rejection or opposition. It emphasizes complete reliance on Allah alone, highlighting His supreme authority and the futility of seeking dependence on anything or anyone else. It underscores the importance of steadfast faith and trust in Allah, reminding believers of His ultimate power and sovereignty over all things.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The opening of this verse with the disjointed letters 'Alif, Lam, Ra' suggests a divine and mysterious aspect of the revelation. It highlights the significance and solemnity of the message that follows. The reference to the 'Wise Book' underscores the Qur'an's role as a source of profound guidance and wisdom, emphasizing its divine origin and unerring nature. It calls on the reader to recognize the authority and sacred knowledge contained within the scripture.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Is it a wonder to the people that We have sent revelation to a man from among themselves, (instructing him) to warn the people and give good news to those who believe that they will have a precedence of honor with their Lord? Yet the disbelievers say, 'Indeed, this is an obvious magician.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and astonishment of people when a prophet arises from among them. It highlights that divine messages are sent to a human messenger to warn and bring glad tidings. The verse also underscores the rejection from disbelievers, who dismiss the prophet's message by labeling him as a magician. This reveals the recurring theme of denial and the struggle prophets face in delivering God's message amidst disbelief.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He arranges each matter; there is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, highlighting His ability to govern all affairs from a position of supreme authority. The reference to Allah establishing Himself above the Throne indicates His control and management over the cosmos. It underscores the concept that intercession is not possible without His permission, reinforcing the need for direct worship and devotion to Him. The verse serves as a reminder to recognize and reflect on His sovereignty and to engage in sincere worship.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] true. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it, that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse reminds humanity that their ultimate return is to Allah, affirming the certainty of God's promise. It emphasizes God's sovereignty in creation and resurrection, highlighting that the purpose of this cycle is to dispense justice. Believers who engage in righteous deeds will be rewarded fairly, whereas disbelievers will face severe punishment due to their persistent denial of the truth.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account (of time). Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deliberate creation and design of the universe by Allah, highlighting the functional differences between the sun and the moon. The sun is described as a source of direct light, while the moon's light is reflective. By setting the moon in phases, Allah provides a means for humans to measure time and calendars. The verse underlines that every aspect of creation is purposeful (created 'in truth'), and encourages reflection and understanding of these signs as a testament to divine wisdom for those who seek knowledge.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the existence of clear signs of Allah’s power and wisdom in the natural phenomena of day and night changes and in the creations within the heavens and the earth. For those who are mindful and conscious of Allah (those who fear Him), these signs are evident and serve as reminders of His greatness and the importance of living in accordance with His guidance.
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us, and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who are indifferent to the prospect of encountering God in the Hereafter and have found complacency and satisfaction solely in worldly life. Their focus on temporal pleasures and comforts has led them to be oblivious to the signs and revelations of God. It highlights a spiritual negligence and warns of the consequences of being detached from divine guidance and eternal realities.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Their abode will be the Fire because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the punishment of Hellfire is a consequence of the evil deeds committed by individuals. It underscores the idea of accountability and recompense, implying that those who engage in wrongful actions and fail to seek repentance or change their ways will ultimately face dire consequences in the afterlife. The emphasis on 'what they used to earn' points to the concept of moral responsibility and the direct link between one's actions and their outcomes in the divine justice system.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them by their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the promise of divine guidance and eternal reward for the believers who combine faith with righteous actions. It emphasizes that true faith must be accompanied by good deeds, and in return, Allah promises to guide them to paradise, a place described as having rivers flowing beneath, symbolizing continuous sustenance and eternal bliss.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their call therein will be, 'Exalted are You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.' And the last of their call will be, 'Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds!'
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the inhabitants of Paradise. It emphasizes their constant state of glorifying Allah, exchanging greetings of peace, and concluding by expressing gratitude and acknowledging Allah's sovereignty. It reflects the ultimate tranquility and fulfillment experienced by those in Paradise, where their every utterance and interaction mirrors their contentment and reverence for Allah.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil (they invoke) as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended for them. But We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and wisdom by contrasting human impatience and short-sightedness with divine forbearance. If Allah were to respond to people's wrongful and hasty desires for harm as swiftly as He grants their requests for good, their lives would quickly end due to the consequences of their own actions. However, Allah, in His wisdom, allows time for reflection and repentance, thereby granting people opportunities to turn away from their misdeeds. Meanwhile, those who deny the afterlife and disregard divine accountability are left to persist in their disobedience and confusion, wandering aimlessly without realizing the imminent consequences of their actions.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: When distress touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, sitting, or standing. But when We remove his distress, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us to remove any distress that touched him. Thus it is made pleasing to the transgressors that which they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human tendency to turn to God in moments of distress and hardship, seeking His help and relief. However, once the distress is alleviated, people often forget their dependence on God and their previous supplications. This forgetfulness and ingratitude highlight the moral failing and spiritual negligence seen in many individuals, especially the ones who excessively indulge in wrongful deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of consistent faith and gratitude towards God in both good times and bad.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by past nations who engaged in injustice and wrongdoing. Despite being provided with clear signs and guidance through their messengers, these communities chose not to believe. It highlights the principle that those who persist in criminal behavior and reject divine guidance are ultimately held accountable and face destruction. The historical precedents serve as warnings for present and future generations to adhere to justice and righteousness to avoid similar fates.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them so that We may observe how you will do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of human existence and leadership. It signifies that one generation succeeds another by the will of Allah, who observes the actions and decisions of the successors. It serves as a reminder of human responsibility and accountability in managing earthly affairs, encouraging reflection on how one utilizes the opportunities and resources bestowed by Allah in alignment with His guidance.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, ‘Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it.’ Say, ‘It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.’
interpretation: This verse addresses the resistance and demands of disbelievers who, upon hearing the clear signs of Allah’s revelations, reject them and challenge the Prophet to bring a different Qur'an or alter it. The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to respond by declaring his inability to alter the divine revelation because he is bound to follow what is revealed to him. This underscores the idea that the Qur'an is a divine and unchangeable text, and altering it is against the Prophet’s mission and would result in severe punishment from Allah. The verse also reinforces the concept that revelation stands above human desires and whims.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had lived among you a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to tell the people that if it had been God's will, he would not have recited the Qur'an to them, nor would they have known of it. The verse also highlights that the Prophet had lived among them for a long period before the revelation, implying they already knew his character and truthfulness. Therefore, they should use their reason to recognize the divine source of the message he is delivering.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severe wrongdoing of those who falsely attribute lies to Allah or reject His revelations. It emphasizes the grave injustice in such actions and underscores that those who engage in these acts of deception and denial will not attain success. The term 'wrongdoers' (mujrimoon) here signifies individuals who persist in sin and rebellion against divine guidance.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse addresses the flawed logic of idol worshippers who turn to false gods, believing these intermediaries can influence divine favor. The verse challenges their baseless claims by asserting Allah's comprehensive knowledge, which they dare to contradict. It emphasizes Allah's transcendence and the futility of associating partners with Him, thereby reaffirming the need for direct worship and reliance on Allah alone.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind was not but one community [united in religion], but [then] they differed. And if not for a word that proceeded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them immediately concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humanity originally existed as a unified community, perhaps in belief or purpose, but eventually diverged into differing factions or beliefs. The subsequent differences among people are part of their free will and the trials in life permitted by God. The 'word that proceeded from your Lord' refers to God's decree or predestination that allows for human life to unfold with these differences, often as a test of faith and moral character. Without such divine allowance, these disputes among humanity would have been resolved immediately by divine judgment, rather than being part of the earthly experience.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: They say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, the unseen belongs to Allah, so wait. Indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the demand of disbelievers for a miraculous sign from the Prophet as proof of his prophethood. The response provided emphasizes that knowledge of the unseen, including the occurrence of miracles, is within the exclusive domain of Allah. It also implies that humans must have patience and faith in Allah's wisdom and timing, as both the believers and the Prophet are reminded to wait for Allah's decree.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold! They devise a plot against Our verses. Say, 'Allah is swifter in planning.' Indeed, Our messengers record that which you plot.
interpretation: This verse addresses human nature and how people often react after experiencing hardship followed by relief. It highlights the tendency of some to become ungrateful or even scheming against divine guidance once they find themselves in a better situation. The passage serves as a reminder that Allah's plans are more precise and swift than human machinations. Moreover, it emphasizes accountability, as the actions and schemes of people are recorded by divine messengers, ensuring that nothing escapes divine judgment.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: He it is who enables you to travel by land and sea, until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a favorable wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a tempestuous wind and the waves come upon them from every side and they think that they are surrounded. They call upon Allah sincerely, devoting their faith to Him alone, 'If You save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to remember and turn to Allah sincerely during times of extreme distress and danger. It signifies how humans might often take blessings for granted when conditions are favorable, but in times of crisis, they revert to genuine faith and supplication. The verse highlights the importance of acknowledging and maintaining one's faith and gratitude towards Allah, not only in distressing times but consistently, reflecting the deeper spiritual lesson of steadfastness and sincere devotion.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, [being merely] the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the behavior of those who, after being saved from distress by Allah, revert to committing injustices and transgressions on Earth. It serves as a reminder that such wrongful acts only harm the individuals themselves, despite their pursuit of worldly gains. Ultimately, it underscores the accountability before Allah in the Hereafter, where every action will be judged and each person will be informed of their deeds.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The example of the life of this world is but like rain which We have sent down from the sky that the plants of the earth absorb - [those] from which men and livestock eat - until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified and its people suppose that they have capability over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse draws an analogy between the transient nature of the worldly life and rain that nurtures the plants, which eventually wither away. It demonstrates the fleeting beauty of worldly possessions and accomplishments. When people become overly confident in their ability to control their circumstances and environment, divine intervention can abruptly change their situation, rendering their previous state almost nonexistent. This is a reminder to reflect on the temporary nature of worldly life and the importance of spiritual mindfulness and awareness of God's omnipotence and the signs He provides.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's invitation to a state of eternal peace, which can be understood as paradise or a harmonious life led by divine guidance. The 'straight path' implies the righteous way of life prescribed by God, indicating that divine guidance is a selective grace bestowed upon those whom God chooses. This underscores the themes of divine mercy and the importance of following the path of righteousness as decreed by Allah for true peace and fulfillment.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and extra. No darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. Those are companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who do good deeds, promising them the best of rewards and even more beyond their expectations. Their reward includes eternal life in Paradise, free from any form of disgrace or hardship. It highlights the concept of divine justice and mercy, reassuring believers that their righteous actions will be met with abundant and everlasting blessings.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: But those who have earned [blame for] evil do a reward of like [evil] and humiliation will cover them. They will have from Allah no protector. It will be as if their faces are covered with pieces of the night – so dark [are they]. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who engage in sinful deeds. It emphasizes the principle of justice, where the recompense for evil actions will be equivalent to the offense. The imagery of darkness and the absence of a protector from Allah highlight the severity and isolation the wrongdoers will face. The eternal nature of their punishment in Hell underscores the importance of righteous conduct and the dire consequences of moral transgressions.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And [warn of] the Day when We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, '[Remain in] your place, you and your partners.' Then We will separate them, and their 'partners' will say, 'You did not used to worship us.'
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered by Allah. It specifically addresses those who committed shirk (associating partners with Allah), highlighting that they and their supposed partners in worship (idols or other deities) will be separated. The so-called partners will then disavow any connection with their worshippers, denying that they commanded or desired such worship. This reveals the futility and falsehood of associating others with Allah and underscores the ultimate accountability and truth that will be established in the hereafter.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: But Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you. We were certainly unaware of your worship [of us].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate witness to all actions and intentions among people. It underscores the ignorance of the believers about the idol worship practices of others, indicating their absolute detachment and disapproval of such practices. The verse serves to highlight that only Allah's testimony and judgment are relevant and sufficient.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There, every soul will experience [the consequences of] what it did in the past, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and lost from them will be what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine justice and accountability in the Hereafter. Every individual will face the outcomes of their deeds and no falsehoods or fabrications they relied on will help them. It emphasizes the ultimate return to Allah, who is the true Master and Judge, underscoring the futility of deceit and the inevitability of truth.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who owns hearing and sight, and who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living, and who arranges [every] matter?' They will say, 'Allah.' So say, 'Then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse calls upon people to reflect on the sources of their sustenance and the natural processes around them, affirming that these are controlled by a higher power, Allah. It highlights the divine control over life and death, as well as the divine regulation of the universe. The rhetorical question it poses—'Then will you not fear Him?'—serves as a reminder for people to be conscious of their duty to Allah, encouraging mindfulness and reverence towards Him.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. So what is there after the truth except error? How are you then averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and authority of Allah as the one true Lord. It makes a compelling argument that there is no reality or path that can lead to the truth except acknowledging and worshipping Allah. Any diversion from this truth is deemed as misguidance and error, questioning how one can be turned away from such evident truth and fall into misguidance.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus the Word of your Lord has come true against those who rebel, that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of God's decree concerning those who persist in rebellious and sinful behavior. It highlights the spiritual blindness and obstinacy of those who have knowingly chosen to reject faith. The phrase 'the Word of your Lord has come true' signifies the fulfillment of God's promise and warning against the unbelievers who have continuously turned away from guidance. Therefore, their disbelief is not a random occurrence but a consequence of their consistent defiance and corruption.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Is there any of your partners who begins creation and then repeats it?' Say, 'Allah begins creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the nature of creation and resurrection. It questions the belief in partners or idols having divine attributes by challenging if any of them possess the ability to initiate creation and bring it back to life. The verse then affirms that only Allah has the power to both create and resurrect, highlighting His unique and supreme power. It concludes by expressing astonishment at how people can be misled into believing otherwise despite this clear distinction.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Are there any of your partners who guide to the truth?' Say, 'Allah guides to the truth. Then is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who guides not unless he is guided? Then what is [wrong] with you - how do you judge?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the logic of following those who have no intrinsic guidance abilities compared to the divine guidance of Allah. It underscores the superiority of Allah’s guidance and calls into question the rationale of following anyone or anything else. The rhetoric questions at the end emphasize the inconsistency and irrational nature of choosing other forms of guidance over Allah's perfect and direct guidance.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them do not follow except assumption. Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of many people to rely on conjecture and assumption rather than concrete evidence or truth. It serves as a reminder that assumptions and speculations cannot replace the truth or change reality. Additionally, it emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the actions and inner workings of individuals, indicating that one cannot hide behind false pretenses or assumptions in the eyes of the divine.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And it was not [possible] for this Qur'an to be produced by other than Allah, but [it is] a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the [former] Scripture, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it could not have been fabricated by anyone other than Allah. It also emphasizes that the Qur'an confirms previous revelations and provides an extensive, clear explanation of the prior Scriptures. The verse reassures believers that the Qur'an is undoubtedly from the Lord of all existence, thereby reinforcing its authenticity and trustworthiness.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Say, 'Then bring forth a surah like it and call upon for assistance whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skeptics who claim that Prophet Muhammad fabricated the Qur’an. It challenges them to produce even a single chapter comparable to the Qur’an, highlighting the divine origin and unmatched eloquence of the text. It implies that if they are truthful in their claims, they should be able to enlist help from anyone other than Allah to achieve this. The verse underscores the impossibility of replicating the Qur’an’s unique literary and spiritual qualities, serving as proof of its divine authenticity.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But they have denied that which they have not encompassed in knowledge and whose interpretation has not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of people to reject divine messages without fully understanding them. It highlights that this denial is often based on ignorance and a lack of comprehension of the deeper wisdom behind the revelations. The verse draws a parallel with past communities who similarly rejected prophetic messages and faced dire consequences. The instruction to 'observe' serves as a warning and a prompt for reflection on the fate of those who acted unjustly and rejected the truth, encouraging the audience to learn from history and avoid repeating the same mistakes.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing responses to divine messages among people; some accept and believe, while others reject. It underscores that God is fully aware of the true nature and intentions of those who oppose or seek to corrupt the truth, emphasizing divine omniscience and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: But if they deny you, [O Muhammad], say, 'For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and accountability. It underlines that each person is responsible for their own actions and choices. If people reject the message of the Prophet, he is instructed to remind them that his actions and adherence to the divine message are his own responsibility, while their actions and disbelief are their own responsibility. There is a clear separation between the Prophet’s mission and the choices of those who reject it, highlighting the principle of personal accountability in Islam.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but can you make the deaf hear even though they do not understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge faced by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in conveying the message of Islam to those who are metaphorically 'deaf' and 'unintelligent.' Despite their physical ability to hear, their hearts and minds are closed off to understanding and accepting the truth. The verse illustrates the futility of trying to guide those who are stubbornly resistant to enlightenment, emphasizing that true comprehension and acceptance must come willingly from within.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they cannot see?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the challenge of guiding people who are spiritually blind. It underscores that some individuals, despite witnessing clear signs and receiving guidance, remain unable to perceive the truth due to their spiritual blindness. The verse emphasizes the limitations of human effort in guiding others and suggests that divine intervention is necessary for true enlightenment.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who are wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of Allah, asserting that He does not inflict injustice upon anyone. Instead, it is human actions, choices, and behaviors that lead to their own harm or suffering. The verse serves as a reminder for individuals to take responsibility for their own deeds and recognize that the consequences arise from their own actions rather than divine unfairness.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: On the Day He gathers them, it will be as if they had not stayed in the world except for an hour of the day, getting to know each other. Those who denied the meeting with Allah will have certainly lost, and they were not guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of the Afterlife. It portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment of clarity where the illusion of time in this world becomes apparent, leading to the realization that life was fleeting. It highlights the regret and loss of those who denied the reality of meeting Allah, emphasizing the consequences of their lack of guidance and disbelief.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you in death, to Us is their return; then God is witness over what they do.
interpretation: This verse indicates that whether the Prophet Muhammad witnesses the fulfillment of divine promises and warnings in his lifetime or not, ultimately, everyone will return to God. God is the ultimate judge and witness to all actions, and He will hold everyone accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes the certainty of divine justice and the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal principle that every community receives guidance through a prophet or messenger sent by God. It underscores the concept of divine justice, ensuring that judgment will be fair and unbiased, with no one being wronged. When their messenger has conveyed God’s message and the time for reckoning has come, justice will be served equitably among all people.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and doubt of those who question the promise of the Hereafter or the coming of the Day of Judgement. It highlights their challenge to the prophetic message, demanding to know the exact timing of divine fulfilment, reflecting a lack of faith and an attitude of disbelief.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'I have no power to bring benefit or harm to myself except as Allah wills. For every nation is a time; when their time comes, they cannot delay it by a single hour nor advance it.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete dependency of all beings on Allah's will, highlighting that even the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not have control over his own benefit or harm, except by the will of Allah. It underscores the concept that every nation and individual has a predetermined lifespan, and once their appointed time arrives, it cannot be postponed or hastened. This serves as a reminder of the divine decree and ultimate sovereignty of Allah over the affairs of life and death.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day, for which aspect of it would the criminals be impatient?'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who persist in wrongdoing and mock the idea of divine retribution. It challenges them to reflect on their impatience for punishment as if it is something trivial. The verse underscores the folly and arrogance of such people, highlighting that divine punishment can come at any time, whether day or night, unexpectedly and inevitably, and it would be wise for the wrongdoers to reconsider their stance and seek repentance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Is it only now, when it has come to pass, that you believe in it? [How late!] And you used to [mockingly] ask for this to be hastened!
interpretation: This verse addresses those who, despite having had ample warnings and opportunities to believe, only come to faith when confronted with the reality of the promised event. It serves as a critique of the insincere and mocking attitude of those who dismiss divine warnings and only realize their errors when it's too late for their belief to be of any use. The verse implores people to respond genuinely and promptly to divine messages rather than waiting until the consequences are evident.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who did wrong, 'Taste the eternal punishment! Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the wrongdoers, emphasizing that the punishment they face is a direct consequence of their actions. The usage of 'eternal punishment' signifies the gravity and permanence of their retribution. It serves as a reminder of the principle of divine justice, where individuals are held accountable and receive recompense strictly based on their deeds.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, 'Is it true?' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it is true. And you will not cause failure [to Allah].'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is being questioned by disbelievers who are skeptical about the Day of Judgment and the truthfulness of the revelations he brought. They sarcastically ask if the prophecy about the Day of Judgment is real. The command to say 'By my Lord, it is true' emphasizes the certainty and unwavering truth of the prophecy. The latter part of the verse assures that no matter their disbelief or attempts to refute the truth, they cannot escape or hinder God's decree. This reinforces the concept of accountability and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: If every soul that wronged had all that is on earth, it would offer it as ransom. And they will conceal their remorse when they see the punishment, and judgment will be made between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound regret that wrongdoers will feel on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the futility of material wealth in the face of divine justice. Even if the wrongdoers possessed everything on earth, they would willingly give it all up to avoid the punishment. The verse also highlights the inevitability and fairness of God's judgment, assuring that everyone will receive what they deserve, without any injustice.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is the truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and the earth, signifying His ultimate authority and control. It asserts the certainty and truthfulness of Allah's promise, indicating that whatever He decrees will undoubtedly come to pass. However, it also highlights a common human shortcoming: a lack of awareness or comprehension of this fundamental truth. This underscores the need for faith and knowledge in understanding and accepting the divine truth.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate sovereignty of God over life and death, emphasizing that all living beings owe their existence and eventual return to Him. It serves as a reminder of God's supreme power and the inevitable nature of human mortality and accountability in the afterlife.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses all of humanity, emphasizing the comprehensive nature of divine revelation. It highlights that the messages from God serve multiple essential functions: offering moral and spiritual guidance, providing healing and comfort for the human heart and soul, and bestowing mercy specifically upon those who believe. The verse underscores the holistic impact of divine words on the well-being of individuals and communities, stressing their importance in leading a righteous and fulfilling life.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, 'In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to find joy and satisfaction in the blessings and mercy bestowed by Allah rather than in material wealth and possessions. It emphasizes the superiority of spiritual fulfillment and divine grace over worldly gains, urging individuals to prioritize and celebrate their connection with the divine.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, 'Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision, of which you have made some lawful and some unlawful?' Say, 'Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or are you inventing [something] about Allah?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the wrongful practice of people arbitrarily deeming certain provisions permissible or forbidden according to their own desires rather than divine guidance. It challenges them by asking whether their decisions have divine sanction or if they are fabricating lies against Allah. The verse underscores the importance of adhering strictly to God's commandments in determining what is lawful (halal) and unlawful (haram), emphasizing that divine laws cannot be overridden by human whims or traditions.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what do those who invent falsehood about Allah think on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the grave sin of fabricating lies against Allah, emphasizing the severe consequences such actions will entail on the Day of Judgment. It calls into question what those who commit this transgression believe their fate will be when they face divine accountability. The verse also highlights Allah’s immense generosity and mercy towards humanity, contrasting it with the ingratitude exhibited by the majority of people. This underscores the ethical and moral imperative for truthfulness and gratitude in one’s relationship with the Divine.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And you are not engaged in any matter or recite any of the Qur'an, and you do not do any deed but We are witness over you when you engage in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heavens or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is constantly aware of all actions, whether they are small or large, and nothing is hidden from His knowledge. It reassures believers that their deeds are observed and recorded by Allah, encouraging mindfulness and sincerity in their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, indicating that everything is within His purview and meticulously documented.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Unquestionably, for the allies of Allah there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status of the 'allies of Allah,' indicating that those who are close to God, and live their lives in alignment with His guidance, are granted a sense of security and peace. They are assured protection from fear and freedom from sorrow, reflecting their firm faith and reliance on Allah. It highlights the spiritual and emotional well-being granted to true believers.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who have believed and were fearing Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights two key qualities of true believers: faith in Allah and a consciousness of Him that manifests as piety or mindfulness of His commandments. It's a reminder that belief is not merely a declaration but is coupled with actions that demonstrate reverence and fear of Allah. This combination of faith and piety forms the foundation of a righteous life in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them are glad tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: This verse affirms that true believers will receive good news both in this life and the next, highlighting the unwavering and unchangeable nature of Allah's words and promises. It emphasizes that adherence to faith and righteousness leads to ultimate success and salvation, which is described as the greatest achievement one can attain.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And do not be grieved by what they say. Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad and by extension to all believers. It advises not to be distressed by the words or accusations from others, emphasizing that ultimate honor and power rest solely with Allah. This underscores divine awareness and justice, pointing out that Allah is fully aware of all sayings and actions, and He possesses complete knowledge and understanding of every situation. Hence, believers are encouraged to find solace and strength in their faith, trusting in Allah's supreme authority and wisdom.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not actually follow [His] partners. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all beings in the heavens and on earth belong solely to Allah. It criticizes those who worship others besides Allah, stating that they are not truly following any divine partners but rather are following baseless assumptions and falsehoods. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate authority and exclusivity of Allah's divinity, urging believers to refrain from associating partners with Him.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: It is He who made for you the night to rest in and the day giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deliberate design in the alternation of night and day by Allah. The night is created for rest and recuperation, while the day is designed for activity and seeing the world around us. This systematic and purposeful alternation serves as a sign of divine wisdom and mercy for those who attentively listen and reflect. It invites contemplation and recognition of Allah's blessings and meticulous creation, urging humans to acknowledge and be grateful for these signs.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, 'Allah has begotten a son.' Glory be to Him! He is self-sufficient! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Do you have any authority for this claim? Do you say about Allah what you do not know?
interpretation: This verse addresses a common misconception, specifically refuting the claim that Allah has begotten a son. It emphasizes Allah's transcendence, self-sufficiency, and sovereignty over all creation. By questioning the authority and knowledge behind such a claim, it highlights the importance of speaking truthfully about divine matters and recognizing the limitations of human understanding regarding the nature of Allah.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against those who deliberately fabricate lies about Allah, which includes attributing false characteristics or claims to Him. The phrase 'will not succeed' implies divine disapproval and the ultimate failure both in this life and the Hereafter. It underscores the gravity of speaking untruthfully about the Divine and reveals that such actions lead to spiritual and moral ruin, emphasizing the importance of honesty and integrity in faith.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly pleasures and the inevitability of returning to God for judgment. It serves as a stern warning that those who persist in disbelief and ingratitude will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of faith and the temporary nature of worldly life compared to the eternal nature of the Hereafter.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the story of Noah, when he said to his people: 'O my people, if my staying (with you) and my reminding (you) of the signs of Allah is hard on you, then I have put my trust in Allah. So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates. Then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite.'
interpretation: This verse narrates the story of the Prophet Noah (Nuh) as he addresses his people, expressing his steadfastness and reliance on Allah despite their resistance. He challenges them to gather all their strength and their allies to execute whatever plan they have against him, reflecting his utter trust in Allah's support and his fearless commitment to his mission. The directive to his people to not hesitate ('let not your plan be obscure to you') indicates Noah's confidence in the truth of his message and demonstrates the futility of opposing Allah's will. This passage highlights the theme of unshakeable faith in divine providence and the ineffectiveness of worldly schemes against divine purpose.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be of the Muslims (those who submit to Allah).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the selflessness and sincerity of the messenger's mission, stating that the messenger does not seek any material gain or reward for delivering the message. Instead, the reward lies solely with Allah. It also underscores the messenger's commitment to submission to Allah's will, highlighting that his actions are driven by divine command rather than personal interest.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah illustrates the consequences of rejecting divine guidance by recounting the story of a prophet who was denied by his people. Despite their denial, Allah saved the prophet and his followers by placing them on the ark, making them inheritors of the earth. Those who rejected the divine signs were punished through drowning. This serves as a warning and a lesson, emphasizing the importance of heeding divine messages and the fate that befalls those who ignore such warnings.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent messengers after him to their people, and they brought them clear proofs. But they would not believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse indicates that after a prophet passes, God continues to send messengers to guide their communities with clear and undeniable signs. However, the persistent disbelief and rejection of these signs by the people lead them to reinforce their denial. This persisting rejection results in a spiritual sealing of their hearts, symbolizing an obstinate refusal to accept guidance despite clear evidence. It underscores the consequence of continuous disbelief and transgression, emphasizing the closure of hearts to faith as a form of divine justice for those who repeatedly reject God’s messages.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then, after them, We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his establishment with Our signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse depicts the mission of Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron, sent by God to guide Pharaoh and his followers. However, due to their arrogance and persistent wrongdoing, they rejected the signs and messages brought to them. It underscores the nature of stubbornness and pride as barriers to acknowledging the truth, leading to moral and spiritual failure.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Indeed, this is clear magic.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the response of some individuals when confronted with undeniable truth and divine guidance. Despite the truth's clarity and evidence, they dismiss it as 'magic,' indicating a deep-seated resistance and denial. This reaction exemplifies how people can reject what threatens their preconceptions and comforts, choosing to label truths they cannot or do not wish to understand as mere illusion or trickery. The verse serves as a commentary on the human tendency to avoid confronting challenging truths.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said, 'Do you say [this] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? But magicians will not succeed.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses challenges the skepticism and accusations of sorcery directed towards the truth he brings. He questions why people dismiss the clear truth by labeling it as magic, emphasizing that those who engage in deception and sorcery will ultimately fail. This implies that truth, symbolized by divine guidance and miracles, is distinct from and superior to illusion and falsehood.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said, 'Have you come to turn us away from what we found our fathers following, so that you two may have grandeur in the land? And we are not going to believe you two.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the resistance of people to prophetic messages that challenge their long-held traditions and power structures. The individuals speaking are accusing the messengers of attempting to lead them away from their ancestral beliefs for personal gain and dominance. The statement indicates stubbornness and rejection, highlighting the struggle prophets faced in conveying divine guidance against societal inertia and established norms.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every learned magician.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's reaction to the signs shown by Moses (Musa). Feeling threatened by Moses' divine miracles, Pharaoh resorts to summoning the best magicians in his kingdom to challenge Moses and demonstrate that his power and control over his realm are still unshaken. This confrontation between divine truth and human deception sets the stage for the subsequent events where the superiority of Moses' divinely granted abilities would become evident against the mere trickery of the magicians.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: So when the magicians came, Moses said to them: 'Throw down whatever you will throw.'
interpretation: This verse describes a moment of confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. It illustrates Moses' confidence and trust in the power of God, as he encourages the magicians to demonstrate their own abilities first. The context suggests that Moses is secure in the knowledge that God's power will prevail over any sorcery or illusion the magicians might present. This moment sets the stage for a divine demonstration of true miracles, underscoring the theme that human trickery cannot match the power of God.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: So when they threw, Moses said, 'What you have brought is [only] magic. Indeed, Allah will expose its worthlessness. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of corrupters.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Prophet Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh's court. When the magicians cast their spells, Moses declared that their actions were merely illusions and deceitful tricks, not true miracles. He reassures that Allah will render their efforts fruitless and make their falsehood apparent. This emphasizes the divine principle that the deeds of those who sow corruption and deceit will never be sustained or deemed successful. It underscores the power of divine truth over human deceit.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah vindicates the truth by His words, even though the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse underscores that Allah’s decree and words will always prevail to establish the truth, irrespective of the opposition from wrongdoers. It emphasizes divine justice and the inherent power of Allah’s commands to bring forth truth and righteousness, demonstrating that despite any resistance from those who commit crimes, truth will ultimately be triumphant.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: But none believed Moses except some offspring [i.e., youths] among his people, for fear of Pharaoh and his establishment that they would persecute them. And indeed, Pharaoh was haughty within the land, and indeed, he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: In this verse, it is highlighted that only a minority, particularly the younger generation, among the people of Moses believed in his message due to the oppressive and terrifying rule of Pharaoh. The fear of severe repercussions from Pharaoh and his influential officials led most to hide their faith or outright deny it. Pharaoh's arrogance and his indulgence in tyranny and excess were significant barriers to the broader acceptance of the truth brought by Moses.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims.'
interpretation: Moses is addressing his people, urging them to put their trust in Allah if they truly believe in Him and are sincere in their submission as Muslims. This emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in God's plan and guidance, particularly in times of difficulty or uncertainty.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: They said, 'In Allah we put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers’ declaration of trust in Allah in the face of adversity. It is a plea for protection from being overwhelmed or influenced by wrongdoers, and a supplication to not become a cause of temptation or trial for them. It underscores the importance of seeking divine assistance to remain steadfast and avoiding falling into the traps set by those who do not adhere to righteous paths.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication for divine intervention and protection, asking for God's mercy to rescue the believers from the harm and influence of those who reject faith. It highlights the importance of seeking God's help in times of distress and the reliance on His mercy for deliverance from adversities imposed by disbelievers.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired Musa and his brother [saying]: 'Take for your people houses in Egypt, and make your houses [facing the] Qiblah, and establish prayer and give glad tidings to the believers.'
interpretation: This verse recounts a divine command given to Prophet Musa (Moses) and his brother Harun (Aaron). They are instructed to settle their people in Egypt and to make their homes places of worship oriented towards the Qiblah. The emphasis on establishing prayer underscores its importance as a pillar of faith, and they are also encouraged to bring good news to the believers, strengthening their faith and perseverance.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, so that they may lead people astray from Your path. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing God, expressing his concern about the influence of Pharaoh and his advisors. He acknowledges that God has granted them worldly wealth and splendor, which they use to mislead people from the true path of God. Moses prays for God to strip them of their wealth and harden their hearts, making them unable to believe until they face severe consequences. This plea highlights the struggles of the righteous against the forces of corruption and misguidance, and reflects a desire for divine intervention to restore justice and truth.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, 'Your supplication has been answered. So be steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and adherence to divine guidance following the acceptance of a prayer. It advises staying firm in the path laid out by God and refraining from emulating those who are ignorant or who do not follow divine wisdom. The focus is on steadfastness and avoiding misguided actions that deviate from divine teachings, highlighting that true knowledge and success come through following God's guidance.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We delivered the Children of Israel across the sea; then Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Pharaoh, realizing the inevitable end during the drowning, declares his belief in the God of the Children of Israel. This acknowledgment comes too late for Pharaoh, suggesting the futility of seeking repentance only at the moment of death. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith and repentance before it is too late, and it also serves as a reminder of God's justice and the ultimate downfall of tyranny and oppression.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: Now? When you had previously disobeyed and were among the corruptors?
interpretation: This verse addresses a moment of regret that comes too late. It implies that the realization and repentance for one's misdeeds, when faced with inevitable consequences, are not sufficient to absolve one of guilt. The emphasis is on the necessity of timely obedience and righteous conduct, highlighting that repentance in the face of undeniable consequences lacks sincerity and impact.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: So today We will save you in body that you may be to those who succeed you a sign. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when God decided to preserve the body of Pharaoh as a tangible sign for future generations. The preservation serves as a profound warning to those who come after him about the consequences of arrogance and disbelief. Despite such clear signs, many people remain oblivious or indifferent to the lessons being taught by God's revelations and the historical events He orchestrates.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And We provided the Children of Israel with an honest dwelling place, and We provided them with good things. And they did not differ until after the knowledge had come to them; indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah granted the Children of Israel a noble dwelling and provided them with numerous blessings. However, their unity was disrupted only after they received divine guidance, leading to disagreements. The verse assures that Allah will ultimately resolve their disputes and judge them on the Day of Resurrection. It emphasizes how divine knowledge can sometimes lead to differences among people due to varying interpretations and underscores the final judgment by Allah as the ultimate resolution of all disputes.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among those who doubt.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him of the truthfulness of the revelation he has received. It suggests that if there is any doubt, he can consult those who have previously received divine scriptures, as they can confirm the consistency and truth of God's message. Ultimately, it emphasizes that the truth has been made clear by God and warns against falling into doubt.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And do not be of those who deny the signs of Allah, for you will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a clear warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and acceptance of Allah's signs and revelations. Rejecting or denying these divine signs equates to a great loss both in this world and in the hereafter. It underlines the importance of acknowledging and living by the guidance provided by Allah to avoid spiritual and eternal ruin.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that there are individuals who are so firmly set in their disbelief that it has been decreed by God that they will not come to faith. It underscores the concept of divine decree and the inevitability of God's will, suggesting that despite the clear signs and messages, these individuals are unable to change their state due to their persistent rejection of faith.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: Even if every sign were to come to them, until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and obstinacy of some people who refuse to believe even when presented with clear signs from Allah. It suggests that despite numerous signs and warnings, their disbelief persists until they ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the form of a severe punishment. This emphasizes the importance of heeding divine guidance and the reality of divine justice.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: Then has there not been a single city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rarity of entire communities genuinely believing and benefiting from their faith. The people of Jonah are presented as an exception; when they repented and believed, God lifted their worldly punishment and granted them reprieve, illustrating God's mercy and the temporal nature of His chastisements.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: Had your Lord willed, all those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely. Then, would you compel people in order that they become believers?
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of free will in belief. It signifies that if Allah had willed, He could have made all human beings believers, but He chose to give them free will to either believe or disbelieve. It emphasizes that the role of a prophet or a believer is not to force belief upon others but to convey the message. Belief is ultimately an individual choice guided by personal conviction and divine guidance, not by compulsion.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: It is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah, and He will place defilement upon those who will not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith is ultimately granted by the will of Allah, indicating divine sovereignty over human belief. It also highlights the consequences for those who refuse to reason and reflect, suggesting that a lack of rational engagement with divine signs leads to spiritual impurity and moral corruption.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون
