translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Judgment, and bring them to the Fire; and wretched is the place to which they are led.
interpretation: This verse implies a stark warning about the consequences of blindly following misguided leaders. It underscores the ultimate responsibility of leaders for their followers, especially on the Day of Judgment. Misguided leaders who lead their people away from the path of righteousness will face severe consequences, as will those who choose to follow them. The 'Fire' symbolizes severe punishment and the 'wretched place' denotes the regret and sorrow that accompany such a fate. It serves as a cautionary message to reflect on one's guidance and leadership, ensuring they align with divine guidance.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And they were followed in this [world] with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift which is given.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the consequences for those who defy the commandments of God. In this world, they are burdened with a curse, and in the Hereafter, their fate is sealed with punishment. The 'gift' mentioned denotes their eventual recompense, which is described as wretched, emphasizing the severe and inevitable nature of divine retribution for their actions.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: That is from the news of the towns, which We relate to you. Of them, some are standing and some are mown down.
interpretation: This verse refers to the stories of previous communities and civilizations that faced divine consequences for their actions. The 'standing' towns symbolize those stories or communities that still have remnants visible or whose lessons remain relevant, while 'mown down' refers to those that have been completely eradicated. It emphasizes the importance of learning from history and the ultimate justice and power of God in dealing with human actions.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods, whom they invoked besides Allah, were of no use to them when the command of your Lord came, and they did not increase them in anything except destruction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of personal accountability and the futility of idolatry. When divine judgment befell the disbelievers, it was clear that their afflictions were a consequence of their own actions. The deities they worshipped other than Allah offered them no protection or benefit. Instead of aiding them, their false gods only contributed to their ruin, highlighting the ultimate impotence of anything worshipped besides the one true God. Moreover, this serves as a reminder that reliance on anything other than Allah invariably leads to loss and devastation.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: Such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and certainty of God's punishment for communities that persist in wrongdoing and injustice. It serves as both a warning and a reminder that divine retribution is both inevitable and severe for those who transgress moral and ethical boundaries. The verse highlights the importance of justice and righteousness in avoiding divine wrath.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which the people will be collected, and that is a Day [which will be] witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the signs provided for those who are conscious of the Hereafter and its consequences. It highlights the Day of Judgment, a day when all of humanity will be gathered together. This day is not only a focal point of divine justice but also a witnessed event, indicating that it is a definitive and observable reality. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to prepare for this ultimate day of accountability.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And We do not delay it except for a limited term.
interpretation: This verse indicates that any delay in divine action or decree is purposeful and according to a specific timeline determined by God. It highlights the precision and intention behind God’s plan, assuring believers that everything occurs at its appointed time within His wisdom and knowledge.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and control of Allah on the Day of Judgment where no one will be able to speak or intercede without His permission. It underscores the idea that human destinies are controlled by Allah's decree, with individuals being categorized as either wretched or prosperous based on their deeds and His ultimate judgment. It serves as a reminder of the impermanence of worldly status and the ultimate divine justice that will prevail.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: But as for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire. In it they will have sighing and groaning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning about the consequences of moral and spiritual failure. The term 'wretched' refers to those who have denied faith and persistently engaged in sinful actions. Being subjected to the Fire symbolizes enduring the severe and eternal punishment in Hell. 'Sighing and groaning' depict deep anguish and suffering, emphasizing the severity of the retribution for those who turn away from the path of righteousness and divine guidance. This verse is meant to encourage introspection and adherence to a life of faith and moral integrity.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will. Indeed, your Lord is an accomplisher of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse suggests the permanence and continuity of divine decrees and the conditions of existence in the afterlife. It acknowledges that whatever state Allah has willed for the heavens and the earth will persist unless He decides otherwise. The verse reinforces the concept of Allah's ultimate authority and the absolute nature of His will in determining the fate of all beings. It emphasizes that Allah has the power to enact His desires and none can alter His decisions.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: As for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a gift without end.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal bliss and reward for the righteous in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the permanence of their stay in Paradise, contingent on the divine will but highlighting that the blessings they receive are unceasing and generously bestowed. It underscores the infinite mercy and generosity of God towards those who are granted entry into Paradise.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: So do not be in doubt about what these people worship. They worship nothing except as their ancestors worshipped before. And indeed, We will grant them their share undiminished.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to doubt the misguided practices of the disbelievers, as their worship is merely a continuation of their ancestors' baseless traditions. It also serves as a reminder of divine justice—that everyone will receive their due recompense fully, without any diminishment, whether it be punishment for their misguidance or reward for their faith and righteousness.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but it came under disputes. Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, the matter would have been judged between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the common theme of divine revelation being given to prophets, which often results in differing opinions and disputes among their people. The mention of a 'prior decree' from Allah suggests His wisdom and timing in postponing immediate judgment to allow for specific divine purposes, such as the opportunity for repentance and guidance. The phrase 'disquieting doubt' reflects the persistent skepticism and uncertainty some people have towards the messages from God, despite the clarity and truth contained within them.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, each will be fully compensated by your Lord for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability. It reassures that every individual shall receive the full recompense of their actions from Allah, who is fully aware of all their deeds. It underscores that nothing escapes God's knowledge and that ultimate justice will be served by Him without fail.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: So be steadfast as you have been commanded, and those who have turned in repentance with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his mission, adhering firmly to the commands given by Allah. It also extends this counsel to those who repent and join him in faith, emphasizing the importance of maintaining righteousness and avoiding overstepping boundaries. The verse concludes by reminding them that Allah is fully aware of their actions, serving as both a reassurance and a warning to uphold their commitments sincerely and diligently.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you would not have other than Allah any protectors; then you would not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a clear moral stance and not aligning oneself with those who commit injustice or wrongdoing. Such an association could lead to severe consequences, both spiritually and morally, culminating in divine retribution signified by the 'Fire.' The verse also underscores the absence of any true protectors besides Allah, suggesting that relying on other sources for protection or support in such matters is futile. Ultimately, this verse is a stern warning against complicity in injustice and a reminder of the singularity of divine governance and support.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of regular prayer throughout the day and night, highlighting specific times for establishing it. It conveys the powerful impact of good deeds, especially prayer, in erasing sins and misdeeds, serving as a moral and spiritual reminder for those who are mindful of their faith and wish to maintain their spiritual purity.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and perseverance, reassuring believers that their good deeds and righteous actions will not go unrewarded by Allah. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining patience in the face of trials and challenges, with the promise that Allah sees and values the efforts of those who strive to do good.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: So why were there not, among the generations before you, those of enduring discrimination forbidding corruption on earth—except a few of those We saved from among them? But those who wronged pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse laments the scarcity of righteous individuals in previous generations who would denounce corruption and sinful behavior on Earth. It highlights that only a few were saved due to their righteousness, while the majority remained engrossed in their indulgent lifestyles and consequently became wrongdoers or criminals. It serves as a reminder of the importance of standing against moral corruption and the consequences of neglecting such responsibilities.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. It indicates that Allah does not punish communities arbitrarily or unjustly. The destruction of towns or peoples would only occur if there is pervasive wrongdoing and corruption, without any attempts at rectification or reformation by its inhabitants. The verse underscores the importance of striving for righteousness and reform as protective measures against divine retribution.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and will in the creation of diversity among humans. It indicates that God's choice to allow differences and a variety of beliefs, cultures, and opinions serves a purpose. These differences encourage human beings to engage in dialogue, understand each other better, and strive for personal and communal growth. It reaffirms the idea of free will, suggesting that uniformity is not in God's design for humanity, and the inherent differences among people are intentional and part of the divine plan.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: Except those on whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. But the word of your Lord is fulfilled: 'I will fill Hell with jinn and men all together.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who receive God's mercy and those who do not. It emphasizes that God's mercy is selective and purposeful. The latter part of the verse underscores the inevitable fulfillment of God's decree, indicating that Hell will be filled with both jinn and humans who have gone astray. This serves as a reminder of divine justice and the consequences of deviating from righteousness.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: All that We relate to you of the stories of the messengers is to make your heart firm. And in this has come to you the truth, an exhortation, and a reminder to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose behind recounting the stories of past prophets to the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights that these narratives serve to strengthen his heart, affirming the truth and divine message he is conveying. Additionally, the verse underscores that these stories are meant to be a source of counsel and reflection for the believers, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe, 'Work according to your position; indeed, we are working.'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to address the non-believers, asserting that everyone should continue in their respective ways and positions. It implies a steadfastness in faith and deeds for the believers, emphasizing that their actions are aligned with their beliefs, despite the opposition. This can also be seen as a message of tolerance and mutual respect for the different paths people take, while highlighting the importance of remaining firm and committed to one's faith.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And wait, indeed we are waiting
interpretation: This verse conveys a sense of reassurance and patience, emphasizing perseverance in the face of trials or uncertainties. It suggests that both the speaker and the addressee should remain steadfast, with the understanding that outcomes will unfold in due time according to divine wisdom.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all matters will be returned. So worship Him and put your trust in Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah, asserting that only He has knowledge of the unseen realms of the heavens and the earth. All matters, actions, and outcomes are ultimately in His control. Therefore, it advises believers to devote themselves to worshipping Allah and to place complete trust in Him, assuring them that Allah is fully aware of their deeds and actions.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse points to the Qur'an as a book of clear guidance and wisdom. The mention of 'Alif, Lam, Ra' serves as an indication of the mysterious nature of the Qur'an's origins and its divine source. The phrase 'clear Book' emphasizes the clarity and comprehensibility of its message for those who seek understanding and guidance.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language specifically, which holds significance for several reasons. It acknowledges the clarity and precision of Arabic as a language capable of conveying deep meanings and divine instructions. The purpose of highlighting the language emphasizes the importance of understanding the message directly without translation-related ambiguities. It suggests that the message is intended to be clear and comprehensible to its initial audience, the Arabs, and by extension, to all of humanity as an invitation to seek deeper comprehension and insight.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and significance of the Qur'anic revelations presented to Prophet Muhammad. It underscores that the stories narrated in the Qur'an are the most excellent and full of wisdom, specifically revealed by Allah to the Prophet. Additionally, it points out that prior to this revelation, the Prophet was unaware of these profound narratives and the divine wisdom they encompass, highlighting the transforming impact and the guidance provided by the Qur'an.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: When Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a pivotal moment where Joseph (Yusuf) shares a profound dream with his father, Jacob (Yaqub). The dream, which is symbolic and prophetic, indicates future events where Joseph will attain a high status and his family will show great respect and recognition of his elevated position. The eleven stars represent his eleven brothers, while the sun and the moon symbolize his father and mother. This dream sets the stage for the unfolding narrative of Joseph's trials and ultimate rise to prominence, exemplifying his deep connection with divine guidance and the importance of dreams in conveying future truths.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: He said, 'O my dear son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a father's wisdom and caution to his son, advising him to keep his visions or dreams private to protect against jealousy and harm from others, in this case, his brothers. The verse further highlights the role of Satan in sowing discord and enmity among humans, emphasizing the need for vigilance against such divisive influences.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's special selection and favor towards Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), granting him knowledge and wisdom, specifically the skill of interpreting dreams. It signifies the completion of divine favor not only on Joseph but also on his forefathers, emphasizing God's continuous and wise support for His chosen servants. Furthermore, it underscores the importance of trust in God's wisdom and omniscience in His choices and guidance.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: There was certainly in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his brothers as a significant lesson for those who seek knowledge and understanding. It suggests that their experiences contain important signs and moral teachings about faith, patience, jealousy, forgiveness, and the ultimate triumph of good over evil. The verse encourages reflection on these events to derive wisdom and guidance.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: When they said, 'Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a strong group. Indeed, our father is in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse captures a moment of jealousy and resentment expressed by Joseph's brothers. They are troubled by the preferential treatment they perceive Joseph and his brother receive from their father. Despite being a capable and strong group, they feel neglected and attribute this to their father's mistake or error in judgment. The verse highlights the dynamics of familial relationships and human susceptibility to envy and misunderstanding within close kin.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Kill Joseph or cast him out to some (other) land; that the favor of your father may be given to you alone, and after that you may be righteous folk.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of conspiracy among the brothers of Joseph, driven by jealousy and a desire for their father's undivided attention and favor. It reveals their willingness to commit grievous acts out of envy, but also their intent to repent and become righteous after removing their perceived obstacle. It underlines themes of sibling rivalry, the destructive power of jealousy, and the complex human emotions that drive people to wrongdoing, with a focus on the hope for eventual repentance and rectification.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: One of them said, 'Do not kill Joseph, but if you must do something, throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up.'
interpretation: This verse highlights an instance of divine intervention wherein one of Joseph's brothers, driven by an internal moral compass or perhaps divine inspiration, suggests a less severe alternative to killing him. This brother's proposal to cast Joseph into a well also introduces the theme of fate and destiny orchestrated by a higher power, hinting at Joseph's ultimate survival and future rise to prominence. The verse underscores God's protective oversight and the unfolding of divine plans through seemingly tragic events.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, 'O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere advisors?'
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph's brothers are trying to convince their father, Jacob, to trust them with Joseph. They are assuring their father of their sincerity and good intentions towards their younger brother, despite their underlying jealousy and hidden agenda. It highlights the theme of deceit and the complex dynamics within familial relationships, where individuals might mask their true motives with words of assurance and loyalty.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: Send him with us tomorrow to enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Joseph (Yusuf) and his brothers. Here, his brothers are persuading their father, Jacob (Ya'qub), to send Joseph with them. They assure their father that Joseph will have a good time and they will take care of him. This reflects their ulterior motive to remove Joseph from their father's protection, driven by jealousy and rivalry.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are unaware of him.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep concern and worry of Prophet Jacob (Yaqub) regarding the safety of his son Joseph (Yusuf). Jacob expresses his fear that while his other sons are preoccupied or negligent, a wolf might attack and devour Joseph. This statement underscores Jacob's protective nature as a parent and his intuitive sense of potential danger, hinting at his awareness of the deceptive intentions of his other sons. It also highlights themes of trust, betrayal, and parental love within the narrative.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said, 'If a wolf were to devour him while we are a strong group, then we would surely be losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the conversation among the brothers of the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when they were planning to take him away from their father, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob). They assure their father that they are strong enough to protect Yusuf from any harm, mocking the idea that a wolf could devour him under their watch. This verse highlights their deceit and the false sense of security they portray to cover their ill intentions.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: So when they took him away and agreed to throw him down into the bottom of the well, We inspired him, 'You will surely inform them about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity].'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when he was abandoned by his brothers. Despite their betrayal, Allah reassures Yusuf with divine inspiration, promising him that he will one day inform his brothers of their wrongdoing, without them recognizing him initially. This reflects the themes of trust in divine wisdom, the eventual revelation of truth, and the assurance of justice and vindication.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their father, weeping, in the evening.
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). It describes the moment when his brothers returned to their father, Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), pretending to be grief-stricken after having cast Yusuf into a well. Their weeping was an attempt to deceive their father about Yusuf's fate, showcasing their treacherous and deceitful nature. The verse highlights themes of betrayal, sorrow, and the facade of false emotions.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our belongings, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the moment when the brothers of Joseph (Yusuf) return to their father, Jacob (Yaqub), with a fabricated story to explain Joseph's absence. They claim that a wolf devoured Joseph while they were racing, knowing their father would find it difficult to believe them because of their dubious past actions. The verse highlights themes of deceit, guilt, and the challenge of trust within familial relationships. It also sets the stage for the unfolding of Joseph's story, marked by trials and eventual triumph against the backdrop of his brothers' treachery.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they brought upon his shirt false blood. He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe.'
interpretation: This verse narrates part of the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), where his brothers return with his shirt stained with false blood, attempting to deceive their father Jacob (Yaqub). Jacob, however, perceives their deceit and responds with patience and trust in Allah. The verse highlights themes of trust, patience in the face of deceit and suffering, and reliance on Allah's support and justice.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And there came a company of travelers; they sent their water-drawer and he let down his bucket. He said, 'Good news! Here is a boy.' And they concealed him, taking him as merchandise; and Allah was knowing of what they did.
interpretation: This verse narrates the moment when a caravan of travelers discovers Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in a well, where he was thrown by his jealous brothers. The water-drawer is surprised and delighted to find a boy, but the travelers' immediate reaction is to conceal him as they see a potential gain by selling him as a slave. Despite their actions, the verse reminds us that Allah is fully aware of all deeds and intentions, underscoring His omniscience and justice.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they sold him for a reduced price - a few pieces of silver - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
interpretation: This verse refers to the sale of the Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) by his brothers. They sold him for a meager price, illustrating their disregard and lack of appreciation for his value. The phrase 'of those content with little' suggests their willingness to part with Joseph without recognizing his worth or potential, highlighting themes of betrayal, undervaluation, and the initial stages of Joseph's journey which eventually leads to his rise in status by the grace of God.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: The man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, 'Take good care of him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we might adopt him as a son.' Thus We established Joseph in the land to teach him the interpretation of events. Allah's Will always prevails, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Yusuf (Joseph) is sold into slavery in Egypt and how his master, who noticed his potential, instructs his wife to treat him well. It highlights the beginning of Yusuf's journey in Egypt and alludes to the deeper, divine plan behind his circumstances. The latter part underscores that Allah's will and wisdom are paramount and always come to fruition, even if people do not always comprehend the divine orchestration behind events.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that upon reaching full maturity, an individual is endowed by Allah with wisdom and knowledge as a reward for their righteousness and good conduct. It underscores the divine principle of rewarding those who strive for moral and ethical excellence, highlighting the importance of personal development and piety in Islamic teachings.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, 'Come, you.' He said, 'I seek the refuge of Allah. Indeed, He is my Lord. He has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) being tempted by the wife of the Egyptian nobleman in whose house he resided. When she attempted to seduce him and closed the doors to ensure privacy, Yusuf rejected her advances by seeking refuge in Allah. He expressed his gratitude for the nobleman's kindness and acknowledged that betraying his trust would be an act of wrongdoing. This response highlights Yusuf's unwavering faith, moral integrity, and recognition that true success and righteousness come from adherence to divine principles and avoiding transgression.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the temptation he faced from the wife of the Egyptian official who bought him. Despite her strong inclination and attempt to seduce him, Yusuf would have fallen into error if he had not witnessed a divine sign or proof from Allah, which served as a powerful deterrent. This divine intervention illustrates Allah's protection over His devout servants, preserving them from committing sins and immoral acts. Yusuf's steadfastness and purity are highlighted, emphasizing his status as a chosen and sincere servant of Allah, committed to righteousness.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back. They found her master at the door. She said, 'What is the recompense for the one who intended evil for your wife except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?'
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the 'Aziz (Potiphar). It depicts the moment when Yusuf attempted to flee from the pursuit of the 'Aziz's wife, who then falsely accused him of trying to harm her. The verse highlights the immediate consequences of temptation and false accusation, reflecting the themes of integrity, patience in adversity, and the trials faced by those who strive to uphold righteousness.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: He said, 'She was the one who tried to seduce me.' And a witness from her family testified, 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she is telling the truth, and he is a liar.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) is defending himself against the false accusations of the wife of the Egyptian official who tried to seduce him. The testimony from a witness belonging to her household is suggested as a means to determine the truth. The logic presented is that if Yusuf’s shirt is torn from the front, it would indicate an attempt to resist her advances, thus proving his innocence. This approach underscores the importance of evidence and fairness in judging accusations.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), when he was falsely accused by the wife of his master. The tearing of the shirt from the back indicates that Yusuf was trying to escape, thereby proving his innocence. This verse illustrates the principles of evidence and justice, emphasizing the importance of considering physical evidence to determine the truth.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your women's plan. Indeed, your plan is great.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of Al-Aziz (Potiphar). When Al-Aziz saw that Yusuf's (Joseph's) shirt was torn from the back, he realized that it was the wife who was at fault, as she had been the one to proposition Yusuf and then falsely accuse him when he resisted. The mention of 'your plan is great' indicates the intensity and cunning nature of the trap she set for him, reflecting broader comments on human behavior and the nature of deceit.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: Joseph, turn away from this, and (O woman) ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you have been of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse addresses two characters: Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and the woman who attempted to seduce him. The command to Joseph is to disregard the incident and move on, indicating that he is not at fault. The woman, on the other hand, is advised to seek forgiveness for her sin, acknowledging that she has committed a wrongful act. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and turning away from sin, highlighting individual responsibility for one's actions.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And women in the city said, 'The wife of Al-‘Aziz is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her to be in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the societal gossip surrounding the wife of Al-‘Aziz and her attempt to seduce Joseph (Yusuf). It shows how quickly a personal scandal can become public and subject to judgment by others. The women of the city express their opinion that the wife of Al-‘Aziz has been overtaken by passion, leading her to act improperly, which they view as a clear mistake or misguidance. This verse highlights themes of human frailty, the power of desire, and how quickly reputations can be affected by public opinion.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared a banquet for them. She gave each one of them a knife and said to Joseph, 'Come out before them.' When they saw him, they were so amazed by him that they cut their hands and said, 'Good God! This is no human being; this is but a noble angel.'
interpretation: The verse narrates an incident with Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and the women of Egypt, illustrating their reactions to his exceptional beauty. The women, initially skeptical of the lady's (the Aziz's wife) infatuation, are struck with profound astonishment upon seeing Joseph, to the point where they unwittingly cause themselves harm. This episode highlights not only Joseph's extraordinary physical attractiveness but also human tendencies towards impulsive reactions when faced with overwhelming beauty. In a broader sense, it underscores the trials Joseph endured despite his righteousness and noble character, and it portrays the nature of divine beauty and the resulting reverence it can inspire.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: She said, 'That is the one you blamed me for. Indeed, I did try to seduce him, but he firmly refused. And if he does not do what I order him to, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased.'
interpretation: This verse describes a moment where the wife of Al-Aziz openly admits to her attempt to seduce Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and acknowledges his resistance to her advances. It also highlights her determination to punish Yusuf if he does not comply with her demands, showcasing her authority and the potential consequences he faces for maintaining his integrity and chastity.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse showcases Prophet Joseph's (Yusuf's) steadfastness and deep faith in his Lord. Despite the severe temptation and pressure from the women of Egypt, particularly the wife of the nobleman, Joseph chooses to prefer prison over committing a sinful act. He calls upon Allah for divine support and protection against their seduction, expressing his vulnerability and his fear of succumbing to their schemes. It emphasizes the importance of seeking divine help when faced with moral dilemmas and temptations, highlighting the concept of choosing righteousness over wrongdoing even if it leads to personal hardship.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plot. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), specifically when he was confronted with the scheming of women who tried to tempt and defame him. Yusuf prayed to Allah for help, and Allah answered his prayer by thwarting their plans. The verse emphasizes Allah’s attributes of being all-hearing and all-knowing, highlighting that He is aware of the machinations against His righteous servants and is fully capable of protecting them and ensuring justice.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that they should imprison him for a time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the decision taken by the authorities to imprison Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) despite the clear evidence of his innocence. The 'signs' imply the indications of truth and divine messages that were witnessed but ignored. This portrayal highlights themes of trial, patience, and divine wisdom, as Prophet Joseph's imprisonment was part of a larger divine plan for his eventual rise to power and the fulfillment of his destiny.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing wine.' The other said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one who does good.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) while in prison. Two fellow prisoners approached him to interpret their dreams. One dreamt of pressing wine, and the other of carrying bread on his head, from which birds ate. They asked Yusuf for an interpretation, recognizing his righteousness and goodness. The passage highlights Yusuf's status as a person of trust and wisdom even in dire circumstances, as well as the belief in the significance of dreams and their interpretations in conveying divine messages or premonitions.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, 'You will not receive any food that you are provided except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) who is addressing his fellow prisoners. He tells them that he has the ability, given by Allah, to interpret dreams or foretell outcomes even before they occur. This divine knowledge is a sign of his prophetic status. He also makes a clear dichotomy between his belief system, which acknowledges Allah and the Afterlife, and the disbelief of the people he has abandoned. This places emphasis on divine guidance and the superiority of faith in Allah and the Hereafter over disbelief.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes following the monotheistic faith of the forefathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It highlights the importance of not associating any partners with Allah, underscoring the fundamental principle of Tawhid (the oneness of God). The passage acknowledges that being guided to this pure belief is a divine favor and blessing. However, it also points out the common human trait of ingratitude, as most people do not recognize or appreciate this divine blessing.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, are different lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse reflects the monotheistic message addressed by Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) to his fellow prisoners. By posing a rhetorical question, it emphasizes the superiority of worshipping one omnipotent God over following multiple conflicting divinities. Joseph highlights the unity and absolute power of Allah as opposed to the divided and weaker nature of many gods or idols, urging his companions to recognize and submit to the One true God.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: You worship nothing besides Him except names which you have named, you and your forefathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. The command is for none but Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the right religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the futility of idol worship by pointing out that these idols are merely names without any divine backing or authority. It emphasizes that ultimate authority and judgment belong solely to Allah, who has decreed monotheism as the correct path. The verse underscores the importance of recognizing Allah’s exclusive right to be worshipped, while also lamenting that many people fail to understand this fundamental truth.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will serve wine to his master, and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph (Yusuf) addresses his fellow prisoners who asked him to interpret their dreams. He explains that one of them will be released and return to his former position as a cupbearer, serving wine to his master. The other one, however, will be crucified, and birds will peck at his head. Joseph emphasizes that this is the final and decreed outcome of the dreams they had sought his interpretation for, highlighting the predetermined nature of their fate as revealed through his prophetic insight.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, 'Mention me before your master.' But Satan made him forget to mention him to his master, so he remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the incident where Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) asked the cupbearer who was to be released to mention him to the king so that he could be freed from prison. However, Satan caused the cupbearer to forget Yusuf's request, resulting in Yusuf remaining imprisoned for several additional years. This underscores the theme of patience and reliance on God’s plan, illustrating that human actions and intentions are subject to divine wisdom and timing.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And the king said: I saw in a dream seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and (seven) others dry. O my nobles, explain to me my vision if you can interpret visions.
interpretation: This verse depicts a moment where the king elaborates a troubling dream he experienced. It highlights the vision of contrasting conditions—fat versus lean cows and green versus dry ears of corn. The king seeks the wisdom of his nobles, signaling his recognition that the dream contains important, deeper meanings that require expert interpretation. This sets the stage for the subsequent exploration of the dream's meaning, emphasizing the need for divine insight and wisdom in understanding such symbolic messages.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, 'Jumbled visions! And we are not knowledgeable in the interpretation of dreams.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment when individuals dismiss the significance of dreams by labeling them as mere jumbled visions, acknowledging their own lack of expertise in interpreting such dreams. It highlights human limitations in understanding the spiritual or symbolic messages that might be conveyed through dreams, suggesting that true wisdom and insight in dream interpretation are not within the grasp of everyone.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: And the one who was saved from the two of them, who remembered after a time, said, 'I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his time in prison. One of the two prisoners, whose dream interpretation by Joseph had come true, remembers Joseph after a period of time when the king needs an interpretation of his dream. The man offers to help by seeking Joseph's interpretation, highlighting Joseph's ability given to him by Allah and how past interactions and knowledge can come to fruition in future needs.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us the vision of seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and others dry, so that I may return to the people and inform them.
interpretation: This verse portrays a moment where Joseph, known for his wisdom and ability to interpret dreams, is being consulted by others seeking understanding. The dream of the seven fat cows and seven lean cows represents a period of abundance followed by famine. The green and dry ears of corn further signify these contrasting times. The questioner hopes that Joseph's interpretation will provide valuable insights, enabling them to prepare and inform others about the forthcoming events, highlighting the significance of foresight and planning in life.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: He said, 'You will plant for seven consecutive years. So whatever you harvest, leave it in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat.'
interpretation: This verse offers practical advice for times of abundance and scarcity. It emphasizes the importance of prudence and foresight by storing surplus produce during plentiful years for use in times of need. Leaving the grain in its spikes suggests a method of preservation that ensures food security and minimizes waste. The small portion to be consumed implies moderation even in times of plenty. This guidance is not only a literal instruction for agricultural practice but also serves as a metaphor for wise management of all resources.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then will come after that seven difficult years which will consume what you have laid up for them, except a little from which you will store.
interpretation: This verse is part of Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph's) interpretation of the Pharaoh's dream in which he foretells of seven years of famine that will follow seven years of abundance. During these hard years, the reserve of grains stored during the prosperous years will be consumed, except for a small portion that will be preserved. The verse emphasizes the importance of planning and saving during times of abundance to face future hardships and trials. It teaches lessons of foresight, prudence, and resilience in the face of challenges.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse refers to a prophetic interpretation of a dream foretelling a period of fertility and abundance following a time of hardship and drought. It highlights the cyclical nature of fortune, indicating that there will be a time of relief and prosperity after suffering. The mention of rain symbolizes divine mercy and rejuvenation, while pressing olives and grapes suggests economic activity and productivity, signifying the return of favorable conditions and sustenance for the community.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: The king said, 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, 'Return to your lord and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when the king of Egypt sent for Joseph after hearing about his ability to interpret dreams. However, Joseph, seeking to clear his name from any wrongdoing related to the incident with the women who had falsely accused him, requested that the king first investigate their actions to prove his innocence. This demonstrates Joseph's integrity, patience, and trust in God's knowledge and justice.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: He said, 'What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph?' They said, 'Perfect is Allah! We know about him no evil.' The wife of Al-Aziz said, 'Now the truth has come to light. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.'
interpretation: In this verse, the ruler questions the women who attempted to seduce Joseph. They confess that Joseph was innocent and blameless. The wife of Al-Aziz then admits her guilt and confirms that Joseph was truthful all along. This verse highlights themes of truth, repentance, and justice. It underscores the moral integrity of Prophet Joseph and the ultimate triumph of truth over deceit.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence and that Allah does not guide the plan of the betrayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the integrity and righteousness of a person who remains faithful even when not being observed. It underscores the moral belief that true righteousness is evident when one's actions are consistent with their principles, regardless of surveillance. Additionally, it highlights the divine principle that deceit and betrayal are not supported by Allah, affirming that schemes built on such foundations are ultimately destined to fail.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is prone to evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards sin and evil unless safeguarded by divine mercy. It acknowledges human imperfection and the constant battle with inner desires, reminding believers that it is through God's mercy that they can avoid wrongdoing. The verse reassures that God is forgiving and merciful, offering hope and solace to those who seek His grace and strive to overcome their base inclinations.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: The king said, 'Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself.' Then, when he spoke to him, he said, 'Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the king of Egypt, after hearing of Joseph's special abilities and wisdom, decides to summon him to the palace. Recognizing Joseph's intelligence and integrity, the king appoints him to a trustworthy and influential position. This signifies the beginning of Joseph's rise to power and the recognition of his virtue and capability.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: He said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land; indeed, I will be a knowing guardian.'
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) when he interpreted the king's dream and then offered his services to manage the storehouses of the land during the upcoming years of abundance and famine. His request to be in charge is based on his confidence in his own knowledge and trustworthiness. By stating that he is 'knowing' and 'guardian,' Joseph is highlighting his qualifications for the role, emphasizing his ability to manage the resources wisely and ethically.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: Thus, We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine plan and benevolence in Joseph's life. It illustrates how God's providence and mercy facilitate the success and well-being of His righteous servants. Joseph's ability to settle and choose his place in the land symbolizes the fulfillment of God's promise to reward and elevate those who remain patient and virtuous despite trials. It reassures believers that their good deeds and steadfastness will not go unrecognized or unrewarded by Allah.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are conscious of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of the rewards in the Hereafter compared to worldly gains. It encourages believers to maintain their faith and consciousness of Allah (taqwa) because the ultimate, eternal reward is far more valuable than any temporal benefits that can be achieved in this life. The verse seeks to reassure the faithful that their righteous conduct and piety will be rewarded by Allah in the most significant way, which is in the Hereafter.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when the brothers of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) arrive in Egypt and meet him. Joseph, now in a position of power, recognizes them instantly, but his brothers do not recognize him due to the significant changes in his appearance and status. This encounter prepares the stage for the unfolding of Joseph's plan to reveal his identity and test the repentance and transformation of his brothers.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?'
interpretation: This verse depicts a moment in the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) where he, after providing his brothers with provisions, asks them to bring their youngest brother (Benjamin) to him as proof of their sincerity. Joseph highlights his fairness and generosity in giving them full measure and being a hospitable host, thereby encouraging them to fulfill his request. This invitation serves multiple purposes: ensuring his younger brother's safety, testing his brothers' honesty, and setting up a reunion that leads to eventually revealing his own identity to them.
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure (of grain) for you with me, nor will you come near me.
interpretation: This verse reflects a condition set by a significant authority figure, likely foreshadowing a pivotal moment in a narrative. It emphasizes the importance of compliance with a specific demand—in this case, bringing a particular person—to receive a benefit, which is grain. The stern consequence of non-compliance, involving the denial of essential sustenance and access, underscores the seriousness of the situation and the power dynamics at play.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, 'We will try to coax his father away from him, and indeed we are determined to do it.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to separate him from their father by using persuasive tactics. Their words indicate a strong resolve to achieve their goal, which underscores themes of manipulation and familial conflict.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: He said to his servants: 'Put their merchandise in their saddlebags so they will recognize it when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back.'
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moment in the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), when he instructed his servants to secretly place the goods belonging to his brothers back in their bags after they had purchased provisions from him. Joseph hoped that when his brothers discovered the return of their merchandise, they would be compelled to come back. This action reflects Joseph's wisdom and strategic planning to ensure his family would return, thus facilitating a reunion and the unfolding of God's greater plan for them. It also highlights themes such as familial bonds, divine wisdom in guiding seemingly mundane decisions, and the subtle means by which God can influence events to achieve a higher purpose.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been denied [further] measure, so send with us our brother that we may get [the measure], and indeed, we will be his guardians.'
interpretation: This verse describes a conversation between the sons of Jacob and their father. The sons returned from Egypt, where they had faced difficulty obtaining provisions. They explained to their father that they were denied further provisions and requested that their younger brother, Benjamin, be sent with them on their next trip to secure the needed supplies. They reassured Jacob of their commitment to protect Benjamin. Their appeal underscores themes of responsibility, trust, and the struggle to meet familial obligations amidst challenging circumstances.
orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He replied, 'Should I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother before? But God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Jacob's (Prophet Yaqub's) reluctance and lack of trust in sending his son Benjamin with his other sons, given the past betrayal involving Joseph (Prophet Yusuf). It shows Jacob’s reliance on divine protection despite his concerns, emphasizing God's ultimate safeguarding and infinite mercy. This highlights the importance of faith and trust in God's plans and mercy even in challenging circumstances.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, 'O our father, what more could we desire? Here is our merchandise returned to us, and we will provide for our family and protect our brother and obtain an extra measure of a camel's load. This is an easy measure.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) discover that the goods they had taken to trade in Egypt were secretly returned to them in their baggage. They see it as a divine favor and a sign of good fortune, which they report to their father, Yaqub (Jacob). They emphasize that they can now honor their commitment to protect their brother and secure provisions for their family, viewing the extra measure they received as an additional blessing. The verse reflects themes of divine providence, trust, and the importance of familial responsibilities.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: He said, 'I will never send him with you until you give me a promise by Allah that you will surely bring him back to me unless you are surrounded.' And when they had given him their promise, he said, 'Allah is the Witness over what we say.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a dialogue where a father expresses his reluctance to send his son with his brothers without a solemn promise to ensure his return unless unforeseen circumstances prevent them. It shows the deep concern and protective nature of the father, emphasizing the seriousness of promises made in the name of Allah and recognizing Allah as the ultimate witness to all commitments.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who rely [indeed] rely.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the advice of Prophet Jacob (Ya'qub) to his sons. He instructs them to enter the city through different gates as a precautionary measure, possibly to avoid envy or harm. However, he emphasizes that ultimately, he has no power over the will of Allah and that any precautionary measure is only effective with Allah's permission. The verse underscores the importance of reliance on Allah and acknowledges His supreme authority and judgement. It is a reminder to trust in Allah's plan while taking practical steps in worldly matters.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against [the decree of] Allah at all, but it was a need within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the wisdom of Prophet Jacob (Yaqub) and his actions driven by intuition and spiritual insight. Despite his sons following his guidance, it was ultimately the will of Allah that prevailed, demonstrating that human efforts are subordinate to divine decree. Jacob's wisdom is highlighted as a fruit of divine teaching, which many people fail to perceive or comprehend. The emphasis is on recognizing the limits of human agency in the face of God's omnipotence, and on valuing the guidance received through prophetic knowledge.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said: Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of reunion between Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his full brother Benjamin. Joseph comforts Benjamin, revealing his true identity and offering reassurance. Despite the difficulties they have faced due to their brothers' actions, Joseph encourages Benjamin not to be disheartened, indicating Joseph's forgiveness and the bond of brotherhood.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: When he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the drinking-cup in the saddlebag of his brother. Then a herald called out, 'O caravan, you are indeed thieves.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the moment when Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) orchestrates a scheme to keep his youngest brother, Benjamin, with him in Egypt. By placing the royal cup in Benjamin's bag, Joseph sets the stage for accusing the brothers of theft. This act leads to a pivotal moment in the story, ultimately revealing Joseph's identity to his brothers and reuniting the family. The verse highlights themes of divine wisdom, the unfolding of God's plan, and the tests of trust and loyalty among the brothers.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, and turned towards them, 'What is it that you are missing?'
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of inquiry and concern, indicating an effort to identify a loss or issue. It exemplifies the communal involvement and collective responsibility often emphasized in the Qur'an, where members of the community are expected to assist and support each other in times of difficulty or confusion. The engagement suggests an active participation in resolving matters and ensuring communal harmony.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said, 'We have lost the king's cup, and whoever brings it shall have a camel load [of reward], and I guarantee it.'
interpretation: This verse occurs in the context of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). The brothers of Yusuf are being accused of theft by his servants. The 'king's cup' refers to the cup used by the ruler, which Yusuf had his men place in his brother Benjamin's sack. The proclamation made here is designed to set the scene for the discovery of the cup and the ensuing events. It highlights the seriousness of the accusation and the significant reward offered for the cup's return, underscoring the importance of the item and the desperation of the situation.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you certainly know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we are not thieves.'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment of intense defense by the brothers of Joseph, as they reply to the accusation of stealing. Swearing by Allah, they assert their innocence and emphasize their integrity and honorable intentions. The expression conveys their desperation and frustration in proving their honesty while under suspicion, shedding light on the deep tension and struggle for justice present in their narrative.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said, 'Then what shall be his recompense, if you should be liars?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a questioning meant to challenge the truthfulness of someone's claim. The speakers are demanding to know the consequences or punishment if the claimants are proven to be deceitful. It highlights themes of justice and accountability, emphasizing that falsehood must face repercussions.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They said, 'His punishment should be that he in whose bag it is found should himself be the penalty. This is how we punish wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse occurs in the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf). His brothers, who previously wronged him, find themselves in a situation where one of them is accused of theft. The punishment they declare, that the thief becomes a slave, is a manifestation of divine justice and a way to teach them a moral lesson about the consequences of their own past injustices. It highlights the concept of retributive justice in the moral order administered by God.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Then he began with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he brought it out from his brother’s bag. Thus do We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother according to the king’s law unless Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights several key themes: the divine nature of Joseph's (Yusuf's) success, the subtlety of God's plans, and the underlying wisdom and superiority of God's knowledge over human knowledge. It underscores that despite human efforts and laws, the ultimate outcome is determined by God's will. This passage is meant to inspire trust in God's plan, emphasizing that human beings may not always understand the divine wisdom behind events. Moreover, it highlights the theme of exaltation, where God raises in status those He chooses, and asserts that no matter how knowledgeable a person is, God's knowledge surpasses all.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, 'If he steals, there was a brother of his who had stolen before.' But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are in a worse situation, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse narrates an incident where Joseph's brothers accuse their younger brother of theft and attempt to justify it by referring to an alleged previous theft by Joseph himself. Joseph, however, silently suppresses any external reaction and internally acknowledges their betrayal without disclosing his true feelings. Instead, he remarks on their worse moral position and highlights that Allah is fully aware of the truth and their fabrications. This verse underscores themes of patience, internal strength, and the ultimate knowledge and justice of Allah.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, 'O mighty one, indeed he has a father who is an old man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good.'
interpretation: In this verse, the brothers of Benjamin appeal to the high-ranking official (who is actually their brother Joseph, though they do not recognize him) by acknowledging his kindness. They highlight the distress that taking Benjamin would cause to their aged father, Jacob, and offer themselves as substitutes out of compassion and desperation. This scene demonstrates their willingness to sacrifice for their father's well-being and illustrates the themes of mercy, familial duty, and the recognition of righteous character in others.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, 'We seek refuge in Allah from that; indeed, we would be wrongdoers if we took anyone except him with whom we found our property.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a strong commitment to justice and fairness. It underscores the principle that punishment should only be imposed on the actual perpetrator, not on innocent individuals. This aligns with the broader Islamic principle of fairness and accountability, emphasizing that one should not be unjust in their actions toward others and that seeking refuge in Allah is a way to maintain righteousness.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: So when they despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, 'Do you not know that your father has taken an oath from you in the name of Allah and before that, you failed in your duty regarding Joseph? Therefore, I will never leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me. And He is the best of judges.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of intense despondency among the brothers of Joseph (Yusuf) when they realize they might not be able to fulfill their father's wishes regarding their younger brother, Benjamin. The eldest brother reminds them of their oath to their father and their previous failure with Joseph, demonstrating his sense of responsibility and determination to rectify their past mistakes. The verse emphasizes themes of accountability, repentance, and faith in divine justice.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not witness except what we knew. And we were not guardians of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment where the sons of Prophet Jacob (Ya’qub) are returning to their father to inform him about the supposed theft committed by their brother Benjamin. It reflects their predicament and their attempt to explain that they are only conveying what they witnessed and that they had no knowledge of the unseen events that led to this situation. The verse highlights themes of familial duty, honesty in witnessing, and human limitations in knowing the unseen.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the town where we were and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse pertains to a historical narrative found in the Qur'an, specifically related to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers.
