Importantly, it extols patience and suggests that forbearance and patience in the face of harm are superior ethical responses and spiritually more rewarding for the patient individuals.
orig: وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير للصابرين

translation: And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they conspire.
interpretation: This verse advises steadfastness and patience, emphasizing that true patience is granted by Allah. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad to not be saddened by the disbelief or the actions of others, and to not let their plots cause him distress. It highlights the importance of relying on divine support during difficult times and maintaining inner peace despite external challenges.
orig: واصبر وما صبرك إلا بالله ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تك في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's support and guidance are bestowed upon individuals who possess piety (taqwa) and righteousness through their good deeds. It suggests a profound relationship where divine presence and assistance are contingent upon one's awareness of Allah's presence, making conscientious efforts to live a life aligned with His guidance, and actively engaging in acts of goodness and righteousness. This implies a call to both spiritual consciousness and compassionate, ethical behavior as means to attain Allah's nearness.
orig: إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون

translation: Glory be to Him Who made His servant to go on a night from the Sacred Mosque to the farthest mosque whose precincts We have blessed, so that We may show him some of Our signs. Surely He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse commemorates the miraculous Night Journey (Isra) of the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the divine power and glory of Allah, showcasing His ability to orchestrate extraordinary events. The journey from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem highlights the spiritual and physical connection between two holy sites. The phrase 'whose precincts We have blessed' underscores the significance and sanctity of the area. The purpose of the journey, 'to show him some of Our signs,' speaks to the profound spiritual revelations that the Prophet Muhammad received during this miraculous event. Lastly, the attributes of Allah as 'the Hearing, the Seeing' reaffirm His omnipotence and omniscience, assuring believers of His constant awareness and presence.
orig: سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guide for the Children of Israel, (saying), 'Do not take any protector besides Me.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and supremacy of divine guidance provided through the scriptures given to Moses. It underscores the importance of exclusive reliance on Allah as the sole protector and guide, warning against seeking intermediaries or other entities for spiritual or worldly protection. This message serves to reinforce the significance of monotheism and the centrality of God's guidance for the Children of Israel, and by extension, for all believers.
orig: وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا

translation: O descendants of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the descendants of those who were saved with Prophet Noah on the ark. It highlights the legacy of gratitude and faithfulness that Noah exhibited, serving as a reminder to his descendants to embody gratefulness and devotion to God.
orig: ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that they would surely cause corruption on the earth twice and that they would surely reach [a degree of] great haughtiness.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah had informed the Children of Israel through divine revelation that they would engage in acts of corruption and arrogance on two significant occasions. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of moral and ethical degradation, emphasizing the pattern of human behavior that deviates from divine guidance. It calls attention to the importance of humility and adhering to righteous conduct to avoid repeated mistakes and their accompanying downfall.
orig: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا

translation: So when the promise came for the first of the two (occasions), We sent against you servants of Ours - those of great military might, and they probed even into the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to a divine promise of punishment for the Israelites when they caused corruption twice on the earth. On the first occasion, God sent powerful servants, likely referring to foreign armies, who thoroughly invaded their land and homes. This event serves as a fulfillment of God's warning that disobedience and corruption lead to severe consequences. The verse highlights God's control over historical events and serves as a reminder of the importance of adherence to divine commands.
orig: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا

translation: Then We gave you back the power over them, and We reinforced you with wealth and children and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse indicates a reversal of fortunes where those who were previously subjugated are given power and resources to overcome their adversaries. It reflects the cyclical nature of human conditions and divine will, emphasizing God's ability to change the state of a community by providing them with increased wealth, offspring, and strength in numbers. This empowers and prepares them for future challenges. The verse underscores God's involvement and control over human destiny, granting prosperity and dominance as part of His divine plan.
orig: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, [you do it] to yourselves. Then when the final promise came, [We sent your enemies] to sadden your faces and to enter the temple in Jerusalem, as they entered it the first time, and to destroy what they had taken over with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of personal responsibility in the deeds one performs—whether good or evil—as the consequences will ultimately return to the individual. It refers to the historical events involving the Children of Israel and the consequences of their actions. When they did righteousness, they benefited from it, but when they transgressed, they faced severe repercussions. The verse also alludes to the events where enemies were sent to humiliate and conquer Jerusalem, underlining that divine promise and justice manifest through historical events, bringing both reward for righteousness and punishment for transgressions.
orig: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا

translation: It may be that your Lord will have mercy on you. But if you revert (to your sins), We shall revert (to Our punishments). And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the balance between divine mercy and justice. It suggests that Allah's mercy is always a possibility for those who seek repentance and improvement. However, if individuals revert to sinful ways, Allah will revert to delivering appropriate punishments. The verse underscores the severity of consequences for persistent disbelief, indicating that Hell is prepared as a strict confinement for those who reject faith. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a sincere and steadfast faith to attain Allah’s mercy.
orig: عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an as a source of guidance towards the most righteous and just way of life. It assures believers who engage in good deeds that they will be rewarded greatly, thereby encouraging a life of piety and moral integrity in accordance with the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا

translation: And for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences for those who deny the existence of an afterlife. It serves as a warning that disbelief in the Hereafter will lead to a form of divine retribution, specifically a painful punishment. The verse underlines the importance of faith in the afterlife as a fundamental component of Islamic belief and serves as both a deterrent against disbelief and a call to adhere to the faith.
orig: وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the impulsiveness and impatience of human beings. It highlights the nature of people to sometimes unwittingly wish for things that might be harmful to them, just as they wish for what is beneficial, due to their hasty nature. It serves as a reminder to be mindful and thoughtful about our prayers and desires.
orig: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

translation: And We have made the night and the day as two signs. Then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years and the account (of time). And We have explained everything in detail.
interpretation: This verse suggests that both night and day are divine signs with distinctive purposes. The night, symbolized by its darkness, is a time for rest and cessation of activities, while the day, illuminated by the sun, is made clear for humans to perform their tasks, seek their livelihoods, and recognize the passage of time. It highlights the orderly and purposeful nature of the universe, designed by God to facilitate human needs and the efficient functioning of their lives. Additionally, the verse underscores God's detailed articulation of His creation to ensure everything serves its intended purpose.
orig: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا

translation: And every person’s deeds We have bound to their neck, and on the Day of Resurrection We will bring forth for them a record which they will find spread open.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of personal responsibility and accountability in Islam. Each individual's actions are closely tied to them, symbolized by the metaphor of being bound to their neck. The imagery of the open record on the Day of Judgment emphasizes the transparency and inevitability of divine justice, where all deeds will be laid bare and every person will be confronted with the reality of their own life's actions without any alteration or concealment.
orig: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا

translation: Read your book; your soul suffices today as your own reckoner.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of personal accountability on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that individuals will be held responsible for their own deeds, and their record of actions (book) will be scrutinized. There will be no need for external witnesses as each person's soul will bear witness to their actions. This serves as a profound reminder that one's own conscience should guide one's actions, knowing that they will ultimately be judged by their own deeds.
orig: اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs, only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and accountability. It indicates that guidance benefits the individual, while misguidance harms only the soul of the misguided. Additionally, it establishes the principle that each person is responsible for their own actions, and no one will be punished for the sins of others. Lastly, it underscores God's justice, affirming that He does not punish a people without first sending a messenger to guide and warn them.
orig: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا

translation: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent, but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice and accountability. It describes how when a society becomes corrupt, particularly through the disobedience and excesses of its wealthy and powerful members, it inevitably leads to its own downfall. This is a reminder that moral decadence and injustice can lead to severe consequences, and it serves as a warning to maintain righteousness and accountability to avert total destruction.
orig: وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the temporal nature of human civilizations and the consequences of persistent wrongdoing. It reflects on the history of past nations who were destroyed due to their continual disobedience after the time of Noah. The latter part of the verse underscores God's comprehensive knowledge and awareness of human actions and sins, asserting His capability for judgment and His omniscience. It emphasizes that nothing escapes God's notice, reassuring believers of His just oversight.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: Whoever desires the immediate [worldly benefits], We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter to burn, condemned and banished.
interpretation: This verse addresses the individuals who prioritize worldly pleasures and gains over the eternal life of the Hereafter. It suggests that Allah may grant some of these immediate desires in this world according to His will and wisdom. However, it warns that such fleeting gains come at a great cost, as those who neglect the Hereafter will face severe consequences in Hell. This serves as a reminder to seek balance and prioritize eternal salvation over temporary worldly gains.
orig: من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as he should while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is appreciated [by Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of actively striving for the Hereafter with sincere effort and faith. It highlights that Allah values and rewards the endeavors of those who seek eternal life and work diligently towards it with a true belief in Him. This underscores the need for both faith and action in the pursuit of spiritual goals.
orig: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا

translation: To each [category] We extend—to these and to those—from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is not restricted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's provision and gifts are extended to all people, regardless of their beliefs or actions. It reflects the inclusiveness and vastness of God's mercy and generosity. Moreover, it implies that God's blessings are not limited or withheld based on human distinctions, inviting everyone to recognize and appreciate the benevolence of their Creator.
orig: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

translation: Look how We have favored some of them over others. But the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying levels of favor and blessings bestowed upon individuals in this world. However, it emphasizes that the differences in this life are insignificant compared to the vast distinctions and higher ranks that will be awarded in the Hereafter. The ultimate reward and honor lie in the life to come, and it serves as a reminder to prioritize eternal success over temporary worldly gains.
orig: انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا

translation: Do not set up another god with Allah, lest you be censured and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse admonishes against associating partners with Allah, emphasizing strict monotheism. It warns that such an act leads to disapproval and abandonment, signifying severe spiritual and social consequences for those who engage in idolatry. The emphasis is on the importance of exclusive devotion to Allah for guidance and support.
orig: لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age while with you, say not to them [so much as], 'uff,' and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the monotheistic principle of worshiping only Allah and underscores the importance of treating parents with the utmost respect and kindness, particularly when they become elderly. It commands believers to refrain from the slightest gesture of impatience or disrespect, represented by saying 'uff,' and to always address parents with honor and gentleness. The directive highlights the high status of parents in Islam and the moral obligation to care for them with compassion and dignity.
orig: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing humility and compassion towards one's parents, recognizing their efforts and sacrifices in raising their children. It teaches the believer to pray for their parents' mercy and well-being, acknowledging the significant role they played in their upbringing. The imagery of lowering a wing suggests an attitude of gentleness and respect, reinforcing the value of honoring and caring for one's parents in Islam.
orig: واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا

translation: Your Lord knows best what is in your souls. If you are righteous, then indeed He is ever forgiving to those who turn to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has complete knowledge of the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals. It offers reassurance to those striving for righteousness by highlighting God's attribute of forgiveness, particularly towards those who repent and seek His guidance with sincerity.
orig: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا

translation: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the rights of relatives, the poor, and travelers by providing them with what they need. It also warns against wasteful expenditure, implying that resources should be used responsibly and in a manner that benefits others, rather than squandered on unnecessary extravagance.
orig: وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of wastefulness, associating it with the rebellious nature of devils. It suggests that extravagance and squander align a person with satanic characteristics, which are rooted in ingratitude and defiance towards God. Thus, it serves as a strong admonition to practice moderation and be thankful for the blessings bestowed by God, avoiding excessive or unnecessary expenditure.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord that you hope for, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse advises that if one cannot assist those in need due to personal limitations while hoping for the mercy and provision from Allah, they should still communicate with them kindly and promisingly. It encourages maintaining compassion through considerate and gentle speech, even when direct help cannot be offered, which reflects the importance of maintaining dignity and positive moral conduct at all times.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And do not make your hand as chained to your neck, nor extend it completely and thereby become blamed and insolvent.
interpretation: This verse advises against both excessive stinginess and extreme generosity. A balanced approach to spending and giving is recommended, ensuring that one does not fall into financial difficulty or face blame for either extreme. It emphasizes the importance of moderation and responsible financial management in one's life.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute control over the distribution of sustenance. It highlights that Allah, with His complete knowledge and awareness of His servants' circumstances, dispenses and withholds provisions as He deems fit. This divine wisdom ensures that His decisions are not arbitrary but are based on a profound understanding of what is best for every individual.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Surely, killing them is a heinous sin.
interpretation: This verse instructs against the pre-Islamic practice of infanticide driven by fear of economic hardship. It emphasizes that God is the ultimate provider for all, assuring that the sustenance of every individual, whether parent or child, is under His care. Thus, taking the life of a child out of fear of poverty is not only unnecessary but also a grave sin. This underscores the sanctity of human life and the importance of trusting in Divine providence.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of committing adultery or fornication by not just prohibiting the act itself but warning against even coming close to it. It underscores the immorality and sinful nature of such actions, highlighting that they corrupt the individual and society, and lead one away from the righteous path. The verse calls for vigilance and self-restraint to maintain purity and uphold moral integrity.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed wrongfully – We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of life, highlighting that the taking of a life is only permissible under a legitimate legal reason. It underscores the gravitas of wrongful killing and grants the victim's heir the right to seek justice. However, it cautions against excessive retaliation, ensuring that justice is pursued within the bounds of fairness and law, reinforcing the principle that the law supports righteous actions and deters vengeance.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in the best way until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical and moral treatment of orphans and their property. It instructs believers not to misuse or unjustly approach the wealth that belongs to orphans, except in a manner that is beneficial for them, and only until they are mature enough to handle their own affairs. Additionally, it underscores the importance of fulfilling promises and covenants, as such commitments will be accountable to Allah. The verse highlights the responsibilities one has towards the vulnerable in society and the seriousness of upholding one's word.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is the best and fairest way to result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in commercial transactions. It instructs believers to give full measure when measuring goods and to use an accurate balance when weighing items. The underlying principle is that just and equitable dealings foster trust and righteousness in society. This directive aligns with the broader Islamic ethical guidelines that promote fairness, reduce deceit, and aim for harmonious social relations.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a clear admonition to only speak and act on matters where one possesses true knowledge. It emphasizes that all forms of receiving and processing information—through hearing, seeing, and feeling—carry a responsibility. Each person will be held accountable for how they use these faculties, reminding the believer to seek truthful knowledge and avoid spreading falsehoods or unfounded claims.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse advises against arrogance and pride. It emphasizes humility by reminding humans of their limitations and smallness in comparison to the vastness of the earth and the height of the mountains. The imagery serves to humble the individual, encouraging behavior that is modest and grounded, highlighting the importance of humility in one's actions and demeanor.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: All of that—its evil is ever, in the sight of your Lord, detested.
interpretation: This verse highlights that certain behaviors and actions are deeply disliked and condemned by Allah. It underscores the importance of adhering to a moral and ethical code that is pleasing to Allah, warning against indulging in actions that incur His displeasure. The verse serves as a reminder that while individuals have free will, they are accountable to a higher moral authority for their deeds.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: This is part of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you. And do not set up another deity alongside Allah, or you will be cast into Hell, blameworthy and rejected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine wisdom revealed by Allah, which includes the core principle of monotheism. It warns against associating any partners with Allah, highlighting severe consequences such as being cast into Hell, facing blame, and being rejected. This underscores the central message of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah) in Islam, and stresses the importance of exclusive worship and reliance on Allah alone.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: Has your Lord favored you with sons and taken angels as females for Himself? Indeed, you say a grave saying.
interpretation: This verse addresses the erroneous beliefs and misconceptions held by people who claimed that Allah has taken angels as daughters while giving them sons. It highlights the absurdity and serious nature of such a statement, emphasizing that attributing gender and familial relationships to the divine is a profound and egregious misstatement. The verse serves as a reproach for those who propagate such disrespectful and unfounded notions about the nature of Allah and His creation.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an so that they may be reminded, but it does not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God has presented various signs, lessons, and messages in the Qur'an in different forms and contexts to facilitate understanding and reflection. However, despite these efforts to guide people towards the truth, those who are disinclined or opposed to its teachings only grow in their resistance and aversion. This emphasizes the obstinacy and refusal of some people to accept divine guidance, regardless of the clarity and diversity of the message presented to them.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: Say, 'If there had been with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of monotheism in Islam and conveys an argument against polytheism. It posits that if there were multiple gods, they would seek supremacy or a higher connection to the ultimate deity, which is Allah, the Owner of the Throne. The verse emphasizes the singularity of God's sovereignty and ultimate authority, negating the existence of any equal or rival deities.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: Exalted is He and high above what they say by great sublimity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and incomparability of God. It confirms that God is far above and beyond any false attributes or descriptions that people may ascribe to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the unique and unparalleled nature of God's existence and qualities, rejecting any form of association or anthropomorphism.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that all of creation, from the vast expanses of the heavens to the smallest entities on earth, glorifies Allah. However, human beings might not perceive or comprehend the way other creations engage in this praise. It serves to remind believers of the omnipresence of divine worship and Allah’s inherent qualities of patience and forgiveness.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed partition.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) recites the Qur'an, a spiritual barrier is created by Allah between him and those who reject belief in the Hereafter. This barrier serves to protect the Prophet from their harmful intentions and disbelief. Additionally, it implies that the disbelievers are unable to truly understand or benefit from the recitation, as their hearts and minds are veiled from its guidance and wisdom due to their own rejection.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn back in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual state of those who reject the message of the Qur'an; their hearts are metaphorically covered, preventing them from understanding its message, and their ears are deaf to its recitation. It emphasizes the deliberate ignorance and aversion of disbelievers towards the Quranic message, particularly when the oneness of God is proclaimed.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: We are most knowing of what they listen to when they listen to you, and when they are in private conversation, when the wrongdoers say, 'You follow not but a man affected by magic.'
interpretation: This verse reflects God's omniscience regarding the intentions and discussions of the disbelievers, even in their private gatherings. It highlights their dismissive and derogatory attitude towards the Prophet Muhammad, accusing him of being under the influence of magic. This underscores their stubborn rejection of the divine message he brings, despite their covert intrigue and attention to his words.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they coin comparisons for you; but they have gone astray, and therefore cannot find a way (to the truth).
interpretation: This verse addresses the attempt of disbelievers to discredit the Prophet Muhammad by creating false analogies or comparisons. Despite their efforts, they have deviated from the truth and are unable to guide themselves or others towards righteousness. It emphasizes the futility and misguidance inherent in their actions.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they say, 'When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we truly be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse captures the skepticism and disbelief of those who doubt the concept of resurrection after death. It reflects their incredulity at the idea that, after being reduced to mere bones and dust, they could be brought back to life in a new form. The verse challenges the limits of human understanding and faith, emphasizing the power of Allah to recreate life from what seems impossible.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, 'Be you stones or iron.'
interpretation: This verse conveys a challenge to those who doubt the resurrection. It suggests that even if they were as hard and enduring as stones or iron, they would still be subject to God's power to resurrect them. The metaphor emphasizes the futility of resisting God's decrees, illustrating that His will is absolute and all-encompassing, regardless of the physical form one might take.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or any other creation which you deem even harder (in your hearts to be resurrected)—they will say, 'Who will bring us back (to life)?' Say, 'The One Who created you the first time.' Then, they will shake their heads at you and say, 'When will that be?' Say, 'Perhaps it will be soon.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of disbelievers regarding resurrection. It emphasizes that no matter how impossible resurrection may seem, Allah, who created them initially, has the power to recreate them. The shaking of heads signifies mockery or doubt, but the response serves to warn them that the event they doubt could come unexpectedly soon, highlighting the certainty of Allah's power and the imminence of the Day of Judgment.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: On the Day He will call you, and you will respond with praise of Him and think that you had not remained [in the world] except for a little.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Resurrection when God will summon all of creation. The response of the people will be immediate and filled with praise for their Creator, recognizing His ultimate authority and power. It indicates that the time spent in the worldly life will seem remarkably short in comparison to the eternal life hereafter. This perspective emphasizes the transient nature of worldly existence and the enduring reality of the Hereafter.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And tell My servants to say what is best. Indeed, Satan sows discord among them. Indeed, Satan is ever, to mankind, a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse advises the believers to use kind and thoughtful speech. It acknowledges that Satan constantly attempts to create conflicts and misunderstandings among humans by exploiting their words and actions. By urging the use of 'the best' words, the verse emphasizes the power of language in fostering peace and harmony, while also recognizing the persistent and unmistakable nature of Satan's enmity towards humanity.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you; if He wills, He will have mercy upon you, or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you over them as a manager.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that He knows His creation better than anyone else. It highlights that mercy and punishment are purely at His discretion, reinforcing the notion of divine will. Additionally, it clarifies the role of the Prophet, indicating that he is not a guardian or controller over the people but rather a messenger who delivers God's message.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly favored some of the prophets over others, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme knowledge over all beings in the heavens and the earth, asserting His divine authority and wisdom. It acknowledges that while all prophets hold a noble status, Allah has distinguished some with unique honors and roles, exemplified by citing Prophet David's special receipt of the Psalms (Zabur), highlighting both the diversity and unity among the prophets.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim [to be gods] besides Him; they do not possess the ability to remove harm from you or change [your condition].'
interpretation: This verse challenges the belief in and reliance on other deities besides Allah. It emphasizes the impotence of these entities, stating that they lack the power to alleviate suffering or alter one's situation. The verse calls for recognition of the sole omnipotence of Allah and serves as a reminder to seek help only from Him, as He alone has control over all matters.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: Those whom they call upon [to worship] themselves seek the means of access to their Lord, [striving as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping beings other than Allah by highlighting that even those beings themselves are in a constant state of seeking closeness to Allah, hoping for His mercy, and fearing His punishment. It underscores the notion that only Allah is worthy of worship as He is the ultimate source of mercy and deliverer of punishment, and even the most revered beings are dependent on Him. The verse also serves as a reminder of the balance between hope in Allah's mercy and fear of His punishment, guiding believers to sincere devotion and righteous conduct.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: There is no city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That has been written in the Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and accountability. It indicates that all communities are accountable to God, and they will face destruction or severe punishment if they persist in their wrongdoing. This is a predetermined decree documented in the divine record, emphasizing the certainty and seriousness of God's judgment.
orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And nothing has prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reason God refrains from sending additional miraculous signs to communities: historical precedent shows that previous peoples, despite witnessing clear signs, still chose to reject them. The mention of Thamud and the she-camel serves as a historical example of such denial. God's sending of signs is meant as a warning and reminder, emphasizing human responsibility and the consequences of ignoring divine guidance.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We told you, 'Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people.' And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people, as was the accursed tree [mentioned] in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him that Allah is fully aware and in control of the people. The 'sight' mentioned here likely refers to either a vision or the Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj) that served as a trial or test for people's faith. The 'accursed tree' symbolizes something deeply negative or corrupt, which adds to the trial. Despite divine warnings, these tests and signs only lead the disbelievers to increase in their rebellion and wrongdoing.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblis. He said, 'Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?'
interpretation: This verse recounts the moment when Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam as an act of respect for the creation of humanity. All the angels complied except for Iblis (Satan), who refused out of arrogance and pride. Iblis' refusal is rooted in his belief of superiority over Adam, created from clay, highlighting his disobedience and the beginning of his role as the adversary to humankind. This act of defiance signifies the first instance of arrogance and disobedience against Allah’s command, setting the stage for the ongoing conflict between good and evil.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: He said, 'Do You see this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few.'
interpretation: This verse captures the arrogance and defiance of Satan (Iblis) after being expelled from Paradise. He challenges Allah, pointing out the honor given to Adam over him and vows to mislead and corrupt Adam's descendants until the Day of Resurrection. This reflects the ongoing enmity between Satan and humanity, and serves as a warning to mankind about Satan's intentions and the importance of remaining vigilant and obedient to Allah.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: He said, 'Go, but whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell will be your recompense, an ample recompense.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a conversation between God and Iblis (Satan) where God permits Iblis to attempt to lead humans astray, but warns that those who follow Iblis will face Hell as their deserved and full recompense. It serves as a reminder of the consequence of choosing to follow evil and the justice of divine punishment.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: Incite whoever among them you can with your voice, rally against them your cavalry and infantry, share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing but deceit.
interpretation: This verse outlines the tactics that Satan uses to mislead and harm humans. By using various forms of temptation and deception, including influencing through speech, using force, and making false promises, Satan aims to lead people away from the path of righteousness. However, it's emphasized that Satan's promises are ultimately deceptive and illusory, highlighting the importance of being vigilant and steadfast in faith to avoid his traps.
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the protection and authority Allah has over His true servants. It reassures them that Satan or any evil cannot have control over them as long as they remain faithful and committed to Allah. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is sufficient as a Guardian and Protector, reinforcing the idea of ultimate reliance and trust in Allah for all matters.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: Your Lord is He who drives the ships for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He is ever Merciful towards you.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's role in facilitating human endeavors and providing means of livelihood, such as enabling ships to traverse the seas. It underscores the idea that the natural world operates under God's command, allowing people to gain from His provisions. Moreover, it emphasizes God's mercy, suggesting that He benevolently provides opportunities and sustenance for humanity.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: When adversity strikes you at sea, those you invoke besides Him vanish; but when He delivers you to the shore, you turn away. And man is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to seek God's help in moments of extreme distress, such as at sea when in danger. However, once they are safe and on solid ground, they often forget or turn away from their devotion to God. The verse underscores human ingratitude and fickleness in faith, emphasizing the inconsistency in human behavior towards the divine.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Do you feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you or send against you a storm of stones? Then you would find no protector for yourselves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the potential consequences of human complacency and arrogance. It emphasizes the power and control of Allah over natural phenomena and serves as a warning that security in worldly matters cannot protect one from divine retribution. It calls on people to remain mindful of their actions and rely on the protection and mercy of Allah, rather than feeling overly secure in their own measures.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it once again and send upon you a hurricane of wind and drown you for what you disbelieved? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us an avenger.
interpretation: This verse highlights the vulnerability of humans and the power of God over natural elements. It questions the sense of security people might feel and warns them of the possibility that God could subject them once again to perilous conditions, such as a devastating wind, in response to their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of ingratitude and disbelief, and it reiterates that in such circumstances, people would have no one to champion their cause against God's will.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided them with good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor bestowed upon human beings by their Creator. It emphasizes the special status given to the children of Adam by highlighting their ability to traverse land and sea, their access to various provisions and blessings, and their elevated position compared to much of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the unique role and responsibilities humans have been given and encourages gratitude for the blessings and honor they have received.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: The Day We will call forth every people with their record [of deeds]. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and injustice will not be done to them, [even] as much as a thread [inside the date seed].
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment when each individual will be summoned with their respective leaders or scriptures. Being given the record in one's right hand symbolizes righteousness and success, indicating that such people will be permitted to read their record with satisfaction and assurance, knowing they won’t be wronged in the slightest measure. It emphasizes the ultimate fairness and justice of God's judgment.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: But whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who fail to perceive the truth and guidance from God in their worldly life, who are metaphorically 'blind,' will remain in spiritual blindness in the Hereafter. Moreover, their misguidance in the afterlife will be even greater, as their rejection of divine guidance in this world leads to an intensified distance from the true path in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you in order to make you invent about Us something else; and then they would have taken you as a friend.
interpretation: This verse warns of external pressures and temptations that aim to divert the Prophet Muhammad from adhering to divine revelation. It highlights the seriousness of the tests he faced, where certain people sought to manipulate him into fabricating statements about God. This verse underscores the firm stance required to maintain integrity and faithfulness to divine guidance, warning that yielding to such temptations would lead to false friendships based on inauthentic foundations.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine support given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his mission. It highlights the human susceptibility to external pressures and the potential ease of being swayed. However, it underscores that divine intervention plays a crucial role in ensuring that the Prophet remains firm and does not deviate from the path of righteousness despite external influences. This serves as a reminder of the importance of relying on divine support in the face of challenges and temptations.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: Then We would have made you taste double (punishment) in life and double (punishment) in death, and then you would not find any helper against Us.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against disobedience, particularly directed at the Prophet Muhammad, illustrating that if he were to fabricate any revelations, his punishment would be severe. The emphasis on 'double' in both life and death underscores the gravity of such an act and the complete lack of any protector or helper against divine retribution.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, they were about to drive you from the land to evict you from it. But then, they would not have remained after you, except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse reflects the struggles faced by the Prophet Muhammad and his followers during the early days of Islam, highlighting the opposition and attempts by adversaries to expel them from their land. It underscores divine assurance that those who attempt to disrupt the mission of the Prophet and displace the believers would eventually see their plans fail and their own time in power be short-lived. The verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet and his followers of God's protection and the temporary nature of their opponents' dominance.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: Such was Our way with the messengers We sent before you. And you will find no change in Our way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency and unchangeable nature of God's laws and methods through history. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad and believers that the challenges and opposition they face are part of a divine tradition experienced by previous prophets. Thus, it offers comfort and encouragement to remain steadfast, trusting in the divine plan that has always led to the ultimate success of God's messengers.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish the Prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the recitation at dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and timing of Islamic prayers. It instructs believers to perform their prayers regularly from midday when the sun begins to decline until the night. The verse also highlights the special significance of the dawn prayer, noting that the recitation of the Qur'an during this time is particularly witnessed, possibly by angels or an added divine presence, underscoring its spiritual importance and the tranquility it brings.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And during a part of the night, pray Tahajjud beyond what is obligatory for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised position.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to engage in the voluntary night prayer, known as Tahajjud, in addition to the obligatory prayers. The act of praying during the night is presented as a means by which he may be granted a special honored position by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It signifies the importance of extra devotional acts and their potential to elevate one's status with Allah.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, 'My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'
interpretation: This verse is a supplication in which a believer asks God for guidance and integrity in all endeavors. The 'sound entrance' and 'sound exit' symbolize seeking righteousness and truth in all actions and decisions, ensuring one's paths are just and sincere. The request for 'supporting authority' underscores the need for divine aid and strength to overcome challenges, emphasizing reliance on God's power and wisdom to succeed and gain support in righteous causes.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, 'Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the triumph of truth and the inevitable downfall of falsehood. It emphasizes that truth, represented by Divine revelation and guidance, is everlasting and will ultimately prevail. In contrast, falsehood, no matter how persistent, is transient and doomed to disappear. This passage encourages believers to hold steadfast to the truth and reassures them of its ultimate victory over any form of deceit or falsehood.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We send down from the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an serves as a source of both spiritual and moral healing and mercy for those who have faith. However, for those who persist in wrongdoing and injustice, it further exposes their errors and results in greater detriment, as they reject its guidance and deepen in their deviation.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: But when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inconsistent nature of humans in their relationship with Allah. When granted blessings, they often become heedless and ignore their devotion to Allah. However, when faced with hardship, they become despondent and lose hope. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining faith and gratitude in all circumstances, rather than being fickle and ungrateful depending on one's situation.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, 'Each works according to his manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the individuality of actions and intentions, emphasizing that each person acts in alignment with their own inherent nature and understanding. It reinforces the concept that ultimate knowledge and judgment regarding who is truly guided and righteous lie solely with Allah, reminding believers to remain humble and focused on their own path of righteousness while trusting in Allah's wisdom and judgment.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you about the soul. Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the profound and mysterious nature of the soul, emphasizing that its true essence and knowledge are known only to Allah. It highlights the limited nature of human understanding and knowledge, reminding believers to acknowledge and accept the divine wisdom and the limits of their comprehension.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could surely do away with that which We revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself regarding it any protector against Us.
interpretation: This verse indicates the absolute power and authority of Allah over His revelation. It serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a divine gift which, if Allah so wills, can be taken away. This reinforces the notion of divine authority and the transient nature of worldly assurance, emphasizing reliance on Allah alone rather than on any intermediary or protector when it comes to matters of faith and divine guidance.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: But a mercy from your Lord; indeed, His favor upon you has been great.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound mercy and favor of Allah upon the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, the believers. It emphasizes that the blessings and guidance provided by Allah are not random but a deliberate act of immense grace and kindness. This also serves to remind the readers of the underlying benevolence of the divine in every favor and mercy granted, encouraging gratitude and recognition of Allah's boundless generosity.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say, 'If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unparalleled and divine nature of the Qur'an. It challenges both humans and supernatural beings (jinn) to produce something comparable but asserts that they would be unable to do so, even if they worked together and supported one another. This highlights the Qur'an's unique eloquence, depth, and divine origin, reinforcing the belief in its authenticity and divine revelation.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an every [kind] of example for the people, but most of the people refused [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, explaining that it provides a wide array of examples and teachings to guide humankind. Despite this extensive guidance, it observes human nature's frequent inclination towards ingratitude and disbelief. This underscores the challenge faced in guiding people towards faith and righteousness, illustrating the depth of entrenched disbelief even when clear guidance is provided.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they say, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and demand for miracles by some people as a condition for faith. It showcases their reluctance to believe in the message of the prophet unless they witness supernatural signs, indicating a propensity towards demanding physical proofs rather than having faith in the divine message conveyed through the prophet.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or you have a garden of date palms and grapes, and make rivers gush forth in their midst abundantly.
interpretation: This verse explores the disbelief and demands of the skeptics who challenge the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to perform miraculous acts, such as creating a lush garden with date palms and grapevines and causing rivers to flow through it plentifully, to prove his prophethood. The emphasis is on their unrealistic demands for physical signs and miracles, which serve as a distraction from the true message of faith and spiritual understanding. It highlights the materialistic mindset of those who deny the message of Islam, focusing on earthly wonders rather than the divine guidance offered by the Qur'an.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you have claimed or bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad, demanding him to prove his prophethood through miraculous signs, such as causing the sky to fall in pieces or bringing Allah and the angels visibly before them. It highlights their obstinate disbelief and reliance on extraordinary demands rather than sincere faith and reflection. The verse denotes their deep-seated skepticism and reluctance to accept the divine message based on clear signs and reasoning.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And even then, we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read. Say, 'Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the demands of skeptics who doubted the Prophet Muhammad's authenticity and demanded miraculous signs, such as a house of gold or ascending to the sky, to believe in him. The response emphasizes the Prophet's human nature and his role as a messenger, highlighting that miraculous signs are not the criteria for faith. It underscores the importance of recognizing the divine message over seeking extraordinary, materialistic proofs.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, 'Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and refusal of some people to believe in the guidance brought by the Prophet simply because he was a human being. It highlights the irrationality of their disbelief and their expectation that a divine message should be delivered by some extraordinary being rather than a human. This serves to emphasize that Allah's wisdom in choosing human messengers is part of His divine plan and that guidance can come through relatable, accessible means.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, 'If there were angels walking around on earth, feeling safe, We would have sent down to them an angel from the heavens as a messenger.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of divine messages and messengers. It emphasizes that if angels were the inhabitants of the earth, the divine messenger sent to them would have been an angel. This implies that God's wisdom considers the nature and needs of the recipients when determining the form of the messenger. Since humans are on earth, the messengers sent to them are human in form to ensure relatability and understanding, enhancing the effectiveness of the divine message.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the ultimate witness and judge of truth. It reassures that Allah’s knowledge and perception encompass all actions and thoughts of His servants, serving as a reminder that divine oversight and judgment are ever-present. This speaks to the absolute and decisive authority of Allah, encouraging believers to turn to Him for validation and reassurance in the face of disputes or accusations.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whomever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whomever He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and control of Allah over guidance and misguidance. It declares that only those guided by Allah are truly on the right path, and those whom He allows to stray will find no protector besides Him. On the Day of Resurrection, the consequences of one’s actions will manifest vividly: those who were led astray will be raised in a state of utmost helplessness, embodying their spiritual blindness, muteness, and deafness. Their final abode will be Hell, where their punishment will intensify, reflecting the severity of their deviation from divinely-guided paths during their earthly life.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse explains that the punishment of the disbelievers is a consequence of their denial of the divine signs and their skepticism about the resurrection. By questioning the possibility of being brought back to life after turning into bones and dust, they reveal their lack of faith in God's power to recreate existence, thus justifying the recompense they face.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Did they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse anything except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse stresses the omnipotence of Allah, highlighting His ability to create the universe and, similarly, human beings. It emphasizes that Allah has set a definite term for all creation, which is inevitable and certain. Despite this, those who commit injustices and wrongdoings persist in their disbelief and rejection of the divine truth, thereby sealing their own fate.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, 'If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold (them) out of fear of spending. And ever has man been stingy.'
interpretation: This verse addresses human nature, highlighting a tendency towards stinginess and fear of loss. It suggests that even if humans had access to the infinite mercy and wealth of God, they would still be reluctant to give or spend, driven by an inherent fear of depletion and a desire to hoard resources. This verse serves as a critique of human selfishness and a reminder of the generous and boundless nature of divine mercy, contrasting it with human limitations.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: Indeed, We gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, 'Indeed I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support granted to Prophet Moses in the form of nine clear signs or miracles, which served as evidence of his prophethood. Despite these signs, Pharaoh dismissed Moses' message as sorcery, showing a hardened heart and a refusal to accept divine truth. It serves as a reminder of the resistance faced by prophets and the rejection of divine signs by those who are obstinate.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He said, 'You know well that none has sent down these (signs) except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights, and I surely think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.'
interpretation: This verse is a response to Pharaoh wherein a clear assertion is being made about the divine origin of the signs that have been sent down. It emphasizes that these signs are from the Lord of the heavens and the earth, meant to provide insight and guidance. There is also a direct and bold pronouncement about Pharaoh's condition, indicating that his persistent denial and arrogance have led to his ruin. It reflects the obstinate nature of Pharaoh and the inevitable consequences of rejecting divine truth.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: So he intended to drive them out from the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the tyrant Pharaoh's attempt to expel the Children of Israel from Egypt. However, his deceitful plan was thwarted by divine intervention, leading to the ultimate destruction of Pharaoh and his forces through drowning. It highlights the consequences of arrogance and injustice, illustrating that oppressive actions against the innocent will eventually lead to ruin and divine retribution.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, We will bring you forth in (one) gathering.'
interpretation: This verse indicates that after the period of wandering, the Children of Israel were commanded to settle in the land appointed for them. It then alludes to a future event, the Day of Judgment, when they will be gathered together. This emphasizes both the temporal settlement in this world and the eventual gathering for judgment in the Hereafter, signifying divine control over both worldly and spiritual destinies.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an was revealed with truth and for a truthful purpose. It underscores the divine and authentic nature of the message that it carries. Furthermore, it clarifies the dual role of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a giver of glad tidings to those who believe and do good works, and a warner to those who reject faith and indulge in wrongdoing. This verse encapsulates the balance of hope and warning as central aspects of Islamic teachings.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deliberate and gradual revelation of the Qur'an, highlighting the wisdom behind its phased delivery. It underscores the importance of reflecting on the Qur'an deeply and understanding it over time, rather than hastily. The methodical revelation was intended to allow people to internalize its teachings and implement its guidance in their lives progressively.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, 'Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark difference in responses to the revelation of the Qur'an. It highlights that true knowledge and wisdom lead to humility and submission to God's words. Those who were granted knowledge recognize its truth and are compelled to prostration out of respect and acknowledgment of its divine origin, regardless of the disbelief or skepticism of others.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, 'Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'
interpretation: This verse is an expression of the believers' recognition and gratitude towards God. They acknowledge the perfection and glory of their Lord, affirming that what God has promised—be it mercy, reward, or judgment—has surely come to pass. It underscores faith in God's promises and the fulfillment of His word, reinforcing the believers' trust in divine wisdom and justice.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional and spiritual impact that the revelations have on the believers. Their response of falling down in prostration and weeping signifies a profound sense of humility and devotion. The act of weeping in this context illustrates the overwhelming feeling of reverence and submission to Allah, showing that true faith and recognition of divine truth lead to greater humility and piety.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, 'Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names.' And do not recite too loudly in your prayer or too quietly but seek between that an [intermediate] way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and the magnificence of God, whether He is called Allah or the Most Merciful, as all Names are equally supreme and beautiful. It also provides guidance on maintaining a balanced approach in worship, specifically in prayer, advising neither to be overly loud nor excessively quiet but to adopt a moderate approach. This balance fosters mindfulness and sincerity in devotion.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has no partner in His dominion and has no need for a protector out of weakness; and glorify Him with great glorification.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and majesty of Allah. It rejects any notion of Allah having a son or partner, highlighting His complete independence and self-sufficiency. The verse calls for praising and glorifying Allah, recognizing His unmatched sovereignty and power, and reflects the core Islamic tenet of monotheism. It reinforces the concept that Allah does not require any help or assistance, further setting Him apart from any created being.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: Praise be to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude and reverence to Allah for bestowing the Qur'an upon Prophet Muhammad, referred to as His Servant. The phrase 'has not made therein any deviance' emphasizes the perfection, clarity, and consistency of the Qur'an, signifying that it is free from any contradictions or errors and offers a straight path for guidance.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: It is upright to warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do good deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual purpose of the message of the Qur'an: to warn and to give glad tidings. The warning serves as a reminder of the severe consequences for those who disbelieve and engage in unrighteous actions. On the other hand, it reassures the believers who engage in righteous deeds that they will receive a generous reward. This balance of fear of divine retribution and hope for divine reward is intended to guide people towards a righteous and balanced life.
