interpretation: This verse reflects a prophetic prayer made by Zakariya (Zachariah) asking for a righteous offspring who would carry forward his spiritual legacy and the legacy of the family of Jacob. It signifies the importance of spiritual inheritance and the plea for future generations to remain devout and be favored by God.
orig: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا

translation: O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name.
interpretation: This verse addresses Prophet Zechariah, announcing the miraculous birth of his son, John (Yahya). The verse highlights the unique nature of John's name and the special status he will hold. It reflects God's power to bestow blessings and the divine plan that includes extraordinary events and individuals.
orig: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the astonishment and wonder of Prophet Zechariah regarding the divine promise of having a child despite his old age and his wife's barrenness. It captures the human aspect of questioning the feasibility of great miracles while also foregrounding the power and capability of divine intervention. The verse emphasizes God's ability to accomplish what may seem impossible to human beings.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا

translation: He said, 'So it will be. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing.'
interpretation: This verse communicates God's omnipotence and ability to create life effortlessly. It highlights the ease with which God can bring about events and outcomes, reminding believers that God's power transcends human limitations. By referencing the creation of a human from nothing, it emphasizes the miraculous nature of divine creation, reinforcing faith in God's supreme capability and authority.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, being sound.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Zakariya (Zechariah) is asking Allah for a sign to confirm his wife's pregnancy, as it was a miraculous event given their advanced age. Allah responds by giving him a sign: Zakariya will be unable to speak to people for three nights despite being in good health. This sign serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's ability to create miracles and signifies that His commands are carried out perfectly, irrespective of natural circumstances.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

translation: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary and signaled to them to glorify Allah in the morning and in the evening.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Zachariah (peace be upon him), after being blessed with the news of a child despite his old age, comes out from his place of worship and communicates to his people through signs, urging them to remember and praise Allah regularly, both in the morning and evening. This signifies the importance of persistent worship and gratitude towards Allah, regardless of the circumstances.
orig: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا

translation: O John, take the Scripture with determination. We granted him wisdom while still a child.
interpretation: In this verse, God addresses Prophet John (Yahya), urging him to embrace the divine commandments with steadfastness and earnest commitment. The verse emphasizes the exceptional nature of John's spiritual maturity, highlighting how he was endowed with wisdom even from a young age. This serves as an example of divine favor and the importance of resolute faith and earnest engagement with divine teachings.
orig: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة وآتيناه الحكم صبيا

translation: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues bestowed upon a righteous individual from Allah. 'Affection from Us' signifies divine love and compassion granted by Allah. 'Purity' refers to spiritual and moral cleanliness. The quality 'he was fearing of Allah' denotes the individual's piety and consciousness of Allah, guiding their actions and decisions. The verse underscores that such qualities are gifts from Allah and mark the character of those truly devoted to Him.
orig: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا

translation: and dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being obedient and dutiful to one's parents, portraying such behavior as an integral aspect of righteousness. The verse contrasts this virtue with the negative traits of being stubborn and disobedient, suggesting that true piety and moral uprightness include respect and kindness towards parents. It highlights the honor and value placed on family relationships and the moral responsibility one has to maintain them through respectful behavior.
orig: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse conveys a divine blessing of peace upon the individual at three significant stages of existence: birth, death, and resurrection. It signifies the importance of these key transitions in one's life and the continuity of God’s mercy and protection throughout. This also serves to underline the sacred nature of the individual's mission and life, reassuring believers of divine support and peace in times of change and uncertainty.
orig: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا

translation: And mention in the Book (the story of) Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
interpretation: This verse highlights the piety and modesty of Mary. It signifies an important moment of spiritual solitude and preparation, emphasizing her special status and dedicated worship. The setting 'toward the east' may also symbolize enlightenment and guidance, resonating with themes of divine presence and the direction of prayer in Islamic tradition, underscoring her role in the unfolding divine plan.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: She took a veil to screen herself from them; then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared before her as a perfect man.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Maryam (Mary), the mother of Isa (Jesus), secluded herself from her people for privacy and devotion. In this state of seclusion, Allah sent the Angel Jibril (Gabriel) to her in the form of a perfectly human man. This encounter signifies the divine intervention and the beginning of the miraculous birth of Isa, emphasizing the purity and chosen status of Maryam. The veil she took symbolizes both her modesty and her separation for a higher divine purpose.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: She said, 'I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah.'
interpretation: This verse portrays a moment of Mary seeking protection from an unexpected visitor, highlighting her piety and trust in the Most Merciful (Allah). Her invocation of God's name underlines the emphasis on seeking divine refuge in moments of uncertainty or potential harm, showcasing her faith and strength.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: He said, 'I am only a messenger of your Lord to announce to you the gift of a pure boy.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when the angel Gabriel addresses Mary (Maryam), assuring her that he is a messenger from Allah sent to grant her the news of a forthcoming son, a pure and virtuous child, who will be born miraculously. This signifies the divine nature of Jesus’ (Isa’s) birth and underscores the purity and sanctity of his life right from conception, highlighting the miraculous intervention of God in human affairs.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: She said, 'How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, Maryam (Mary), is expressing her astonishment and confusion at the announcement of her giving birth to a son despite being a virgin and living a chaste life. This reflects her purity and the miraculous nature of the birth of her son, Isa (Jesus), as described in the Qur'an.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: He said, 'Thus said your Lord, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that what appears miraculous to humans is effortless for Him. The reference to making 'him' a sign and mercy to the people underscores the divine purpose in the miraculous birth of a prophet, serving as a clear indicator of God's power and a source of guidance and compassion to humanity. The phrase 'a matter [already] decreed' signifies the certainty and inevitability of Allah's will, highlighting His supreme authority over all affairs.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Mary (Maryam) conceives Jesus (Isa) and, realizing the enormity of her situation, seeks solitude away from her community. The act of withdrawing signifies her awareness of the extraordinary nature of her pregnancy and possibly a need for safety, privacy, and perhaps to ponder upon the divine event she is experiencing.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: Then the pains of labor drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the intense emotional and physical distress experienced by Maryam (Mary) during childbirth. In her moment of vulnerability and isolation, she expresses a deep sense of despair, wishing she had been forgotten and spared from her trials. This highlights the human experience of pain and anguish, even among the most pious and chosen individuals, and underlines the profound trials that can come with divine missions.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: Then he called her from beneath her: 'Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.'
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Maryam (Mary) when she is in the pains of childbirth and feeling distressed. Allah sends an angel to comfort her and assure her that she is not alone. The message is one of divine support and providence, emphasizing that God is aware of her situation and has already provided for her needs. The stream mentioned symbolizes the provision and mercy of Allah, signifying that He takes care of His servants in their times of hardship.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
interpretation: This verse refers to Maryam (Mary) during the time of childbirth, where she is guided to shake the trunk of a palm tree. The act of shaking the tree, resulting in fresh dates falling, symbolizes the importance of action and self-effort even in the face of divine intervention. The fresh dates also signify nourishment and ease during her difficult time, highlighting God's compassion and provision in moments of hardship.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to any man.'
interpretation: This verse provides comfort and reassurance, instructing to find solace and not worry. It specifically addresses Mary, telling her to eat and drink peacefully and to not be troubled. If she encounters anyone, she is to explain that she has vowed a fast of silence to God, signifying a period of reflection or devotion during which she will not engage in communication with others. This signifies reliance on divine support, even in challenging times, and highlights the importance of finding peace and solace in faith.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: "Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.'"
interpretation: This verse addresses the moment when Maryam (Mary) returns to her community carrying her newborn son, 'Isa (Jesus). The community's reaction reflects their astonishment and disbelief at her giving birth, particularly since she was known to be chaste. They accuse her of an unprecedented and forbidden act, demonstrating their inability to comprehend the miraculous nature of Jesus's birth and indicative of the cultural and societal norms regarding morality and purity at the time.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse is addressing Mary, the mother of Jesus, emphasizing her noble lineage and the purity of her parents. The reference to 'sister of Aaron' serves to draw a parallel to the pious lineage of Aaron, the brother of Moses, highlighting her family's longstanding righteousness. This serves to counter any accusations against Mary's chastity, reinforcing her purity and the honor of her family.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: But she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous event of baby Jesus speaking from the cradle. When Mary was confronted by people questioning her about the baby, she pointed to infant Jesus. The people were skeptical and questioned how it could be possible to communicate with a newborn. This sets the stage for Jesus’s miraculous speech, which serves as a sign of his prophethood and divine mission from a very young age, emphasizing the power and will of God to enable miracles.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: He said, 'I am indeed a servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a Prophet.'
interpretation: In this verse, it is when Jesus (Isa), peace be upon him, speaks from the cradle, affirming his servitude to Allah and the source of his prophecy and knowledge. It emphasizes the idea that Jesus, although bestowed with special attributes and divine guidance, is still fundamentally a servant of God. This declaration points to the humility and obedience inherent in divinely chosen individuals and underscores the source of their wisdom and leadership—directly from God, which includes the mission to guide and teach humanity according to divine injunctions.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And He made me blessed wherever I am and enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I live.
interpretation: This verse reflects the qualities bestowed upon a devout servant of Allah. Being 'blessed wherever I am' signifies that the person carries divine grace and positive influence irrespective of their location. The emphasis on the continuous practice of prayer and giving alms (zakah) underlines the importance of maintaining spiritual and social responsibilities throughout one's life. It suggests that the true sign of faith involves consistent adherence to these pillars, demonstrating one's devotion to God and commitment to helping others.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of filial piety and kindness towards one's mother, emphasizing that goodness and humility towards parents are virtues blessed by God. It warns against being arrogant and harsh, suggesting a correlation between one's conduct towards parents and overall moral character.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I will be raised to life again.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of three key moments in human existence: birth, death, and resurrection. It highlights the divine protection and tranquility bestowed upon an individual at these critical junctures. Specifically, in the context of Prophet Isa (Jesus), it underscores the miraculous nature of his birth, the serenity during his departure, and the certainty of his eventual resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder of God's encompassing mercy and the continuity of spiritual peace through life's transitions.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse asserts the true identity and nature of Jesus, emphasizing his humanity as the son of Mary and declaring this as the truth. It addresses the disputes and different views surrounding Jesus, affirming the Islamic perspective on his role and essence. The phrase 'the word of truth' underscores the authoritative nature of this statement in the context of religious discussions and theological debates.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: It is not befitting for Allah to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute transcendence and omnipotence of Allah. It refutes any notion of God having offspring, underlying the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of God in Islam. The verse also highlights Allah's supreme command and creative power, illustrating that His will is executed simply by His command.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic tenet of monotheism, urging both the speaker and the audience to acknowledge Allah as the sole deity and to engage in His worship. It underscores that recognizing and serving Allah is the true and righteous path, guiding individuals towards a moral and secure way of living.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse indicates the internal divisions and disagreements among various groups regarding matters of faith and truth. It warns those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief, foreshadowing the dire consequences they will face on the Day of Judgement. The 'tremendous Day' refers to the Day of Resurrection, a day of monumental significance where every soul will be held accountable for its beliefs and deeds.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us! But today, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark difference between the present blindness of the wrongdoers and their eventual clarity on the Day of Judgment. In their current lives, they are in a state of manifest misguidance, unable or unwilling to perceive the truth. However, on the Day of Judgment, their senses will be heightened, making them acutely aware of the reality and gravity of their actions and the truth they had previously ignored. This serves as a warning to heed the message and guidance provided before it's too late.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided; and [yet] they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the Day of Judgment, referred to here as the Day of Regret. It highlights the sorrow and regret that will overwhelm those who did not heed the signs and messages of God, as they will be caught unprepared when the final decision is made. The verse also emphasizes the current state of many people who live in heedlessness, unaware and unbelieving in the approaching reality of this significant day.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate dominion and sovereignty of Allah over the entire earth and all its inhabitants. It signifies that, regardless of human ownership or control, everything will return to Allah, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly possession and the inevitability of returning to the Creator for final judgment and accountability.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and reflecting upon the life of the Prophet Abraham. It underscores his esteemed status as a truthful and trustworthy individual and his esteemed role as a prophet. This serves as an encouragement for believers to emulate his virtues of honesty, integrity, and faithfulness in their own lives.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?'
interpretation: This verse depicts a moment of questioning and guidance where a son, in a respectful address, challenges his father's worship of idols. The son highlights the futility of worshipping entities that lack the faculties of hearing and seeing, and that offer no benefit. This can be seen as a call to reason and a move towards the worship of the one true God, emphasizing the importance of worshipping something that has true power and can truly benefit the worshipper.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: "O my father, indeed I have received knowledge that you have not received, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path."
interpretation: This verse represents a dialogue between a prophet and his father, emphasizing the humble yet assertive conveyance of spiritual guidance. The prophet respectfully addresses his father, acknowledging a divinely endowed knowledge and urging him to follow the righteous path. It reflects a compassionate call to embrace faith and truth, underscoring the importance of wisdom and sincerity in guiding loved ones towards the divine path.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea from a concerned individual, probably a son, to his father, urging him to abandon the worship of Satan and recognize the righteousness of the Most Merciful (Allah). It emphasizes that Satan has always been disobedient to Allah and thus is unworthy of worship or following. The verse calls for guidance and adherence to the path of divine mercy and obedience to Allah rather than succumbing to the rebellion and misguidance symbolized by Satan.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so you would be to Satan a companion (in Hellfire).
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep sense of concern and compassion from a son towards his father. The son is warning his father about the consequences of straying away from the path of righteousness. By addressing his father with respect and affection ('O my father'), he expresses his fear that his father might face divine punishment if he continues to reject faith. The punishment from the Most Merciful signifies the seriousness of the situation, showing that even the most compassionate can issue stern consequences. The ultimate warning is about becoming an ally of Satan, which symbolizes complete deviation from divine guidance and resulting in severe spiritual repercussions.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: He said, 'Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a prolonged time.'
interpretation: This verse depicts a conversation between Abraham and his father (or his people), showcasing the strong opposition and threat faced by Abraham for rejecting the polytheistic deities they worshipped. The threat of stoning and the command to stay away for a long period reflect the intensity of the confrontation and the seriousness of the conflict between monotheism, represented by Abraham, and the prevailing idolatrous beliefs. It highlights the courage of Abraham in maintaining his faith in the One God despite severe threats and societal pressure.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: He said: Peace be upon you! I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the importance of maintaining courteous and compassionate interactions, even with those who might oppose or reject one's beliefs. It reflects a strong sense of personal responsibility and devotion to seeking forgiveness on behalf of others, highlighting trust in God's grace and kindness. This can be seen as an encouragement to endure with patience and continue to supplicate for others, showcasing empathy and spiritual concern.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah and will call upon my Lord. I hope that I will not be unhappy in my supplication to my Lord.
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination of the speaker to distance himself from those who worship deities other than Allah and to devote himself solely to worshiping and supplicating to Allah. It highlights a hopeful trust in the benevolence and responsiveness of Allah to sincere supplication, indicating a belief that through patience and faith, one can attain peace and fulfillment.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: So when he had left them and those they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each of them We made a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward given to a prophet, commonly understood to be Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim), who distanced himself from his people and their idolatrous practices. In response to his faith and devotion, Allah blessed him with his son Isaac (Ishaq) and grandson Jacob (Ya'qub), both of whom were also honored with prophethood. This reflects the themes of faith, divine reward, and the continuation of prophetic legacy.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We granted them of Our mercy, and We made for them a reputation of high honor.
interpretation: This verse speaks of Allah's benevolence and grace bestowed upon certain individuals, acknowledging His mercy and favor as a source of their esteemed and honorable status. It signifies that divine blessings not only encompass material and spiritual benefits but also include a lasting and respected reputation among people, which is a mark of Allah's recognition and validation of their righteousness and virtues.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of Prophet Moses in Islamic tradition, highlighting his status as a chosen and purified servant of God. It reaffirms his dual role as both a messenger, conveying God's divine guidance, and a prophet, endowed with a particular mission. This distinction underscores the high regard in which Moses is held, serving as a model of dedication and fidelity to God's commands.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We called him from the right side of the mount, and made him draw near to Us for a conversation in secret.
interpretation: This verse speaks about Allah's interaction with Prophet Musa (Moses). Allah called Prophet Musa from the right side of Mount Sinai and brought him close to converse in secrecy. The verse highlights the special status of Prophet Musa, his close communication with Allah, and signifies the honor and direct guidance he received from Him.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We bestowed upon him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine mercy and support granted by Allah to His prophets. Specifically, it highlights how Allah, in His infinite grace, provided Prophet Musa (Moses) with his brother Harun (Aaron) as a prophet to assist and support him. This partnership underscored the importance of solidarity and mutual aid in fulfilling prophetic missions, emphasizing that divine missions often require cooperation and shared responsibilities.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the character and status of Prophet Ishmael (Ismail) in Islamic tradition. It praises his honesty and reliability, specifically regarding his fulfillment of promises. Additionally, it acknowledges his dual role as both a messenger and a prophet, emphasizing his significant position within the succession of prophetic figures. This serves as an example for believers to emulate his virtues of truthfulness and commitment.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And he used to enjoin upon his people prayer and zakah and was to his Lord pleasing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character and devotion of a righteous individual who not only adheres to the key pillars of worship—prayer (salah) and almsgiving (zakah)—but also ensures that his family observes these practices. His commitment to these principles and his leadership in guiding his family in faith make him pleasing to his Lord, illustrating the importance of personal piety and the nurturing of a faith-driven household.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: In this verse, God instructs the Prophet Muhammad to mention Idrees (Enoch). Idrees is praised for being a truthful person and a prophet, emphasizing his high moral character and elevated status. This serves as a reminder to value truthfulness and acknowledges the various prophets sent to guide humanity.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This verse refers to the exaltation and honoring of a specific individual or prophet by Allah, elevating them to a status of high honor and distinction, signifying their importance and righteousness in the sight of Allah.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: They are those whom Allah has blessed from among the prophets from the descendants of Adam, and from those We carried with Noah, and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from among those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall in prostration and weep.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of the prophets and those chosen by Allah throughout human history. From Adam to Noah, and from Abraham to Israel, it emphasizes a lineage of divinely guided individuals who were blessed and favored by Allah. Their response to the recitation of Allah's verses – falling in prostration and weeping – showcases their deep faith, humility, and reverence for the divine message. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being receptive and emotionally connected to the revelations of Allah.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: But there came after them successors who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the decline of moral and spiritual discipline among the followers who came after the righteous predecessors. It emphasizes the detrimental consequences of neglecting one's religious duties, particularly prayer, and succumbing to worldly desires. The neglect of these core spiritual practices leads to a path of deviation and ultimately, significant regret or punishment. It serves as a stern warning to maintain the integrity of faith and devotion to prevent such an outcome.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and justice of Allah. It highlights that no matter one's past actions, if a person sincerely repents, embraces faith, and follows up with righteous deeds, they will be granted entry into Paradise and will not suffer any injustice. It underscores the principles of repentance, faith, and positive action as the path to redemption and divine reward.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been coming.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of Heaven (Jannah) as promised by Allah to His righteous servants who have faith in the unseen. It emphasizes the certainty of Allah's promise, indicating that it is a definitive and inevitable reality. The term 'Gardens of perpetual residence' signifies eternal bliss and reward for those who believe and adhere to Allah's guidance.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: They will not hear therein any ill speech—only [greetings of] peace—and they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tranquility and serenity in Paradise, where no vain or harmful talk exists, only peaceful greetings. It also emphasizes the abundant and regular provision of blessings to the inhabitants, illustrating a constant state of fulfillment and contentment throughout the day.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: That is the Paradise which We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were pious.
interpretation: This verse underscores that Paradise is a divine reward and inheritance specifically reserved for those servants who exhibited piety and righteousness in their lives. It emphasizes the link between one's actions, particularly in terms of piety and devotion, and the attainment of eternal reward. The use of the word 'inheritance' signifies that it is a promised and rightful possession for those who have fulfilled their duties and lived in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between, and your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the descent of angels or revelation is solely by the command of Allah, highlighting His supreme authority and control over all things. It also underscores that Allah possesses total knowledge of the past, present, and future, and He is free from forgetfulness. This serves to reassure believers of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, and to underscore that everything happens according to His divine will.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone similar to Him?
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty and majesty of Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists in the heavens and the earth and everything in between. It commands the believers to worship Allah alone and remain patient and steadfast in their devotion and service to Him. The rhetorical question posed at the end emphasizes the uniqueness and incomparability of Allah, reaffirming that there is no one and nothing that is equal or similar to Him in His essence and attributes, thereby underscoring His absolute monotheism.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And man says, 'When I am dead, will I be brought forth alive?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and doubt that many people harbor about the possibility of life after death. It captures a common existential question and reflects human curiosity and uncertainty about what happens after we die. The question underscores humanity's limited understanding and often cynical perspective regarding the promise of resurrection and the afterlife as conveyed by divine revelations.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse prompts humans to reflect on their origins and recognize the power and mercy of God in their creation. It serves as a reminder of human humility and the transient nature of existence, encouraging gratitude and reverence towards the Creator.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: Then, by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a stern warning that all individuals, along with the devils who led them astray, will be gathered and made to face the consequences of their actions. The imagery of people being brought to their knees around Hell underscores the seriousness and gravity of the punishment awaiting those who disbelieve and commit evil deeds.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst against the Most Merciful in insolence.
interpretation: This verse indicates that during the Day of Judgment, God will single out individuals from every group or community who were the most rebellious and insolent against Him. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and the particular focus on those who showed severe arrogance and disobedience towards the Most Merciful, highlighting that their actions will not go unnoticed and unpunished.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then We are most knowing of those most worthy of burning therein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's ultimate knowledge and justice in determining who is most deserving of punishment in Hell. It underscores the concept that God, in His infinite wisdom, is fully aware of the actions and intentions of individuals, and it is based on this comprehensive understanding that He assigns the appropriate recompense or punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine justice and the consequences of one’s deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
interpretation: The verse indicates that every person will come into contact with the reality of Hell, suggesting that the passage through or encounter with Hell is an inescapable decree from Allah. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this encounter as a divine decree, signifying the ultimate justice and comprehensive accountability in the Hereafter. It serves as a solemn reminder that the effects of one's actions in this life are inevitable and unavoidable.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that Allah will differentiate between the righteous, who have lived with piety and consciousness of Allah, and the wrongdoers, who have acted unjustly and arrogantly. The pious will be granted salvation, whereas the wrongdoers will be left in a state of utter humiliation, symbolized by being on their knees, representing both physical and moral downfall.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two groups is better in position and superior in assembly?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and superficial judgments of the disbelievers, who equate material wealth and social standing with true success. They challenge the believers by comparing their worldly status, overlooking the spiritual and eternal values that the believers hold. It serves as a reminder that true worth is not determined by earthly measures but by one's faith and adherence to divine guidance.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them who were better in equipment and outward appearance.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly wealth and beauty. It emphasizes that many prosperous and seemingly invincible generations before the current one have been destroyed by God despite their superior material comforts and appearances. The core message is to highlight the importance of humility and righteousness over pride in material success and external beauty, underscoring the ultimate authority and justice of God in determining the fate of peoples and civilizations.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension until, when they see what they were promised - either punishment or the Hour - they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are in error or disbelief will be allowed by Allah, the Most Merciful, to continue in their ways for a period of time. However, when the promised events such as divine punishment or the Day of Judgment (the Hour) eventually arrive, it will become clear who truly held a weaker position and was more vulnerable. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that ultimately, the truth will be unveiled, and the consequences of one's actions will be evident. It underscores the temporary nature of worldly power and the ultimate triumph of divine justice.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah increases those who were guided, in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for return.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah grants additional guidance to those who seek it and follow the right path. It emphasizes that good deeds, especially those with lasting impact, hold greater value and reward in the sight of Allah. The verse also draws attention to the eternal benefits of righteous actions, suggesting that they lead to better outcomes in the Hereafter.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children?'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who arrogantly deny divine signs and boast of their worldly possessions and future prospects. It reflects their misplaced confidence and their failure to recognize that true success and provision come from Allah, not from their own merits or efforts. The verse serves as a reminder that material wealth and progeny are not the ultimate indicators of divine favor or success in this life or the hereafter.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim knowledge of the unseen or future without divine authority, questioning whether they possess any special access to hidden knowledge or an assured promise from God, highlighting human limitations and the necessity of humility before divine wisdom.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: No! We will record what he says and extend for him from the punishment extensively.
interpretation: This verse underscores that God is fully aware of the defiant claims made by disbelievers and that such assertions will be documented and held against them. It serves as a warning that continuous punishment will extend as a consequence of their persistent denial and falsehood, emphasizing the accountability and the inescapable nature of divine justice.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And We will inherit what he mentioned, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly possessions and human claims. It indicates that whatever a person boasts about or claims in this life will ultimately belong to Allah upon their death. Moreover, every individual will stand before Allah alone, without any material possessions or worldly support, to account for their deeds.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken beside Allah gods, hoping that they might be helped (by them) or receive honor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the error and futility of those who turn to other deities besides Allah, believing that these false gods will provide them with support, protection, or honor. It emphasizes the misguided nature of their worship and reliance on these entities, as true help and honor can only come from Allah alone.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: No! They will reject their worship and become opponents against them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and ultimate rejection of those who worship others besides Allah. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, these false deities or idols will disavow the worship offered to them and instead will stand as accusers against those who wrongly worshipped them. The verse highlights the clear misguidance and ultimate regret faced by those who do not worship Allah alone.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: Do you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them to [evil] with [constant] incitement?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are influenced by the devils, who encourage and agitate them towards evil and sinful behaviors. It emphasizes the role of these entities in leading people away from the path of righteousness and towards actions that are in opposition to divine will. The verse serves as a warning about the presence and impact of these malicious forces and underscores the importance of seeking protection and guidance from God to remain steadfast in faith.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: So do not be impatient over them. We are only counting out [to them] a number.
interpretation: This verse is advising patience when dealing with transgressors or those who deny the truth. It reassures that there is a divine plan in place, and that every moment, action, and intention is being meticulously recorded and accounted for by Allah. The phrase 'We are only counting out [to them] a number' implies that a specific period of respite or a fixed term is being allotted to them. During this time, they have the opportunity for reflection and repentance. Ultimately, it emphasizes the inevitable accountability and divine justice that will manifest in due time.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when those who have lived righteous lives, guided by their faith and piety, will be gathered and presented to Allah, the Most Merciful. The term 'delegation' signifies honor and respect, implying that the righteous will be given a special status and reception in the presence of Allah. It reflects the ultimate reward for their devotion and piety during their earthly lives.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst.
interpretation: This verse depicts a vivid and severe outcome for those who have committed grave sins and disobediences—termed as 'criminals'. They are portrayed as being driven towards Hell, indicating a sense of inevitability and a loss of control over their fate. The mention of 'thirst' signifies their desperate state and the suffering they will endure, highlighting the stark contrast to the comfort and fulfillment promised to the righteous. This serves as a powerful admonition and a reminder of the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: They have no power of intercession, except those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the power of intercession on the Day of Judgment does not lie with everyone, but exclusively with those who have established a special covenant with Allah, the Most Merciful. This covenant implies true faith, righteousness, and sincere devotion. It emphasizes the importance of a sincere relationship with Allah as a requisite for intercession, highlighting the limitations of unauthorized intercession and redirecting the believers’ focus to their personal piety and accountability.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the false claim made by some people who suggest that Allah, referred to here as the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman), has taken a son. This statement is refuted and criticized in the Qur'an because it contradicts the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. In Islam, Allah does not have offspring or partners, and attributing such human characteristics to Him is considered a grave error.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: You have done an atrocious thing.
interpretation: This verse points out the severity and gravity of the action addressed, suggesting that it is something deeply wrong and harmful. It serves as a strong rebuke, highlighting the serious nature of the offense committed.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heavens almost rupture therefrom and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe and overwhelming effects of certain grievous actions or statements, notably those involving shirk (associating partners with Allah). It illustrates the magnitude of the reaction of the cosmos, created by Allah, which almost splits apart in response to the gravity of such acts. It is a vivid reminder of the seriousness of attributing partners to Allah and the monumental impact this has in the balance of the universe. The heavens, earth, and mountains are depicted as almost unable to bear the enormity of this transgression, symbolizing the profound disturbance caused by deviance from pure monotheism.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.
interpretation: This verse condemns the assertion that Allah, the Most Merciful, has begotten a son. It emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any association of partners or offspring with Him. Such claims are regarded as a serious deviation from the core belief in the absolute monotheism of Islam.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of God's absolute and unique oneness, rejecting any notion that He could have a son or any kind of human-like lineage. It underscores that attributing human characteristics or familial relationships to the Divine is inconsistent with the nature of the Most Merciful, who transcends all these human attributes. The verse aims to clarify and affirm the pure monotheism central to Islamic belief.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: There is no one in the heavens and the earth but that he will come to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all creation. Every being in the heavens and the earth is completely subservient to Allah and will ultimately return to Him as His servant. It highlights the fundamental Islamic concept of monotheism (Tawhid) and underscores the humility that all creatures must acknowledge before their Creator.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: He has enumerated them and counted them precisely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's comprehensive knowledge and meticulous accounting of all things. It conveys the idea that nothing escapes God's awareness, and He meticulously keeps track of every detail. This could be a reminder to believers of God's omniscience, encouraging them to live conscientious and righteous lives, knowing that all their actions are observed and recorded by God.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And each one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual accountability that every person will face on the Day of Judgment. Each person will stand alone before Allah, without any support from family, friends, or social status. It underscores the importance of personal responsibility for one's actions and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong correlation between faith, righteous deeds, and divine love. It suggests that true belief, coupled with good deeds, results in Allah’s love and affection. This divine affection could manifest in various forms, such as inner peace, love among people, or blessings in both the worldly life and the hereafter. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to consistently engage in good actions and maintain their faith, assuring them of divine favor and support.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings to the righteous and warn by it a hostile people.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an has been revealed in a manner that is clear and easy to understand, particularly in the Arabic language, which was the language of the Prophet Muhammad. The purpose of this revelation is twofold: first, to give glad tidings to the pious and God-conscious individuals who follow the guidance, and second, to serve as a warning to those who are stubborn and antagonistic towards the message. It emphasizes the dual role of the Qur'an as a source of both encouragement and admonition.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them! Do you perceive of them anyone or hear from them a sound?
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of human civilizations and serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It emphasizes that numerous powerful and prosperous communities of the past were ultimately destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and disbelief. The rhetorical questions at the end highlight the utter disappearance of these civilizations; no trace of them remains, nor any sound of their existence is heard, serving as a contemplation point for the contemporaries to heed the warning and turn back to righteous living.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: Ta-Ha.
interpretation: This verse consists of the disjointed letters 'Ta' and 'Ha,' which are among the mysterious, alphanumeric characters found at the beginning of certain chapters in the Qur'an. The specific meanings of these letters are not definitively known, and they are considered one of the Qur'an's great linguistic and theological mysteries. Scholars believe they serve as a divine code, signaling the miraculous nature of the Qur'an's composition and inviting deeper contemplation and reflection on the text.
orig: طه

translation: We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an was revealed not as a burden or cause of distress, but as a source of guidance, comfort, and mercy. It serves as a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad and to all believers that the purpose of the revelation is to provide guidance and facilitate a path to spiritual fulfillment and well-being.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: But a reminder to those who fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and a form of guidance specifically for those who have reverence and fear of Allah. It implies that the true benefit and understanding of the divine message are most accessible and impactful to those who are conscious of their spiritual and moral responsibilities.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting its revelation as coming from the Creator of both Earth and the high heavens. It seeks to remind the reader of the immense power and authority of the one who sent down the message, reinforcing the significance and the truthfulness of the Qur'anic guidance.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Merciful, who is established on the Throne.
interpretation: This verse signifies the transcendence, authority, and sovereignty of Allah. 'The Most Merciful' (Al-Rahman) emphasizes His attribute of boundless mercy, and His establishment on the Throne symbolizes His supreme power and control over the universe. It reassures believers of Allah's omnipotence and His all-encompassing mercy.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute ownership and sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It reinforces the idea that every element of the universe, from the heavens to the earth and everything in between, as well as what lies beneath the soil, belongs to Allah. This underscores His supreme authority and the encompassing nature of His dominion, suggesting that nothing exists outside of His control and knowledge.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and omniscience. It highlights that whether a person speaks openly or keeps their thoughts concealed, God is fully aware of both the spoken words and the unspoken secrets within hearts. It serves as a reminder of God's intimate awareness of human intentions and inner thoughts, guiding believers to be mindful of their actions and words, as nothing is hidden from divine awareness.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, affirming that there is no other deity but Him. It also highlights that Allah possesses the most beautiful and perfect names, which reflect His attributes and essence. These names serve as a means for believers to understand Allah's grandeur and to call upon Him.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: Has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: This verse serves as an introduction to a narrative about the Prophet Moses. It invites the listener to reflect upon Moses' life and experiences, emphasizing the importance and relevance of his story. It sets the stage for lessons to be learned from Moses' encounters and the divine messages he received. The question form personalizes the message, making it more engaging and prompting introspection.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When he saw a fire and said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the moment when Prophet Moses (Musa) sees a fire and decides to go towards it, leaving his family behind temporarily. He hopes to obtain a light or receive guidance. This illustrates a moment of hope and anticipation for divine guidance, indicating a pivotal moment where an encounter with the divine is imminent. It emphasizes the human quest for enlightenment and divine communication in times of need.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: But when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!'
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Moses approached the burning bush on Mount Sinai and was addressed by Allah. The verse signifies a profound and transformative event in Moses' life, marking the beginning of his prophetic mission. The direct call from Allah underscores Moses' selection for a divine purpose and highlights the importance of obedience and readiness to respond to God's call.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command from Allah to Moses upon his arrival at the sacred valley of Tuwa, signifying the sanctity of the place through the act of removing his sandals. It emphasizes the need for reverence and humility before the divine presence. The instruction highlights the spiritual transformation and readiness required for Moses to undertake his prophetic mission.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special selection of the Prophet by God for a divine mission. It underscores the importance of attentively listening and adhering to the messages and revelations from God, implying a responsibility to recognize, internalize, and act upon divine guidance faithfully.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of monotheism, emphasizing that Allah is the sole deity deserving of worship. It calls upon believers to devote themselves exclusively to Allah, underscoring the importance of worship and particularly the practice of regular prayer as a means to maintain a constant awareness and remembrance of Allah. This directive establishes the foundation for a life centered around devotion and the presence of Allah in the believer's daily actions.
orig: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming—I almost conceal it—so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of the Day of Judgment and God's deliberate intention in almost concealing its exact time. The purpose of this concealment is to ensure that every individual is judged fairly and rewarded or punished based on their efforts and actions without being influenced by the knowledge of the exact timing of the Hour. This encourages sincerity and consistent striving towards righteousness.
orig: إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

translation: So let not one avert you from it who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you would then perish.
interpretation: This verse warns against allowing oneself to be swayed or misled by individuals who do not believe in the teachings of the Qur'an and instead follow their own desires and inclinations. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and adherence to divine guidance, highlighting the potential consequences of deviating from this path, which could lead to one's spiritual and moral downfall.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse features a direct question from God to Prophet Moses, highlighting a moment meant to draw Moses’ attention to his staff. The question sets the stage for demonstrating God’s miraculous powers through Moses, as what follows in the narrative is the transformation of the staff into a serpent. This also serves to establish Moses’ role as a prophet and the bearer of God's signs.
orig: وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى

translation: He said, 'It is my staff; I lean upon it, and with it, I bring down leaves for my sheep, and I have other uses for it.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is speaking to God, explaining the various purposes of his staff. The staff symbolizes not only a physical tool that assists him in tending to his flock and providing stability but also signifies his reliance and trust in God's guidance and support. The mention of 'other uses' indicates the multifaceted nature of the means provided by God, serving multiple functions that support both worldly needs and spiritual duties.
orig: قال هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ولي فيها مآرب أخرى

translation: He said: 'Throw it down, O Moses!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment where Allah commands Moses to cast down his staff. This command is a demonstration of divine power and authority, leading up to a miraculous event that would prove Moses' prophethood and the truth of his mission. It signifies trust in divine instruction and the unfolding of a supernatural sign, underscoring the theme of faith in God’s commands and the wonders He can perform through His messengers.
orig: قال ألقها يا موسى

translation: So he threw it down, and behold, it was a snake, moving swiftly.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Moses, upon God's command, cast his staff to the ground, and it miraculously transformed into a snake. The event signifies the power and authority bestowed upon Moses by God, demonstrating that he is supported by divine miracles in his mission. It is a moment of awe and serves to affirm the prophets' divine mandate, emphasizing God's capability to alter the natural order to fulfill His purposes.
orig: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

translation: He said, 'Take it and do not fear. We will return it to its former condition.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes trust in divine protection and assurance. It suggests that what might seem daunting or miraculous is within God's power to control and restore to its original state. The command to 'take it and do not fear' underscores the importance of faith and courage in the face of seemingly difficult tasks, with the promise that God will restore things to how they should be.
orig: قال خذها ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will come out white without disease—another sign.
interpretation: This verse is a part of the dialogue between Allah and Prophet Moses (Musa). It signifies a miracle granted to Moses, where placing his hand under his arm and then bringing it out would reveal it to be shining bright white without any illness or harm. This miracle, along with others granted to Moses, serves as a sign of his prophethood and the divine support he possesses to confront Pharaoh and lead the Israelites. It underscores Allah's power and the authenticity of the divine message bestowed upon Moses, encouraging faith and trust in his mission.
orig: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى

translation: So that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse indicates the purpose of demonstrating Allah’s divine signs to the people. These signs serve as clear evidence of Allah’s supreme power, wisdom, and authority. By manifesting these signs, Allah aims to guide people towards faith, reflection, and acknowledgment of His presence and omnipotence.
orig: لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

translation: Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse depicts a divine command directing the Prophet Moses to approach Pharaoh. It underscores Pharaoh's excessive transgression and tyranny. The verse serves as a prelude to the grand narrative of Moses confronting Pharaoh's oppression and guiding his people towards liberation. It also exemplifies the broader Quranic themes of divine justice and the responsibility of prophets to deliver God's message to those in power, irrespective of opposition or danger.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my chest.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Moses' (Musa's) invocation to Allah for spiritual and emotional strength. By asking for an expansion of his chest, he seeks ease, confidence, and the ability to overcome any anxieties or hindrances in fulfilling his mission. It symbolizes a plea for inner peace, clarity, and the fortitude necessary to convey the divine message effectively.
orig: قال رب اشرح لي صدري

translation: And make my task easy for me.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication requesting divine assistance in making one's endeavors smooth and free from difficulties. It reflects a humble recognition of human limitations and a reliance on God's support to overcome challenges and achieve goals more effectively.
orig: ويسر لي أمري

translation: And untie the knot from my tongue.
interpretation: This verse speaks to a plea for clarity and effectiveness in communication. It signifies a request for ease in expressing oneself, removing any barriers that might hinder clear and coherent speech. This can be seen as a broader metaphor for seeking assistance in overcoming personal obstacles that prevent one from conveying their thoughts and messages effectively.
orig: واحلل عقدة من لساني

translation: understand my speech
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea or desire for one's words to be comprehended by others. It emphasizes the importance of clear communication and understanding in conveying messages effectively. The speaker seeks that their spoken messages are grasped correctly, highlighting the significance of mutual comprehension in dialogue or discourse.
orig: يفقهوا قولي

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family
interpretation: This verse reflects a request for support and assistance from a trusted member of one's family. It underscores the importance of seeking help from close and reliable family members in carrying out significant duties or tasks, indicating a preference for collaboration and trust within the familial bonds.
orig: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: This phrase indicates a direct reference to Prophet Aaron (Harun) who is acknowledged as the brother of Prophet Moses (Musa). In various contexts within the Qur'an, mentioning 'Aaron, my brother' signifies the close familial and supportive relationship between Aaron and Moses. It often emphasizes the unity and cooperation between them in their prophetic mission and in facing the challenges posed by their community or adversaries.
orig: هارون أخي

translation: Strengthen my back with him.
interpretation: This verse is a plea to Allah for support and reinforcement through the assistance of another individual. It signifies the importance of seeking strength through unity and companionship, showcasing that the burden of responsibilities and challenges can be alleviated when supported by trustworthy and dependable allies.
orig: اشدد به أزري

translation: And associate him in my task
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for assistance in sharing a significant responsibility or task. It underscores the importance of collaboration and seeking support from others when undertaking important missions. This highlights a key principle in Islamic teaching about the value of partnership and collective effort in fulfilling duties.
orig: وأشركه في أمري

translation: So that we may glorify You much
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of frequent remembrance and glorification of Allah. It signifies a deep devotion and continual praise for God's greatness, illustrating a desire to remain constantly conscious of His presence and attributes. This also shows a commitment to acknowledging God's role in all aspects of life, recognizing His blessings, and expressing gratitude consistently.
orig: كي نسبحك كثيرا

translation: And we will remember You much.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of frequent remembrance of God. In the context of worship and daily life, continual awareness and recollection of God’s presence and attributes are encouraged as a means to align one's actions and thoughts with divine will.
orig: ونذكرك كثيرا

translation: Indeed, you have always been seeing us.
interpretation: This verse recognizes God's omnipresent awareness and supervision over human actions and conditions. It reflects an acknowledgment of His continuous vigilance, reminding believers of God's perpetual presence and insight into their lives, encouraging mindfulness and a sense of accountability in their behavior.
orig: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا

translation: He said, 'You have been granted your request, O Moses.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of divine acceptance and approval of Moses's supplication. It reflects God's responsiveness to the prayers and needs of His prophets, emphasizing His mercy and readiness to support His messengers in their missions.
orig: قال قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

translation: And We have certainly bestowed favor upon you another time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuous and recurring blessings and favors bestowed by Allah upon an individual, emphasizing divine benevolence and the importance of recognizing and being grateful for these repeated acts of kindness.
orig: ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى

translation: When We inspired your mother with what was inspired
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when God communicated divine guidance to the mother of Moses. It underscores the intervention and protection granted by God during crucial moments, highlighting the importance of divine will and the role of mothers in the spiritual and physical preservation of their children. The use of 'inspired' indicates a direct and special communication from God, ensuring that His plans for Moses' mission are set into motion even from his infancy.
orig: إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

translation: ‘Put him into the chest, then cast it into the river. The river will throw it onto the bank; there, he will be taken by one who is an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.’ And I cast love over you from Me so that you would be brought up under My eye.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses as an infant, where God commands Moses' mother to place him in a chest and cast it into the river. This commandment was in response to the Pharaoh's decree to kill the newborn Hebrew boys. The river was to carry the chest to a place where it would be found by the Pharaoh's household, specifically by Pharaoh's wife, who would take the infant Moses in. Despite being in the hands of enemies, the protection and love of God enveloped Moses, ensuring that he would be safe and nurtured under divine care and grow up to fulfill his God-given mission. This narrative underscores themes of divine protection, destiny, and the unfolding of God's plan even in seemingly perilous circumstances.
orig: أن اقذفيه في التابوت فاقذفيه في اليم فليلقه اليم بالساحل يأخذه عدو لي وعدو له وألقيت عليك محبة مني ولتصنع على عيني

translation: When your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will nurse him?' So We returned you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained for years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse recounts several key events in the life of Prophet Moses (Musa). It highlights the divine plan and protection over him from his infancy to his prophetic mission. It references how his sister played a role in reuniting him with his mother, symbolizing divine mercy and familial bonds. The verse also recalls an incident where Moses unintentionally killed a man, yet God saved him from the repercussions and subjected him to various trials to prepare him for his future duties. His years in Madyan are depicted as a formative period, emphasizing the importance of patience and divine timing in his journey. Ultimately, it underscores the theme of divine guidance and destiny.
orig: إذ تمشي أختك فتقول هل أدلكم على من يكفله فرجعناك إلى أمك كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن وقتلت نفسا فنجيناك من الغم وفتناك فتونا فلبثت سنين في أهل مدين ثم جئت على قدر يا موسى

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse signifies a direct and personal selection by Allah. It conveys the notion of being specially chosen for a divine purpose, highlighting a unique and extraordinary role that is intimately connected with serving and fulfilling Allah's will.
orig: واصطنعتك لنفسي

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah to Prophet Moses (Musa) and his brother Aaron (Harun). It emphasizes the importance of carrying out their mission with the support of divine signs (miracles) and the necessity of constant remembrance of Allah. The repetition and persistence in remembering Allah serve as a source of strength and guidance for them as they confront the challenges ahead.
orig: اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ولا تنيا في ذكري

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Moses and Aaron, instructing them to approach Pharaoh, as he has exceeded all bounds of tyranny and disobedience.
