It underscores the duty of confronting injustice and guiding those who have strayed back to righteousness, emphasizing the importance of conveying the message of truth even to the most powerful and seemingly irredeemable figures.
orig: اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: Speak to him gently, that perhaps he may be mindful or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse advises the approach of kindness and gentleness in communication, even towards those who are wrong or misguided. The aim is to encourage reflection and fear of Allah, guiding them back to the right path. It underscores the importance of compassion and patience in efforts of correction and guidance.
orig: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the apprehension and humility of Prophet Moses (Musa) and his brother Aaron (Harun) when they are commanded by Allah to confront the Pharaoh. Their plea to Allah signifies their reliance on divine support and their fear of the Pharaoh's potential reaction, either to impose immediate harm upon them or to act with excessive arrogance and tyranny. It exemplifies the human vulnerability and the need for courage and faith when standing against oppressive powers.
orig: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى

translation: He said, 'Fear not, indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.'
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron of God's constant presence and support. By affirming that He hears and sees everything, God provides them with the confidence and courage to face their daunting mission. It highlights the concept of divine oversight and protection, emphasizing that God is fully aware of their circumstances and will guide them accordingly.
orig: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى

translation: So go both of you to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have brought you a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the mission of Moses and Aaron to the Pharaoh. It emphasizes their role as messengers of Allah, calling for the release of the Children of Israel and an end to their suffering. The sign from the Lord illustrates divine authority, while peace is promised to those who accept and follow divine guidance. The message highlights the importance of submitting to divinely ordained directives and the consequent blessings for compliance.
orig: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم قد جئناك بآية من ربك والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine revelation that punishment is decreed for those who reject the truth and turn away from the guidance that has been sent to them. It serves as a stern warning about the serious consequences of denying the messages of the prophets and choosing to stray from the path prescribed by Allah. It highlights the accountability individuals will face for their actions and their deliberate choices to ignore divine guidance.
orig: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

translation: He said: 'Who then is your Lord, O Moses?'
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is questioning Moses to challenge his claim of divine authority and to assert Pharaoh's own position as a ruler who is skeptical of any power beyond his own. This question sets the stage for Moses to declare the oneness and supremacy of Allah, which is central to his prophetic mission.
orig: قال فمن ربكما يا موسى

translation: He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided it.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of God's creation and guidance. It emphasizes that God not only created everything in its unique form but also provided guidance for each creation to fulfill its purpose. This reflects the meticulous and all-encompassing wisdom and care of God in the universe, ensuring that every entity, living or non-living, follows a divinely ordained path.
orig: قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

translation: He said, 'What about the former generations?'
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is questioning Moses about the fate of the earlier generations, possibly to challenge the legitimacy of Moses' message or to assert the continuity of his own traditions. This indicates Pharaoh’s resistance to change and reluctance to accept a divine message that contradicts the practices of his ancestors. It underscores the common human inclination to cling to established beliefs and customs, even in the face of new, transformative revelations.
orig: قال فما بال القرون الأولى

translation: He (Moses) replied, 'The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute and perfect knowledge of Allah. It underscores the notion that all matters, including intricate details and future events, are known and recorded by Allah in a divine record. It builds on the belief in God's infallibility and omniscience, emphasizing that unlike human beings, Allah does not make mistakes nor does He forget anything. This reassurance serves to remind believers of the comprehensive and flawless nature of divine knowledge and wisdom.
orig: قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى

translation: He who made the earth a cradle for you and made paths for you therein and sent down water from the sky, then We brought forth thereby pairs of diverse plants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's benevolence and power in creating a harmonious environment for human life. By referring to the earth as a 'cradle,' it highlights the nurturing and stable environment provided by God. The mention of paths indicates guidance and the facilitation of movement and progress. The reference to water from the sky and the diversity of plants symbolizes sustenance and the beauty of creation. It underscores the interdependence of all living things and the meticulous design of the environment, which supports life in myriad forms.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى

translation: Eat and pasture your cattle. Indeed, in that are signs for those of intelligence.
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah encouraging people to utilize the resources provided to them, such as food and livestock, emphasizing that these are blessings and signs from Allah. It calls on those with intellect and understanding to recognize these signs and reflect on the wisdom and mercy of Allah in providing sustenance and provisions essential for life. It underscores the importance of gratitude and acknowledgement of divine beneficence.
orig: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: From it (the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out once again.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cycle of human existence, originating from the earth, being returned to it after death, and ultimately being resurrected from it. It underscores the divine power and control over life, death, and resurrection, reminding humanity of their humble beginnings and the inevitability of their return to the Creator.
orig: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى

translation: And We certainly showed him all Our signs, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse refers to an individual who was shown clear and undeniable signs from Allah, representing the truth and divine guidance. However, despite the overwhelming evidence and the clarity of these signs, he chose to deny and reject them out of arrogance or stubbornness. This reflects the theme of free will in the Qur'an, where individuals are given the choice to accept or reject faith and guidance, and it emphasizes the consequences of refusing to acknowledge the truth even when it is made manifestly clear.
orig: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the confrontation between Prophet Musa (Moses) and the Pharaoh's people. The accusation directed at Musa implies a deep-seated fear and resistance from the ruling class, who perceive Musa’s divine signs and miracles as a threat to their authority and possession of the land. They dismiss his miracles as mere sorcery, thereby undermining the divine message and portraying Musa as someone using trickery rather than truth, to dispossess them.
orig: قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

translation: So bring for us a magic like it, and make an appointment between us and you which we will not fail to keep, neither we nor you, in a place convenient [for both].
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge posed to Moses by Pharaoh's sorcerers. The sorcerers are confident in their skills and challenge Moses to a contest of magic, setting an agreed upon time and place. This reflects the human tendency to confront perceived threats with tests of ability, often missing the deeper significance of divine signs and miracles.
orig: فلنأتينك بسحر مثله فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت مكانا سوى

translation: He said, 'Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning.'
interpretation: This verse refers to a moment where Prophet Musa (Moses) sets a specific time for a confrontation with the sorcerers of Pharaoh. The 'day of the festival' is noted as a significant time when people would gather. By setting the meeting at 'mid-morning,' it indicates a period when visibility is high, and the anticipation of a public and clear demonstration could lead to the truth prevailing over falsehood. It emphasizes the importance of transparency and the confrontation being witnessed by many, ensuring that the outcome would be seen and understood by all present.
orig: قال موعدكم يوم الزينة وأن يحشر الناس ضحى

translation: So Pharaoh withdrew, devised his plot, and then came back.
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's stubbornness and arrogance. Despite the clear signs and warnings given to him, he chose to turn his back on the truth. Instead of reflecting and correcting his ways, he decided to cunningly scheme against the message and the messenger, illustrating his deep-seated enmity and refusal to submit to divine authority.
orig: فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده ثم أتى

translation: Moses said to them, 'Woe to you! Do not invent lies against Allah, or He will exterminate you with a punishment. Indeed, he who fabricates (lies) has failed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights a stern warning from Prophet Moses to his people, urging them against fabricating lies about Allah. Moses warns them of severe divine repercussions for such actions and stresses that falsehood, especially against the divine, only leads to failure and ruin. It emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and the grave consequences of deceit.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: But they disagreed among themselves about the matter and kept their discussion secret.
interpretation: This verse highlights a situation where a group of people are in disagreement about an important issue and choose to keep their deliberations concealed. The secrecy may indicate their uncertainty, fear of external judgment, or the gravity of the decision at hand. It suggests themes of division, internal conflict, and potentially the presence of conflicting interests or beliefs within a community.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said, 'These are certainly two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your exemplary way of life.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the reaction of Pharaoh's followers to Moses and Aaron's mission. They accuse both prophets of being magicians with the intent to destabilize their society and remove the people from their land. This reflects the resistance met by divine messengers when confronting deeply entrenched systems of power and highlights the fear that the truth can pose to those benefiting from the status quo.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: So resolve upon your plan and then come forward in line. And he has succeeded today who has overcome.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the disbelievers or those who oppose the truth, urging them to gather all their schemes and come forth collectively to challenge. The final part of the verse provides a declaration of success for those who have achieved dominance or prevailed, highlighting the triumph of truth and righteousness over deceit and falsehood. It emphasizes that ultimate success lies with those who uphold what is right and just, despite the adversaries' plots.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the confrontation between Prophet Musa (Moses) and the magicians of Pharaoh. It represents a moment of challenge and decision. The magicians give Moses the choice to either cast his own staff first or allow them to cast theirs first, implying a test of power and faith. The underlying message is about the reality and power of divine miracles versus human trickery, showcasing the ultimate triumph of truth and faith over deceit and illusion.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: He said, 'You throw first.' Then, when they threw, their ropes and staffs appeared to him by their magic to be moving like snakes.
interpretation: This verse refers to the encounter between Prophet Musa (Moses) and the magicians at the court of Pharaoh. When the magicians threw down their ropes and staffs, their sorcery created an illusion that made these objects seem as if they were moving. This sets the scene for the demonstration of true divine power versus mere illusion, emphasizing the difference between the miracles of a prophet and the tricks of magicians.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: So Moses conceived a fear within himself.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human side of Prophet Moses (Musa), indicating that despite being a prophet, he experienced natural human emotions such as fear. This fear could be due to the enormity of the task he faced or the challenge posed by the sorcerers. It also shows that having fear is not inherently wrong, but what matters is how one overcomes it. In the subsequent verses, God's reassurance and support alleviate Moses's fear, emphasizing the theme of divine assistance and trust in God.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: We said, 'Fear not, indeed it is you who are superior.'
interpretation: This verse provides reassurance and encouragement, indicating divine support and the assurance of victory and superiority over adversaries. It emphasizes that fear should not dominate one's actions when one has faith and divine backing. It is often interpreted as a message to remain steadfast and confident in the face of challenges.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between divine miracles and mere illusions created by magicians. It highlights the supremacy of God's power, indicating that true divine intervention will inevitably prevail over deceit and trickery. Additionally, it serves as a warning that those who rely on deception and sorcery will ultimately fail in their endeavors.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
interpretation: In this verse, the magicians who were initially opposing Moses, upon witnessing the undeniable signs and miracles granted to Moses by Allah, recognized the truth and power of his message. Their immediate reaction was to prostrate themselves in submission and declare their belief in the one true God, identifying Him as the Lord of both Aaron and Moses. This act of faith highlights the transformative power of witnessing divine truth and the readiness of sincere hearts to accept it, regardless of their prior intentions or beliefs.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, 'Do you believe in Him before I permit you? Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, so I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more enduring.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Pharaoh and the magicians who, upon witnessing the miracles of Moses (Musa), believed in the One True God. Pharaoh, angered by their defiance and their acceptance of Moses' God without his permission, accuses them of conspiracy and threatens them with severe punishment. He aims to instill fear and demonstrate his power, warning them of dire consequences, which highlights his tyrannical and oppressive rule. The reference to cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion on palm trees emphasizes the brutal methods he uses to control and intimidate his subjects.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, 'We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us, and over Him who created us. So decree whatever you are going to decree, you can only decree for this worldly life.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness and conviction of the believers in the face of threats and pressures from powers of the earthly world. They express their unwavering dedication to the divine signs and to God who created them, highlighting their readiness to face any worldly consequences. It emphasizes the temporality and limited scope of earthly judgments compared to the eternal significance of adherence to divine truths. The believers' declaration underscores their ultimate allegiance to God, regardless of temporal authority or threats they might encounter in worldly life.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to practice. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse reflects the firmness of faith of the believers in their Lord. It highlights their hope for forgiveness for their past sins, including those actions they were forced into, such as practicing magic. Furthermore, it emphasizes their acknowledgment of Allah's supremacy and eternal essence compared to the transient nature of worldly power and compulsion. The verse showcases the believers' prioritization of divine forgiveness and the eternal nature of the divine over temporary earthly influences.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dire consequence of coming before God as a sinner. It describes Hell as a place where punishment is so severe that it strips away the essence of life without providing the relief of death. This serves as a stark warning to strive for righteousness and avoid sinful behavior, as the outcome of persistent wrongdoing is unending suffering in a state where neither the tranquility of life nor the finality of death can be found.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds—for those will be the highest ranks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who approach God with genuine faith and have demonstrated their belief through righteous actions will be granted elevated positions in the hereafter. It highlights the importance of both faith and good deeds in achieving spiritual success and divine reward.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. Such is the reward for those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the eternal paradise promised to those who purify themselves spiritually and morally. The imagery of lush gardens and flowing rivers symbolizes ultimate peace, contentment, and the divine reward awaiting the righteous. It emphasizes the importance of self-purification and moral integrity as pathways to divine favor and everlasting bliss.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We inspired to Moses, 'Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken, nor be afraid.'
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah’s command to Prophet Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt by night, ensuring their safety through the miraculous parting of the sea. This act of divine intervention underscores God's power and mercy, providing a path of escape in a seemingly impossible situation. It reassures believers that with God's guidance, they need not fear any pursuit or danger as long as they follow His commands.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, but there covered them from the sea that which covered them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate fate of Pharaoh and his soldiers as they tried to pursue the Israelites who were divinely assisted. Their pursuit leads to their complete engulfment by the sea, symbolizing the overwhelming and inescapable nature of divine retribution against tyranny and disobedience.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's role as a misguided leader who led his people away from the path of righteousness. It underscores the significant responsibility of leadership and the severe consequences of leading others astray. Pharaoh's actions are presented as a direct cause of his people's deviation from the truth, emphasizing the importance of guidance and the moral obligations of those in positions of authority.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of Mount Sinai, and We sent down to you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Israelites, reminding them of Allah's favor in rescuing them from their oppressors, specifically their exodus from Egypt under the tyranny of Pharaoh. It highlights Allah's guidance and blessings, such as arranging a sacred meeting at Mount Sinai where He provided them with divine instructions. Additionally, Allah's provisions of manna and quails symbolize His sustenance and care for the Israelites during their journey through the desert. The verse calls attention to the need for gratitude and obedience to divine commands in recognition of these mercies.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat of the good things which We have provided for you and do not transgress therein, lest My wrath should descend upon you. And those upon whom My wrath descends have certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of Allah's blessings and a warning against misuse or transgression concerning those blessings. The command to 'eat of the good things' emphasizes gratitude and moderation, while the admonishment against excess or wrongdoing ('do not transgress') highlights the principles of ethical conduct and respect for divine provisions. The warning about Allah's wrath serves as a grave reminder that consequences follow actions, and those who incur His wrath face severe spiritual downfall.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s boundless mercy and readiness to forgive those who turn back to Him with sincere repentance. It outlines the conditions for divine forgiveness: repentance (acknowledgement of sins and seeking forgiveness), firm belief in Allah, righteous deeds (actions that align with divine commandments), and steadfastness in following the right guidance. It signifies that true repentance is not merely a verbal declaration but must be accompanied by genuine faith, good conduct, and persistence in the right path.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Moses, questioning why he hurried away from his people. It can be interpreted as a gentle reminder from God for Moses to consider the reasons behind his actions and the importance of his people. It highlights the significance of responsibility and leadership, emphasizing that a leader should not abandon their people without significant cause.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: He said, 'They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, traditionally understood to be Prophet Musa (Moses), is explaining to Allah the reasons for his actions. By saying that his people are following closely behind him ('upon my tracks'), he emphasizes their unity and adherence to his guidance. His haste in coming to Allah underscores his eagerness to seek divine approval and signifies his deep devotion and desire to fulfill his religious duty. It implies a prioritization of divine pleasure over all worldly concerns.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, 'Indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray.'
interpretation: This verse describes a moment when Moses (Musa) is informed that his people have been tested and subsequently misled after his departure. The trial is brought about by the actions of the Samiri, who leads the people astray. This underlines the theme of faith being tested and the consequences of following misguided leaders. It serves as a reminder to adhere firmly to the righteous path, even in the absence of strong leadership.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful. He said, 'O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time of my absence too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?'
interpretation: In this verse, the Qur'an conveys a moment of deep frustration and disappointment for Prophet Moses upon his return to his people. Despite God's favorable promises, the people faltered in their faith and commitment during his absence. Moses questions whether it was the perceived delay that led them astray, or if they chose willful disobedience, thereby inviting divine anger. This scenario underscores themes of patience, adherence to divine guidance, and the consequences of breaking one's commitments.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, 'We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were laden with burdens from the ornaments of the people, so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri suggest.'
interpretation: This verse suggests a conversation where those being addressed explain their actions by saying they did not intentionally break their agreement. Instead, they were influenced by external circumstances; specifically, they were burdened with the ornaments of other people and cast them into the fire, following the suggestion of the Samiri. The verse highlights how external influences and the persuasion of influential individuals can lead a community to diverge from their promises and commitments.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: So he brought out for them a [mere] calf, a body with a lowing sound, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident where the Israelites, in the absence of Prophet Moses (Musa), were led astray by Samiri to worship a golden calf. Despite witnessing numerous signs of God's oneness and power, they fell into idolatry, revealing the ease with which faith can be compromised without steadfastness and guidance. The verse highlights the human propensity to relapse into familiar yet erroneous beliefs and the critical need for adhering to true guidance.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that it cannot return to them any speech and has no power either to harm them or benefit them?
interpretation: This verse prompts reflection on the futility and impotence of idolatry. It challenges individuals to recognize that idols, which cannot communicate or exert any influence on their worshippers' well-being, are inherently powerless. This emphasizes the importance of seeking aid and guidance from Allah alone, who possesses ultimate authority and capability.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And Aaron had certainly said to them before, 'O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful; so follow me and obey my order.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the guidance provided by Aaron (Harun) to his people when they created and worshipped the golden calf in his brother Moses' (Musa's) absence. Aaron reminds them that their submission to the calf is a test, emphasizing the importance of obedience to the true God, the Most Merciful. Aaron calls upon them to follow him and adhere to his directives, reinforcing the idea of prophetic authority and the continuous call to monotheism and righteous conduct in the face of trials.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, 'We will not cease to devote ourselves to it until Moses returns to us.'
interpretation: The verse reflects the stubbornness and determination of the people who chose to worship an idol in the absence of Prophet Moses. Despite being aware of the true faith, they are adamant in their misguided practice and assert that they will continue in their deviant worship until Moses comes back to guide and correct them. It highlights their dependence on Moses for guidance and their vulnerability to losing their way in his absence.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said: O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
interpretation: In this verse, Moses addresses his brother Aaron, questioning him on why he did not intervene when the people started to deviate from the right path. The implicit meaning underscores the importance of leadership and responsibility in guiding others toward righteousness and preventing their deviation from divine commands. Moses is expressing his disappointment and seeking an explanation, highlighting accountability among those in positions of authority, especially in matters of faith.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: Did you not follow me? Have you disobeyed my command?
interpretation: This verse reflects a situation where a leader or a person of authority is questioning someone who was expected to follow their directives. It highlights the importance of obedience and the consequences of not adhering to the given instructions. In a broader spiritual context, it can be interpreted as a reminder of the necessity of following divine commandments and the repercussions of straying from that path.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said: 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Truly, I feared that you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel and have not observed my word.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a conversation between Moses and his brother Aaron. Aaron is pleading with Moses not to hold him accountable by physical reprimand for the actions of the Israelites in his absence. Aaron explains that he acted in a way he thought was best to avoid further division and disobedience among the people. This reflects the challenges of leadership and the importance of compassion and understanding between leaders, especially when faced with the shortcomings of their followers.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He (Moses) said: 'What, then, is your case, O Samiri?'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is confronting Samiri, a figure involved in leading the Israelites astray by promoting the worship of the golden calf. Moses is inquiring about the reason or motive behind Samiri's actions. It reflects a moment of accountability and seeking understanding of the intentions that led to the act of idolatry among the Israelites. This interaction underscores the themes of leadership, responsibility, and the consequences of guiding a community away from the worship of one true God.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: He said, 'I perceived what they did not perceive, so I took a handful from the messenger's trail and threw it, and thus my soul enticed me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects on the actions and internal justifications of an individual who took a unique action based on their perception and understanding that differed from others. It highlights the power of self-rationalization and the influence of one's own soul in leading them to make such decisions. The verse can be seen as a warning about the potential pitfalls of following one's own desires without proper guidance and the consequences that can arise from misinterpreting or acting beyond the intended message of guidance.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He said, 'Then go, for indeed, it is decreed for you in [this] life to say, "No contact." And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you have remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it into the sea with a blast.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the fate of a disbeliever who has shown obstinate rejection of truth and led others astray, indicating divine punishment in both this life and the Hereafter. Their worldly experience will be marked by isolation ('No contact') and they will face assured recompense in the afterlife. The false god they worshipped will be destroyed utterly, symbolizing the futility of their devotion to anything other than the true God.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا

translation: Your god is only Allah, who there is no deity except Him. He has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the monotheistic belief central to Islam, affirming that Allah alone is the only deity worthy of worship. It also underscores Allah's omniscience, meaning that His knowledge is all-encompassing and nothing is outside His awareness.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus We relate to you, [O Muhammad], some stories of what happened before. And We have certainly given you from Us a message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an includes narratives from previous events as a means of providing guidance and wisdom. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that what has been revealed to him is a divine message, filled with lessons and historical accounts to enlighten and educate its readers. It underscores the continuity and consistency of divine guidance throughout human history, using past events to inform present and future actions.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: But whoever turns away from it will carry a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of turning away from divine guidance. It indicates that those who ignore or reject the teachings of the Qur'an will face the burden of their actions on the Day of Judgment. This can be understood as a spiritual and moral weight that they will have to bear due to their decisions and actions in the earthly life, highlighting the importance of adhering to divine guidance for salvation and ease in the afterlife.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: Abiding therein eternally, and evil for them will be that burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse indicates that certain individuals will face eternal consequences in the afterlife for their actions, specifically denoting the burden of their deeds as grievous on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the severity and permanence of their punishment, serving as a warning to all about the importance of righteous conduct and the fearsome nature of divine retribution.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day the Horn is blown, and We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, a time of great accountability and revelation. The blowing of the Horn signifies the commencement of this inevitable and momentous event, awakening and gathering all beings. The term 'blue-eyed' (زرقا) here is often interpreted metaphorically to describe the criminals as being in a state of extreme fear, horror, or spiritual blindness. This depiction highlights their utter helplessness and the severity of their impending judgment. It serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's actions and the ultimate justice that will be administered by Allah.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They will murmur among themselves, 'You stayed only ten (days)'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, where people will be in a state of confusion and astonishment. In their bewilderment, they will converse among themselves, trying to make sense of their time in the worldly life, mistakenly thinking it was only ten days. This illustrates the brevity of worldly life in comparison to the hereafter, and the limited perception humans have of time when faced with the eternal reality of the afterlife.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in conduct will say, 'You remained not but one day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's complete and all-encompassing knowledge of the statements and thoughts of people. It highlights the contrast between human perception and divine awareness, particularly in the context of the Day of Judgment when human understanding of time and reality is grossly underestimated. The phrase 'best of them in conduct' suggests that even the wisest or most righteous humans will profoundly misjudge their stay on Earth when confronted with the eternal reality of the hereafter. This serves as a reminder of the limitations of human understanding in the face of divine omniscience.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, 'My Lord will blow them away with a blast.'
interpretation: This verse speaks to the impermanence of even the most seemingly immovable aspects of the world, such as mountains. It emphasizes the omnipotence of God, capable of obliterating the mountains with mere will, signifying the transient nature of worldly elements before divine power and the eventual transformation on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: And leave it as a level, barren plain.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the totality of divine power in transforming the earth, which will be flattened and made barren. It highlights the potency and decisiveness of God's will in reshaping creation, possibly as a sign of resurrection or ultimate judgment. This transformation reflects the transition from a world of life and activity to a realm of desolation, underscoring themes of impermanence and divine authority.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: You will see no crookedness therein, nor any curving.
interpretation: This verse refers to the perfect and flawless nature of the creation, specifically highlighting the uniformity, balance, and seamless orderliness within it. It signifies that there are no imperfections or deviations, symbolizing the divine precision and meticulousness embedded by the Creator. This observation can be extended metaphorically to the principles and laws established by divine guidance, which are devoid of error and imbalance.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: On that Day, they will follow the Caller with no deviation, and all voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but whispers.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, depicting a scene of absolute obedience and solemnity. People will follow the divine Caller without any deviation, signifying their complete submission to God's command. The mention of hushed voices indicates a profound reverence and awe before the presence of the Most Merciful, where even the slightest sounds will be subdued, reflecting the seriousness and gravity of the moment.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except by one to whom the Most Merciful has granted permission and has accepted their word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, intercession will not be beneficial to anyone unless Allah, the Most Merciful, grants permission for it and is pleased with the intercessor's words and deeds. It underscores the ultimate authority and mercy of Allah, highlighting that even intercession is subject to His will and approval, reinforcing the importance of earning His favor through righteous actions and sincere faith.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipresence, illustrating that His knowledge is infinite and comprehensive. Humans, regardless of their efforts, cannot fully grasp or encompass the entirety of God's wisdom or knowledge. This serves to remind believers of the limitations of human understanding in contrast to the divine, encouraging humility and reliance on God's guidance.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate submission and humility of all beings in the presence of Allah, who is described as the Ever-Living and the Sustainer. On the Day of Judgment, everyone will be humbled before Him, recognizing His supreme authority and eternal life. The verse also underscores the severe consequences of wrongdoing and injustice, indicating that those who carry the burden of injustice will face failure, reflecting the moral gravity of oppression and wrongdoing in the sight of Allah.
orig: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما

translation: And whoever does righteousness while being a believer – he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who perform righteous deeds with genuine faith should have no fear of being wronged or denied their due reward. It reassures believers that their efforts will not go unrecognized or unappreciated by Allah, and they will not suffer any form of injustice or loss in the Hereafter. This serves as a motivation for the faithful to continue their good deeds, trusting that their actions are always in the sight of Allah and will be justly rewarded.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid (sin) or it would cause them remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic, a language that was clear and accessible to its initial audience. By diversifying the types of warnings and reminders it contains, the scripture aims to guide people towards piety and mindfulness of their actions. It serves to awaken their conscience and encourage moral and spiritual reflection, urging them to avoid sins and remember their responsibilities to Allah and to one another.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا

translation: So exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And do not hasten with (recitation of) the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme position as the ultimate Sovereign and embodiment of Truth. It advises patience in receiving divine revelation, recognizing that understanding and wisdom come in due time through God's process. Furthermore, it encourages a humble pursuit of knowledge, underscoring the importance of continually seeking to expand one's understanding and spiritual insight through prayer and supplication to God.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما

translation: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
interpretation: This verse refers to the covenant or command that Allah gave to Adam, the first human created. Despite the warning given to him, Adam forgot and lacked firm resolve in fulfilling the command, which led to his mistake. The verse highlights the human tendency to forgetfulness and the struggle to maintain steadfastness in following divine guidance.
orig: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblis. He refused.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when God commanded the angels to show respect towards Adam by prostrating to him, highlighting Adam's honored status as the first human being created by God. All the angels complied except for Iblis, who refused out of arrogance and pride. This act of defiance by Iblis marks the beginning of his role as the adversary to humanity, emphasizing themes of obedience, humility, and the consequences of pride and rebellion against divine command.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى

translation: Then We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of Paradise and cause you to fall into misery.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning to Adam about the adversarial nature of Satan. It highlights the impending consequences of being misled by Satan, which are the loss of the bliss of Paradise and the onset of hardship. It underscores the importance of vigilance and obedience to divine commandments to maintain one's state of grace and well-being.
orig: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى

translation: Indeed, it is [promised] for you that you will not be hungry therein nor will you be unclothed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and comforts provided by God in paradise. It assures the believers that in paradise, they will be free from the basic struggles of hunger and lack of clothing, emphasizing the completeness and perfection of the provisions prepared by God for the righteous.
orig: إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

translation: And you will not thirst therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comforts and blessings provided in Paradise, where the inhabitants are protected from thirst and the harshness of the sun. It indicates a state of perpetual ease, comfort, and protection from physical discomforts, showcasing the completeness of the divine provision and care in the hereafter.
orig: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى

translation: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cunning and deceitful nature of Satan, who entices Adam by appealing to his desire for eternal life and everlasting dominion. It highlights the subtlety of temptation and the susceptibility of even the first human, Adam, to be misled by the promise of immortality and power, which ultimately leads to his fall.
orig: فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

translation: Then they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Adam and his spouse disobeyed Allah's command by eating from the forbidden tree. As a consequence, their previously concealed private parts became exposed, prompting them to cover themselves with leaves from Paradise. This act is depicted as the first instance of human disobedience to Allah, highlighting the innate vulnerability and the tendency to err within human nature. The verse underscores the importance of obedience to divine commandments and the immediate, tangible consequences of disobedience.
orig: فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

translation: Then his Lord chose him, so He turned to him in forgiveness and guided him.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness. Despite any transgressions made by an individual, Allah's grace remains available if the person turns back to Him with sincerity. It emphasizes that divine guidance is a result of Allah's mercy and choosing, and implies that sincere repentance is always met with forgiveness and guidance.
orig: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى

translation: He said, 'Descend from it [Paradise]—all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter].'
interpretation: This verse addresses the expulsion of Adam and his offspring from Paradise after the fall. It highlights the theme of human enmity and conflict as a consequence of this fall. However, it also offers a hopeful promise: divine guidance will reach humanity, and adherence to this guidance will lead to a life free from misguidance in the world and distress in the Hereafter. This indicates the importance of following divine instructions for a righteous and fulfilling life.
orig: قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

translation: But whoever turns away from My Reminder will certainly have a miserable life, and We will raise them up blind on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of staying connected with Divine guidance. It warns that those who neglect or turn away from the remembrance of God will lead a life filled with hardship and discontent. Furthermore, it foretells a severe consequence for such individuals on the Day of Judgment, where they will be resurrected in a state of blindness, symbolizing their spiritual blindness and deviation in life. It underscores the importance of adhering to God's guidance for a fulfilling life and a favorable outcome in the hereafter.
orig: ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

translation: He will say, 'My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a person's plea and sense of bewilderment on the Day of Judgement when they find themselves blinded despite having sight in their worldly life. It symbolizes a spiritual blindness resulting from ignoring divine guidance and revelations during their lifetime. The blindness here is a metaphor for the person's lack of insight and adherence to faith, which has now manifested in a literal sense as a form of retribution or consequence for their heedlessness and disobedience in the temporal world.
orig: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

translation: Thus did Our signs come to you, but you forgot them; and in the same way, you will be forgotten today.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of neglecting or ignoring divine guidance. It serves as a reminder that those who choose to forget or disregard the signs and teachings sent by God will face a reciprocal treatment in the afterlife. Just as they neglected God's instructions in their earthly life, they will be neglected and forgotten on the Day of Judgment. This illustrates a principle of divine justice, where the treatment one chooses to accord to divine guidance is mirrored back to them in the hereafter.
orig: قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

translation: Thus do We recompense those who transgress and do not believe in the signs of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and everlasting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences faced by those who indulge excessively in sin and fail to believe in God's signs. It highlights that their punishment will not only be severe but also enduring in the Hereafter. This serves as a strict warning to encourage faith and righteous conduct, as the temporal sufferings of this world are minimal compared to the eternal punishments reserved for the hereafter.
orig: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

translation: Is it not a guidance for them how many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they now walk? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to people that previous generations who denied the truth were destroyed. The current inhabitants walk through the ruins of these previous civilizations, which should serve as evident signs of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes that these signs are intelligible and serve as lessons specifically for those who possess intellect and wisdom, encouraging reflection and mindfulness.
orig: أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: And if it were not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation and a specified time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that without a prior decree or command from Allah, the judgment or consequence would have already been inevitable and due at an appointed time. It reflects the divine wisdom and planning in the timing of events and the unfolding of Allah's will. The preceding 'word' serves as a divine intervention that delays immediate judgment, highlighting Allah's mercy and the predestined nature of events.
orig: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse advises patience in the face of criticism or opposition, urging one to maintain constant remembrance and glorification of Allah. By praising Allah at various times of the day and night, a person can find inner peace and reassurance, ultimately achieving contentment and divine approval. It emphasizes the importance of regular spiritual discipline and devotion in achieving tranquility and satisfaction in life.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [certain] categories of them [polytheists and disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad] [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. But the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse advises against coveting the temporary pleasures and material wealth possessed by others, particularly those who do not hold faith. The worldly splendor they enjoy is a means of testing them, not an indication of true, lasting value. It reminds believers that the sustenance provided by God—whether in this life or the hereafter—holds greater and permanent worth, urging a focus on spiritual and eternal blessings over transient earthly gains.
orig: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayer within one's family and being patient and persistent in this duty. It reassures that God is the true provider, alleviating any concerns about sustenance. Ultimately, it underscores that righteousness leads to the best outcome, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى

translation: And they say, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and demands for miracles by those who doubt the Prophet's message. It chastises their insistence on new signs when clear evidence and wisdom were already provided in previous scriptures. It emphasizes that the Qur'an and earlier revelations share a consistent message, urging believers to recognize and accept the divine truth presented to them.
orig: وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before this, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent tendency of humans to seek excuses for their failures or shortcomings. It suggests that even if those who denied the truth were punished before being given clear guidance, they would still argue that they were not given a fair chance to follow the right path. It emphasizes the fairness and mercy of Allah in sending messengers and providing guidance before enacting punishment, giving individuals ample opportunity to understand and accept the truth and thus avoid disgrace.
orig: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى

translation: Say, 'Each one is waiting; so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided.'
interpretation: This verse is a proclamation of patience and a challenge to those who doubt or oppose the message of Islam. It emphasizes that the true course of events will reveal who is rightly guided and following the correct path. The believers are advised to remain steadfast and patient, as the truth will become clear over time. The verse also provides reassurance that those who adhere to the righteous path will ultimately be vindicated.
orig: قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى

translation: The time of their reckoning has drawn near for the people, while they are in heedlessness turning away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to humanity about the impending judgment and accountability that awaits them. It emphasizes that despite the closeness of this moment, many people remain distracted and indifferent, neglecting to prepare for it. The verse calls for introspection and awareness, urging people to turn their attention towards their actions and their ultimate accountability.
orig: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون

translation: Whenever any new revelation comes to them from their Lord, they listen to it playfully.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dismissive and playful attitude of some individuals towards divine messages. Even when presented with new revelations from their Lord, instead of taking them seriously and reflecting on their meaning and significance, these individuals merely listen in a frivolous manner, lacking sincerity and reverence.
orig: ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

translation: Their hearts distracted, the wrongdoers confide to each other privately, 'Is he not but a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you see it?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dismissive attitude of the wrongdoers towards the Prophet's message. Their hearts are heedless, engaged in distractions, and they secretly mock the Prophet, questioning his human nature and suggesting that following him is akin to succumbing to magic or illusions. It underscores their willful ignorance and the irony of recognizing the truth yet still choosing to deny it.
orig: لاهية قلوبهم وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون

translation: My Lord knows whatever is said in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all utterances and speech, both in the vast expanses of heavens and on the earth. Furthermore, it highlights two of His attributes: He is the All-Hearing, meaning nothing escapes His hearing, and the All-Knowing, meaning His knowledge encompasses all things. This serves as a reminder of the comprehensive nature of divine awareness and understanding, implicitly urging believers to be mindful of their words and actions.
orig: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض وهو السميع العليم

translation: But they say, 'Muddled dreams,' Nay, he has fabricated it, Nay, he is a poet. Let him then bring us a sign as the former prophets were sent [with].
interpretation: This verse highlights the various accusations and dismissals that the disbelievers direct towards the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). They attempt to undermine the message of the Qur'an by attributing it to mere dreams, accusing the Prophet of fabricating it, or labeling him as a poet. The demand for a miraculous sign similar to those given to previous prophets is a reflection of their persistent skepticism and refusal to accept the divine origin of the Qur'an without tangible proof.
orig: بل قالوا أضغاث أحلام بل افتراه بل هو شاعر فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون

translation: No city which We destroyed believed before them; so will they believe?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuation of disbelief among past civilizations that were destroyed due to their rejection of faith. It questions whether the current people who are being warned will believe, implying a pattern of human behavior that tends to repeat despite warnings and consequences observed in history.
orig: ما آمنت قبلهم من قرية أهلكناها أفهم يؤمنون

translation: And We did not send before you [O Muhammad] except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse asserts that God's practice has always been to send human messengers, not angels or superhuman beings, to convey His revelations to humanity. It emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge from those who are well-versed in the scriptures (people of the message) when one lacks understanding, thereby promoting the value of inquiry and learning within the faith.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And We did not make them bodies that ate no food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: This verse conveys that human beings, including the prophets, are created with natural human needs and limitations. They require sustenance and are not exempt from the cycle of life and death. This reinforces the understanding that prophets, despite their divine mission, shared the basic human experiences of mortality and dependency on food, underscoring their humanity and relatability to the people they were sent to guide.
orig: وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام وما كانوا خالدين

translation: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, and We saved them and those We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fulfillment of God's promise to the righteous, showcasing divine justice in rescuing those whom God chooses to save, while simultaneously punishing those who engage in excessive wrongdoing. It reflects the principle that God's promises are always upheld, and serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of oppressive and extravagant behavior.
orig: ثم صدقناهم الوعد فأنجيناهم ومن نشاء وأهلكنا المسرفين

translation: We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation specifically addressing humanity. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and reflecting upon the guidance and reminders it contains. The rhetorical question at the end encourages individuals to use their intellect and reason to understand and appreciate the profound messages conveyed in the Holy Book.
orig: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a city We destroyed that was committing wrong, and We produced after it another people.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and justice in dealing with wrongdoing. It serves as a warning to those who commit injustice and oppression, emphasizing that such actions will lead to their downfall. Furthermore, it assures that Allah replenishes and establishes new communities in place of those that are destroyed, indicating His continuous creation and maintenance of balance in the world.
orig: وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين

translation: Then, when they perceived Our punishment, behold, they (tried to) flee from it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden realization of the disbelievers when they sense the impending punishment from Allah. In their panic and fear, they attempt to escape the consequences of their actions, but it emphasizes the inevitability of divine retribution and the futility of trying to evade it.
orig: فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون

translation: Do not run away, but return to the luxuries in which you indulged and to your homes, so that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who are fleeing in fear, instructing them to return to their lives of comfort and indulgence in their homes. It emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and judgment, urging them to confront rather than evade the consequences of their actions. The instruction to return 'to what you were given' symbolizes facing one’s deeds and recognizing that escaping physical spaces will not equate to escaping divine justice.
orig: لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects an acknowledgment of guilt and wrongdoing by those who have strayed from the path of righteousness. It portrays a moment of realization and regret, often associated with the Day of Judgment, where individuals recognize their failures and the consequences of their actions. The exclamation 'Woe to us!' underscores the severity of their situation and their despair at the realization of their own injustices.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And that cry of theirs ceased not until We made them as a mown-down field, extinct.
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate and inevitable destruction of those who persist in their wrongful ways despite repeated warnings. It serves as a reminder of the consequence of defiance and the finality of God's decree. The imagery of a 'mown-down field' symbolizes complete eradication, indicating that once Divine judgement is executed, there is no escape or return.
orig: فما زالت تلك دعواهم حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deliberate and purposeful nature of God's creation. It serves as a reminder that the universe and everything within it were not created without reason or meaning. The verse invites reflection on the intentional design and divine wisdom behind the existence of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between, urging humans to recognize and contemplate the greater purpose and order within the creation.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: Had We intended to take a pastime, We could surely have taken it from Us, if We were to do so.
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of God's transcendence and the futility of attributing frivolity or trivial activities to Him. It emphasizes that if God had wanted to engage in amusement or distraction, He could have taken it from within His own divine nature, but such actions are inherently contrary to His essence and purpose. The statement underscores the seriousness and gravity of God's actions and intentions, highlighting His supreme wisdom and the purposeful nature of His creation.
orig: لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين

translation: Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and behold, falsehood vanishes. Woe to you for what you describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the triumph of truth over falsehood, indicating that when truth confronts falsehood, it utterly destroys it. It serves as a reminder of the inevitable victory of righteousness and a warning to those who engage in fabricating falsehoods about the divine, alerting them to the consequences of their actions.
orig: بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق ولكم الويل مما تصفون

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vast dominion and absolute authority of Allah over all creations in the heavens and earth. It highlights that those who are nearest to Allah, such as angels, remain humble and unceasingly devoted in worship, without any fatigue or pride. This serves as a reminder for humans to adopt a similar attitude of humility and relentless devotion towards their Creator.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They exalt [Him] night and day [and] do not slacken.
interpretation: This verse highlights the constant and unwavering praise and glorification of Allah by the angels. It emphasizes their dedication and continuous devotion without any interruption. The verse serves to illustrate the ideal of relentless worship and commitment to acknowledging the greatness of Allah at all times.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can resurrect the dead?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of polytheism by questioning the ability of earthly gods to bring the dead back to life. It implies that such power belongs solely to Allah and that idols or gods created by humans cannot hold such divine capabilities. This verse serves to highlight the futility and irrationality of worshipping any entity other than the one true God.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: Had there been within the heavens and earth gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse asserts the oneness and supremacy of Allah, positing that the existence of multiple deities would lead to chaos and corruption in the universe. It emphasizes that the order and harmony observed in the natural world is a testament to the singular divine authority of Allah. The verse also glorifies Allah, acknowledging His perfection and distancing Him from any false attributes or descriptions that might be attributed to other deities.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah over His creation. It signifies that Allah’s actions are beyond human questioning or accountability due to His ultimate wisdom and justice. In contrast, human beings will be held accountable for their own actions and will be questioned about them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, 'Produce your proof. This is the reminder for those with me and the reminder for those before me.' But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheistic belief by questioning the validity of taking other deities besides Allah. It calls for proof or evidence to support such claims. The verse emphasizes that the guidance provided in the scripture is consistent with that given to previous prophets, highlighting the continuity and unity of divine revelation. Despite this, the verse laments that many people are ignorant of the truth and thereby choose to ignore the divine message.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that, 'There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency and continuity of the monotheistic message across all prophets sent by Allah. It underscores the fundamental tenet of Islamic faith that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. The directive to worship Allah alone is central to all prophetic missions, highlighting the unity and singularity of divine worship throughout history.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that Allah, the Most Merciful, has taken a son, emphasizing His transcendence above such allegations. Instead, it clarifies that those referred to are honored servants of Allah, who are created and dignified by Him, but not His offspring. The verse upholds the monotheistic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, denying any association or offspring.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse highlights the submissive nature of angels, demonstrating their complete obedience to Allah. They do not speak out of turn nor do they act on their own accord; instead, they await Allah's command and carry out His instructions dutifully. This emphasizes the absolute authority and control of Allah over His creation, as well as the impeccable discipline and governance of the celestial beings in serving His will.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for him whom He approves. And they, for fear of Him, are apprehensive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah, indicating His complete knowledge of all matters past, present, and future, which encompasses everything that lies before and behind His creations. It emphasizes the exclusive and conditional privilege of intercession, which is granted only to those whom Allah is pleased with. It further underscores the humility and reverence that even the most honored beings hold towards Allah, being in a state of constant awareness and awe of His supreme authority and majesty. This conveys the essence of accountability, divine justice, and the profound respect owed to Allah by all creation.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever among them says, 'Indeed, I am a god besides Him,' that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of claiming divinity alongside Allah, stressing that such an assertion is met with the gravest consequence: Hell. It reflects the Qur'anic principle that the ultimate justice of Allah will be enacted upon those who wrongfully elevate themselves to a position reserved solely for the Divine. The verse serves as a stark warning to deter any form of polytheism or idolatry, emphasizing the singularity and supremacy of Allah in Islamic monotheism.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
interpretation: This verse calls on disbelievers to reflect on the evidence of creation as a sign of Allah's power and existence. It refers to the heavens and the earth once being a single, unified entity before being separated, which can be interpreted as an allusion to the Big Bang theory or a similar cosmological event. This transformation is highlighted as a divine act. Additionally, the reference to everything living being made from water underscores the essential role of water in sustaining life, pointing to a foundational biological fact. The verse challenges the reader to recognize these signs and, in doing so, calls for belief in the divine origin and maintenance of the universe.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein [mountain] passes [as] roads that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the precision and wisdom in God's creation of the earth. The mountains are positioned to provide stability to the earth, preventing it from shaking and causing harm to its inhabitants.
