interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority of Allah over life and death as well as the natural cycles, like day and night. It is a call for reflection and understanding of His sovereignty and control over all aspects of existence. The rhetorical question at the end urges humans to use their intellect to recognize and submit to the omnipotence and wisdom of Allah.
orig: وهو الذي يحيي ويميت وله اختلاف الليل والنهار أفلا تعقلون

translation: Nay, they say like what the former people said.
interpretation: This verse addresses the repetitive nature of disbelief and rejection of the message of the prophets. It highlights that the objections and denials raised by the contemporaries of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) mirror those of previous generations who also doubted and rejected their prophets. The verse serves as a reminder that such skepticism and stubbornness are not new and emphasizes the continuity of human nature in resisting divine guidance.
orig: بل قالوا مثل ما قال الأولون

translation: They say, 'When we are dead and have become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of disbelievers regarding the concept of resurrection after death. It highlights their incredulity about the possibility of being brought back to life once their bodies have disintegrated into dust and bones. The underlying message is to affirm the power of God in being able to resurrect the dead, emphasizing that human doubts do not limit divine capabilities.
orig: قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Indeed, we were promised this, we and our forefathers before; this is nothing but legends of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the message of the Qur'an by asserting that the promises and warnings it contains are the same as those given to their ancestors, dismissing them as mere myths and ancient tales without relevance or truth. This reflects a common attitude of denial and refusal to accept divine guidance, suggesting a deeper unwillingness to recognize or change one's own flawed beliefs and behaviors.
orig: لقد وعدنا نحن وآباؤنا هذا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, 'To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question aimed at the disbelievers, urging them to recognize and acknowledge the sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation. It challenges those who doubt or deny divine authority to contemplate and admit who truly controls the earth and everything within it. This reflection serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate power and dominion, encouraging humility and submission to His will.
orig: قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Then will you not remember?'
interpretation: This verse highlights a common acknowledgement among people about Allah's sovereignty. It prompts believers to reflect on their recognition of Allah's dominion and urges them towards deeper remembrance and consciousness of their faith. The rhetorical question serves as a reminder that acknowledging truth should naturally lead to mindful contemplation and adherence to divine guidance.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تذكرون

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed to make the listener or reader reflect on the majesty and sovereignty of Allah. By referencing the seven heavens and the Great Throne, the verse emphasizes the vastness and supreme authority of Allah over all creation. It serves to remind believers and non-believers alike of the omnipotence of Allah, encouraging recognition and submission to His ultimate rulership and power.
orig: قل من رب السماوات السبع ورب العرش العظيم

translation: They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Then will you not fear [Him]?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of recognizing Allah's sovereignty and encourages the audience to develop a sense of piety and mindfulness towards Him. It serves as a reminder that acknowledging Allah's authority should naturally lead to a respectful fear or consciousness of Him, prompting adherence to His guidance and commandments.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تتقون

translation: Say, 'In whose hand is the dominion over everything, and He protects while no one can protect against Him, if you should know?'
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and authority of God over all creation. It emphasizes that God’s dominion encompasses everything, signifying His omnipotence and supreme control. Moreover, it underscores His unmatched ability to provide protection, indicating that while He can protect anyone from harm, no one can shield against His will. It invites reflection on the fundamental truth of God's unparalleled power and guardianship.
orig: قل من بيده ملكوت كل شيء وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, 'It belongs to Allah.' Say, 'Then how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who acknowledge that all belongs to Allah but still go astray in their beliefs and actions. It questions the irrationality of recognizing Allah's sovereignty while still being misled or confused in following falsehoods. Essentially, it challenges the inconsistency between their acknowledgment and their misguided behavior or beliefs.
orig: سيقولون لله قل فأنى تسحرون

translation: Nay, We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message delivered to the disbelievers is the absolute truth from Allah. Despite being presented with clear signs and guidance, the disbelievers reject the truth and persist in falsehood. Their denial and false accusations against the message highlight their unwillingness to accept divine guidance, reflecting a deliberate choice to turn away from the truth.
orig: بل أتيناهم بالحق وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor is there with Him any [other] deity. [If there were], then each deity would have taken what it created, and some of them would have sought to overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe [concerning Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, asserting that He does not have a son nor does He share His divinity with any other entity. It also highlights the inconsistency and disarray that would result if multiple gods existed, as each would act independently and seek dominance, leading to conflict. This serves to affirm the fundamental Islamic belief in monotheism and the perfection of Allah's singular authority and power, free from any imperfection or association attributed to Him by others.
orig: ما اتخذ الله من ولد وما كان معه من إله إذا لذهب كل إله بما خلق ولعلا بعضهم على بعض سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, exalted is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience, acknowledging His complete knowledge of both the unseen and the seen realms. It further establishes His transcendence and purity, asserting that He is far above and beyond any partners or associates that people might attribute to Him. This serves as a reminder of the absolute monotheism in Islam, where God stands alone in His supremacy and glory.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة فتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Say, 'My Lord, if You should show me that which they are promised,'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad is supplicating to Allah, expressing total surrender to Allah’s will. The Prophet asks Allah to show him the promised punishment for the disbelievers if it is to occur during his lifetime. The plea highlights the divide between belief and disbelief and serves to remind the followers about the inevitable divine justice. Essentially, it is an acknowledgment of both the mercy and the justice of Allah, where the Prophet seeks to be aligned with divine decree regardless of its nature.
orig: قل رب إما تريني ما يوعدون

translation: So, my Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The speaker is beseeching Allah for protection and guidance, asking not to be included or surrounded by those who indulge in injustice or sinful behavior. This reflects a desire to stay righteous and avoid influences that could lead one astray from the path of virtue.
orig: رب فلا تجعلني في القوم الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We are able to show you what We have promised them.
interpretation: This verse reassures that God has the power to fulfill His promises, including showing Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the believers the consequences that the disbelievers will face. It underscores the omnipotence of God and His ultimate control over the destiny of all beings, promising justice and the eventual triumph of truth.
orig: وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون

translation: Repel evil with that which is better. We are most knowing of what they describe.
interpretation: This verse encourages the use of grace and kindness as a means to counteract and neutralize evil or wrongdoing. It emphasizes that positive responses can transform negative situations. The latter part reassures that Allah is fully aware of what others attribute or accuse, highlighting that one’s actions, even when not immediately vindicated, are observed and recorded by the Divine.
orig: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة نحن أعلم بما يصفون

translation: And say, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the devils.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's protection against the evil influences and temptations of Satan and his associates. It encourages believers to actively seek divine refuge in order to remain steadfast in righteousness and avoid the pitfalls of malevolent whisperings that can lead them astray.
orig: وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine protection from the presence and influence of evil entities, whether they be physical beings or spiritual forces. It underscores the human need for God's shelter against negative influences and the desire for spiritual purity and safety.
orig: وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون

translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'My Lord, send me back.'
interpretation: This verse touches upon the theme of regret that people will have at the moment of death. It reflects the human desire for another chance to correct their wrongs and prove their righteousness, but it also underscores the permanence of death and the finality of one’s earthly actions. The plea to return suggests a realization of the wasted opportunities and the urgency to rectify one's life, which is no longer possible.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون

translation: So that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind. No! It is only a word he is saying; and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This verse conveys the regret of a person after death, expressing a desire to return to life to perform righteous deeds. However, Allah asserts that this is just an utterance with no substance, emphasizing the finality of death and the impossibility of returning. The 'barrier' mentioned signifies a boundary or interim state (Barzakh) between the worldly life and the Hereafter, lasting until the Day of Resurrection, underscoring that actions must be taken while alive as there are no second chances post-mortem.
orig: لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: Then when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the Trumpet is blown, signifying the commencement of the final reckoning. On that day, earthly relationships, social ties, and familial bonds will cease to hold any significance. People will be solely concerned with their own deeds and fate, devoid of any inclination to inquire about or seek help from their relatives or acquaintances.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

translation: Then those whose scales are heavy – it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability. The 'scales' symbolize the weighing of one's deeds on the Day of Judgment. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be deemed successful, highlighting the importance of righteous actions, faith, and morality in achieving ultimate success in the hereafter.
orig: فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: But those whose scales are light - it is they who have lost their souls, in Hell, they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the fate of those whose good deeds are insufficiently weighed against their bad deeds. The 'scales' metaphorically represent the measure of one's actions. Those who find their scales light, implying a deficiency of righteous deeds, face profound spiritual loss. This loss is so grave that they are deemed to have essentially forfeited their own souls. The eternal nature of the punishment in Hell underscores the severity of failing to lead a life of moral and spiritual integrity according to divine guidelines.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون

translation: The Fire will sear their faces, and they will be therein, disfigured.
interpretation: This verse portrays the severe punishment and anguish that the disbelievers will face in the Hereafter. The image of fire searing their faces signifies intense suffering and disgrace. The term 'disfigured' indicates the dehumanizing and painful transformation due to their rejection of faith, illustrating the gravity of divine retribution and highlighting the stark consequences of disbelief and sin.
orig: تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون

translation: Were not My verses recited to you and you used to deny them?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the notion of accountability for one's response to divine guidance. It underscores the fact that the signs and revelations from God were presented to people, yet they chose to reject and deny them. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding the divine messages.
orig: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker acknowledges their own failings and misguidance. They attribute their condition to their own misfortune and missteps which led them away from the right path. There is an admission of personal fault and a recognition of the consequences of their deviation from righteousness. This utterance reflects a form of repentance and an appeal to divine mercy, recognizing the human tendency to err and seeking forgiveness and rectification from God.
orig: قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين

translation: Our Lord, remove us from it [Hell]; and if we were to return [to evil], we would indeed be wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of those suffering in Hell, acknowledging their wrongdoings. They beseech God to rescue them, promising not to revert to their sinful ways. It underscores the themes of repentance, the acceptance of guilt, and the earnest yearning for divine mercy and another chance to live righteously.
orig: ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

translation: He will say, 'Remain despised therein and do not speak to Me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of ultimate judgment where those condemned to Hell are commanded by Allah to remain in their state of disgrace and silence. It underscores the finality of their punishment and the irrevocable nature of their fate, serving as a stern reminder of the consequences of their actions and the seriousness of divine judgement.
orig: قال اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون

translation: Indeed, a group from My servants would say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the plea of the believers who sincerely turn to Allah in faith, seeking His forgiveness and mercy. It underscores the qualities of humility and reliance on Allah's compassion, emphasizing that Allah is the most merciful and the most forgiving. The verse calls upon the believers to recognize their dependence on divine mercy and to continuously seek Allah's forgiveness, reflecting a deep sense of spiritual awareness and devotion.
orig: إنه كان فريق من عبادي يقولون ربنا آمنا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: But you took them in mockery to the point that it made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of those who ridiculed the believers, thereby neglecting the remembrance of Allah. Their mockery and laughter at the faithful led them to stray from divine guidance. It serves as a warning about the consequences of such actions, emphasizing the importance of remaining respectful and mindful of Allah's teachings.
orig: فاتخذتموهم سخريا حتى أنسوكم ذكري وكنتم منهم تضحكون

translation: Indeed, I have rewarded them this Day for their patience - they are indeed the winners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and resilience in the path of faith. It highlights that divine reward is granted to those who endure hardships with patience, suggesting that ultimate success and triumph belong to those who remain steadfast in their beliefs despite facing adversities.
orig: إني جزيتهم اليوم بما صبروا أنهم هم الفائزون

translation: He will say, 'How many years did you remain on earth?'
interpretation: This verse presents a moment of accountability in the Hereafter, where God asks humans to reflect on the transient nature of their worldly life. It serves as a reminder to believers to live a life of righteousness and mindfulness of the afterlife, as the time spent on earth will seem fleeting compared to eternity.
orig: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

translation: They said, 'We have remained a day or part of a day.' Ask those who count [the time].
interpretation: This verse reflects the perception of time in the afterlife, where those resurrected from death will feel as though their earthly life was extraordinarily brief. It highlights the fleeting nature of worldly existence and underscores the importance of accounting for one's actions in preparation for the hereafter.
orig: قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم فاسأل العادين

translation: He will say, 'You stayed not but a little - if only you had known.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limited and fleeting nature of human life on earth compared to the eternal afterlife. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly existence and underscores the importance of being conscious and mindful of one's deeds and actions. If people truly understood this brevity, it might lead them to live more righteously and with greater awareness of the consequences of their actions.
orig: قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون

translation: Did you then think that We had created you in jest (without any purpose), and that you would not be returned to Us?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of purposeless existence and emphasizes accountability before God. It serves as a reminder that human creation is intentional and meaningful, with an eventual return to the Creator for judgment. The verse urges reflection on the significance of life and the responsibilities it entails toward one’s actions and their consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا وأنكم إلينا لا ترجعون

translation: So exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transcendence and supreme authority of Allah, affirming His sovereignty and ultimate reality. The phrase denies the existence of any deity other than Allah, reinforcing the concept of monotheism. The reference to Allah as 'Lord of the Noble Throne' signifies His dominion and control over all creation, emphasizing His majesty and the honor inherent in His dominion.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا إله إلا هو رب العرش الكريم

translation: And whoever invokes besides Allah another deity for which he has no proof – then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse addresses the gravity of associating partners with Allah, emphasizing that idolizing other deities without any divine evidence is futile. It underscores the inevitability of accountability before Allah, who alone will judge such transgressions. Furthermore, the verse categorically states that those who disbelieve and persist in polytheism will not achieve success in the hereafter, highlighting the exclusivity of divine worship for attaining salvation.
orig: ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به فإنما حسابه عند ربه إنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: And say, 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse is a beautiful supplication reminding believers to seek forgiveness and mercy from Allah, acknowledging Him as the ultimate source of compassion and mercy. It highlights the importance of humility and turning to Allah for both forgiveness of sins and the bestowing of mercy, recognizing that no one can be more merciful than Allah Himself.
orig: وقل رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: A surah which We have sent down and made [that within it] obligatory and revealed therein verses of clear evidence that you might remember.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the surah being mentioned is divinely revealed and its commands are obligatory for the believers to follow. The 'clear evidence' refers to the signs and instructions within the surah that guide and remind the faithful about their responsibilities and duties, prompting them to remember and adhere to the teachings.
orig: سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها وأنزلنا فيها آيات بينات لعلكم تذكرون

translation: The [unmarried] woman or [unmarried] man found guilty of sexual intercourse - lash each one of them with a hundred lashes, and do not be taken by pity for them in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes a severe punishment for fornication, emphasizing that the prescribed punishment must be carried out without leniency, reflecting the seriousness of the offense in the eyes of Allah. It underscores the importance of adhering to divine commands and shows that the community's participation as witnesses serves as a social and moral deterrent to such actions, reinforcing collective accountability and upholding moral conduct in society.
orig: الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا كل واحد منهما مائة جلدة ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من المؤمنين

translation: The adulterer marries none but an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress marries none but an adulterer or an idolater. And this is forbidden for the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of adultery and idolatry, presenting them as moral transgressions that confine individuals to relationships with others of similar disregard for divine guidance. It emphasizes the principle that believers should hold themselves to higher moral standards and avoid unions with those who engage in such sins, thus protecting the sanctity and integrity of the Muslim community.
orig: الزاني لا ينكح إلا زانية أو مشركة والزانية لا ينكحها إلا زان أو مشرك وحرم ذلك على المؤمنين

translation: And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - flog them with eighty stripes and do not accept their testimony ever after. And they are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse addresses the serious matter of falsely accusing chaste women of adultery. It establishes stringent requirements for proving such a grave accusation—namely, the necessity of four witnesses. If the accusers fail to present these witnesses, they are to be subjected to a severe punishment of eighty lashes. Additionally, their credibility is permanently tarnished, as their testimony is no longer accepted in any legal matter. The verse underscores the gravity of slander and aims to protect the honor and dignity of individuals, particularly women. It highlights the importance of justice and the severe consequences of false accusations, branding the accusers as defiantly disobedient to the moral and social order prescribed by the faith.
orig: والذين يرمون المحصنات ثم لم يأتوا بأربعة شهداء فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة ولا تقبلوا لهم شهادة أبدا وأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and rectify themselves, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It reassures those who have committed sins that if they sincerely repent and make an effort to rectify their wrongdoings, Allah will forgive them. This reminds believers that it is never too late to turn back and seek Allah's forgiveness and that His mercy encompasses all who are genuinely remorseful and strive to improve.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the witness of one of them [shall be] four testimonies [swearing] by Allah that indeed, he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where a husband accuses his wife of adultery but lacks external witnesses to support his claim. The requirement for him to swear by Allah four times underscores the seriousness of such accusations and the emphasis on truthfulness. It ensures that false accusations are not made lightly, stressing the gravity and sanctity of marital relations. This mechanism serves to protect the integrity and dignity of individuals involved while maintaining a strict adherence to truth and justice.
orig: والذين يرمون أزواجهم ولم يكن لهم شهداء إلا أنفسهم فشهادة أحدهم أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الصادقين

translation: And the fifth [oath will be] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he should be among the liars.
interpretation: This verse addresses the procedure for dealing with accusations of adultery within a marriage when there are no witnesses. Specifically, it refers to the sworn statements made by the husband, who must testify four times about the truthfulness of his accusation and then invoke a curse upon himself in the fifth oath if he is lying. This highlights the serious consequences and personal accountability involved in making such grave allegations, placing the matter in the hands of divine judgment when human evidence is unavailable.
orig: والخامسة أن لعنت الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين

translation: It will avert the punishment from her if she testifies four times by Allah that he is indeed telling a lie.
interpretation: This verse addresses a situation where a woman is accused of adultery, providing her a way to defend herself by swearing four times by Allah that the accusation is false. It underscores the importance of bearing witness and the serious nature of such oaths in Islamic law, offering a method to maintain justice and protect the innocent.
orig: ويدرأ عنها العذاب أن تشهد أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين

translation: And the fifth [oath will be] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he should be among the truthful.
interpretation: This verse discusses the procedure of Li'an (mutual cursing) in Islamic law, where a husband who accuses his wife of adultery without four witnesses can swear four times by Allah of her guilt, and the fifth oath invokes Allah's curse upon himself if he is lying. Here, the verse indicates that the wife's fifth oath is different; she calls upon Allah's wrath upon herself if her husband's accusation is true. This underscores the seriousness of the oaths and the grave consequences of dishonesty in such severe allegations, emphasizing accountability and the sanctity of marital relations.
orig: والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين

translation: Were it not for the grace of Allah and His mercy upon you, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless grace and mercy that Allah extends to His creation. It underscores that human beings are fallible and prone to sin, yet Allah is always willing to forgive those who repent. The attributes of Allah as Oft-Returning and All-Wise emphasize that His forgiveness is not arbitrary; it is coupled with profound wisdom and understanding of human nature.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله تواب حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who came with falsehood are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what [punishment] he has earned from the sin, and he who took upon himself the greater portion thereof - for him is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the incident of slander or false accusations made against a person or group within the community. It emphasizes that such trials, although seemingly negative, can ultimately serve a beneficial purpose by exposing the truth and testing the community's faith and resilience. Each individual involved in the falsehood will be held accountable for their actions, and those who played a major role in propagating the lie will face severe consequences. This serves as a reminder of the importance of integrity, accountability, and trust within the community.
orig: إن الذين جاءوا بالإفك عصبة منكم لا تحسبوه شرا لكم بل هو خير لكم لكل امرئ منهم ما اكتسب من الإثم والذي تولى كبره منهم له عذاب عظيم

translation: Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think well of themselves [and say]: This is an obvious falsehood?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a positive opinion of fellow believers and refraining from accepting or spreading baseless accusations. The verse urges believers to adopt a mindset of goodness and integrity, reflecting a community's moral strength by rejecting slander and maintaining trust among its members.
orig: لولا إذ سمعتموه ظن المؤمنون والمؤمنات بأنفسهم خيرا وقالوا هذا إفك مبين

translation: Why did they not produce four witnesses? Because if they do not produce the witnesses, then they are liars in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of providing strong evidence when making serious accusations, such as acts of immorality. It sets a high standard of proof, requiring four witnesses, to prevent false accusations and protect individuals' honor and dignity. Those who fail to meet this standard are deemed liars by Allah, highlighting the importance of truthfulness and the severe consequences of slander.
orig: لولا جاءوا عليه بأربعة شهداء فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

translation: And if it had not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, you would have been touched for that (lie) in which you were involved by a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense grace and mercy that Allah bestows upon humanity, both in this world and in the Hereafter. It highlights Allah's willingness to forgive and protect people from severe consequences despite their mistakes or transgressions. It serves as a reminder that without the divine favor and mercy of Allah, mankind would face great hardships and penalties for their wrongdoings, underscoring the importance of being grateful and mindful of Allah's benevolence.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته في الدنيا والآخرة لمسكم في ما أفضتم فيه عذاب عظيم

translation: When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge and thought it was insignificant while it was, in the sight of Allah, tremendous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of spreading false information or rumors, emphasizing that speaking without knowledge and assuming such acts to be trivial can have serious consequences in the sight of Allah. It serves as a warning to be cautious with one's words and to ensure that they are based on truth and knowledge, as what may seem minor to humans can be of significant importance to Allah.
orig: إذ تلقونه بألسنتكم وتقولون بأفواهكم ما ليس لكم به علم وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم

translation: And why, when you heard it, did you not say, 'It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You; this is a great slander'?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of believers to refrain from spreading false rumors or gossip. Instead, they should recognize such talk as slander and declare their disassociation from it. It underscores the importance of integrity in speech and the recognition of Allah's sanctity by avoiding actions and words that go against moral and ethical principles. The verse calls for mindfulness and self-restraint in communication, urging the community to uphold truth and purity in their interactions.
orig: ولولا إذ سمعتموه قلتم ما يكون لنا أن نتكلم بهذا سبحانك هذا بهتان عظيم

translation: Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder and warning from Allah to the believers, urging them to refrain from repeating a specific wrongdoing or sin. It underscores the importance of adhering to the moral and ethical guidelines prescribed by faith, implying that true belief necessitates learning from past mistakes and striving to avoid them in the future. The emphasis on 'if you are believers' highlights that genuine belief is reflected in one's actions and conscious efforts to abide by divine commandments.
orig: يعظكم الله أن تعودوا لمثله أبدا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Allah makes clear to you the signs, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah provides clarity and guidance through the signs and revelations He sends. The attributes of Allah being 'Knowing' and 'Wise' highlight His comprehensive knowledge and perfect judgment. Therefore, the guidance He provides is both accurate and beneficial for those who seek to understand His will and follow His path.
orig: ويبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who like that immorality should be spread [or publicized] among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against the dissemination of immorality and scandal among believers. It underscores the serious consequences of such actions, both in this life and in the Hereafter. Spreading indecency damages societal morals and harms individuals' reputations. The verse also highlights the limited understanding and knowledge of humans compared to Allah, reminding believers to trust in His wisdom and judgement.
orig: إن الذين يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم في الدنيا والآخرة والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And if it were not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense grace and mercy of Allah upon humanity. It underscores that human beings are recipients of God's compassion and kindness, and without His favor, they would face profound difficulties. Importantly, it serves as a reminder that Allah's nature is inherently kind and merciful, encouraging believers to feel gratitude and to seek His mercy in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله رءوف رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, indeed, he commands immorality and wrongdoing. And if it had not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure, ever; but Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against following the deceptive paths laid out by Satan, emphasizing that such paths lead to immorality and evil deeds. It underscores the idea that human beings cannot achieve purity or moral righteousness on their own; rather, it is through Allah's mercy and favor that they are purified. Moreover, it reassures the believers of Allah's omnipresent awareness and wisdom.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء والله سميع عليم

translation: And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to those who are blessed with wealth and virtue to continue supporting their relatives, the needy, and those who have migrated for the sake of Allah, even if they have been wronged by them. It encourages believers to pardon and overlook the faults of others, emphasizing that they should aspire for God's forgiveness by practicing forgiveness themselves. The verse underscores the attributes of Allah as Forgiving and Merciful, urging believers to embody these qualities in their interactions with others.
orig: ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى والمساكين والمهاجرين في سبيل الله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who [falsely] accuse chaste, unaware, and believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter; and they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of accusing chaste, unaware, and believing women of adultery without evidence. It emphasizes that such slanderous behavior is met with divine disapproval and severe consequences both in this life and in the Hereafter. The curse and the promise of great punishment highlight the importance of protecting the honor and dignity of individuals, especially women, in society.
orig: إن الذين يرمون المحصنات الغافلات المؤمنات لعنوا في الدنيا والآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse depicts the Day of Judgment, highlighting the gravity of one's actions. On this day, the very parts of the human body that were involved in actions—such as tongues for speech, hands for deeds, and feet for movement—will testify truthfully against them. It underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the inescapable nature of one's own deeds serving as evidence, emphasizing personal accountability and the thoroughness of God's judgment.
orig: يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: On that Day, Allah will pay them in full their deserved recompense, and they will come to know that Allah alone is the Ultimate Truth, Perfectly Clear in what He does.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Day of Judgment when people will be judged and given their due recompense for their deeds. It highlights that on this day, the absolute justice and truth of Allah will be evident to everyone. The verse assures that Allah's judgment is infallible and transparent, emphasizing the ultimate reality and clarity of His justice and essence.
orig: يومئذ يوفيهم الله دينهم الحق ويعلمون أن الله هو الحق المبين

translation: Impure women are for impure men, and impure men are for impure women; and pure women are for pure men, and pure men are for pure women. Those are declared innocent of what they say; for them is forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse delineates the moral and ethical alignment between men and women, suggesting that people of similar virtue are best paired together. It stresses the idea that those who are pure in character and deed are absolved of false accusations and promises them divine forgiveness and bountiful blessings. Implicitly, it highlights the importance of maintaining personal purity and moral integrity for both men and women.
orig: الخبيثات للخبيثين والخبيثون للخبيثات والطيبات للطيبين والطيبون للطيبات أولئك مبرءون مما يقولون لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants; that is better for you, that you might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking permission and exchanging greetings before entering someone else's home. It upholds the principles of respect, privacy, and social etiquette in a community. By following this guidance, believers demonstrate mindfulness and consideration towards others, fostering harmonious relationships and mutual respect.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها ذلكم خير لكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: But if you do not find anyone therein, do not enter them until permission is given to you. And if it is said to you, 'Go back,' then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting others' privacy and boundaries. It instructs that one should not enter another's house without permission, symbolizing broader principles of respect and societal etiquette. By advising to return if entry is denied, it underscores humility and self-restraint. Adherence to these guidelines is not only morally superior but also seen favorably by Allah, who is aware of all actions.
orig: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم وإن قيل لكم ارجعوا فارجعوا هو أزكى لكم والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited in which there is convenience for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse indicates that it is permissible to enter uninhabited houses if they contain something beneficial for you, such as a shelter or a place to store goods. It also stresses that Allah is aware of one's intentions and actions, both overt and hidden. The stipulation of this permission underlines the importance of maintaining ethical behavior and intentions, even in actions that seem minor or are done in private.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تدخلوا بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their modesty; that will make for greater purity for them. Surely, Allah is well aware of all they do.
interpretation: This verse instructs believing men to practice modesty by lowering their gaze to avoid looking at what is prohibited, and to guard their private parts, indicating the importance of sexual morality. The guidance aims to foster personal and communal purity and righteousness. It also underscores that Allah is fully aware of human actions, highlighting the importance of adhering to these commands sincerely and consistently.
orig: قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم ويحفظوا فروجهم ذلك أزكى لهم إن الله خبير بما يصنعون

translation: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their modesty; that they should not display their beauty and ornaments except what (ordinarily) appear thereof; that they should draw their veils over their bosoms and not display their beauty except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or the slaves whom their right hands possess, or male attendants free of sexual desires, or small children who have no sense of the shame of sex. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their ornaments. And turn to Allah all together, O believers, that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse outlines guidelines for the modest behavior and dress of believing women in Islam. Women are instructed to lower their gaze and protect their modesty, while also covering their beauty, except for what naturally appears. Specific exceptions are given for close male relatives and certain others who would not pose a threat to their modesty. The mention of drawing veils over their bosoms emphasizes covering intimate areas. Additionally, it advises against actions that might draw undue attention to a woman's beauty. The concluding directive for all believers to turn to Allah indicates the importance of repentance and seeking success through divine guidance.
orig: وقل للمؤمنات يغضضن من أبصارهن ويحفظن فروجهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا ما ظهر منها وليضربن بخمرهن على جيوبهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا لبعولتهن أو آبائهن أو آباء بعولتهن أو أبنائهن أو أبناء بعولتهن أو إخوانهن أو بني إخوانهن أو بني أخواتهن أو نسائهن أو ما ملكت أيمانهن أو التابعين غير أولي الإربة من الرجال أو الطفل الذين لم يظهروا على عورات النساء ولا يضربن بأرجلهن ليعلم ما يخفين من زينتهن وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And marry those among you who are single and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to support the marriage of single individuals and their righteous slaves, emphasizing the importance of providing social and financial support for those seeking to marry. It assures that poverty should not be a deterrent to marriage, as Allah's bounty and provision are vast and encompassing. The verse also underscores Allah's infinite knowledge and generosity, highlighting His capability to provide for those who trust in Him.
orig: وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله والله واسع عليم

translation: And let those who do not find the means to marry keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them out of His bounty. And if any of your slaves seek a deed of emancipation, execute it for them if you know there is good in them; and give them something out of the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not force your girls into prostitution if they desire chastity, seeking the temporary interests of worldly life, and whoever forces them, then indeed, after their compulsion, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses several important social and ethical issues. Firstly, it advises those who are unable to marry to maintain chastity until Allah provides for them. Secondly, it encourages the emancipation of slaves who seek their freedom and to support them financially. Thirdly, it strictly prohibits forcing women into prostitution, emphasizing the importance of consent and chastity. Lastly, the verse assures that those who are coerced are not held accountable for actions they were forced into, highlighting Allah's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء إن أردن تحصنا لتبتغوا عرض الحياة الدنيا ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن غفور رحيم

translation: We have certainly sent down to you clear Verses and examples from those who passed on before you and an admonition for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and guidance of the divine revelations sent to humankind. It points out that the Qur’anic verses are clear and understandable, providing lessons and moral examples from historical events and people who lived in the past. Moreover, it serves as an admonition or counsel specifically for those who are pious and conscious of Allah, encouraging them to heed and reflect upon these teachings for their moral and spiritual edification.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليكم آيات مبينات ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم وموعظة للمتقين

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is in glass, the glass as if it were a brightly shining star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of light to describe Allah's guidance and wisdom permeating the heavens and the earth. The niche and lamp represent the heart of a believer filled with divine light, which illuminates and clarifies truth. The blessed olive tree's oil glowing without fire emphasizes the inherent purity and clarity of divine guidance. 'Light upon light' signifies multiple layers of enlightenment and guidance provided by Allah. It underscores that only those whom Allah wills are guided to this divine light, reflecting His omniscience and Almighty wisdom in guiding humanity.
orig: الله نور السماوات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein, exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and significance of places of worship, such as mosques. It highlights that Allah has commanded that these places be honored and elevated, both physically and spiritually. The continuous remembrance and glorification of Allah, from morning until evening, signifies the integral role these spaces play in the daily lives of believers. It underscores the importance of maintaining the sanctity of these places and ensuring they are used for the remembrance and worship of Allah.
orig: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

translation: Men who are not distracted by trade or sale from the remembrance of Allah, performing prayer, and giving zakat. They fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong faith and commitment of certain men who prioritize their religious duties over their worldly activities. Their devotion to the remembrance of Allah, performing regular prayers, and giving charity (zakat) remains unwavering despite their engagement in commerce. This steadfastness is driven by their awareness and fear of the Day of Judgment, a day marked by immense turmoil when people's inner and outer states will be transformed. Their piety and sincere dedication to faith reflect their deep spiritual conviction and consciousness of accountability before Allah.
orig: رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

translation: So that Allah will reward them according to the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty. And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless generosity and fairness of Allah. It implies that Allah rewards individuals not merely for their actions but according to the best of their actions, thus providing greater return for their good deeds. Additionally, Allah's provision and bounty are limitless and not confined by human measures; He bestows upon whom He wills in a manner that transcends finite calculations. This portrays a sense of hope and encouragement for believers to strive for goodness, reassuring them of Allah's ample rewards and unrestricted grace.
orig: ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: But those who disbelieve—their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one thinks it is water, but when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing. However, he finds Allah with him, who will pay him his due. And Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy to convey the futility of the deeds of those who reject faith. It compares their works to a mirage in a desert, which misleads the thirsting person into thinking it is water. In the same way, disbelievers may think their actions will bring them benefit and salvation, only to find out they are in vain when they face reality. Ultimately, they will encounter Allah, who will hold them accountable, emphasizing the quickness and certainty of divine judgment.
orig: والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده فوفاه حسابه والله سريع الحساب

translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describing the states of those who are distant from divine guidance. They are likened to being in profound, layered darkness, unable to perceive or find their way. Just as one would struggle to see their hand in such darkness, these individuals cannot see spiritual truth without the light of guidance from Allah. It emphasizes the importance of divine enlightenment and suggests that without it, people remain lost and enveloped in moral and spiritual obscurity.
orig: أو كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فما له من نور

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the birds with wings spread? Each [of them] has known its [means of] prayer and exalting [Him], and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of worship and glorification of Allah. It reminds us that all of creation, from the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth to the birds in the sky, are engaged in acts of worship and know their specific ways to praise and exalt Allah. The verse serves to highlight the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah, who is fully aware of all actions and acts of devotion, suggesting that everything in the universe is in a state of submission to Him.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسبح له من في السماوات والأرض والطير صافات كل قد علم صلاته وتسبيحه والله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and the earth. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability to Allah, where all beings will return to Him for judgment and recompense. It reinforces the concept of divine authority and the transient nature of worldly life in comparison to the eternal afterlife.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله المصير

translation: Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them into a mass, and you see the rain emerge from within it? And He sends down from the sky, from mountains (of clouds) within it, hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the phenomenon of cloud formation and precipitation as an example of Allah's omnipotence and control over natural processes. It serves as a reminder of the power and precision of divine orchestration. The clouds, driven and assembled by Allah, become a mechanism through which rain and hail are dispensed, impacting those whom Allah chooses. Additionally, the brightness of the lightning is so intense that it can dazzle or overwhelm the human eye, signifying the extraordinary and awe-inspiring nature of Allah's creations. The verse thus emphasizes the meticulous and purposeful way in which the natural world operates under divine command, showcasing both mercy and might in how blessings and challenges are distributed.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله ركاما فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد فيصيب به من يشاء ويصرفه عن من يشاء يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those with vision.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on natural phenomena as signs of Allah's power and wisdom. The alternation of night and day serves as a reminder of the continuous, sustaining presence of the Divine. It calls upon those who are perceptive and insightful to recognize and contemplate the deeper truths and lessons embedded in the patterns of the natural world.
orig: يقلب الله الليل والنهار إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: And Allah has created every living creature from water. Among them are those that move on their bellies, and among them are those that walk on two legs, and among them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the diversity of life created by Allah and highlights His omnipotence in forming different types of creatures from water. It points to the miracle of creation, emphasizing that Allah has the power and authority to create beings in various forms and modes of movement. The mention of different creatures walking on their bellies, two legs, and four legs serves to display the variety and complexity of life, ultimately attributing all this diversity to the will and capability of Allah.
orig: والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع يخلق الله ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, We have sent down clear revelations. And Allah guides whom He wills to the Straight Path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains clear signs and guidance from Allah. The ultimate guidance to the path of righteousness is a divine prerogative, granted by Allah to those He wills. It underscores the belief that human understanding and spiritual insight are under Allah's control, and He directs individuals towards truth and moral rectitude according to His wisdom.
orig: لقد أنزلنا آيات مبينات والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And they say, 'We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey'; then a party of them turns away thereafter, and those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the inconsistency between words and actions among some people who profess belief in Allah and His Messenger and claim to obey them. However, when it comes to actual implementation and adherence to the teachings, a group among them turns away, indicating hypocrisy. Genuine faith is demonstrated through consistent actions, and mere verbal declarations without corresponding deeds do not make one a true believer.
orig: ويقولون آمنا بالله وبالرسول وأطعنا ثم يتولى فريق منهم من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: But when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a party of them turns aside in refusal.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and hypocrisy of certain people who, despite their outward claims of faith, turn away when asked to submit to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. It underscores the importance of true submission and trust in divine guidance, and calls out the reluctance or refusal of some to accept decisions that go against their desires or personal interests.
orig: وإذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم إذا فريق منهم معرضون

translation: But if the right is on their side, they come to him in prompt obedience.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and hypocrisy of those who are unwilling to accept judgment unless it benefits them. When the decision aligns with their interests ('if the right is on their side'), they quickly and willingly accept it ('in prompt obedience'). This behavior contrasts with their reluctance or resistance when the judgment does not favor them, shedding light on their self-serving approach to justice and truth.
orig: وإن يكن لهم الحق يأتوا إليه مذعنين

translation: Is there a disease in their hearts, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them? No, it is they who are the unjust.
interpretation: This verse questions the motives behind the disbelief and disobedience of certain individuals. It suggests three possible reasons for their attitude: a sickness in their hearts (symbolic of moral or spiritual corruption), doubt in their minds, or fear of injustice from God and His Messenger. The verse explicitly refutes these excuses by asserting that it is actually these individuals who are committing injustice, thereby highlighting their own culpability and the intrinsic flaw in their beliefs and actions.
orig: أفي قلوبهم مرض أم ارتابوا أم يخافون أن يحيف الله عليهم ورسوله بل أولئك هم الظالمون

translation: The only statement of the (true) believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is that they say, 'We hear and we obey.' And those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude and disposition of true believers when they are called upon to follow the judgments or commandments of Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes the importance of obedience and willingness to accept divine guidance without hesitation or resistance. The phrase 'We hear and we obey' signifies complete submission to the will of Allah, which is portrayed as the path to true success. This also underscores the idea that faith is not just a matter of belief but also of action and adherence to divine laws.
orig: إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah and is mindful of Him, then it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, highlighting that true success is achieved through a combination of adherence to divine commandments and conscious mindfulness of Allah's presence. It suggests that both fear (awe) of God and active piety lead to ultimate success, underscoring that a holistic approach to faith—encompassing both belief and righteous action—ensures prosperity in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يطع الله ورسوله ويخش الله ويتقه فأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go forth. Say, 'Do not swear. [Such] obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with that which you do.'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who swear strong oaths in the name of Allah to demonstrate their willingness to obey commands. The message from Allah, conveyed through the Prophet, advises against making such oaths. Instead, true obedience is shown through consistent and sincere actions, not mere words or declarations. Allah's omniscience encompasses all actions, making empty promises unnecessary. Sincere and genuine obedience is what counts and is recognized by Allah, who is fully aware of both outward deeds and inner intentions.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن أمرتهم ليخرجن قل لا تقسموا طاعة معروفة إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only that duty with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be rightly guided. And there is not upon the Messenger except the [responsibility for] clear notification.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger. It acknowledges the autonomous choice individuals have in accepting or rejecting the message but clarifies that the responsibility of the Prophet is solely to convey the clear message. The emphasis is on guidance through adherence to divine directives, highlighting that true guidance and righteousness come from following the Prophet's teachings. The verse also delineates the distinction of accountability between the Prophet and the people: the Prophet is accountable for delivering the message, while the people are accountable for their response to it.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن تولوا فإنما عليه ما حمل وعليكم ما حملتم وإن تطيعوه تهتدوا وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will certainly grant them succession to authority upon the earth as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that – then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's promise to the believers who engage in righteous deeds. It assures them of succession to leadership and authority on earth, as was granted to previous communities of faith, establishing their religion firmly. Furthermore, it promises to replace their fear with security, underscoring the condition of exclusive worship of Allah without associating any partners with Him. The verse then warns that those who disbelieve following the fulfillment of this promise are considered defiantly disobedient, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness and righteousness in the relationship with Allah.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم وليبدلنهم من بعد خوفهم أمنا يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ومن كفر بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of three fundamental practices in Islam: establishing regular prayer (salah), giving to charity (zakah), and obeying the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). By adhering to these key components of faith, believers may attain Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It highlights the integrated approach to worship and social responsibility, as well as following the Prophet's guidance as a path to divine compassion.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape in the land; their abode will be the Fire, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that disbelievers cannot evade Allah's authority and justice, regardless of their actions on earth. Their final destination is the Fire, symbolizing their ultimate punishment. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the inevitability of divine retribution.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض ومأواهم النار ولبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not yet reached puberty among you ask your permission [before entering] at three times: before the dawn prayer, when you put aside your garments [for rest] at noon, and after the evening prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them beyond these [periods], for they continually circulate among you - some of you among others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining privacy and modesty within the household. It instructs believers to ensure that even those who serve them and children who have not yet reached puberty ask for permission before entering private areas at specific times when people are likely to be undressed or in a state of rest. These designated times are before dawn prayer, at noon when resting, and after the evening prayer. Outside these times, interaction is more casual and less restrictive. This guidance reflects Allah's wisdom and knowledge in promoting respect for personal space and dignity within familial and social settings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليستأذنكم الذين ملكت أيمانكم والذين لم يبلغوا الحلم منكم ثلاث مرات من قبل صلاة الفجر وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ومن بعد صلاة العشاء ثلاث عورات لكم ليس عليكم ولا عليهم جناح بعدهن طوافون عليكم بعضكم على بعض كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask for permission as those before them asked for permission. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of modesty and privacy. When children reach the age of puberty, they are instructed to seek permission before entering private spaces, just as adults do. This command ensures respect for personal boundaries and integrity within the household. The verse also emphasizes God's meticulous guidance and wisdom in laying down such rules, reflecting divine knowledge and the practical benefits of following these teachings for societal harmony and personal dignity.
orig: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And as for women past childbearing who have no hope of marriage, it is no sin for them if they put off their outer garments without displaying their adornment. But to be modest is better for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses elderly women who are no longer hopeful of getting married. It permits them to relax their dress code by removing their outer garments, provided they do not display any adornments that might attract attention. The stipulation emphasizes the importance of modesty but recognizes the unique circumstances of older women. Nevertheless, maintaining a certain level of modesty is considered superior. Furthermore, the verse reinforces the omniscience of Allah, reminding believers that He hears and knows all actions and intentions.
orig: والقواعد من النساء اللاتي لا يرجون نكاحا فليس عليهن جناح أن يضعن ثيابهن غير متبرجات بزينة وأن يستعففن خير لهن والله سميع عليم

translation: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick, nor upon yourselves if you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house] of a friend. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other - a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse underscores Islamic teachings of inclusivity and compassion by stating that those with physical ailments or disabilities are not to be burdened. Additionally, it provides guidance on social norms within the community, particularly in sharing food and respect toward family and friends. The emphasis on saying greetings of peace when entering homes symbolizes a culture of harmony and goodwill, affirming that such practices are divinely sanctioned and encouraged to foster understanding among believers.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common interest, they do not depart until they have asked his permission. Verily, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for something of their own affairs, give permission to whom you will among them and ask Allah's forgiveness for them; verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of true believers, emphasizing their faith in Allah and His Messenger, and their respect for the Prophet's authority, particularly in matters of communal importance. It also underscores the importance of seeking permission and demonstrates respect and consideration for leadership. By asking forgiveness for them, it acknowledges human fallibility and the need for divine mercy, reinforcing the compassionate and forgiving nature of Allah.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves as the call of one of you to another. Allah knows those of you who slip away concealing themselves behind others. So let those beware who dissent from his order, lest fitnah strike them or a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers to treat the call and command of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with utmost respect and not like any ordinary call among themselves. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of those who try to avoid their duties by sneaking away and that disobeying the Prophet's directives could lead to severe consequences, either in the form of a trial (fitnah) or a grievous punishment. It serves as a reminder of the gravity of adhering to the Prophet's guidance and the divine awareness of one's intentions and actions.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He knows what you are upon. And the Day they will be returned to Him, then He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah. It declares that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, signifying His ultimate authority and control. The verse reassures that Allah is fully aware of the states and actions of individuals. It also serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment, where all will be returned to Allah, and He will disclose the deeds they have done, reinforcing accountability. The verse concludes by reaffirming Allah's encompassing knowledge, highlighting that nothing is beyond His awareness.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exalted nature and supreme blessings of Allah, who revealed the 'Criterion' (the Qur'an) to His servant, Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the purpose of this divine revelation: to serve as guidance and a warning to all of humanity, emphasizing the universal mission of the Prophet and the comprehensive nature of the message.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He has not taken a son, nor has He a partner in His dominion. He created everything and determined it with precise determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah in His dominion over the entire universe. It refutes any notion of Allah having offspring or partners, highlighting His unparalleled authority and singularity. The verse also underscores Allah's wisdom and meticulousness in creation, indicating that everything is purposefully and precisely designed by Him.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: Yet they have taken besides Him other deities that create nothing but are themselves created. And they possess not for themselves any harm or benefit, nor do they possess [power to cause] death or life or resurrection.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who take other deities besides Allah, emphasizing that these deities are devoid of any creative power and are themselves creations. It highlights their impotence, as they cannot cause harm or benefit nor do they have control over life, death, or resurrection. This underscores the futility of worshipping anything other than the One true God, who alone has these sovereign abilities.
orig: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

translation: "And those who disbelieve say, 'This (Quran) is nothing but a lie that he has invented, and others have helped him at it.' Indeed, they have produced an unjust wrong and a lie."
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations made by disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They claim that the Qur'an is a fabrication and that he had assistance from others in creating it. The verse counters by declaring these accusations as baseless and unjust, underscoring the divine origin of the Qur'an and the wrongful nature of the disbelievers' claims.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

translation: And they say, 'Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon.'
interpretation: In this verse, the disbelievers accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an by copying old tales and having them dictated to him regularly. This statement is an attempt to undermine the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'anic revelations by implying that they are merely human inventions based on ancient stories.
orig: وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Say, 'It has been sent down by He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed by Allah, who possesses complete knowledge of all hidden matters in the heavens and the earth. It underlines His omniscience, indicating that nothing is beyond His awareness. Additionally, it highlights Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, suggesting that His vast knowledge is coupled with compassion and readiness to pardon. This serves as a reassurance to the believers of Allah's encompassing wisdom and benevolence.
orig: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, 'What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why has not an angel been sent down to him to be a warner with him?'
