The verse emphasizes the virtue of judging people based on their character and abilities, rather than superficial factors.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: He said, 'I intend to wed one of these two daughters of mine to you on the condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be a favor from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous.'
interpretation: In this verse, we see an example of a mutually beneficial agreement made under Islamic principles. The man offers his daughter's hand in marriage to another under the condition that he serves the family for a specified time, reflecting customs of the time where marriage agreements could involve service or labor. The offeror assures him that if he chooses to serve more than the required eight years, it will be out of his own kindness, indicating the voluntary nature of the additional service. Additionally, the man emphasizes that he does not intend to cause hardship, portraying a sense of fairness and righteousness in his proposal, further aligning with the Islamic value of justice and benevolence.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'That is established between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice to me, and Allah is a witness to what we say.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a contractual agreement between two parties, ensuring that whichever term of service is completed, there will be no wrongdoing or injustice. It stresses the importance of fulfilling agreements and highlights that Allah is the ultimate witness to all promises and transactions, underscoring the importance of honesty and accountability in dealings.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: Then, when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived a fire in the direction of Mount Tur. He said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I can bring you some information from it or a burning stick so that you may warm yourselves.'
interpretation: This verse describes a pivotal moment in the life of Prophet Moses. After he fulfilled his service term, he embarked on a journey with his family. Along the way, he witnessed a fire on Mount Tur, which drew his attention. He decided to investigate the phenomenon, hoping to gather valuable information or a burning stick to provide warmth for his family. This moment signifies a turning point, as the fire leads Moses to direct communication with God, ultimately heralding his prophetic mission. Thus, this verse underscores themes of duty, family care, curiosity, and the beginning of divine guidance.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot from the tree: 'O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse describes a pivotal moment in the story of Prophet Moses (Musa) when he encounters a divine presence. The voice calling from the right side of the valley, in a blessed spot near a tree, signifies a holy and significant event. The declaration 'I am Allah, Lord of the worlds' establishes the identity of the voice as none other than God. This moment marks the beginning of Moses' prophetic mission, affirming his role as a messenger chosen by Allah to lead and guide his people.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And [he was told], 'Throw down your staff.' But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not look back. [Allah said], 'O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the moment when Prophet Moses was commanded by Allah to throw down his staff, which then transformed into a serpent. Moses, struck by fear, fled but was reassured by Allah not to be afraid and to return, as he was under divine protection. The verse signifies the importance of trusting in Allah’s power and protection, even in situations that appear frightening or overwhelming. It also highlights the miraculous signs given to the prophets to establish their divine connection and authority.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: Place your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease, and draw your arm close to you to ward off fear. These are two evidences from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah advises Moses to perform two miraculous signs in front of Pharaoh and his assembly. The first is placing his hand into his pocket and having it come out shining white, signifying purity and divine intervention without any ailment. The second is drawing his arm close to calm his fear, symbolizing reassurance and protection from Allah. These signs are meant to be proof of Moses' prophethood and the divine message he carries, demonstrating God's power and authority to a stubborn and sinful audience.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I killed one of them, and I fear they will kill me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and apprehension of Prophet Moses when he acknowledges to God that he had previously killed a man from the people of Pharaoh, and therefore, he feared retribution. It showcases a moment of vulnerability and honesty, where Prophet Moses seeks reassurance and protection from God in the face of his past actions and the potential threats he perceives.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: My brother Aaron is more eloquent than me in speech, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: This verse conveys Prophet Moses’ (Musa) request to God for support from his brother Aaron (Harun) due to Aaron’s eloquence. Moses anticipates resistance and disbelief from the people he is sent to guide, thus he seeks Aaron’s companionship and assistance for better communication and reinforcement of his message.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, 'We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will grant you both an authority so they will not reach you. With Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors.'
interpretation: This verse signifies God's promise of support and empowerment to His chosen messengers, specifically Moses and his brother Aaron. It underscores the divine assurance that their mission shall be fortified by God's might and the authority bestowed upon them. Despite the opposition they face, they are assured of victory through the signs and commandments of God, highlighting the ultimate triumph of divine guidance and those who adhere to it.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: But when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, 'This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have never heard of this among our ancestors of old.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and disbelief of the people to whom Prophet Moses was sent. Despite the clear signs and miracles that Moses brought, they accused him of practicing magic and dismissed his message as imposture. This response indicates a deep-seated resistance to changing their inherited beliefs and traditions, highlighting the challenges faced by prophets in bringing their communities to the truth.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, 'My Lord is most knowing of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be the succession in the home. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Moses (Musa) emphasizes the ultimate wisdom and justice of God (Allah). It reassures that God is fully aware of who brings true guidance and of those who will ultimately attain a favorable end in the Hereafter. The verse also stresses that wrongdoers, those who act unjustly and oppress others, will not succeed in achieving true success, whether in this world or in the Hereafter. This serves as a reminder of accountability and divine justice.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses; and indeed, I think he is among the liars.'
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is depicted as arrogantly declaring himself the only god recognized by his people, dismissing any divine authority other than his own. He instructs Haman to construct a lofty tower, symbolizing an attempt to physically reach and challenge the God of Moses. Pharaoh's skepticism and mockery reveal his hardened heart and disbelief in the truth brought by Moses. This verse highlights the futility of Pharaoh's arrogance and resistance against divine guidance.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and wrongful conduct of Pharaoh and his soldiers, who acted with hubris and oppression on earth. It also underscores their denial of accountability before God, believing that they would not face any consequences or be brought back to Him for judgment. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate return to God and the fallacy of assuming impunity from divine justice.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. See then what was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse recounts the downfall of Pharaoh and his army as a consequence of their oppression and tyranny. It serves as a powerful reminder of the fate that befalls those who engage in wrongdoing and injustice. The verse underscores the concept of divine retribution, emphasizing that no matter how powerful or invincible the oppressors may seem, their end is inevitable and serves as a lesson for others.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse conveys a warning about those who lead others towards misguidance and evil. It emphasizes the severe consequences these leaders will face on the Day of Resurrection. Despite their positions of influence in this world, they will find no support or assistance in the Hereafter, highlighting the ultimate accountability for guiding others towards harmful paths.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine retribution for those who incur God's wrath through their defiant and sinful actions. The curse in this world signifies continuous disgrace and misfortune, while the ultimate humiliation and rejection are reserved for them on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a stern warning and a call for moral rectitude and piety.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as an enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the scripture given to Prophet Moses (the Torah) as a source of enlightenment, guidance, and mercy for the people after the destruction of previous disobedient nations. It underscores the ongoing divine mission to provide humanity with direction and the hope that they will reflect and learn from past mistakes. The message underscores God's continued care and provision for humanity through sacred texts, aiming to lead them toward righteousness and mindfulness of divine instructions.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the matter, and you were not among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that he was not physically present when Allah communicated with Moses. It underscores that the Prophet's knowledge of these events is through divine revelation, reinforcing the authenticity of the Qur'an as a source of knowledge about past events that he could not have known otherwise.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We created generations [after generations], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending [messengers].
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has created many generations over time, each living for its appointed duration. It emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was not present among the people of Madyan to recite Allah’s revelations to them. Instead, it was Allah’s practice to send messengers to convey His messages to different communities. The verse underscores the continuity of divine guidance through various prophets across different eras and communities, showcasing Allah’s consistent care and concern for humanity's spiritual well-being.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And you were not on the western side when We revealed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses to that. But We produced [many] generations, and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending [messengers]. And you were not at the side of Mount Sinai when We called [Moses], but [were sent] as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting that he was not physically present during the significant events involving earlier prophets, such as Moses at Mount Sinai. It emphasizes that despite this, he has been sent as a messenger by God's mercy to warn and guide a people who had not previously received a warner. This underscores the continuity of God's guidance and affirms Muhammad's prophethood through divine revelation rather than personal witness.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: If not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands have put forth and they would say, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs and been among the believers?'
interpretation: This verse indicates that people often face consequences for their actions and might wish later that guidance had been sent to them beforehand to avoid those consequences. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and following divine guidance when it is available, rather than lamenting its absence after suffering misfortune.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?' Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before? They said, 'Both are works of magic supporting each other,' and they said, 'Indeed, we are disbelievers in both.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the rejection and skepticism faced by prophets when delivering the divine message. It highlights the irrational demands of the disbelievers who, despite witnessing the truth, ask for signs similar to those given to previous prophets, such as Moses. The verse underscores their continuous pattern of disbelief, as they dismissed Moses' miracles and now accuse both Moses and the current prophet (Muhammad) of performing magic. It illustrates the persistent refusal of disbelievers to accept the truth due to their prejudices and preconceived notions.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, 'Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah challenges those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an and the previous scriptures (like the Torah), asking them to produce a book that provides better guidance if they are truly sincere in their claims. This challenge underscores the unmatched guidance and wisdom contained in the revealed books and asserts the authenticity and superiority of the divine revelations over any human creation.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that they are only following their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance instead of personal desires. It indicates that those who reject the message of the Prophet and continue to follow their own whims are inherently misguided. Furthermore, it conveys a strong admonition that Allah does not provide guidance to those who persist in wrongdoing and injustice. The underlying message is a call to adhere to the path laid out by divine revelation and to avoid being led astray by one's own inclinations.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that clear and sufficient guidance has been provided through divine revelation, aiming to remind and exhort the people to reflect and remember the fundamental truths and duties laid out by God. It highlights the importance of the message in urging individuals to return to righteousness and faith.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture before, they believe in it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of Allah's message throughout time. It acknowledges that there are people among those who received earlier scriptures (like the Torah and the Gospel) who recognize the truth of the Qur'an and believe in it. This underlines the idea that true revelation from Allah transcends time and is recognized by those who sincerely seek the truth, regardless of the form in which it was initially revealed.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were [even] before it Muslims [submitting to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of true believers when the Qur'an is recited to them. They affirm their faith in its divine origin, recognizing it as the ultimate truth revealed by their Lord. The verse also emphasizes their prior submission to Allah, indicating a continuity and consistency in their worship and faith even before the Qur'an was revealed. This declaration reaffirms their acknowledgment and acceptance of divine guidance as an integral part of their spiritual journey.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: They will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lofty reward for those who exhibit patience, the virtue of responding to wrongdoings with good deeds, and the importance of spending from the provisions given by Allah. It emphasizes that those who endure challenges with patience and counteract harm with benevolence are spiritually elevated and will be doubly rewarded. Additionally, it underscores the act of charitable giving as a noble and rewarded deed.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say, 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we seek not the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the behavior of the truly pious believers when faced with trivial or foolish talk; they choose to disengage and steer away from it. Instead of engaging in disputes or arguments, they assert their own path of righteousness and respect others' paths. By wishing peace and declaring their disinterest in engaging with ignorance, they maintain their dignity and uphold moral integrity. This conveys the broader Islamic principle of responding to negativity with patience and peace.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine authority and wisdom of Allah in granting guidance. It serves as a reminder that human effort alone cannot guarantee guidance or faith for others, even for those whom one loves dearly. Ultimately, it is Allah's prerogative to guide whomever He wills. This underscores the belief in Allah's supreme knowledge and control over the matters of faith and righteousness.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, 'If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land.' Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which fruits of all kinds are brought, as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the fears of people who hesitate to embrace the message of the Prophet (PBUH) due to concerns about losing their socioeconomic security and stability. God reminds them of His divine provision and the security He has granted them in their homeland, specifically the sanctity and bounty of Mecca. It emphasizes that their sustenance and safety have been ensured by divine decree, illustrating their misplaced anxieties and lack of understanding or awareness of God's care and omnipotence. The verse subtly admonishes the lack of faith and ignorance among those who are fearful, encouraging trust in God's provision when following the divine guidance.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: How many a city have We destroyed whose people were ungrateful for their means of livelihood? Those are their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who are the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a reminder about the consequences of ingratitude and arrogance towards God's blessings. It highlights that numerous communities that were once prosperous and self-satisfied were ultimately destroyed by divine intervention due to their ingratitude. Their abandoned dwellings stand as silent witnesses to their downfall, and it underscores that all things ultimately return to God; He is the true inheritor of all.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother city a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. It indicates that Allah does not punish a community or destroy its cities without first sending a messenger to guide and warn them by delivering His revelations. This shows both the fairness in giving people a chance to heed the guidance and the accountability for those who persist in wrongdoing despite clear warnings. Thus, destruction comes only as a consequence of persistent and blatant injustice by the people.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment of the life of this world and its adornment, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly possessions and pleasures, reminding believers that what Allah has in store is far superior and eternal. It calls on individuals to reflect deeply and prioritize their spiritual and eternal well-being over the fleeting and often deceptive allure of material wealth and beauty.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Is then the one to whom We have promised a good promise which he will meet [on the Day of Resurrection] like the one whom We have provided with enjoyment of worldly life but who will be, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who receive the divine promise of a blessed afterlife due to their faith and righteous deeds, and those who indulge in the temporary pleasures of worldly life, only to face accountability and potential punishment on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the transient nature of worldly gains compared to the enduring reward of a good promise from Allah.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, a pivotal moment when God will question the disbelievers about the false deities and entities they associated with Him. It highlights the futility and falsehood of polytheism and the reality of divine accountability. The question posed by God underscores the absence and powerlessness of the so-called 'partners,' emphasizing the oneness and supremacy of God.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those upon whom the Word will have come into effect will say, 'Our Lord, these are the ones we misled. We misled them as we ourselves were misled. We declare our disassociation from them to You. They did not use to worship us.'
interpretation: This verse represents a scene on the Day of Judgment where those who led others astray will confess their own misguidance and attempt to absolve themselves of responsibility by declaring their disassociation from their followers. It highlights the acknowledgment and regret of the deceivers who admit their own misguidance and the falsehood of their leadership. Their defense that their followers did not actually worship them underscores their attempt to shift the believers' accountability. Overall, this verse emphasizes personal responsibility and the ultimate futility of following misguided leaders at the expense of true worship and guidance.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it will be said, "Call upon your partners" and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshiping entities other than Allah. On the Day of Judgment, those who associated partners with Allah will realize that these so-called partners have no power to help them. The verse underscores the realization and regret of those who did not follow the right path, as they witness the severe consequences of their misguided actions. It serves as a profound reminder of the importance of monotheism and guidance in Islam.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: On the Day He will call them and say, 'What did you answer the messengers?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when God will question people about their responses to the prophets and messengers He sent to guide them. It emphasizes accountability and encourages reflection on how one has adhered to divine guidance and the messages conveyed by the prophets.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: So the [significant] news will be blinded to them that Day, and they will not [be able to] ask one another.
interpretation: This verse signifies a time of ultimate reckoning, where individuals will be rendered unable to comprehend or discuss the crucial truths and events unfolding before them. In their state of bewilderment and shock, they will lack the capacity to seek answers or debate, highlighting a moment of divine judgment where human faculties and understanding fail.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But as for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, it is hoped that they will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the path to success and salvation as defined by the Qur'an. It emphasizes the importance of three key actions: repentance (returning to God and seeking forgiveness for past wrongs), maintaining faith (believing in God and His guidance), and performing good deeds (acting in ways that are just and beneficial). The use of the word 'hoped' indicates that while these actions significantly increase one's chances of attaining success, ultimate success is still subject to God's will and mercy.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah in creation and choice. It underscores that human beings do not have ultimate control over their own fate or the matters of the universe; instead, it is Allah who decides and determines everything according to His wisdom. The verse also highlights the necessity of glorifying Allah and repudiating any form of idolatry or association of partners with Him. This signifies the importance of recognizing Allah's unique status and ultimate power, encouraging believers to submit and trust in His divine decisions.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and intimate knowledge of human thoughts and actions. It serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is kept in the depths of one's heart or expressed openly. This awareness encourages believers to maintain sincerity and integrity in their faith and deeds, knowing that Allah is fully aware of their innermost intentions and external behaviors.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. His is the praise in the first life and the Hereafter, and His is the final decision, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the singularity and exclusivity of Allah's divinity, declaring that worship and gratitude are due to Him alone throughout all phases of existence. It underscores that ultimate authority and judgment belong to Allah, and reminds believers that they will ultimately return to Him for reckoning. This serves as a reaffirmation of faith in Allah's supreme power and justice.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not listen?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and singular authority of Allah. It poses a rhetorical question to make people reflect on the impossibility of anyone other than Allah being able to control such natural phenomena as the alternation between night and day. It invites contemplation on divine power and serves as a reminder to recognize and listen to the signs of Allah's existence and sovereignty.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should make the day continuous over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?'
interpretation: This verse invites contemplation on the omnipotence and singularity of Allah by posing a hypothetical scenario: if the day were to persist without end, only Allah has the power to bring about the night. It emphasizes humanity’s dependence on Allah’s controlled balance of the universe, urging people to recognize His unmatched authority and to be aware of the blessings He bestows, such as the alternation of day and night for rest and activity.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And out of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek from His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy of Allah in creating the alternation of night and day, providing a balance between rest and work. The night is a time for rest and rejuvenation, while the day offers opportunities to seek sustenance and engage in activities. This harmonious arrangement serves both physical and spiritual needs, prompting a sense of gratitude towards Allah for His thoughtful provision and the organized order in life.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And [warn of] the Day when He will call them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse envisions a scene on the Day of Judgment where Allah will question the misguided individuals about the false deities or partners they associated with Him during their lives. It emphasizes the futility and falsehood of their beliefs, highlighting the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah. This interrogation serves to expose the baselessness of their claims and to affirm the concept of Tawheed (monotheism), underlining that no entity deserves worship or partnership alongside Allah.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, 'Produce your proof,' and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability and justice of the Day of Judgment. Each nation will have a witness who will testify to their actions, and they will be asked to provide evidence for their beliefs and deeds. At that moment, it will become clear that all truth and ultimate judgment belong to Allah alone. The falsehoods and fabrications people clung to in life will abandon them, revealing their baselessness and leading to their realization of Allah's absolute authority and truth.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant.'
interpretation: This verse references Qarun, a wealthy and arrogant man from the people of Prophet Moses. Despite his vast wealth and the strength required to manage it, his behavior is condemned. His people advise him against excessive pride and joy in his wealth, reminding him that Allah disapproves of such exultation associated with arrogance and disrespect towards others. This serves as a lesson on the dangers of wealth leading to hubris and the importance of humility and gratitude to Allah.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to use the wealth and blessings that Allah has provided to strive for success in the hereafter while also making sure they do not neglect their worldly responsibilities. It encourages a balanced approach to life, promoting the pursuit of both spiritual and material well-being. Additionally, it urges individuals to act with benevolence and integrity, reflecting the goodness they have received from Allah and warning against causing harm or disorder in society, as such actions are displeasing to Allah.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, 'I was only given it because of knowledge I have.' Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed, before him, generations who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals about their sins will not be asked.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance of those who attribute their success to their own knowledge or efforts, ignoring the role of divine will. It warns against such pride by reminding that previous generations who were mightier and wealthier faced destruction due to their arrogance and disobedience. Thus, it serves as a caution against self-conceit and a reminder of the transient nature of worldly gains in comparison to the permanence of divine judgement.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, 'Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
interpretation: This verse describes Qarun, a wealthy man from the people of Moses, who flaunts his riches, invoking envy among those who yearn for worldly gains. These individuals express a desire to possess similar wealth, highlighting human tendencies to be dazzled by material possessions and to equate prosperity with true success and happiness, overlooking spiritual and moral facets of life.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: But those who were given knowledge said, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds; and none are granted it except the patient.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the value of knowledge and wisdom, which lead to recognizing that the rewards from Allah are far superior to worldly gains. It underscores the importance of faith and righteous deeds, and emphasizes that only those who are steadfast and patient will attain these divine rewards. Patience here is portrayed as a key virtue in achieving true success and eternal rewards from Allah.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and there was no company to aid him against Allah, nor was he of those who (could) defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse indicates the fate of Qarun (Korah), a wealthy but arrogant individual who refused to acknowledge his wealth and power as gifts from Allah. His punishment serves as a warning that material wealth and human support are futile against the divine will. It emphasizes the ultimate authority and power of Allah over all things and the importance of humility and gratitude towards Him. The verse also highlights the consequences of arrogance and ingratitude, demonstrating that without Allah’s protection, no external help can suffice.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, 'Oh, how Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. If not for the favor of Allah upon us, He would have caused it to swallow us too. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed!'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of realization and humility among those who once envied Qarun (Korah) for his wealth. It underscores that sustenance and success are granted by Allah’s will alone, and not by one's own efforts or merits. The verse also serves as a warning that disbelief and arrogance in one's wealth or status will not lead to true success. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing divine grace and being grateful, as well as acknowledging that true prosperity is rooted in faith and righteousness, not in material wealth.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the everlasting reward of the Hereafter is reserved for individuals who refrain from seeking superiority or causing corruption in the world. It underscores the principle that true success and ultimate happiness are meant for those who practice humility, righteousness, and piety. The verse serves as a reminder that the pursuit of moral integrity and avoidance of arrogance and misdeeds lead to a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except as they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. It underscores that those who perform good deeds will be rewarded with something even better, demonstrating Allah's generosity. Conversely, those who commit evil deeds will encounter just recompense equivalent to their actions, reflecting the principle of moral accountability and fairness in the divine judgment.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will take you back to a place of return. Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that the same God who has obligated the revelation of the Qur'an upon him will ensure his return to his rightful place, whether in a literal or metaphorical sense of fulfillment and completion of his mission. The command to proclaim that Allah alone knows who is rightly guided and who is misguided emphasizes trusting in God's ultimate judgment and knowledge, underscoring the limitations of human discernment in spiritual matters.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: You did not expect that the Book would be sent down to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord, so do not be an advocate for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad did not anticipate receiving the divine revelation of the Qur'an. The Quran's arrival is depicted as an act of mercy from Allah, underscoring the unexpected and gracious nature of divine guidance. The latter part of the verse advises the Prophet, and by extension the believers, not to support or aid those who reject the truth of the divine message, underscoring a distinction between the followers of truth and those who deny it.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And let them not avert you from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord and do not be of those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes steadfastness in faith and commitment to spreading the message of Islam despite opposition. It encourages believers to remain firm in their adherence to the teachings revealed to them and to persist in calling others to the worship of Allah alone, shunning any form of associating others with Him. The verse underscores the importance of resilience in the face of challenges and staying true to monotheism.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of worshipping Allah and the ultimate monotheistic principle in Islam. It asserts that no other entity should be invoked or worshipped alongside Allah, as He is the only true deity. The verse further underscores the transient nature of everything in existence except Allah, highlighting His eternal nature and the eventual return of all creation to Him for judgement. It serves as a reminder of the imperishable and absolute sovereignty of Allah over all things.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are disjointed letters found at the beginning of several surahs (chapters) in the Qur'an. Their specific meaning is known only to Allah. Scholars have various interpretations, often suggesting that they serve as a means to draw attention or as a marker indicating the miraculous and inimitable nature of the Qur'an.
orig: الم

translation: Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and will not be tested?
interpretation: This verse highlights that simply professing belief is not sufficient; true faith will be tested through trials and tribulations. It implies that such tests are a necessary part of the spiritual journey to differentiate between those who are steadfast in their faith and those who are not.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And certainly We tried those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine testing and the purpose behind it. Allah tests individuals, as He did with those before, to reveal the true nature of their faith. Through these trials, those who are sincere in their belief are distinguished from those who are false. It emphasizes that trials and difficulties are a means for spiritual discernment and purification, highlighting the importance of genuine faith and integrity in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think they can escape Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of those who commit evil acts. It challenges their false belief that they can evade divine justice. The verse serves as a reminder that all actions are observed by Allah, and that escaping the consequences of one's deeds is a grave misjudgment. This warning underscores the importance of moral responsibility and the reality of divine retribution.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed, the term of Allah is coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of meeting Allah, stressing that the appointed time determined by Allah for this meeting will undoubtedly come to pass. It provides reassurance and encouragement to the believers, affirming Allah’s awareness and understanding of all matters. It reminds the faithful of the importance of striving for righteousness and maintaining hope, as Allah is ever-listening to their supplications and fully aware of their intents and actions.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives only strives for the benefit of himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the efforts and struggles an individual undertakes in the path of righteousness are ultimately for their own benefit. It underscores the self-serving nature of striving in good causes, as these actions contribute to one's own spiritual growth, self-improvement, and attainment of divine rewards. The verse also highlights the absolute independence and self-sufficiency of Allah, indicating that He does not require the actions or worship of human beings, as He is beyond any need or dependency on the creation.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of divine forgiveness and reward for believers who commit themselves to faith and righteous actions. It reassures that their sins will be erased and they will be compensated in the best manner for their good deeds, encouraging a focus on virtuous living and steadfastness in faith.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents. But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the paramount importance of treating one's parents with kindness and respect. However, it also sets a boundary; if one's parents urge them towards polytheism or actions that contradict the knowledge and commandments of God, obedience in such matters is not required. Ultimately, the verse reminds believers that their return is to God, who will hold them accountable for their deeds, thus encouraging a balance between filial piety and spiritual integrity.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reinforces the Quranic theme of the connection between faith and righteous action. It promises believers who couple their faith with ethical and moral behavior a place among the righteous. This illustrates the Islamic principle that true faith manifests through good deeds, and those who live by these principles are guaranteed a place in a community of the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, 'Indeed, We were with you.' Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all creatures?
interpretation: This verse addresses the duplicity and inconsistency of some people's faith. It highlights those who claim belief in God but falter under trials and tribulations, considering human trials as severe as divine punishment. However, when success and triumph are achieved, they hastily proclaim their allegiance to the successful group. This behavior underscores their lack of sincere faith. The verse concludes by affirming that God is fully aware of what lies in the depths of people's hearts, emphasizing that true faith is known to God regardless of external declarations or actions.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse indicates that through trials and tests, Allah will distinguish between the true believers and the hypocrites. The true nature of individuals' faith will be revealed, highlighting the sincerity or insincerity of their belief. It emphasizes the importance of genuine faith and the certainty that divine knowledge encompasses all, revealing the true intentions and states of people's hearts.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitful tactics used by disbelievers to mislead believers from the righteous path. The disbelievers attempt to assure believers that they would bear any resulting sins if the believers abandoned their faith. However, the Qur'an makes it clear that no soul can bear the burden of another's sins, and thus these promises are false and deceptive. It warns believers to be wary of such deceit and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: They will certainly bear their own burdens and other burdens along with their own, and they will definitely be questioned on the Day of Judgment about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that individuals will not only bear the consequences of their own actions but also the consequences of leading others astray. Furthermore, it stresses that on the Day of Judgment, people will be questioned about the lies and falsehoods they spread, pointing to the severity of misleading others and fabricating untruths.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years; and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in calling his people to the path of righteousness for a significantly long period, 950 years. Despite his prolonged effort, the people did not heed his message and continued in their wrongdoing. Consequently, they faced divine retribution in the form of a flood. The verse highlights themes of prophetic endurance, human obstinacy in sin, and the eventual divine justice.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the story of Noah and the great flood. It highlights God's mercy and power in saving Noah and the believers with him in the ark, while also serving as a lesson and a sign for all of humanity. The preservation of Noah and his companions' lives amidst the calamity stands as a reminder of God's ability to deliver the righteous from tribulations and serves as a warning of His judgment.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the steadfastness of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in his mission to guide his people towards the worship of Allah alone and to maintain piety. It underscores the fundamental principle of monotheism and the consciousness of God as core components of righteousness and well-being. Moreover, it emphasizes the wisdom and benefit inherent in following divine guidance, implying that true knowledge and understanding lead one to recognize the importance of worshipping and fearing Allah.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You only worship idols besides Allah and create falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess any provision for you. So seek provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the act of worshipping gods other than Allah, stating that such deities are merely idols and represent falsehoods. It emphasizes that these idols have no power to provide sustenance. Therefore, people are urged to seek their provision directly from Allah, worship Him alone, and show gratitude to Him, as ultimately, everyone will return to Him for judgment.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny, then already nations before you have denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except the [duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the Prophet as merely a conveyor of divine messages. It addresses the disbelievers, reminding them that their denial is not a new phenomenon, as previous nations before them also rejected their messengers. The core message is that rejection does not detract from the truth or the mission of the Prophet, and his duty is solely to deliver the message clearly. The ultimate accountability lies with the individuals who receive the message.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Do they not see how Allah initiates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, emphasizing His ability to create life from nothing and then to bring it back after death. It serves as a reminder of the cyclical nature of creation and resurrection, and underscores the ease with which Allah can accomplish what may seem impossible or difficult to human beings. This concept serves to strengthen the belief in the afterlife and reaffirm faith in Allah's absolute power.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed, Allah, over all things, is competent.'
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the natural world and the origins of creation as evidence of Allah's supreme creative power. It suggests that by observing the beginnings of life in the natural world, one can gain insight into Allah's ability to resurrect and bring forth new life in the Hereafter. The ultimate message is to affirm God's omnipotence and His control over all things.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and He has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and discretion of Allah in dispensing both punishment and mercy. It serves as a reminder of His ultimate authority over all creation and the inevitability of returning to Him for final judgment. It encourages individuals to be mindful of their actions, seek His mercy, and acknowledge His supreme power in determining their fate.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you will not cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth or in the heaven. And you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, indicating that neither in the earthly realm nor in the heavenly realm can anyone escape or thwart His power and will. It also highlights the dependence of all beings on Allah by stating that there is no protector or helper other than Him, underscoring the futility of seeking refuge or assistance from any other source.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: But those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in the meeting with Him, it is they who have despaired of My mercy. And for them there is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the fundamental consequences of disbelief in Allah's revelations and the afterlife. It emphasizes that rejecting faith and the prospect of encountering Allah leads to a hopeless state regarding divine mercy. Such individuals have given up on receiving Allah’s compassion, indicating both a spiritual loss and a profound separation from divine grace. Consequently, their ultimate fate is severe punishment, underscoring the gravity of their disbelief and the importance of faith in achieving salvation and mercy.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Kill him or burn him.' But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse recounts the response of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) people when he called them to monotheism and challenged their idol worship. They reacted with hostility, suggesting to kill or burn him. However, Allah miraculously saved him from the fire, emphasizing the divine protection granted to His prophets and reinforcing the concept of faith in Allah’s signs and interventions for believers.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he said, 'You have taken idols instead of Allah, creating affection between yourselves in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection, you will deny one another and curse one another, and your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.'
interpretation: This verse warns against the worship of idols and other false deities besides Allah. It emphasizes that such practices may create temporary bonds between people in this worldly life, but ultimately, these relationships will turn into animosity and betrayal on the Day of Resurrection. On that day, those who followed idolatry will reject and curse each other due to their misguided actions, and their final destination will be the Fire, with no one to save them from this fate. The verse serves as a powerful reminder of the consequences of turning away from true monotheism and the severe repercussions in the afterlife.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: So Lot believed in him. He said, 'Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the conviction and steadfastness of Prophet Lot (Lut) in his faith, highlighting his decision to follow Prophet Abraham's (Ibrahim) call to monotheism despite societal pressures. It denotes Lot's determination to dedicate himself entirely to God's cause, emphasizing his awareness of God's supreme authority and wisdom, which reassures him in his decision to emigrate.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob and placed in his descendants prophethood and the scripture; and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings given to the Prophet Abraham, including his sons Isaac and Jacob, who continued his lineage of prophethood. It emphasizes that divine revelation and guidance have been preserved through his descendants. Additionally, it underscores that Abraham was rewarded both in his earthly life and will be among the righteous in the Hereafter, reflecting the idea that true faith and steadfastness are rewarded in both this world and the next.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse speaks of Prophet Lot (Lut) addressing his people and condemning their immoral behavior, which was unprecedented among any previous nations. It highlights the severity of their wrongdoing and serves as a warning that their actions are particularly egregious and against the natural moral order established by God.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you indeed approach men and cut off the road [for travelers], and commit in your meetings [every] evil? But the answer of his people was not except that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the actions of the people of Lot (Lut), who were engaging in immoral behavior by approaching men for sexual acts, obstructing paths, and indulging in shameless activities publicly. The verse highlights their defiance and arrogance, as they ridicule the warning of Prophet Lot by challenging him to bring Allah's punishment if he speaks the truth. This reflects their disbelief and stubbornness in continuing their sinful ways despite the prophet's admonition.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, support me against the corrupting people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine assistance in overcoming those who spread corruption and disorder. It signifies a deep sense of reliance on God's power to uphold justice and righteousness against the forces committed to disrupting moral and social order.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with good news, they said, 'Indeed, we will destroy the people of this town. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse narrates the event of God's messengers arriving to inform Prophet Abraham of impending divine retribution on a particular community due to their persistent wrongdoing and injustices. The 'good news' refers to an announcement made to Abraham, which provides a contrast to the grave news about the town's fate. The messengers assert that the town's destruction is justified by the moral corruption of its inhabitants, emphasizing the significance of justice and the consequences of oppressing and engaging in sinful behavior.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, within it is Lot.' They said, 'We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse recounts a conversation between prophets and divine beings, underscoring God's omniscience and justice. Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) informs the divine messengers about the presence of Prophet Lot in the doomed city. The messengers assure him of their awareness and assert the selective mercy of God, indicating that Lot and his family will be saved due to their righteousness, except his wife who will face the same fate as the disbelievers due to her alignment with the corrupt people. This emphasizes the theme of divine justice and the distinction made between the righteous and the wicked.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, 'Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse describes the visit of divine messengers to the Prophet Lot (Lut). Lot felt distress and discomfort upon their arrival, fearing for their safety and the response of the people. The messengers reassured him not to fear or grieve, informing him that he and his family would be saved from the impending punishment except for his wife, who chosen to remain among those who would suffer. The verse highlights themes of divine intervention, protection for the righteous, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: Indeed, We will bring down on the people of this town a punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the divine justice and retribution that is to befall upon a community due to their persistent sinful behavior and transgressions. It serves as a warning to those who continually refuse to obey and adhere to the righteous path, highlighting that divine intervention and punishment are consequences of sustained disobedience and immorality.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And We left therein a clear sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the remnants of past civilizations or events, left by Allah, serve as clear signs or proofs for those who use their intellect and reason. It implies that the history and traces of previous communities contain lessons and wisdom for intelligent and thoughtful individuals to understand and reflect upon, leading them to recognize the truth and guidance provided by Allah.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to [the people of] Madyan, We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the message of Prophet Shu'ayb who was sent to the people of Madyan. He called them towards monotheism, worshiping only Allah, and to have consciousness of the afterlife (Hereafter), guiding their actions by the expectation of being accountable on the Last Day. Additionally, he admonished them to avoid engaging in harmful behaviors and spreading corruption and disorder on the earth. The core theme here is a call for a moral and pious life, maintaining societal harmony and righteousness.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by a community that rejected the message of their prophet. Despite being warned, their obstinance led to a severe divine punishment, manifesting as an earthquake, resulting in their sudden and total destruction within their own homes. The imagery of them being 'fallen prone' underscores the immediacy and the absolute nature of their downfall as a result of their disbelief and denial.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And [we destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. And Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, and they were endowed with perception.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical reminder of the destruction of the people of 'Aad and Thamud, two ancient communities who were annihilated due to their persistent disobedience to God. It highlights that the remnants of their dwellings stand as a visible sign and a warning. The verse emphasizes that Satan deceived them by making their sinful actions seem attractive, leading them astray from the right path. Despite having the capacity for understanding and discernment, they chose to follow their misguided ways. This serves as a cautionary message about the consequences of succumbing to temptation and ignoring divine guidance.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman—Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they were not outrunners [of Our punishment].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the confrontation between Moses and some of the most prominent figures of defiance in history: Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. Despite the clear signs and proofs Moses presented, these figures chose arrogance and pride over acceptance of Divine guidance. Their arrogance led them to believe that they could surpass or escape the consequences of their actions, but the verse reminds us that no one can outrun or avoid the punishment of God. It serves as a warning against the dangers of pride and the ultimate futility of denying divine truth.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: So each We seized for their sin: some of them We sent a storm of stones, some were seized by the blast, some We caused the earth to swallow, and some We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of persistent wrongdoing and disbelief. It highlights Allah's justice in punishing different communities according to their sins, reflecting the diversity of the punishments that befell them—ranging from storms of stones, deafening blasts, and the earth swallowing them, to drowning. This variety of punishments serves as a stern warning and a reminder that divine retribution is tailored to the actions of individuals or groups. Importantly, the verse emphasizes that Allah is never unjust; rather, it is the people who subject themselves to such fates through their own wrongful actions. This stresses personal accountability and the inherent justice in divine intervention.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like that of the spider who builds a house. But indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of the spider's web to illustrate the fragility and insufficiency of relying on anything other than Allah for support and protection. Just as a spider's web is easily broken and provides no real security, similarly, the alliances and dependencies formed with other entities instead of Allah are weak and unreliable. The verse emphasizes the wisdom and necessity of placing one's trust in Allah alone, as all other sources of reliance are ultimately frail and impermanent.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever thing they call upon other than Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of all the entities or deities that people invoke or worship besides Him. It reinforces the futility of such practices, as these entities hold no power or wisdom. The verse further asserts Allah's attributes of being all-powerful and all-wise, highlighting His superiority and the erroneous nature of attributing divinity or power to anything other than Him.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of possessing knowledge and understanding in grasping the deeper meanings of the examples and parables presented in the Qur'an. It highlights that true comprehension goes beyond superficial reading and is accessible only to those who sincerely seek wisdom and possess a discerning mind. Thus, it encourages the pursuit of knowledge and reflection on the divine teachings to fully benefit from God's guidance.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful and truthful creation of the universe by Allah, suggesting that the intricacy and order of the heavens and the earth serve as a clear sign of His existence and omnipotence. It is a call for believers to reflect on the divine wisdom and power inherent in creation, fostering a deeper sense of faith and understanding of the divine order.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to regularly recite the Qur'anic revelations and to establish regular prayer, emphasizing that prayer acts as a deterrent against immoral and unjust behavior. The verse underscores the immense importance of remembering Allah, suggesting that such remembrance is of greater significance than all else. Allah's awareness of human actions is highlighted, reminding believers of His omniscience and encouraging them toward righteous conduct.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'
interpretation: This verse advises Muslims to engage in discussions with the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) in a manner that is kind and respectful, unless they are unjust and oppressive. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging the common ground between the faiths, particularly the belief in one God, and highlights the shared submission to God's will.
