The call for respectful dialogue aims to foster mutual understanding and peace, while also standing firm against injustice.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And so We have revealed to you the Book. Those to whom We gave the Scripture believe in it, and among these [people] are those who believe in it. And none reject Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation, highlighting that the Qur'an is part of the same tradition as previous scriptures. It acknowledges that there are people among previous recipients of the scriptures who recognize and believe in the Qur'an as a continuation of God's message. The verse also delineates between believers who accept the signs of Allah and disbelievers who reject them, indicating that rejection of divine signs is a hallmark of disbelief.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And you (O Muhammad) were not a reader of any scripture before it, nor did you write one with your right hand. Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an by highlighting that Prophet Muhammad was unlettered; he did not read or write any books prior. This fact undermines any claim from skeptics that he authored the Qur'an himself, as it would be unlikely for an illiterate individual to produce such a profound text. Therefore, this serves to solidify the argument that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: Rather, it is clear signs in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our signs except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quranic revelations are clear and evident to those who possess knowledge and recognize truth. It highlights the deep, internal understanding that believers have of these divine messages. Additionally, it condemns the actions of those who willfully reject these signs, identifying them as unjust and wrongdoers who choose to deny the clear evidence presented to them.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they say, 'Why have not signs been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who demand miraculous signs to validate the prophethood of Muhammad. It emphasizes that the power to send signs rests solely with Allah, and it is not for the Prophet to produce them at will. The primary role of the Prophet is to deliver the message and warn people clearly about the consequences of ignoring or rejecting it. The verse teaches reliance on divine wisdom and timing, and underscores the Prophet's duty as a conveyor of divine guidance rather than a performer of miracles on demand.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: Is it not enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sufficiency and profound significance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation and guidance for humanity. It highlights that the act of the Qur'an being sent and recited is an ample sign of God's mercy and serves as a constant reminder and reflection for those of faith. The verse implies that the believers should find reassurance and spiritual nourishment in the Qur'an, as it continually offers guidance and mercy for those who are open to its message and believe in it.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who have believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - it is they who are the losers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as a witness to the truth and falsity of people's beliefs and actions. It implies that human judgments or accusations are secondary to Allah's ultimate knowledge and judgment. It also underscores the dire consequences for those who reject the truth of Allah and believe in falsehood, marking them as true losers in the ultimate sense, both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment, but had it not been for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them. And it will surely come to them suddenly while they perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who mockingly demand the immediate occurrence of divine punishment. It emphasizes that such punishment is governed by a predetermined time established by Allah, and it is out of human control. The text warns that when the penalty eventually arrives, it will do so unexpectedly, catching the disbelievers off guard and unprepared. This serves as a reminder of divine justice and the importance of faith and patience, as well as the inevitability of divine will manifesting at an appointed time.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They urge you to bring about the punishment, while Hell will certainly encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the impatience of the disbelievers who mockingly demand the immediate arrival of divine punishment as a proof against the warnings given by the Prophet. It reassures that Hell is an inevitable reality that surrounds the disbelievers, emphasizing the certainty and inescapability of divine retribution for those who reject faith.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: On the Day when the punishment will envelop them from above them and from under their feet and it will be said, 'Taste [the result of] what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inescapable and all-encompassing nature of divine retribution for those who have committed wrongdoings. It illustrates that the punishment will be so overwhelming that it will cover every aspect of their existence, symbolized by it coming from above and below them. The phrase 'Taste what you used to do' underscores the principle of justice and accountability; the sufferers will directly experience the consequences of their own actions, reinforcing the Qur'anic theme that every individual is responsible for their deeds and will face appropriate recompense.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to worship Allah alone and reminds them that if they encounter difficulties in practicing their faith due to their environment, they should consider relocating to a place where they can fulfill their religious duties more freely. It underscores the vastness of Allah’s creation and assures believers that there are always opportunities to find a place suitable for worshiping Him properly. The emphasis is on the importance of worship and faithfulness to Allah, regardless of the challenges they may face.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul will taste death. Then to Us will you be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death for every living being, regardless of their status or power. It reminds believers of the transient nature of life and the certainty of returning to God for judgment. The verse serves as a call for humans to live righteously and be mindful of their actions, knowing that they will ultimately be accountable to their Creator.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: But those who believed and did righteous deeds - We will surely settle them in lofty dwellings of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers who back their faith with righteous actions will be rewarded with high and eternal places in Paradise, characterized by the blissful imagery of rivers flowing beneath. It highlights the enduring and excellent reward awaiting those who strive and act righteously in their lives.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: Those who are patient and upon their Lord do they rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God. It suggests that the individuals who exhibit patience in the face of difficulties and trials, and place their complete trust and reliance on God, are the ones who are truly guided. These qualities are critical components of faith, highlighting that perseverance and dependence on Divine wisdom and support are key virtues for a believer.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many a creature there is that does not carry its [own] provision. Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's boundless provision and care for all living beings. It underscores the idea that many creatures do not store or carry their own sustenance, yet Allah ensures their survival. This serves as a reminder to humans of Allah's constant attention to the needs of His creation, encouraging reliance on His providence and recognizing His omniscience and responsiveness to all needs.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?' They would surely say, 'Allah.' Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency in the beliefs of those who acknowledge Allah as the Creator yet deviate into polytheism or idolatry. By pointing out that even they recognize Allah's ultimate power and creativity, it questions their logic in turning away from His exclusive worship. The verse implies a rhetorical astonishment at the people's deviation despite their recognition of Allah's sovereignty, urging them to reflect and turn back to true monotheism.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the distribution of sustenance is under Allah's control and varies according to His wisdom and will. It highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge and stresses that sustenance is not a measure of one's worth, but a direct result of divine will and wisdom. This encourages believers to trust in Allah's plan and rely on His wisdom in all matters of provision.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who sends down the water from the sky and thereby revives the earth after its lifelessness?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Praise be to Allah!' But most of them do not understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the acknowledgement even by disbelievers that Allah is the one who sends down rain and revitalizes the earth. Despite recognizing this divine act, many do not truly comprehend or reflect on the implications of this acknowledgment. They fail to connect the natural wonders to Allah's greater wisdom and power. It invites believers to praise Allah and contemplate His creation deeply, understanding and recognizing His signs and wisdom.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And what is the life of this world except amusement and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient and superficial nature of worldly life, emphasizing it as mere play and amusement. In contrast, it highlights the permanence and true essence of the Hereafter, which is of far greater importance and reality. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their ultimate goal, the Hereafter, fulfilling their duties to Allah and being mindful of their actions on earth. It calls for a deeper understanding and reflection on the part of believers to recognize the fleeting nature of worldly life and to prepare for the eternal life to come.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: So when they embark on a ship, they invoke Allah, being sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse illustrates human nature's inconsistency and ingratitude. In times of extreme distress and helplessness, people often sincerely turn to Allah, acknowledging His power and supplicating exclusively to Him for rescue. However, once they are saved and return to safety, they quickly forget their sincere devotion and revert to associating others with Allah, engaging in acts of shirk (idolatry or polytheism). This behavior highlights a lack of steadfast faith and a forgetfulness of the divine grace they experienced.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: Let them deny what We have given them and let them enjoy themselves, for they will soon know.
interpretation: This verse suggests an admonishment to those who reject the blessings and guidance provided by God. It indicates that such individuals, though allowed to indulge in their current worldly pleasures, will eventually face the consequences of their disbelief. It serves as a warning that ultimate enlightenment and realization of the truth will come to them, but possibly when it is too late to amend their ways.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made [Mecca] a safe sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them? Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the favor of Allah do they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique protection and sanctuary status granted to Mecca (the Sacred Mosque) by Allah, amidst dangers in the surrounding areas. It calls out the ingratitude and misguided beliefs of individuals who reject Allah's blessings and follow falsehood instead. Despite the clear sign of Mecca's safety and blessing, many still choose to deny the truth and grace provided by Allah.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the gravest injustice is lying about Allah or rejecting the truth when it is presented. It underscores the severity of such actions by linking them to the ultimate consequence of Hell, reserved as a fitting punishment for those who persist in disbelief and falsehood. It serves as a stern warning to remain truthful and accept divine guidance.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: As for those who strive hard in Us (Our Cause), We will surely guide them to Our paths (i.e. Allah's religion - Islamic Monotheism). And verily, Allah is with the good-doers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the promise of divine guidance for those who exert effort and strive sincerely in the cause of Allah. The exertion mentioned can be taken to mean both physical and spiritual efforts to adhere to and promote the teachings of Islam. The verse assures believers that such sincere efforts will not go in vain; rather, they will be met with Allah's guidance towards the righteous path. Furthermore, it emphasizes that Allah's presence and support are with those who perform good deeds and act with excellence in their actions and intentions.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are disjointed letters (Alif, Lam, Meem) known as 'Muqatta'at'. Their exact meaning is hidden and known only to Allah. They are seen as a sign of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, encouraging the reader to reflect on the divine wisdom and the inimitable nature of the Book.
orig: الم

translation: The Romans have been defeated
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where the Byzantine Empire (Romans) faced a significant defeat. It signifies the transient nature of worldly power and fortunes, and serves as a reminder that situations can and do change with God's will.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: in the lowest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome.
interpretation: This verse references a historical event where the Byzantine Empire, initially defeated, will eventually claim victory. It highlights the temporal nature of worldly affairs and conveys the message that situations of defeat can be reversed by the will of Allah. It serves to assure believers of the ebb and flow of fortunes and encourages perseverance and faith in divine wisdom and timing.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the temporal nature of worldly events, emphasizing that all matters, whether before or after a given event, are under the control of Allah. It reassures the believers that despite any hardships or delays, eventual triumph and happiness are assured for them by divine decree. The verse serves to inspire patience and trust in Allah's wisdom and timing.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: With the help of Allah, He helps whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's support is paramount and is granted to those He chooses. It underscores Allah's dual attributes of great power and dominance (Al-Aziz) and His infinite mercy (Ar-Raheem). This duality assures believers that, despite His immense strength, His actions are also guided by mercy. Moreover, it encourages reliance on divine assistance while highlighting the notion that ultimate decision and victory come solely from Allah's will.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The promise of Allah - Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and reliability of God’s promises. It reassures believers that whatever Allah has promised, whether rewards for good deeds or warnings of consequences for wrong deeds, will undoubtedly come to pass. However, it highlights the lack of knowledge or understanding among most people, implying that many do not recognize or appreciate the truth and inevitability of Allah's promises.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know only the outer aspect of the life of this world, but of the Hereafter they are unaware.
interpretation: This verse points to the superficial understanding people often have of worldly life, focusing solely on its materialistic and apparent aspects. It highlights a stark contrast with their negligence and lack of awareness towards the afterlife, emphasizing that true wisdom encompasses knowledge and preparation for the Hereafter, not just the transient world.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: And do they not reflect upon themselves? Allah created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in truth and for an appointed term. Yet many of the people are, in the matter of the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse urges people to engage in self-reflection and recognize the purposeful creation of the universe by Allah. It highlights the truth and the finite nature of everything created. Despite the evident signs, many people remain in disbelief regarding the inevitable meeting with their Creator, indicating a warning against neglecting this essential aspect of faith.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and had constructed more upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins. And they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to those who ignore the signs of God and persist in their ways of disbelief and injustice. It calls on people to reflect on the fate of past civilizations that were mightier and more prosperous but faced destruction due to their transgressions and rejection of prophetic guidance. The verse underscores that God's judgment is just, and any suffering incurred is a result of people's own wrongful actions. By contemplating these historical lessons, individuals are urged to correct their behavior and heed divine guidance.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then the outcome for those who committed evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate fate of those who persist in committing evil and disbelieve in the signs of Allah. Their end is the worst outcome as a result of their actions and attitudes towards the divine revelations. Their disbelief and mockery of Allah's signs lead to severe consequences, emphasizing the seriousness of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of sincere belief and respect for Allah's messages.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cycle of life and creation as initiated by Allah. It emphasizes His power to create and recreate, underscoring the inevitability of returning to Him for final judgment. The process of creation and re-creation serves as a reminder of both Allah’s omnipotence and the transient nature of worldly life, encouraging believers to remain conscious of their ultimate return to the Divine and to live their lives in accordance with His guidance.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: On the Day when the Hour will be established, the criminals will be struck with despair.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, highlighting a moment of ultimate accountability and consequence. It emphasizes that when the Final Hour arrives, those who are guilty of wrongdoing will be engulfed in a state of utter despair. This despair stems from their realization of the truth and the inevitable consequences of their actions. It serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and being mindful of the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And they will have no intercessors from among their associates, and they will disbelieve in their associates.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on false deities or partners besides Allah for intercession on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that those who associated others with Allah will find no one to intercede on their behalf and will ultimately deny and reject the very beings they associated with Allah, recognizing their error and the truth of Tawhid (the oneness of God).
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will become separated.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Day of Judgment, marking the moment when all of humanity will be separated according to their deeds. It highlights the definitive separation between the righteous and the wicked, emphasizing the finality of divine justice and the clear distinction made between those who have done good and those who have done evil. On this day, there will be a clear, irrevocable division reflecting the moral and spiritual choices made during their lifetimes.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, delighted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith coupled with righteous actions leads to immense joy and reward in the hereafter. The 'garden' symbolizes paradise, a place of eternal bliss, and 'delighted' indicates the profound happiness and satisfaction that believers will experience as a result of their faith and good deeds.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the fate of those who reject faith and the signs of Allah, as well as the reality of an afterlife. It serves as a stern warning that such individuals will face inevitable punishment. The phrasing emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of this consequence, highlighting the gravity of disbelief and rejection of divine truth.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
interpretation: This verse is a call to constantly remember and glorify Allah, especially during the transitional times of day—morning and evening. These times mark the cycle of daily life and are key moments for reflection and gratitude. It emphasizes the importance of regular, mindful worship and recognition of Allah's greatness and bounties at the beginning and end of our daily activities.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: To Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and (exalted is He) at nightfall and when you are at midday.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the constant and universal nature of praise and gratitude due to Allah. It highlights that Allah is worthy of praise at all times and places, encompassing all the realms of existence—from the heavens to the earth. The mention of specific times, 'at nightfall' and 'when you are at midday,' underscores the importance of remembering and acknowledging Allah throughout the different phases of the daily cycle, signifying continuous devotion and gratitude.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living, and brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine power and capability of Allah to create and transform life in various forms. It highlights the cycle of life and death, showcasing Allah's ability to resurrect and renew life, both in a physical and spiritual sense. The mention of bringing forth life from seemingly dead matter and vice versa serves as a reminder of the resurrection and the ultimate return to Allah after death.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [through the earth].
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of human creation as one of the signs of God's power and wisdom. The transformation from lifeless dust to living, thinking beings underscores the divine ability to bring forth life from inorganic matter. It also serves to remind humans of their humble origins and the greatness of the Creator, encouraging a reflection on the marvels of existence and the omnipotence of God, who has the capacity to create, sustain, and diversify life on Earth.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom and purpose behind the creation of human partnerships, specifically the relationship between spouses. It points out that the spousal bond is meant to provide tranquility, affection, and mercy, reflecting the inherent need for companionship and emotional connection in human nature. The verse also serves as a reminder of the signs of God's wisdom and mercy, urging individuals to reflect on these elements of creation to gain deeper spiritual understanding and appreciation of His provisions.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed, in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse points to the existence and greatness of Allah through the observable phenomena in the universe. The creation of the vast heavens and earth, and the rich variety in human languages and physical appearances, are seen as evidence of a divine creator. These signs are meant to be recognized by those who seek knowledge and understanding, indicating that diversity and complexity in the natural world are intentional acts of God meant to inspire reflection and acknowledgment of His power and wisdom.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights two significant aspects of human life as signs of God's existence and mercy: the natural cycle of sleep and wakefulness, and the human pursuit of livelihood. Sleep, whether during the night or day, is a vital, rejuvenating gift that showcases divine wisdom in the creation of life. Additionally, the pursuit of sustenance is a means through which people benefit from God's bounty. Such phenomena are reminders to those who are attentive and reflect deeply on the workings of the world, recognizing the underlying signs of God's care and provision.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And of His signs is that He shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and aspiration, and He sends down rain from the sky by which He brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse reflects on some of the natural phenomena as signs of God's power and wisdom. The lightning, evoking both fear and hope, indicates dynamic forces beyond human control, which can inspire awe and reliance on God. The rain reviving the earth symbolizes God's mercy and His ability to restore life, indicating a broader spiritual and physical rejuvenation. These signs are meant to engage the thoughtful and encourage deeper reflection on the underlying reality and purpose of existence, emphasizing that comprehension and appreciation of these signs require rational consideration and intellectual engagement.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And of His signs is that the heaven and earth stand by His command; then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, immediately you will come forth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority of Allah over the universe. The stability of the heavens and the earth exists solely by His will. Furthermore, it signifies that the resurrection will occur instantly at His command, emphasizing both His omnipotence and the certainty of the afterlife.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over all beings in the heavens and the earth. It highlights that every creature, whether aware or not, is ultimately under Allah's dominion and subject to His will. The term 'devoutly obedient' indicates a state of submission to the divine order, underscoring the inherent recognition of Allah's authority by all of creation.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And He it is who initiates the creation then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme power and ability to initiate creation and then to resurrect it, highlighting that this process is effortless for Him. It also underscores His unparalleled attributes both in the heavens and the earth, reinforcing His omnipotence and wisdom. The verse invites reflection on the greatness and uniqueness of Allah's dominion and attributes.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He sets forth for you a parable from your own selves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal in it, fearing them as you fear each other? Thus do We detail the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse presents an analogy to make people reflect on the concept of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It suggests that just as individuals do not share their own possessions equally with their slaves or subordinates, it's irrational to consider associating others with Allah in His dominion and provision. By emphasizing this point, the verse aims to guide the people to the understanding of monotheism and the oneness of Allah, encouraging them to apply their intellect to recognize the signs of His exclusive divinity.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: But those who do wrong follow their desires without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has led astray? And for them there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided actions of those who follow their vain desires without proper knowledge or understanding. It underscores the divine principle that guidance is ultimately from Allah, and when He allows someone to go astray, no one can guide them back to the right path. It also emphasizes the helplessness of such individuals, as they have no supporters or protectors to aid them in their misguided state.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse guides believers to remain steadfast and sincere in their faith, adhering to the natural disposition (fitrah) instilled by Allah in humanity. It underscores the belief that the core principles of Islam are in harmony with the innate nature created by Allah, and these principles are unalterable. The verse also laments that many people remain unaware or ignorant of this inherent and true path, highlighting the need for awareness and understanding of divine guidance.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Turning in repentance to Him, and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of continually turning to Allah in repentance and maintaining a state of piety and consciousness of Him. It instructs believers to establish regular prayers as a means of maintaining a connection with Allah and to avoid falling into the sin of shirk, which is associating partners with Allah. The directive underscores the centrality of monotheism and consistent worship in the life of a believer.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who create divisions within their religion, forming distinct factions, each proud and satisfied with their own beliefs and interpretations. It critiques the fragmentation and prideful adherence to differing doctrines rather than unity in the faith.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when adversity touches the people, they call upon their Lord, turning in repentance to Him. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, a group of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights a common human behavior: people often turn to God sincerely in times of hardship, recognizing His sovereignty and seeking His help. However, once God alleviates their suffering and grants them relief, many revert to previous patterns of associating partners with Him or neglecting His commandments. This reflects a tendency toward ingratitude and inconsistency in faith, which the Qur'an criticizes, urging believers to maintain fidelity to God in both times of distress and ease.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: So they may deny what We have given them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse highlights a warning towards those who reject or deny the blessings and guidance given by Allah. It suggests that those who choose to persist in their disbelief or ingratitude can continue to enjoy the temporary pleasures of this world. However, the verse serves as a stern reminder that the consequences of their actions will soon be made clear to them, likely referring to the accountability and judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority which speaks of what they were associating with Him?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers' justification for associating others with Allah. It questions whether they have received any divine authority or revelation that endorses their polytheistic practices. The rhetorical nature of the question emphasizes that there is no legitimate scriptural basis for their actions, thereby highlighting the baselessness of shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse underscores the importance of following true divine guidance rather than unfounded claims.
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice therein, but if evil afflicts them because of what their hands have sent forth, immediately they despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature in response to blessings and hardships. When people experience mercy and blessings, they are quick to feel joy and contentment. However, when they face difficulties, especially those resulting from their own actions, they quickly fall into despair. The verse urges reflection on human inconsistency and the need for steadfastness in faith and reliance on Allah, regardless of circumstances.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: Do they not see that Allah enlarges the provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine providence, emphasizing that Allah controls the distribution of sustenance. The expansion and restriction of provision are part of His wisdom and plan. It serves as a reminder to the believers of Allah's ultimate authority and the signs of His presence in providing and testing His creation. The intended audience is encouraged to recognize and reflect upon these signs, reinforcing their faith and trust in Allah’s decisions.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: So give the relative his right, as well as the needy and the traveler. That is best for those who seek the Countenance of Allah, and it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's obligations towards relatives, the needy, and travelers. It underscores the virtue of generosity and charity as acts that are particularly valued by those who seek the pleasure of Allah. By highlighting these actions, the verse implies that caring for others and addressing their needs is a significant aspect of faith and a pathway to true success and prosperity in the eyes of God.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Whatever you give for interest to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah. But whatever you give in charity, seeking the Countenance of Allah— it is these who will get a manifold increase.
interpretation: This verse differentiates between two forms of monetary transactions: usury (interest) and charity. Usury is a form of profit that people may strive to increase their wealth, but it is not recognized or blessed by Allah. On the other hand, giving charity with the pure intention of seeking the pleasure of Allah is significantly rewarded and considered as truly proliferating and beneficial in the sight of Allah. The verse emphasizes the moral and spiritual value of altruism and sincere intention over the mere accumulation of wealth through practices like usury.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you to life again. Is there any of your 'partners' who can do any of these things? Exalted is He and High above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and absolute sovereignty of Allah over all aspects of life, from creation to sustenance, death, and resurrection. It calls into question the validity of associating partners with Allah, highlighting the incapacity of these so-called partners to perform any divine acts. The verse glorifies Allah's transcendence and rejects polytheism by affirming His exclusive rights as the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Resurrector.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Corruption has spread on land and sea because of what men's hands have wrought, that He may let them taste some of what they have done, so that they may return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of human actions on their surroundings, emphasizing that corruption and disorder in the world are a direct result of people's deeds. The trials and difficulties that arise are intended as a form of wake-up call, encouraging people to reflect, repent, and return to a path of righteousness and ethical behavior.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were polytheists.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning. By urging people to travel and observe the remnants of previous civilizations, it encourages reflection on the consequences of disbelief and polytheism. The emphasis on the fate of those who engaged in such behaviors highlights the importance of monotheism and adherence to divine guidance to avoid a similar end.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: So direct your face toward the correct religion before a Day comes from Allah of which there is no repelling. That Day, they will be divided.
interpretation: This verse urges individuals to commit themselves earnestly to the true and upright path of faith before the arrival of the inevitable Day of Judgment, which is ordained by Allah and cannot be averted. On that day, humanity will be divided based on their deeds and faithfulness.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him; and whoever does righteousness, they are preparing [it] for themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. Disbelief harms the individual who disbelieves, leading to spiritual detriment and ultimate accountability. Conversely, those who perform righteous deeds benefit themselves, as these acts contribute to their spiritual well-being and eternal reward. It underscores the personal nature of faith and righteousness, highlighting that each person's actions have direct repercussions on their own state in this life and the hereafter.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and mercy in Islamic theology. It highlights that Allah rewards those who have faith and engage in righteous actions, reflecting His grace and generosity. Conversely, it indicates a disapproval of those who reject faith, emphasizing that disbelief is met with divine disfavor. The verse serves to motivate believers to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds, knowing that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded by Allah.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And of His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings and to let you taste His mercy and so the ships may sail at His command and so you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights several manifestations of Allah's mercy and power. The sending of the winds signifies Allah's control over nature, providing favorable conditions that bring good news, such as the anticipation of rain. This action allows humanity to experience His mercy firsthand. Additionally, it enables the functioning of maritime travel, which is essential for trade and the seeking of sustenance, showing how Allah's commands facilitate human endeavors. The verse concludes by urging gratitude, reminding humans that these blessings and favors are opportunities to express thankfulness for Allah's bounty and care.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: Indeed, We sent messengers before you to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consistent pattern in divine history where God has sent messengers to guide their communities with clear evidence. It emphasizes God's justice by illustrating that those who persist in wrongdoing face retribution. Additionally, it reassures that aiding the believers is a divine obligation, affirming God's unwavering support for those who possess faith and righteousness.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: It is Allah who sends the winds, so they stir up the clouds; then He spreads them in the sky however He wills, and He makes them fragments, so you see the rain emerge from within them. And when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and authority of Allah in controlling natural phenomena such as the wind and rain. It underscores His sovereignty and the intricate balance He maintains in the universe. The act of sending winds to stir the clouds, spreading them, and causing rain to fall serves as a reminder of His mercy and provisions for His creation. The subsequent joy of those who receive the rain reflects human dependence on divine sustenance and the appreciation of Allah's blessings.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And though before it was sent down upon them, before that, they were in despair.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the state of despair and helplessness that people experienced before the revelation came to them. It emphasizes the transformative power of divine guidance and revelation which brings hope and light to those who were previously lost and despondent. The verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God's intervention in human affairs, rescuing people from their moments of darkness and leading them towards faith and righteousness.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: So observe the effects of the mercy of Allah - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that [same one] will give life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse invites believers to reflect upon the observable signs of Allah's mercy in nature, specifically how He revitalizes the barren earth with life, turning it fertile and productive. By drawing this parallel, it strengthens the faith in Allah's power to resurrect the dead, affirming His omnipotence and control over all things. The verse seeks to instill a deeper appreciation of divine capability and the continuous cycle of life and death as manifestations of God's will.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We sent a [harmful] wind and they saw [their crops] turning yellow, they would remain thereafter disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human faith and gratitude. It suggests that despite receiving blessings from Allah, people quickly become ungrateful or disbelieving when faced with adversity. The imagery of crops turning yellow from a harmful wind represents how people's faith can wither under trials, pointing to the importance of steadfastness and trust in Allah's wisdom and mercy, even during difficult times.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs, retreating.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that some people are so obstinate in their denial and rejection of the truth that they are likened to the dead or the deaf. Just as one cannot communicate with the dead or the deaf when they deliberately turn away, one cannot guide those who are willfully ignorant and refuse to listen to the divine message, regardless of how compelling or clear the message is. It underscores human limitations in influencing others who have decided to reject guidance.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: But you cannot guide the blind out of their straying; you can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, so they submit.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human efforts in guiding others, emphasizing that true guidance comes only from Allah. It acknowledges the Prophet's role in conveying the message, but also the inherent responsibility of individuals to open their hearts to faith. The 'blind' here refers metaphorically to those who are spiritually blind, who will not benefit from the guidance regardless of its clarity. Only those who have faith in Allah's signs and willingly submit to His will can truly hear and accept the guidance offered.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then after weakness gave strength, then after strength, gave weakness and grey hair. He creates whatever He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stages of human life as a reminder of Allah's power and wisdom. It underscores the cycle of human development, from initial weakness at birth, to a period of strength during adulthood, followed by a return to weakness in old age. It serves as a reflection on the transient nature of human life and Allah's supreme authority over all that exists.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: On the Day when the Hour is established, the criminals will swear they did not stay but an hour. Thus they were deluded.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment and highlights the regret and confusion of the wrongdoers. It emphasizes their illusion and self-deception about the shortness of their time on Earth compared to eternity, underscoring their ultimate realization of their misguided lives.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, 'You certainly remained according to the decree of Allah until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the knowledgeable believers and those who were heedless. On the Day of Resurrection, the knowledgeable and faithful will affirm that the period of waiting as decreed by Allah has come to an end, bringing the reality of the Promised Day into clear perspective. It underscores the importance of Divine knowledge and faith in understanding and preparing for the Hereafter, contrasting it with the ignorance and disbelief of those who failed to realize and prepare for this inevitable day.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: So on that Day, the excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, nor will they be allowed to appease.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of divine justice on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that those who have committed wrongdoings will find no benefit in their excuses, and they will not be given a chance to plead or seek forgiveness. The opportunity for repentance and correction is available in this world; however, once the final judgment arrives, such opportunities cease, highlighting the importance of living a righteous life and seeking forgiveness in a timely manner.
orig: فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur’an every [kind of] example. But if you should bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, 'You are but falsifiers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, indicating that it contains examples and lessons for all aspects of human life. However, it also highlights the persistent disbelief among some people. Despite the clear signs and examples provided, those who reject faith are quick to dismiss and accuse the believers and the message of falsehood. This reflects a deeper unwillingness to accept the truth, regardless of the evidence presented.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and justice, imposes a seal on the hearts of individuals who persist in ignorance and rejection of truth. This sealing is a consequence of their own choices, emphasizing a divine response to their intentional disregard for knowledge and guidance. It highlights the importance of seeking and accepting divine knowledge and the consequences of willful ignorance.
orig: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون

translation: So be patient, for the promise of Allah is true. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in faith. Believers are encouraged to trust in the certainty of Allah's promise, despite any external pressures or doubts from those who lack conviction. It serves as a reminder that true faith requires resilience and a strong belief in the ultimate fulfillment of divine promises.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are disjointed Arabic letters, known as 'Muqattaʿat' or 'disjointed letters', which appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is not definitively known and is considered a divine mystery, inviting reflection and scholarly interpretation. Many scholars believe these letters have significant spiritual meaning and serve to capture the listener's attention, indicating the inimitability of the Qur'an.
orig: الم

translation: These are the verses of the wise Book
interpretation: The term 'wise' emphasizes the Qur'an’s profound knowledge, guidance, and its ability to provide insight and resolution to life’s complexities. It suggests that the teachings within it are not just rules, but are infused with deep wisdom intended to guide humanity towards righteousness, understanding, and ethical living.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: a guidance and mercy for the doers of good
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the teachings of the Qur'an serve as a source of direction and compassion specifically for those who strive to do good deeds. It highlights the importance of virtuous actions and suggests that divine guidance and mercy are granted to those who actively pursue righteousness.
orig: هدى ورحمة للمحسنين

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they, of the Hereafter, are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes three core characteristics of true believers: they are diligent in their prayer (salah), they fulfill their obligation of giving zakah (alms or charity), and they possess firm belief in the Hereafter. These attributes underscore a balanced devotion that is both spiritual and social, reaffirming that genuine faith encompasses both regular worship and active concern for the welfare of others, combined with a resolute conviction in life after death.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: They are on guidance from their Lord, and they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who follow divine guidance are truly led by Allah, and as a result, they achieve ultimate success. It underscores the direct correlation between adhering to the principles laid out by Allah and attaining success in both this life and the hereafter. The term 'success' here is comprehensive, encompassing not just material or worldly success, but more importantly, spiritual and eternal success.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead others from the way of Allah without knowledge and who takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who engage in frivolous or misleading discussions and entertainment that distract themselves and others from the teachings and path of Allah. Such actions are taken without true understanding or knowledge, and they mock the guidance provided by Allah. The verse warns that this behavior will lead to a severe, humiliating punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث ليضل عن سبيل الله بغير علم ويتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if there were a deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of some people towards the Divine revelations. It highlights their arrogance and deliberate neglect despite being presented with clear signs. Their pretense of deafness symbolizes a willful ignorance and refusal to understand or accept the truth. Such behavior leads to a severe warning of a painful punishment, stressing the spiritual consequences of ignoring divine guidance.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليه آياتنا ولى مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that faith combined with righteous actions will lead them to eternal happiness and reward in paradise. It emphasizes the importance of both belief and good deeds as the path to divine favor and ultimate contentment.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات النعيم

translation: They will abide therein forever. This is the true promise of Allah, and He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the rewards or consequences in the hereafter, as decreed by Allah. It affirms that Allah's promises are absolute and unfailing, highlighting His supreme power and perfect wisdom in administering justice and mercy. This serves to remind believers of the certainty and importance of their actions in this life, as they relate to their ultimate fate in the hereafter.
orig: خالدين فيها وعد الله حقا وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He created the heavens without any pillars that you see and cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with you; and He spread in it all kinds of creatures. And We sent down water from the sky, and We made to grow therein every noble pair.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's creation and His meticulous design of the universe. The heavens are depicted as being established without visible supports, emphasizing the omnipotence and unparalleled capability of God. The mountains are presented as stabilizing forces on Earth to ensure its balance. The mention of various creatures indicates the diversity and richness of life that God has spread across the planet. The reference to rain from the sky, which fosters growth, symbolizes the sustenance and continuous blessings provided by God, nourishing every aspect of creation. Overall, this verse underscores the divine artistry and wisdom in maintaining the harmony and stability of the natural world.
orig: خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وبث فيها من كل دابة وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: This is the creation of Allah. So show Me what those other than Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unmatched power of Allah in creation and challenges people to compare what others besides Allah have created. It serves as a reminder that those who ascribe partners to Allah or deny His power are clearly misguided. They fail to recognize the evident signs of God's unique power and authority in creation and continue to persist in their wrongful and erroneous beliefs.
orig: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه بل الظالمون في ضلال مبين

translation: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom [and said], 'Be grateful to Allah.' And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude, highlighting Luqman as an exemplar of wisdom. Gratitude is presented as a personal benefit; showing thankfulness to Allah enhances one's own well-being. Conversely, ingratitude does not harm Allah, as He is self-sufficient and inherently worthy of all praise. Thus, the verse underscores that gratitude is more about self-improvement and recognizing divine blessings rather than affecting the status of the Divine.
orig: ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله ومن يشكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن الله غني حميد

translation: And when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, 'O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association with Him is great injustice.'
interpretation: This verse captures the wisdom imparted by Luqman to his son, emphasizing the gravity of associating partners with Allah. It highlights that shirk, or polytheism, is a profound injustice and the greatest wrong one can commit because it violates the fundamental tenet of monotheism and the unique sovereignty of Allah. The verse underscores the importance of pure monotheistic belief as the foundation of faith and morality.
orig: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing gratitude and respect towards one's parents, particularly the mother who endures great hardship during pregnancy and nursing. It reminds believers of their duty to acknowledge and appreciate the sacrifices parents make. Moreover, the ultimate gratitude should be directed towards God, as He is the final destination and the source of all blessings and guidance.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن وفصاله في عامين أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير

translation: But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where one's parents might urge them to commit shirk (associating others with Allah), which is a grave sin in Islam. It instructs believers not to obey their parents in this, but still to treat them with kindness and respect in worldly matters. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the path of those who repent and turn to Allah, as ultimate accountability lies with Allah, who will judge all actions and intentions upon return to Him. This underscores the balance between maintaining familial respect and adhering firmly to one's faith.
orig: وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي ثم إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O my son, if it be but the weight of a mustard seed, and even if it were hidden in a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. It teaches that even the smallest act, no matter how hidden or inconsequential it may seem, is known to Allah and will be brought forth and accounted for. This conveys the importance of mindfulness in one's actions and the recognition that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge and judgment, reinforcing the theme of divine justice and the intimate awareness Allah has of His creation.
orig: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, this is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of a few key principles in leading a righteous life. It advises steadfastness in performing prayers, advocating for good, and standing against evil. The verse also highlights the necessity of patience when facing challenges and adversities, indicating that these qualities are essential traits for anyone striving for moral and spiritual perseverance.
orig: يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.
interpretation: This verse advises against arrogance, vanity, and pride in one's demeanor and behavior. It encourages humility and modesty in interactions with others, reminding believers that Allah disapproves of those who are boastful and full of self-pride. By emphasizing these qualities, the verse promotes a sense of social harmony and personal self-awareness.
orig: ولا تصعر خدك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: This verse advises on the virtues of modesty and humility. It emphasizes the importance of not being arrogant or loud in one's demeanor. By urging to lower one's voice and be moderate in walking, it highlights the respect one ought to have for others by avoiding haughtiness and unnecessary disruption. The comparison to the braying of donkeys serves as a metaphor to stress that excessive loudness or boisterous behavior is unbecoming and offensive.
orig: واقصد في مشيك واغضض من صوتك إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected for you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, both apparent and hidden? But among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense bounty and blessings that Allah has granted humanity, both visible and unseen, by subjecting the entire creation for our benefit. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and mercy. The verse also highlights a contrasting group of individuals who, despite these clear signs and blessings, engage in debates about Allah without proper knowledge, guidance, or reliance on divine scriptures. This reflects on the human tendency to question and dispute divine matters without basis, urging believers to recognize and appreciate Allah's omnipresent signs and avoid baseless arguments.
orig: ألم تروا أن الله سخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing.' Even though Satan is inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse addresses the stubborn attitude of those who blindly follow ancestral traditions instead of accepting divine guidance. It highlights the danger of adhering to such traditions without question, especially when they lead to misguided paths. The reference to Satan's invitation emphasizes how these traditional practices can sometimes align with erroneous beliefs, leading individuals away from the truth and towards severe consequences.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان الشيطان يدعوهم إلى عذاب السعير

translation: Whoever submits himself to Allah and is a doer of good, he has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the outcome of all matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submission to Allah and performing righteous deeds. It assures that those who do so are holding onto a reliable and strong support that will guide them through the challenges of life. It also reaffirms that ultimately, the resolution and judgment of all matters rest with Allah. This indicates a sense of trust and reliance on divine wisdom and justice in the outcome of all affairs.
orig: ومن يسلم وجهه إلى الله وهو محسن فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And whoever disbelieves—let not their disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse provides comfort to the believers by telling them not to be distressed by those who reject faith. It reassures that everyone's ultimate return is to Allah, who has full knowledge of all actions and the innermost thoughts. The message underscores Allah's encompassing awareness and justice, suggesting that each individual's deeds will be accounted for, and inner intentions will be revealed and judged by Allah, the All-Knowing.
orig: ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره إلينا مرجعهم فننبئهم بما عملوا إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: We let them enjoy themselves for a little while, then We shall drive them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that although some individuals may experience temporary enjoyment and worldly pleasures, it serves as a test. Eventually, if they persist in their wrongdoing and fail to repent, they will face severe consequences and divine retribution for their actions. It underscores the temporal nature of worldly pleasures compared to the enduring nature of the hereafter and God's ultimate justice.
orig: نمتعهم قليلا ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

translation: And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Praise be to Allah'; but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the innate recognition of God's sovereignty within human nature, even among those who may not fully practice faith. It highlights that acknowledgment of a Creator is almost universal, yet it also criticizes that many people lack true understanding or awareness of the deeper implications of this belief. The directive to 'say, Praise be to Allah,' serves as a reminder to give due gratitude and recognition to God, alongside an implicit call for deeper reflection and understanding.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and ownership over all of creation, both in the heavens and the earth. It highlights Allah's self-sufficiency, indicating that He is free from any need or dependency on His creation. Furthermore, it denotes that despite His independence from creation, Allah is deserving of all praise and gratitude from His creation due to His perfect attributes and bounties.
orig: لله ما في السماوات والأرض إن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If all the trees on earth were pens and the ocean, with seven more oceans besides it to back it up, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless nature of Allah's wisdom and knowledge. It uses powerful imagery to convey that even if the entire world's trees were turned into pens and the oceans were ink, it would still be insufficient to write down all of Allah's words. This underscores the infinite and incomprehensible nature of divine wisdom and the inexhaustible nature of His words. It also attributes to Allah the qualities of being Almighty and Wise, highlighting His supreme power and ultimate wisdom.
orig: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute ease with which Allah can create and resurrect all of humanity. It underscores the unity and equality of all human beings by comparing their collective creation and resurrection to that of a single soul. Additionally, it serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware and comprehending of all things, as He is both all-hearing and all-seeing.
orig: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah makes the night enter into the day and makes the day enter into the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a specified term, and that Allah is Acquainted with what you do?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on Allah's supreme power and control over natural phenomena such as the alternation of night and day and the orbits of the sun and moon. It highlights that these celestial occurrences follow a precise, divine order set by Allah, emphasizing His omnipotence and meticulous knowledge of all actions. It serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of the cosmos and human deeds, and calls for mindfulness of Allah's omnipresence in everything.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري إلى أجل مسمى وأن الله بما تعملون خبير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood; and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah. It affirms that Allah alone embodies the ultimate truth and reality, while any other deities or entities that people might invoke or worship are essentially baseless and false. Furthermore, it highlights Allah's exalted and majestic nature, reaffirming His position as the highest and greatest, unparalleled in His attributes and worthy of exclusive worship and reverence.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Do you not see that ships sail through the sea by the grace of Allah to show you some of His signs? Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse draws attention to the marvels of navigation and sea travel, emphasizing that such phenomena occur by Allah's grace. It serves to remind believers of the divine signs present in such everyday events, encouraging them to reflect on these wonders with patience and gratitude. It signifies that true understanding and appreciation of these signs come from those who exhibit perseverance and thankfulness towards Allah's bounties.
orig: ألم تر أن الفلك تجري في البحر بنعمت الله ليريكم من آياته إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when waves come over them like canopies, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, there are some of them who are moderate [in faith]. And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous and ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse refers to how people, in times of dire need and danger, such as being overwhelmed by immense waves at sea, turn to Allah with sincere devotion and supplication.
