However, once they are saved and brought back to safety, their sincerity often diminishes, and their true nature reveals itself — some become moderate in their faith while others reject the signs and the blessings they experienced, showing ingratitude and treachery. It highlights the inconsistency often found in human behavior, especially in relation to faith and gratitude towards Allah.
orig: وإذا غشيهم موج كالظلل دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر فمنهم مقتصد وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا كل ختار كفور

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. So let not the worldly life delude you, nor let the Deceiver delude you about Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a solemn reminder to all people to be conscious of their duties towards their Creator and to be wary of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that on that decisive day, familial ties will not provide any benefit; each individual will be responsible for their own actions. The verse underscores the certainty of Allah's promise and advises against being misled by the temporary allurements of worldly life or by deceivers who might lead one away from the truth about Allah.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Allah alone has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and exclusive knowledge and sovereignty of Allah. It signifies that only Allah has the knowledge of the final Hour (Judgment Day) and the intricate details of future occurrences. The verse highlights divine control over natural phenomena such as rain and the creation process. It underscores human limitations in foreseeing their future or ultimate end, stressing reliance on and submission to Allah's omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت إن الله عليم خبير

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: This verse contains the mysterious letters 'Alif, Lam, Meem,' which are known as 'Muqatta'at' or 'disjointed letters.' The precise meaning of these letters is not known and has been a subject of contemplation and study among scholars. It is believed that these letters serve various purposes, such as drawing attention to the text, indicating the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, or holding a deeper, undisclosed meaning known only to Allah.
orig: الم

translation: The revelation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse asserts the divine origin and absolute certainty of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a revelation from the Supreme Creator, the Lord of all realms and existence. It underscores the authenticity and unassailable truth of the message contained within the Qur'an, inviting believers to trust and follow its guidance without any doubt.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the message of the Qur'an. It affirms that the Qur'an is indeed the truth from Allah, intended to warn and guide a people who had not previously received such a warning. The purpose of this divine intervention is to provide an opportunity for these people to find the right path and achieve spiritual guidance.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يهتدون

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or intercessor; so will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse underscores the omnipotence of Allah as the Creator of the entire universe, including the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes that Allah alone is sovereign, ruling over all creation from His Throne. The verse also points out the futility of relying on any protectors or intercessors other than Allah, urging people to remember and reflect on this profound truth. The message is one of monotheism, urging an exclusive reliance and devotion to the one true God.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع أفلا تتذكرون

translation: He plans the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and complexity of Allah’s divine management over the universe. It underscores His supreme authority and control over all affairs in the heavens and the earth. The reference to a ‘day’ being equivalent to a thousand years as per human reckoning highlights the relative perception of time, illustrating that divine actions follow a different temporal scale that humans may find incomprehensible. This serves to remind believers of the grandeur and meticulousness of Allah’s governance and the idea that divine timing and processes transcend human understanding.
orig: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, highlighting His ability to perceive both the visible and hidden aspects of creation. It also balances His power with His mercy, indicating that His might does not negate His compassion. This duality assures believers of Allah's comprehensive nature, as both a formidable force and a source of infinite mercy.
orig: ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم

translation: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perfection and precision in Allah's creation, emphasizing His attributes as the ultimate Creator. It signifies that everything Allah created is flawless and serves a purpose. By mentioning the creation of man from clay, it underscores human beings' humble origins and the divine act of creation, which transforms basic elements into complex, purposeful life. This can serve as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and an encouragement for humans to reflect on their place in the universe and their relationship with the Creator.
orig: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

translation: Then He made his progeny from a quintessence of despised fluid.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the humble and lowly beginnings of human creation. It emphasizes the divine power and wisdom in transforming something seemingly insignificant into a complex and dignified human being. This awareness is meant to instill humility in humans, reminding them of their origins and encouraging gratitude and reverence towards their Creator.
orig: ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the meticulous creation of human beings by God, emphasizing the divine breath of life bestowed upon them, which symbolizes a direct connection to the divine. It underscores the provision of essential faculties - hearing, vision, and intellect, urging introspection on the limited gratitude shown by humans towards these profound gifts. This lack of gratitude is a prompt for humans to reflect on their blessings and express more gratitude for the inherent capabilities that enable them to experience and understand the world.
orig: ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And they say, 'When we are lost within the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?' Rather, they are, in the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of disbelievers regarding the resurrection and life after death. They question the possibility of being recreated after their physical bodies have decomposed and merged with the earth. The verse then points out that their real issue is not the physical improbability of resurrection, but rather their denial of the Day of Judgment and their meeting with Allah. Their disbelief in the Hereafter is a major barrier to their faith.
orig: وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض أإنا لفي خلق جديد بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

translation: Say, 'The Angel of Death, who has been entrusted with you, will take your souls; then to your Lord you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of death and the inevitability of returning to Allah for judgment. The Angel of Death is a designated entity responsible for taking the souls of people at the time of their death. Following this, each individual will return to their Creator, where they will be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the importance of being mindful of one's conduct in anticipation of the hereafter.
orig: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: If you could only see when the guilty will hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], 'Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will do righteous deeds. Indeed, we are now certain.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the regret and desperation of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment when they confront their Lord. They acknowledge their sins and express a desire to return to earthly life to rectify their actions by performing righteous deeds, having now gained certainty in the truth they previously neglected. It emphasizes the finality of judgment and the lost opportunity for repentance and good deeds, highlighting the importance of sincere faith and righteousness in life.
orig: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

translation: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me will come into effect: that I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and the freedom of human choice. It suggests that God, in His ultimate wisdom, has given humans and jinn the ability to choose their paths. Though God has the power to guide every soul directly, He allows individuals to exercise their free will. The verse also underlines the consequence of misusing this free will, stating that Hell will be filled with those who choose to reject guidance. Thus, it is a reminder of both the responsibility that comes with free will and the reality of divine justice.
orig: ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: So taste [punishment] for what you forgot of the meeting of this, your Day; indeed, We have [accordingly] forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of neglecting to prepare for the Day of Judgment. Those who disregarded the meeting with their Lord and failed to adhere to His commands will face perpetual punishment as a result of their deeds. The phrase 'We have [accordingly] forgotten you' signifies that because they ignored divine guidance, they will be neglected in their time of need. Essentially, it underlines the principle of divine justice: actions have consequences, and deliberate neglect of spiritual responsibilities leads to enduring suffering.
orig: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of true believers: they are deeply moved by the signs of Allah, which compels them to immediate worship and humility. Their reaction is to prostrate, a position of ultimate submission, and to glorify Allah, acknowledging His greatness and mercy. Importantly, they display humility, avoiding arrogance in their faith and actions, which implies a sincere and wholehearted devotion to Allah's guidance.
orig: إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their sides forsake their beds, to invoke their Lord in fear and hope; and they spend (in charity) out of what We have bestowed upon them.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the deep devotion and piety of certain believers who forego the comfort of sleep to pray to their Lord with a balance of fear and hope. This dual sentiment is a recognition of God’s greatness and mercy. Additionally, it highlights their generous nature as they spend from the provisions granted to them by God. The verse portrays an image of sincere and active worship, combining spiritual acts with acts of charity.
orig: تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unseen and unimaginable rewards that await the righteous in the hereafter. It highlights the concept that human understanding is limited when it comes to the bounties and pleasures that Allah has prepared for those who lead virtuous lives. The term 'comfort for eyes' symbolizes ultimate joy and satisfaction, suggesting that the rewards will surpass any earthly pleasures. This acts as an assurance and motivation for believers to adhere to righteous deeds, reinforcing the principle that divine recompense is beyond human comprehension.
orig: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Then is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental distinction between a believer who follows the divine guidance and a person who engages in sinful disobedience. It serves to emphasize that the moral and spiritual conditions of the two are not the same, and they will not be treated equally in the sight of God. This differentiation underscores the importance of faith and righteous conduct, affirming that adherence to the path of faith brings a unique status and reward that cannot be equated with the position of someone who persistently rejects divine commands.
orig: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Refuge as their lodging for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith and engage in good deeds, promising them eternal abode in the Gardens of Paradise. It emphasizes that these rewards are directly related to their actions and efforts in leading a life in accordance with divine guidance, underscoring the importance of both belief and practice in achieving spiritual success and eternal peace.
orig: أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون

translation: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge will be the Fire. Every time they want to get out of it, they will be returned to it, and it will be said to them, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who persist in their rebellion and disobedience against God's commands. It describes the punishment of Hell as a place from which there is no escape for such individuals. Their repeated attempts to flee will be futile, and they will be continuously returned to the Fire. Furthermore, the verse underscores the gravity of their denial and disbelief by illustrating that their suffering is a direct consequence of their rejection of the truth. This serves to reinforce the concept of accountability and the inevitability of divine justice for those who turn away from faith.
orig: وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return [i.e., repent].
interpretation: This verse suggests that a lesser punishment or hardship is sometimes imposed upon people in this world as a warning or reminder, providing an opportunity for them to repent and return to righteousness before facing the more severe punishment of the Hereafter. It underscores God's mercy in giving people chances to change their ways before the final judgment.
orig: ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe injustice of ignoring divine guidance after receiving clear reminders. It emphasizes that those who deliberately reject and turn away from the signs and teachings of Allah, despite being reminded, are committing a grave wrong. Furthermore, it serves as a stern warning that such persistent rejection will inevitably lead to divine retribution, marking these rejecters as criminals in the sight of Allah, destined to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها إنا من المجرمين منتقمون

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt over his meeting. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad and the believers by highlighting the continuity of divine revelation. It emphasizes that just as Moses was given the Scripture, which served as guidance for the Israelites, there should be no doubt about the legitimacy and truth of his prophethood. The reference to Moses also underscores the importance of following divine guidance and the consistency in the message delivered by different prophets.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل

translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and [when] they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the conditions under which certain individuals were chosen as leaders among their people. It emphasizes two crucial characteristics: patience and firm belief in God's signs. Patience here can be understood as enduring trials and hardships while maintaining integrity and faith. Certainty in God's signs refers to having an unwavering belief in the divine messages and revelations. Through these qualities, they are granted the responsibility of guiding others by God's command, indicating that true leadership in the Islamic context is rooted in spiritual and moral excellence.
orig: وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate nature of divine justice and the role of God as the final arbiter in all matters of dispute and disagreement among people. It emphasizes that while differences and conflicts may occur in this worldly life, it is Allah who will conclusively and fairly resolve these differences in the hereafter, on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder of accountability and the importance of adhering to faith and righteousness, trusting that ultimate justice rests with Allah.
orig: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, which they walk past in their places of residence? Surely in that are signs. Do they not then hear?
interpretation: This verse draws attention to the destruction of past generations as a lesson and a warning for the present people. By inviting them to reflect on the remnants of those who were annihilated for their disobedience, it emphasizes the inevitability of divine retribution and urges them to heed these lessons. The rhetorical question at the end underscores their neglect and inattention to these evident signs, calling them to be more perceptive and responsive to God's guidance.
orig: أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات أفلا يسمعون

translation: Have they not seen how We drive the water to the barren land and produce thereby crops from which their livestock and they themselves eat? Will they not then see?
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah in reviving the dead land by bringing forth water to it, resulting in the growth of vegetation which sustains both livestock and humans. It serves as a reminder of Allah's continuous provision and the signs of His existence and might. The verse encourages reflection and observation of these natural phenomena as evidence of divine grace and urges humankind to recognize and be grateful for the sustenance provided by Allah.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and demand for proof by those opposing the Prophet Muhammad. They question the promised victory and judgment by asking when it will occur, challenging the truthfulness of the Prophet's message. This reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an, where disbelievers often demand immediate signs or miracles as proof of the divine message, while faith requires trust in the unseen and patience for God's timing.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'On the Day of Conquest the belief of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality and absolute justice of the Day of Judgment. It declares that once the decisive moment of Allah's final judgment arrives, it will be too late for disbelievers to repent or embrace faith. Their belief at that point will not be acknowledged, nor will they be given any further grace period. This serves as a stark reminder to embrace faith and seek righteousness before the final hour comes.
orig: قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to distance himself from those who persistently reject his message and to remain patient. It implies that both the Prophet and his adversaries are in a state of anticipation, but it subtly reassures that the divine plan will eventually unfold, revealing the truth and bringing justice. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God's timing.
orig: فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون

translation: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a command to the Prophet Muhammad to maintain his consciousness of Allah and caution against yielding to the influences of disbelievers and hypocrites. It also subtly advises the Muslim community, through the Prophet, to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by those who do not share their beliefs. Allah's attributes of being All-Knowing and Wise are emphasized to reassure that His guidance and commandments are based on profound wisdom and understanding.
orig: يا أيها النبي اتق الله ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the guidance and revelations given by Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah has complete knowledge and understanding of all actions, encouraging a sense of accountability and mindfulness in one's conduct.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And put your trust in Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying completely on Allah in all matters, suggesting that trust in Allah should be absolute and unwavering. It reinforces that Allah is fully capable of handling and managing all affairs, providing reassurance and comfort to the believer.
orig: وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Allah has not made for any man two hearts within him; nor has He made your wives whom you declare unlawful your mothers; nor has He made your adopted sons your (true) sons. That is your saying with your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the (right) way.
interpretation: This verse addresses certain misconceptions and cultural practices that were prevalent at the time. The mention of 'two hearts within him' underscores the idea that a person's loyalties and affections cannot be divided in contradictory ways. The notion of declaring one's wife as a mother was a pre-Islamic practice called 'zihar,' which undermined the sanctity of marital relations. Additionally, the verse clarifies that adopted children do not carry the same legal and blood ties as biological children, emphasizing the importance of truthful relationships and divine guidance over human conventions. Overall, it highlights that God's dictates are based on truth and wisdom, guiding believers towards the right path.
orig: ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه وما جعل أزواجكم اللائي تظاهرون منهن أمهاتكم وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم ذلكم قولكم بأفواهكم والله يقول الحق وهو يهدي السبيل

translation: Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are [still] your brothers in religion and those entrusted to you. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only for] what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of linking individuals to their paternal lineage for the sake of justice and proper identification. However, in cases where the paternal lineage is unknown, the verse underscores the spirit of brotherhood and mutual care within the religious community. Additionally, it acknowledges human error and intentions, reassuring believers that Allah is forgiving and merciful, focusing on the intentions of the heart rather than unintended mistakes.
orig: ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of blood relationship are closer to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you may do what is right to your close associates. This is inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual and social responsibilities that the Prophet Muhammad holds over the believers, surpassing even their own personal concerns. His wives are given an honorary status as mothers, indicating a deep respect and special status within the community. Moreover, the verse clarifies that blood relations have priority in matters of inheritance and familial rights according to God's decree, yet it still allows for kindness and just behavior towards close associates or allies. This directive is part of the divine ordinance, emphasizing the structured and just nature of social and familial relationships as prescribed by God.
orig: النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله من المؤمنين والمهاجرين إلا أن تفعلوا إلى أوليائكم معروفا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of the divine message sent by God through various prophets over time. The 'covenant' refers to the commitment made by the prophets to deliver God's message to their people faithfully and uphold His commands. By specifically naming Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the verse emphasizes the unity of the prophetic mission and the seriousness of their responsibilities. The 'solemn covenant' signifies the weight and importance of their duty to guide humanity towards righteousness and submission to God's will.
orig: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: That He may question the truthful about their truth. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of truthfulness among the believers, indicating that those who are truthful will be questioned about their adherence to the truth. It also serves as a stern warning to disbelievers, informing them of the severe punishment prepared for them due to their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم وأعد للكافرين عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when hosts came to you and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse calls the believers to reflect on the blessings and support Allah has given them in times of adversity. It reminds them of a specific instance where enemy forces threatened them, but Allah intervened by sending a mighty wind and unseen forces to assist them. The verse underscores Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, emphasizing that He sees and is aware of all their actions and circumstances. This serves to reinforce the believers' faith and trust in Allah's protection and support during difficulties.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جاءتكم جنود فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted (in fear) and hearts reached the throats and you assumed about Allah [various] assumptions.
interpretation: This verse describes a moment of intense fear and distress faced by the believers, specifically during the Battle of the Trench. It illustrates the dire situation when enemy forces approached them from all directions, causing overwhelming anxiety manifest in their eyes and hearts. The believers were so engulfed in their fear that they began to have doubts and various thoughts about Allah, questioning His support and protection. This verse serves as a reminder of the human inclination to doubt in times of extreme difficulty, and emphasizes faith and trust in Allah even in the most challenging circumstances.
orig: إذ جاءوكم من فوقكم ومن أسفل منكم وإذ زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر وتظنون بالله الظنونا

translation: There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trials and severe challenges that the believers faced, highlighting their steadfastness and faith in the face of overwhelming adversity. It serves as a reminder of the tests of faith that believers may encounter and the importance of perseverance and trust in God during such tribulations.
orig: هنالك ابتلي المؤمنون وزلزلوا زلزالا شديدا

translation: And [remember] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, 'Allah and His Messenger did not promise us except delusion.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the negative and cynical attitudes of the hypocrites and those with weak faith during times of trial. It illustrates their lack of trust and conviction in the promises of Allah and His Messenger. Their words reveal their inner doubts and disbelief, marking a stark contrast to the true believers who maintain their faith despite challenges. This serves as a reminder of the importance of steadfastness and trust in divine promises, especially during difficult times.
orig: وإذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض ما وعدنا الله ورسوله إلا غرورا

translation: And when a faction of them said, 'O people of Yathrib, there is no stability for you [here], so return [home].' And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, 'Indeed, our houses are unprotected,' while they were not exposed. They did not intend except to flee.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wavering faith and panic of some of the people of Medina (then Yathrib) during a time of conflict. It reflects their lack of trust in the protection provided by God and their Prophet, seeking excuses to leave the battlefield. Instead of facing adversity, they wished to retreat under the pretense of safeguarding their homes, which were already secure. This attitude is depicted as a form of cowardice and a lack of true commitment to their faith and community.
orig: وإذ قالت طائفة منهم يا أهل يثرب لا مقام لكم فارجعوا ويستأذن فريق منهم النبي يقولون إن بيوتنا عورة وما هي بعورة إن يريدون إلا فرارا

translation: Had they been invaded from all sides and then been asked to dissent, they would have done so with little hesitation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness and lack of true commitment among certain groups. It suggests that, under pressure or temptation, these individuals would readily abandon their faith or principles. The verse emphasizes the superficiality of their loyalty, showing that their devotion is not deeply rooted. This can serve as a warning to believers to cultivate a sincere and steadfast faith.
orig: ولو دخلت عليهم من أقطارها ثم سئلوا الفتنة لآتوها وما تلبثوا بها إلا يسيرا

translation: And they had already pledged to Allah before not to turn their backs and flee. And a covenant with Allah must be answered for.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who had made a solemn promise to remain steadfast and not retreat in the face of adversity. Despite their earlier commitment, they failed to uphold their pledge. It serves as a reminder that promises made to Allah carry significant weight and accountability. In the broader context, it emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and the serious spiritual and ethical implications of breaking promises, particularly those made to the Divine.
orig: ولقد كانوا عاهدوا الله من قبل لا يولون الأدبار وكان عهد الله مسئولا

translation: Say, 'Never will fleeing benefit you if you should flee from death or killing; and then [if you did], you would not be given enjoyment except for a little.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of trying to escape one's destined end, whether it be death or being killed. It emphasizes the notion that life and its pleasures are transient and limited, no matter how one tries to prolong or avoid the inevitable. Ultimately, running away from fate will not yield significant benefits, and any enjoyment gained through such attempts would be minimal and short-lived.
orig: قل لن ينفعكم الفرار إن فررتم من الموت أو القتل وإذا لا تمتعون إلا قليلا

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you from Allah if He intends to harm you or intends to show you mercy?' And they will not find for themselves any protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that no one can shield or offer refuge to individuals from Allah's will, whether it is harm or compassion. It serves as a reminder of the futility of seeking protection or assistance from any entity other than Allah, reinforcing the concept of monotheism and dependence on Allah alone.
orig: قل من ذا الذي يعصمكم من الله إن أراد بكم سوءا أو أراد بكم رحمة ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Allah is aware of those among you who hinder others and those who say to their brethren, 'Come to us,' while they hardly ever go to battle.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges Allah's awareness of the individuals among the believers who discourage others from participating in the defense of the community. These people call their companions to stay behind with them, displaying a lack of true commitment to the collective effort and only participating in the struggle minimally or not at all. The verse highlights the importance of sincerity and full participation in communal responsibilities, condemning the attitudes of those who seek to avoid their duties by dissuading others.
orig: قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم والقائلين لإخوانهم هلم إلينا ولا يأتون البأس إلا قليلا

translation: They are miserly towards you. When fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one overcome by death. But once the fear has gone, they smite you with sharp tongues, being greedy for wealth. They have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds. And that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocrisy and cowardice of certain individuals. When danger approaches, they are frightened and helpless, but once it passes, they become boastful and harsh, indicative of their insincere faith and greed. Their actions and intentions are ultimately futile because of their lack of genuine belief, resulting in the nullification of their deeds by Allah. This underscores that true faith is tested and proven through consistent behavior, particularly in times of fear and ease alike. Allah’s judgment is effortless and inevitable.
orig: أشحة عليكم فإذا جاء الخوف رأيتهم ينظرون إليك تدور أعينهم كالذي يغشى عليه من الموت فإذا ذهب الخوف سلقوكم بألسنة حداد أشحة على الخير أولئك لم يؤمنوا فأحبط الله أعمالهم وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: They think that the confederates have not withdrawn; and if the confederates should come again, they would wish to be in the deserts with the Bedouins, asking for news about you. And if they were among you, they would not fight except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who doubt or are fearful of the return of opposition forces after they have withdrawn. It highlights the cowardice and lack of commitment of some individuals. These people would prefer to stay away from conflict in the safety of the deserts with the Bedouins, merely seeking information about the ongoing battles rather than participating directly. Even if they were present among the believers, their contribution to the fight would be minimal, indicating their insincerity and lack of true dedication to the cause.
orig: يحسبون الأحزاب لم يذهبوا وإن يأت الأحزاب يودوا لو أنهم بادون في الأعراب يسألون عن أنبائكم ولو كانوا فيكم ما قاتلوا إلا قليلا

translation: Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Prophet Muhammad as a model of exemplary conduct for those who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment and are mindful of Allah frequently. It emphasizes the Prophet's role in providing a tangible example of how to live a righteous and devout life, encouraging believers to emulate his actions and character in their own lives.
orig: لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر وذكر الله كثيرا

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us; and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.' And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the believers' reaction upon seeing the coalition of enemy forces. Instead of fear or despair, their faith and trust in Allah's promises are strengthened. They recognize the fulfillment of divine prophecy and respond by deepening their belief and surrender to God's will. It highlights the resilience and unwavering commitment of the true believers in the face of adversity.
orig: ولما رأى المؤمنون الأحزاب قالوا هذا ما وعدنا الله ورسوله وصدق الله ورسوله وما زادهم إلا إيمانا وتسليما

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah. Some of them have fulfilled their vow by death, and some are still waiting, but they have never changed in the least.
interpretation: This verse commends the steadfastness and fidelity of true believers who remain unwavering in their commitments to Allah. It highlights two groups of men: those who have already sacrificed their lives for the sake of their promise and those who are still alive and await their turn, yet continue to remain resolute and unchanged in their devotion and dedication. It underscores the virtue of constancy and faithfulness in one’s duties and promises to Allah, setting a high moral standard for the believers.
orig: من المؤمنين رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه فمنهم من قضى نحبه ومنهم من ينتظر وما بدلوا تبديلا

translation: That Allah may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn mercifully towards them. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will reward individuals for their honesty and integrity. Conversely, for those who display hypocrisy, Allah has the power to punish them but also the choice to forgive and guide them towards repentance. It underlines Allah's attributes as both Just and Merciful, highlighting the importance of sincerity in faith while also reminding of the potential mercy available to all, even those who have erred.
orig: ليجزي الله الصادقين بصدقهم ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء أو يتوب عليهم إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good. And sufficient was Allah for the believers in battle, and ever is Allah Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's control and protection over the believers. It recounts how He thwarted the plans of the disbelievers who were full of anger, leaving them with no success in achieving any good against the believers. This verse highlights the divine protection granted to the faithful, asserting that Allah Himself is sufficient to defend and aid the believers in their struggles. It underscores the power and might of Allah, affirming that He is always capable of providing strength and victory to those who believe in Him.
orig: ورد الله الذين كفروا بغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرا وكفى الله المؤمنين القتال وكان الله قويا عزيزا

translation: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Book from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts (so that) a group (of them) you killed, and you took captive a group.
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific historical event where the allies among the People of the Book (Jews in this context) who supported the enemies of the Muslims were defeated. It signifies the divine intervention that caused terror in their hearts, leading to their downfall. One group faced death, while another was taken captive. The verse illustrates the consequences of betrayal and the fulfillment of divine justice, reflecting on the seriousness of allegiance and loyalty in times of conflict.
orig: وأنزل الذين ظاهروهم من أهل الكتاب من صياصيهم وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب فريقا تقتلون وتأسرون فريقا

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the concept of divine providence and victory granted by Allah to the believers. It highlights that Allah's grace enabled them to gain not just the possessions but also territories previously unexplored by them, reinforcing the themes of divine support, empowerment, and the boundless capacity of Allah to grant success. This often serves as a reminder of trust in Allah’s comprehensive power over all matters.
orig: وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم وأرضا لم تطئوها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives, 'If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a gracious manner.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, offering them a choice between the material comforts and adornments of this worldly life and the spiritual and moral responsibilities of being the wives of the Prophet. It suggests that those who prefer worldly pleasures over their unique and demanding roles can be allowed to leave honorably and with provision. This reflects the balance between compassion and the high expectations placed on them due to their special positions in the Muslim community.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك إن كنتن تردن الحياة الدنيا وزينتها فتعالين أمتعكن وأسرحكن سراحا جميلا

translation: But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, offering them a choice between the material comforts of this world and the spiritual and moral satisfaction found in devotion to Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. It signifies the high status and significant reward that awaits those who choose a life of righteousness, faith, and obedience, emphasizing the greatness of the reward prepared by Allah for those who act justly and in accordance with their faith.
orig: وإن كنتن تردن الله ورسوله والدار الآخرة فإن الله أعد للمحسنات منكن أجرا عظيما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever among you commits a clear immorality, the punishment for her will be doubled, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the elevated standards and responsibilities that come with their proximity to the Prophet. It conveys that their actions are under greater scrutiny due to their influential positions. Consequently, any clear immoral act committed by them would result in a punishment that is twice as severe compared to others. This serves as a stern reminder of the expectations on them to maintain exemplary conduct, and emphasizes Allah's omnipotence in enacting justice.
orig: يا نساء النبي من يأت منكن بفاحشة مبينة يضاعف لها العذاب ضعفين وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her reward twice; and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of obedience and righteous deeds, specifically directed towards the wives of the Prophet. It promises a doubled reward for their devout compliance to Allah and His Messenger, highlighting their elevated status and distinction. Additionally, it assures them of generous and honorable sustenance, both in this life and the hereafter, reflecting the special consideration and grace bestowed upon them for their dedicated faith and virtuous actions.
orig: ومن يقنت منكن لله ورسوله وتعمل صالحا نؤتها أجرها مرتين وأعتدنا لها رزقا كريما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women, if you fear Allah. Then do not be too soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing their unique status and the higher moral expectations placed upon them. It advises them to maintain a respectful and firm tone in their speech to avoid attracting those with impure intentions. This guidance underscores the importance of modesty and propriety, highlighting the role of women in setting a standard of behavior that aligns with Islamic principles of piety and respect.
orig: يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض وقلن قولا معروفا

translation: And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves like the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification.
interpretation: This verse addresses the women of the Prophet's household, advising them to remain in their homes and maintain modesty, refraining from the flamboyant behavior characteristic of pre-Islamic ignorance. They are also instructed to fulfill their religious duties, such as prayer (salah) and almsgiving (zakat), and to obey Allah and the Prophet. The ultimate intention of these directives is to purify and elevate the moral and spiritual status of the Prophet's household, thereby removing any form of impurity or sin.
orig: وقرن في بيوتكن ولا تبرجن تبرج الجاهلية الأولى وأقمن الصلاة وآتين الزكاة وأطعن الله ورسوله إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس أهل البيت ويطهركم تطهيرا

translation: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, reminding them to remember and reflect upon the verses of the Qur'an and the wisdom that is recited in their homes. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of divine guidance and wisdom. By highlighting that Allah is Subtle and Acquainted with all things, it reassures that God’s knowledge encompasses every aspect of their lives, urging them to adhere to the divine message faithfully.
orig: واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة إن الله كان لطيفا خبيرا

translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who do so - for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of piety and righteousness in Islam, encompassing both genders equally. It emphasizes that spiritual qualities such as faith, obedience, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, and remembrance of Allah are meritorious traits for all believers, regardless of gender. The verse assures that for such individuals, Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward, indicating the immense value and ultimate reward of cultivating these virtues.
orig: إن المسلمين والمسلمات والمؤمنين والمؤمنات والقانتين والقانتات والصادقين والصادقات والصابرين والصابرات والخاشعين والخاشعات والمتصدقين والمتصدقات والصائمين والصائمات والحافظين فروجهم والحافظات والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات أعد الله لهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of Allah and His Messenger in the life of a believer. It signifies that true faith requires complete submission to divine commands, without wavering or seeking personal preference. The statement underscores that deviating from this path leads to manifest error, highlighting the importance of obedience and alignment with divine will as key components of Islamic belief and practice.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن ولا مؤمنة إذا قضى الله ورسوله أمرا أن يكون لهم الخيرة من أمرهم ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد ضل ضلالا مبينا

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: The verse highlights a significant event in the life of Prophet Muhammad where he advised Zayd, his adopted son, to keep his wife and fear Allah. The Prophet, however, concealed his own feelings and the divine revelation that Zaynab would eventually be his wife. The verse underscores the importance of fearing Allah above all else, including societal norms. The subsequent marriage between the Prophet and Zaynab served to establish a precedent in Islamic law, ensuring there is no stigma or restriction on marrying the former wives of adopted sons. This action was to remove any discomfort or societal barriers for believers, affirming that Allah’s commandments will always be fulfilled.
orig: وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه وأنعمت عليه أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه وتخشى الناس والله أحق أن تخشاه فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا زوجناكها لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: The Prophet is not at fault for what Allah has ordained for him. This is the way of Allah among those who passed away before. And the command of Allah is a decree determined.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not to be blamed or questioned for acting on what Allah has mandated for him, reinforcing the idea that divine commands are paramount and must be fulfilled. It also indicates that this principle has always been a part of Allah's way with previous prophets and communities. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah's commands are predestined and unchangeable, underscoring the belief in divine decree and predestination.
orig: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear anyone but Allah. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility and courage required to convey Allah's messages faithfully. It highlights that true believers should fear Allah alone, rather than any other beings or potential threats. The phrase 'And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner' reassures believers that Allah is ultimately aware of all actions and will provide the necessary accountability and judgment. The message encourages believers to maintain their focus and trust in Allah’s judgment, regardless of worldly pressures or fears.
orig: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and final prophetic mission of Muhammad. It clarifies that Muhammad does not hold a paternal relationship with any man among the believers, signifying that his authority and relationship are purely spiritual and divine. As the 'Seal of the Prophets,' Muhammad completes the line of prophecy, indicating that no prophets will come after him. Furthermore, it concludes by highlighting Allah's omniscience, reinforcing that God's knowledge encompasses all aspects of creation and His decision in matters of prophethood is based on His infinite wisdom.
orig: ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to engage in frequent and continual remembrance of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of keeping Allah in one's thoughts and consciousness regularly, indicating that such remembrance should not be sporadic or rare, but rather a constant and significant part of a believer's life. This act of frequently remembering Allah is an essential aspect of maintaining faith, devotion, and spiritual connection with the Divine.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to praise and glorify Allah continuously, specifically in the morning and evening. This serves as a reminder to maintain a constant connection with the divine throughout different times of the day, fostering mindfulness and gratitude towards Allah's presence and blessings in one's life.
orig: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: He it is who sends blessings upon you, as do His angels, that He may bring you forth from darkness into light; and He is merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine compassion and mercy that God bestows upon the believers. It emphasizes that both God and His angels are actively involved in guiding the faithful from the obscurity and difficulties of darkness towards the enlightenment and clarity of light. This transition signifies moving from ignorance or hardships to knowledge, spiritual awareness, and ease. The passage reassures believers of God’s continuous support, emphasizing His deep care and mercy for those who have faith.
orig: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

translation: Their greeting the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace.' And He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, the righteous will be welcomed by Allah with the greeting of 'Peace,' signifying safety, tranquility, and divine satisfaction. Their faith and good deeds will be honored by Allah through the promise of a generous and noble reward in the hereafter, emphasizing the ultimate reward for piety and righteousness.
orig: تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, affirming his roles as a witness to humanity's actions, a bearer of glad tidings for those who follow the righteous path, and a warner against the consequences of straying from it. It highlights the multifaceted mission of the Prophet, emphasizing his importance and the comprehensive nature of his message to guide people towards faith and righteousness.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And inviting to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Prophet Muhammad as a messenger who calls people towards Allah with His permission, and as a source of guidance and enlightenment for humanity, akin to a bright light that dispels darkness and ignorance, leading people towards the path of righteousness and divine truth.
orig: وداعيا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجا منيرا

translation: And give good news to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.
interpretation: This verse promises believers a significant reward from Allah, underlining His generosity and mercy. It serves as encouragement and motivation for believers to continue their faith and righteousness, reassuring them of divine favor and a positive outcome in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلا كبيرا

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and ignore their hurtful talk, and place your trust in Allah. For Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse advises steadfastness and reliance on Allah in the face of opposition from disbelievers and hypocrites. It instructs believers not to follow or be influenced by those who reject faith or are deceitful in their beliefs. Instead, they should disregard any harmful speech or actions from such individuals and trust in Allah's guidance and protection, as He is the best guardian and support.
orig: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is not for you any waiting period to count concerning them. So provide for them and release them in a gracious manner.
interpretation: This verse is addressing believers, specifically in the context of marriage and divorce. It clarifies that if a marriage contract is made but the marriage is not consummated, there is no 'iddah (waiting period) required before the woman can remarry. The instruction is to provide some form of parting gift and to ensure that the divorce is handled with kindness and respect. This reflects the broader Qur'anic principle of fair and considerate treatment of women, even in situations of marital dissolution.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا

translation: O Prophet, We have made lawful to you your wives whose dowries you have paid, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman who offers herself to the Prophet if the Prophet wishes to marry her; this is only for you, and not for the believers. We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse provides specific allowances for the Prophet Muhammad regarding marriage, highlighting certain relationships and prerogatives unique to his position. It underscores the divine facilitation in his personal affairs to ensure he faces no hardship, while reiterating Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy. Such provisions were designed to support the Prophet's unique mission and circumstances without imposing similar obligations on the broader Muslim community.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم لكيلا يكون عليك حرج وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: You may put aside whichever of them you will, and take to yourself whichever you will, and if you desire any you have set aside, there is no blame on you. That is better so that their eyes may be cool and they may not grieve and may all be content with what you give them. Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is Ever-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse provides the Prophet Muhammad with guidance on managing his relationships with his wives, granting him the flexibility to interact with them in a manner that best maintains harmony and personal contentment. By allowing the Prophet this discretion, the verse aims to ensure that his wives feel at peace and reduce potential sadness or dissatisfaction. It underscores that such arrangements are made with divine understanding and wisdom, acknowledging the intricate emotional dynamics involved and encouraging an approach that fosters mutual satisfaction and emotional tranquility within the household. Allah's wisdom and patience in understanding human emotions are highlighted, reassuring that His guidance is perfectly attuned to their needs.
orig: ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما

translation: It is not lawful for you [O Muhammad] to marry other women after this, nor to exchange them [i.e., your present wives] for [other] wives, even if their beauty were to please you, except what your right hand possesses. And ever is Allah, over all things, an Observer.
interpretation: This verse restricts the Prophet Muhammad from marrying additional women or replacing his current wives, despite any attraction he might feel towards other women. The exception to this command is the enslaved women he lawfully possesses. This decree emphasizes the special and distinct position of the Prophet’s marriages and underscores that Allah is an all-seeing observer, ensuring His commandments are followed and that there is no transgression in personal desires or marital relations.
orig: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج ولو أعجبك حسنهن إلا ما ملكت يمينك وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا

translation: O you who believe, do not enter the homes of the Prophet unless you are permitted for a meal, [and then] not so early as to wait for its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that [behavior] was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you. But Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not [conceivable or lawful] for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the private space and time of the Prophet Muhammad and his household. Believers are advised to follow proper etiquette when visiting, indicating the sanctity and decorum expected around the Prophet's home. The verse also establishes the practice of hijab for the Prophet's wives, marking a distinction to maintain purity of the heart and to prevent any form of transgression. The prohibition on marrying the Prophet's wives after his death further underscores their honored and unique status, safeguarding their dignity and the sanctity of the Prophet's legacy. The underlying message is one of reverence, respect, and maintaining the sanctity of the Prophet’s family as a means of upholding piety and proper conduct.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما

translation: If you reveal anything or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness. Whether our actions, thoughts, or intentions are made public or kept private, they are all known to Allah. This serves as a powerful reminder to maintain sincerity and righteousness in all aspects of our lives, as nothing escapes Allah's awareness. The verse emphasizes accountability and the omnipresence of divine knowledge, encouraging believers to act with integrity at all times.
orig: إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: There is no blame on them (the women) if they appear before their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, or those whom their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Verily, Allah is Ever an Observer over all things.
interpretation: This verse outlines specific exemptions for women regarding who they can appear before without covering themselves as they would in front of strangers. These exemptions include close male relatives and others within their intimate circle. The instruction emphasizes the importance of observing modesty and piety, reminding believers that Allah watches over all actions, ensuring that the rules of modesty are both a personal and spiritual responsibility.
orig: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن واتقين الله إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by stating that both Allah and His angels honor him. It then calls upon the believers to also send blessings and peace upon the Prophet, acknowledging his significance and following divine guidance in showing reverence. The act of sending blessings (Salawat) is a means of connecting with the Prophet's teachings and seeking spiritual closeness to him, reinforcing unity and respect within the Ummah (Muslim community).
orig: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما

translation: Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of showing disrespect or aggression towards Allah and His Messenger. It highlights that such actions incur severe consequences, both in this world and the Hereafter. The use of 'curse' signifies divine repudiation and exclusion from His mercy, and 'humiliating punishment' suggests both physical and moral suffering prepared for them. It serves as a warning to uphold reverence and respect towards the divine and prophetic sanctity.
orig: إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly born upon themselves a slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave sin and moral corruption in harming believers unjustly. It warns of the significant spiritual consequences for those who falsely accuse or harm others without cause. By labeling such actions as slander and clear iniquity, it underscores the importance of justice, honesty, and the protection of the dignity of all individuals. This serves as a reminder of the ethical standards Muslims are expected to uphold and the severe repercussions of violating these principles.
orig: والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a directive to the Prophet Muhammad asking him to instruct his wives, daughters, and believing women to cover themselves with their outer garments. The primary purpose of this instruction is to ensure that they are recognized as modest and pious women, which serves as a means to protect them from harm and harassment. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah’s attributes of being Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that these guidelines are not meant to be burdensome but are derived from divine wisdom and compassion.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and those who spread rumors in the city do not cease, We shall surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse addresses the consequences for hypocrites and mischief-makers in the community who fail to abandon their negative behavior. God warns that if these individuals do not desist from their harmful actions, He will empower the Prophet to take a stance against them. This implies that their behaviors will no longer be tolerated, and they will be confronted decisively, leading to their marginalization and eventual expulsion from the community for a period. The verse underscores the importance of maintaining a sincere and harmonious environment in the society and the consequences of spreading discord and falsehood.
orig: لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

translation: Accursed wherever they are found, they are seized and massacred completely.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who are accursed due to their egregious actions against the divine commands and the believers. It suggests that such individuals will face severe consequences and divine retribution wherever they are, indicating that their punishment is both inevitable and thorough. The severity of the language underscores the gravity of their sins and acts as a stark warning to those who engage in similar behaviors.
orig: ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا

translation: Such has been the way of Allah with those who passed on before; and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchanging and consistent nature of God's practices and decrees throughout history. It reassures believers that the principles and laws established by Allah for previous generations remain constant and reliable. This continuity underscores the fairness and sovereignty of divine will, suggesting that the moral and spiritual laws governing the world are both timeless and universally applicable.
orig: سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: The people ask you about the Hour. Say, 'Its knowledge is only with Allah. And what can make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's knowledge regarding the timing of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of human limitations in understanding divine wisdom and the importance of trusting in Allah's perfect knowledge. It also hints at the possibility of the Hour being imminent, encouraging constant spiritual preparedness and piety.
orig: يسألك الناس عن الساعة قل إنما علمها عند الله وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

translation: Verily, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and has prepared for them a blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences for those who reject faith in Allah. The term 'curse' signifies divine rejection and exclusion from mercy, while the 'blazing fire' represents severe punishment in the hereafter. This verse serves as a stern warning about the reality of divine justice and the importance of faith.
orig: إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا

translation: Abiding therein forever; they will find no protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment for those in Hell, stating that they will remain there forever. It underscores the absence of any ally or helper for them, indicating complete abandonment and isolation as a result of their actions in life. This highlights the concept of ultimate justice and the consequences of deviating from the path of righteousness.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: On the Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, 'How we wish we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and anguish of those who disobeyed Allah and His Messenger when they face the punishment of Hell. It emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance and prophetic teachings in this life to avoid such torment in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا

translation: And they will say, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our great men, and they led us astray from the [right] way.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret of individuals on the Day of Judgment, acknowledging that they blindly followed their leaders and influential people who misled them. It underscores the importance of personal responsibility and critical thinking in matters of faith and righteousness, rather than placing absolute trust in human authority figures.
orig: وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا

translation: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea to Allah for severe retribution upon those who have caused great harm and misguidance. The supplication for double the punishment signifies a profound sense of injustice and the seriousness of the transgression, while the plea for a significant curse underscores the desire for a decisive, divine repudiation of their actions. It highlights the weight of responsibility and accountability in misguiding others.
orig: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب والعنهم لعنا كبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses; then Allah cleared him of what they said. And he was, in the sight of Allah, honorable.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers not to emulate those who wronged or slandered the prophet Moses. It emphasizes that despite the accusations and harm directed towards him, Allah vindicated Moses, proving his innocence and maintaining his esteemed status before Allah. The lesson here is to avoid unjust behavior, especially against righteous individuals, and to trust that truth and justice will ultimately prevail as ordained by Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين آذوا موسى فبرأه الله مما قالوا وكان عند الله وجيها

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to have consciousness and fear of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of speaking justly and truthfully. The directive to speak words of appropriate justice encompasses honesty, integrity, and fairness in communication, reflecting a broader ethical and moral responsibility in one's speech and interactions with others. This serves as guidance for maintaining just relationships and upholding righteousness in personal and communal dealings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: He will rectify your deeds for you and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Divine promise to reform the deeds and forgive the sins of those who are obedient. It highlights the importance of following both Allah and His Messenger, stating that such obedience leads to significant success. The 'great attainment' refers to the ultimate reward in the Hereafter, indicating that spiritual success is linked to sincere faith and compliance with divine guidance.
orig: يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man undertook to bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of 'Trust' which encompasses responsibilities and obligations bestowed by God. The heavens, the earth, and the mountains symbolize the immense challenges and the gravitas of such a responsibility that even these grand creations perceived as overwhelming.
