However, mankind accepted this Trust, indicative of human potential and free will. It highlights human traits of being unjust and ignorant, suggesting that while humanity has the capacity for great responsibility, it often errs in judgment and ethical integrity. This acceptance signifies the unique position and accountability of human beings in the divine order.
orig: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

translation: That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and women and the polytheist men and women, and that Allah will pardon the believing men and believing women. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse delineates the justice and mercy of Allah. It indicates that those who are hypocrites and those who commit polytheism will face punishment for their actions, reflecting divine justice. Conversely, the verse highlights Allah's capacity for mercy and forgiveness towards those who believe, indicating that sincere repentance and faith lead to divine pardon. It balances the concepts of divine retribution and mercy, emphasizing accountability while also offering hope for redemption to believers.
orig: ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive dominion and sovereignty of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. It underscores that all things, whether in the present world or the Hereafter, are under His control and deserving of praise. The verse emphasizes Allah's wisdom and thorough knowledge of everything, underscoring that His governance is rooted in wisdom and complete awareness of all matters.
orig: الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وله الحمد في الآخرة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends therein; and He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and control over the natural processes and the universe. It highlights His intimate awareness of everything from the smallest acts of nature to the grandest celestial events. Additionally, it underscores His merciful and forgiving nature, offering reassurance of His compassion and grace despite the vastness of His power and knowledge.
orig: يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو الرحيم الغفور

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.' [He is] the Knower of the unseen; not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of disbelievers regarding the coming of the Hour, or the Day of Judgment. It assures them of its certainty, swearing by Allah's name. The verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem. Everything is recorded in a clear register, illustrating the comprehensive and all-encompassing nature of divine knowledge and the inevitability of divine judgment.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's promise to those who have faith and engage in good deeds. It underscores the ultimate rewards of divine forgiveness and generous sustenance that believers will receive in return for their righteousness. The verse aims to motivate individuals to maintain their faith and continue performing virtuous acts, assuring them of Allah's benevolence and the bountiful rewards awaiting them.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: But those who strive against Our verses to frustrate (them) - those will have a painful punishment of foul nature.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals who actively oppose and seek to undermine the signs and revelations of Allah. Their efforts to create obstacles and prevent others from understanding or accepting divine guidance are seen as a serious transgression. Consequently, they are warned of a severe and painful punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the inevitable divine justice they will face.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what was revealed to you from your Lord is the truth and guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition and affirmation of those endowed with knowledge regarding the divine origin of the revelation given to the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes that such individuals see the truth in the message, acknowledging it as guidance from an omnipotent and praiseworthy deity. This serves to reinforce the authenticity and authority of the Qur'anic message, urging believers to trust and follow its guidance.
orig: ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been disintegrated in complete disintegration, you will [then] be [recreated] in a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and mockery of the disbelievers towards the concept of resurrection and life after death. They sarcastically question the validity of a man (the Prophet) who claims that humans will be re-created after being completely disintegrated. The verse showcases their disbelief in the miraculous power of Allah to resurrect and bring forth a new creation from something that had entirely perished.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق إنكم لفي خلق جديد

translation: Has he fabricated a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him? Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far error.
interpretation: This verse challenges the accusations of falsehood and madness directed toward the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that the real issue lies with those who reject belief in the Hereafter. Their denial leads them to a path of significant misguidance and suffering, emphasizing the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith in the Hereafter.
orig: أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

translation: Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the sky and the earth? If We will, We could cause the earth to swallow them, or We could let fall upon them fragments from the sky. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It serves as a warning to those who are heedless of Allah's signs and who reject His message. The reference to the sky and the earth surrounding them signifies the omnipresence and power of Allah, who controls all aspects of existence. The verse warns of the potential consequences—such as the earth swallowing them or fragments falling from the sky—as a demonstration of Allah's control and as a means to urge people to repent and turn back to Allah. The verse concludes by emphasizing that these signs are clear for anyone who is willing to reflect and turn in repentance to Allah.
orig: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماء والأرض إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], 'O mountains, repeat [Our praises] with him, and the birds [as well].' And We made pliable for him iron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favors and blessings bestowed upon Prophet David by God. David was given unique gifts, including the ability to command the mountains and birds to join him in praising God. Additionally, God made iron pliable for David, allowing him to work with it effectively. This verse emphasizes God's power to bestow unique abilities upon His prophets and the honor and assistance provided to them in fulfilling their divine missions.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود منا فضلا يا جبال أوبي معه والطير وألنا له الحديد

translation: Make full coats of mail and measure the links well. And work righteousness. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of diligence, skill, and precision in one's work, specifically in the context of making coats of mail (a form of armor). It also underscores the significance of righteous actions and maintaining integrity in all endeavors, with a reminder that God is always observant of our deeds. The combination of practical work and moral behavior reflects a holistic approach to life, merging craftsmanship with ethical living.
orig: أن اعمل سابغات وقدر في السرد واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [journey was that of] a month - and its afternoon [journey was that of] a month, and We made flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper. And among the jinn were those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever deviated among them from Our command - We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the extraordinary blessings bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, emphasizing his control over the wind and his access to resources like liquid copper. It also highlights the obedience of the jinn to Solomon's command, given by God's permission, and the severe consequences for those who disobey. This underscores the theme of divine authority and the rewards or punishments associated with adherence or deviation from God's commands.
orig: ولسليمان الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر وأسلنا له عين القطر ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه ومن يزغ منهم عن أمرنا نذقه من عذاب السعير

translation: They made for him what he willed: palaces, statues, basins as large as reservoirs, and fixed cauldrons. 'Work, O family of David, in gratitude.' And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and capabilities granted to Prophet Solomon (Sulaiman) by Allah, allowing him to command jinn to create grand constructions and objects. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude for these divine favors. The exhortation to the family of David to work in gratitude serves as a reminder that acknowledging and thanking Allah for His bounties is a form of worship and obedience. The verse concludes with a reflection on the rarity of those who truly embody thankfulness, underscoring the value of recognizing and appreciating Allah's favors.
orig: يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات اعملوا آل داوود شكرا وقليل من عبادي الشكور

translation: Then, when We decreed Solomon’s death, nothing indicated to them that he was dead except a worm from the earth, eating his staff. Thus, when he fell down, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating torment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a lesson in the limits of knowledge, especially concerning the unseen. It highlights the event of Prophet Solomon's death, which went unnoticed by the jinn who served him until a worm gnawed through his staff, causing his body to fall. This exposed the jinns' ignorance of the unseen and underlined that despite their abilities, they cannot possess the all-encompassing knowledge that belongs solely to Allah. The verse admonishes arrogance in one's abilities and emphasizes humility and the recognition of divine wisdom and power.
orig: فلما قضينا عليه الموت ما دلهم على موته إلا دابة الأرض تأكل منسأته فلما خر تبينت الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين

translation: There was, certainly, in the stories of Sheba a sign for their dwelling place: two gardens to the right and to the left. Eat from the provisions of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a forgiving Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon the people of Sheba, emphasizing the fertile land and abundant provisions granted to them by Allah. It serves as a reminder to recognize and appreciate divine bounty, to consume responsibly, and to express gratitude towards the Creator. Moreover, it underscores the harmony between a blessed, prosperous environment ('a good land') and the divine attributes of mercy and forgiveness ('a forgiving Lord'). The prosperity of Sheba is a call to reflection on the importance of gratitude and righteousness in the face of divine blessings.
orig: لقد كان لسبإ في مسكنهم آية جنتان عن يمين وشمال كلوا من رزق ربكم واشكروا له بلدة طيبة ورب غفور

translation: But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their two gardens with gardens of bitter fruit, tamarisks, and something of sparse lote trees.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of people's neglect and disobedience to divine guidance. The 'flood of the dam' symbolizes a destructive force that altered their once prosperous state. The substitution of fruitful gardens with less desirable vegetation signifies a loss of blessings and bounty due to their actions. It serves as a reminder of the impermanent nature of worldly success and the importance of adhering to spiritual and moral principles to maintain divine favor.
orig: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل

translation: That is their recompense for disbelieving and for us not recompensing anyone except the ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice where the punishment or reward is a direct result of one's actions, particularly highlighting disbelief and ingratitude as reasons for receiving negative recompense. It showcases the principle that God's retribution is precise and based on the actions and attitudes of individuals.
orig: ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

translation: And We placed between them and the cities which We had blessed, visible cities, and We determined the stages [of journey] between them: 'Journey between them safely by night or day.'
interpretation: This verse indicates God's provision and planning for human travel and connectivity between blessed cities. The 'visible cities' symbolize that God's blessings and guidance are clear and accessible, ensuring safe and secure travel. It reflects the broader concept of divine support in the daily lives of people, promoting ease and security in their endeavors.
orig: وجعلنا بينهم وبين القرى التي باركنا فيها قرى ظاهرة وقدرنا فيها السير سيروا فيها ليالي وأياما آمنين

translation: And they said, 'Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys,' and they wronged themselves, so We made them as tales and scattered them with a total scattering. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse reflects on a people who, driven by ingratitude and arrogance, asked for increased distances between their journeys, likely desiring more material gain. In their misguided request, they wronged themselves. As a consequence of their actions, they were punished by being turned into mere stories of the past and were dispersed utterly. The verse emphasizes that such outcomes contain lessons and signs for those who practice patience and gratitude, reminding the believers of the importance of humility and thankfulness for the blessings and conveniences provided by God.
orig: فقالوا ربنا باعد بين أسفارنا وظلموا أنفسهم فجعلناهم أحاديث ومزقناهم كل ممزق إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And Iblis (Satan) had already confirmed through them his assumption, so they followed him, except for a group of believers.
interpretation: This verse elucidates the successful deception of Iblis over most of humanity, as he had anticipated their susceptibility to his enticements. It highlights the general disposition of people to follow misleading temptations. However, it also underscores a crucial exception: a distinct group of true believers who resisted and remained steadfast in their faith, not succumbing to Iblis's deception. This implies the rarity and value of true faith and resilience against evil influences.
orig: ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه فاتبعوه إلا فريقا من المؤمنين

translation: And he had no authority over them, except that We might test who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is a Guardian over all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind allowing certain influences or tests in people's lives, specifically mentioning that Satan had no inherent power over people except that it served as a means to distinguish true believers in the Hereafter from those who doubt. This differentiation through trials and challenges ultimately demonstrates one's faith and trust in God's oversight and guardianship over all affairs.
orig: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim [to be gods] besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor is there for Him from among them any assistant.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping or invoking beings other than Allah. It declares that these beings, whether they are idols, deities, or other entities, have no power or control over any aspect of creation, be it in the heavens or the earth. They do not share in Allah's dominion and are incapable of assisting Him in any way. The verse underscores the oneness and absolute sovereignty of Allah, illustrating that no one else deserves worship or reverence.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض وما لهم فيهما من شرك وما له منهم من ظهير

translation: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits, until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they will say [to one another], 'What has your Lord said?' They will say, 'The truth.' And He is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah in granting intercession. It underscores that no one can intercede on behalf of others without Allah’s explicit permission, highlighting His supreme control over matters of judgment and mercy. When the terror is lifted from people's hearts, their immediate focus is on seeking the truth revealed by Allah. This constant search for divine command and the declaration that Allah always speaks the truth reaffirm His exalted status and grandeur as the ultimate Judge and Protector.
orig: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم قالوا ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الحق وهو العلي الكبير

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah. And indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights a rhetorical question that points to Allah as the sole provider of sustenance from the heavens and the earth. It also presents a dichotomy between guidance and error, implying that the truth is evident and that either the believers or the disbelievers are on the right path or clearly astray. The verse encourages self-reflection on one's beliefs and subtly asserts the truth of the monotheistic message by emphasizing divine provision and the stark contrast between the guidance of faith and the misguidance of disbelief.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, 'You will not be asked about our sins, nor shall we be questioned about what you do.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual accountability in matters of faith and actions. It suggests that each person is responsible for their own deeds and will not bear the burden of others' sins. Moreover, it underscores the principle of personal responsibility and the separation of individual actions in the eyes of divine judgment.
orig: قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine judgment and the ultimate gathering of people by God's will. It reassures believers that any disputes or differences will be resolved with absolute justice and knowledge by God, who is the ultimate and all-knowing arbitrator. The verb 'yaf-tah' (يَفْتَحُ) suggests the opening or revealing of truth, reinforcing the concept that true justice will be manifest in the divine judgment.
orig: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم

translation: Say, 'Show me those whom you have attached to Him as partners.' No! Rather, He alone is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of Allah, by challenging those who associate partners with Him. The rhetorical question underlines the futility and falsehood of idolatry. By declaring 'No!', the verse categorically rejects any notion of partnership with Allah, affirming that true might and wisdom belong solely to Him, reinforcing His attributes of being the Most Powerful and the Wise.
orig: قل أروني الذين ألحقتم به شركاء كلا بل هو الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal mission of the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that he was sent to all of humanity with the dual message of glad tidings for those who embrace the faith and warnings for those who reject it. Despite the clarity and comprehensiveness of his message, it highlights a common theme in the Qur'an: most people remain unaware or ignorant of the true significance of his prophethood and the message he brings.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who do not believe in the prophecy. They challenge the believers by questioning the timing of the promised events, insinuating doubt about the truthfulness of the prophecy. It underscores the test of faith and the certainty of divine promises, despite human impatience and skepticism.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'For you is the appointment of a Day [when you can neither] delay it by an hour nor bring it forward.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inalterable and predetermined nature of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that its timing is fixed by divine decree and cannot be hastened or postponed by any human intervention. It reminds us of the inevitability and certainty of this momentous event, urging believers to prepare for it through righteous living and unwavering faith.
orig: قل لكم ميعاد يوم لا تستأخرون عنه ساعة ولا تستقدمون

translation: The disbelievers say, 'We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in what came before it.' But if you could see when the wrongdoers will be made to stand before their Lord, throwing blame at each other. Those who were oppressed will say to the arrogant ones, 'If it were not for you, we would have been believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn refusal of disbelievers to accept the Qur'an and previous revelations. It then shifts to a scene on the Day of Judgment, where the oppressors and the oppressed exchange accusations. The oppressed blame the arrogant leaders for leading them astray, suggesting that their disbelief and wrong actions were heavily influenced by those in positions of power. This moment of mutual recrimination underscores the accountability each individual holds and the profound regret that will be felt by all parties involved for their choices and actions against divine guidance.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لن نؤمن بهذا القرآن ولا بالذي بين يديه ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون عند ربهم يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

translation: Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, 'Was it we who prevented you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals [yourselves].'
interpretation: This verse captures a dialogue between the arrogant leaders and their followers on the Day of Judgment. The powerful individuals, who led their followers astray, deny responsibility and shift the blame back onto their followers, claiming that the followers were already inclined towards wrongdoing. This exchange highlights the theme of personal responsibility and the importance of individual accountability in one's pursuit of truth and righteousness, irrespective of external influences.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم بل كنتم مجرمين

translation: And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, 'Rather, it was [your] conspiracy of night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and attribute to Him equals.' But they will all confide regret when they see the punishment; and We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse highlights a dialogue that will occur on the Day of Judgment between those who were oppressed and those who were arrogant. The oppressed will blame the arrogant for deceiving them and leading them away from faith in Allah. They will mention that it was a continuous plot, day and night, to make them disbelieve and equate others with Allah. Upon seeing the punishment, both groups will feel profound regret. The verse concludes by emphasizing that the disbelievers will face just recompense for their actions, symbolized by the shackles placed on their necks, representing their eventual realization of the consequences of their deeds.
orig: وقال الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا بل مكر الليل والنهار إذ تأمروننا أن نكفر بالله ونجعل له أندادا وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وجعلنا الأغلال في أعناق الذين كفروا هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We did not send into a city any warner except that its affluent said, 'Indeed, we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the common historical reaction of affluent and powerful individuals in societies to the message of prophets and messengers. Despite clear warnings and guidance, those enjoying wealth and status are often resistant to change and in denial of the truth. Their position and comfort lead them to reject the message, fearing the disruption of their societal advantages and the responsibilities that faith would demand. It serves as a reminder of the recurring resistance among the influential when faced with divine guidance, as well as the challenges that prophets have historically encountered in conveying their messages.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And they said, 'We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and false sense of security among some people who believed that their material wealth and numerous offspring would protect them from divine retribution. It emphasizes the mistaken belief that worldly assets are indicators of divine favor and invincibility against Allah’s punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and safety lie in righteous conduct and adherence to divine guidance, not in material prosperity.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. But most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate provider and controller of sustenance. It highlights the divine wisdom and discretion in granting or withholding provision according to His will. Humans, in their limited understanding, often fail to recognize the deeper purpose and wisdom behind the distribution of resources. It serves as a reminder to trust in Allah's plan and justice, and to understand that provision is not solely a result of one's efforts but is also dependent on divine will.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you nearer to Us in position; but it is [by] he who has believed and done righteousness. For them there will be the double reward for what they did, and they will be in the upper chambers [of Paradise], safe [and secure].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that material wealth and offspring do not inherently bring one closer to Allah. It highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds as the true means of spiritual elevation. The verse reassures that those who believe and perform good deeds will be rewarded manifold and will attain a secure and elevated status in the hereafter. The focus is on internal spiritual growth and ethical conduct, rather than external possessions or social status.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: But those who strive against Our signs to frustrate (them) - those will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who actively work against the divine signs and messages. Attempting to defy or invalidate these signs is a direct opposition to the divine will. Consequently, such individuals are assured of facing punishment. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of opposing divine guidance and the importance of adhering to the path prescribed by God.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. But whatever thing you spend [in His cause] - He will compensate it; and He is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the belief that God's wisdom governs the distribution of resources among His servants. It acknowledges that God may expand or constrain sustenance as He wills, reflecting His ultimate authority and knowledge of what is best for each individual. Furthermore, it reassures that any money or resources spent in the way of God will be replenished by Him, emphasizing the concept of divine provision and encouraging generosity and trust in God's sustenance. The phrase 'He is the best of providers' affirms that no one can provide better or more plentifully than God, encouraging believers to rely on Him with confidence.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all and then say to the angels, 'Was it you that these people used to worship?'
interpretation: This verse discusses the Day of Judgment when all beings will be gathered, and Allah will address the angels, questioning them whether they were the ones whom disbelievers falsely worshiped. This emphasizes the futility and error of idolizing anyone or anything other than Allah and highlights the ultimate accountability and clarity that will come on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They will say, 'Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them. In fact, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment in the Hereafter where those who had been misguided confess their error. They acknowledge that Allah alone is the true Protector and disown any entities they had wrongly worshiped or served, specifically noting that many had turned to the jinn for worship, become devoted or influenced by them. This admission highlights the contrast between true faith in Allah and the misguided practices of idolizing or following other beings.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: So today no one can benefit or harm another, and We will say to those who did wrong, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire, which you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment, a time when no one will have the power to help or harm another. It specifically addresses those who have committed injustices, stating that they will be made to experience the punishment of Hell, which they previously dismissed or denied. The verse serves as a reminder of accountability and the inevitable divine justice that awaits those who engage in wrongful acts and disbelief.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, 'This is just a man who wants to turn you away from what your forefathers worshipped.' And they say, 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie.' And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent rejection and skepticism faced by the Prophet Muhammad and his message. The disbelievers accuse him of trying to mislead them away from their ancestral worship traditions, labeling his teachings as mere fabrications and obvious magic. This resistance underscores their unwillingness to accept the divine revelation due to deep-rooted cultural and ideological biases.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We had not given them any scriptures which they could study, nor did We send to them before you, [O Muhammad], any warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people addressed here had neither received any previous divine scriptures nor been sent a prior warner or messenger before Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the novelty and significance of Muhammad's prophethood as a new and distinct revelation to these people, indicating that their prior ignorance of divine guidance is now being addressed through this new message.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: Those before them also denied, and these (pagans) have not attained even a tenth of what We had given them. Yet they rejected My messengers; how (terrible) was My disapproval.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consistent pattern of denial and rejection by those who came before the current generation being addressed. Despite not having received even a fraction of the blessings and signs granted to earlier communities, the current deniers follow the same path of disbelief. It emphasizes that the punishment and disapproval faced by previous communities for their denial serve as a severe warning to those who repeat their mistakes.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, 'I only advise you of one thing: that you stand for Allah, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought.' There is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere contemplation and seeking truth for Allah's sake, both in groups and individually. It addresses any doubts about the sanity of the Prophet Muhammad, reinforcing that he is not possessed but serves as a sincere warner from Allah about impending severe consequences for those who ignore the guidance.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, 'Whatever reward I might have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from Allah, and He is a Witness over all things.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the selflessness of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) mission, clarifying that he does not seek any worldly reward or compensation for conveying God's message. His true recompense is expected solely from Allah, reinforcing the purity and sincerity of his prophetic duty. Additionally, it underlines Allah's omnipresent knowledge and observation, asserting that He is an omniscient witness to all actions and intentions.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord hurls the truth. Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and omniscience of God. It conveys that God asserts the truth with authority and is fully aware of all hidden and unseen matters. It assures believers that divine knowledge encompasses everything, visible and invisible, and thus they should trust in God's wisdom and judgments.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: Say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood neither creates anything new nor restores anything.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the triumph of truth over falsehood. When truth arrives, falsehood is rendered powerless—it cannot initiate any new actions nor can it restore anything it has lost. This signifies the ultimate victory and permanence of truth, aligning with the principle that falsehood is inherently weak and transient while truth is powerful and enduring.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, 'If I go astray, I only stray to the loss of my own soul; but if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. He is All-Hearing, Ever-Near.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility in the matter of divine guidance and misguidance. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to declare that any deviation from the right path is solely his own fault, reflecting the individual's accountability for their actions. Conversely, any guidance he attains is purely a result of divine revelation and not his own doing. It reinforces the proximity of Allah to His servants, highlighting that He is all-hearing and close, aware of their needs and prayers.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: If you could see when they will be terrified, but there will be no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby.
interpretation: This verse is describing a scene from the Day of Judgment, where those who were disbelievers or wrongdoers will be stricken with fear and panic, realizing there is no way to escape the consequences of their actions. Their punishment will come swiftly, as if they are seized from a place very close by, signifying the proximity and inevitability of their fate.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they said, 'We believe in it,' but how for them will be the receiving (of faith) from a distant place?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of belated belief. It suggests that acknowledging faith at a time when it is too late—symbolized by the 'distant place'—holds no real merit or benefit. The verse emphasizes the importance of timely acceptance and understanding, implying that opportunities for sincere faith and repentance should be seized without delay.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: They had already disbelieved in it before, and they cast (doubt) from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who had already rejected the truth of the message prior to its manifestation or arrival. Their skepticism and denial are described metaphorically as casting doubts or accusations from a 'distant place,' indicating not only their physical or intellectual distance from the truth but also the unreasonable nature of their objections. It suggests that their disbelief is not based on genuine inquiry or close examination but rather on preconceived biases or misconceptions.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah describes the fate of those who reject the truth and persist in doubt. When it is too late, a barrier is established between them and their desires - possibly a reference to their missed opportunities for redemption or the pleasures they sought in this world. This scenario mirrors the fate of previous generations who similarly denied the truth. The recurring theme is the consequences of persistent skepticism and unwillingness to believe in the divine message, resulting in eventual regret and separation from their desires.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: All praise belongs to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Maker of the angels as messengers with wings—two, three, or four. He increases in the creation whatever He wills. Indeed, Allah is Powerful over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unmatched power and wisdom of Allah as the Creator of the universe, including the heavens and the earth. It specifically highlights His creation of the angels with varying numbers of wings, symbolizing their diverse roles and capabilities as messengers. The verse also underscores Allah’s absolute authority and ability to enhance His creation in any manner He desires, signifying His omnipotence over all matters.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens up for people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it thereafter. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and wisdom of Allah. It conveys the message that all forms of mercy and blessings are entirely within Allah's control. No one can obstruct the mercy Allah decides to bestow, nor can anyone release it if He chooses to withhold it. This underscores the belief in Allah's absolute authority and His ultimate wisdom in dispensing grace and managing human affairs. The verse encourages reliance on Allah's judgment and fosters a sense of trust in His decisions, affirming that He is all-powerful and all-wise in His governance.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse calls upon all of humanity to reflect on the blessings and provisions they receive, reminding them that there is no other creator or provider besides Allah. It emphasizes the concept of monotheism by questioning people's reasoning when they turn away from Allah, despite the evident signs and sustenance He provides. The verse aims to awaken a sense of gratitude and recognition of Allah's exclusive divinity and beneficence.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: But if they deny you, so were messengers denied before you. And to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by reminding him that previous messengers were also denied by their people. It serves to comfort and fortify him in the face of disbelief and rejection, emphasizing that all affairs ultimately return to Allah for judgment and resolution, establishing a sense of divine justice and sovereignty.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O people, the promise of Allah is true. So do not let the worldly life delude you, and do not be deceived about Allah by the Deceiver.
interpretation: This verse addresses all of humanity, affirming the certainty of Allah’s promise, which often refers to the afterlife, the Day of Judgment, and the reward and punishment that come with it. It serves as a warning against being misled by the temporary pleasures and distractions of the worldly life, which can cause one to forget or neglect the eternal reality. The term ‘Deceiver’ refers to any force, be it Satan or otherwise, that causes individuals to doubt or stray from their faith in Allah and His promises.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: Satan's enmity towards humanity is highlighted, urging believers to recognize and treat him as an adversary. His intentions are destructive, aiming to lead people astray and ultimately to Hellfire. This verse serves as a warning to remain vigilant against his deceptions and to avoid following his misguided path.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the consequences of disbelief and belief. It highlights the severe punishment awaiting those who reject faith and emphasizes the mercy and generous reward that awaits those who are faithful and engage in virtuous deeds. The emphasis is not only on belief but also on the importance of accompanying that belief with righteous actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate justice and mercy of God, encouraging believers to maintain both faith and good conduct.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Is one whose evil deed is made attractive to him so he considers it good [like one rightly guided]? For indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself perish over them in regret. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of having one's wrongdoings appear pleasing in their own eyes, leading them to believe that they are on the right path. It underscores that guidance and misguidance are ultimately determined by Allah's will. The advice not to grieve excessively over others' misguidance serves as a reminder that each person's fate is known to Allah, who is fully aware of their actions. This comforts believers, reaffirming that their primary role is to convey the message and maintain their own righteousness without being overcome by the distress of others' choices.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds. Then We drive them to a dead land and give life to the earth after its lifelessness. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and mercy of Allah by comparing the miracle of reviving dead land with rain to the resurrection of human beings. Just as lifeless earth is rejuvenated with rain, the dead will be resurrected by Allah's command. It emphasizes Allah's control over natural phenomena and establishes an analogy to assure believers of the certainty of resurrection and life after death, highlighting His ability to bring life from seeming emptiness and death.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: If any do seek glory, to Allah belong all glory. To Him ascend all goodly words, and the righteous deeds exalt them. But those who plot evils—for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of such will perish.
interpretation: This verse underscores the belief that ultimate honor and glory belong solely to Allah. It emphasizes that sincere, good words and righteous actions are elevated to Him, illustrating the value of piety and virtue. Conversely, it warns that those who engage in evil schemes will face severe punishment, and their deceitful plans will eventually fail, reflecting the futility of wrongdoing against the divine order.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then He made you mates. And no female conceives nor gives birth except with His knowledge. And no aged person is granted a length of life nor is his lifespan lessened but that it is in a Register. Indeed that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah in the creation and sustenance of life. It highlights the stages of human creation, starting from dust to a sperm-drop, and then forming into pairs as mates. It underscores that every aspect of existence, from conception to aging, is within Allah's knowledge and decree. Nothing happens outside of His will, and everything is recorded in a divine register. This reassures believers of Allah's supreme power and control over all matters, making the seemingly complex processes of life easy for Him.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: The two bodies of water are not alike: one is fresh and sweet, pleasant to drink, and the other salty and bitter. Yet from each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments to wear. And you see the ships plowing through them so that you may seek His bounty and be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in Allah's creation and the different resources provided to humanity. Despite the contrasting nature of fresh and salty waters, both serve valuable purposes for human benefit. Freshwater is pleasant to drink and sustains life, while salty water, despite its bitterness, offers edible seafood and materials for creating ornaments. The sight of ships navigating these waters demonstrates human endeavor and the seeking of Allah's provision. Ultimately, this variety and provision are reasons to invoke gratitude towards Allah for His boundless grace and wisdom in providing for human needs.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. And those whom you invoke other than Him do not possess [as much as] the membrane of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme power over the natural order and celestial bodies, illustrating His control over time through the alternation of night and day. It highlights Allah's sovereignty and contrasts it with the impotence of other entities that people might call upon, pointing out their inability to possess even something as insignificant as the thin membrane over a date seed. This stark comparison serves as a reminder of the futility of idolizing or invoking anyone other than Allah.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: If you call upon them, they cannot hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association. And none can inform you like One Acquainted with all matters.
interpretation: In this verse, it is emphasized that calling upon other entities besides Allah is futile because they cannot hear or respond to the supplications of the people. Even if they could hear, they lack the power to respond. On the Day of Judgment, these entities, which were wrongly associated with Allah, will disassociate themselves from such worshippers and reject any partnership attributed to them. The verse underlines the futility of worshipping anyone other than Allah and asserts that only Allah, who is fully informed and acquainted with all things, can provide the perfect guidance and reality of matters.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inherent dependence of human beings on Allah for their sustenance and well-being. It underscores the idea that all needs, whether physical, spiritual, or emotional, can only be fulfilled by Allah, who is entirely self-sufficient and deserving of all praise. Additionally, it serves as a reminder to remain humble and acknowledge one's neediness in contrast to Allah's absolute richness and generosity.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over creation. It serves as a reminder of human dependency on divine will and the transient nature of human existence. Ultimately, it warns against arrogance and encourages humility, as Allah has the authority to replace any creation according to His will.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and unlimited capability of Allah. Regardless of how difficult or impossible something may seem to human beings, it is not beyond Allah's power to accomplish. It serves as a reminder of His supreme authority and ability over all things.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to carry some of its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and have established prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of individual responsibility in Islam. Each person is accountable for their own actions and cannot transfer their burdens to others, signifying the importance of personal responsibility and moral integrity. The call to those who fear Allah and establish prayer highlights the importance of sincere faith and the practice of obligatory worship in seeking God's guidance and mercy. The act of purification or self-purification is emphasized as a benefit to one's own soul, reinforcing the concept of inner personal development and accountability. Ultimately, all matters return to Allah, indicating the eternal and ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing.
interpretation: This verse draws a metaphorical distinction between those who are spiritually ignorant or heedless ('the blind') and those who possess insight and understanding ('the seeing'). It underscores the disparity in the levels of awareness and perception between individuals, emphasizing the importance of seeking knowledge and enlightenment in one's spiritual journey.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: Nor darkness, nor light
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast and separation between darkness and light, symbolizing the differentiation between falsehood and truth, ignorance and knowledge, disbelief and faith. It suggests that just as darkness and light cannot coexist, similarly truth and falsehood are distinct and opposite to each other.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: Nor the shade nor the heat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between two extremes, illustrating that just as shade and heat are distinctly different and opposites, so too are other aspects and conditions. It may be understood as a metaphor for the stark differences between righteousness and sin, comfort and hardship, or guidance and misguidance. It serves as a reminder that in life, contrasting conditions exist, each with its own unique qualities and consequences.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And not equal are the living and the dead. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse draws a metaphorical distinction between those who are spiritually alive and those who are spiritually dead. The spiritually alive are responsive and receptive to Divine guidance and wisdom, while the spiritually dead are impervious to it, akin to those who are literally dead and buried, unable to hear or respond. The phrase underscores that it is ultimately Allah who grants the capacity to listen and understand His message, beyond the power of any human, including the Prophet, to reach those who are unreceptive.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: You are only a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a messenger whose primary duty is to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to deliver God's message. It underscores the limited scope of his mission, which is to convey the message and admonish, not to compel belief or enforce divine commandments.
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that there had passed within it a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mission of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger sent with the truth to deliver both glad tidings and warnings. It also reinforces the idea that every nation throughout history has received guidance through a messenger or a warner, highlighting the consistent and universal nature of divine guidance across different communities and eras. This continuity underscores the importance of heeding the messages brought by the prophets as part of the divine plan for human guidance and moral accountability.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And if they deny you, so did those before them deny. Their messengers came to them with clear signs, scriptures, and the enlightening book.
interpretation: The verse provides reassurance to Prophet Muhammad by reminding him that denial and rejection by the people is not a new phenomenon. Previous messengers also faced similar resistance and disbelief from their communities despite bringing clear signs and divine scriptures. It implies that opposition to divine guidance is a recurring theme in human history, and it serves as a lesson for the Prophet to remain steadfast and patient in his mission.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how (terrible) was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences faced by those who reject faith and persist in their disbelief. It underscores the power and justice of divine retribution, illustrating that God's punishment for the disbelievers is both inevitable and severe. This admonition encourages believers to reflect on the outcomes of past communities who faced divine wrath due to their denial, leading to a greater sense of accountability and mindfulness in adhering to the tenets of faith.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We produce with it fruits of varying colors? And in the mountains are streaks of white and red, of varying shades, and raven-black.
interpretation: This verse reflects the diverse and intricate signs of Allah’s creation. By describing the different fruits and the varied colors found in nature—from the produce to the mountain ranges—it illustrates the intricate details and beauty in creation, which point towards the power and wisdom of Allah. The diversity in colors and forms is a manifestation of divine creativity and serves as a reminder of the omnipotence and meticulous planning inherent in the natural world. It calls believers to recognize and appreciate these signs as evidence of the divine presence and power in the universe.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among people and moving creatures and grazing livestock are various colors similarly. Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity in creation, highlighting the variety of colors among humans, animals, and livestock. It underscores that true reverence and awe towards Allah arise from knowledge and understanding. The learned and knowledgeable individuals among His servants are those who truly fear and respect Him, recognizing His greatness and authority. The verse concludes by reminding that Allah is both Mighty and Forgiving, indicating His powerful and merciful nature.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, expect a transaction that will never perish.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of those who are devoted to the recitation of the Qur'an, are consistent in their prayers, and are generous in their charity both in private and in public. Their acts of devotion and charity are likened to an investment that guarantees everlasting returns and blessings from Allah, emphasizing the enduring spiritual and eternal benefits of their righteous actions.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: That He may give them their rewards in full and increase them out of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ultimate justice and generosity. It suggests that not only will God reward people fully for their good deeds, but He will also increase that reward from His own bounty. Additionally, it highlights God's qualities of being forgiving towards human shortcomings and appreciative of their efforts, reinforcing the idea that God is both merciful and generous beyond measure.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what came before it. Verily, Allah is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, which has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, is the ultimate truth. It serves as a confirmation of the previous scriptures, validating their fundamental messages and guidance. Additionally, it highlights that Allah has complete knowledge and awareness of His servants' actions and intentions, ensuring that His guidance is perfectly tailored for them.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen from Our servants; among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is what is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God has bestowed the holy scriptures upon those He has specially chosen among His servants. These individuals embody different levels of righteousness and piety: some fall into sin, some strive for moderation, and some excel in doing good deeds by the grace of God. The verse emphasizes the diversity of believers' spiritual states and highlights the immense favor and blessing of being chosen to receive and uphold God's message. It underscores God's mercy and acknowledges the varying capacities of people in their journey towards spiritual excellence.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal paradise promised to the righteous believers, emphasizing the rewards and luxurious adornments they will enjoy. The imagery of gold, pearls, and silk signifies not only the material beauty and comfort of paradise but also the spiritual and moral elevation of those who attain it. The description serves to motivate believers to strive for righteousness and perseverance in their faith, as these rewards symbolize the blessings and eternal happiness awaiting the faithful.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they will say, 'Praise be to Allah who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' gratitude to Allah for alleviating their sufferings and sorrows in this life and the Hereafter. It underscores Allah's attributes as Forgiving and Appreciative, indicating that He not only forgives the sins of His servants but also acknowledges and rewards their good deeds. The expression of praise and thankfulness portrays a deep sense of relief and contentment among the faithful, recognizing that any grief they endured was met with divine compassion and grace.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: Who has settled us in the Home of Eternity out of His bounty. We are not touched therein by any fatigue, nor are we touched therein by any weariness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings and bounties granted by Allah to the believers in the afterlife. It speaks of an eternal abode where God's grace ensures complete comfort and peace, devoid of any form of exhaustion or hardship. It reflects the ultimate reward and a state of eternal contentment and rest for those who have been graced to dwell in paradise.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: But those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell; death will not be decreed for them so they may die, nor will its torment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe punishment for disbelievers, emphasizing that their suffering in Hell will be unending and enduring. It signifies that death as a means of escape will be denied to them, and the torment will persist without any relief. This is portrayed as a just recompense for ingratitude and rejection of faith. The verse underscores the seriousness of disbelief and ingratitude, warning of the consequences of turning away from divine guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they will cry out therein, 'Our Lord, remove us; we will do righteousness—other than what we were doing.' But did We not grant you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember, and the warner had come to you? So taste [the punishment], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pleas of those in Hell who cry out for another chance to do good deeds, different from what they used to do in their worldly life. It stresses that enough time and opportunities were given during their lifetimes to remember and heed the guidance sent to them, including warnings and messengers. The verse emphasizes accountability and the irreversibility of their punishment, highlighting that in their wrongdoing, they had ample opportunity to turn back but chose not to. Now, they must face the consequences without any aid or support.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating His awareness of all hidden aspects of both the heavens and the earth. It further highlights that Allah possesses intimate knowledge of the innermost thoughts and feelings of individuals, underscoring His comprehensive and profound understanding of all matters, both visible and hidden.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: He is the One who made you successors on the earth. So whoever disbelieves, their disbelief will be against them. The disbelief of the disbelievers only increases their Lord's hatred for them. The disbelief of the disbelievers only increases their loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has appointed humans as successors on earth, giving them a responsibility. Those who choose disbelief do so to their own detriment, and their continuous rejection of faith only escalates God’s disapproval and deepens their own spiritual and moral ruin. It underlines the consequences of disbelief and the self-inflicted nature of its harm.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, 'Have you considered your partners whom you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are upon clear evidence from it? No, but the wrongdoers promise each other nothing but delusion.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists by questioning the legitimacy and power of the deities they worship besides Allah. It emphasizes that these so-called partners have neither created anything on earth nor have any participation in the heavens. Moreover, it questions if there is any divine scripture that provides evidence for their worship. The verse then concludes by highlighting that those who engage in such practices are merely misleading each other and living in falsehood, promising nothing but illusion and deceit.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah and His control over the universe. It points out that the stability of the heavens and the earth is solely by Allah’s will, and if it were not for His continuous maintenance, they would cease to exist. This serves as a reminder of Allah's immense power and how dependent the entire creation is on Him. Furthermore, by describing Allah as Forbearing and Forgiving, it highlights His patience and mercy towards His creation despite their faults.
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than any other community. But when a warner came to them, it only increased their aversion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the irony and hypocrisy of those who take solemn oaths by God, claiming that they would follow guidance if it were provided to them. However, when a warner (prophet or messenger) actually appears with the guidance they desired, instead of embracing it, their rejection and aversion only intensify. It highlights the human tendency to resist change and hold on to established beliefs, even when presented with clear evidence or divine intervention.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: Out of arrogance in the land and plotting evil; but the evil plot envelops only the authors of it. So do they expect anything except the way of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change, and you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of arrogance and malicious plotting against others. It underscores that such evil deeds will ultimately backfire on the perpetrators themselves. Additionally, it highlights the constancy of the divine laws, making it clear that the patterns set by Allah in dealing with past communities will not change for anyone. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the unalterable nature of Allah's decrees.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power. And Allah is not to be caused failure by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder for people to ponder over the fate of previous nations who were mightier and more powerful, yet met their downfall due to their disobedience and arrogance. It emphasizes that no matter how strong or advanced a civilization is, nothing can challenge or hinder Allah's will and power. It calls for humility, reflection, and acknowledgment of Allah's supreme knowledge and capability over all things in the universe.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature. But He defers them for a specified term. And when their time comes, then indeed Allah has ever been, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah’s immense mercy and patience, highlighting that if He were to hold people accountable immediately for their wrongs, all living things would be annihilated. Instead, Allah grants respite until a designated time, offering humans the opportunity to repent and amend their ways. Ultimately, this reflects Allah's comprehensive awareness and just oversight over His creation, emphasizing the balance between divine justice and mercy.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: Ya-Sin.
interpretation: This verse consists of the disjointed letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿāt), which are unique letter combinations found at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is not definitively known, and they are considered a part of the Qur'an's miraculous nature. Many scholars believe they underscore the inimitability and divine origin of the Qur'an, serving as a reminder that its complete knowledge is known only to Allah.
orig: يس

translation: By the wise Quran
interpretation: This verse highlights the Quran's intrinsic wisdom and profound teachings. It emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Quran, suggesting that it serves as a guide for moral and ethical conduct, offering wisdom to those who seek knowledge and understanding.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: Indeed, you are among the messengers
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine affirmation of the Prophet Muhammad's status as a legitimate messenger of God. It emphasizes the importance and legitimacy of his prophethood, reassuring both him and the believers of his divinely mandated mission. This validation is crucial for strengthening the faith of his followers and affirming the authenticity of his teachings.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: On a straight path
interpretation: The verse emphasizes guidance towards a clear and righteous path, indicating the significance of adhering to a path that is morally and spiritually upright in Islam. This straight path is often associated with the guidance provided by Allah through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It signifies the true way of living that leads to divine pleasure and ultimate success in the hereafter.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: The revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and attributes of the Qur'an. It indicates that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who possesses the qualities of might and mercy. 'Mighty' (al-'Aziz) suggests Allah's absolute power and authority, while 'Merciful' (ar-Rahim) highlights His compassion and willingness to forgive. Together, these attributes reassure believers of the divine source of their guidance, emphasizing that it comes from One who is both capable of protecting and willing to show mercy.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and so they are heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of sending the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger. It emphasizes the need for divine guidance for those who had not received previous warnings through their ancestors. The mention of 'heedless' indicates their ignorance and lack of awareness about the divine message, necessitating a reminder and call to faith.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: The Word has indeed proved true against most of them, so they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that a majority of people have been destined to reject faith due to their persistent disbelief and stubbornness. It suggests that the divine judgment against them has become inevitable because of their repeated refusal to accept the truth. As a result, they have sealed their hearts against faith, rendering themselves unable to believe.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are up to their chins so their heads are forced up.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and moral constraints placed upon those who reject faith and guidance. The shackles represent their inability to perceive truth or act righteously, resulting in an elevated state of arrogance and heedlessness. Their forced-up heads symbolize their stubbornness and unwillingness to humble themselves or seek the correct path.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون
