translation: And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: This verse signifies the spiritual blindness and obstruction faced by those who reject faith and divine guidance. The barriers symbolize the obstacles to perceiving truth and understanding the message of Islam, indicating that due to their own obstinance and rejection, they are unable to see the path to righteousness and salvation.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: It is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them—they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse signifies the condition of those whose hearts are sealed towards faith. Despite the Prophet’s efforts in delivering the message, their disbelief remains unchanged. It underscores the concept that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and some individuals, due to their stubbornness or other divine reasons, will not accept the message regardless of the warnings given to them.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give them good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the warnings and guidance of the Qur'an will be heeded by those who truly follow its teachings and have a sincere fear of Allah, even though they cannot see Him. It highlights the deep faith required to follow divine guidance without tangible evidence. Moreover, it provides reassurance and optimism by promising such believers not only forgiveness for their shortcomings but also an honorable and generous reward from Allah.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم

translation: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme power over life and death, illustrating His ability to resurrect the dead. It also highlights God's meticulous and comprehensive recording of every individual's actions, both their deeds and their lingering impacts. The verse reassures that nothing escapes God’s knowledge and everything is perfectly kept in a clear register, underlining divine justice and accountability.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And set forth to them an example, the people of the town, when the messengers came to it
interpretation: This verse introduces an allegorical narrative to convey profound lessons. The ‘people of the town’ and ‘the messengers’ reference a historical or hypothetical situation used as a teaching tool. The emphasis is on the reaction of the townspeople to the messengers sent by God. It highlights themes of guidance, divine mission, and the varying human responses to truth and prophecy, calling the audience to reflect on their own reactions to divine messages.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: When We sent to them two apostles, but they denied them both, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, 'Indeed, we are messengers to you.'
interpretation: This verse references the instance when Allah sent two messengers to a community, and despite their clear guidance, the people rejected them. To reinforce the message, Allah sent a third messenger as a sign of support and the importance of the message being delivered. This highlights the persistent compassion and patience of Allah, and the seriousness of the divine message being conveyed to people for their guidance and reform.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They said: 'You are nothing but humans like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed anything. You are only telling lies.'
interpretation: This verse captures the response of disbelievers to the prophets. It reflects their skepticism and denial, emphasizing their refusal to believe that divine revelation could be entrusted to human beings similar to themselves. The disbelievers also reject the idea of any message coming from the Most Merciful, accusing the prophets of fabricating lies. This speaks to the broader human tendency to doubt and discredit what seems unfamiliar or challenges existing beliefs.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord knows that we are indeed sent to you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the firm conviction and confidence of the messengers in their divine mission. By invoking the knowledge of their Lord, they emphasize the authenticity of their message and reaffirm that their role as messengers is divinely sanctioned. It suggests that regardless of doubt or rejection from their audience, their mandate is clear and divinely endorsed.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And our duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the prophets and messengers, highlighting that their primary duty is to deliver the message from God clearly and understandably. It underscores the principle that guidance is in God's control, and the task of the prophets is not to enforce belief but to communicate the divine revelation, leaving the acceptance of the message to the individuals.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, 'We consider you an ill omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you from us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment where the disbelievers are speaking to prophets or righteous individuals, accusing them of being a bad omen or source of bad luck. They threaten them with severe punishment if they do not stop their preaching. The verse highlights the rejection and hostility faced by prophets and their followers from those who oppose their message. It also demonstrates how the truth bearers often confront intimidation and physical threats in their mission to spread divine guidance.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, 'Your bad omen is with yourselves. (Do you call it bad luck) because you are admonished? Nay, but you are a people transgressing all bounds.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the erroneous belief in superstitions and omens. The prophets or messengers respond to their people, highlighting that the misfortunes or perceived bad luck lie within the people's own actions and not due to the admonishments or warnings given by the prophets. The term 'transgressing' signifies that the people are not only rejecting the message but are also engaging in excessive wrongdoing. It's a reminder that omens and superstitions hold no power, and true accountability lies in one's own deeds and attitudes.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, 'O my people, follow the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of individual initiative and urgency in supporting the message of the prophets. The man from the farthest end of the city symbolizes those who, moved by genuine concern and recognition of truth, take immediate and public action even if it means going against the popular sentiment of their community. It underscores the idea that guidance should be accepted and spread, regardless of the challenges or distances involved.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: Follow those who do not ask of you any payment and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse urges people to follow those who guide them towards the right path without seeking any material compensation. The emphasis is on the sincerity and selflessness of true guides or prophets who lead others purely for the sake of their well-being and spiritual growth, rather than for personal gain.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned?
interpretation: This verse reflects a rhetorical question posed by someone who recognizes the profound reasons for worshiping Allah, the Creator. It emphasizes the natural inclination to worship and show gratitude to the one who has fashioned us, acknowledging that ultimately, all beings will return to Him for judgment and recompense. The verse serves as a reminder of the pivotal relationship between the Creator and the created, underlining the inevitability of returning to Him, thus urging acknowledgment and worship of Allah.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

translation: Shall I take other gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah (the Most Merciful) over all matters and the futility of seeking protection or intercession from other deities. It calls into question the logic of idol worship and underscores that only Allah has the power to benefit or harm. The verse serves as a reminder to put one's trust solely in Allah and not rely on other false gods, as they hold no real power or authority.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I am in clear error.
interpretation: This verse could be expressing a moment of self-realization or confession by an individual who acknowledges their deviation from the right path. The phrase emphasizes the clarity and undeniability of the error they are in, highlighting a sense of regret and the need for rectification. It serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of self-reflection and repentance in one's spiritual journey.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the conviction and faith of a believer who has embraced the message of his Lord and calls upon others to heed his words. It demonstrates the courage to declare one's faith openly, even in the face of adversity or disbelief from others. Additionally, it highlights the importance of listening and reflecting upon the truths presented by those who have found faith and are willing to share their experiences and insights with sincerity.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: It was said, 'Enter Paradise.' He said, 'If only my people knew.'
interpretation: This verse speaks to the moment when a righteous individual is granted entry into Paradise. Upon receiving this ultimate reward, the individual expresses a heartfelt wish that their community could be aware of the truth and the consequences of righteous living. It reflects a profound sense of compassion and concern for others, even at the peak of personal triumph.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: Because my Lord has forgiven me and made me of the honored ones.
interpretation: This verse reflects a sense of divine grace and mercy. The speaker recognizes the immense forgiveness granted by their Lord, acknowledging it as a reason for being elevated to a status of honor. It underscores the transformative power of God's forgiveness, which not only absolves the individual of their past sins but also elevates their standing, emphasizing the themes of redemption and the value of divine favor.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and simplicity of God's will. It highlights that God does not need to deploy angelic armies or supernatural forces to carry out His decisions or to bring about consequences for people's actions. The mere command of God is sufficient to enact His will, demonstrating His supreme authority and the ease with which He can execute His plans. It serves as a reminder that the might of God is not reliant on grandiose displays but is inherent in His very command.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: It was but one shout, and suddenly they were extinguished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sudden and decisive nature of divine intervention or punishment. It illustrates how a single command or event from Allah can bring about a complete and instantaneous transformation, in this case, turning people from being alive to dead as if they were extinguished like a flame. It serves as a reminder of the power and authority of Allah over all creation.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: Alas for the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him.
interpretation: This verse expresses a lamentation over the fate of people who consistently reject and ridicule the messengers sent to them by God. It highlights the recurring pattern of human behavior towards divine guidance and underscores the tragedy and regret that accompanies such obstinate rejection. The verse serves as a warning and a call for self-reflection, encouraging individuals to examine their attitudes towards messages of truth and guidance.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, who will never return to them?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of human civilizations and the consequences of ignoring divine guidance. It emphasizes the importance of reflecting on history and recognizing the lessons that come from the downfall of past generations who strayed from the path prescribed by God. The verse seeks to awaken a sense of awareness and accountability, encouraging individuals to heed the messages of the prophets and avoid the mistakes of those who came before them.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us all together.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inescapable Day of Judgment where every individual will be gathered and brought forth to face divine justice. It underscores the concept of accountability, emphasizing that none will be exempt from this gathering and all actions will be brought to light in the presence of Allah.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We give it life and bring forth from it grain, and from it they eat.
interpretation: This verse signifies the miracle of life and resurrection by illustrating how Allah causes the barren land to become fertile and produce sustenance. It highlights Allah's power to bring life from death, serving as a reminder of His ability to resurrect and sustain all creation. It underscores the themes of divine intervention, providence, and the dependence of all beings on Allah's will and mercy.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused springs to gush forth within them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine benevolence and power of God in creating abundant natural resources and beautiful landscapes for human benefit. The gardens of palm trees and grapevines symbolize sustenance and prosperity, while the springs represent the nurturing and life-giving aspects of God's creation. It serves as a reminder of the blessings provided by God and the importance of acknowledging and being grateful for these provisions.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: That they may eat from its fruit. And their hands did not make it. Will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and bounties provided by Allah, emphasizing that the fruits they consume are not solely a product of human labor but a divine gift. It calls for gratitude and acknowledgment of Allah's provision and mercy.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: Glory be to Him who created all the pairs from what the earth produces and from themselves and from things they do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and boundless creativity of Allah. It emphasizes that every aspect of creation, from the vegetation of the earth to the beings themselves and even unknown entities, is a result of Allah’s divine craftsmanship. This serves as a reminder of the intricate and diverse nature of life, all originating from a single, deliberate act of creation by Allah. Furthermore, the verse invokes humility and awe in believers, urging them to recognize and appreciate the vastness of Allah's knowledge and power that transcends human understanding.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And a sign for them is the night; We remove from it the [light of] day, so they are [left] in darkness.
interpretation: This verse points to the natural phenomenon of day and night as a sign of Allah's power and control over the universe. The transitioning from day to night is depicted as an act of divine will, emphasizing the miraculous nature of such daily occurrences that humans often take for granted. It serves as a reminder of the omnipotence of Allah and the intricate balance and order He maintains in the cosmos.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term (appointed). That is the Decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the precise and unerring nature of the universe’s order as established by Allah. The movement of the sun on its specific trajectory, and the predetermined duration of this path, reflect the immense wisdom and power of Allah. It suggests that everything in the cosmos operates under divine control and follows a meticulous plan ordained by the All-Mighty and All-Knowing Creator. This emphasizes God's supreme authority and knowledge over all creation.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns like the old date stalk.
interpretation: This verse highlights the systematic and deliberate order in the creation of celestial bodies, particularly the moon. The mention of the moon's phases underscores the precision and regularity in the natural world ordained by Allah. The comparison to an old date stalk serves to illustrate the cyclic nature and continuous renewal inherent in the moon's journey, pointing towards the deeper wisdom and authority of the Creator in maintaining the balance and function of the universe.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the order and precision in the universe as established by Allah. It highlights that celestial bodies like the sun and moon follow preordained paths and schedules, maintaining the balance of day and night. This natural order underscores the divine wisdom and power of the Creator, reminding humans of the meticulous design and regulation present in the cosmos.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and omniscience by referencing a historical event where He safeguarded past generations (likely referring to Noah's Ark). It's meant to remind the listeners of God's continuous guidance and protection, reinforcing the importance of being grateful and obedient to Him. The 'laden ship' signifies the means of survival and deliverance provided by God amidst calamities.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We created for them from the likes of it that which they ride.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's provision and mercy by highlighting that He has created various means of transportation for humanity. Just as God provided the ships for people to ride on water, He also created other forms of transportation (such as animals and later inventions like vehicles) that people use for their journeys on land. It underscores the divine care in facilitating human movement and trade, emphasizing that all such benefits originate from God's creativity and generosity.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And if We will, We could drown them; then no one responding to a cry would there be for them, nor would they be saved
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all creation. It highlights the vulnerability and dependence of human beings on divine mercy. The notion of drowning represents someone's helpless situation, implying that without Allah's protection and intervention, no external help can prevent the fate decreed by Him. It serves as a reminder to maintain piety, recognize one's fragility, and depend on divine will.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: Except as a mercy from Us and provision for a time.
interpretation: This verse signifies that any respite or sustenance provided to people, despite their transgressions, is a manifestation of Allah's mercy. It underscores that such provisions are temporal and serve as a test or opportunity for individuals to return to righteousness before their final judgment.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Beware of what is before you and what is behind you; perhaps you will receive mercy.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers, urging them to be mindful of the consequences of their actions both in the present and the past. It serves as a warning that their current and past behaviors could lead to divine retribution, but also extends an offer of mercy if they heed the warning and change their ways. The verse emphasizes the importance of self-awareness and repentance to attain Allah's mercy.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: No sign comes to them from their Lord, except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent attitude of denial and heedlessness exhibited by some people towards the signs and revelations sent by God. Despite the clear and evident signs from their Lord, they consistently reject and ignore them. This behavior indicates a conscious choice to turn away from divine guidance, reflecting a deeper level of spiritual obstinacy and ingratitude.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Spend from what God has provided for you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed those whom, if God had willed, He would have fed? You are only in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who reject faith when asked to give charity. They argue that if God had wanted to provide for the needy, He would have done so Himself, using this reasoning to justify their unwillingness to help others. It reveals their misunderstanding and misuse of divine will as an excuse for their lack of compassion and responsibility towards their fellow human beings. Their response is characterized as a clear deviation from the moral and ethical principles that faith advocates.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of disbelievers regarding the fulfillment of divine promises, particularly the Day of Judgment. They challenge the believers and the Prophet with sarcasm, questioning when this promised event will occur if the believers are indeed truthful. It showcases their lack of faith and their demand for immediate proof of unseen events which, according to Islamic teachings, are known only to God and will occur at a divinely appointed time.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They are not awaiting except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of the final judgment. It serves as a warning that the Day of Judgment will come unexpectedly while people are engaged in their daily disputes and distractions. The imagery of a single blast suggests the power and decisiveness of God's command, leaving no time for repentance or escape.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: Then they will not be able to make any bequest, nor will they return to their families.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sudden, unexpected nature of the final moment of life and the Day of Judgment. People will not have the opportunity to communicate their last wishes or return to their loved ones. It underscores the importance of living a life of righteousness and preparedness, as the end can come without warning.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown; then at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection when the Trumpet is blown, signifying the end of the world and the beginning of the afterlife. It describes the sudden and immediate resurrection of the dead from their graves, hastening towards their Lord for judgment. This event underscores the suddenness and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the power and control of Allah over all creation and the certainty of accountability for one's actions.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the realization and regret of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. Upon being resurrected from their graves, they express their distress and astonishment, recognizing that the promises of Allah and the warnings of His messengers about the Day of Judgment were indeed true. Their exclamation reflects a mixture of disbelief, fear, and acknowledgment of the truth they had previously denied or ignored.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: It was but one cry, and behold, they were all brought before Us.
interpretation: This verse underscores the swiftness and decisiveness of God's command. The 'one cry' signifies the ease with which God can bring about the resurrection or any significant event. It implies that all of humanity will be gathered before God in an instant, emphasizing His absolute power and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment where everyone will be held accountable.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: So today no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate justice of the Day of Judgment, where every individual will receive exactly what they deserve based on their actions. It serves as a reminder that no injustice will occur and that recompense will be precisely aligned with one's deeds. It's an affirmation of divine fairness and accountability, encouraging believers to act righteously in their lives.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in [joyful] occupation -
interpretation: This verse describes the pure joy and contentment experienced by the inhabitants of Paradise. On that Day, they will be engrossed in delightful activities. This indicates a state of eternal satisfaction and pleasure, free from worry or sorrow, symbolizing the ultimate reward for their righteous deeds in this world.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: They and their spouses, in shade, reclining on thrones.
interpretation: This verse paints a picture of the eternal bliss and comfort that awaits the righteous in paradise. It emphasizes both the physical comfort and the companionship they will enjoy. The shade signifies protection and peace, while reclining on thrones symbolizes honor, relaxation, and a life free from the trials and toils of the earthly existence.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: There they will have fruit, and whatever they ask for will be granted to them.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards that the righteous will receive in Jannah (Paradise). They will enjoy an abundance of fruits and have every desire fulfilled. It signifies the bountiful and generous nature of the rewards given to those who have led a virtuous life, emphasizing the endless joy and satisfaction they will experience.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound declaration of peace from Allah, the Most Merciful, to the righteous. It implies a promise of divine tranquility and reassurance, signifying Allah's compassion and mercy towards His servants. The expression embodies the ultimate serenity and contentment granted by the Creator.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: But stand apart today, you criminals!
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers and wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, commanding them to separate themselves from the righteous. It underscores the divine justice that will be served, where the evildoers will be distinctly segregated from the believers to face their punishment.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity about the covenant made with God to avoid the worship of Satan, who is recognized as a clear and manifest enemy to mankind. The verse emphasizes the explicit command and the clarity of Satan's enmity, stressing the importance of adhering to God’s guidance and staying away from deceptive practices that lead away from the truth and righteousness.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And that you worship Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental Islamic concept that the worship of Allah alone is the correct and righteous path in life. It underscores monotheism and directs believers to follow the path of worship and obedience to Allah, which leads to righteousness and avoids deviations and misguidance.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, he led astray from among you a great multitude. Then did you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse addresses the reality that many individuals have been led away from the righteous path by harmful influences or temptations. It challenges the listener to reflect on their own discernment and wisdom, implying that proper reasoning and consciousness could have prevented one from being led astray. It underscores the importance of awareness and rational thinking in spiritual and moral matters.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is Hell, which you were promised.
interpretation: In this verse, the Qur'an issues a stark reminder of the consequences of disobedience and disbelief. It emphasizes the reality and inevitability of Hell for those who were warned but chose to ignore the guidance and commandments of Allah. This serves as both a warning to the disbelievers and a reinforcement for believers to adhere to their faith and righteousness.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: Taste you (this Day) for that you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse addresses disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, conveying a direct consequence of their disbelief. It implies that their denial of the truth has led them to this moment of punishment. The verse emphasizes accountability and the unavoidable result of one's actions, illustrating the principle of divine justice.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: On this day We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse underscores a scene from the Day of Judgment where human faculties themselves will bear witness to one's deeds. Despite attempts at denial or justification, physical actions represented by hands and feet will speak the truth about an individual's conduct. It emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and the comprehensive nature of divine justice, where even one's own body becomes a testament to their actions.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes; then they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see?
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute power and authority of Allah. It suggests that if Allah willed, He could take away people's ability to see, thereby rendering them incapable of finding the right path. This serves as a warning to mankind to be mindful of their actions and to recognize the blessings, including their sensory abilities, as gifts from Allah. It emphasizes human dependence on divine mercy and guidance to stay on the correct path.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places; then they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and will of Allah. It highlights that if Allah had wished, He could have altered the very state of disbelievers, rendering them immobile and unable to progress or return. This serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the extent of divine authority over creation. It aims to instill awareness of dependence on Allah's will and a reminder of the consequences of straying from righteous guidance.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And he to whom We grant long life We reverse in nature; will they not then understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural process of aging that Allah has decreed for human beings. It signifies the physical and sometimes mental decline that comes with old age, reminding people of their mortality. The verse serves as an admonition for humans to reflect on their lives, the temporal nature of worldly existence, and to understand the signs of divine wisdom and power in creation. It encourages self-awareness and contemplation on the ultimate fate of humankind and the life hereafter.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it appropriate for him. This is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not a poet and the Qur'an is not a product of poetic imagination. Instead, it is a divine revelation meant to remind and guide humanity. The verse highlights the distinct nature of the Qur'an as a clear and articulate message from God, differentiating it from human literary expressions.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: To warn whoever is alive and fulfill the word against the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur’an serves as a reminder and a warning specifically directed at those who are spiritually alive, i.e., those who are receptive to its message. It also highlights the inevitability of Allah's judgment against those who persist in disbelief, emphasizing the dual role of the Qur'an as both a guide and a final testament to the truth of Allah's promises and warnings.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: Do they not see that We have created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the blessings of creation, specifically the cattle that serve multiple purposes in human life. It emphasizes God's sole authorship in creating these animals, highlighting human ownership and benefit as a direct favor from God. The verse encourages gratitude and acknowledgment of God’s providence and the intricate design and mercy embedded in the sustenance provided to humanity.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We tamed them for them, so some of them they ride, and some they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions granted by Allah to humankind. It emphasizes that animals have been subdued for human use, serving both as a means of transportation and as a source of nourishment. This illustrates the divine wisdom and mercy in creating resources beneficial for human life, fostering a sense of gratitude and responsible stewardship towards these blessings.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And for them therein are [other] benefits and drinks, so will they not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the various bounties and resources provided to humans for their use and enjoyment. It calls attention to the inherent benefits and sustenance (in the form of drinks) available, urging humankind to reflect on these blessings and express gratitude. The rhetorical question at the end underscores the expectation of thankfulness and acknowledgment of divine providence as a natural response to the abundance provided.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken gods other than Allah, that they might be helped.
interpretation: This verse addresses the misguided actions of people who, instead of putting their trust and faith in Allah, resort to worshipping other deities in the hopes that these false gods will provide them with support and protection. It highlights the futility and error of seeking help and reliance on anything or anyone other than Allah, emphasizing the oneness and supreme power of Allah as the ultimate provider and helper.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: They cannot help them, though they will be brought forth as soldiers in their defense.
interpretation: This verse indicates the futility of relying on false deities or idols for help. Despite the fact that these deities are depicted as if they have armies and can offer protection, in reality, they are powerless and unable to provide any support. The verse underscores the importance of turning to Allah alone for aid and guidance, implying that only genuine faith and reliance on God can result in true assistance and salvation.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: So do not be distressed by what they say. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse offers reassurance and comfort to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to the believers. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of both the hidden and open aspects of people's actions and thoughts. This serves as a reminder that divine knowledge encompasses everything, providing solace that one need not be troubled by others' words or deeds, as Allah's awareness and justice are all-encompassing.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: Did man not see that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then, behold, he is a manifest adversary.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble beginnings of human life, starting from a mere sperm-drop, which is a reminder of human vulnerability and dependency on divine creation. It also highlights the irony of man becoming argumentative and confrontational despite his origins, suggesting a misplaced sense of pride and challenging human tendency to forget their true nature and dependency on God.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, 'Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?'
interpretation: This verse addresses human skepticism regarding the resurrection and the power of Allah. It highlights the contradiction in questioning Allah's ability to resurrect the dead when one overlooks the fact that human creation itself is a sign of His power. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah’s omnipotence and the certainty of resurrection, encouraging believers to trust in His capabilities.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, 'He will give life to them who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse asserts the power and knowledge of Allah, emphasizing His ability to resurrect the dead just as He created them initially. It reassures believers of Allah's omnipotence and comprehensive awareness of His creation, reminding them that resurrection is within His limitless capability.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: He who made for you from the green tree, fire, and then you ignite from it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's power and wisdom in creating diverse elements that serve humanity in surprising ways. It emphasizes the miraculous transformation of green, living trees into fuel for fire, symbolizing the potential within nature and the divine capability to bring forth benefits that might not be immediately apparent. It also underscores the interconnectedness and interdependence of creation, where elements seen as opposites—like green trees and fire—are parts of a harmonious system designed by God.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and capability of Allah as the Creator. It is a rhetorical question that asserts Allah's ability to create anything, including a recreation of what already exists. The mention of Allah being 'the Knowing Creator' further highlights His wisdom and comprehensive knowledge in His creative powers. This verse invites believers to reflect on the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, reinforcing their faith in His supreme control over all creation.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and effortless power of Allah's will. It highlights that Allah's command is both immediate and deterministic; when He wishes for something to occur, it simply happens by His command 'Be,' and it comes into existence. This powerful testament speaks to the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah over all creation, underscoring the ease with which divine will is executed.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: So glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority and control of Allah over all creation, emphasizing His unrivaled sovereignty. It serves as a reminder of the eventual return to Allah for judgment and accountability, underscoring the transient nature of worldly life and the ultimate reality of divine governance and afterlife.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: By those [angels] lined up in rows
interpretation: This verse invokes the image of angels who stand in disciplined ranks, ready to execute God's commands. It implies the order, unity, and purpose among the angels, serving as a divine example of how believers should act in their devotion and duties. The alignment in rows symbolizes harmony and collective action in fulfilling divine will.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: And those who drive (the clouds) forcefully
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are tasked with driving the clouds or directing the winds. It emphasizes the might and discipline of these divine messengers as they fulfill their duties according to Allah's commands. This highlights the order and control within the divine system, pointing to the greater order and power of Allah over the universe.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: And those who recite the message,
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels or beings who continuously recite the divine messages and revelations of Allah. It highlights the importance and reverence of remembering and recounting the sacred scriptures, emphasizing the role of such beings in spreading and preserving divine guidance.
orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid, which is the oneness of God. It serves as a fundamental principle in Islam, affirming that there is no other deity besides Allah. This oneness underscores the importance of recognizing and worshipping a single, indivisible creator who is sovereign over all creation. It calls the believers to focus their devotion, faith, and obedience solely on Allah, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the sunrises.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive sovereignty and dominion of Allah over the entire cosmos. By referring to Allah as the 'Lord of the heavens and the earth,' it underscores His control over all celestial bodies and terrestrial entities. The mention of 'whatever is between them' highlights His governance over the intermediary space, including everything within the universe. Lastly, referring to Allah as the 'Lord of the sunrises' signifies His authority over natural phenomena and the cycles of time, indicating that every aspect of creation operates under His divine command.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and artistic majesty in creating and adorning the heavens. The stars are described as a form of decoration, emphasizing their beauty and the divinely ordered cosmos. This serves to remind humans of the splendor and perfection of God's creation, encouraging them to reflect on the greater wisdom and power behind the universe.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And as protection from every rebellious devil
interpretation: This verse highlights the protection granted by Allah against malevolent forces, specifically unruly and defiant devils. It signifies that the divine arrangement of the universe provides security and safeguards believers from harm caused by these evil entities, underscoring Allah's supreme power and mercy.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: They cannot listen to the exalted assembly (of angels) and are pelted from every side,
interpretation: This verse speaks about the efforts to prevent malicious entities, such as devils, from eavesdropping on the conversations of the higher assembly of angels. They are driven away and repelled from all directions, highlighting the protection and sanctity of divine knowledge and decrees from evil interference.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: Rejected, and for them is a perpetual punishment.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine rejection and continuous punishment awaiting those who persist in disbelief and opposition to the truth. The term 'dahooran' implies being driven away or repelled, indicating that these individuals are cast out from God’s mercy. The 'perpetual punishment' (عذاب واصب) underscores the enduring and relentless nature of the suffering they will face, emphasizing the serious consequences of their actions and the justice of divine retribution.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except one who snatches [some words] by theft, but they are pursued by a burning flame, piercing [in brightness].
interpretation: This verse refers to the jinn who attempt to eavesdrop on the higher realms to steal information. Despite their efforts, they are swiftly met with a scorching, piercing flame that prevents them from obtaining and spreading such knowledge. This symbolizes divine protection of sacred wisdom and the futility of those who seek it through illicit means.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: So ask them, 'Are they harder to create, or those We created?' Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah challenges people by asking rhetorically whether the creation of humans is more difficult than the creation of other entities. By reminding them that they were created from sticky clay, it emphasizes the power and capability of Allah in creation, urging humans to recognize their origins and the might of their Creator.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: But you are amazed while they mock.
interpretation: This verse addresses the reactions of disbelievers to the truth of the message being conveyed. While the Prophet (and believers) marvel at the divine signs and revelations, the disbelievers dismiss such wonders and respond with ridicule. This highlights the differing attitudes towards faith and the challenges faced in calling people towards the path of righteousness.
orig: بل عجبت ويسخرون

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are heedless and ignore the reminders about the signs and commandments of Allah. It highlights a state of spiritual negligence where individuals fail to reflect on or act upon the guidance provided to them, illustrating a resistance or indifference to spiritual and moral accountability.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they see a sign, they ridicule.
interpretation: This verse addresses the reaction of those who, upon witnessing the signs and proofs of Allah's existence and power, choose to mock and belittle them instead of taking heed. Their ridicule reflects a deeper resistance to accepting the truth and guidance presented to them. It highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of individuals who dismiss divine signs despite clear evidence, signifying a broader theme of rejection and disbelief in the face of divine revelation.
orig: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون

translation: And they said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the reaction of the disbelievers who dismiss the miraculous signs and divine revelations brought by the Prophet as mere sorcery. Their response denotes not only a denial of the divine message but also a deep-seated resistance to accepting the truth, often resorting to labeling it as magic to undermine its legitimacy and influence.
orig: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: When we are dead and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who doubt the resurrection after death. It highlights a common rhetorical question posed by non-believers, reflecting their incredulity at the concept of being brought back to life after their physical bodies have decayed and turned to dust and bones. The verse serves to challenge these doubts and affirm the possibility of resurrection, emphasizing the power of the divine to recreate life in any form.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse is part of a broader discourse on the skepticism of disbelievers regarding the resurrection. Here, it refers to the questioning attitude of the disbelievers who find it hard to believe that their ancestors, who have long passed away, could be resurrected. This skepticism reflects their doubts about the power and promise of God to resurrect the dead, a key theme in the Qur'an's teachings about the afterlife and divine justice.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say: Yes, and you shall be utterly humbled.
interpretation: This verse, directed to the Prophet Muhammad, serves as a divine assertion of the ultimate power and authority of God. Regardless of human disobedience or arrogance, the final outcome will be complete submission and humility before God. It underscores the inescapable nature of God's will and the futility of resisting divine decree.
orig: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون

translation: It will be only one shout, and at once they will be observing.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the suddenness and inevitability of the Day of Judgment. The 'one shout' signifies a powerful, divine command that will instantly bring people back to life, witnessing the reality of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the swiftness and the certainty of this event, leaving no room for delay or escape.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون

translation: And they say, 'Oh, woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense.'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment of profound realization and regret for those who have rejected faith and righteousness when confronted with the reality of the Day of Judgment. The exclamation 'Oh, woe to us!' signifies their despair and recognition of the impending punishment and accountability that they can no longer escape from. It highlights the ultimate justice and the inevitable consequences of one's actions that are embodied in the Day of Recompense.
orig: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين

translation: This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Day of Judgment, a significant event in Islamic belief where all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds. The term 'الفصل' (al-fasl) implies a decisive separation, marking a clear distinction between truth and falsehood, believers and disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the reality of this day, emphasizing its inevitability and the importance of being mindful and prepared for the final judgment.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Assemble those who did wrong, along with their mates and what they used to worship
interpretation: This verse discusses the gathering of wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, indicating that they will be brought forth with their counterparts or similar wrongdoers and the false gods or idols they worshipped. It underscores the divine judgment that awaits those who committed injustices and engaged in idolatry, emphasizing accountability and the ultimate separation based on their actions and beliefs.
orig: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون

translation: Instead of Allah, lead them to the path of Hell.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of following guides or deities other than Allah. It emphasizes that such misguidance will ultimately lead to a path of suffering and torment in Hell. The verse serves as a stern warning to remain steadfast in the worship and guidance of Allah alone.
orig: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم

translation: And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.
interpretation: This verse reflects the scene of judgment where individuals are brought to account for their actions. It indicates that no one can bypass scrutiny or avoid responsibility for their deeds. The angels or guardians are commanded to halt people to ensure that they face questioning, emphasizing the comprehensive and inevitable nature of divine justice.
orig: وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون

translation: What is [wrong] with you that you do not help each other?
interpretation: This verse is directed towards those who fail to support one another in the face of wrongdoings or trials. It emphasizes the importance of mutual assistance and solidarity within the community. The underlying message is a call to collective responsibility and unity, urging people not to remain passive or indifferent when others are in need of help or when justice is at stake.
orig: ما لكم لا تناصرون

translation: But today they are in submission.
interpretation: This verse indicates a state of surrender or acceptance towards a current situation, often related to the consequences of one's actions. It reflects the notion that, despite previous attitudes or behaviors, individuals reach a point of acknowledgment and passivity in the face of inevitable outcomes.
orig: بل هم اليوم مستسلمون

translation: And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other.
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene where individuals converse with each other, reflecting on their past actions and decisions. It indicates a moment of self-assessment and mutual questioning, suggesting a time of reckoning where people seek to understand their experiences and outcomes through dialogue. This could be interpreted as a part of the events in the Hereafter, where people discuss their earthly lives and the consequences they face, providing a moment of mutual reflection and insight.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They will say, 'Indeed, you used to come at us from the right.'
interpretation: In this context, 'coming from the right' signifies approaching with righteous or seemingly convincing arguments and influence. This verse highlights how people reflect on those who misled them by presenting deceit disguised as virtue. It serves as a reminder to be vigilant against those who cloak harmful intentions with the appearance of truth and goodness.
orig: قالوا إنكم كنتم تأتوننا عن اليمين

translation: They said, 'No! But you were not believers.'
interpretation: This verse addresses a dialogue, likely involving a denial or rebuttal from one group to another. It underscores the importance of true faith and the assertion that mere claims to belief without genuine faith are not sufficient. It challenges the authenticity and integrity of one's iman (faith), highlighting the constant scrutiny and introspection required to be true believers in the sight of Allah.
orig: قالوا بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And we had no authority over you, but you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the idea of personal accountability and the nature of unjust actions. It suggests that no external force had control over the individuals; rather, their own propensity towards transgression led them to their actions. It highlights the importance of personal responsibility in one's moral and ethical conduct.
orig: وما كان لنا عليكم من سلطان بل كنتم قوما طاغين

translation: Then the Word of our Lord has been proven true against us; indeed, we will taste [the punishment].
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization and acceptance of the inevitable consequence of one's actions, as decreed by God. The individuals acknowledge that what their Lord has foretold will inevitably come to pass, and they are now resigned to experiencing the repercussions of their deeds, which in this context, indicates tasting the punishment.
orig: فحق علينا قول ربنا إنا لذائقون

translation: So we misled you, for indeed we were [ourselves] deviators.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the influence of misguidance by those who were already astray, indicating that deviation begets further deviation. It reflects an admission of collective responsibility and the perpetuation of misguided paths, emphasizing the cyclical nature of misguidance where those who are deviated lead others astray too.
orig: فأغويناكم إنا كنا غاوين

translation: Indeed, they on that Day will be sharing in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the notion of shared accountability and collective suffering in the Hereafter. It underscores the idea that those who have committed wrongdoings will face the consequences together, indicating a collective responsibility and a shared experience of divine retribution.
orig: فإنهم يومئذ في العذاب مشتركون

translation: Indeed, thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that God's justice includes the appropriate punishment of wrongdoers. It underscores the moral order established by God, where those who commit crimes and engage in immoral behavior will inevitably face consequences. The punishment meted out is not arbitrary but is in accordance with divine justice and wisdom.
orig: إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: Indeed, they used to become arrogant whenever it was said to them, 'There is no deity except Allah.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject the message of monotheism. Despite the clear and straightforward truth of 'There is no deity except Allah,' their pride prevents them from accepting it. This arrogance stems from a sense of superiority or stubborn attachment to their own beliefs and traditions, highlighting a profound resistance to submitting to the will of Allah.
orig: إنهم كانوا إذا قيل لهم لا إله إلا الله يستكبرون

translation: And they say, 'Shall we indeed leave our gods for a mad poet?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the disdain and mockery directed towards the Prophet Muhammad by disbelievers. They dismiss his call to monotheism by deriding him as a poet afflicted by madness, thereby justifying their attachment to their traditional deities. The verse captures their unwillingness to abandon familiar idols in favor of the monotheistic message he brought, highlighting the societal and psychological resistance to his teachings.
orig: ويقولون أئنا لتاركو آلهتنا لشاعر مجنون

translation: Yet he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad in bringing forth the truth—divine knowledge and guidance— and in affirming the messages of the previous prophets. It underscores the continuity of the divine message throughout time, establishing the credibility and validity of Prophet Muhammad in the lineage of messengers sent by Allah. The emphasis is on the truthfulness of his message and the confirmation that he, like the prophets before him, is a legitimate conveyor of God's will.
orig: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

translation: You will surely taste the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks directly about the certainty and inevitability of experiencing severe punishment. It serves both as a warning and a statement of consequence for actions that go against divine commandments. The emphasis on 'tasting' the punishment adds a layer of vividness, suggesting that the experience will be both intense and unavoidable for those who have committed wrongs.
orig: إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم

translation: And you will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual accountability in Islam. It conveys that each person will be judged and compensated strictly based on their own actions and deeds. It reinforces the idea of personal responsibility and the fairness of divine justice, where no one will bear the burden of another's actions, and each will receive what they have earned, whether good or bad.
orig: وما تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse distinguishes the sincere and devoted servants of Allah, emphasizing that they are excluded from the negative fates or consequences faced by others. It highlights the special status and protection granted to those who are truly devoted and sincere in their worship and service to Allah.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: Those will have a known provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there is a specific and predetermined sustenance allocated for certain individuals. It underscores God's omniscience and perfect planning in providing for His creation. The certainty of this provision highlights divine order and justice, reassuring believers of God's care and meticulous attention to their needs.
orig: أولئك لهم رزق معلوم

translation: Fruits; and they shall be honored.
interpretation: This verse highlights the bountiful rewards and the high status that await the righteous in the afterlife, emphasizing the provision of an abundance of fruits as symbols of divine grace and the honor bestowed upon them in paradise.
orig: فواكه وهم مكرمون

translation: In the Gardens of Delight
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal and blissful paradise that the righteous and pious will be rewarded with in the afterlife. It symbolizes a place of ultimate happiness, tranquility, and abundant blessings prepared by Allah for those who have lived their lives according to His guidance.
orig: في جنات النعيم

translation: On thrones facing each other,
interpretation: This verse describes the believers in Paradise, highlighting the sense of equality, brotherhood, and social harmony that will exist among them. They will be seated on thrones, facing one another, signifying mutual respect, a communal atmosphere, and a state of eternal comfort and companionship.
orig: على سرر متقابلين

translation: They will be served a cup from a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene from the afterlife in Paradise. It highlights the luxurious and eternal bliss awaiting the believers, where they will be served with a fresh, unending supply of drinks from a pure and pristine source. The imagery suggests not just physical refreshment but also spiritual satisfaction and joy.
orig: يطاف عليهم بكأس من معين

translation: White, delicious to the drinkers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the pure and enjoyable nature of the drinks provided in Paradise. These drinks are described as ‘white’ to emphasize their purity and perfection, and they are a source of delight for those who drink them, reflecting the ultimate reward and satisfaction awaiting the righteous in the afterlife.
orig: بيضاء لذة للشاربين

translation: It [Wine] will not cause them intoxication nor will they be exhausted by it.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the wine of Paradise, which is different from the wine of this world. Unlike worldly wine, which can cause intoxication and lead to negative effects such as a loss of control and physical discomfort, the wine in Paradise is pure and free from harm. It provides pleasure without the drawbacks, indicating a state of bliss and comfort granted to the inhabitants of Paradise.
orig: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون

translation: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, with large, [beautiful] eyes
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings that await the righteous in the afterlife, specifically mentioning the presence of pure companions who are modest and chaste. It signifies the exclusive and devoted nature of these companions, emphasizing their beauty and the serenity of the eternal reward prepared for the faithful.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف عين

translation: As if they were delicate eggs well protected.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of 'delicate eggs well protected' to describe the purity, beauty, and pristine nature of something or someone. It signifies that the subject being described is preserved in its most precious and unblemished form, embodying innocence, fragility, and perfection.
orig: كأنهن بيض مكنون

translation: Then they will approach one another, inquiring of each other.
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene from the Hereafter where people, after having witnessed the outcomes of their lives, turn to each other with questions and reflections. It suggests an atmosphere of accountability, seeking understanding, or perhaps expressing remorse and curiosity about the paths they took and the decisions they made. The context implies a moment of realization and introspection about the consequences of their earthly actions.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: A speaker among them will say, 'Indeed, I had a companion [on earth],
interpretation: This verse refers to an individual in the afterlife who recalls having a friend or companion during their worldly life. The context suggests that this companionship may have had significant implications, possibly influencing their beliefs and actions. It highlights the profound impact of relationships and the moral or spiritual influences they may exert on one's life.
orig: قال قائل منهم إني كان لي قرين

translation: He said, 'Are you truly among the believers?'
interpretation: This verse likely reflects a moment of questioning or doubt directed towards someone, probing the authenticity of their faith. It suggests that faith may require evidence or proof of sincerity and commitment.
orig: يقول أإنك لمن المصدقين

translation: When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of disbelievers regarding the resurrection and judgment after death. They question the possibility of being resurrected and held accountable once they have decayed into dust and bones. The verse highlights their disbelief and presents the rhetorical question as a way to challenge their understanding of divine power and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمدينون

translation: He said, 'Would you like to look?'
interpretation: In this passage, Allah recounts a dialogue that signifies a moment of revelation or understanding. The speaker, presumably a prophet or righteous person, invites the audience to witness or be aware of a significant truth. It suggests a pivotal point where the listeners are prompted to observe and realize the consequences or truths that are being revealed to them. This can be understood as an invitation towards reflection, awareness, and acknowledging divine reality.
orig: قال هل أنتم مطلعون

translation: So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate consequence of one's actions, emphasizing the stark reality of divine justice. It serves as a reminder that those who engage in wrongdoing will face dire repercussions in the hereafter. The imagery of seeing someone in the midst of Hellfire underscores the severity of the punishment and the inevitability of accountability.
orig: فاطلع فرآه في سواء الجحيم

translation: He said, 'By Allah, you almost ruined me.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is expressing a narrow escape from a severe harm or misguided path that was almost inflicted upon them by another person. It reflects a moment of realization and relief at having avoided a significant danger, and perhaps highlights the importance of vigilance and the influence others can have on one's decisions and life path.
orig: قال تالله إن كدت لتردين

translation: And if it were not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been of those brought in (to Hell).
interpretation: This verse highlights a sense of gratitude and recognition of divine grace. It reflects the acknowledgment that without God's mercy and blessings, one could easily fall into misfortune or punishment. The speaker is expressing a humble realization that their safety and well-being are directly tied to the favor of God, emphasizing human dependence on divine grace for protection from evil or punishment.
orig: ولولا نعمة ربي لكنت من المحضرين

translation: Shall we not then die?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question highlighting a sense of wonder or disbelief at the concept of resurrection or afterlife. It's suggesting that there might be more than just physical death, alluding to the eternal consequences or existence beyond this life. It emphasizes the inevitability of death for all beings, and by posing it as a question, it is meant to provoke reflection and contemplation on the transient nature of life and what follows thereafter.
orig: أفما نحن بميتين

translation: There is nothing but our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief of those who deny the Resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They assert that after their first death, there will be no further life or punishment, dismissing the concept of accountability in the hereafter. This mindset reveals their ignorance of the divine promise of life after death and the recompense awaiting every soul based on their deeds.
orig: إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate success and victory, which is often understood as the attainment of Paradise and the approval of Allah. It signifies that the true and greatest achievement one can aspire to is spiritual fulfillment and divine reward, surpassing any worldly gains or accomplishments.
orig: إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم

translation: For the like of this let the workers [on earth] work.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving and working diligently towards virtuous deeds and the rewards promised by God. It encourages believers to focus their efforts on achieving spiritual goals and pursuing actions that are pleasing to God, suggesting that the ultimate reward is worth all the hard work and dedication.
orig: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

translation: Is that a better hospitality or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: This verse contrasts the bountiful hospitality awaiting the righteous in Paradise with the dreadful punishment awaiting sinners in Hell, symbolized by the ominous Tree of Zaqqum. The Qur'an uses this imagery to encourage reflection on one's actions and the repercussions they may have in the afterlife.
orig: أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that certain challenges or tests are specifically designed for those who commit injustice or wrongdoing. These trials serve not only as a means of punishment but also as an opportunity for the wrongdoers to reflect on their actions, recognize their errors, and potentially find the path to repentance and righteousness.
orig: إنا جعلناها فتنة للظالمين

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that grows from the bottom of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse references a tree known as Zaqqoom, which is described in the Qur'an as growing in Hell (Jahannam). It symbolizes the severe punishment and torment awaiting the disbelievers and sinners in the afterlife. It serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness and rejecting divine guidance.
orig: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم

translation: Its fruit is as if it were the heads of devils.
interpretation: This verse uses a vivid and grim image to emphasize the horrifying and repulsive nature of the fruit from the tree growing in hell. By comparing it to the 'heads of devils,' the verse aims to invoke a sense of fear, revulsion, and stark warning about the severe consequences and the terrifying aspects of hellfire for those who transgress and do not follow the righteous path.
orig: طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين

translation: For indeed they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The 'it' here denotes the Tree of Zaqqoom, which produces extremely bitter fruit. The disbelievers will be forced to eat from this tree as a form of divine retribution. Despite its bitterness and their suffering, they will have no choice but to consume it and fill their stomachs, indicating prolonged and unavoidable punishment.
orig: فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون

translation: Then, indeed, they will have after it a mixture of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse pertains to the punishment of the wicked in the afterlife. It emphasizes the severity and continuity of their suffering, indicating that after experiencing one form of torment, they will encounter yet another excruciating one—specifically, the torment of being forced to drink a mixture of boiling water. This serves as a stark warning about the consequences of sinful behavior and disbelief.
orig: ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم

translation: Then indeed their return will be to the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable consequence for those who turn away from the path of righteousness and engage in sinful actions. It serves as a stern warning of the final destination that awaits the wrongdoers, highlighting the concept of accountability and the dire repercussions of disobedience to divine guidance.
orig: ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم

translation: Indeed, they found their fathers astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of individuals to blindly follow the practices and beliefs of their forefathers without questioning their validity. It serves as a cautionary note against the perpetuation of false or misguided traditions and emphasizes the need for personal discernment and the pursuit of true guidance.
orig: إنهم ألفوا آباءهم ضالين

translation: Then they hasten on their footsteps back to it.
interpretation: This verse suggests the swiftness and eagerness with which people return to their old ways or mistakes despite having the opportunity to change or improve. It reflects a human tendency to revert to familiar habits or behaviors, even when those habits are not beneficial.
orig: فهم على آثارهم يهرعون

translation: And indeed, most of the former peoples went astray before them.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the deviation from the right path is not a new occurrence. Historically, a majority of the earlier generations also went astray and away from divine guidance. It serves as a reminder of the persistent challenge of maintaining faith and righteousness throughout human history.
orig: ولقد ضل قبلهم أكثر الأولين

translation: And We certainly sent among them warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's continuous guidance to humanity by sending prophets and messengers to warn and remind people of the righteous path. It emphasizes the mercy and care of God in ensuring that no nation is left without guidance, as these warners come to convey the divine message, ethics, and laws, urging societies to adhere to faith and righteousness to avoid divine punishment.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين

translation: So see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to heed divine warnings, emphasizing that those who ignored such guidance faced dire consequences. It underscores the importance of paying attention to the lessons of past communities who were warned but chose to disregard the admonitions, leading to their downfall. The verse encourages reflection on the outcomes of the disobedient as a means to anchor oneself in righteousness and obedience to God's directives.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that amongst all people, those who are truly devoted and sincere in their worship and relationship with Allah are set apart. They are granted protection, guidance, and are favored by Allah due to their devout faith and steadfastness. It highlights the special status and divine selection of these pious individuals.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And Noah had certainly called upon Us, and [We are] the best of responders.
