It relates to an episode where he is instructed to take a bunch of grass and strike with it to fulfill an oath he made, which shows the merciful and understanding nature of God's commands, allowing flexibility while fulfilling personal vows. The verse highlights Job's steadfastness and constant devotion to Allah, marking him as a model of patience and righteousness.
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, those of strength and [religious] vision.
interpretation: This verse calls for the remembrance of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, highlighting their notable qualities of strength and insightful vision. It emphasizes their exemplary roles as individuals of strong faith and profound understanding, serving as models for followers to emulate in their devotion and spiritual clarity.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: Indeed, We purified them with a pure thought: the remembrance of the Home (in the Hereafter).
interpretation: This verse signifies that certain individuals were chosen and purified by Allah to possess a distinguishing quality, which is the constant remembrance and mindfulness of the Hereafter. It underscores the importance of keeping the concept of the eternal abode in one's thoughts, which helps guide and purify actions in this worldly life.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And indeed they are, in Our presence, of the chosen and the best.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who are referred to as 'they' hold a special and esteemed status in the sight of Allah. They are not just chosen, but are among the most select and virtuous individuals. This honor indicates their righteousness, faithfulness, and the exceptional nature of their deeds, which have earned them a distinguished place with Allah.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And mention Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl; and all are among the outstanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of certain prophets who are esteemed for their righteousness and moral excellence. By mentioning Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl specifically, it emphasizes their exemplary qualities and contributions as leaders and followers of divine guidance. It serves as a reminder of their virtuous deeds and encourages the believers to look up to these individuals as role models of faith and piety.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return.
interpretation: The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who are pious and righteous. It emphasizes the concept that life in this world is temporary, and the ultimate success lies in the hereafter. For the righteous, who live in accordance with divine guidance, there is a promise of a beautiful and favorable final abode, underscoring the importance of maintaining faith and moral integrity.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors will be opened for them.
interpretation: This verse promises the righteous believers an eternal abode in paradise where they will reside forever. The mention of the doors being open signifies ease of entry, honor, and the welcoming nature of paradise for those who have led a life of piety and devotion. It highlights the rewards awaiting the faithful, emphasizing a state of everlasting peace and the divine hospitality they will receive.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This verse depicts the blissful state of the righteous in the hereafter. They are described as reclining, a sign of comfort and relaxation, enjoying the pleasures of paradise abundantly provided for them. The reference to fruit and drink symbolizes both physical sustenance and the spiritual satisfaction that comes from divine bounty, indicating a state of complete fulfillment and contentment.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And with them will be chaste women, restraining their glances, of equal age.
interpretation: This verse describes the companions in paradise who will be given to the believers. The 'chaste women' who are 'restraining their glances' signifies their modesty and purity, indicating they will be devoted and loyal to their partners. The phrase 'of equal age' suggests harmony and compatibility, emphasizing the ideal and balanced nature of the relationships in the heavenly realm.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: This verse stresses the certainty of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that the promises and warnings given throughout the Qur'an will undeniably come to pass. It serves as a reminder of accountability, urging individuals to reflect on their actions and prepare for the inevitable day when all will be judged and recompensed according to their deeds.
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision for it will never be exhausted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite and unending nature of the provision from Allah. It signifies that the sustenance and blessings granted by Allah are boundless and eternal, never running out or being depleted. This not only applies to material sustenance but also to spiritual and moral guidance, emphasizing the continuous and everlasting support from Allah to the believers.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: Indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return.
interpretation: This verse warns those who are unjust and exceed the limits set by Allah, indicating that their final destination will be a terrible and dreadful one. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and disobedience to divine commandments.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: Hell, in which they will burn; and what a wretched resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe punishment awaiting the disbelievers and wrongdoers in Hell. The use of the term 'wretched resting place' serves to emphasize the stark contrast between the expectations of comfort and the reality of endless suffering in the afterlife for those who reject faith and commit sins. It acts as a stern warning and a call to righteousness and moral integrity.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: Then let them taste it—boiling water and festering fluid.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who have rejected faith and committed wrongful deeds. The punishment described is both severe and unrelenting, utilizing imagery of boiling water and festering fluid to convey the intensity and repulsiveness of the suffering. It underscores the consequences of turning away from divine guidance and emphasizes the seriousness of accountability in the Hereafter. The verse is meant to instill a sense of fear and urgency, urging people to reconsider their actions and return to righteous behavior to avoid such dreadful punishment.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And others of similar kind.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there will be pairs or groups of similar nature or kind. It emphasizes the concept of companionship and similarity, possibly referring to the pairing of individuals with like characteristics or conditions. This could relate to the broader theme of justice, where individuals are matched according to their deeds and qualities.
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a crowd rushing in along with you; no welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire.
interpretation: The verse depicts a scene of judgment where a group of condemned individuals is being led into the Hellfire. Those already in Hell express their disdain, indicating that the newcomers will share the same terrible fate. This passage highlights the severity of divine retribution and the fate awaiting those who have earned God's wrath.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They will say, 'No! You (too) are not welcome! You brought this upon us; what an evil place to stay!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the mutual recrimination and blame among the denizens of Hell. It emphasizes the concept of accountability in Islam, where individuals are responsible for their own actions and their consequences. Despite the shared suffering, there is no comfort or solidarity, only further torment through mutual blame. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the gravity of one's choices and their potential outcomes in the hereafter.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us—double the punishment for them in the Fire!'
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of the inhabitants of Hell asking Allah to increase the punishment of those who misguided them. It highlights the intense regret and animosity among the dwellers of Hell and underscores the severity of the consequences of leading others astray.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they will say, 'What has happened to us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?'
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene from the Day of Judgment where the disbelievers express confusion and concern over the absence of individuals they had previously regarded as evil or sinful. It implies a sense of surprise or reconsideration of their judgments and assumptions in light of the divine reality being revealed. The verse serves as a reminder that human judgments are fallible, and ultimate judgment belongs to Allah alone.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes failed to notice them?
interpretation: This verse suggests a self-reflective inquiry where one is questioning their own past attitudes and perceptions. It highlights the possibility of having treated others unjustly or with derision, and it also alludes to the blindness or negligence in recognizing the true worth or presence of certain individuals. The verse serves as a moral reminder to reflect on one's behavior and attitudes towards others, urging a reconsideration of past judgments or actions.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: Indeed, that is the true argument between the people of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse asserts the reality of the disputes and arguments among the inhabitants of Hell. It emphasizes that their condemnation and mutual recriminations are genuine and serious, highlighting the intense regret and blame they place on one another for their actions that led them to such a fate. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of straying from the righteous path.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, 'I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as merely a warner to mankind, stressing that his primary mission is to deliver the message of monotheism. It reaffirms the concept of the oneness of Allah, who is not only singular but also possesses the attribute of overwhelming power over all creation. It serves as a reminder of the exclusive divinity and ultimate authority of Allah, calling people to acknowledge and submit to His supreme will.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and authority of Allah over all creation, encompassing the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. It highlights two key attributes of Allah: His might and power (العزيز) and His capacity to forgive (الغفار). The combination of these attributes assures believers of both the strength and mercy of their Lord, encouraging them to recognize His supreme rule and seek His forgiveness.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, it is great news
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and magnitude of the message being conveyed. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to declare that what is being discussed is of profound importance. This could refer to the themes of monotheism, the afterlife, or the revelations received, highlighting that the message of Islam is not trivial, but rather an extraordinary and crucial announcement for mankind.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: You turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who neglect or ignore the message or guidance being provided. It implies a warning or a reminder about the consequences of disregarding important counsel or divine instruction. The act of turning away signifies a deliberate choice to avoid engagement with the truth or guidance offered, suggesting a deeper reflection on the reasons for such refusal and the potential spiritual ramifications.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human limitation in understanding the divine matters or the discourses of the exalted assembly (the angels). It underscores the need for humility and reliance on divine revelation for knowledge about the unseen and metaphysical realms.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: Nothing is revealed to me except that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's primary role is to serve as a clear warner to the people. His duty is to convey the message of God plainly and unambiguously, acting as a messenger who warns of consequences and offers guidance. The authority and message he delivers are not of his own making, but divinely revealed.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, 'I am creating a human being from clay.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Allah informs the angels about His intention to create human beings from clay. It signifies the unique and deliberate act of creation by Allah, emphasizing both the physical and metaphysical aspects of humanity's origin. The use of clay highlights humankind's humble beginnings, while the announcement to the angels underscores the importance and significance of this creation in the divine scheme.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine process of creating human beings, emphasizing their unique status by mentioning the act of Allah's breath of life into them. The command for the angels to prostrate signifies respect and recognition of the special creation and sanctity of human beings, illustrating their eminent position in the natural order as a result of divine intervention and favor.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: Then all the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together.
interpretation: This verse highlights the collective act of obedience and reverence shown by the angels towards Allah's command. The prostration signifies their submission to God's will and recognition of His authority. It also emphasizes the unity and consensus among the angels in fulfilling what is decreed by Allah, reflecting the harmony and discipline in the divine order.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblis (Satan) who was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the defiance and pride of Iblis when he refused to bow to Adam as commanded by Allah. His arrogance led him to a state of disbelief and rebellion, underscoring the gravity of pride and disobedience in leading one away from the path of faith and submission to God's will.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He (Allah) said, 'O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Did you become arrogant, or were you already among the exalted?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hubris of Iblis (Satan) who refused to bow to Adam as commanded by Allah. It highlights the elements of arrogance and pride, questioning whether Iblis considered himself too superior to follow Allah’s command or if he was inherently among those who defy divine authority. The verse underscores the importance of humility and obedience to Allah's will.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and pride of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to bow to Adam as commanded by Allah. Iblis' argument is based on his belief that fire (his origin) is superior to clay (Adam's origin). This statement exemplifies disobedience rooted in pride and prejudice, highlighting the importance of humility and obedience to divine commandments.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled.'
interpretation: This verse is part of the dialogue between Allah and Iblis (Satan) following Iblis' refusal to prostrate to Adam. Allah commands Iblis to leave Heaven, declaring him accursed and banished. The verse signifies the consequence of disobedience and rebellion against divine command, emphasizing the severance of Iblis from the grace and mercy of Allah. It serves as a warning about the dire outcomes of arrogance and defiance toward God's will.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse reflects God's eternal condemnation and punishment upon a transgressor, in this context, often interpreted as referring to Satan. The 'Day of Recompense' signifies the final judgment day, emphasizing the perpetuity and severity of this curse. It implies an irrevocable separation from divine mercy and a continuous state of divine disapproval.
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: In this verse, Iblis (Satan) is speaking to Allah, asking for a reprieve until the Day of Resurrection. This request reflects Iblis's awareness of the consequences of his defiance but also his desire to continue his mission of leading humans astray until the end of time. It highlights the ongoing battle between good and evil and the patience of Allah in allowing free will and the ultimate accountability of creation on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are of those who are reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse refers to a dialogue between Allah and Iblis (Satan) after his refusal to bow to Adam. By stating 'Indeed, you are of those who are reprieved,' Allah grants Iblis a delay in his punishment until the Day of Judgment. This period of reprieve allows Iblis to tempt and misguide humans, testing their faith and righteousness. The verse reflects the themes of free will, the test of faith, and the ultimate accountability of actions in the afterlife.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the appointed time.
interpretation: This verse is interpreted as a reference to a specific moment chosen or designated by Allah, most often understood to be the Day of Resurrection or Judgment. It signifies a divinely preordained time when certain events will unfold, indicating the sovereignty and ultimate control of Allah over all matters and the eventual unfolding of divine justice and reckoning.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, 'By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the declaration made by Satan to mislead humanity from the path of righteousness. It showcases his intent to exploit his influence and power to divert as many souls as possible. Despite Satan's vow, the ultimate authority and power rest with Allah, and it serves as a reminder for believers to seek refuge and guidance from Allah to remain steadfast in their faith and resist Satan's temptations.
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your sincere servants among them.
interpretation: This verse highlights that among humanity, there are individuals who are truly devoted and sincere in their servitude to God. These sincere servants are distinguished from others because of their genuine faith and dedication. The context suggests that such individuals are protected from falling into deception or wrongdoing due to their unwavering fidelity to God.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said, 'The truth [is my oath], and the truth I say.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine emphasis on truthfulness. It highlights that God's pronouncements are characterized by absolute truth and that what follows is an unchangeable declaration grounded in His unerring wisdom and justice. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate authority and reliability of God's word.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them that follow you, all together.
interpretation: This verse reflects God's stern warning to Satan and his followers among humans and jinn. It emphasizes the severe consequence for those who choose to follow the path of evil and disobedience, highlighting the certainty and inevitability of divine justice for persistent rebellion against God's commands.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for it any payment, and I am not of the pretentious.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad is commanded to convey to the people that his mission and delivery of the message of Islam is not motivated by any material gain or personal interest. He clarifies that he seeks no reward or compensation from them for his efforts. Additionally, he emphasizes that he is sincere and genuine in his role as a messenger, not exaggerating or feigning qualities to impress or deceive. This highlights the purity and selflessness expected in the delivery of divine guidance.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: It is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a universal message and reminder for all people, regardless of their background or status. It underscores the divine intention for the Qur'an to be a source of guidance, reflection, and moral instruction for all humanity.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely know the truth of its information after a time.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the reality or truth of a matter will become clear and evident after a certain period. It speaks to the idea of patience and the eventual unveiling of what is true and just, implying that with time, knowledge or understanding of certain events or revelations will be manifest.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation directly to Allah. It characterizes Allah with two of His majestic attributes—'Al-Aziz' (the Exalted in Might), signifying His absolute power and dominance, and 'Al-Hakim' (the Wise), highlighting His infinite wisdom. This combination of power and wisdom underscores the inimitable nature of the Qur'an, reinforcing that its guidance is both supreme and judiciously crafted for human benefit.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth. So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, affirming that it was revealed with truth and purpose. It serves as a command for Prophet Muhammad and by extension, all followers, to worship Allah with complete sincerity and devotion, ensuring that all religious practices and beliefs are purely for Him, free from any form of hypocrisy or idolatry. This sincerity in worship is seen as a foundational aspect of true faith.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Indeed, sincere devotion is due to Allah alone. And those who take protectors besides Him say, 'We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.' Surely Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and stubborn disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true and sincere worship belongs solely to Allah, dismissing any justification for worshipping other entities as intermediaries. It condemns the practice of associating partners with Allah under the pretext that they bring one closer to Him. The verse asserts that Allah alone will judge the disagreements among people regarding their beliefs and practices. It also highlights that guidance from Allah will not be granted to those who are persistently deceitful and ungrateful for the truth.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from whatever He willed of what He creates. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah, refuting any notion of Him having a son or offspring. It highlights that, hypothetically, had Allah willed to take a son, He is capable of choosing from His creation. However, the verse then immediately glorifies Allah, affirming His absolute uniqueness and supremacy, thus underscoring the impossibility and inappropriateness of such an idea. It concludes by reinforcing that Allah is the One (unique in His essence and attributes) and the Prevailing (Al-Qahhar), indicating His complete dominion and power over all creation.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He makes the night overlap the day and the day overlap the night. He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetually Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful creation of the universe by Allah, highlighting His control over cosmic phenomena such as the alternation of night and day and the orbits of the sun and the moon. It underscores Allah's authority and power over creation, reminding the believers of His attributes as both mighty and forgiving. The verse encourages acknowledgment of Allah's grandeur and mercy, urging people to reflect on the orderly and precise nature of the universe as signs of His omnipotence and benevolence.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you from the cattle eight pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three layers of darkness. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and oneness of human origin, underscoring that all humans are created from a single soul. It highlights the divine creation process, starting from a single entity to the diverse existence around us, including the provision of livestock for human benefit. The reference to creation stages in the womb in 'three layers of darkness' signifies the intricate and deliberate nature of human development. It reaffirms the dominion and unparalleled sovereignty of Allah, challenging the reader on why they would turn away from worshipping Him alone.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is Free from need of you. But He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse underscores the independence and self-sufficiency of Allah, emphasizing that human belief or disbelief does not affect His divine essence. However, Allah prefers gratitude and belief from His servants and disapproves of disbelief, not out of need, but out of His wisdom and care for their well-being. It also stresses personal responsibility, indicating that each individual is accountable for their own actions and cannot bear the sins of others. Ultimately, every soul will return to Allah, who is fully aware of the innermost intentions and actions of individuals, and will inform them about their deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: When distress befalls man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. But when He bestows a favor upon him from Himself, he forgets what he was praying for before and sets up rivals to Allah to mislead others from His path. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; you are certainly one of the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature's tendency to turn to God during times of trouble and forget His grace when in ease. It addresses the ingratitude and forgetfulness of people who, upon receiving favor from Allah, turn away and associate others with Him. The warning at the end emphasizes that such behavior leads to severe consequences in the Hereafter, specifically being among those destined for Hell.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who are devoted worshippers, engaged in prayers, filled with the consciousness of accountability in the Hereafter, and hopeful for the mercy of Allah, and those who are ignorant or indifferent. It emphasizes that such devoted individuals possess true knowledge and wisdom. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces that only people of deep understanding truly comprehend and reflect upon these matters, appreciating the value of knowledge and devotion.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.'
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, urging them to maintain their consciousness and fear of God. It promises that those who excel in good deeds will receive goodness in this world and that God's blessings and opportunities are vast and abundant. The verse reassures that those who show patience and perseverance will be granted an immense and unquantifiable reward, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness and trust in God’s wisdom and mercy.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and purity of intention in the worship of Allah. It highlights the command given to the Prophet Muhammad to dedicate his worship solely to Allah, free from any form of hypocrisy or idolatry. This instruction serves as a reminder to believers to maintain integrity in their devotional practices, ensuring that their faithfulness and acts of worship are directed to Allah alone without seeking any personal gain or worldly recognition.
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I was commanded to be the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine command given to the Prophet Muhammad to lead by example in submitting to the will of Allah. As the final messenger in Islam, he is tasked with embodying complete submission, setting a precedent for his followers to embrace and uphold the principles of Islam with unwavering faith and dedication.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's profound consciousness of accountability to Allah. It reflects a deep sense of fear and reverence for the consequences of disobedience to God's commands, highlighting the seriousness of the Day of Judgment and the magnitude of divine retribution. This serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of adhering to divine guidance to avoid dire consequences in the afterlife.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'I worship Allah, sincere to Him in my religion.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah with pure sincerity, without any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It highlights the commitment to devote one's religious practices and beliefs solely to Allah, undiverted by personal gain, societal pressures, or insincere intentions.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: So worship what you will besides Him. Say, 'Indeed, the losers are the ones who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.' Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of idolatry and disbelief. It conveys that those who choose to worship entities other than Allah are the true losers, as their actions will lead to the ultimate loss of both themselves and their loved ones on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase 'manifest loss' emphasizes the clear and unequivocal nature of this spiritual and existential defeat.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: They will have canopies of fire above them and canopies (of fire) beneath them. With this Allah warns His servants: 'O My servants, then fear Me!'
interpretation: This verse is a vivid depiction of the torments of the hereafter, describing the severe punishment awaiting those who reject Allah's guidance. It emphasizes the dual sources of agony – both above and below – symbolizing the all-encompassing nature of divine retribution. By portraying this dire warning, Allah aims to instill a sense of fear and accountability among His servants, urging them to heed His commands and live righteously. The call to 'fear Me' is a reminder of His ultimate authority and the importance of conscious and devout living to avoid such a fate.
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: And those who avoid the worship of false gods and turn to Allah will have good news. So give good news to My servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue and reward of monotheism in Islam. It calls for the rejection of all forms of idolatry and the exclusive worship of Allah. Those who purify their faith by avoiding the worship of false gods and sincerely turn to Allah in repentance and devotion are promised glad tidings and divine blessings. This promise of good news is an encouragement for believers to persevere in their faith and continue to seek closeness to Allah.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to the word (of God) and follow the best of it, those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of being attentive and discerning when listening to guidance, particularly divine revelation. It recognizes and commends individuals who not only hear but also adopt the best and most righteous aspects of guidance into their lives. Such individuals are deemed to be rightly guided by Allah and are described as people endowed with true understanding and wisdom because they can differentiate between various messages and choose the most virtuous path.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Is then one against whom the sentence of punishment is justified (to be helped)? Can you save one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine justice. It questions the possibility of rescuing someone who is doomed to punishment as decreed by God, emphasizing that such a person cannot be saved from the consequences of their actions, nor can anyone else intervene to negate God's judgment once it is established. The rhetorical questions underscore human limitation against the ultimate sovereignty of God in matters of justice and retribution.
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have lofty rooms, above them other lofty rooms built, beneath which rivers flow. This is the promise of Allah, and Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse assures the believers who are conscious of their Lord (those who have Taqwa) that they will be rewarded with high and exalted dwellings in the Hereafter. These dwellings will be layered and opulent, with rivers flowing beneath them, symbolizing perpetual bliss and divine grace. The verse emphasizes that this is a promise from Allah, stressing that Allah never breaks His promises, thus providing reassurance and motivation for the believers to continue their righteous deeds and maintain their piety.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and causes it to flow as springs in the earth, then produces thereby crops of varying colors; then they dry and you see them turned yellow; then He makes them debris? Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cycle of life and the power of Allah in creating and transforming nature. It highlights the process of water descending from the sky, nourishing the earth, and generating diverse vegetation, which eventually withers and turns to debris. This natural cycle serves as a profound reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the omnipotence of Allah, prompting reflection and understanding for those who are wise and discerning.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: Is one whose heart Allah has opened to Islam, so that he has received light from his Lord, like one whose heart rejects it? Woe, therefore, to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Such are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who accept faith with an open heart and those who reject it with hardened hearts. It emphasizes that true guidance is a gift from Allah and that those who embrace it are enlightened by divine wisdom. In contrast, those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah are warned of severe consequences and are described as being in clear misguidance. The verse underscores the value of spiritual receptiveness and the peril of spiritual insensitivity.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unparalleled and profound impact of the Qur'an on those who are conscious of Allah. The 'best statement' refers to the Qur'an, described as consistent and possessing repeated themes, which deepen understanding and contemplation. The physical reaction of shivering skin represents a deep emotional and spiritual response in those who revere Allah, indicating a profound awe and fear. This transforms into tranquility and peace found in the remembrance of Allah. The guidance mentioned is divine and selective, highlighting that ultimate guidance comes solely from Allah, and those led astray by divine will, find no other guidance.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Is then one who shields himself with his face against the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection (like the one who is safe from it)? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inescapable and severe nature of the punishment that awaits wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection. It portrays the futility of any attempted defense against divine retribution, highlighting that one's own face, a vulnerable and sensitive part of the body, is all that stands against the fierce chastisement. The address to the wrongdoers to 'taste' what they have earned underscores the justice and reciprocity of their punishment, reflecting the inevitable consequences of their actions in this life.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those before them also denied the truth, and so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by previous nations who rejected the divine truth. It serves as a warning, indicating that the punishment for such denial is inevitable and can come unexpectedly. The message emphasizes the importance of heeding divine guidance to avoid unforeseen suffering.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in worldly life. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse warns against the consequences of rejecting God's guidance. The immediate disgrace in this world serves as a foretaste of a much greater and more severe punishment in the Hereafter. It underscores the importance of awareness and understanding of the truth to avoid such fates, emphasizing the gravity of the suffering that awaits those who persist in their disbelief and unrighteousness.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an in providing guidance. By presenting a variety of examples and parables, the Qur'an aims to make its teachings accessible and relatable to all people, urging them to reflect and internalize the moral and spiritual lessons it imparts.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: A Quran in Arabic, without any crookedness, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and perfection of the Quran's message, highlighting that it is conveyed in the Arabic language without any deviation or distortion. The purpose of this precise and straightforward communication is to guide people towards righteousness and mindfulness of God. It suggests that the unambiguous nature of the Quran is intended to facilitate better understanding and adherence to its teachings.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah sets forth an example: a man belonging to many partners who are quarreling, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of two types of men to illustrate the concept of monotheism versus polytheism. The man with multiple disputing partners represents those who worship multiple gods, leading to confusion and conflict. The man wholly devoted to one master represents a believer who worships only Allah, leading to harmony and clear purpose. The verse concludes by praising Allah and noting that many people lack understanding of this clear truth.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitable reality of death for everyone, including the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the transient nature of life, highlighting that no human, regardless of their status or role, is exempt from mortality. This realization encourages humility, reflection on one's deeds, and the preparation for the afterlife.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, individuals will be brought before God and disputes will arise among them. It suggests accountability and the resolution of conflicts under divine judgment. Each person's actions and the truths they may have concealed will be examined, emphasizing the gravity and comprehensiveness of divine justice.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave injustice and wrongdoing of those who fabricate lies about Allah and reject the truth when it is presented to them. It emphasizes that no one is more unjust than such individuals. The verse also serves as a warning, implying that Hell is the inevitable abode for those who persist in disbelief and falsehood, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And the one who has brought the truth and [they who] believed in it – those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the high status of those who deliver the truth and believe in it. It highlights that they are the people who possess taqwa, or God-consciousness. The verse reflects the importance of both conveying and accepting the truth, suggesting that true righteousness is achieved through sincere belief and propagation of truthful messages.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine generosity and grace granted to those who act righteously and with virtue. It assures the believers that their righteous deeds will be rewarded abundantly in the hereafter, fulfilling their every desire. This notion reinforces the incentive to remain steadfast in goodness and faith, as the ultimate recompense from Allah is beyond human comprehension and infinitely fulfilling.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah. It signifies that Allah will forgive the believers’ worst deeds if they repent sincerely and will reward them based on the best of their good deeds. It emphasizes hope and encouragement for continual righteous behavior, assuring that sincere intention and actions will be recognized and rewarded generously by Allah.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they threaten you with those they worship other than Him. And whoever Allah leaves astray—for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as the protector and sustainer of His servants. Despite the threats or fears imposed by others and their false deities, a true believer should trust in Allah alone. It also highlights the concept of divine guidance, noting that if Allah allows someone to go astray, no one else can provide guidance for that person.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whoever Allah guides - there is none that can mislead him. Is not Allah Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of Allah in guiding individuals. When Allah grants guidance, no force can lead such a person astray. It also highlights Allah's attributes of being mighty and possessing the power to exact retribution, indicating that His guidance is intertwined with His justice and supreme control over all affairs.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm, or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him [alone] rely the [wise] reliers.'
interpretation: This verse is conveying the concept of Tawhid (monotheism) and the futility of relying on false gods or intermediaries besides Allah. It depicts a scenario where people acknowledge Allah as the Creator but still turn to other deities for help. The verse emphasizes that only Allah has control over harm and mercy, rendering other supposed powers ineffective. Therefore, the believer should place complete trust in Allah, as He is sufficient and reliable for all needs and protection.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. And you are going to know.'
interpretation: This verse is a directive for individual accountability, emphasizing that everyone should act according to their understanding and position. It conveys a message of perseverance and resoluteness in one's actions, assuring that the truth and outcomes of these actions will be revealed in due time. It underscores the inevitability of ultimate knowledge and justice, reassuring that efforts are recognized and will be judged accordingly.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: Whoever is visited by a disgraceful punishment and upon whom descends an everlasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the consequences for those who do wrong. It indicates that they will face not only a disgraceful punishment in this life, which will bring them shame and dishonor, but also an eternal and unrelenting punishment in the hereafter. It serves as a stern warning against engaging in sinful behavior and emphasizes the gravity of divine retribution.
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for the people in truth. So whoever is guided—it is for his own benefit; and whoever goes astray—he only goes astray to his own detriment. And you are not a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an as a guide for humanity, revealed with truth. It underscores personal responsibility in spiritual matters, indicating that the consequences of guidance or misguidance are borne by the individual. The Prophet Muhammad is reminded that his role is to convey the message, not to enforce adherence, reflecting the principle of free will and individual accountability in Islam.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over life and death. Allah seizes the souls at the moment of death and also during sleep, which is considered a minor form of death. He retains the souls of those who are destined to die, while the others are sent back until their appointed time. This process serves as a clear sign for those who reflect on the divine power and the mysteries of life and death.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Have they taken others as intercessors besides Allah? Say, 'Even though they do not possess any power nor do they understand?'
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question challenging the act of taking intercessors or mediators other than Allah. It highlights the futility and irrationality of seeking help and intercession from entities that possess no power and lack understanding. The verse emphasizes the exclusive authority and capability of Allah, urging believers to rely solely on Him.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs [the right to allow] intercession entirely. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse underscores that the ultimate authority for intercession lies solely with Allah. He alone has control over the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His supreme sovereignty and power. Furthermore, the mention of returning to Allah serves as a reminder of the accountability in the Hereafter, where everyone will be judged by Him alone.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when Allah is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those other than Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights a distinction between the believers and the non-believers in their emotional reactions to the mention of Allah. The hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter feel discomfort and aversion when Allah is mentioned by Himself, indicating their resistance to monotheistic faith. Conversely, they feel a sense of joy and satisfaction when others, possibly idols or deities aside from Allah, are mentioned, illustrating their attachment to different beliefs and their preferences for polytheism or secular matters over the remembrance of the Divine Unity.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse highlights God's ultimate authority and knowledge, emphasizing that He alone is the Creator and Knower of all things, both hidden and manifest. It calls upon the believer to acknowledge God's role as the ultimate judge who will resolve all differences and disputes among His servants. This invocation serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence, urging humankind to seek His guidance and justice in all matters.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Even if the wrongdoers possessed all that is on earth and as much again with it, they would offer it to ransom themselves from the severity of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection; and there will appear to them from Allah that which they had never reckoned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of the punishment awaiting the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that even if they possessed vast wealth, it would not suffice to save them from the torment prepared for them. The verse further highlights that they will be confronted with aspects of Allah's retribution that they had not anticipated. This serves as a stern warning about the futility of material wealth in the face of divine justice and the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with Allah's guidance.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And the evil consequences of what they did will become apparent to them, and that which they used to ridicule will engulf them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable realization of the consequences of one's actions, particularly those of a sinful nature. It underscores the idea that mockery and ridicule of divine warnings will ultimately lead to a just recompense, as the mocked truths will manifest in their reality, leaving no escape for those who engaged in derision. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the moral law of cause and effect within a spiritual framework, where actions, good or bad, have definite repercussions.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: When trouble touches the human being, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow a favor upon him from Us, he says, 'I have been given it only because of knowledge.' Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fickle nature of humans who turn to God in times of distress but often forget His grace when they are relieved of their suffering and endowed with blessings. Instead of recognizing these blessings as a test or a trial from God, they arrogantly assume they have received them due to their own knowledge or abilities. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain humility and awareness of God's continuous role in our lives, acknowledging that both hardship and ease are part of the divine plan, and that true understanding lies in recognizing and appreciating this reality.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, they had said it before them, but what they used to earn did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a recurring pattern in human behavior, where people repeat the same mistakes of defiance and disbelief as those before them. Despite their efforts and material gains, these were of no benefit in the face of divine accountability. It serves as a reminder that worldly achievements cannot shield one from the consequences of ignoring or rejecting spiritual truths and divine commandments.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So they were afflicted with the evil consequences of what they did; and those who have wronged of these people will be afflicted with the evil consequences of what they did, and they will not escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice, emphasizing that people will face the repercussions of their own wrongful actions. It also serves as a warning to the wrongdoers that their actions will lead to negative outcomes and that they cannot evade the consequences set by divine decree.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute authority and control over the distribution of sustenance. It serves as a reminder that the provisions one receives, whether in abundance or in limitation, are determined by God's will. The variation in provision is meant to be a sign for believers, prompting them to reflect on their faith and recognize the divine wisdom behind such decisions. This understanding fosters trust in God's plan and encourages gratitude and patience irrespective of one's material circumstances.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of Allah's boundless mercy. It calls out to those who have wronged themselves through sin, offering them hope and urging them not to despair. The key message is that no matter the extent of one's sins, Allah's capacity to forgive is greater. It emphasizes that Allah is not only forgiving but also merciful, encouraging people to turn back to Him with sincere repentance and trust in His mercy.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And return [in repentance] to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of seeking forgiveness and submitting to Allah before it is too late and divine punishment befalls. It emphasizes that once the punishment arrives, there will be no one to offer support or aid. This serves as a warning to turn towards faith and righteousness proactively rather than reactively.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: This verse urges the followers to adhere to the highest and most excellent guidance revealed by Allah. It is a call to prioritize and act upon the most elevated principles of the divine message. The warning here is clear: the consequence of ignoring this guidance could lead to a sudden and unforeseen punishment, which serves as a reminder of the ephemeral and unpredictable nature of life. Thus, the verse emphasizes urgency and attentiveness in heeding divine instructions.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Lest a soul should say, 'Oh, how great is my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah and that I was among the mockers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret and remorse a soul will feel on the Day of Judgment for having neglected their duties towards Allah. The individual recognizes that their indifference and mocking behavior towards piety and consciousness of Allah has led them to this moment of sorrow and repentance. It serves as a warning to take one's responsibilities towards faith seriously and not to make light of matters of spirituality and devotion.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or [lest] it say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse reflects on the regret and self-reproach a person might feel on the Day of Judgment for not having followed the guidance of Allah in their lifetime. It underscores the importance of actively seeking and adhering to divine guidance rather than blaming fate or circumstance. The verse emphasizes that one should not procrastinate in seeking righteousness, as waiting for divine intervention without personal effort can lead to regret.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or [lest] it say when it sees the punishment, 'If only I had another turn so I could be among the doers of good.'
interpretation: This verse captures the sentiment of regret that will be expressed by those who face punishment in the Hereafter. It reflects a longing for a second chance to perform righteous deeds and reform oneself. It serves as a warning to heed the guidance provided by Allah in this life and strive to be among the doers of good before it is too late, as the opportunity for redemption and righteousness is found in the present life, not after witnessing the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Yes, indeed, My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who have received clear signs and revelations from God but chose to reject them due to arrogance and willful disbelief. It underscores the accountability of individuals for their conscious rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing that the denial and arrogance in response to God's signs lead to being categorized among the disbelievers. This serves as a reminder of the moral and spiritual consequences of one's choices regarding faith and submission to divine authority.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of lying about Allah, highlighting the shame and disgrace they will face on Judgment Day. Their blackened faces symbolize their dishonor and the dark nature of their deeds. The verse also serves as a warning against arrogance, reinforcing that Hell is the ultimate abode for the proud and haughty who reject the truth and elevate themselves unjustly.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will save those who feared Him by their attainment; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward for those who are conscious of Allah (have taqwa). It assures that they will be saved and granted success. Their piety acts as a shield from harm and sorrow, highlighting the divine protection and peace granted to the righteous both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and creative power of Allah over all existence. It highlights that Allah not only brings everything into being but also manages and governs all affairs with supreme authority and wisdom. Believers are reminded to place their trust in Allah, acknowledging His ultimate control over the universe.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, and those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's dominion and control over the entire universe, symbolized by the 'keys' to the heavens and the earth. It highlights the ultimate authority and sovereignty of Allah. Additionally, the verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs and revelations of Allah, indicating that such disbelief leads to true loss, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to address those who urge him to turn away from the worship of Allah and commit acts of idolatry. Calling them 'ignorant ones' highlights their lack of understanding and awareness of the severe mistake they are making. The verse serves as a strong reminder of the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped and rejects any attempt to mislead the believers towards polytheism or idolatry.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون

translation: And it was already revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with Allah, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of associating partners with Allah, highlighting that even the noble actions of prophets and their followers would be rendered void if they were to commit shirk (idolatry or polytheism). It serves as a stern warning to maintain pure monotheism and the sincerity of worship solely for Allah, as failing to do so leads to the loss of all good deeds and ultimate failure in the afterlife.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: But worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah exclusively and expressing gratitude for His blessings. It calls on believers to devote themselves to Allah's worship and to maintain a thankful attitude, recognizing Allah as the source of all goodness and mercy.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the incomprehensible might and majesty of Allah, emphasizing that human beings fail to truly grasp His greatness. On the Day of Judgment, the entirety of creation will be under His control, symbolizing His unparalleled power and sovereignty. This serves as a reminder to recognize the futility of associating others with Allah, as He is exalted far above any partners or equals.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Judgment, where the first blowing of the trumpet signifies the end of the world, causing the death of all living beings except those whom Allah spares. The second blowing heralds the resurrection, where all will be resurrected and stand before Allah for judgment. It emphasizes the power and control of Allah over life, death, and resurrection.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the Day of Judgment, where divine justice and illumination illuminate the earth. The 'record' symbolizes the deeds of individuals being presented, and the presence of prophets and witnesses indicates the immense gravity and fairness of the proceedings. The assurance that none will be wronged emphasizes the absolute and perfect justice administered by Allah.
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Every soul will be fully compensated for what it did. And He is Most Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability in Islam. It reassures that every individual's actions will be comprehensively evaluated and rewarded or punished accordingly by Allah, who possesses complete and perfect knowledge of all their deeds. This serves as a reminder of personal responsibility and encourages moral behavior, knowing that nothing escapes divine awareness.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene of the disbelievers being led to Hell on the Day of Judgment. Upon their arrival, the gates of Hell open, and its keepers question them about whether they had been warned by messengers. The disbelievers acknowledge that indeed messengers came to them, but they still earned the punishment due to their disbelief. The verse highlights the justice of divine punishment and the importance of heeding the messages brought by God's prophets.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It will be said, 'Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who are arrogant and prideful. It highlights the severe consequences that await such individuals in the afterlife, specifying that their eternal abode will be Hell—a place of lasting torment and misery. The mention of 'enter the gates of Hell' symbolizes the irrevocable finality of their fate. This message underscores the sin of arrogance and the importance of humility and righteousness.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who were mindful of their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups until, when they get there and its gates are [already] opened, its keepers will say, 'Peace be upon you; you have done well; so enter it to abide eternally therein.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who are righteous and conscious of God throughout their lives. It portrays a serene and joyous scene where the pious are led in dignified groups to the gates of Paradise, which are opened for them. The keepers of Paradise greet them with peace and commendation for their good deeds, inviting them to enter and dwell therein forever. The imagery of groups suggests a sense of community and collective joy in righteousness. The eternal abode signifies the everlasting nature of reward for the righteous, stressing the importance of piety and moral conduct.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they will say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth, so we may settle in Paradise wherever we will.' How excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers!
interpretation: This verse reflects the gratitude of the believers on the Day of Judgment, acknowledging Allah’s fulfillment of His promise to grant them Paradise. The inheritance of the earth suggests the entitlement to dwell in any part of Paradise they desire. The phrase 'excellent is the reward of the workers' emphasizes the high regard and value of the righteous actions undertaken by the believers during their earthly life, leading to their ultimate reward in the Hereafter.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'All praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse provides a vision of the Day of Judgment where the angels are surrounding the Throne of Allah, glorifying and praising Him. It signifies that ultimate justice will be served as Allah will judge all matters with absolute truth. The declaration of 'All praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds' emphasizes the recognition of Allah's sovereignty and the fulfillment of divine justice, culminating in universal acknowledgment and praise of His lordship.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ha Meem.
interpretation: The letters 'Ha Meem' are from the group of disjointed or 'Muqatta'at' letters found at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is not definitively known, and they are believed by many scholars to be a form of divine code, a signal drawing attention to the text that follows. They underscore the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its linguistic inimitability. Some interpretations suggest that these letters serve as a reminder of the mysterious and profound nature of God's revelation.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, referred to as 'the Book,' is a divine revelation directly from Allah, who is described with two of His attributes: 'Al-Aziz' (the Mighty) and 'Al-Alim' (the Knowing). 'Al-Aziz' highlights God's supreme power and authority, ensuring the protection and implementation of His divine will, while 'Al-Alim' underlines His infinite knowledge, guaranteeing the wisdom and guidance contained in the revelation. Together, these attributes emphasize the reliability, authority, and wisdom of the Qur'an as a source of guidance for humanity.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Infinite in bounty. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the [final] return.
interpretation: This verse encapsulates several of Allah's attributes, emphasizing His mercy and acceptance of repentance alongside His capacity for severe punishment when warranted. This balance underscores the comprehensive nature of His divine authority and justice. It ends with the assertion of His singular divinity and the inevitable return of all beings to Him, reminding believers of the ultimate accountability to Allah.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve. So do not be deceived by their [uninhibited] movement throughout the land.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only individuals who argue against the signs of Allah are those who have rejected faith. It addresses the believers, advising them not to be misled or swayed by the apparent success or freedom of the disbelievers as they move about and thrive in the world.
