The underlying message is to remind the faithful that worldly success is not an indicator of ultimate truth or righteousness and that true success lies in adhering to the faith and recognizing Allah's signs.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them, and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they disputed by falsehood to refute the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of previous nations rejecting their messengers and attempting to undermine them. They used false arguments to deny the truth of the messages brought by the prophets. Despite their efforts, God's retribution was inevitable and severe. It serves as a warning about the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and engaging in deceit against the truth.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse indicates the inevitability of divine justice for those who persist in disbelief. It emphasizes that God's decree is firm and unchangeable, ensuring that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions by being destined for the Fire. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed: 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the actions of the angels who carry the Throne of Allah and those around it. They continuously glorify Allah, affirm their faith in Him, and seek forgiveness on behalf of believers. The prayer of the angels reflects their awareness of Allah's encompassing mercy and knowledge. They plead for the forgiveness and protection of those who have repented and faithfully followed Allah's path, emphasizing the importance of repentance, adherence to divine guidance, and the quest for divine mercy in avoiding the torment of Hellfire.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication asking Allah to admit the believers to eternal gardens of paradise that He has promised them. It also seeks the same for their righteous family members - parents, spouses, and descendants. The verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of being the Almighty and Wise, suggesting that He has the power and wisdom to fulfill such promises and prayers. It reflects the interconnectedness of family in spiritual reward and acknowledges the righteous deeds of one's loved ones in the hope of collective entry into paradise.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And protect them from the evil consequences [of their deeds]. And he whom You protect from evil consequences that Day - You will have given him mercy. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse invokes a plea to Allah to shield the believers from the negative repercussions of their deeds on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that those whom Allah protects from the torment and sins on that significant day are recipients of His immense mercy. This divine protection and mercy ultimately lead to the 'great attainment,' symbolizing eternal salvation and success in the hereafter.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be addressed, 'The hatred of Allah for you was greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and you disbelieved.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers, conveying that Allah's aversion towards them is far greater than their self-loathing or remorse, particularly because they actively chose to reject faith after being invited to it. It signifies the severity of their choice and the profound disapproval from the Divine perspective for their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They will say: 'Our Lord, You have made us die twice and given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there any way to get out?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment acknowledging the justice of God. Having experienced both physical and spiritual death twice, they realize the reality of their sins and seek a way out of their predicament. Their plea highlights the finality and seriousness of divine judgment and the importance of recognizing and amending faults in one's lifetime.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because, when Allah alone was called upon, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgment is with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief of people who reject the oneness of Allah. When Allah alone is worshipped, they deny Him, but when others are associated with Him, they find it acceptable. This indicates a profound inconsistency and misplaced priorities in their belief system. The verse emphasizes that ultimate judgment and authority lie solely with Allah, who is exalted and supreme, underscoring the importance of pure monotheism and the futility of associating partners with God.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: He it is who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. But none remembers except those who turn in repentance.
interpretation: This verse underscores the signs of God's existence and power, observable in the natural world and the sustenance provided from the sky in forms such as rain. It emphasizes that only those who sincerely turn back to God, acknowledging their dependence on Him, will truly recognize and remember these divine signs. It invites believers to reflect on their surroundings and encourages a repentant heart, understanding that true remembrance of God comes through humility and acknowledgement of one's own shortcomings.
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So invoke Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of directing one's worship and supplications solely to Allah with genuine sincerity, irrespective of the opposition or displeasure from disbelievers. It acknowledges that true faith requires devotion that transcends external pressures and societal disdain, underscoring the strength and purity of one's belief in Allah alone.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: Exalted in rank, Owner of the Throne, He sends the Spirit of His command to whom He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's elevated status and sovereign authority. It emphasizes that God, who is exalted and possesses the Throne, chooses to bestow the divine message upon select individuals among His servants. These chosen individuals are entrusted with the responsibility to warn humanity about the Day of Meeting, which reflects the accountability and judgment awaiting in the hereafter. The 'Spirit' here typically refers to revelation or divine inspiration, underscoring the gravity and significance of the prophetic mission.
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: The Day they will come forth, nothing about them will be concealed from Allah. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allah, the One, the Irresistible.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment when all humans will be fully exposed to the divine scrutiny of Allah. Nothing about their deeds, intentions, or states will remain hidden from Him. The verse emphasizes the ultimate and exclusive sovereignty of Allah on that day, highlighting His unmatched and irresistible authority and power. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Surely, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each individual will receive the consequences of their actions, whether good or bad, with absolute fairness and without any form of injustice. Allah's justice is emphasized here, highlighting that He will account for every deed swiftly and accurately, ensuring that no one is wronged.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them of the Day of Approaching Death (the Day of Resurrection) when the hearts will be at the throats, filled (with distress). For the wrongdoers, there will be neither a devoted friend nor an intercessor who is obeyed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a dire warning about the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the sheer fear and anxiety that will grip individuals, to the extent that their hearts will feel as if they are in their throats. It starkly points out that the wrongdoers will find themselves utterly alone and bereft of any close friends or intercessors who can argue on their behalf or be heeded. The verse underscores both the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the severity of its consequences for those who have led their lives in injustice and sin.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah’s knowledge encompasses both the seen and the unseen, including the subtle, secretive actions and inner thoughts of individuals. It emphasizes that nothing escapes His awareness, not even the deceitful glances or the hidden emotions within the hearts, underscoring the importance of sincerity and integrity in both actions and thoughts.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge not with anything. Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the supreme authority and justice of Allah in contrast to the powerlessness of the false deities or intermediaries that people might worship alongside Him. It asserts that only Allah has the true ability to judge and execute justice with perfect knowledge and awareness, while the others have no real authority or capacity to make judgments. It emphasizes the attributes of Allah as all-hearing and all-seeing, reinforcing His omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and left stronger traces upon the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins. And they had not from Allah any protector.
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who are heedless and do not reflect upon the fate of previous nations who were superior in might and achievements but met their downfall due to their sins and transgressions. It emphasizes the principle that no human strength or legacy can protect one against divine retribution when it is decreed. It calls for humility and remembrance of divine accountability, encouraging believers to learn from historical precedents and adhere to moral and righteous conduct.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the clear signs and messages sent by Allah through His prophets. It signifies that Allah’s retribution is inevitable for those who persist in their disbelief despite being presented with clear evidence of the truth. The attributes of Allah being powerful and severe in punishment underscore the seriousness and the inevitable nature of divine justice.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And We did certainly send Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Prophet Moses (Musa) as a messenger equipped with both miraculous signs and clear, indisputable authority. The signs refer to the miracles bestowed upon him by Allah to demonstrate his legitimacy and divine backing. The 'clear authority' indicates his unequivocal ability to argue, guide, and lead his people effectively. It underscores the support that Allah provides to His chosen messengers to fulfill their missions.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, and they said, 'A lying magician.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the typical response of those in power who reject the messages of prophets. Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah dismiss the prophetic message by accusing the prophet of being a magician and a liar. This signifies the common tactic of those in authority to undermine truth and maintain their grip on power by discrediting and marginalizing those who challenge their legitimacy or call for spiritual and moral reform.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive.' But the plan of the disbelievers is not except in error.
interpretation: This verse addresses the reaction of the disbelievers to the truth brought by Moses from Allah. The disbelievers devised a cruel plan to kill the male offspring of those who believed and to spare their women, hoping to eradicate the believers. However, the verse emphasizes that such schemes by the disbelievers are ultimately doomed to fail, as they are founded on misguidance and error. It highlights the futility of opposing divine truth and assures that Allah's will prevails over the plots of those who deny Him.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Leave me to kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land.'
interpretation: Pharaoh expresses a desire to kill Moses, revealing his fear and insecurity. Despite recognizing Moses's divine connection, Pharaoh chooses to frame Moses as a potential threat to the societal and religious order. This reflects Pharaoh's unwillingness to accept change and highlights his authoritarian rule. His mention of corruption in the land represents a projected justification to maintain his control and suppress any challenge to his power.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: Moses said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Accountability.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Moses is addressing his people, declaring his reliance on God for protection against the arrogant individuals who deny the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the significance of humility and faith in the afterlife, and warns against the dangers of pride and disbelief. Moses models seeking divine refuge as a means to confront and overcome the challenges posed by such individuals, reinforcing the importance of steadfast faith in God's justice and accountability.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said, 'Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of that which he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and wisdom of a believer within Pharaoh's court who, despite the threat to his life, speaks out against the injustice of killing a man (Moses) simply for declaring faith in Allah. He appeals to logic by pointing out that if Moses is lying, it will not harm them, but if he is truthful, they will face dire consequences. It underscores that Allah does not support those who are excessive in their wrongdoing and deceitful, stressing the importance of integrity and truth in leadership and decision-making.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people, sovereignty is yours today, being dominant in the land. But who would protect us from the punishment of Allah if it came to us? Pharaoh said, 'I do not show you except what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct.'
interpretation: In this verse, an advisor or a member of Pharaoh's court addresses the people, warning them of Allah's potential punishment despite their current dominance. Pharaoh, however, dismisses this concern, presenting himself as the ultimate authority whose guidance should be followed. This showcases the arrogance and misguided leadership of Pharaoh, contrasting human authority with divine power and accountability. Pharaoh's statement reflects his delusion of self-righteousness and his intent to maintain control over his people by asserting his perceived infallibility.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And the one who believed said, 'O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the companies (the allied forces)'
interpretation: This verse reflects the concern of a believer for his people, warning them of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience to God. The 'day of the companies' refers to the coalition of tribes that waged war against the Muslims in the Battle of the Trench, signifying a dire punishment awaiting those who oppose divine guidance. It underscores the importance of heeding prophetic warnings to avoid collective calamity.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: Similar to the behavior of the people of Noah, and 'Aad, and Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not intend injustice for the servants.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the disbelieving nations of the past—such as those of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud—and the contemporary rejecters of the message. It serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by those who persist in disbelief and rebellion against divine guidance. The concluding part underscores Allah's justice, highlighting that any suffering or punishment is a result of people's own actions, and not because of any inherent desire of Allah to wrong His servants.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: O my people, I fear for you a Day of mutual calling (i.e., the Day of Judgment).
interpretation: This verse reflects a warning and a deep concern for the well-being of the community, emphasizing the impending reality of the Day of Judgment. The 'Day of mutual calling' signifies a time of accountability and distress where people will call out to each other for help and salvation. It is a reminder of the consequences of one's actions and the urgent need for righteousness and repentance.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: The Day you will turn your backs fleeing; no protector will you have from Allah. Whoever Allah leaves to stray - there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when people will attempt to flee from their fate, but there will be no one to protect them from the judgment of Allah. It emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah in guiding or leaving individuals to go astray. It underscores the concept that without Allah's guidance, no one can find the right path, and those whom He decides to let go astray will have no means of receiving guidance.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And there had certainly come to you Joseph before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt of that which he brought to you until, when he died, you said, 'Never will Allah send a messenger after him.' Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and skeptic.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the historical account of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) who came with clear signs and guidance. Despite his clear proofs, people continued to doubt and reject his message. Their skepticism persisted until his death, after which they assumed that no further messengers would come from Allah. This disbelief and stubbornness exemplify a mindset that leads to misguidance. The verse underscores the idea that those who consistently transgress and harbor doubt are left to stray by Allah as a result of their own persistent denial and wrongful actions.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who argue concerning the signs of Allah without any authority given to them—it is greatly abhorrent in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus, Allah seals up every heart of an arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals who dispute or challenge the veracity and authority of Allah's revelations without any justified basis or knowledge. Such actions are denounced not only by Allah but also by the believers. The verse warns that such prideful and defiant behaviors result in spiritual consequences, specifically, that Allah will seal the hearts of those who are arrogant and oppressive, making them impervious to guidance and truth.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build me a tower that I might reach the means.'
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh exhibits his arrogance and hubris by commanding Haman to construct a lofty tower, believing he can reach the means or ways leading to the heavens. This represents Pharaoh's delusion of earthly power and his desire to overstep his mortal bounds. The verse highlights the futility and ignorance of such pride, contrasting human limitations with divine omnipotence.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: The ways into the heavens, so that I may look at the God of Moses; but indeed, I think he is a liar.” And thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the (right) way. And the plot of Pharaoh did not end except in ruin.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the arrogance and delusion of Pharaoh, who falsely thinks that he can ascend to the heavens and confront the God of Moses to disprove him. His suspicion about Moses being a liar is ironic and arrogant, illustrating his denial of the truth. The verse also highlights how evil deeds can appear attractive to wrongdoers, leading them further astray. Ultimately, Pharaoh's scheming and plotting are destined for failure and destruction, underscoring the futility of opposing divine will.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: 'And the one who believed said: 'O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of righteousness.''
interpretation: The verse highlights the earnest plea of a believer who is calling his people to follow the path of righteousness, urging them to adhere to guidance that leads to moral and spiritual well-being. This reflects a sincere concern for the well-being of his community and emphasizes the importance of following divinely inspired guidance to achieve a righteous and prosperous life.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter is the home of permanent settlement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly life and contrasts it with the permanence of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to prioritize spiritual and eternal values over temporal and materialistic pursuits, urging believers to focus on their ultimate goal of attaining success in the Hereafter.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by the like thereof; but whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah in rewarding and punishing human actions. It underscores that evil deeds will be met with a precise and fair recompense, neither more nor less. Conversely, those who engage in righteous actions, irrespective of their gender, and possess genuine faith will be granted entry into Paradise. The limitless and bountiful provisions they will receive there reflect the boundless generosity of Allah, signifying an eternal reward that is beyond human measurement or comprehension.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people, why is it that I invite you to salvation while you invite me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the lament of a person who is sincerely calling his people towards guidance, truth, and salvation. He contrasts his noble invitation to the path of righteousness and deliverance with their contrary efforts to lead him towards misguidance, sin, and ultimately punishment in the Hellfire. The verse emphasizes the tragic irony and the deep concern of the caller for his people's welfare, highlighting the divergence between the paths of faith and disbelief.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse portrays a dialogue between someone resisting the pressure to abandon their faith in Allah and associate others with Him without any knowledge or justification. It also highlights the person's appeal to the inviting party to recognize and turn to Allah, who is powerful and forgiving. This emphasizes the dichotomy between misguided invitations towards disbelief and shirk (associating partners with Allah) versus the call to embrace the One true God who is both mighty and ever-forgiving.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: There is no doubt that what you call me to has no claim (to be invoked) in this world or in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and invalidity of calling upon entities other than Allah for help or guidance, highlighting that such entities hold no power either in this world or in the Hereafter. The verse further underscores the inevitable return of all beings to Allah for ultimate judgment. It concludes by stressing the fate of those who exceed the limits set by Allah, warning that transgressors will reside in the torment of the Fire. This serves as a powerful reminder of the oneness of Allah, the consequences of setting partners with Him, and the importance of adhering to His guidance.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: So you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: The speaker here is conveying a message of patience and trust in divine justice. By stating that others will remember the words being spoken later on, it implies the enduring truth and wisdom in the message. The act of entrusting one's affairs to Allah signifies complete reliance on and faith in God's perfect judgment and oversight. The affirmation that Allah is seeing of His servants reassures believers that their situations and struggles are fully known to God, who watches over and ultimately decides with fairness and mercy.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: So Allah protected him from the evils they plotted, and the people of Pharaoh were enveloped by the worst of punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection granted by Allah to the righteous against the schemes of their adversaries. It underscores the concept that while wicked people may plot and plan, ultimately, they cannot escape Allah's justice. The punishment that they intended for others will backfire on them, as seen in the fate of Pharaoh's people who faced severe retribution for their misdeeds. This serves as a reminder of the moral law of recompense and Allah's ultimate authority in delivering justice.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening. And the Day the Hour appears (it will be said), 'Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment.'
interpretation: This verse warns of the continuous and inescapable torment faced by wrongdoers, specifically the people of Pharaoh, in the afterlife. It highlights both the relentless nature of their punishment in the grave and the ultimate severe punishment awaiting them on the Day of Judgment. The dual exposure to the Fire—morning and evening—emphasizes the perpetual nature of their suffering and serves as a severe admonition against disbelief and tyranny.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And [mention] when they will dispute in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were followers of you, so can you avert from us a share of the Fire?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a scene from the Hereafter where the weak, who blindly followed the arrogant leaders in wrongdoing, are now in the Fire of Hell. They turn to their former leaders, asking for help and deliverance from their torment. This reflects the helplessness and despair of those who place their trust in misguided leadership and the reality that, in the afterlife, no one can alleviate the divine punishment decreed by Allah. It emphasizes accountability and the futility of relying on worldly power or influence in the face of divine justice.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant said, 'Indeed, all [of us] are in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the arrogant individuals who, despite their status or sense of superiority, acknowledge their shared fate with others in a situation of divine judgment. It underscores the ultimate authority of God in adjudicating between His servants, emphasizing that no earthly rank or arrogance can mitigate the equitable and inevitable judgment passed by Allah.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Supplicate your Lord to lighten for us a day from the punishment.'
interpretation: This verse shows a moment of desperation where the inhabitants of Hell are pleading with its keepers to request even a slight reprieve from their suffering. It reflects the intense regret and helplessness they feel, recognizing the severity of their punishment and understanding that it cannot be alleviated by their efforts alone. This plea to the guardians indicates their acknowledgment of the authority and mercy of God, even in their dire state.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They will say, 'Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?' They will say, 'Yes.' They will say, 'Then supplicate [yourselves], but the supplication of the disbelievers is not except in error.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment where disbelievers will be confronted with the fact that messengers were sent to them with clear signs and warnings. Despite acknowledging this truth, their attempts to supplicate or seek help will be futile as their rejection of faith has caused them to be in a state of misguidedness and error. It underscores the theme of accountability and the consequences of not heeding divine guidance.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's promise to aid His messengers and the believers both in their worldly life and in the Hereafter. In this life, they will receive divine support and guidance in their mission and through their trials. On the Day of Judgment, when everyone will be held accountable and witnesses will testify to their deeds, the believers will find Allah’s help in their favor, ensuring their ultimate success and salvation.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: On the Day when the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them; the curse will be upon them, and for them is the worst abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of the wrongdoers' attempts to justify their actions on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that their excuses will be of no avail, and they will face divine condemnation and a dreadful outcome. The 'curse' signifies God's rejection and the 'worst abode' refers to Hell, a place of ultimate punishment and suffering for their persistent wrongdoing and defiance of divine commandments.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And We certainly gave Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance provided to Prophet Moses and His people, the Israelites. It signifies the transmission of sacred knowledge and religious law through the scriptures, emphasizing the continuity and fidelity of God's messages through His prophets and their successors. This underscores the importance of divine guidance in maintaining faith and righteous living across generations.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: A guidance and a reminder for those endowed with understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as both a source of guidance and a reminder. It highlights that these benefits are particularly accessible to people of intelligence and discernment, referred to as 'those endowed with understanding.' It underscores the importance of reflection and comprehension in grasping the divine messages, suggesting that the teachings of the Qur'an become most effective when approached with a thoughtful and reflective mind.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and persistence in faith because the promise of Allah is true and certain. It also underscores the necessity of seeking forgiveness for one's sins, which reflects a state of humility and repentance. Moreover, it highlights the significance of glorifying and praising Allah regularly, both in the evening and the morning, as a means to maintain a constant connection with the Divine and to cultivate gratitude and mindfulness.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, there is nothing within their breasts except pride which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who argue against the signs and messages of Allah without any valid evidence or authority. It highlights that their motivations are driven by arrogance, an attribute they can never fulfill or justify. The verse concludes by advising believers to seek refuge in Allah, reaffirming His attributes as the All-Hearing and All-Seeing, implying that Allah is fully aware of the intentions and actions of all individuals.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grandeur and complexity of the creation of the heavens and the earth compared to the creation of humans. It emphasizes that despite human beings often seeing themselves as the pinnacle of creation, the cosmos and the earth are far vaster and more intricate. Additionally, it suggests a critique of human myopia, as many fail to recognize or appreciate the greater scale of creation beyond their own existence.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse draws a distinction between the spiritually blind and the seeing, symbolizing those who are ignorant of or reject divine guidance versus those who are aware and embrace it. It further contrasts the believers who engage in good deeds with those who commit misdeeds. The final part underscores human tendency to rarely reflect on these fundamental differences. Essentially, it calls for awareness, remembrance, and active pursuit of righteousness, highlighting the disparity in outcomes for different moral choices.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of the coming of the Day of Judgment, reinforcing that there should be no skepticism about its occurrence. Despite this, it highlights a common human disposition: many people remain heedless or in denial about this inevitable truth, often due to material distractions or lack of spiritual awareness. It serves as both a warning and a call to faith, urging believers to prepare for this inevitable reality.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supplication (dua) in one's relationship with God. It assures believers that God is always listening and ready to answer their prayers. However, it also serves as a warning to those who arrogantly neglect worship and supplication, stating that such disdainful behavior will lead to their downfall and punishment in Hell. This underscores the value of humility and devotion in Islamic faith.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom and mercy in creating a natural order that benefits humanity, specifically the alternation of night and day. The night is designed for rest, providing a necessary respite for the body and mind. The day, on the other hand, is illuminated to allow people to go about their activities and fulfill their needs. This balance reflects Allah's care for human well-being and serves as a reminder of His continuous favor and generosity. However, the verse also points out a common human failing: ingratitude. Despite the clear signs of Allah's grace, many people fail to appreciate and acknowledge these blessings in their daily lives.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator and Lord of all that exists. It calls out the futility and error of turning away from Allah and being misled into believing in false deities or ideologies. It serves as a reminder of the clear evidence of Allah's existence and attributes, urging believers to recognize and worship Him alone.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus do those who deny the signs of Allah turn away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent nature of those who reject Allah's signs and guidance. It emphasizes the commonality among disbelievers across different times, indicating a deliberate and conscious decision to turn away from divine truth, resulting in their misguidance. This turning away is portrayed as a consistent behavior among those who refuse to acknowledge Allah's revelations.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: Allah is the One who made for you the earth as a place of settlement and the sky as a canopy, and shaped you, and perfected your shapes, and provided for you from the good things. That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs of Allah's creation and the bounties He has provided for humans. It underscores the earth being a stable place, the sky serving as a protective structure, the perfection in human creation, and the provision of good sustenance. These are signs to recognize Allah's greatness, urging believers to reflect on the blessings and the power of their Creator, celebrating His majesty and dominion over all the worlds.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unique and exclusive divinity of Allah, affirming that He is the only deity worthy of worship. It highlights His eternal life and existence, urging believers to invoke and worship Him with sincere devotion and purity in their faith. The verse concludes by praising Allah's dominion over all creation, acknowledging His supreme authority and sovereignty as the Lord of all worlds.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah since clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic tenet of monotheism, highlighting that worship should be directed solely towards Allah. It underscores the prohibition against idolatry or associating others with Allah in worship. Furthermore, the verse reflects the necessity to heed the clear signs and revelations provided by Allah, which guide believers towards the truth. The instruction to submit to 'the Lord of the worlds' signifies ultimate obedience and surrender to Allah’s will, reinforcing the centrality of tawhid (the oneness of God) in Islam.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: He is the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you forth as a child, then [He develops you] so that you reach your [time of] maturity, then [further] so that you become elderly. And among you is he who is taken in death before [that], so that you may reach a specified term; and perhaps you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse tracks the stages of human creation and life as a demonstration of God's power and plan. It begins with the initial creation of humanity from dust, highlighting the humble beginnings of humans. It then follows the biological stages of human development from conception to old age, illustrating the natural progression and the divine planning involved in each phase. The mention of death at various stages serves as a reminder of the fragility of life and the predetermined nature of each person's lifespan. Ultimately, it aims to encourage reflection and understanding of the divine wisdom and purpose behind human existence.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: He is the one who gives life and causes death, and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over life and death. It underscores that everything in existence operates under His command and will. The phrase 'Be, and it is' signifies His effortless ability to create and enact His will, highlighting His omnipotence and the immediacy of His divine commands.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, how they are turned away?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, all believers, pointing to the perplexing behavior of people who argue against the divine revelations. Despite the clarity and truth of Allah's signs, these individuals are led astray due to their obstinacy and denial. It underscores the futility of their arguments and depicts a sense of bewilderment at their rejection of evident truths, implying that such deviation is a result of their own choices and the consequences thereof.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who deny the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers, they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject or deny the divine revelations and messages sent through the prophets. It serves as a warning that their disbelief and rejection of the divine guidance will not go without consequence. They will ultimately realize the truth and the gravity of their denial, facing the consequences in the hereafter.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When shackles are around their necks and chains; they will be dragged.
interpretation: This verse is describing the severe punishment and humiliation faced by the wrongdoers in the hereafter. The imagery of shackles and chains symbolizes the inescapable and harsh consequences of their actions, indicating that their deeds have led them to a state of utter subjugation and despair.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: Into boiling water, then they will be burned in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment awaiting those who deny the truth and lead a life of sin. It signifies that they will first be subjected to extreme torment through immersion in boiling water and then burnt in the fire. This serves as a powerful warning to believers about the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, urging them to adhere to the path of righteousness.
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, 'Where are those [false gods] you used to associate [with Him]?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and falsehood of associating partners with Allah. On the Day of Judgment, those who indulged in polytheism will be confronted with the stark reality of their erroneous beliefs. They will be questioned about the deities they wrongly revered and relied upon, emphasizing that no false god can offer them any support or deliverance. This serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of monotheism and the ultimate accountability for one’s beliefs and actions.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: They will say, 'They have deserted us,' but, in fact, we were not invoking anything before.' Thus does Allah lead the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and realization of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They acknowledge that the deities they worshipped besides Allah have abandoned them, recognizing that those entities were powerless and unworthy of worship. Their false beliefs and practices led them astray, and as a result, Allah allowed them to persist in their misguidance. The verse emphasizes the futility of idolatry and the consequences of rejecting true guidance.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you used to rejoice on the earth without right and you used to be insolent.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who found joy and arrogance in their wrongful acts and behaviors on earth. It admonishes such individuals for their unjustified happiness and excessive pride, indicating that these attitudes and actions have led to their deserving consequences. The context suggests a moral lesson about the dangers of rejoicing in harmful or unjust deeds and the importance of humility and righteousness.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and prideful, highlighting the severe consequences of such behavior. The mention of entering the gates of Hell and the eternal suffering therein underscores the gravity of arrogance and pride in the eyes of Allah. It emphasizes the divine justice that awaits those who persist in their hubris, reminding believers to cultivate humility and righteousness in their lives.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes patience and reliance on the certainty of Allah's promise. It reassures that regardless of whether the consequences of the disbelievers’ actions are witnessed by the Prophet during his lifetime or not, ultimate accountability and return to Allah are unavoidable. The call to patience is a reminder that Allah’s plans are precise and His justice will manifest, providing comfort and perseverance in the face of adversity.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you; among them are those [whose stories] We have related to you, and among them are those [whose stories] We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign [or verse] except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth, and the falsifiers will thereupon lose [all].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent many messengers over time, some of whose stories are known and others unknown. It underscores that these messengers could only perform miracles or bring signs by the permission of Allah, highlighting their dependence on divine will. Ultimately, it assures that when Allah's judgment is decreed, it will be executed justly, reaffirming that those who deny the truth and propagate falsehood will face ruin in the end.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: It is Allah who made for you the grazing animals upon which you ride, and some of them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's benevolence and providence by emphasizing how He has provided humans with livestock that serve multiple essential purposes. These animals are not only a means of transport but also a source of sustenance. It underscores the divine wisdom in the creation and the blessings bestowed upon humans, encouraging them to reflect on and be grateful for these provisions. Additionally, it serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of life and the sustenance system put in place by Allah.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And you have in them [various] benefits and that you may satisfy upon them a need in your breasts; and upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted benefits of the animals that God has provided humankind. Beyond serving as sources of direct material benefit, like food and clothing, these animals also fulfill deeper, personal needs within people, such as the desire for transportation and carrying burdens. This dual role of provision and convenience underscores a broader divine wisdom in the creation of living beings, emphasizing humanity's reliance on God's provision for both essential and auxiliary purposes.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah will you deny?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the numerous signs and miracles from Allah visible in the creation and in lives. It challenges the reader to acknowledge these signs and reflect on their divine origin. Denial of such signs would imply a deliberate disregard for the omnipotence and wisdom of Allah, prompting self-reflection on one's belief and acknowledgment of divine evidence.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in power and in the traces they left on the earth. But all that they used to earn availed them not.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the fate of previous civilizations that were mightier and more affluent yet ultimately faced destruction due to their misdeeds. It emphasizes the impermanence of worldly power and wealth, highlighting that these cannot save one from divine retribution. By urging believers to learn from history, it serves as a reminder of the consequences of ignoring divine guidance and the importance of leading a righteous life.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the arrogance and ignorance of those who mocked divine guidance brought by the messengers. It highlights their misplaced confidence in their own knowledge, which led them to dismiss and ridicule the clear signs and proofs presented to them. Ultimately, their mockery and rejection of the truth brought about their downfall, showing that true understanding and salvation come from heeding divine messages, not from human pride or knowledge.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: But when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and reject that which we used to associate with Him."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reaction of people when they face divine retribution. It highlights their sudden realization and acknowledgment of the oneness of Allah, rejecting all forms of shirk (associating partners with Allah) which they had previously engaged in. This reflects the immense impact of witnessing divine punishment, pushing individuals to recognize and admit the truth of monotheism, albeit at a point where it might be too late for redemption.
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: But their faith could not benefit them once they saw Our punishment. This is Allah’s way that has always been, regarding His servants. And there the disbelievers lost all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith must be genuine and timely. It highlights that once divine punishment arrives, it is too late for repentance or belief to be of any benefit. This verse serves as a warning that God's established way is consistent: people are given ample opportunity to believe and obey, but once His judgment is enacted, those who persist in disbelief will face inevitable loss and regret.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation: Ha Mim.
interpretation: These letters are among the mysterious letters that appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their exact meaning is unknown, and they are considered one of the miracles of the Qur'an. They may serve to draw attention, indicate a form of divine challenge, or as a sign of the inimitability of the Qur'anic text. Scholars also suggest that they could be an invocation or have a symbolic and esoteric significance known only to God.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message of the Qur'an is a direct revelation from Allah, who is characterized by immense mercy and compassion. It implies that the guidance within the Qur'an stems from divine kindness and is intended to benefit humanity. By invoking these attributes, the verse reassures believers of the benevolent nature of the divine message they are receiving.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a comprehensive and detailed scripture, presented in the Arabic language, which is intended for those who seek knowledge and understanding. The use of 'Arabic Qur'an' highlights the importance of the language for clear conveyance of its message, and ‘for a people who know’ underscores the necessity of seeking and using knowledge to comprehend and implement its teachings.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: As a bringer of good tidings and a warner. But most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the Prophet as a giver of glad tidings and a warner. Despite his efforts, the majority of people ignore his message and refuse to listen. It highlights human tendencies to reject guidance and the consequences of such heedlessness.
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they say, 'Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition. So work; indeed, we are working.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the rejection and resistance faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from some people who were stubborn and unwilling to accept the message of Islam. Their hearts were metaphorically 'covered', implying they were not open to understanding the truth. The 'deafness' in their ears signifies their intentional ignorance, and the 'partition' indicates a deliberate separation or barrier they created between themselves and the Prophet. This resistance and opposition to the divine message required continued perseverance and effort from both parties in their respective beliefs and actions.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, 'I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that he is a mortal messenger chosen to convey divine revelation, affirming the oneness of God. It calls believers to follow a righteous path directed towards God and seek His forgiveness, while warning against the grave sin of associating partners with God, which leads to severe consequences.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give the zakat and, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving zakat (charitable alms) in Islam, linking the act of charity directly to faith. It indicates that failing to give zakat is not just a lapse in social responsibility, but a sign of disbelief in the Hereafter. The verse suggests that belief in the afterlife should naturally lead one to be charitable and fulfill their religious obligations, and neglecting this duty is equated with a rejection of faith in the life to come.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the connection between faith and actions in Islamic teaching. It asserts that true belief in God must be reflected in one's deeds, particularly in righteous actions. For those who uphold this principle, the verse promises a continuous and unending reward. This can be understood not only as the eternal rewards of the afterlife but also as the spiritual fulfillment and peace that accompanies living a life of faith and good deeds. The phrase 'غير ممنون' suggests that this reward is not subject to cessation or diminution, indicating its permanence and perpetuity.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, 'Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief of people who reject the Creator of the earth and attribute partners or equals to Him. It emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that He alone is the Creator of all things within a specific timeframe. The verse serves as a reminder and a reprimand against associating others with Allah, affirming His unique status as the Lord of all worlds and calling for acknowledgment of His divine authority and oneness.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed on it (the earth) firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days without distinction - for [the information of] those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's deliberate and meticulous creation of the earth, emphasizing the stability provided by mountains, the blessing and provision of sustenance for all living beings, and the systematic ordaining of resources over a specific period. It suggests a divine order, balance, and purpose in the creation, catering to the needs and inquiries of those who seek knowledge and understanding of divine wisdom.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come into being, willingly or by compulsion.' They said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the majestic command of Allah in creating the universe. The heavens and the earth were initially in a primordial, chaotic state described as 'smoke.' Allah's command for them to come into existence—whether they complied willingly or under duress—signifies the absolute submission of all creation to the divine will. It emphasizes that the creation of the universe was an intentional act by Allah, orchestrated with precision, power, and authority. The response 'We come willingly' conveys the inherent obedience and subservience of all elements of creation to God's will.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: And He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in the creation of the heavens. By stating that the seven heavens were completed in two days and each was given its own command, it reflects the meticulous planning and order within creation. The mention of adorning the nearest heaven with lamps (interpreted as stars) highlights the beauty and purposefulness in the design of the universe. The final part underscores Allah's attributes of might and comprehensive knowledge, indicating that everything is precisely measured and intentionally crafted by Him.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: But if they turn away, then say, 'I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the message of Islam. It refers to the historical punishments that befell the ancient peoples of 'Aad and Thamud due to their persistent disobedience and rejection of their prophets. The reference to a 'thunderbolt' indicates a sudden and severe punishment from God. The verse highlights the importance of heeding divine warnings and the potential consequences of ignoring them.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, [saying], 'Worship not except Allah.' They said, 'If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down the angels. So indeed we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and disbelief of certain communities when faced with divine guidance. Despite receiving clear messages from prophets, they chose to reject the message of monotheism by demanding a miraculous sign, specifically the appearance of angels, as proof of divine will. Their response reflects a deep-seated refusal to accept the prophets' call to worship only Allah, indicating a challenge to the authenticity and authority of the messengers.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: As for 'Aad, they behaved arrogantly upon the earth without right, and they said, 'Who is stronger than us in might?' Did they not see that Allah who created them was stronger than them in might? But they were rejecting Our signs.
interpretation: 'Aad represents a people who, consumed by their arrogance, believed in their own unparalleled strength and dismissed any force greater than their own. This verse underscores the folly of their pride by pointing out the obvious: the Creator, Allah, who brought them into being, wields far greater power than any of His creations. Yet, despite clear signs and evidence of this truth, they persisted in their denial. The lesson conveyed is the danger of arrogance and the importance of recognizing and submitting to the supreme power and signs of Allah.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: So We unleashed upon them a furious wind for ˹several˺ miserable days to make them taste the torment of disgrace in this worldly life. But the torment of the Hereafter will be far more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse discusses the consequences faced by a disobedient people, symbolized by the 'furious wind' sent against them. It serves as a divine punishment for their wrongdoing, making them experience disgrace and misery in their current life as a forewarning of an even worse fate in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of divine retribution and stresses that none will be able to assist or save them from this decree.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of the Thamud people who were provided with guidance by Allah but chose to reject it in favor of their misguided ways. It serves as a stern reminder that preferring misguidance over divine guidance leads to severe consequences, represented here by the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment. This punishment is directly correlated with their deeds and choices, emphasizing accountability and the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in wrongdoing despite clear signs and guidance.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection and deliverance granted to those who possess both faith and piety. It underscores the importance of maintaining a steadfast belief in Allah and a consciousness of His commands and prohibitions. The combination of belief and piety ensures that individuals align their actions with their faith, leading to their salvation from trials and afflictions.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: On the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the opponents of Allah will be assembled and driven towards Hellfire. It emphasizes the ultimate consequence of their opposition to divine guidance, portraying a scene of organized and inevitable punishment, highlighting the seriousness and certainty of divine retribution for disbelief and enmity towards God's commands.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable moment of truth on the Day of Judgment, where individuals will confront their actions. Their own faculties—hearing, sight, and skin—will serve as witnesses against them, detailing their deeds. It underscores the theme of accountability and the veracity of divine justice, where no action, whether concealed or overt, can escape the all-encompassing witness of one's own body parts. It admonishes people to be mindful of their actions, considering the ultimate and unavoidable scrutiny they will face.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: They will say to their skins, 'Why have you testified against us?' They will say, 'We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and the comprehensive nature of Allah's knowledge and power. On the Day of Judgment, even people's own bodies will testify to their actions, underscoring that nothing can be hidden from Allah. It showcases the ultimate authority of Allah over all creation, demonstrating how everything in existence, including human faculties, is under His command and will ultimately return to Him for judgment.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you were not covering yourselves, lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to conceal their actions from others while forgetting that they cannot hide anything from Allah. It underscores the false assumption that God's knowledge is limited, reminding believers of the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. This serves as a caution against hypocrisy and encourages sincerity and awareness that every action and even the inner thoughts are known to Allah, who will hold everyone accountable on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a caution against harboring false assumptions or doubts about Allah. It underscores the consequences of such erroneous beliefs, leading to spiritual and moral downfall. The 'assumption' refers to a lack of faith or misunderstanding about Allah's nature and power, which results in ultimate failure and loss. The verse aims to remind believers to maintain a correct and sincere understanding of their Lord to avoid ruin and be among those who are successful.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: If they are patient, the Fire will be a residence for them; and if they seek to appease, they will not be among those who are allowed to appease.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable and inescapable nature of divine punishment for certain wrongdoers. It suggests that endurance or patience will not alleviate their suffering in Hell, and even if they seek forgiveness or try to justify their actions, they will not be granted reprieve. It serves as a stern warning about the severity and absolute nature of the consequences of their misconduct.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them. And the word has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse conveys the notion that certain individuals are influenced by companions, whether human or jinn, who beautify and rationalize their past and future misdeeds. This illusion and misguidance lead them to persist in error and sin. The consequence of their actions places them among those who have previously faced divine judgment and suffered loss as a result of their failure to heed divine guidance. Thus, it serves as a warning about the detrimental impact of surrounding oneself with negative influences and the inevitability of accountability.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the strategy of the disbelievers who aimed to obstruct the message of the Qur'an by preventing others from listening to it and creating distractions. Their motivation was to maintain their influence and prevent the transformative impact of the Qur'anic revelations on the community. It reflects an attempt to undermine the message of truth through deliberate interference.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So We will surely let those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate consequence for those who reject faith and persist in their misdeeds. It emphasizes that divine justice will ensure severe punishment for their disbelief and that they will face the harshest recompense for their immoral actions. The passage serves as a warning, highlighting the gravity of disbelief and unethical behavior in the eyes of God and the certainty of accountability in the hereafter.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah—the Fire. For them therein will be the home of eternity as recompense for what they used to, of Our signs, reject.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence for those who oppose the messages and signs of Allah. It presents the fire of Hell as the permanent abode for such individuals, underscoring that their punishment is directly related to their persistent denial and rejection of divine revelations. The eternal nature of their dwelling in the Fire serves as a powerful deterrent and a grave warning to those who choose to be adversaries of God's guidance.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieve will say: 'Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men - we will put them under our feet so they will be among the lowest.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the sentiments of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, expressing their desire for retribution against those who misled them. They wish to humiliate their deceivers, both from the jinn and humankind, by placing them under their feet, thereby expressing their anger and desire for them to be in a position of extreme disgrace and suffering. This indicates the intense regret and realization of the consequences of being misled from the path of righteousness.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remained steadfast - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], 'Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of true faith and steadfastness.
