It also serves as a stern reminder of the Day of Judgment, when all falsehood and those who propagate it will be exposed and suffer loss. The verse calls for reflection on one's actions and beliefs in anticipation of that inevitable day of divine justice.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يخسر المبطلون

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling, every nation will be called to its record [and told], 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid and powerful scene of the Day of Judgment where every nation and community is depicted as kneeling, symbolizing submission and humility before God's absolute authority. Each nation will be summoned to answer for its own deeds based on the record of their actions. The term 'kneeling' conveys a sense of urgency, respect, and recognition of the gravity of the moment. The recompense mentioned signifies that individuals and groups will be held accountable for their actions and will receive just rewards or punishments accordingly. This verse underscores the themes of accountability, divine justice, and the inevitability of the final judgment.
orig: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: This is Our book that speaks of you in truth. Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine accountability. It implies that on the Day of Judgment, one's deeds will be transparently recorded and presented as an accurate account of their actions. The phrase 'Our book' refers to this divine record, which speaks truthfully, underscoring God's omniscient nature and justice. It serves as a reminder for believers to live righteously, knowing that all actions, good or bad, are being recorded and will be reviewed.
orig: هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

translation: As for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.
interpretation: This verse highlights the integral Islamic principle that faith must be coupled with righteous actions. It promises believers who embody both attributes the ultimate reward of divine mercy. Such a reward is characterized as the 'clear triumph,' emphasizing the supreme nature of this spiritual success compared to worldly achievements. It serves to motivate believers to engage consistently in good deeds, paired with sincere faith, to attain Allah's encompassing mercy and ultimate success in the hereafter.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيدخلهم ربهم في رحمته ذلك هو الفوز المبين

translation: But as for those who disbelieved: Were My revelations not recited to you? Yet you were arrogant and became a guilty people.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who disbelieved, noting that despite having been exposed to the divine revelations, they responded with arrogance and chose to persist in their wrongdoing and disbelief, thereby becoming a guilty and sinful people. It emphasizes the rejection of truth due to pride and its consequences on one's moral state.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا أفلم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فاستكبرتم وكنتم قوما مجرمين

translation: And when it is said that the promise of Allah is true and the Hour – there is no doubt about its coming, you said, 'We do not know what the Hour is. We assume it to be nothing but conjecture, and we are not convinced.'
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who, upon being reminded of the certainty of Allah's promise and the coming of the Last Hour, respond with skepticism and doubt. Instead of believing in the clarity and truth of the Divine promise, they treat it as mere speculation. Their lack of conviction and certainty in such fundamental matters points to a deeper spiritual deficiency and a refusal to heed clear signs and warnings from God.
orig: وإذا قيل إن وعد الله حق والساعة لا ريب فيها قلتم ما ندري ما الساعة إن نظن إلا ظنا وما نحن بمستيقنين

translation: And the evil consequences of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable realization and manifestation of the negative consequences of one's actions. It signifies that those who mockingly disregard or ridicule divine warnings and moral guidance will eventually face the consequences of their actions, becoming enveloped by the very reality they once derided. The verse underscores the importance of sincerity and heedfulness in one’s conduct, as the ultimate accountability and recompense are inescapable.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And it will be said, 'Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours; and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the repercussions of ignoring divine guidance and the Hereafter. It illustrates that those who neglect their duty towards God and disregard the reality of the Day of Judgment will face dire consequences. On that day, they will find no assistance or refuge except the Fire, symbolizing divine retribution for their actions in this world. The mention of 'forgetting' underscores the reciprocal nature of their neglect and the severe spiritual abandonment they will experience as a result.
orig: وقيل اليوم ننساكم كما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: That is because you took the signs of Allah in jest and the life of this world deceived you. So today they will not be removed from it, nor will they be asked to appease (Allah).
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who mock the signs of Allah and are deluded by worldly life. It serves as a stern warning that such individuals will face a day of reckoning where they will neither escape punishment nor be given a chance to seek forgiveness. It underscores the gravity of disregarding divine guidance and prioritizing temporal pleasures over spiritual responsibilities.
orig: ذلكم بأنكم اتخذتم آيات الله هزوا وغرتكم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم لا يخرجون منها ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: So all praise is to Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive sovereignty and majesty of Allah. By acknowledging Allah as the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it recognizes His absolute authority over all creation. It calls for gratitude and praise to be directed solely to Him, who sustains and rules over the entire universe and everything within it.
orig: فلله الحمد رب السماوات ورب الأرض رب العالمين

translation: To Him belongs all grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and majesty of Allah over the entire universe. It highlights His supreme authority and unmatched wisdom. The terms 'Almighty' and 'Wise' indicate that His power is immense and coupled with perfect wisdom, meaning that His decisions and actions are always just and prudent. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine grandeur that encompasses all creation, both in the heavens and on earth.
orig: وله الكبرياء في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Ha Meem.
interpretation: These are two of the 'mysterious letters' or 'Muqatta'at' that appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. The exact meaning and purpose of these letters are not definitively known; they are considered a divine mystery. Scholars have various interpretations, but generally, they are seen as a unique feature of the Qur'anic text that adds to its inimitability and miraculous nature. They underscore the transcendental nature of the revelation and the limitations of human comprehension.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation directly to Allah, who possesses both might and wisdom. It underscores that the content of the Qur'an is not of human origin but from a supreme and all-knowing source. The attributes 'All-Mighty' and 'All-Wise' highlight that Allah has the power to protect and enforce the message of the Qur'an while also possessing the wisdom to guide humanity through its teachings.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything between them except with truth and for an appointed term. Yet those who disbelieve are turning away from what they have been warned about.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe and all that is within it is purposeful, not random, and follows divine justice and order. It also indicates that everything has a predetermined lifespan or end. The verse further underscores the obstinacy of the disbelievers who choose to ignore the divine warnings and messages meant for their guidance. It serves as a reminder of accountability and the consequences of heedlessness.
orig: ما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى والذين كفروا عما أنذروا معرضون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a scripture before this or a remaining trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges those who worship other than Allah to reflect upon the objects of their worship and question their abilities and roles in creation. It asks them to consider whether their deities had any part in creating the earth or have any power in the heavens. It invites them to present any scriptural evidence or remnants of knowledge that support their claims. Essentially, the verse highlights the futility of idol worship and underscores the exclusive sovereignty and creative power of Allah.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا أو أثارة من علم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And who is more astray than one who invokes besides Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and misguidance of those who call upon others besides Allah, seeking help or intercession. These entities, whether they are idols, spirits, or deceased beings, are incapable of responding to their supplications and remain oblivious to such calls. The verse underlines the ultimate truth that only Allah has the power to respond to prayers and underscores the importance of monotheism and reliance upon the One True God.
orig: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة وهم عن دعائهم غافلون

translation: And when the people are gathered, they [false deities] will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idol worship and other forms of false deities that people may follow. On the Day of Judgment, these false deities will not advocate on behalf of their followers; instead, they will disown and oppose them. This emphasizes the theme of accountability and reinforces the importance of worshipping only Allah, who is the true and just deity deserving of worship. It reflects the transient and deceptive nature of misplaced faith in anything other than the One True God.
orig: وإذا حشر الناس كانوا لهم أعداء وكانوا بعبادتهم كافرين

translation: But when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the reaction of disbelievers when confronted with the clear and evident signs or verses of the Qur’an. Despite the clarity and self-evident truth of these divine revelations, the disbelievers dismiss them as mere magic. This dismissal represents their refusal to accept the message and guidance contained in the Qur'an, choosing instead to undermine its divine origin by attributing it to sorcery. This reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an of disbelief and the various ways in which truth is rejected by those unwilling to acknowledge it.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم هذا سحر مبين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Say, 'If I have fabricated it, you will not hold anything against me from Allah. He is most knowing of what you are involved in. Sufficient is He as Witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations made by opponents of the Prophet Muhammad, who claim that he has fabricated the Qur'an. The Prophet is instructed to respond by stating that if he indeed fabricated it, they would have no power to protect him from Allah's judgment. This conveys the message that Allah is fully aware of the truth and the actions of all individuals. It underlines the notion of divine justice, emphasizing that Allah is the ultimate witness and judge. It concludes by highlighting Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that despite the accusations and wrongdoing, Allah's nature is inclined towards forgiveness and compassion.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فلا تملكون لي من الله شيئا هو أعلم بما تفيضون فيه كفى به شهيدا بيني وبينكم وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, 'I am not something original among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am nothing but a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and humanity of Prophet Muhammad, acknowledging that he is not different from the previous messengers sent by God. It also underscores the idea that the Prophet himself does not have knowledge of the unseen future for himself or his followers; instead, his role is to faithfully follow the divine revelation given to him and to deliver a clear warning to the people. The verse underlines the importance of revelation in Islam and the Prophet's commitment to his duty as a messenger without claiming any special power or knowledge beyond that which is bestowed upon him by God.
orig: قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل وما أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي وما أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if it (the Qur'an) is from Allah and you disbelieve in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you were arrogant?' Surely, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers by asking them to reflect on the possibility that the Qur'an might indeed be from Allah, especially considering that a knowledgeable individual among the Children of Israel has recognized the truth in it and believed. Their disbelief, coupled with arrogance, is presented as a barrier to guidance. Allah does not guide those who commit injustice by rejecting the truth and displaying arrogance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله وكفرتم به وشهد شاهد من بني إسرائيل على مثله فآمن واستكبرتم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it.' And when they do not guide themselves by it, they will say, 'This is an ancient falsehood.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and dismissive attitude of disbelievers towards the believers and the divine message they have accepted. The disbelievers argue that if the belief held by the believers were genuinely beneficial, they themselves would have recognized it first. This reflects their pride and reluctance to accept that others might have insight that they do not. Additionally, their final claim that the guidance is merely an 'ancient falsehood' underscores their stubbornness and refusal to open their minds to new truth.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه وإذ لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم

translation: And before it was the Scripture of Moses as a guide and a mercy. And this (Qur'an) is a confirming Book in an Arabic tongue, to warn those who have wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of divine revelation by acknowledging the Torah, given to Moses, as a guide and a mercy. It emphasizes that the Qur'an, revealed in clear Arabic, confirms and upholds the previous scriptures. The purpose of the Qur'an is to warn those who commit injustice and to give glad tidings to those who do good, underscoring the Qur'an's role in moral guidance and its universal message of righteousness.
orig: ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا لينذر الذين ظلموا وبشرى للمحسنين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remained steadfast - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and emotional security granted to those who sincerely recognize Allah as their Lord and maintain a steadfast path of righteousness and faith. The promise of freedom from fear and sorrow signifies both a reward in the Hereafter and a state of inner peace in this life, embodying the ultimate assurance of divine protection and guidance.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and reward in the Hereafter. It assures the believers that their righteous deeds and steadfastness in faith will be duly rewarded with eternal abode in Paradise. The verse highlights the inseparable link between one's actions in this world and the recompense they will receive in the afterlife, underscoring the core Islamic principle of accountability and the ultimate reward for piety and righteousness.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الجنة خالدين فيها جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: We have enjoined upon man (care) for his parents. His mother carried him, (increasing her) in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the (final) destination. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in (this) world with kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me (in repentance). Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and showing kindness to one's parents while acknowledging the hardships the mother endures during pregnancy and early child-rearing. It also highlights a critical moment in life, at the age of maturity (often considered forty), when an individual reflects on gratitude and responsibility—both to God and to parents. The verse encourages supplication for the ability to do good deeds pleasing to God and to seek righteousness for one's descendants. It underscores a turning point marked by repentance and conscious submission to Islam, reinforcing the balance between filial piety and obedience to divine commands.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه إحسانا حملته أمه كرها ووضعته كرها وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا حتى إذا بلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة قال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأصلح لي في ذريتي إني تبت إليك وإني من المسلمين

translation: They are those from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. [They will be] among the companions of Paradise, [in fulfillment of] the true promise which they had been promised.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness. It highlights that God will accept the best deeds of the believers and forgive their sins, ensuring them a place in Paradise. This promise of Paradise is a truthful and assured promise from God, offering hope and encouragement to the faithful to strive towards good and rely on Divine mercy for their shortcomings.
orig: أولئك الذين نتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم في أصحاب الجنة وعد الصدق الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: But the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be raised up when generations before me have already passed on?' while they call to Allah for help [and say], 'Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth.' But he says, 'This is not but legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the defiant attitude of an individual who dismisses his parents' warnings about the afterlife. His disrespectful exclamation shows his rejection of the resurrection and divine accountability. The parents, anxious and distressed, plead with him to believe in Allah's promise, emphasizing its truth. However, the individual remains stubborn, considering the warnings as mere myths of ancient times. This highlights a broader theme in the Qur'an of struggling between faith and disbelief, and the challenges faced by believers in guiding their loved ones.
orig: والذي قال لوالديه أف لكما أتعدانني أن أخرج وقد خلت القرون من قبلي وهما يستغيثان الله ويلك آمن إن وعد الله حق فيقول ما هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable consequence faced by those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelief. It draws a parallel with previous nations, among both jinn and human beings, who disregarded divine guidance and thus met their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate loss encountered by those who choose a path of transgression and highlights the universality of this divine principle across different communities and generations.
orig: أولئك الذين حق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And for all are degrees [rewarded] for what they have done. And He will fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and accountability before Allah. It highlights that every individual will be rewarded or compensated according to the deeds they have performed, with varying levels or degrees of recompense. Furthermore, it reassures that these recompenses will be equitable, and no one will face any form of injustice or unfair treatment. The divine justice system is such that each action is meticulously accounted for and rewarded fairly.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وليوفيهم أعمالهم وهم لا يظلمون

translation: On the Day when those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, [it will be said], 'You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation because you were arrogant upon the earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the fate of those who disbelieved and indulged in the pleasures of the worldly life without consideration for the afterlife. It serves as a stark reminder that earthly indulgences, when accompanied by arrogance and disobedience to divine commandments, lead to severe consequences in the hereafter. The 'extreme humiliation' and punishment they face are a direct result of their arrogance and defiance of righteousness on earth.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون

translation: And mention the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in the [region of] al-Ahqaf - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - [saying], 'Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Ad in the region of al-Ahqaf. It emphasizes the continuous warning from various prophets both before and after Hud, urging people to worship only Allah. Hud's warning highlights the severe consequences of idolatry and disobedience to Allah, emphasizing his fear for their fate on the Day of Judgment. The repetition of messages across different prophets underscores the consistency and importance of monotheism in Islamic teachings.
orig: واذكر أخا عاد إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف وقد خلت النذر من بين يديه ومن خلفه ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said: 'Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the defiance and skepticism of the people who are addressed by the prophet. They challenge the legitimacy of the prophet's message and demand immediate proof of the promised consequences. It illustrates their attachment to their own beliefs and their demand for tangible validation before accepting any change.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I was sent with, but I see you are a people who are ignorant.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker emphasizes that ultimate knowledge belongs only to Allah, underscoring human limitations in understanding divine matters. By conveying the message sent by Allah, the speaker is fulfilling his prophetic duty, contrasting the divine guidance with the ignorance of the people he addresses. This highlights the recurrent theme in the Qur'an of prophets facing rejection and misunderstanding from their communities.
orig: قال إنما العلم عند الله وأبلغكم ما أرسلت به ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: But when they saw it as a dense cloud approaching their valleys, they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.' Rather, it is that for which you were impatient: a wind, within it a painful punishment.
interpretation: In this verse, the people perceive a thick cloud approaching and assume it will bring the much-needed rain. However, God clarifies that this cloud, which they eagerly awaited, is not bringing rain, but rather a devastating wind with severe punishment. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of their impatience and disbelief, underscoring the importance of faith and the potential for divine retribution when warnings are not heeded.
orig: فلما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا بل هو ما استعجلتم به ريح فيها عذاب أليم

translation: Destroying everything by the command of its Lord, and they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the guilty people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah's will in bringing about destruction as a form of divine retribution. It underscores that when people persist in their wrongdoing and criminal behaviors, they ultimately face severe consequences decreed by Allah. The remnants of their dwellings serve as a stark reminder of their fate, illustrating that no matter how powerful or secure they may feel, they cannot escape divine justice. This serves as a warning and lesson for others to avoid similar fates by adhering to righteousness and obedience to God's commandments.
orig: تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: And We had established them in such as We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and vision and hearts; but their hearing and vision and hearts availed them nothing since they were rejecting the signs of Allah, and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns against the arrogance and disbelief of past communities who, despite being endowed with superior faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding, failed to benefit from them because they rejected divine signs. Their downfall and the consequences they faced serve as a reminder that material advantages and sensory abilities are futile if they are not used to recognize and submit to the truth. The verse also highlights the inevitability of divine retribution for those who mock and deny the revelations of Allah.
orig: ولقد مكناهم فيما إن مكناكم فيه وجعلنا لهم سمعا وأبصارا وأفئدة فما أغنى عنهم سمعهم ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم من شيء إذ كانوا يجحدون بآيات الله وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of [those] cities, and We have diversified the signs that perhaps they might return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by previous communities that rejected the signs and guidance from Allah. The destruction of neighboring cities is mentioned to instill a sense of caution and reflection. By highlighting that signs and warnings were given in various forms, the verse emphasizes the mercy and patience of Allah in giving people multiple opportunities to turn back to righteousness. It underscores the importance of heeding divine guidance to avoid a similar fate.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا ما حولكم من القرى وصرفنا الآيات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Then why did those they took as deities besides Allah as a means of nearness not help them? But they had strayed from them, and that was their falsehood and what they had been inventing.
interpretation: This verse points out the futility and falsehood of idol worship and taking others besides Allah as means of intercession. It emphasizes that during times of true need, those idols or false deities do not come to the aid of their worshippers. Instead, these supposed gods are completely disconnected from them, revealing that what the people believed in and fabricated were mere lies and inventions without any basis in truth or reality. It admonishes the believers to recognize and reject such falsehoods.
orig: فلولا نصرهم الذين اتخذوا من دون الله قربانا آلهة بل ضلوا عنهم وذلك إفكهم وما كانوا يفترون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We directed to you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, 'Listen quietly.' And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universality of the Qur'an, indicating that its message is not only for humans but also for jinn. The verse emphasizes the importance of attentively listening to the divine message and the responsibility to share the acquired wisdom with others. It underscores the accountability of all beings, whether human or jinn, in spreading and adhering to the guidance of the Qur'an.
orig: وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن يستمعون القرآن فلما حضروه قالوا أنصتوا فلما قضي ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين

translation: They said, 'O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it. It guides to the truth and to a straight path.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition by a group of people (commonly understood to be the jinn) of the divine origin and credibility of the Qur'an. They acknowledge that the Qur'an, revealed after the Torah, confirms the previous scriptures and also provides clear guidance towards truth and righteousness. It signifies the continuity and consistency of divine revelation, reinforcing the universal message of monotheism, ethics, and spiritual guidance present in Islam.
orig: قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقا لما بين يديه يهدي إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم

translation: O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him. He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a call to heed the message of Allah and have faith in Him. It emphasizes the importance of responding positively to divine guidance as a means to attain forgiveness and protection from severe repercussions. The verse encourages collective responsibility and spiritual awakening, urging the community to embrace faith and the promise of divine mercy and salvation.
orig: يا قومنا أجيبوا داعي الله وآمنوا به يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويجركم من عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot escape in the earth and will not have any protectors besides Him. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of Allah. It states that those who ignore or reject the divine call cannot escape Allah's reach, no matter where they are on earth. Moreover, such individuals will not find any protectors or allies besides Allah. The verse concludes by labeling these people as being in clear error, highlighting the grave consequences of turning away from divine guidance.
orig: ومن لا يجب داعي الله فليس بمعجز في الأرض وليس له من دونه أولياء أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Do they not see that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth and did not fail in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and creative power of Allah. By pointing to the creation of the heavens and the earth, it underscores that such a magnificent creation did not exhaust or tire Allah. Therefore, it logically follows that resurrecting the dead is well within His power. It serves as a reminder of the certainty of resurrection and Allah's absolute control over all things in the universe.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهن بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى بلى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire [it will be said], 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the final judgment faced by those who rejected faith, highlighting their ultimate confrontation with the truth they previously denied. When asked if the reality of Hell is evident, their affirmation acknowledges the certainty of divine justice. This interaction emphasizes the grave consequences of disbelief and serves as a solemn reminder of the importance of faith and the reality of the hereafter.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as were those of determination among the messengers and do not be impatient for them. It will be, on the Day they see that which they are promised, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse serves as both a comfort and a directive to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and by extension to all believers. It encourages patience and perseverance in the face of trials, just as the resolute messengers before him showed steadfastness. Additionally, it warns against being overly hasty for divine judgment on the wrongdoers. The verse posits that when the Day of Judgment arrives, the duration of worldly life will seem insignificant, almost as short as an hour in the day. This reflection serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternity of the afterlife. Ultimately, the verse underscores that destruction is destined for those who persist in disobedience and corruption, serving as both a warning and an encouragement to remain steadfast in faith.
orig: فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ولا تستعجل لهم كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ فهل يهلك إلا القوم الفاسقون

translation: Those who disbelieve and hinder [others] from the path of Allah, He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those who not only reject faith but also actively obstruct others from following the path of Allah. Their efforts and deeds, regardless of their intent or perceived merit, will ultimately be in vain and hold no value in the sight of Allah. This serves as a warning that obstructing divine guidance has severe repercussions.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم

translation: But those who have believed and done righteous deeds and believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and improve their condition.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both faith and righteous conduct. It recognizes belief in the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad as the ultimate truth from God. By holding true faith and performing good deeds, believers are promised divine forgiveness for their misdeeds and an overall betterment of their state, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وآمنوا بما نزل على محمد وهو الحق من ربهم كفر عنهم سيئاتهم وأصلح بالهم

translation: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus Allah presents to the people their comparisons.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the paths taken by disbelievers and believers. Disbelievers are led by falsehood and deception, while believers are guided by the truth that comes from Allah. This distinction is meant to illustrate the consequences of one's choices and Allah uses such comparisons to teach and guide people towards the right path.
orig: ذلك بأن الذين كفروا اتبعوا الباطل وأن الذين آمنوا اتبعوا الحق من ربهم كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse addresses the conduct of believers during armed conflict. It instructs to decisively confront those who oppose the faith in battle, ensuring their defeat and captivity. Following the conflict, the treatment of captives can include either magnanimity or ransom, indicating the importance of mercy and pragmatism even in times of war. The verse clarifies that Allah's will could have executed justice without the need for human engagement, but the trials of battle serve as a means for testing the faith and resolve of believers. It also reassures that the sacrifices made by those who perish in this cause are not forgotten and their deeds are eternally safeguarded.
orig: فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق فإما منا بعد وإما فداء حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها ذلك ولو يشاء الله لانتصر منهم ولكن ليبلو بعضكم ببعض والذين قتلوا في سبيل الله فلن يضل أعمالهم

translation: He will guide them and improve their condition.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's promise to those who have faith and follow the divine guidance. It reassures believers that God will not only guide them on the right path but also improve their overall state, providing tranquility and resolving their worries. It reflects the comprehensive support and rectification that God offers to the faithful in both spiritual and worldly aspects of their lives.
orig: سيهديهم ويصلح بالهم

translation: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah promises the believers that they will be admitted to Paradise, which He has described and made familiar to them through the revelations. It emphasizes that the rewards for their faith and righteous actions are not vague or uncertain; rather, Allah has already provided them with a clear understanding and depiction of the eternal bliss they will receive. This assurance helps to strengthen their resolve and provides comfort and motivation in their worldly struggles.
orig: ويدخلهم الجنة عرفها لهم

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal relationship between faith and divine support. Believers are encouraged to uphold and defend the principles of God. In doing so, they will receive God's assistance and stability in their endeavors. It highlights the importance of active faith and the assurance of divine aid for those who strive in His cause.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم

translation: But those who disbelieve – for them is misery, and He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences faced by those who reject faith. Disbelievers will face a state of despair, and their actions, regardless of their worldly success or effort, will ultimately be in vain and devoid of real benefit in the eyes of the Divine. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of deeds disconnected from the belief in and submission to God.
orig: والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم وأضل أعمالهم

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of rejecting divine revelation. When individuals harbor animosity or disdain towards the guidance sent by Allah, their actions, no matter how seemingly good, lose their spiritual value and efficacy in the sight of Allah. It underscores the importance of aligning one’s heart with divine will to ensure that one’s deeds are accepted and rewarded.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كرهوا ما أنزل الله فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed the end of those before them? Allah destroyed everything over them, and similar (fates await) the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse urges people to reflect on the historical consequences faced by those who denied the truth before them. By traveling and observing the remnants of past civilizations that were destroyed due to their defiance and disbelief, individuals can learn a powerful lesson about the divine retribution that awaits those who follow the same path. It serves as a warning that disregarding the signs and messages of Allah can lead to severe consequences, similar to what previous disbelieving communities experienced.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم دمر الله عليهم وللكافرين أمثالها

translation: That is because Allah is the Protector of those who have believed, but the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse underscores the contrasting fates of believers and disbelievers. For those who have faith, Allah is their guardian and supporter, guiding and protecting them through life's challenges. In contrast, disbelievers, by rejecting this divine relationship, find themselves without a true protector in both spiritual and worldly matters. This highlights the importance of faith in establishing a connection with divine support and guidance.
orig: ذلك بأن الله مولى الذين آمنوا وأن الكافرين لا مولى لهم

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as grazing livestock eat, and the Fire will be a residence for them.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the ultimate fates of believers and disbelievers. Believers who have faith and perform good deeds are promised eternal paradise with rivers flowing beneath, symbolizing purity, sustenance, and eternal bliss. On the other hand, disbelievers are depicted as those who seek temporary worldly pleasures, likened to animals that only live to eat and enjoy. Their final abode, however, will be the fire of hell, signifying the severe and eternal punishment awaiting them for their disbelief and heedlessness of spiritual matters.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

translation: And how many a city was stronger than your city which drove you out? We destroyed them, and there was no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the power and might of past civilizations that were more formidable than the community from which the Prophet Muhammad was exiled (i.e., Mecca). It serves as a reminder that despite their strength, these nations were ultimately destroyed by Allah due to their disobedience and rejection of the divine message. It underscores the concept that no worldly power can shield against divine retribution, and it offers reassurance to the Prophet and his followers that those who oppose them will not escape Allah's justice.
orig: وكأين من قرية هي أشد قوة من قريتك التي أخرجتك أهلكناهم فلا ناصر لهم

translation: Is someone who stands on clear evidence from their Lord like someone whose evil deeds are made appealing to them and they follow their desires?
interpretation: This verse draws a stark contrast between two types of individuals: those who receive clear guidance and evidence from their Lord, and those who are deluded by their own evil actions, finding them attractive and thus following their own desires. It highlights the difference in clarity and righteousness between following divine guidance and being led astray by one's own whims, emphasizing the importance of seeking truth and moral integrity over succumbing to one's baser inclinations.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه كمن زين له سوء عمله واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: The example of Paradise, which the righteous have been promised, is [that] in it are rivers of water unaltered, rivers of milk the taste of which never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey, in which they will have from all kinds of fruits and forgiveness from their Lord. [Can this be] like [the reward of] those who abide eternally in the Fire and are given to drink scalding water that will sever their intestines?
interpretation: This verse contrasts the eternal rewards for the righteous in Paradise with the torment awaiting those who reject faith in Hell. It emphasizes the purity and everlasting nature of the pleasures in Paradise—unaltered water, ever-fresh milk, delightful wine, and pure honey—signifying the profound contentment and joy that await the faithful. Conversely, it starkly portrays the suffering in Hell, where inhabitants are condemned to drink boiling water that causes severe agony. The verse calls on believers to reflect on these contrasting outcomes and to strive for righteousness to attain the promised rewards of Paradise.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون فيها أنهار من ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين وأنهار من عسل مصفى ولهم فيها من كل الثمرات ومغفرة من ربهم كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but when they leave you, they say to those who have been given knowledge, 'What did he just say?' Those are the ones of whom Allah has sealed their hearts and who have followed their desires.
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people who outwardly appear to be listening to the Prophet Muhammad but are inwardly dismissive and skeptical. When they step away, they mockingly question those who possess true understanding about what the Prophet has said, revealing their lack of sincerity and understanding. Allah has sealed their hearts due to their persistent rejection and preference for following their earthly desires over divine guidance. Their hearts being sealed signifies their conscious choice of ignorance and misguidance.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: But as for those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal nature of divine guidance and righteousness. When individuals seek and adhere to divine guidance with sincerity, Allah, in return, increases their ability to understand and follow the right path. Moreover, by adhering to this guidance, He grants them the means and strength to protect themselves from moral and spiritual dangers, essentially enhancing their piety and God-consciousness.
orig: والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى وآتاهم تقواهم

translation: Are they waiting for the Hour to come upon them suddenly? But some of its signs have already come. So what will their remembrance be when it has come upon them?
interpretation: This verse addresses the heedless who ignore the signs of the approaching Day of Judgment. It questions their expectation concerning its sudden arrival, noting that some of its foretold signs have already appeared. The verse underscores that, once the Hour arrives, it will be too late for them to amend their ways or heed the reminders they previously ignored.
orig: فهل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة فقد جاء أشراطها فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the foundational Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah, urging believers to seek knowledge and certainty of this truth. It further instructs the faithful, including the Prophet, to seek forgiveness for their sins, demonstrating humility and the importance of repentance. The verse also highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, who is aware of our every action and condition, reinforcing the themes of divine omniscience and accountability.
orig: فاعلم أنه لا إله إلا الله واستغفر لذنبك وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات والله يعلم متقلبكم ومثواكم

translation: And those who believe say, 'Why has a surah not been sent down?' But when a precise surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. But more appropriate for them would have been [obedience and] a word of appropriate respect.
interpretation: This verse addresses the reaction of different groups towards divine revelation and directives. Believers who are sincere in their faith desire more guidance through the revelation of new surahs (chapters or verses). However, when a clear and decisive surah comes down, particularly mentioning difficult commands such as fighting, it exposes the true state of others whose faith is weak or diseased. Their trepidation and fear show that their commitment to God's commands is shaky. The verse emphasizes that instead of showing fear and hesitation, it would have been more fitting for these individuals to respond with obedience and respectful words, demonstrating their trust in God's wisdom and commands.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا لولا نزلت سورة فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة وذكر فيها القتال رأيت الذين في قلوبهم مرض ينظرون إليك نظر المغشي عليه من الموت فأولى لهم

translation: Obedience and good words. And when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and the sincerity in one's words and actions. It suggests that true commitment and honesty in following Allah's commands, especially during decisive moments, lead to better outcomes. Thus, maintaining truthfulness and acting righteously in accordance with divine guidance is portrayed as beneficial for believers.
orig: طاعة وقول معروف فإذا عزم الأمر فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرا لهم

translation: But if you turn away, perhaps you will spread corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship.
interpretation: This verse warns believers of the consequences of turning away from God's guidance. It highlights two specific forms of misbehavior: spreading corruption on earth and breaking family ties. The verse underscores the importance of maintaining social harmony and familial relationships as part of a righteous conduct and warns against the societal breakdown that can result from neglecting these duties.
orig: فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their vision.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences for those who have deviated from the path of righteousness and persist in wrongdoing. The curse of Allah signifies His divine displeasure, and as a result, they are metaphorically deafened and blinded. This means they are unable to perceive the truth or heed guidance, emphasizing the severity and spiritual ramifications of straying from God's commandments.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم

translation: Do they not then reflect on the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of contemplating and understanding the Qur'an. It suggests that the failure to deeply engage with the text may be due to metaphorical 'locks' on one's heart, representing ignorance, stubbornness, or a refusal to open oneself up to its guidance and wisdom. The verse calls for introspection and the removal of these 'locks' to truly benefit from the divine message.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها

translation: Indeed, those who turned back after guidance had become clear to them, Satan enticed them and prolonged hope for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequences for those who consciously reject the truth after it has been made clear to them. It emphasizes that Satan plays a pivotal role in misleading such individuals by making falsehoods seem tempting and giving them false hopes, leading them further away from the path of righteousness.
orig: إن الذين ارتدوا على أدبارهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى الشيطان سول لهم وأملى لهم

translation: That is because they said to those who hate what Allah has revealed, 'We will obey you in part of this matter,' but Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who outwardly show compliance with the believers but align themselves with those who oppose Allah's revelations. They reassure these antagonists by promising partial obedience to their wishes. It highlights their duplicity and reminds us that Allah is fully aware of their hidden intentions and covert alliances, exposing the insincerity of their faith and their attempts to appease both sides for their own advantage.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا للذين كرهوا ما نزل الله سنطيعكم في بعض الأمر والله يعلم إسرارهم

translation: Then how [will it be] when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to the disbelievers and wrongdoers about the consequences they will face upon their death. The imagery of angels striking faces and backs symbolizes the severe and humiliating punishment that awaits those who persist in their defiance and wrongdoing. It underscores the gravity of their actions and the inevitable justice that will be administered by divine decree. The verse emphasizes the role of angels as enforcers of God's will and the inescapable nature of divine retribution.
orig: فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم

translation: That is because they followed what displeased Allah and disliked His approval, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of choosing actions and behaviors that go against the commands and will of Allah. It speaks to the moral and spiritual failure of individuals who deliberately follow what is displeasing to Allah and detest seeking His pleasure. As a result of their persistent disobedience and aversion to seeking Allah’s pleasure, all their deeds become null and void, meaning they lose any potential reward or merit they could have earned. The verse serves as a stark warning of the ramifications of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of aligning one's actions with what is pleasing to Allah.
orig: ذلك بأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not expose their malice?
interpretation: This verse addresses those who harbor hypocrisy or ill intentions within their hearts. It serves as a reminder and a caution that no matter how well one might conceal such sentiments, Allah is fully aware of what lies hidden within and has the power to reveal them. It emphasizes the divine attribute of Allah being fully knowledgeable of the inner thoughts and intentions of every individual.
orig: أم حسب الذين في قلوبهم مرض أن لن يخرج الله أضغانهم

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; but you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to make it evident who the hypocrites and disbelievers are by their external signs. However, even without these signs, their true nature can often be discerned from the subtleties and undertones in their speech. It emphasizes that while humans may struggle to identify deceit, Allah's knowledge encompasses all actions and intentions of people, ensuring divine justice and awareness of authenticity in faith and actions.
orig: ولو نشاء لأريناكهم فلعرفتهم بسيماهم ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول والله يعلم أعمالكم

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you and those who are patient, and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine trial of believers to distinguish those who earnestly strive in the path of Allah and exhibit patience through adversity. It underscores the importance of perseverance and resilience as qualities that are illuminated through life's challenges. Allah's testing serves as a revelation of individuals' true character and commitment, highlighting the intrinsic value of sincere effort and steadfastness in faith.
orig: ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject faith and obstruct others from following the path of Allah, as well as those who oppose the Prophet after witnessing clear guidance. It emphasizes that their actions will not affect Allah or diminish His divine authority in any way. Instead, their malicious efforts will only lead to their own harm, culminating in the nullification of their deeds. Their attempts to undermine the divine message and guidance will ultimately fail, showcasing the futility of opposing the will of Allah.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله وشاقوا الرسول من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger as a fundamental aspect of the faith. It serves as a reminder that righteous actions must be accompanied by adherence to divine and prophetic guidance. Furthermore, it warns believers that their deeds can be rendered void if they fail to maintain this obedience, implying that faith, intention, and action are integrally connected in Islam. Thus, it underscores the necessity of sincerity and constancy in one's devotion and actions towards fulfilling religious obligations.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers - never will Allah forgive them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and the act of leading others away from the path of Allah. It underscores the concept that dying in a state of disbelief, particularly after actively preventing others from following Allah’s guidance, results in a complete lack of forgiveness from Allah. This serves as a warning to those who reject faith and obstruct the spiritual journey of others, highlighting the eternal consequences of their actions.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله ثم ماتوا وهم كفار فلن يغفر الله لهم

translation: So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse urges the believers to maintain their resolve and not to seek peace out of fear or weakness when they are in a position of strength. It reassures them that Allah is with them, providing support and ensuring that their efforts and righteous actions will not go unrewarded. The message reinforces the importance of steadfastness and the promise of divine assistance and justice.
orig: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

translation: The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement. But if you believe and remain conscious of God, He will grant you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient and trivial nature of worldly life, comparing it to mere play and amusement. It emphasizes that true fulfillment and meaningful rewards come from faith and piety. By believing in God and living righteously, believers are promised divine rewards that far surpass any material wealth, indicating that God values spiritual integrity over worldly riches and does not burden believers by demanding their wealth.
orig: إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم

translation: If He were to ask you for them and press you, you would withhold, and He would expose your unwillingness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards reluctance and miserliness when pressed to give up their wealth or resources. It suggests that if God were to demand significant sacrifices, many would reveal their true nature of stinginess and hidden resentment. This serves as a reminder to remain generous and willing in contributing without compulsion, to avoid exposing negative traits and ensuring sincerity in one's intentions.
orig: إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ويخرج أضغانكم

translation: Here you are—those invited to spend in the cause of Allah—but among you are those who withhold out of greed. And whoever withholds only withholds [benefit] from himself; and Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving in the path of Allah and highlights the consequences of stinginess. The act of giving benefits the individual more than it benefits Allah, as Allah is free of any need while humans are inherently needy. It also serves as a warning: if people turn away from their duties, Allah will replace them with others who are more willing and obedient. The underlying message is the encouragement of generosity and the reminder that Allah's plans are beyond human control.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء تدعون لتنفقوا في سبيل الله فمنكم من يبخل ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

translation: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.
interpretation: This verse stands as a reassurance and a declaration of triumph. It refers to the victory and divine support bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. This 'clear conquest' can be interpreted not solely as a military victory but also as a significant spiritual and moral triumph, symbolizing the spread of Islam and the success of its message. It reflects the acknowledgment of divine assistance and the fulfillment of God's promises to the believers.
orig: إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا

translation: That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It highlights that Allah's forgiveness encompasses both past and future sins, signifying a complete purification. Furthermore, it underscores the continuation of divine blessings and guidance, leading the Prophet towards the righteous path. This is not only a personal reassurement to the Prophet but also serves as a broader demonstration of Allah's compassion and guidance for all believers.
orig: ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما

translation: And Allah will grant you a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance and divine promise from Allah to the believers, indicating that they will receive His support and achieve a significant, honorable victory. The word 'mighty' emphasizes the strength and grandeur of the success that Allah is promising, highlighting His power and the effectiveness of His assistance.
orig: وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا

translation: He it is Who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, that they might have more faith added to their faith - for to Allah belong the forces of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is full of knowledge and wisdom.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role in providing peace and tranquility to the believers to strengthen their faith. It underscores that the increase in one's faith is a divine gift aimed at bolstering the believers' trust and commitment. Additionally, it highlights Allah's dominion and authority over all creation, reminding the believers of His omnipotence and the wisdom behind His actions. This should inspire confidence and reliance on Allah's greater plan, knowing that His knowledge and wisdom encompass all matters in the heavens and the earth.
orig: هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: to admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally and to remove from them their misdeeds - and ever is that, in the sight of Allah, a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for the believers, both men and women, who have faith in Allah. They are promised everlasting residence in paradise, a place of immense serenity and joy characterized by flowing rivers. Moreover, their sins will be forgiven, signifying a complete purification. This assurance of eternal bliss and absolution from sins represents a significant and immense success from Allah's perspective, emphasizing His mercy and the grandeur of His rewards for the faithful.
orig: ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما

translation: And [so] He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil nature. Upon them is a misfortune of evil nature; and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell. And evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who harbor hypocritical and polytheistic beliefs, particularly those who hold negative assumptions about Allah. It illuminates the severe consequences awaiting them, emphasizing divine displeasure, curses, and the ultimate punishment of Hell. The verse serves as a stern warning against insincerity and disbelief, highlighting Allah's justice and the severe outcomes for those who choose to misinterpret or maliciously assume the worst of Him. It underscores the idea that one's beliefs and intentions towards Allah carry significant consequences both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: ويعذب المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات الظانين بالله ظن السوء عليهم دائرة السوء وغضب الله عليهم ولعنهم وأعد لهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme power and control over the entire universe. The 'soldiers of the heavens and the earth' symbolize all forces and entities, both visible and invisible, that are under God's command. By stating God is 'Exalted in Might and Wise,' it reinforces the notion of His unparalleled authority and His wise governance over all creation. This serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the intricate wisdom behind His actions and decrees.
orig: ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive roles of the Prophet Muhammad in his mission. As a witness, he bears testimony to the truth of God's message. As a bringer of good tidings, he offers hope and encouragement to those who follow the path of righteousness. As a warner, he cautions against the consequences of disobedience and transgression. Thus, his role is multi-faceted, aiming to guide humanity towards a holistic understanding and practice of divine guidance.
orig: إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: That you (people) may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor Him and respect Him and glorify Him morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of faith in Allah and His Messenger, emphasizing the duties of believers not only to have faith but also to support and honor the Prophet Muhammad. Additionally, it highlights the continual remembrance and glorification of Allah throughout the day, signifying the importance of regular and consistent devotion in one's life.
orig: لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The Hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself; and he who fulfills that which he has promised Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine significance of the pledges made to the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting that such acts are, in reality, commitments to Allah Himself. The metaphorical phrase 'the Hand of Allah is over their hands' indicates divine oversight and support. It reinforces the importance of honoring one's commitments, as breaking them harms the individual, while keeping them brings divine reward and favor.
orig: إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله يد الله فوق أيديهم فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله فسيؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: Those desert Arabs who were left behind will say to you, "Our wealth and families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, "Then who can prevent Allah at all if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Rather, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted."
interpretation: This verse addresses the excuses given by certain desert Arabs who did not join the Prophet in his expeditions, using their wealth and family responsibilities as reasons for their absence. However, their words are insincere and do not reflect their true intentions or beliefs. The verse highlights the futility of their excuses by emphasizing that, ultimately, no one can impede Allah's will, whether it is to bring harm or benefit. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of their real motives and actions.
orig: سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made pleasing in your hearts. And you assumed an assumption of evil and became a people ruined.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who doubted the return of the Prophet and the believers from their expedition, revealing their lack of faith and trust in divine support. It highlights that their disbelief was not only an external but an internal condition, where they found satisfaction in their skepticism and ultimately held negative expectations that led to their moral and spiritual downfall.
orig: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا

translation: But those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the critical importance of belief in both Allah and His Messenger. It highlights the severe consequences that await those who choose to disbelieve, illustrating the gravity of their choice by the mention of a 'blazing fire' prepared for them. The verse serves as a stern warning and a dire reminder of the repercussions in the hereafter for rejecting the core tenets of Islam.
orig: ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty over the universe, highlighting that all matters of forgiveness and punishment are solely within His discretion. It reminds believers of God's immense mercy and forgiveness, while also acknowledging His authority to administer justice. The verse serves to instill both hope and humility in believers, encouraging them to seek God's mercy while remaining conscious of His omnipotence.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Those who lagged behind will say when you set forth to take the spoils, 'Let us follow you.' They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, 'You shall not follow us; thus has Allah said before.' Then they will say, 'Nay, but you envy us.' Nay, they understand but little.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who did not participate in a previous expedition and now wish to join the believers in taking the spoils of war. Their request to join is insincere and aims to undermine the divine decree, as Allah had already designated the spoils for those who actively participated. The Prophet is instructed to remind them of God's earlier command that their participation is not allowed. When denied, they accuse the believers of envy, demonstrating their lack of true understanding of the divine wisdom and decrees. This highlights the importance of sincere intention and the adherence to divine commandments.
orig: سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله من قبل فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا

translation: Say to those who stayed behind of the Bedouins, 'You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you may fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Bedouins who did not participate in previous battles, informing them that they will be summoned to confront a strong enemy. It emphasizes the conditional reward from Allah if they obey and participate in the battle, and warns of severe consequences if they turn away as they did previously. The verse underscores themes of duty, obedience, and the balance between reward and punishment in the context of faith and communal responsibility.
orig: قل للمخلفين من الأعراب ستدعون إلى قوم أولي بأس شديد تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما

translation: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the sick. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there is no blame or burden on individuals who have physical disabilities such as blindness, lameness, or illness. These conditions exempt them from certain religious obligations that they may find difficult or impossible to perform. The verse also highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, promising paradise as a reward for obedience, while warning of severe punishment for those who turn away from their duties and reject the divine guidance.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما

translation: Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.
interpretation: This verse refers to the event of the Pledge of the Tree (Bai'at al-Ridwan), where the Prophet Muhammad's companions pledged their unwavering support under a tree. Allah acknowledges the sincerity and purity of their hearts and, as a reward, grants them a sense of peace and an upcoming victory. This signifies Allah's approval and the spiritual and material rewards that come from true faith and commitment.
orig: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا

translation: And many gains they will take. And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the numerous spoils or benefits that the believers will acquire. It underscores that these gains come from the omnipotence and wisdom of Allah, emphasizing His supreme power and boundless wisdom in distributing such bounties. It serves as a reminder that material gains are ultimately a result of divine grace and should be seen within the context of Allah's overarching wisdom and might.
orig: ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Allah has promised you many gains that you will acquire, and He has hastened this for you and withheld the hands of people from you so that it may be a sign for the believers and so that He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's promise of future victories and rewards for the believers, signifying His support and intervention in their favor. The immediate gains serve as an encouragement and a testament to His backing, aiming to reinforce the faith of the believers and guide them towards righteous living and adherence to the straight path.
orig: وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And there are others which you have not yet been able to achieve, but Allah has already encompassed them. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that even though there are objectives and challenges they have not yet achieved or overcome, Allah's power and knowledge encompass everything. It emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and ability to bring about outcomes beyond human reach or understanding. Therefore, believers should trust in Allah's plan and capabilities, knowing that He is fully competent in all matters.
orig: وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: If those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs (in flight). Then they would not find any protector or helper.
