translation: And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and scripture; and among them are those who are guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the divine mission of the prophets Noah and Abraham, highlighting that God chose to place prophethood and scripture within their progeny. It emphasizes a dual outcome among their descendants—while some embrace guidance, many turn away in rebellious disobedience. This underscores the recurring theme in the Qur'an of individual responsibility and the varying acceptance of divine guidance among people, even within a blessed lineage.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا وإبراهيم وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: Then We sent after them Our messengers and followed them with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. And We placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. But monasticism, which they innovated, We did not prescribe for them except [that they did so] seeking the pleasure of Allah; but they did not observe it with due observance. So We gave the ones who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuity and culmination of divine guidance through a lineage of messengers, culminating with Jesus (peace be upon him) and the revelation of the Gospel. Despite the initial genuine compassion and mercy instilled in Jesus' followers, monasticism emerged as an innovative practice beyond divine prescription. This monasticism was intended to seek Allah's pleasure but was not properly upheld. Consequently, rewards were granted to the sincere believers, while many fell into disobedience. The verse highlights divine mercy, the natural human deviation from intended practices, and the distinction between true believers and those who stray from righteous conduct.
orig: ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا وقفينا بعيسى ابن مريم وآتيناه الإنجيل وجعلنا في قلوب الذين اتبعوه رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية ابتدعوها ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله فما رعوها حق رعايتها فآتينا الذين آمنوا منهم أجرهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and will provide for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to maintain their faith in Allah and to continue their belief in the Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It promises that those who do so will receive a double share of Allah's mercy, a guiding light to help them navigate their lives, and forgiveness for their transgressions. The emphasis on Allah's qualities as Forgiving and Merciful highlights the compassion and benevolence of Allah towards those who are devoted and sincere in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وآمنوا برسوله يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته ويجعل لكم نورا تمشون به ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: This is so that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah and that the bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse communicates that the bounty and grace of Allah are under His absolute control and distribution. It serves to remind the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) that they have no authoritative claim or control over Allah's favors. The verse emphasizes that it is solely Allah who bestows His blessings according to His wisdom and will, reinforcing the concept of divine sovereignty and generosity.
orig: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون على شيء من فضل الله وأن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: Allah has certainly heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue; indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges that Allah is aware of the grievances and disputes that individuals have, particularly in the context of marital issues. It emphasizes that Allah listens to the concerns of those who turn to Him and seeks justice. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipresence and His ability to hear and see all, assuring believers that their struggles and complaints are known to Him and will not go unheard.
orig: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها وتشتكي إلى الله والله يسمع تحاوركما إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Those among you who separate from their wives by [saying they are as their] mothers - they are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse addresses a pre-Islamic practice known as 'Zihar,' where a husband would declare his wife to be like his mother, thereby forbidding himself from marital relations with her. The verse refutes this notion by stating that their wives are not their mothers—only the women who gave birth to them can be considered their mothers. It condemns this practice as a morally objectionable and false statement. Nonetheless, the verse concludes with a reminder of Allah's forgiving nature, indicating that even those who have committed such wrongful acts can seek and receive forgiveness from Allah.
orig: الذين يظاهرون منكم من نسائهم ما هن أمهاتهم إن أمهاتهم إلا اللائي ولدنهم وإنهم ليقولون منكرا من القول وزورا وإن الله لعفو غفور

translation: And those who pronounce ẓihār from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said, they must free a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished thereby; and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of ẓihār, where a man likens his wife to a prohibited relative, thereby making her forbidden to him. If he wishes to retract this statement and continue marital relations, he is required to free a slave before resuming intimate relations. This stipulation serves as both a serious admonition and a means to discourage the careless use of such prohibitions. Furthermore, it underlines that Allah is fully aware of the actions and intentions of individuals, promoting accountability and encouraging sincere repentance.
orig: والذين يظاهرون من نسائهم ثم يعودون لما قالوا فتحرير رقبة من قبل أن يتماسا ذلكم توعظون به والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: But whoever does not find [a means] - then a fast of two months consecutively before they touch one another; and whoever is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor people. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allah and His Messenger; and those are the limits [set by] Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the atonement for certain prohibited actions by emphasizing the importance of repentance and adherence to specified rituals to seek forgiveness. Fasting for two consecutive months or feeding sixty poor individuals illustrates the seriousness of making amends and promotes discipline and compassion in the community. The directive to believe in Allah and His Messenger underscores that these acts are not mere formalities but are meant to deepen one's faith and awareness of divine boundaries. The mention of a painful punishment for disbelievers serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين من قبل أن يتماسا فمن لم يستطع فإطعام ستين مسكينا ذلك لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتلك حدود الله وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are to be abased as those before them were abased. And We have certainly sent down clear verses. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences faced by those who oppose divine guidance and the prophets sent by Allah. It underscores that rebellion against God and the Prophet is not a new phenomenon but one that has consistently led to disgrace throughout history. The 'clear verses' refer to the undeniable signs and teachings that have been revealed, making the truth evident. For those who persist in disbelief and opposition, the verse warns of a severe and humiliating punishment, highlighting the gravity of rejecting divine truth.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله كبتوا كما كبت الذين من قبلهم وقد أنزلنا آيات بينات وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: The Day Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah had accounted it, while they forgot it. And Allah is over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Resurrection when all humans will be brought back to life by Allah, who will then reveal to them their deeds. These actions, although forgotten by the individuals themselves, have been meticulously recorded by Allah. It emphasizes Allah's encompassing knowledge and His role as a constant witness over everything, reminding believers of the importance of accountability and the omniscience of Allah.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? There is no secret conversation among three but He is the fourth of them, nor among five but He is the sixth of them, nor fewer than that nor more but He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, underscoring that He is aware of every whisper, secret conversation, and thought even if it involves as few as three or more people. It serves as a powerful reminder that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge, no matter how secretive. On the Day of Resurrection, everyone will be held accountable for their actions, as Allah's infinite knowledge encompasses all things. This awareness is meant to inspire mindfulness and God-consciousness in one's actions and interactions.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم أين ما كانوا ثم ينبئهم بما عملوا يوم القيامة إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel, then they return to what they were forbidden and conspire in sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting that Allah has not greeted you with, and they say among themselves, 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?' Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy and disobedience of certain individuals who, despite being explicitly forbidden from engaging in secretive and harmful conspiracies, persist in such behavior. Their actions go against the commands of Allah and the teachings of the Prophet. Moreover, they mock the prescribed Islamic greeting and question why they are not immediately punished by Allah for their words, displaying a flawed understanding of divine justice. The verse warns that their ultimate recompense will be Hell, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions and attitudes.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نهوا عن النجوى ثم يعودون لما نهوا عنه ويتناجون بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وإذا جاءوك حيوك بما لم يحيك به الله ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, when you converse privately, do not converse about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger but converse about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse advises the believers on proper conduct during private conversations. It counsels against discussing sinful or aggressive actions and disobedience to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Instead, it encourages conversations that promote righteousness and piety. The verse also serves as a reminder to be conscious of Allah, as everyone will ultimately be gathered before Him for judgment. This emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral integrity and God-consciousness in all interactions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وتناجوا بالبر والتقوى واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Secret conversations are only from Satan, to sadden those who have believed, but he cannot harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the strategy of Satan to create doubt and sorrow among believers through secret whispers. It reassures the believers that any distress caused by these whispers is harmless unless permitted by Allah. Thus, believers are encouraged to place their trust in Allah, understanding that He is the ultimate protector and controller of their fate.
orig: إنما النجوى من الشيطان ليحزن الذين آمنوا وليس بضارهم شيئا إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make space in your gatherings,' then make space; Allah will make space for you. And when you are told, 'Arise,' then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of humility and cooperation among believers. It urges them to show respect and consideration for one another, whether by making room for others during gatherings or by heeding directives to leave. Furthermore, it highlights the exalted status of those who possess faith and knowledge, implying that such virtues lead to higher ranks in the eyes of Allah. The verse also serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of everyone's actions, encouraging believers to act with righteousness and integrity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قيل لكم تفسحوا في المجالس فافسحوا يفسح الله لكم وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: O you who have believed, when you privately consult the Messenger, present a charity before your consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [the means], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to give charity prior to seeking a private audience with the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the importance of intentionality and mindfulness in their actions. It serves to purify them and ensure sincerity in their request to consult the Messenger. However, if one is unable to afford this charity, it reassures them that Allah is forgiving and merciful, understanding their circumstances and not imposing undue hardship.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة ذلك خير لكم وأطهر فإن لم تجدوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Are you afraid of spending in charity before your private consultation? If you do not do so, and Allah has pardoned you, then establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses a concern among the believers regarding spending in charity before private consultations with the Prophet Muhammad. It acknowledges their apprehension and comforts them by mentioning Allah's forgiveness for those who didn't follow this command. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining fundamental practices such as prayer, zakah (almsgiving), and general obedience to Allah and His Messenger. The underlying message is that acts of worship and righteousness remain paramount, and Allah, being fully aware of their actions, emphasizes His omniscience and the need for sincere adherence to His guidance.
orig: أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات فإذ لم تفعلوا وتاب الله عليكم فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الله ورسوله والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Have you not seen those who have turned towards a people who have earned the wrath of Allah? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to falsehood while they know [they are lying].
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who have aligned themselves with disbelievers who have incurred Allah's anger. It highlights their insincerity by mentioning that they swear oaths to lies knowingly. The verse emphasizes their alienation; they do not truly belong to either the believers or the disbelievers. Their actions place them outside the community of the faithful, underscoring the severity of hypocrisy and deceit.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين تولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم ما هم منكم ولا منهم ويحلفون على الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, it is evil that which they used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in wrongdoing and immoral actions. It highlights the consequence of severe punishment as a result of their persistent evil deeds. The verse reinforces the concept of divine justice, where those who continuously engage in unethical behavior will face the repercussions prepared by Allah. This is a reminder to adhere to righteous conduct and avoid actions that lead to divine displeasure.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They have taken their oaths as a cover, so they averted [people] from the way of Allah, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrisy and deceit of some individuals who use their false oaths as a shield to cover their true intentions. They mislead others and obstruct them from following the path of Allah. As a consequence of their actions, they are promised a humiliating punishment. The verse highlights the seriousness of insincerity and manipulation in matters of faith and underscores the divine justice that awaits those who corruptively lead others astray.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله فلهم عذاب مهين

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worldly possessions and family ties when it comes to salvation and protection from divine retribution. It underscores the principle that material wealth and familial connections have no bearing on one's standing with Allah and cannot shield one from the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a stern reminder of the permanence of the punishment for those who reject divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing, highlighting the eternal nature of their suffering in the Fire.
orig: لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, thinking that they have something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of hypocrites and disbelievers who deceive themselves into thinking they can deceive Allah. On the Day of Resurrection, they will attempt to lie and swear to Allah as they did to people in this world, believing their falsehoods and schemes will work. However, their deceit is futile, and Allah exposes their true nature, affirming that they are indeed the liars.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فيحلفون له كما يحلفون لكم ويحسبون أنهم على شيء ألا إنهم هم الكاذبون

translation: Satan has gained mastery over them and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan. Truly, it is the party of Satan that will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse signifies the detrimental effects of allowing Satan to dominate one's thoughts and actions, leading to the neglect of the remembrance of Allah. It emphasizes that those who fall under Satan's influence belong to his faction, and ultimately, this allegiance will result in their loss and failure. It serves as a warning to remain vigilant and to keep Allah's remembrance central in one's life to avoid such a fate.
orig: استحوذ عليهم الشيطان فأنساهم ذكر الله أولئك حزب الشيطان ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most abased.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences for those who actively resist or oppose the commandments and mission of Allah and His Prophet. Such opposition not only leads to spiritual and moral degradation but also results in being disgraced and humiliated in this world and the hereafter. It serves as a warning that defiance against divine authority brings about utter humiliation.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله أولئك في الأذلين

translation: Allah has decreed, 'Most certainly I will prevail, I and My messengers.' Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty.
interpretation: This verse conveys a divine promise and assurance of victory for Allah and His messengers. It underlines the ultimate power and strength of Allah and His capacity to ensure that His will and the missions of His prophets will triumph despite earthly challenges. It serves to comfort and encourage the faithful, emphasizing that divine support is ever-present and unbeatable.
orig: كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah - they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strong loyalty and devotion that true believers must have towards Allah and His Messenger, even to the extent of prioritizing their faith over family ties if such ties are in opposition to divine guidance. It underscores the principle that true faith manifests itself in aligning one’s loyalties and affections according to divine commandments, rather than blood relations. Moreover, it highlights the special spiritual support and the promise of eternal paradise that Allah grants to those who show such unwavering commitment. Those who belong to the 'party of Allah' are assured of eternal success and divine satisfaction, highlighting the ultimate triumph of faith and dedication to divine principles.
orig: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه ويدخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of Allah's sovereignty and the constant state of His creation’s glorification for Him. Everything in both the heavens and the earth acknowledges and glorifies Allah, reflecting His omnipotence and supreme wisdom. The attributes 'Almighty' and 'All-Wise' point to Allah's absolute power over all things and His profound wisdom in the creation and ordering of the universe. This recognition serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all creation in its submission to the will of Allah.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who expelled the disbelievers among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah came upon them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts. They demolished their houses with their own hands and with the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of insight.
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where a group of the People of the Book who disbelieved were expelled from their homes. Despite their reliance on fortifications for security, they were caught off guard by God's decree and faced consequences they had not anticipated. Their fear led them to destroy their own homes, symbolizing internal collapse and the futility of opposing divine will. The admonition here is for those with insight to learn from this example, recognizing the omnipotence of God and the ultimate futility of relying solely on worldly defenses against His will.
orig: هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم لأول الحشر ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

translation: Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have certainly punished them in this world, and in the Hereafter, they will have the torment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse indicates that although the immediate punishment for the transgressors was exile, a more severe punishment was reserved for the Hereafter. It reflects Allah’s justice, showing that worldly consequences are only a part of divine retribution, with ultimate justice being served in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the idea that divine decree supersedes all, and even when leniency is shown in worldly terms, it does not exempt one from accountability in the life to come.
orig: ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah, then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the serious consequences for those who actively resist and oppose Allah and His Messenger. It highlights that rebellion against divine guidance and prophetic teachings is met with severe repercussions from Allah. The severity of the punishment serves as a warning and a deterrent against such opposition, emphasizing the importance of aligning oneself with divine will and prophetic direction.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Whatever you cut down of [their] palm trees or left standing on their trunks - it was by permission of Allah and so He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse addresses the actions taken by the believers in a situation involving the destruction or preservation of palm trees. Such actions are specified as being done with Allah's permission, implying divine sanction and purpose. The ultimate aim mentioned here is to bring disgrace upon those who are defiantly disobedient, highlighting the divine strategy to expose and punish those who act against God's commandments and the believers.
orig: ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله وليخزي الفاسقين

translation: What Allah bestowed on His Messenger from them—and you did not spur for it any horses or camels— but Allah gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the gains acquired (referred to as 'fay') by the Prophet Muhammad from the non-believers were not through physical means such as combat or effort expended by the Muslims (i.e., horses or camels). Instead, it is by Allah's will and authority that these gains were obtained. This demonstrates Allah's ultimate power and control over all matters, indicating that success and provision come from Allah's decree and not solely from human effort.
orig: وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever God has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns, it is for God and the Messenger and for the relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer—so that it may not merely circulate between the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it. And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of equitable distribution of wealth and resources within the Muslim community. It instructs that spoils of war or gains obtained by the community should serve the welfare of all, including the poor and disadvantaged, to prevent an economic imbalance where wealth remains in the hands of the affluent. Additionally, it underscores the obligation of Muslims to follow the guidance and prohibitions set by the Prophet Muhammad, reinforcing the notion of obedience to divine command and living in a God-conscious manner to avoid severe consequences.
orig: ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and aiding Allah and His Messenger – they are the truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse refers to the early Muslim emigrants (the Muhajirun) who faced significant hardships, including expulsion from their homes and loss of property, for the sake of their faith. Their actions are driven by a sincere desire for Allah's favor and approval. Their commitment to supporting the divine cause and the Prophet Muhammad despite severe challenges and sacrifices establishes their truthfulness and unwavering faith.
orig: للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: And [also for] those who were settled in the home [i.e., al-Madīnah] and [adopted] the faith before them. They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their hearts of what they [i.e., the emigrants] were given but give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary qualities of the Ansar (the helpers) in Medina who received the emigrants (Muhajirun) from Mecca with open hearts and generosity. The verse praises the Ansar for their unselfish love and the absence of envy towards their brothers in faith. It stresses the virtue of altruism and the importance of giving preference to others even in times of personal hardship. The passage also underscores the spiritual success that comes from overcoming one's own greed and selfishness, portraying such restraint as a path to true prosperity and divine approval.
orig: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And [there is a share for] those who came after them, saying, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and unity among believers across generations. It emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness not just for oneself but also for fellow believers who have preceded us. Moreover, it advises against harboring any ill feelings towards other faithful individuals, promoting harmony and compassion within the community of believers. The verse concludes by acknowledging God's attributes of kindness and mercy, encouraging mutual respect and forgiveness among the faithful.
orig: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم

translation: Have you not seen those who practice hypocrisy, saying to their brothers who have disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, 'If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will not obey, in your case, anyone ever; and if you are fought, we will surely aid you.' But Allah testifies that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of hypocrites who offer false promises of support to their disbelieving counterparts among the People of the Book. They claim solidarity and commitment, stating they will leave with them if they are expelled and defend them if they are attacked. However, Allah exposes their deceit, affirming that these hypocrites are not sincere in their declarations and will not keep their promises. This verse underscores the theme of hypocrisy and the divine awareness of one's true intentions.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Indeed, if they are expelled, they will not leave with them; and if they are fought, they will not aid them. And [even] if they should aid them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the insincere allies who, despite their promises, will neither support nor stand by their companions in times of need. It emphasizes the unreliability and cowardice of such false friends, suggesting that even if they pretend to offer help, they will ultimately abandon those they claimed to support when faced with real danger.
orig: لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: You are more fearful in their hearts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses how certain groups or individuals fear human beings more than they fear Allah. The reason for this fear is their lack of understanding and comprehension of the true power and importance of Allah. They are criticized for their ignorance and misplaced fears, highlighting their spiritual shortcomings and lack of proper insight into the divine reality.
orig: لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls. Their hostility towards each other is intense. You think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the confrontation with certain groups who, despite seeming unity, are deeply divided internally. Their external show of strength and fortified defenses mask their internal discord. This lack of true unity is attributed to their failure to comprehend and apply true wisdom and understanding. The verse highlights the futility and weakness inherent in disunity among people and implies an encouragement to seek deeper understanding and unity.
orig: لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعا وقلوبهم شتى ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Like those shortly before them, they tasted the evil consequences of their conduct, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel with previous peoples who experienced the dire repercussions of their wrongdoings. It serves as a warning that those who persist in sinful behaviors will inevitably face suffering and retribution, both in this life and in the hereafter. The 'painful punishment' underscores the severity of the consequences awaiting those who disregard divine guidance.
orig: كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Like the example of Satan when he says to man, 'Disbelieve,' but when he disbelieves, he says, 'Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse sheds light on the deceptive nature of Satan. It illustrates how Satan may entice humans into disbelief and sinful actions, promising them benefits or satisfaction. However, once the person succumbs to Satan's temptations and commits the sin, Satan abandons them, declaring his own fear of Allah and disassociation from the sinner. This serves as a warning about the insidious tactics of Satan and underscores the importance of remaining vigilant and faithful to Allah, who is the ultimate judge and protector.
orig: كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: So the end result for both of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein eternally. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable outcome for those who commit injustices and wrongdoings. It serves as a stern warning that their actions will lead to eternal punishment in the Fire, emphasizing the seriousness of living a life in defiance of divine guidance and justice. The eternal nature of their abode underscores the gravity of their sins and the ultimate justice of Allah.
orig: فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mindfulness about one's actions and their consequences. Believers are encouraged to maintain consciousness of God's presence and judgments, and to reflect on their deeds in preparation for the Hereafter. It underscores accountability as a fundamental aspect of faith, reminding the faithful that God is fully aware of all their actions, urging them to live righteously to attain His approval and avoid His displeasure.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of neglecting the remembrance of Allah. Forgetting Allah leads to a loss of one's true self, meaning one's sense of purpose, direction, and morality is compromised. Those who fall into this state are described as 'defiantly disobedient,' indicating a severe deviation from the righteous path.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of the Garden. The companions of the Garden are the victorious ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate distinction and disparity between those who follow a righteous path and those who do not. It highlights the ultimate success and victory of those who attain Paradise (Garden) over those condemned to Hellfire. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of one's choices and actions in the context of faith and obedience to God, stressing that true success is determined by one's moral and spiritual alignment with divine guidance.
orig: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون

translation: Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense power and majesty of the Qur'an by illustrating that even a massive, unyielding mountain would be humbled and shattered by the divine words out of fear of Allah. It underlines the profundity and seriousness of the Qur'anic message, suggesting that if something as grand and powerful as a mountain would be moved by it, then humans, with their faculties of understanding and emotion, should be even more receptive and reflective. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity to consider the weight and significance of the divine message and reflect upon its impact on their lives and spiritual state.
orig: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and exclusivity of Allah as the only deity, highlighting His knowledge of both the hidden and the apparent aspects of existence. It also underscores His attributes of being merciful and compassionate, reminding believers of His benevolence and care for His creation.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and unparalleled attributes of Allah, enumerating His divine qualities and affirming His singular status as the only deity. It refutes any form of polytheism or the association of partners with Allah, highlighting His supremacy and perfection in various aspects. The attributes mentioned—Sovereign, Pure, Perfection, Bestower of Faith, Overseer, Exalted in Might, Compeller, and Superior—illustrate the vastness of His power, authority, and sanctity, calling believers to recognize His ultimate authority and to reject any form of idolatry or association with Him.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine attributes of God, acknowledging Him as the Creator, the One who brings things into existence, and the Fashioner who gives everything its form. It underscores His possession of the most beautiful names, symbolizing His qualities and attributes. The verse also reflects that all of creation, both in the heavens and on the earth, glorifies Him, signifying His supreme authority and wisdom. Lastly, it highlights His might and wisdom, affirming that He is powerful and possesses ultimate wisdom in His actions and decrees.
orig: هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, having driven out the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out for jihad in My cause and seeking My pleasure, you confide to them affection, but I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse advises the believers against forming alliances or nurturing affectionate relations with those who are declared enemies of Allah and who have rejected the truth of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the contradiction in supporting those who oppose the believers’ fundamental faith and mission. The verse reminds the believers of the persecution they faced for their belief in God and emphasizes the sincerity required in their jihad and pursuit of God's pleasure. It also serves as a stern warning that God is omniscient, fully aware of their hidden and apparent actions. Transgressing this directive is equated with deviating from the righteous path.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء تلقون إليهم بالمودة وقد كفروا بما جاءكم من الحق يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم إن كنتم خرجتم جهادا في سبيلي وابتغاء مرضاتي تسرون إليهم بالمودة وأنا أعلم بما أخفيتم وما أعلنتم ومن يفعله منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: If they gain dominance over you, they would be your enemies and extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers about the intentions and actions of certain adversaries. It emphasizes that if these opponents were to gain power over the believers, they would act with hostility not just physically but also verbally, expressing malice and wishing to lead them away from their faith. The verse highlights the importance of being cautious and aware of the true nature and goals of these enemies.
orig: إن يثقفوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء وودوا لو تكفرون

translation: Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, familial relations and offspring will be of no advantage to anyone. It underscores the concept of individual accountability, where each person will be judged based on their own deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of every action, indicating His omniscience and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: لن تنفعكم أرحامكم ولا أولادكم يوم القيامة يفصل بينكم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, there is for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, 'Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than Allah. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone.' But not the statement of Abraham to his father, 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power to do for you anything against Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to look up to Abraham and his followers as role models for their unwavering faith and principled stance against idolatry. It highlights their firm rejection of polytheism and their clear, uncompromising message to their own people, while also illustrating the compassionate side of Abraham as he promises to seek forgiveness for his father, despite acknowledging his limitations. Ultimately, the verse reminds believers of the essence of reliance on Allah, repentance, and the acknowledgment of returning to Him.
orig: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه إذ قالوا لقومهم إنا برآء منكم ومما تعبدون من دون الله كفرنا بكم وبدا بيننا وبينكم العداوة والبغضاء أبدا حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه لأستغفرن لك وما أملك لك من الله من شيء ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير

translation: Our Lord, do not make us [objects of] trial for those who have disbelieved and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a plea to Allah, asking Him not to make the believers a source of trial or temptation for those who disbelieve. This could mean not allowing the disbelievers to have power over the believers in a way that might lead the disbelievers to mock or victimize them, thereby testing their faith. Additionally, the supplication seeks Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging His power and wisdom. The believers express their reliance on Allah's might and wisdom to maintain their integrity and avoid becoming a cause of misguidance or doubt in faith for the non-believers.
orig: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse directs the believers to look up to the exemplary conduct of the righteous people mentioned, as a model to follow in their own lives. It particularly addresses those who hope for Allah's satisfaction and the rewards of the Last Day. The mention of Allah being free of need and praiseworthy serves as a reminder that those who turn away from His guidance do so to their own detriment, as His greatness and self-sufficiency are unaffected by human actions.
orig: لقد كان لكم فيهم أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those with whom you have enmity. And Allah is Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even in times of enmity and discord, one should not lose hope in the possibility of reconciliation. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's power to transform hearts and foster love where there was once conflict. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attributes of omnipotence, forgiveness, and mercy, indicating that with divine intervention, seemingly impossible situations can be resolved.
orig: عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة والله قدير والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes, to deal kindly and justly with them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes a principle of justice and kindness towards non-Muslims who do not show hostility towards Muslims. It conveys that, even amidst religious differences, acts of kindness and fairness are commendable and loved by Allah. The verse stresses that hostility should not be met with hostility if the other party is peaceful, thus encouraging coexistence and mutual respect.
orig: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم وتقسطوا إليهم إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - (forbids) that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers not to form alliances or friendships with those who oppose and fight them on the basis of their faith, expel them from their homes, or assist others in such actions. It emphasizes that allying with such adversaries is an act of injustice and aligns the ally with wrongdoers. The directive is rooted in maintaining the integrity and cohesion of the Muslim community in the face of persecution and hostility while distinguishing between everyday cordial interactions and strategic alliances.
orig: إنما ينهاكم الله عن الذين قاتلوكم في الدين وأخرجوكم من دياركم وظاهروا على إخراجكم أن تولوهم ومن يتولهم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing as to their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. But give the disbelievers what they have spent [in dowry]. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation. And hold not to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, but ask for what you have spent and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, instructing them on how to handle situations where believing women come to them after having emigrated. It emphasizes the importance of examining their faith to confirm their belief. Once it is established that they are true believers, they must not be sent back to the disbelievers, as lawful marriage is only between believers. The believers are also advised to compensate the disbelievers for the dowry spent on these women. This underscores the importance of fairness and justice in financial matters and the sanctity of marriage in Islam. The verse concludes by reminding that such rulings are divinely ordained, portraying Allah's wisdom and knowledge in making these judgments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا جاءكم المؤمنات مهاجرات فامتحنوهن الله أعلم بإيمانهن فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن وآتوهم ما أنفقوا ولا جناح عليكم أن تنكحوهن إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن ولا تمسكوا بعصم الكوافر واسألوا ما أنفقتم وليسألوا ما أنفقوا ذلكم حكم الله يحكم بينكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and then you have your turn (of captives), then pay those whose wives have gone, the equivalent of what they had spent (on their dowry). And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where Muslim women leave their Muslim husbands to join the disbelievers. It instructs the Muslim community to compensate those husbands who have lost their wives by providing them with an equivalent amount of what they had spent on the marriage. The intent is to ensure justice and fairness for the affected individuals and to remind the believers to maintain their consciousness and fear of Allah, reinforcing their commitment to faith and moral integrity.
orig: وإن فاتكم شيء من أزواجكم إلى الكفار فعاقبتم فآتوا الذين ذهبت أزواجهم مثل ما أنفقوا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: O Prophet, when believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor will they steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) concerning the conditions under which he should accept the allegiance of believing women. It highlights the moral and social responsibilities of these women, including the prohibition of idolatry, theft, adultery, infanticide, inventing false accusations, and disobedience in matters of known righteousness. By instructing the Prophet to ask for Allah's forgiveness on their behalf, it underscores the themes of accountability, moral rectitude, and the mercy of Allah towards those who sincerely repent and pledge to lead a righteous life.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا ولا يسرقن ولا يزنين ولا يقتلن أولادهن ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن ولا يعصينك في معروف فبايعهن واستغفر لهن الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry. They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse advises believers against forming alliances with those who have incurred Allah's wrath, hinting that such people have lost hope in the afterlife. The comparison to disbelievers who have despaired over the deceased underscores their complete loss of faith and hope, serving as a warning to maintain spiritual integrity and loyalty to principles of faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, acknowledges the greatness and perfection of Allah by glorifying Him. It highlights Allah's attributes of being All-Mighty, indicating His supreme power over all things, and All-Wise, signifying His perfect wisdom in creation and governance. The universe, in its entirety, is in a state of submission and praise to Allah, reflecting His omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, emphasizing the importance of aligning one's actions with one's words. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy and encourages integrity and sincerity in both speech and behavior. It underscores the moral responsibility to practice what one preaches and maintain consistency between one's declarations and actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون

translation: Most hateful it is with Allah that you say that which you do not do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave disdain that Allah has for hypocrisy, specifically for those who preach righteousness or make promises but fail to act accordingly. It underlines the moral and ethical importance of consistency between one's words and deeds, urging believers to avoid hypocrisy and to uphold integrity and truthfulness in their actions.
orig: كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined firmly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue and high status of those who strive and fight in the way of Allah with unity and determination. It highlights the importance of discipline, organization, and solidarity among the believers, comparing them to a tightly constructed building, indicating strength, cohesion, and unwavering resolve in their cause.
orig: إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, why do you harm me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?' And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse recounts the challenges faced by Moses from his own people, who, despite knowing his divine mission, caused him harm and trouble. Their deliberate disregard for guidance resulted in Allah turning their hearts away from the path of truth, emphasizing that persistent disobedience leads to a lack of divine guidance. The verse serves as a warning against rejecting prophetic guidance and the peril of hardening one’s heart against divine messages.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, 'O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus (peace be upon him) is depicted as affirming his role as a prophet sent to the Children of Israel, aligning his message with the teachings of the Torah. Additionally, he foretells the coming of another prophet after him, named Ahmad (interpreted by many as referring to Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him). Despite the clear signs and evidences brought by this subsequent prophet, the response of some was to dismiss his message as mere sorcery, reflecting a pattern of resistance and disbelief in the face of divine truth.
orig: وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fabricate lies about Allah, particularly when they are being called to the truth of Islam. It emphasizes the severe nature of such wrongdoing and clarifies that Allah does not provide guidance to those who persist in their injustice and falsehoods. The verse serves as a warning to avoid deceit and distortion of religious truths.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله الكذب وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will complete His light even if the disbelievers hate it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of opposition against the divine truth. The 'light of Allah' represents His guidance and message, which some people attempt to suppress through falsehoods and opposition. However, God's intention to uphold and perfect His guidance is unwavering and cannot be thwarted by human efforts, regardless of the disbelievers’ disdain. It affirms the enduring power and completion of divine truth despite opposition.
orig: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), with clear guidance and the true religion, which is Islam. The purpose of this divine mission is to establish the supremacy and dominance of Islam over all other religious systems. Despite resistance and aversion from those who commit shirk (associate partners with Allah), the truth of Islam will ultimately prevail and be recognized universally. It reflects the unyielding nature of divine will and the inevitable victory of truth over falsehood.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, suggesting that there is a form of 'commerce' or 'transaction' that goes beyond worldly trade. It hints at a spiritual investment—likely involving faith, good deeds, and adherence to divine guidance—that offers the ultimate profit of salvation from painful punishment. The verse underscores the idea that true profit is not measured in material wealth but in spiritual fulfillment and divine reward.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and active commitment in the path of Allah. Belief in Allah and His Messenger is foundational, but it must be complemented with tangible efforts and sacrifices, both financially and personally. Such sincere devotion and striving are ultimately beneficial, offering profound rewards and fulfillment far beyond mere worldly gains, if one truly understands the eternal significance of these actions.
orig: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eternity. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy and reward that Allah promises to those who are faithful and repentant. It emphasizes that forgiveness of sins and entry into paradisiacal gardens, characterized by flowing rivers and delightful residences, constitute the ultimate success and fulfillment in the Hereafter. These divine rewards serve as motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and maintain their faith.
orig: يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And something else you love: help from Allah and a near victory. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the promise of divine support and upcoming victory that believers hold dear. It's an assurance from Allah that He will provide assistance and imminent triumph. The verse encourages the faithful to remain steadfast as they can expect good news and achievements through their faith and patience.
orig: وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah.' And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to be devout helpers and supporters of Allah's cause, akin to how Jesus appealed to his disciples to stand by him in support of Allah. The response from the disciples signifies their commitment and readiness to assist in spreading Allah's message. The verse then reflects on the historical division among the Children of Israel, where one group believed and another disbelieved. Allah provided support to the believers, enabling them to prevail over their adversaries and achieve dominance. The verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty, unity, and perseverance in faith, ultimately assuring that Allah aids those who staunchly uphold His cause.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا أنصار الله كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم فأصبحوا ظاهرين

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of Allah's dominion and the inherent acknowledgment of His greatness by all of creation. The heavens and the earth, as symbols of the entire universe, engage in glorifying Allah, indicating that worship and recognition of His supreme attributes—such as sovereignty, holiness, might, and wisdom—are intrinsic to all beings and elements of creation. This serves to remind humanity of Allah's unparalleled authority and the natural order's submission to His will.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who has sent among the unlettered ones a Messenger (Muhammad) from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. And verily, they had been before in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse underscores God's benevolence in sending Prophet Muhammad, an unlettered person like the people he was sent to, as a messenger. His primary roles include reciting God's revelations, purifying the people morally and spiritually, and imparting knowledge of the Scripture and wisdom. This mission is particularly significant because it addresses a community that was previously in clear deviation from the path of righteousness, emphasizing the transformative impact of the Prophet's guidance.
orig: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And (to) others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's plan to extend His guidance and mercy not only to the current believers but also to future generations who will join the faith later on. It emphasizes Allah's attributes of being Mighty and Wise, indicating that His decisions are rooted in perfect wisdom and power, encompassing all times and generations.
orig: وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: That is the grace of Allah, which He bestows on whom He pleases. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the favors and blessings of Allah are granted according to His wisdom and knowledge. It underscores the idea that divine grace is not earned solely by human efforts but is dispensed by Allah's discretion. The verse also highlights the endless and immense nature of Allah's bounty, suggesting that His generosity knows no bounds.
orig: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah then failed to uphold it is like that of a donkey carrying books. How dreadful is the example of those who reject the signs of Allah! And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse uses the analogy of a donkey carrying books to illustrate those who have been given sacred knowledge (the Torah) but do not practice or understand its essence. Just as a donkey gains no benefit from the books it carries, these individuals derive no true benefit from the divine knowledge they possess because they fail to apply it. It criticizes such people for their rejection of God's signs and highlights that such willful ignorance or neglect of divine guidance renders one unworthy of God's guidance. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the failure to act upon divine teachings.
orig: مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah apart from the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim to be especially favored by Allah—specifically, the Jewish people who asserted their exclusive alliance with Allah. It invites them to wish for death if they are sincere in their belief, as true allies of Allah would be eager to meet Him. The underlying message is to question the validity and sincerity of their exclusive claims to divine favor.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have sent ahead; and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the insincerity of some individuals who, despite their outward assertions, do not truly wish for the consequences or accountability of their actions due to the misdeeds they have committed. It underscores the idea that Allah is fully aware of the injustices and wrongdoings perpetrated by such individuals, and nothing is hidden from His knowledge.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the death from which you flee – indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the futility of trying to escape it. It emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, who is aware of both the unseen and the seen. After death, individuals will be brought back to Allah who will then inform them of their deeds, signifying accountability and the importance of righteous actions in this life.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse is a directive to the believers emphasizing the importance of the Friday congregational prayer (Jumu'ah). It instructs Muslims to hasten towards the remembrance of Allah when the call to prayer is made on Friday and to temporarily abandon their commercial activities. This serves as a reminder of prioritizing spiritual obligations over worldly pursuits, indicating that observing the Friday prayer is more beneficial for one's faith and well-being, bringing greater rewards than any worldly gain.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Then, when the prayer is concluded, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often so that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse guides the believers to resume their daily activities, including seeking their livelihood and engaging in commerce, once they have completed their prayers. It emphasizes the balance between spiritual duties and worldly responsibilities, highlighting that both are important. The instruction to remember Allah frequently even while engaged in worldly pursuits serves to keep one's faith and consciousness of God at the forefront, ensuring that their actions remain morally and ethically guided, which ultimately leads to true success.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: But when they saw a transaction or a diversion, they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, 'What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse addresses a situation where people, upon seeing an opportunity for trade or amusement, abandoned the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as he was delivering a sermon. It underscores the weakness in human nature that prioritizes immediate, worldly gains over spiritual benefits. The verse teaches that what Allah offers, i.e., spiritual and eternal rewards, is far superior to fleeting worldly amusements and material advantages. It also emphasizes that sustenance and provision ultimately come from Allah, thus encouraging believers to trust in Him rather than being overly concerned with material pursuits.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger. And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of hypocrites who outwardly declare their belief in the Prophet Muhammad as the Messenger of Allah, yet inwardly they harbor disbelief and deceit. Allah confirms the truth of Muhammad's prophethood and exposes the hypocrisy of those who falsely claim faith. The verse highlights the distinction between sincere belief and hypocritical lip service, underscoring that true faith is known and validated by Allah, while hypocrisy is condemned and revealed by Him.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: They have taken their oaths as a cover, and thus they hinder [others] from the path of Allah. Surely, evil is what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who use false oaths and deceit as a means to cover their insincerity and wrongdoings. By doing so, they actively prevent others from following the righteous path and cause harm to the spread of faith. The verse condemns their actions, highlighting the moral corruption and negative impact of their deceitful behavior on the community.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved; therefore, their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequence of repeatedly turning away from faith after accepting it. The sealing of hearts symbolizes a divine response, resulting in an inability to comprehend or return to guidance. This reflects the principle that intentional and persistent rejection of faith can lead to a spiritual state where one becomes entirely closed off to the truth and divine guidance.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. [They are] as if they were pieces of wood propped up - they think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse portrays the hypocrites who outwardly appear impressive and speak eloquently, yet lack genuine faith and substance. They are compared to hollow, propped-up wood, symbolizing their inner emptiness. Their constant paranoia, thinking every cry is against them, reflects their guilty conscience. The verse warns believers to be cautious of such individuals, recognizing them as true adversaries whose deceit warrants divine condemnation. Their deception is seen as a significant moral failing.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,' they turn their heads aside and you see them refusing while they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of certain individuals who, despite being offered an opportunity for forgiveness through the intercession of the Prophet, dismiss the invitation with disdain. Their refusal is coupled with a sense of superiority, showcasing their reluctance to humble themselves and seek repentance. The verse serves as a critique of such attitudes and underscores the importance of humility and accepting guidance in seeking forgiveness.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: In this verse, it is emphasized that for certain individuals who persistently engage in rebellion and disobedience against God's commands, asking for their forgiveness is futile because God has decreed that He will not forgive them. This underscores a principle that divine forgiveness is contingent upon sincere repentance and a genuine turning away from sinful behavior. Those who remain defiantly disobedient and persist in their corrupt ways are beyond the scope of divine guidance and forgiveness due to their hardened hearts and continuous rejection of the truth.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.' But to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, yet the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the malintent of the hypocrites who try to weaken the followers of the Prophet Muhammad through economic manipulation, suggesting that withholding support might cause his followers to abandon him. However, Allah reminds them that true sustenance and wealth come from Him, and such scheming cannot alter His divine provision. The verse underlines the idea that hypocrites lack understanding of Allah’s omnipotence and the real sources of provision, which go beyond material means.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, 'If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the meaner.' But honor belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and to the believers; but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and misguided assumptions of the hypocrites who believed that they held the power and honor to control and expel others from the city of Medina. It highlights their ignorance by affirming that true honor and authority belong to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. The verse underscores the divine order and the futility of human pride against Allah’s will.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون
