translation: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the remembrance of Allah over material possessions and familial ties. It warns believers against being distracted by their wealth and children to the extent that they neglect their spiritual duties. The verse underscores that such neglect leads to true loss, as it pulls one away from the ultimate purpose of life and the path to success in the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend [in the way of Allah] from what We have provided you before death approaches one of you and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of utilizing one's wealth for good deeds and charitable actions before death overtakes them. It serves as a reminder that once death comes, one's opportunities to perform good deeds, such as giving charity and acting righteously, are no longer available. The verse reflects the regret people may feel at the time of death for not having done more in their lives to fulfill their religious and moral obligations. It encourages believers to act proactively and make the most of the resources and time they have been given by Allah.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And never will Allah delay a soul when its time has come. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of death. It underscores that every soul has an appointed time of demise, which will not be delayed by any means. It also serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions, promoting a sense of accountability and urging individuals to remain conscious of their deeds in this life.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah; His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and sovereignty of Allah. Everything in existence, whether in the heavens or on earth, glorifies Him, acknowledging His supreme authority and control over all creation. It highlights Allah's unmatched power and the inherent recognition of His majesty by all creatures, who express gratitude and praise His greatness.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He is the One who created you, then some of you are disbelievers and some of you are believers. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of humanity, emphasizing that God is the Creator of all people. It then acknowledges the diversity in people's faith, noting that within humanity, there are both believers and disbelievers. This plurality in belief does not escape God's awareness; He is fully observant of all human actions, suggesting accountability and the importance of conscience in one's deeds.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms; and to Him is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deliberate and purposeful creation of the universe by Allah, who not only brought the heavens and earth into being with true purpose but also meticulously created and perfected human beings in their physical forms. It serves as a reminder of divine craftsmanship and the final accountability to Allah, urging humans to acknowledge His sovereignty and the reality of returning to Him for judgment.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you reveal. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience, highlighting that His knowledge encompasses everything in the heavens and the earth, as well as the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals. It serves as a reminder of the thorough nature of God's awareness, indicating that He is fully cognizant of both public actions and hidden intentions, thus encouraging believers to maintain sincerity and mindfulness in their thoughts and actions.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Has there not reached you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse reminds the audience of the historical consequences faced by those who disbelieved in the past. It serves as a warning that disbelief and rejection of divine guidance lead to severe repercussions in this life and a painful punishment in the afterlife. The mention of the previous disbelievers serves both as a reflection on past events and a reminder of the enduring principles of divine justice.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, 'Shall human beings guide us?' So they disbelieved and turned away. But Allah was independent of them; and Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of previous communities who, despite being presented with clear signs and guidance by the messengers, rejected the truth on the basis that they could not accept being guided by fellow human beings. Their rejection and turning away from the message is criticized, and it is emphasized that their disbelief does not harm Allah, as He is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and the importance of humility in accepting divine guidance.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that, for Allah, is easy.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the assertion made by disbelievers that there will be no resurrection after death. In response, the verse firmly affirms the reality of the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes God's omnipotence and the inevitability of accountability for one's actions. This serves both as a warning to disbelievers and a reassurance to believers about the certainty of the hereafter and divine justice.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light (i.e., the Qur'an) which We have sent down. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah, His Messenger, and the guidance provided through the Qur'an. It calls on people to recognize the divine source of the Qur'an and to follow its teachings. Additionally, it serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions, encouraging individuals to act righteously and with sincerity.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering—that will be the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness—He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Resurrection, referred to as the Day of Gathering, highlighting the stark contrast between those who believed and did righteous deeds and those who didn't. For believers who have faith in Allah and perform good deeds, their sins will be forgiven, and they will be granted eternal life in the gardens of paradise. This ultimate reward is termed as 'the great attainment,' emphasizing the unparalleled success and eternal bliss that awaits the righteous in the hereafter.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—they will be the residents of the Fire, dwelling therein forever. And what an evil destination!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave consequences for those who reject faith and deny the signs of God. It warns that such individuals will face eternal punishment in the Hellfire, stressing the permanence of their dire fate and underscoring the severity of disbelief and denial in the eyes of God.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: No disaster strikes except by permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah - He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief that all events, including calamities, occur by the will and permission of Allah. It encourages faith in Allah, assuring that such faith will result in guidance and tranquility of the heart. It highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge of all matters, reminding believers to trust in His wisdom and plan.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger, highlighting that the core responsibility of the Messenger is to convey the message clearly. It underscores that accountability lies in the act of transmission, while the acceptance and adherence to the guidance rest upon the individuals themselves. The verse also implies that turning away from the message does not diminish the Messenger’s role, as his duty is inherently fulfilled by delivering the message plainly.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah, let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that He is the only deity worthy of worship. It underscores the importance of Tawakkul (trust) in Allah, advising believers to place their reliance and dependency entirely on Him, acknowledging His supreme power and authority in all matters.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the closest relationships, such as those with spouses and children, may sometimes pose challenges to one's faith and devotion. The term 'enemies' is not literal; it signifies that these loved ones might inadvertently lead believers away from their religious duties or cause them to compromise their faith. The verse advises caution in such relationships. However, it also encourages forgiveness, understanding, and leniency—highlighting the importance of maintaining compassion and mercy towards family members. Ultimately, it reminds believers of Allah's attribute of being Most Forgiving and Most Merciful, calling them to embody these qualities in their relationships.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse signifies that wealth and children, while blessings, are also tests from Allah to see how one manages and utilizes them. It indicates that these worldly possessions should not distract one from fulfilling their duties to Allah. Instead, believers are reminded that true and everlasting rewards are with Allah, urging them to prioritize spiritual commitments over material attachments.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend [in the way of Allah]; it is better for your souls. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of God-consciousness to the best of one's ability, adherence to divine guidance, and generosity. It highlights that true success lies in overcoming one's innate greed and selfishness, and that such self-restraint and obedience bring about spiritual prosperity and fulfillment.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you; and Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of giving in charity for the sake of Allah. It assures believers that any act of charity done with good intentions will be rewarded manifold by Allah. Moreover, it promises forgiveness for the giver, highlighting Allah's appreciation and patience. The language used encourages believers to act generously and reassures them that their contributions will not only aid those in need but also benefit them spiritually and eternally.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite knowledge and wisdom of Allah. By referring to Him as the 'Knower of the unseen and the witnessed,' it highlights His awareness of all realities, both hidden and visible. The titles 'Exalted in Might' and 'the Wise' further emphasize His supreme power and the profound wisdom with which He governs the universe. It serves as a reminder of His omnipresence and the perfect balance of might and wisdom in His divine order.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet, when you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period and count the waiting period precisely, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their [husbands'] houses, nor should they (themselves) leave, except in case they commit a clear immorality. Those are the limits [set by] Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse addresses the protocols and ethical guidelines for divorce in Islam, emphasizing that divorces should be timed to allow for proper reckoning of the waiting period (‘iddah). This waiting period serves multiple purposes, including ensuring that the woman is not pregnant, which maintains clarity around issues of paternity and inheritance. It also provides a potential period of reflection and reconciliation. The verse underscores the importance of fearing Allah and adhering to His commands, highlighting that women should not be driven out of their homes nor should they leave, unless they have committed a serious offense. This illustrates the protective and respectful stance Islam envisions towards women even in the process of divorce. Further, it warns against transgressing Allah's limits, as such actions would harm oneself, and signifies that Allah may bring new circumstances in due time, which encourages patience and compliance with divine wisdom.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: And when they have fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for the acceptance of Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him a way out.
interpretation: This verse addresses the importance of fairness and justice in the process of divorce, emphasizing that actions should be conducted with kindness and righteousness. It also stresses the importance of having just witnesses and upholding honesty for the sake of Allah. Additionally, the verse provides reassurance that those who are mindful of Allah and act ethically will be provided with solutions and relief from their difficulties.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And He will provide for him from sources he never could imagine. And whoever puts their trust in Allah, He will be enough for them. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a decreed extent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless provision and support from Allah to those who have unwavering trust in Him. It reassures believers that reliance on Allah brings sufficient support and fulfillment of needs in unexpected ways. The verse also highlights the divine ordination and meticulous planning inherent in Allah's actions, indicating that every aspect of existence is governed by His precise decree.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: As for those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have any doubt, their waiting period is three months, and also for those who have not menstruated. And those who are pregnant, their waiting period is until they deliver their burden. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him of his matter ease.
interpretation: This verse addresses the waiting periods ('iddah) for women in different circumstances as part of the broader rules of divorce. For elderly women who no longer menstruate and for young girls who have not yet started menstruating, the waiting period is set to three months. For pregnant women, the waiting period extends until they give birth. Additionally, the verse highlights a broader spiritual principle: those who are conscious of Allah and follow His commands will find their matters made easier by Him.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: This is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah—He will remove from him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the commands of Allah, which have been revealed for the guidance of humankind. It underscores that those who are conscious of Allah and act with piety will be pardoned for their sins and will receive a significant reward. The verse highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah towards those who maintain their devotion and fear of Him.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: Lodge them (in a section) where you dwell out of your means and do not harm them in order to oppress them. And if they should be pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. And if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment and confer among yourselves in the acceptable way; but if you are in discord, then there may breastfeed for the father another woman.
interpretation: This verse provides guidelines on how to treat divorced women, specifically addressing their lodging and financial support. It emphasizes the obligation to provide adequate housing and not to harm or exert pressure on them. If the woman is pregnant, the responsibility of financial support extends until childbirth. Should she choose to breastfeed the child, she is entitled to payment for this service. The verse encourages mutual consultation and fair dealing in these matters. In cases where an agreement cannot be reached, it suggests that another woman may nurse the child, indicating practical solutions for co-parenting challenges post-divorce.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth; and he whose provision is restricted—let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will soon bring ease after hardship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of spending and charity based on one's means. It encourages those with ample resources to give generously while also acknowledging the limitations of those with less. It reinforces the idea that God does not impose more than what one can handle and assures that hardship will be followed by ease, promoting patience and trust in divine wisdom during challenging times.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: And how many a city was insolent towards the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We took it to severe account and punished it with a dreadful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by communities that exhibit arrogance and disobedience towards divine commandments and the guidance of prophets. It serves as a reminder that persistent defiance and rejection of divine authority can lead to severe repercussions and punishment. The message aims to encourage humility, obedience, and recognition of divine guidance to avoid such unfortunate outcomes.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: And it tasted the evil consequence of its affair; and the outcome of its affair was loss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle that actions have consequences. When a community or an individual engages in wrongdoing, they will inevitably face the repercussions of those actions. The phrase 'tasted the evil consequence' metaphorically describes the direct experience of negative outcomes resulting from their behavior. The final outcome being 'loss' signifies both a material and spiritual downfall, emphasizing that deviating from righteousness ultimately leads to failure and regret.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O you who have understanding, those who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a Reminder.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have faith and possess wisdom and understanding. It warns of severe punishment prepared for the disobedient and encourages the believers to be mindful of Allah. The term 'Reminder' refers to the Qur'an, emphasizing its role as guidance and a means of remembering Allah's teachings. The verse calls upon believers to align their lives with the divine message and to heed the warnings and wisdom provided in the revelation.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: A messenger reciting to you the clear signs of Allah, so that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darkness into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Indeed, Allah has granted for him an excellent provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the messenger in conveying Allah's clear signs to guide the believers from the darkness of ignorance to the light of faith and righteous living. It highlights the importance of belief and good deeds, promising eternal rewards in the form of paradise, where rivers flow underneath, to those who follow this path. The verse reassures that Allah's provision is best and eternal for those who believe and act righteously.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: Allah is He who created seven heavens, and of the earth, the like thereof. His command descends among them so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah by highlighting the creation of the seven heavens and the earth in a similar structure. It underscores that divine commands govern all realms, indicating the meticulous order and control exercised by Allah. The mention of Allah's comprehensive knowledge serves to remind believers of His awareness of all matters, reinforcing His authority and capability over the universe.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad directly, questioning why he would make something forbidden for himself that Allah has allowed, particularly in an effort to appease his wives. It emphasizes that Allah is forgiving and merciful, suggesting that human errors and intentions, especially those aimed at maintaining harmony in family relationships, are understood and forgiven by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize divine commandments over personal or relational compromises.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah has already ordained for you (Muslims) the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah provides guidance and solutions for believers, including the manner in which they can be released from oaths they have sworn. It underscores Allah's role as a protector who knows everything and acts with wisdom. It serves to reassure believers that Allah's commandments are just and beneficial, and that even in matters like oaths, His wisdom provides a way out when necessary.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And [remember] when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement; and when she informed [another] of it and Allah showed it to him, he made known part of it and ignored a part. And when he informed her about it, she said, 'Who told you this?' He said, 'I was informed by the Knowing, the Acquainted.'
interpretation: This verse highlights an incident where the Prophet Muhammad confided a matter to one of his wives, which she later disclosed to another. Allah subsequently informed the Prophet of this disclosure. In response, the Prophet selectively revealed to his wife what had been exposed to him by Allah, indicating his awareness of her actions without fully confronting her. This demonstrates Allah's omniscience and how He supports His Prophet by revealing hidden matters, and it underscores the importance of trust and respect in personal relationships.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: If you two turn in repentance to Allah, (it is better for you), for your hearts have deviated. But if you support one another against him – then indeed, Allah is his Protector, and Gabriel and the righteous of the believers and the angels, moreover, are his assistants.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the situation where two of the Prophet Muhammad's wives were involved in an incident that caused displeasure. It calls them to repent and return to the right path as their hearts have deviated momentarily. The verse also serves as a reminder that if they continue to oppose the Prophet, he has divine support from Allah, the angel Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels, emphasizing that divine and spiritual help is always with the Prophet.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you—submitting [to Allah], believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, and traveling [for Allah's cause]—previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse addresses the possibility of Allah providing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with better spouses if he were to divorce his current wives. The focus is on qualities that are highly valued in Islam: submission to Allah, faith, obedience, repentance, worship, and striving in Allah’s cause. It highlights that these qualities are what make a person truly valued in the sight of Allah, regardless of their previous marital status. The verse serves as a reminder that spiritual and moral attributes are of utmost importance in a marital relationship.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse provides a somber admonition to the believers, urging them to not only be mindful of their own conduct but also to actively guide and protect their families from falling into sin. The imagery of a fearsome Fire fueled by humans and stones, and guarded by stern angels who strictly execute God's orders, serves to underscore the severe consequences of neglecting this responsibility. It emphasizes the importance of personal and familial piety, obedience to divine commands, and the relentless nature of divine justice.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who disbelieve, make no excuses this Day. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have disbelieved, telling them that on the Day of Judgment, their excuses will not be accepted. It emphasizes the accountability and the principle of recompense based on one's deeds, highlighting that the punishment or reward received is a direct result of their own actions in their worldly life.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to turn back to Allah with sincere repentance, emphasizing the importance of genuinely seeking forgiveness and making a commitment to change. It promises that such sincere repentance can lead to the erasure of their sins and entry into Paradise. The verse also assures the believers that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who have faith with him. Their righteousness will be evident through the light emanating from them, symbolizing divine guidance and approval. The believers pray for the completion and perfecting of their light, symbolizing their faith and guidance, and they seek Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging His omnipotence.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be stern with them. Their abode is Hell, and what an evil destination.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to actively struggle against those who reject faith (disbelievers) and those who pretend to believe but act treacherously (hypocrites). It emphasizes a firm and unwavering stance toward these groups, highlighting the severe consequences they face in the hereafter, which is eternal damnation in Hell. The sternness is not for personal affront but to uphold the faith and protect the community from harm.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: Allah presents an example of those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them, so they did not benefit them against Allah at all, and it was said, 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
interpretation: This verse demonstrates that being close to righteous individuals does not guarantee salvation if one chooses the path of disbelief and betrayal. The wives of the prophets Noah and Lot are cited as examples of individuals who lived in the proximity of virtue but opted for a different path. Their relationships with their righteous husbands couldn't protect them from divine punishment, underscoring the principle that each person is accountable for their own faith and actions. It serves as a warning that personal connections or associations cannot replace genuine belief and righteous conduct.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And Allah presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the faith and resilience of the wife of Pharaoh, who despite her husband's tyranny and disbelief, sought refuge and support from Allah. It underscores the importance of unwavering faith and trust in God, even in the face of severe adversity. Her supplication for a place in Paradise and deliverance from injustice serves as an inspiration for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to seek Allah's help in overcoming worldly trials.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And [the example of] Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into [her garment] through Our angel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue and purity of Mary, the mother of Jesus. It emphasizes her chastity and her unwavering faith in God's words and His scriptures. The verse also underscores the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth through God's divine intervention. Furthermore, it acknowledges Mary as a pious and devout servant of God, setting an example of faithfulness and obedience.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse praises the supreme power and authority of Allah, indicating that all sovereignty belongs solely to Him. It emphasizes His absolute ability to control and manage the universe, underscoring His omnipotence and unparalleled capability over all things.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deeds – and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving
interpretation: This verse highlights that both life and death are creations of Allah with a purpose: to test human beings. The test is to determine who among people performs the best deeds, encompassing both righteous actions and sincere intentions. It emphasizes that life's trials are designed to bring out people's best moral and ethical behavior. Furthermore, it reassures believers that Allah is both mighty, having control over all affairs, and forgiving, ready to pardon those who seek repentance and strive sincerely in their actions.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: He created seven heavens in layers. You do not see any inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful. So return your vision, do you see any breaks?
interpretation: This verse highlights the perfection and meticulousness in Allah's creation of the heavens, emphasizing that there is no flaw or inconsistency in His work. It invites reflection on the order and harmony of the universe, encouraging believers to look carefully and recognize the seamless perfection in all that Allah has fashioned. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the impeccable nature of His creation, leading to a greater appreciation and acknowledgment of His divine attributes.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then return your vision twice again. Your vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued.
interpretation: This verse challenges humans to observe the universe meticulously and repeatedly. It implies the boundless complexity and perfection of creation, suggesting that human understanding is limited. Upon rigorous inspection, one will find no flaws in the creation of Allah but will instead realize their own limitations and become humble. The verse emphasizes God's infinite wisdom and power, urging humans to recognize their place in the grand scheme of existence.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made them what is thrown at devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the beauty of the nearest heaven adorned with stars, showcasing God's ability to create aesthetically pleasing wonders. Moreover, these celestial objects serve as missiles against rebellious devils, symbolizing divine protection against evil. The verse concludes by warning of severe punishment for such deviant entities, underscoring the ultimate justice and retribution that awaits them in the hereafter.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: But for those who disbelieve in their Lord, there is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith in God. It highlights the severe consequences of disbelief, stating that such individuals will face the torment of Hell, which is described as a dreadful and miserable end. The verse underscores the gravity of disbelief and the importance of developing and maintaining a strong belief in God as a means to avoid such a grave outcome.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: When they are thrown into it, they hear from it a [dreadful] inhaling while it boils up.
interpretation: This verse vividly describes the terrifying experience of those cast into Hell, emphasizing both the auditory and physical horrors they will encounter. The 'dreadful inhaling' and the image of boiling convey intense suffering, meant to instill fear and serve as a stern warning against sin and disobedience.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, 'Did there not come to you a warner?'
interpretation: This verse describes the intense and overwhelming anger of Hell as it nearly bursts with rage whenever new groups of disbelievers are thrown into it. The keepers of Hell, the angels tasked with guarding it, will question the new arrivals to remind them of the messengers who had warned them about this fate. The question underscores the accountability of the disbelievers, emphasizing that they were given ample warning and opportunities to change their ways, yet they chose to ignore those divine messages.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They will say, 'Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied and said, ‘Allah has sent down nothing. You are but in great error.’
interpretation: This verse highlights the denial and stubbornness of those who rejected the message of the warners sent by Allah. Despite being given clear guidance, they dismissed it by claiming that nothing had been revealed. Their rejection is portrayed as a significant misguidance, emphasizing the severe consequences of turning away from divine revelation and the importance of heeding the truth when it is presented.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they will say, 'If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the remorse and regret of those who are experiencing the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. They acknowledge that their failure to heed the divine message and use their intellect to understand and follow the guidance led them to their current suffering. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of listening to and comprehending the divine guidance in this life to avoid such a fate.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: So they admitted their sin, but far removed (from mercy) are the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate fate of those who have committed sins and subsequently acknowledged them. Despite their acknowledgment, they are destined for severe punishment because mere admission of guilt without sincere repentance and righteous deeds is insufficient for salvation. The phrase 'companions of the Blaze' refers to those who persist in wrongdoing and face the dire consequences in the hereafter.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of having genuine reverence and fear of Allah even when one is not in the public eye or without physical proof of His presence. It highlights the spiritual integrity and sincerity of believers who are conscious of their duties and responsibilities to Allah privately. The reward for such unwavering mindfulness and devotion is immense, entailing both forgiveness of sins and a great reward, underscoring Allah’s boundless mercy and generosity towards His faithful servants.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Whether you conceal your speech or proclaim it, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has complete and perfect knowledge of all human actions and intentions. Whether a person speaks secretly or openly, it is all known to Allah, for He is fully aware of the true inner thoughts and states of the heart. This serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from God's knowledge, and thus humans should be mindful of their innermost thoughts and intentions as well as their outward actions.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God, being the Creator, possesses complete knowledge and understanding of His creation. As the 'Subtle' and the 'Acquainted,' He knows the intricacies and the hidden aspects of everything. It reminds people that nothing escapes God's perfect awareness and wisdom, reinforcing the concept of divine omniscience and the intimate relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: It is He who made the earth manageable for you, so travel through its pathways and eat of His provision. And to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's benevolence in making the earth accessible and hospitable for human life. It encourages humans to traverse the earth, make use of its resources, and recognize that their sustenance comes from God. Moreover, it serves as a reminder of the eventual resurrection and return to God, underscoring the transient nature of worldly life and the importance of a spiritual journey towards the hereafter.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Have you felt secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and suddenly it would sway?
interpretation: This verse challenges those who feel secure in their disbelief or complacency, reminding them of the omnipotence of Allah. It emphasizes that no one should feel immune to divine retribution, as Allah has the power to cause catastrophic events. It encourages humility and consciousness of God's might, warning against arrogance and a false sense of security.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then, you would know how (severe) was My warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the consequences of ignoring divine warnings. By questioning the sense of security that people might feel, it stresses that no one is beyond the reach of God's power and judgment. The mention of a storm of stones symbolizes severe punishment and underscores the importance of heeding prophetic warnings. It calls for humility and awareness of divine authority, urging people to reflect on their actions and the legitimacy of the threats posed by divine messengers.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And certainly, those before them denied - so how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by previous communities who rejected divine messages. It serves as a warning to the present audience, emphasizing the severe repercussions of denial and disbelief. The rhetorical question underscores the certainty and seriousness of God's punishment for those who choose to ignore the truth.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None upholds them except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the natural world as a sign of Allah’s power and mercy. It emphasizes that the ability of birds to fly, spreading and folding their wings, is not merely a result of physical laws but is a sign of Allah's sustaining power. The verse underscores the concept that everything in existence, down to the flight of a bird, is under Allah’s watchful care and control, serving as a reminder of His omnipotence and mercy.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: Or who is it that can be an army for you to aid you besides the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who disbelieve in the power and mercy of Allah by asking them who else they think could possibly aid them against His will. It underscores the futility of relying on any force other than Allah, highlighting the deluded state of those who place their trust elsewhere. It emphasizes that true support and victory come only from the Most Merciful, and those who oppose this reality are living in a false sense of security.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: Who is it that will provide for you if He should withhold His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse challenges humanity's reliance on themselves or others for sustenance, emphasizing that it is ultimately God who controls all provisions. By questioning who else could provide if God chose to withhold, it calls attention to human dependence on divine mercy. Despite this, people often continue in arrogance and turn away from acknowledging this fundamental truth, displaying an obstinate rejection of God's authority and benevolence.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: Is one who walks fallen on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse uses a powerful metaphor to contrast between those who live their lives in error and misguidance (symbolized by walking fallen on their face) and those who follow the right guidance of Allah (symbolized by walking upright on a straight path). It highlights the difference in outcomes and clarity between those lost in confusion and those following divine direction, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the path of righteousness.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'It is He who produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recognition of God as the Creator who has endowed humanity with essential faculties such as hearing, sight, and intellect. Despite these immense blessings, it criticizes the scarcity of human gratitude towards God's favors. It calls attention to the ingratitude that often overlooks these significant gifts, urging a reflection on the importance of being thankful for the divine provisions that are fundamental to human existence and experience.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: Say, 'It is He who has multiplied you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and omnipotence of God in both creation and the eventual return of all beings. God is depicted as the one who dispersed humanity across the earth, and it is to Him that all will ultimately return for judgment and recompense. This serves as a reminder of human accountability and the transient nature of worldly life, urging people to recognize their dependence on God and live in accordance with His will.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and mockery of those who doubt the truth of the prophetic message and the promised Day of Judgment. They challenge the believers, asking when the foretold events will occur if what is being preached is indeed true. This attitude underscores a lack of faith and a demand for immediate evidence, overlooking the spiritual and moral preparations necessary for understanding divine promises.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that ultimate knowledge of all things rests solely with Him. It underscores the limited role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who is tasked with delivering clear warnings and messages from Allah to guide people, without possessing the divine knowledge that Allah alone holds. This encourages humility and reliance on divine wisdom rather than human speculation.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: But when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved became distressed, and it was said, 'This is what you used to call for.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of sudden realization and panic for disbelievers when the promised event, which they had mocked or denied, finally approaches. Their distressed faces reveal their fear and regret. The statement points to the fulfillment of prophecies or warnings that the disbelievers had been previously dismissive of. It emphasizes the certainty of divine retribution and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers, challenging their sense of security and self-sufficiency. It underscores the reality that regardless of what happens to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, the disbelievers cannot escape the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of divine guidance. The rhetorical question emphasizes that no one can save them from the painful punishment that only Allah has control over, reinforcing the ultimate accountability to Allah alone.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will come to know who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of recognizing God as the Most Merciful and the importance of having faith in Him and putting complete trust in His guidance. It further warns those who deny this truth that they will eventually realize who is truly astray and in manifest error. The invocation of God's mercy highlights His compassion, while the call to faith and reliance serves as a reminder of the dependence of believers on divine support. The concluding statement underscores the ultimate clarity that will emerge regarding who has deviated from the right path.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken into the earth, then who could bring you flowing water?'
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the blessings provided by Allah, specifically the essential resource of water. It reminds people of their dependence on Allah for basic necessities and emphasizes His power and mercy. The verse serves as a prompt for gratitude and recognition of divine sustenance, illustrating that if these blessings were to be withdrawn, humans would be helpless without Allah's provision.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and sanctity of the written word and knowledge. The letter 'Nun' serves as a divine, mystical reference, and the following oath by the pen and the act of writing underscores the critical roles of literacy, learning, and the recording of wisdom in human spiritual and intellectual progress.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not insane.
interpretation: This verse serves to reaffirm the Prophet Muhammad's mental soundness and credibility. It assures both the Prophet and his followers that his teachings and revelations are divinely guided and not a result of madness, as some of his detractors might claim. This divine endorsement is meant to bolster the confidence of the believers and affirm the authenticity of the prophetic message.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse assures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his efforts and dedication towards spreading the message of Islam will not go unrecognized. The term 'غير ممنون' implies a reward that is continuous and without end, emphasizing eternal recompense from Allah for his steadfastness and perseverance. It serves as a divine comfort and encouragement, affirming that the divine reward is abundant and everlasting, unmarred by any cessation or diminution.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted moral and ethical qualities of Prophet Muhammad. It serves as both a commendation and an affirmation of his exemplary conduct, which sets a standard for believers to emulate. The verse underscores the importance of good character and ethical behavior in Islam, highlighting that these attributes are esteemed in the eyes of God.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: And you will see and they will see
interpretation: This verse implies that there will come a time when the truth and reality of a situation will become evident to both the Prophet and his opponents. It speaks to the eventual unveiling of the truth, where both parties will witness the outcome of their actions and beliefs.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: Which of you is the afflicted one?
interpretation: In this verse, the Qur'an engages its audience in reflective contemplation, urging individuals to consider their own state and actions. It calls attention to the afflicted or misguided behavior, encouraging self-examination and awareness of one's own potential deviations from the righteous path. This introspection is meant to lead believers towards recognizing and correcting their faults, and realigning themselves with the principles of faith and righteousness.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect knowledge and wisdom in discerning those who have deviated from His path and those who follow it rightly. It implies that human judgment is limited, and ultimate knowledge of guidance and misguidance rests with Allah alone. This understanding encourages humility and reliance on divine insight over human assumptions.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to stand firm and not to follow or adhere to the guidance of those who reject the truth of the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and to avoid being influenced by those who deny the teachings of Islam.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
interpretation: This verse refers to the desires of some disbelievers who wish that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) would compromise or ease up in his dedication to the message of Islam. Their intention is not out of genuine belief or willingness to change but rather to find a middle ground that would allow them to continue in their ways while reducing the tension with the Prophet's steadfast message. It highlights the external pressure on the Prophet to dilute the principles of the faith for the sake of social harmony or mutual agreement, which is not an option for one committed to divine guidance.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
interpretation: This verse advises against following or giving heed to those who frequently take false oaths or engage in empty talk. It implies that such individuals lack integrity and moral standing, and therefore, their words should not be trusted or respected.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: Backbiter, going about with malicious gossip.
interpretation: This verse condemns specific negative behaviors: being a backbiter and spreading malicious gossip. It highlights the ethical teachings in the Qur'an that stress the importance of maintaining integrity in speech and action. Backbiting and gossip not only harm the individual being talked about but also create a toxic environment within the community. The verse calls upon believers to refrain from such destructive behaviors and to cultivate virtues of honesty, kindness, and constructive communication.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: Hinderer of good, transgressor, sinful.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who actively prevents good from happening, transgresses moral boundaries, and engages in sinful behavior. It serves as a critique of such individuals, highlighting their negative traits and the harm they cause in society by obstructing positive actions and engaging in wrongful acts.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: Cruel and, on top of that, an illegitimate pretender.
interpretation: This verse describes a person characterized by harshness and inhumanity, compounded by being of illegitimate birth or pretending to belong to a lineage that he does not. The verse highlights contemptible traits, both in terms of behavior and social status, indicating a severe moral and ethical flaw. It serves as a denunciation of those who embody such negative attributes and acts as a deterrent against such vileness.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: Because he possesses wealth and children.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the attitude of those who take pride in their material wealth and offspring. It implies that such individuals might become arrogant or heedless of their spiritual duties due to their worldly possessions. The verse serves as a reminder that one's spiritual state and relationship with God are not determined by material wealth or offspring, but by piety and righteous actions.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the dismissive attitude of some people towards divine revelation. They accuse the Qur'anic verses of being mere myths or stories of the past, refusing to acknowledge their divine origin and guidance. This response indicates a stubborn rejection and mockery of the message, often driven by arrogance or a refusal to change one's ways.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: We will brand him on the snout.
interpretation: This verse reflects a strong denunciation and severe rebuke. The 'snout' metaphorically signifies the height of arrogance and disdain. Branding is a form of punishment that signifies disgrace and humiliation. Therefore, this verse serves as a warning to those who are prideful and insolent, suggesting that their arrogance will lead to their ultimate humiliation and disgrace.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the early morning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the trials that Allah places upon people to test their faith and patience. The reference to the 'companions of the garden' is a historical event where a group of people were tested by their intention to harvest their garden's fruits without sharing with the poor, leading to the garden's destruction as a divine consequence of their greed and failure to uphold moral responsibilities. It illustrates that similar tests are a part of divine wisdom to cultivate righteousness and humility among believers.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: And they did not make any exception.
interpretation: This verse points to the human habit of making statements or plans without considering the will of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging God's will in all actions and decisions, reminding believers to reflect humility and the dependence on divine will in their speech and intentions.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: So there came upon it an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse alludes to a sudden and unexpected calamity that befell a group of people as a form of divine retribution, highlighting the themes of accountability and the omnipresence of God's power. The fact that it occurred while they were asleep underscores the inevitability and the surprising nature of divine intervention, emphasizing that no one can escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: And it became as though reaped.
interpretation: This verse often describes the aftermath of divine punishment where a once flourishing garden, upon which its owners relied heavily, is transformed overnight into a barren land. This change serves as a stark reminder of the transient nature of worldly possessions and the consequences of ingratitude and neglect of one’s duty towards those in need. It signifies that no matter the abundance and prosperity one might enjoy, it can be taken away in an instant by the will of Allah, highlighting the importance of humility and righteousness.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: And they called out to one another at morning
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene where people are engaging in calling or alerting each other during the early hours of the morning. It emphasizes the urgency or importance of their actions and their unity in purpose at the start of a new day. This could symbolize the beginning of an important task or mission that requires collective effort and alertness.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: Go early to your crops if you intend to harvest.
interpretation: This verse can be interpreted as guidance to seize the right moment and be diligent in managing one's resources. It emphasizes the importance of timely action and dedication in achieving success. The context suggests a lesson about the consequences of neglect or misuse of one's blessings and opportunities.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: So they went off, whispering to one another.
interpretation: This verse describes a moment when a group of people set off together, speaking in low voices to keep their conversation private. The context often involves secrecy or planning, indicating that what they are about to do might not be something they want others to know about. It suggests a sense of conspiracy or quiet plotting among them.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: No poor person shall enter it today against your will.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of access, denying entry to the needy or poor. It reflects a human tendency towards selfishness and exclusivity, often driven by a desire to protect one's own interests, even at the expense of others who are less fortunate. The verse may serve as a moral lesson, encouraging readers to reflect on their own behavior towards those in need.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they went, early in determination, assuming themselves able.
interpretation: This verse depicts people who set out with the determination to achieve something, confident in their own abilities and power. It reflects a mindset of self-reliance and confidence, possibly highlighting human arrogance or self-assuredness in undertaking their plans without seeking divine guidance or acknowledging God's will. The verse serves as a reminder that human efforts are ultimately subject to God's control and that humility and acknowledgment of divine power are essential.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: But when they saw it, they said, 'We are indeed lost.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of sudden realization and acknowledgment of a mistake or misjudgment. It reflects a deeper spiritual awakening where individuals recognize their error in understanding or direction. This can be seen as both an immediate reaction to a physical situation and a metaphor for spiritual or moral disorientation, prompting a need to seek guidance and rectify one's path.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: No, we are deprived!
interpretation: This statement reflects a realization or admission of being deprived or facing loss. It can be understood in the context of acknowledging a situation where, despite efforts or expectations, the desired outcome has not been achieved. This could relate to material, spiritual, or even relational aspects, emphasizing the feelings of being denied or lacking something significant.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: The most moderate of them said, 'Did I not say to you, why do you not glorify (Allah)?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the admonishment by the most reasonable or sensible among a group, urging them to remember Allah and express gratitude. The speaker highlights the importance of glorifying and remembering Allah to prevent misfortune and to stay mindful of the divine presence in their affairs.
orig: قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون

translation: They said, 'Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: In this verse, individuals are acknowledging their mistakes and seeking forgiveness by glorifying Allah. They recognize their wrongdoing and express remorse, demonstrating a sincere repentance and a return to the path of righteousness. This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and self-awareness in one's spiritual journey.
orig: قالوا سبحان ربنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of mutual reproach among a group of people, reflecting on their past actions and the consequences they are facing. It highlights the human tendency to shift blame and the realization of collective responsibility in the face of adversity. The context and deeper implications can be linked to a narrative of moral and ethical lessons in the broader text.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون

translation: They will say, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization and regret of those who deviated from the righteous path. At this moment of acknowledgment, they express their profound remorse and despair over their past misdeeds and transgressions. It serves as a warning to the believers to adhere to the guidance of Allah and avoid arrogance and wrongdoing, emphasizing the severe consequences of straying from the divine commands.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين

translation: Perhaps our Lord will give us something better than it. Truly, we turn to our Lord with hope.
interpretation: This verse reflects a hope and trust in God's mercy and generosity. Even in loss or hardship, there is an underlying belief that God may provide something better in the future. It shows the attitude of relying on God's wisdom and being willing to accept His plans, highlighting a sense of patience, faith, and devotion to God amidst trials.
orig: عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون

translation: Such is the punishment [in this world]. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe nature of the punishment on the Day of Judgment compared to any suffering experienced in this worldly life. It serves as a solemn warning and a call to awareness for those who are heedless of the consequences of their actions, reminding them that divine retribution in the Hereafter will be far more challenging and formidable. It aims to encourage reflection and repentance by presenting the ultimate accountability awaiting in the life to come.
orig: كذلك العذاب ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are pious and conscientious of their duties to their Lord will be rewarded with eternal bliss and pleasure in gardens of paradise. It highlights the value and reward accorded to righteousness and piety in the sight of Allah.
orig: إن للمتقين عند ربهم جنات النعيم

translation: Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who submit to God's will (Muslims) and those who are guilty of wrongdoing (criminals). It highlights the principle of justice in divine judgment, asserting that it would be unjust and irrational to equate the righteous with the wicked. The verse serves as a reassurance to the faithful that their efforts in adhering to God's guidance will be recognized and rewarded distinctly from those who reject or oppose it.
orig: أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين

translation: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is addressing a group of people, questioning their sense of judgment and decision-making. It implies a reproach or criticism of their ability to discern right from wrong, as their conclusions or actions are being challenged. The verse calls for self-reflection and invites the audience to reconsider their reasoning and judgment processes.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: Or have you a book wherein you learn
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim to have divine knowledge or authority that contradicts the Qur'an. It asks rhetorically if they possess another sacred book that provides them with the knowledge they rely upon, thereby questioning the legitimacy and authenticity of any other source of divine guidance aside from the Qur'an.
orig: أم لكم كتاب فيه تدرسون

translation: Indeed, you have in it whatever you choose.
interpretation: This verse implies that the believers will have the freedom of choice and an abundance of blessings in the Hereafter. It highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah in granting the faithful their desires and preferences in the afterlife, underscoring the concept of ultimate reward and satisfaction for those who have lived righteously.
orig: إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون

translation: Or do you have binding oaths upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you decide?
interpretation: This verse addresses the unbelievers' presumptuous claims and false sense of entitlement, emphasizing that they have no binding promises from Allah guaranteeing them whatever they whimsically desire or rule. It underscores the necessity of submitting to Allah’s will and divine decree rather than assuming unfounded rights or expectations.
orig: أم لكم أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة إن لكم لما تحكمون

translation: Ask them which of them will take responsibility for that.
interpretation: In this verse, the Qur'an challenges the doubters and deniers to step forward and take responsibility for their claims. It implies a sense of accountability and showcases the improbability and unlikelihood of anyone stepping up to substantiate false statements against the message of the Qur'an. It underscores the seriousness of making claims and the responsibility one carries in doing so.
orig: سلهم أيهم بذلك زعيم

translation: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners if they are truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief of polytheists by questioning the legitimacy of their so-called partners with God. It sarcastically dares them to present any evidence or proof of their claims if they are truthful. Implicitly, it underscores the lack of any real basis for associating other deities with God, emphasizing the concept of monotheism and the singularity of God's sovereignty.
orig: أم لهم شركاء فليأتوا بشركائهم إن كانوا صادقين

translation: The Day the shin will be uncovered and they are invited to prostration but they will not be able to.
interpretation: This verse refers to a future event on the Day of Judgment where a significant and revealing event will take place, symbolized by the 'uncovering of the shin'. It implies a moment of great truth or reality being exposed. Those who rejected the guidance in their earthly lives will be called to prostrate — to show humility and submission — but they will find themselves unable to do so. This inability symbolizes their ultimate realization and regret for their past disobedience and arrogance. The verse serves as a stark warning and a call for self-reflection in the present life.
orig: يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون

translation: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.
interpretation: This verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment when certain people, who were once in good health and sound condition in their earthly lives, will be filled with a sense of shame and humility. Despite being called to submit in worship during their lifetime, they neglected this call. On that day, their arrogance will be replaced with humiliation and their gaze will be lowered in submission, signifying their regret and acknowledgment of their past negligence.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون

translation: So leave Me to deal with the one who denies this discourse. We will lead them gradually (to their ruin) in a way that they do not realize.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God is fully aware of those who reject the message of the Qur'an and assures that He will handle them in due course. The phrase 'lead them gradually' suggests a slow and deliberate process by which those who deny the message will be led towards their ultimate downfall, implying both divine patience and inevitability of divine justice. This serves as both a warning to the disbelievers and a reassurance to the faithful that truth and justice will prevail.
orig: فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse reflects God's assurance of His ultimate control and authority over all affairs. By stating that He will grant respite to wrongdoers, it signifies His mercy and patience, allowing them opportunities to repent. However, the assertion that His plan is firm underscores the certainty of divine justice. The verse conveys that God's strategic planning is perfect and unassailable, reassuring the faithful of eventual justice and the inevitable consequences for the unjust.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are burdened with debt?
interpretation: In this verse, it is highlighted that the Prophet Muhammad does not seek any monetary reward or payment from the people for delivering the message of Islam. The burden of disbelief and rejection comes solely from their own disposition and not because of any financial demands placed upon them by the Prophet. This serves to emphasize the selfless nature of his mission and refutes any notion that he is motivated by material gain.
orig: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون

translation: Or do they have the unseen (knowledge), so they write (it) down?
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim knowledge of the unseen and the future. It questions their authority and capability to record and predict outcomes that are beyond human comprehension. It implies that only Allah possesses true knowledge of the unseen and cautions against human presumption in matters that surpass human understanding and competence.
orig: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون

translation: So be patient with the decree of your Lord and do not be like the Companion of the Fish, when he cried out while he was distressed.
